nuance: The burning of Kama at Korukkai becomes restraint. இலிங்க வழியது போக்கி is traditionally taken as reversing the way of the sexual organ, holding the seed; it may also refer to the linga of worship. கொறுக்கை is Korukkai, with a likely pun on curbing.

title: இலிங்க புராணம்
theme: Stories of the Linga Purana (இலிங்க புராணம்): the mountain's daughter, Vishnu and Brahma, Ravana, Chandesa and the gods each worshipped or submitted and received the Lord's grace; the Lord who destroyed the three cities is not hard to reach, and is not false to those who love him.
structure_note: A string of puranic episodes (347, 349 to 352) around one assurance (348): the Lord is not out of reach for those with devotion.
source_issues: 351 line 2 (அறுவகை ஆன்ஐந்தும்) is unclear; அறுவகை may be corrupt.

reading: Resolving to reach his feet and looking to our First, she became the daughter of the crowned mountain-king, did firm tapas, and, as the gods knew, worshipped him fully on earth and gave him devotion.
nuance: The goddess is unnamed; the mountain's daughter is Parvati. Even the Lord's consort reaches him by tapas and worship, the means open to devotees.

reading: Do not grow weary thinking the Lord who destroyed the wandering three cities is hard to reach; the Lord is not false to those who love him, and he stands with tenderness and knows their worth.
nuance: புரிவுடையார், those with புரிவு, may be those with love, with longing, or with understanding. பரிசறிவான் may be 'knows their worth' or 'knows what to give them'.

reading: When Brahma and Vishnu circled the sea and did reverence through an age, the bright-flamed First gave the discus to Achyuta in that way, and gave a sword to Brahma as well.
nuance: ஆழி may be the sea or the wheel, and வலம் circling or power; the first two lines are hard to fix. The gift of the discus to Vishnu is a known legend; the sword to Brahma is less familiar.

reading: He who bore twenty arms and lifted the great mountain high had a matchless strength; when the Lord crushed him there and he cried 'Hara!', the Stainless One gave him unending grace.
nuance: Ravana is not named. The verse moves from pride in strength to a single cry and to grace that does not leave: the crushing is the first step of grace.

reading: Chandi, who knew what was coming, heaped fine sand and bathed it with the five products of the cow; when his father came in hostility and wrecked it, he grew angry, cut him with the axe, and received a garland.
nuance: The legend of Chandesa, the cowherd boy who worshipped a sand linga and struck his father's leg when he kicked it over, and was made chief of the Lord's servants and given his garland. அறுவகை (six kinds) and உறுவது அறி are unclear. The verse reports the act and the reward without comment.

reading: The gods all ran together, faces withered, went in distress, sought him and bowed saying 'Lord, we bow'; the One of matchless fame said 'Rise'.
nuance: The occasion is not named; it is often taken as the poison rising from the churned ocean. நம என்று may be the 'namah' of worship.

title: தக்கன் வேள்வி
theme: Daksha's sacrifice (தக்கன் வேள்வி): a rite performed without Siva breaks down when he is angered, and the gods who took part are maimed for lack of his grace; yet Siva is the power within the very fire of the sacrifice, and after his anger he gave grace, so the devotee need not waver.
structure_note: The rite fails at Siva's anger (353, 354); Siva is shown as the nature of the sacrificial fire (355 to 357); the gods are maimed (358) and mantra used for gain is condemned (359); Siva's grace in destroying the asuras (360) and the closing assurance (361).
source_issues: 356: variants அலந்திருந்தானே and அமர்ந்திருந்தானே change the closing sense (troubled, seated) from அலர்ந்திருந்தானே (blossomed); 357's opening supports the text's reading. 357 has the variant அலந்திருந்.
358: variant சிந்தைகை for சிறந்தகை would add 'mind' to the list of maimed parts.
361: variant line 3 reads விளிந்தானத் தக்கனவ் வேள்வியை.

reading: When the Father, the Lord, grew angry, fire burst out through the blazing flame of Daksha's sacrifice, and the gods, unable to finish the worship they had begun, its order broken, scattered.
nuance: The verse does not tell the story's cause, Daksha's leaving Siva out of the rite; it assumes it. What it shows is a rite whose order (முறை) collapses the moment its true Lord is angered.

reading: Seeing the rite performed, Hari rose and said 'this one is not our lord; we have fallen into the binding snare of the world', did penance, and the endless one gave him grace.
nuance: Who says 'எந்தை இவன் அல்ல' and of whom is unclear: it may be Hari disowning Daksha, or a confession that they had taken the wrong lord. சந்தி may mean the twilight rite or simply the ritual. The penance-then-grace pattern is plain.

reading: Just so, in the sacrifice of Brahma's son the Prajapati, though the fire was a marvel, Siva entered into its very nature and stood exulting within it.
nuance: அப்பரிசே (in that way) opens every line, and the next verse repeats the device. அயனார்பதி is read as Daksha, a lord born of Brahma; ஆலிக்கின்றான் may mean exulting, roaring or dancing. The claim, as read, is that even a rite that excludes Siva burns only with his power.

reading: Just so he is the cause of Brahma, Vishnu and the other gods being what they are; just so, entering the fire on every day there is, he became that fire and stood blossomed forth.
nuance: The variants அலந்திருந்தானே (stood suffering, troubled) and அமர்ந்திருந்தானே (stayed seated) give different last words; அலர்ந்திருந்தானே (stood blossomed) is taken up by the next verse's opening, which supports it.

reading: While the gods praised him as the one who had blossomed forth, he looked hard at the low fire that confers lineage so that it was seized; the red Supreme went and caught it, and came running by the great way he delighted in.
nuance: குலந்தரும் கீழங்கி (the lower fire that gives lineage) and the last two lines are obscure; they may describe Siva, as Virabhadra, seizing the sacrificial fire. I can't fix the sense beyond that.

reading: Hari, Brahma, Daksha, the sun, the rising moon, the young goddess, Agni and Indra lost head, face, nose, hand and shoulder: without Hara's grace even those good ones were ruined.
nuance: The list follows the story in which each god at the sacrifice was maimed in one part, Daksha losing his head. The verse pairs gods and body parts only loosely. Its point is the last line: the gods are 'good' (நல்லோர்), and still fall without grace. வாலை is taken as a goddess, perhaps Sarasvati, whose nose was cut in the story.

reading: Gods who did penance and whisper mantras in the ear, who lay out the kitchen of the oblation with mantras and do ear-mantras looking to their own gain: such a gathered mantra is a cruel thing.
nuance: செவிமந்திரம் (ear-mantra, the whispered initiation formula) and குவிமந்திரம் (gathered or concentrated mantra) are technical. கொல் may be a doubt particle or mean 'kills'. As read, the target is ritual turned to self-interest, not mantra itself.

reading: When the many gods begged him to show grace, so that the nine fire-pits of the good might give joy, he who set blazing fire to the cities with his bow did so that the wicked asuras would perish.
nuance: நவகுண்டம் (the nine fire-pits) is a ritual term. The verse sets Siva's destroying the three cities beside the rite: his destruction here protects worship rather than breaking it, the reverse of Daksha's case. The tie between the two halves is my reading.

reading: Though even the clear-minded are shaken, do not you be shaken: the one we reach is our first Lord who sustains us, he of pure word who in anger destroyed Daksha's sacrifice and then gave grace.
nuance: The address turns to the listener (நீ). சுளிந்து ஆங்கு அருள்செய்த, angered and then giving grace, holds the chapter's two sides together. The tradition that Daksha was restored with a goat's head is not in the verse.

title: பிரளயம்
theme: The deluge (பிரளயம்): when the flood covers the world and the gods contend, Siva alone stands as light and mountain above the waters, tells the gods not to fear, and keeps the sea within bounds; the gods praise him without knowing his purpose.
source_issues: 364 line 4 (கண்கடல் செய்யும்) and 366 as a whole are obscure; the sense may be corrupt or depend on lost context.

reading: When the flood rose and covered the dark mountains and the two contended, each crying 'I am king', the Lord alone became a towering light reaching down into the water and stood as a mountain no one could scale, and gave grace.
nuance: இருவர் (the two) are traditionally Brahma and Vishnu, and கோ (king) their claim to supremacy; the verse folds the column of fire story, told fully in chapter 41, into the deluge. ஒருவனும் stresses that he alone stands.

reading: The one who bears the name Lord of the gods of the universe cut through the surging sea and, seeing the world in its fire, ran without falling in and said 'Fear not' so that they would not fall into the mouth of the waves.
nuance: உலகார் அழற்கண்டு may be 'seeing the fire that fills the world' or 'seeing the world's people in distress'. அஞ்சல் (fear not) is the gesture of protection, and the verse's centre.

reading: The immortals and gods whom the cool sea let go bow to him as our Lord encircled by the eight seas, but they do not know the purpose of the one who rises above the sky-sea and beyond it.
nuance: விண்கடல் (sky-sea) and கண்கடல் செய்யும் (makes a sea of the eye, or makes the sea vast) are obscure. The plain point is the gap between worship and knowing: the gods praise him and still don't grasp his intent.

reading: Who in this world can order things as he does, the one praised as self-born and able to create? When the roar of the sea swelled over the bewildering waters, he set a fire within it so that it would not overflow.
nuance: The fire set in the sea is traditionally the submarine mare's-head fire (வடவைத்தீ) that drinks the ocean and keeps it from flooding the land. The verse names only அங்கி (fire). சயம்பு (svayambhu) is often an epithet of Brahma, so the first line may contrast praise of Brahma with Siva's real ordering power.

reading: Going beyond the worship that ruins good qualities, he sought out the friend seated in the lotus whose eye does not fail, took that head, and took up a way of living that heaven does not blame.
nuance: The verse plays on பழி (blame, ruin) in every line. அச்சிரம் (that head) and the one in the lotus point to the story of Siva taking Brahma's fifth head and then going about begging with the skull; that is tradition's reading, and the verse's own sense is obscure. Its link to the deluge is not clear.

title: சக்கரப்பேறு
theme: Receiving the discus (சக்கரப்பேறு): Vishnu's discus comes from Siva, who made and owns all things; Vishnu could not bear it until he worshipped Siva, who divided its power between Vishnu, Shakti and himself; at Daksha's sacrifice the discus Vishnu hurled at Siva's side was useless.
source_issues: 368: variant திரிக்கவொண் (spin, wield) for தரிக்கவொண் (bear) changes the sense.
370 line 4 (அக்கி உமிழ்ந்தது வாயுக் கரத்திலே) is obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: The verse names things the Lord has made and owns: Mal and his gift, ahankara, the elephant, the discus in the sky, the silver mountain, Indra's city Amaravati and the enjoyments of the seven worlds.
nuance: The first two lines are hard to parse: மால் போதகன் may be 'Mal the elephant' or 'Mal the one taught', and காங்காரம் is read as ahankara. The last line is clear: he made and possesses all. The verse sets up the chapter by making the discus one of Siva's possessions.

reading: Damodara, having received the discus but unable to bear it, worshipped Hara with longing, and the fitting good power was divided into a share for him.
nuance: Who makes the share (கூறு செய்தது) is not said; the next verse makes it Siva. The variant திரிக்கவொண்ணாமை (could not spin it) for தரிக்கவொண்ணாமை (could not bear it) changes the difficulty from holding the weapon to wielding it.

reading: Intending it in portions, he divided the good discus: a share he gave to Mal, a share he gave to Shakti, and a share he kept and bore as his own form.
nuance: கூறது (a share) begins every line. The discus here seems to stand for a power (சக்தி) that can be divided rather than a single weapon; what Shakti's share and Siva's share mean is left unstated.

reading: At Daksha's sacrifice, when Damodara loosed his discus at the moon-crowned one among the heroes who shattered the sacrifice, fire was spat out in the hand of Vayu.
nuance: The last line (அக்கி உமிழ்ந்தது வாயுக் கரத்திலே) is obscure: it may mean the discus spat fire, or that it was rendered harmless. In one telling Virabhadra's side swallowed the discus. சசிமுடி (moon-crowned) is Siva or Virabhadra.

title: எலும்பும் கபாலமும்
theme: Bone and skull (எலும்பும் கபாலமும்): Siva rises bearing bones and a skull, and it is his bearing them that keeps the gods' bones and skulls from crumbling into earth.
source_issues: 371: வலம்பன் is unusual and its sense uncertain.

reading: The strong one, first of the jewel-crowned gods, rose bearing bones and a skull; had he not borne them, those bones and skulls would have broken and become earth.
nuance: Tradition reads the bones and skulls as those of Brahma, Vishnu and the gods, which Siva wears after their deaths at the end of an aeon; by bearing them he keeps them. The verse says only that without his bearing them they would fall to dust. வலம்பன் is taken as 'the strong one'; it may be a corrupt or rare word.

title: அடிமுடி தேடல்
theme: The search for the head and feet (அடிமுடி தேடல்): when Brahma and Vishnu each claim to be the Lord, Siva stands before them as a boundless column of fire whose crown and feet neither can find; he is flesh, life and awareness and beyond sun and moon, and is reached not by those who worship for gifts but by those who give themselves to him.
structure_note: The quarrel and the fire (372, 373), Siva as all and beyond all (374), the failed search (375, 376), Brahma and Vishnu within his nature (377), the linga and the true path (378), and the contrast between gods who seek gifts and devotees who reach his feet (379, 380).
source_issues: 373: variant last line நானே அறிந்தேனென் ஆண்மையினாலே (by my own power) reverses the sense of the text's அவனாண்மையாலே (by his power).
377: variant கடலூழித் for கடல் வாழித் changes Vishnu's epithet.
378 and 380 are obscure in places (முங்கண், கோலிங்கமைஞ்சு; வீழித் தலைநீர்) and may be corrupt.

reading: When Brahma and Mal, through their own folly, each said 'I am the Lord', the Supreme stood before them spread out as fire, and they searched for Hara's feet and cried out.
nuance: பேதைமை (folly) is named as the cause of the claim, not of the search. அரற்றுகின்றார் (cry out, lament) ends the verse on their helplessness rather than on any finding.

reading: While they said 'we stand filling the seven worlds', the Lord himself stood as a mass of flame through the seven worlds; I came to know him, the great-gem-throated one who fills the seven heavens, by his own might.
nuance: The first line may be the two gods' boast. The variant last line, நானே அறிந்தேன் என் ஆண்மையினாலே (I knew him by my own power), reverses the sense: the text makes knowledge of Siva his gift, the variant the knower's achievement. With the text, the speaker succeeds where the gods' self-claim failed.

reading: As flesh, as life, as awareness and as fire, as the far heaven and as the holy form of the gods' fire, he passed beyond the pillar of the universe, the sun and the cool moon, and stood as the whole universe that he rules.
nuance: The verse moves from the body (ஊன்) outward to the cosmos, so that Siva is at once in the flesh and beyond the sun and moon. தாணு means pillar and is also a name of Siva; here it may be the axis of the cosmos.

reading: He stood, the tall one, through all the earth and the universe; then the two who sought out his form were afraid; one went up toward the holy crown, and the good anklet-feet could not be found either.
nuance: அஞ்சினர் (they feared) adds what the story often leaves out: the search ends in fear, not just failure. Tradition has Brahma fly up as a swan and Vishnu dig down as a boar; the verse names neither.

reading: The gods close in devotion who praise his red feet, the one who asked for three steps, the sages, and Brahma who makes the worlds by verse: this is how they stride and come to bow their heads.
nuance: The verse plays on அடி (foot, step, metrical foot): சேவடி, மூவடி (Vamana's three steps), பாவடி, தாவடி. பாவடியாலே பதஞ்செய் பிரமன் may mean Brahma who creates by Vedic verse. The last line is read as the great at last bowing to Siva's feet; it may also be ironic.

reading: The four-faced one seated in the lotus and the lord who dwells in the dark sea both share the nature of that great being, who is sensed within the body as its life.
nuance: The syntax could equally say that Brahma and Vishnu are of his nature, or that they abide within it. The variant கடலூழித் தலைவன் (lord of the sea at the aeon's end) changes the epithet for Vishnu. The image of life felt within flesh brings the cosmic Lord inside the body.

reading: The supreme light that rose as an embrace set here a true path above; seeing it, the world embraces it and circles it, and grace may be gained by those who turn to it.
nuance: ஆலிங்கனம் (embrace) puns on இலிங்கம் (linga); the verse is traditionally read as the column of fire becoming the linga that the world worships by circling. முங்கண் (three eyes, or 'the front') and கோலிங்கமைஞ்சு are obscure.

reading: The gods who worshipped the one who gave the sword do not know Hara as we do who gave ourselves to him; they will not reach the feet of him who took us as his own, gave us joy and gave us his feet to hold.
nuance: ஆள்கொடுத்து is used twice: the devotees give themselves (become his servants), and he takes them as his own. The gods worship for a gift (the sword given to Brahma) and so stay outside; the contrast is between worship for boons and self-giving.

reading: To the one who circled through the aeon and asked of him, the four-faced one comes forth and appears; when he said 'give what was ordained, the water from the fallen head', he outshone the light of the sun at the aeon's end.
nuance: The verse is obscure. ஊழி வலஞ்செய்து echoes 349, where Brahma and Vishnu circle Siva through the aeon, and வீழித் தலைநீர் may refer to the Ganga from Siva's head or to the skull of Brahma. Only the close is clear: Siva's light surpasses the sun of the final dissolution.

title: படைத்தல்
theme: Creation (படைத்தல்): from the beginningless Supreme come Shakti, nada and bindu, and from bindu, as Maya, the tattvas, elements and worlds. The gods who create and keep the worlds act within this order; the Lord alone, with his Shakti, is said to create, protect and remove the worlds and to be their life.
structure_note: The chapter opens with the pure order of manifestation (381 to 385: Supreme, Shakti, nada, bindu, the elements), turns to the Lord and Shakti as the pair who create through the gods of the five acts (386 to 403), sums up in the refrain verses on the one who creates, protects and removes (404, 407), and ends with the Lord as the eighty-four lakh kinds of life and with everything as born of bindu (409, 410).
source_issues: 406 and 414 are nearly the same verse (கூடும் பிறவிக் in 406, கூடு மரபிற் in 414, and 414's variant restores கூடும்பிறவிக்); one is probably a duplicate.
404 and 407 are the same quatrain with ஒருவனுமே and ஓராயமே; ஓராயமே may be a corruption.
405: the variant last line ஐந்தார் பிறவி அமைத்து நின்றானே reverses the sense of the received அந்தார் பிறவி அறுத்துநின் றானே.
399: the count of parts (முப்பால், ஒன்று, மற்றைய மூன்று) does not add up as read.
385: கான் and தேன் do not fit the expected sequence of elements and may be corrupt.
384: சாத்துமான் is obscure.

reading: The supreme beyond the supreme, without beginning or end, unites as knowledge with its consort power; as light spreads in that, the flawless Para appears, and from her nada shines.
nuance: பராபரம் and பராபரை are a male and female pair, traditionally Siva and his Shakti; the variant பராபரன் makes the first explicitly personal. The order Supreme, Shakti, Para, nada is the tradition's sequence of pure manifestation; the verse states it compactly and the steps are not fixed by it alone.

reading: In nada is bindu, and in nada and bindu Siva and Shakti come within, flawless; as they divide, knowledge and action are born, and bindu rises out of the will that impels them.
nuance: ஞானம், கிரியை and இச்சை are traditionally Shakti's three powers of knowing, acting and willing. வாதித்த (impelling, or arguing) is unusual here.

reading: What was not comes to be in Shakti's place and stays mingled within like light in a gem; that Being which opened the way for it to become mighty is, if one tries to put it into words, farther than far.
nuance: இல்லது can mean 'what does not exist' or 'what has no abode'; the reading turns on it. கல்லொளி, light in a stone or gem, is an image of presence that is inside yet unmixed. The last line is plain: the source is beyond speech.

reading: From that farness the light becomes a Shakti, nada joins with longing and becomes a bindu, and Sadasiva becomes the support of the five beginning with earth, with Shakti as their binding.
nuance: சாத்துமான் at the end is obscure; I take it loosely as 'that which binds or holds'. The five from earth are the elements. The verse continues 383's தூராதி தூரமே by opening with தூரத்தில்.

reading: In mahat space arises and air grows, water mingles and hardens, the five crowd together and become the five elements, and standing in the flower the worlds take form.
nuance: மான் is taken as mahat, the great tattva, and the verse as the usual chain of elements from space to earth; கான் (forest, or fire) and தேன் (honey) are hard to fit to that chain and may be corrupt or symbolic. பூ may be the earth or Brahma's lotus.

reading: One He and one She create the world; those who create it have five sons; the creator is also the one seated on the flower, and the one who creates the world is that holy one himself.
nuance: The five sons are traditionally the five lords of the five acts (Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra, Maheshvara, Sadasiva). The verse repeats புவனம் படைப்பான் four times: creation is credited to the pair, to Brahma and to the holy one, and the last line gathers them into one.

reading: The holy Nandi, joined with the Shakti who nurtures cool mahat in every world, in union wholly by nature of the eye, blossoms in the flower of earth's nature.
nuance: கண்ணியல்பாக and மண்ணியல்பாக are paired but unclear; the sense of Siva and Shakti together flowering into the world is clear, the details are not.

reading: In water pleasure is born, in fire light in the body, in air the sounding power of good life's breath, and between water and earth the state of birth.
nuance: The verse seems to match elements to qualities (taste, form, sound, smell) and to the body, but its lines do not give a clean scheme; the variant காய்கதிர் for காயத்திற் would make 'the burning sun's light' instead of 'light in the body'.

reading: With the one who swallowed and spat out the seven worlds, with the head of the gods and the first one, and with the four-faced cause, it is that Being who of old creates this world.
nuance: The one who swallowed the worlds is Vishnu in his familiar myth, the four-faced one Brahma. The verse makes them companions of the creator, not the creator; whether அண்டத்தமரர் தலைவன் and ஆதி are Rudra or the Lord himself is unclear.

reading: With the sky that lies within the vast ocean, the Supreme of Kailasa, and Brahma above on the swelling lotus, he knew how life is placed there.
nuance: The three figures are usually taken as Vishnu (the one in the ocean), Siva of Kailasa and Brahma; the subject of உணர்ந்தானே is not named.

reading: The Cause stands everywhere, mingled in love; Narayana stands as the middle body; the four-faced one, from love of the Lord of the world, shapes its parts and is settled as the world of the Veda.
nuance: காரணன், நாரணன், பாரணன் and ஆரணம் chime. பதஞ்செய்யும் may mean 'makes ready' or 'makes the stations'; நடுவுடல் (middle body) is obscure.

reading: There is a Lord whose kindness is easy to reach, who makes the great gem yield its fruit with ease; staying there as Brahma's light he creates, and I have understood clearly the easy way to the fruit.
nuance: பருமாமணி (great gem) and அயஒளி (Brahma's light, or the light of the unborn) are not fixed by the verse. எளிது (easy) is said three times; the point that the Lord is easy of access is plain.

reading: When the pure one in grace grants going and coming, and growth becomes thought, the merciful one himself strikes and stirs the eight directions that stand high.
nuance: போக்கும் வரவும, going and coming, is commonly taken as death and birth. Calling the one who stirs the directions தயாபரன், the supremely merciful, makes the stirring itself an act of grace.

reading: The spotless one who makes life stands in the middle: he measures my precious life into one life to fit a body, is help to the body that brings earlier suffering, and makes the life good.
nuance: முன்துயர் (earlier suffering) may be the karma that the body brings with it. நடுவு நின்றான் may mean 'stood within' or 'stood impartial'.

reading: In making things become, the Lord who wears bone beads and konrai, with a body adorned like burning red gold, enters the departing soul and is there as its body; he is the master who works becoming.
nuance: அக்கணி is taken as அக்கு அணி, wearing bone or rudraksha beads, and the konrai flower and red-gold body are Siva's marks. போகின்ற சீவன் may be the soul leaving one body for the next.

reading: One He and one She have set to play; the play of the two brings forth everything, many fruits in every season, and the work in one Tiru becomes the whole world.
nuance: திரு is commonly taken as Shakti, so that the world is her work; it could also be read as fortune or holiness. விளையாடல் makes creation play, not labour or need.

reading: The Lord of the worlds enters and knows, the lord with the discus enters and knows, the god on the flower enters and knows; they stand as those who enter and know up to the crown.
nuance: The three are usually Rudra, Vishnu and Brahma. The last line is obscure: முடிக்காகி may mean they know only so far, below the summit, which would set limits on these gods.

reading: The power of anava and the five within it, the lords of effect and cause in their order, born of bindu through the five acts they tend, can be called those from whom anava has not left.
nuance: ஆணவம் is the root impurity of Siddhanta. The verse's claim, as I read it, is that the five lords who carry out the five acts are themselves still bound souls, not the Lord: a strong ranking of the gods below Siva.

reading: Of the three parts that came, one is the rising of Maya; the other three are bindu risen from Maya; since nada, which begot it, is born of Para, this is the ancient play of the supreme Siva.
nuance: The count (three parts, one, then 'the other three') does not add up as read; a word may be lost or முப்பால் may be meant differently. The variant பெற்றவள் makes the begetter female.

reading: Space and the rest, and Sadasiva and the others, went out together within the unfailing Shakti: the great-bodied Isa, Hara, Mal and Brahma, so that space and earth are cared for.
nuance: The last line is unclear; with the variant அளித்ததே it would say that this is what gave space and earth.

reading: In the gracious triangle born of bindu she is Tripura; she settles as Sadasiva, and she performs the five acts.
nuance: அளியார், repeated at each line's head, may mean 'full of grace' or 'like bees'. முக்கோணம் (triangle) and வயிந்தவம் (born of bindu) suggest a yantra. Here the five acts are hers, where 404 gives them to the One.

reading: Manonmani with banded breasts, the auspicious one, mingled as cause and effect; she of the Veda, enchantress of the gods, the full one, is also the knowing at the root of all knowing.
nuance: A string of names of the goddess. With the variant பூதாதி the last line reads 'source of the elements' rather than 'knowing at the root of knowing'.

reading: He agreed to be these: Maheshvara who stands full as himself, Hara and Tirumal who go and move there, and Brahma on the flower who makes.
nuance: The gods are one Lord's forms, as the verse says, but மன்றது செய்யும் for Brahma is unclear.

reading: One alone created the seven worlds, one alone protected them, one alone wiped them away, and one alone is the life with the worlds.
nuance: The fourfold ஒருவனுமே insists on one agent where the chapter elsewhere names several gods and a Shakti. The variant உடலோடுயிர் makes the last line 'the life with the body'.

reading: Our Lord, red-lotus coloured, fire coloured and dark as the rain cloud, stands having cut off the birth that comes in Maya's bond and in union with women of flowered hair.
nuance: The three colours are commonly matched to Brahma, Rudra and Vishnu, all as the one Lord. The variant last line ஐந்தார் பிறவி அமைத்து நின்றானே says the opposite: that he set up five-fold birth. In a chapter on creation the variant fits as well as the received text.

reading: The great Nandi, who made the nature of the births in which soul, body and life come together in all eight directions people search, stands within those who seek him, and I know their way of seeking.
nuance: ஊடும் may mean 'who sulk with him' or 'who pass through', so 'those who seek' is a guess. The verse recurs almost word for word as 414.

reading: One host creates the seven worlds, one host protects them, one host wipes them away, and one host is the life with the worlds.
nuance: The verse repeats 404 with ஓராயமே in place of ஒருவனுமே. ஆயம் can mean a company or a gathering, so the agent may be the Lord's assembled powers; tradition differs on the word, and it may be a corruption of 404's line.

reading: The one Lord and the good two kneaded beings together with the dross of their kinds; to the two who stand ready asking what their task is, he, the first, gives grace.
nuance: The two are usually taken as Brahma and Vishnu, and கோது குலம் as the impure classes of beings. The verse is compressed and the reading is tentative.

reading: In that way he spreads truly as life in eighty-four lakh kinds; to men who talk falsely he stands covered by darkness.
nuance: The eighty-four lakh kinds of birth are a common count, also in the Tevaram, as Sengalvaraya notes. மெய்ப்பரிசு and பொய்ப்பரிசு play true against false manner: the Lord is present in all life, yet hidden from the false.

reading: Sun, moon, fire, the eight guardians, sky with its sound, water and earth, the contending qualities beginning with sound, speech, mind and the rest all come from the bindu of Maya, as is taught.
nuance: The list runs from cosmic bodies to the inner faculties, so that both the outer world and the mind come from one material source.

title: காத்தல்
theme: Protection (காத்தல்): the Lord keeps the world by entering and becoming it: space and darkness, praise and blame, body, life, elements and seasons, love and restraint. He shapes the world and its births as a potter shapes pots, and he holds each life in its body so that it is not cast off.
structure_note: Litany verses of the Lord standing as everything (411 to 416) lead to the potter image (417) and to verses on his holding life in the body (418 to 420). 414 repeats 406 from the chapter on creation.
source_issues: 414 repeats 406 almost word for word (மரபிற் for பிறவிக்); its variant gives 406's reading.

reading: He has entered and stands as open space and as darkness, as praise and as blame, as body and as life; he has entered and stays fixed in the mind.
nuance: The pairs are opposites (light and dark, praise and blame, body and life): the Lord keeps the world by being both sides of it. புகுந்துநின்றான், repeated, makes his presence an entering, not only an encompassing.

reading: He himself stands as the directions and the gods, as body, life and the tattvas, as ocean, mountain and the rest, and he is also the leader of the world.
nuance: The last line adds rule to presence: he is the world and also its head.

reading: As body, as life, as the world, as the ocean, as the dark cloud and the sky that pours rain, as what lies between, unfailing and everywhere himself, the Lord stands as the great way that those who do not come to him do not reach.
nuance: அடையார் can mean 'those who do not reach' or 'enemies'. The variant பெருவெளி makes the last line 'the great open space' instead of 'the great way'.

reading: The great Nandi, who made the nature of the line in which soul, body and life come together in all eight directions people search, stands within those who seek him, and I know their way of seeking.
nuance: Nearly identical to 406; here மரபு (line, order) stands for 406's பிறவி (birth), and the variant restores பிறவி. ஊடும் is unclear, as in 406.

reading: At one time he stands as a lone flame, at another as a fierce gale, at another as cool rain, and at another he is the cool Mayan.
nuance: மாயன் is usually Vishnu, the preserver, which suits a chapter on protection; it can also be read as the one of Maya. The changing forms run from fire and storm to cool rain, from harm to care.

reading: He stands as love, knowledge and restraint, as pleasure and the joy of union, as time past and the aeon, and he sits, with love, in the five.
nuance: ஐந்து (the five) is not named: the senses, the elements or the five acts are all possible. Putting love, restraint and the pleasure of union side by side makes the Lord present in both discipline and desire.

reading: He is the one who shapes the world, setting to it as a potter; he shapes births; the turning wheel, the pot, the small jar and all the rest he alone can shape.
nuance: The verse makes the Lord the potter, the maker, not the clay; tradition reads this as the Siddhanta view that God is the efficient cause while Maya is the material. சுற்றிய சால் may be the potter's wheel or a large pot.

reading: Nandi stands as the body, being the breath within; he who is open space, pure life and the light that earth holds, spreads in the body as the awareness of the inner life and holds it so the life is not cast off.
nuance: வெள்ளுயிர் (white or pure life) and நிலங்கொளி are obscure. The last line is clear: the Lord's keeping is holding life in the body, which values the body as the place of life.

reading: The nature that is hard to bear is also his; when he takes back the many lives there is nothing else; for all seven births that way is yoga's end, and he who stands supporting it is also that earth.
nuance: தாரணி may be the earth, the bearer, or dharana, yogic holding of the mind; the pun with தாங்கி (holding) suits both. யோகாந்தம் is a technical term not fixed by the verse.

reading: Though near he is far; joining in fire and drawing close, he gives a single shoot of knowledge; though he bends low he becomes the many lives on earth, and though he is quiet the Lord makes the earthly body.
nuance: பணுகினும் and தணிகினும் are uncertain words; ஞானக் கொழுந்து (the tender shoot of knowledge) is the clearest image. Fire (அங்கி) may be the sacrificial fire or the inner fire of yoga.

title: அழித்தல்
theme: Destruction (அழித்தல்): the Lord burns the world, the sea and the asuras with fire as his arrow, and the worlds are consumed like rice in the pot. Yet dissolution is also inward and saving: four kinds of saṃhāra run from daily sleep to the dissolution that is the truth of grace, and what returns to the void leaves the void itself unharmed.
structure_note: Cosmic burning (421 to 424) gives way to four verses (425 to 428) that each name the same four dissolutions (நித்த, வைத்த, சுத்த, உய்த்த) but define them differently, then to the image of crop and waste ground (429) and the Lord who destroys deeds (430).
source_issues: 425 to 428 give four differing definitions of the same four dissolutions; they may be variant recensions of one verse kept side by side.
427: line 2 has ஒத்தசங் காரம் where the parallel verses have வைத்த; the variant வைத்தசங் காரங் கேவலம் ஆன்மாவுக் restores it.
427: line 3 is printed with a stray space (டோ ய்வுறல்) for டோய்வுறல்.
430: line 1 reads தீயவைத் தார்மிங்கள், apparently a misprint (perhaps தீயவைத் தார்தங்கள்).

reading: The Lord who made fire burned the wide world, burned the surging sea, burned the asuras; fire is that Lord's arrow in hand.
nuance: Burning the asuras recalls the burning of the three cities, where the arrow is usually Vishnu with fire at its tip; here fire is the whole arrow. அங்கிசெய்து may also be 'wielding fire'.

reading: In the three dissolutions I came to know that the order which stood as one aeon was undone; the world, like soft rice on the boil, and the great land the mountains bore were burnt.
nuance: இலயங்கள் மூன்று and ஒன்றுகற்பாந்த are technical and not fixed by the verse. The image is plain: the world softens and is consumed like rice in the pot.

reading: The earth that gives footing, the eight snowy mountains, the seven seas with their tides and all the rest, the fire takes hold of and burns, and space too; there is no wonder in the heart that knows it.
nuance: பதஞ்செய்யும், உதஞ்செய்யும், குதஞ்செய்யும், விதஞ்செய்யும் rhyme but are hard to gloss; குதம் may be 'destroying' and விதம் 'forms'. The last line may mean the wise are not astonished at the world's end.

reading: The noble stream that came down from the cloud mountain, seeping through the cosmos to the eight directions, he set as fire upon the pit beyond Om.
nuance: குலக்கொடி may be the Ganga or a power such as kundalini; குண்டம் is the fire pit of the rite. The verse seems to make cosmic burning a fire rite beyond the syllable Om, but every term here is open.

reading: Daily dissolution is sleep's long stupor; the held dissolution is the state beyond waking; pure dissolution is kevala where action ceases; the dissolution that lifts up is the truth of the Supreme's grace.
nuance: The four names (நித்த, வைத்த, சுத்த, உய்த்த சங்காரம்) are technical. கேவலம் in Siddhanta usually names the soul's state wholly under anava, which sits oddly with 'pure'. Only the last term is constant across 425 to 428: the highest dissolution is grace.

reading: Daily dissolution is the putting off of the two bodies; the held dissolution is the dissolution of Maya; pure dissolution is immersion beyond the mind; the dissolution that lifts up is the truth of Siva's grace.
nuance: இரண்டுடல் (two bodies) may be the gross and subtle bodies. The same names as 425 receive different definitions.

reading: Daily dissolution is when the instruments' troubles are removed; the matching dissolution is shedding body and life; pure dissolution is immersion in what is beyond; the dissolution that lifts up is the truth of the Supreme's grace.
nuance: ஒத்த stands where 425 and 426 have வைத்த; the variant line வைத்தசங் காரங் கேவலம் ஆன்மாவுக் restores வைத்த and ties it to kevala. கருவி (instruments) are the faculties.

reading: Daily dissolution is in relieving long weariness; held dissolution is in the abiding beginningless bond; pure dissolution is the Supreme's untouched grace; and there is the dissolution that lifts up, when the four are weighed.
nuance: அனாதி (beginningless) is commonly taken as anava, the beginningless impurity. நாலா மதிக்கிலே closes the series by asking that the four be weighed together.

reading: The crop that rises with waste ground as its source, though it sinks back into waste, does not make the old waste waste away; the doings of Mal and Ayan, in the dissolution that does not last, sink as crop of the waste back into that waste.
nuance: பாழ் is barren ground and also the void; the verse plays on it six times. The plain sense is a field: what grows from it returns to it while the ground endures. Taken symbolically, the source (Maya or the void) outlasts what it yields, and even Vishnu's and Brahma's works end there.

reading: There is one strong Lord who set the deeds that reach evildoers to perish; he gave a body, mingled everywhere, set a company that thinks, and set those who understand.
nuance: மாயவைத்தான் may be 'made to perish' or 'set in Maya', and the reading turns on it. On the first reading, destruction here is the destruction of bad karma, a mercy, not a punishment. ஆயம் recalls 407.

title: மறைத்தல்
theme: Concealment (மறைத்தல்), the fourth of the Lord's five acts: the Lord dwells in the heart and in everything he has become, yet the heart does not know his form; he shuts the soul into a body of bone and flesh within the bond of pasa, and even the three gods do not know how he did it. Like the eye that sees all but not itself, he is present and unseen.
structure_note: The Lord unknown though within (431), the soul enclosed in the body by pasa (432, 433), those who do and do not reach him (434, 435), his hiding in what he has made (436, 438), a turn toward grace (437, 439), and the images of clay and eye (440).
source_issues: 436: அரைகின்று and கரகின்றவை look corrupt (perhaps for அறைகின்று, கரக்கின்றவை); the verse cannot be read with confidence.
438: variant கியங்கி யயந்திரு for line 2 changes which gods are named.
439: variant சித்தின் for சித்தன் changes the subject of lines 1 and 2.

reading: The One in the heart, the light dwelling within, the One who never leaves the heart by a single step: though the heart and he are together, the heart does not know his form.
nuance: உள்ளம் opens every line, so the verse keeps returning to the heart that holds him and still cannot see him. That nearness itself is the concealment, which is why the verse opens this chapter. The variant line 3 (உள்ளமும் அவனும் உறவாயிருந்தும், though heart and he are kin) keeps the sense.

reading: The Lord who made birth for joy also shut it up in the sorrow of the bond that causes suffering; fastening skin and flesh to bone and binding it to what went before, it runs on to its end.
nuance: தோற்றசை is read as தோல் தசை (skin and flesh). முன்பிற் கொளுவி, fastening to what is before, is commonly taken as binding the body to past deeds; the verse does not say so. The point is that the same Lord who intends joy conceals the soul inside the body and its bonds. The variant அடைந்தனன் would say the Lord himself entered that sorrow.

reading: Though the Lord, Madhavan and the Vedic one who made pleasure, all three, come and gather together, they do not know how the Hidden One placed the great machine of a body that the Lord made.
nuance: மறையவன் plays on மறை, which means both the Veda and hiding: in line 1 it most naturally names Brahma, in line 4 it can name Siva as the Concealer. Which god the first இறையவன் is (Rudra, or Siva himself) is unclear. இரும்பொறி யாக்கை, the body as a great mechanism, is a striking image. The variant பரிசறியாரே makes the three gods the subject explicitly.

reading: Those who come to know, with a heart and a tongue given to food, the Lord who loves the light of the seeing eye, the First who stands as male, female and neuter forms, will not come near the workings of the distant pool.
nuance: சேண்படு பொய்கைச் செயல், the working of the far-off pool, is obscure. It may be the pool of births, which the knowers escape, or bathing at a distant sacred tank, which they no longer need. ஊண்படு நாவுடை நெஞ்சம் can also be read against the knowers, as the food-bound heart that cannot reach him; the syntax allows both.

reading: The first Lord, who makes the ways by which joy is given to the world that grows clear and to the gods, and the pure white flame with its coiled radiance, stands where darkness ends and yet becomes a dark chamber.
nuance: The paradox of the last line, beyond darkness yet a dark room, fits the chapter: the light is hidden from those he conceals it from. சுருளும் சுடர், the coiled flame, is traditionally taken as a yogic light, perhaps kundalini; the plain sense is simply a radiant fire.

reading: The one worth beholding, who made the limbs that yield grace, the sound, the desire that speaks, the many unlike forms spreading out and the earth, becomes these himself and hides in them.
nuance: அரைகின்று and கரகின்றவை are odd forms; கரக்கின்ற (hiding) is the likely sense of the second and carries the chapter's theme. அங்கங்கள் may be bodily limbs or the Vedangas. The verse is too compressed to fix beyond its drift: he hides by becoming his works.

reading: Knowing the kinship within, I hid the Lord inside me; coming forth, he grants grace again; and the greatness called joy and love, even when it comes out in open worship, becomes an offering too.
nuance: The verse turns concealment round: here the devotee hides the Lord within, and the Lord comes out in grace. வேட்சி may mean desire or sacrifice (from வேட்டல்), so the last line may say open worship is still an offering, or that it turns into longing. The verse leads toward the next chapter, on grace.

reading: Maheshvara, who fills all and stands as himself, Hara and Tirumal who go and move there, and Ayan on the flower who does the work: becoming these, he abides in harmony with them.
nuance: In Siddhanta, Maheshvara is traditionally the god of the concealing act, which may be why he is named first here. மன்றது செய்யும் (doing the work of the hall, or of the assembly) is unclear, and the variant கியங்கி யயந்திரு changes line 2. The verse makes the gods modes of the one Lord, as 386 and 404 do.

reading: Within the gathered bond, the excellent siddha sits on the great bank seeking joy; if one keeps to the rare bank of the Ganga in a way that does not reckon on the shore to come, impurity can be washed away.
nuance: A plain reading is bathing in the Ganga; a yogic reading, common in tradition, places the Ganga within the body and the bank at the crown. வருங்கரை ஓரா (not reckoning the coming shore) and the variant சித்தின் (of consciousness) for சித்தன் leave the subject unclear. அழுக்கு is likely the soul's impurity rather than bodily dirt.

reading: One clay becomes many good vessels; for all the wombs within, there is one; one eye sees many things but does not see itself; the Lord too stands in this way.
nuance: Two images close the chapter. The clay gives one source in many forms; the eye gives the seer who is not seen. The eye may stand for the Lord, unseen because he is the one who sees, or for the soul, which cannot see the Lord who is in it; both readings fit concealment.

title: அருளல்
theme: Grace (அருளல்), the fifth of the Lord's five acts: the Lord who gladly made the worlds, the ages, the elements, the gods and the souls, and who binds and unbinds the body, stays near the mind of those who turn to him; he is in the body as milk is in water, and to see him there is bliss.
structure_note: The body tied and untied by the Lord (441), freedom from death for those who rejoice in nada (442), the potter's will (443), the Lord's eight qualities (444), three verses of repeated creation as gladness (445 to 447), his becoming the souls (448), and his presence as light and as milk in water, ending in the poet's own bliss (449, 450).
source_issues: 442: விச்சும் is unclear; read as விசும்பு (sky), it may be வித்தும் (seed).
449: variant மாபோதகமே for மாபோதமாமே changes the ending from 'great awareness' to 'great teacher'.

reading: The brow-eyed Lord sees to it: he ties and unties this bag of a body, which binds together the wind that blows in the eight directions, fire, the water of circling waves, the great earth and the sky, and is called the seat of life.
nuance: காயப்பை (the body as a bag) is plain, not contemptuous: the stress is on the Lord's tying and untying, birth and death, under a chapter on grace. வட்டத் திரை, circling waves, stands for water among the five elements.

reading: For those who long for the nada that rises and shines at the crown and take their joy in it, there is no Yama; he alone is able to fashion, as a carpenter does, the sky and the three spreading lights for the world.
nuance: உச்சியில் ஒளிதிகழ் நாதம், the shining sound at the crown, is a yogic term taken as the inner sound heard in meditation. விச்சும் is read as விசும்பு (sky), but may be வித்து (seed). The three lights are traditionally sun, moon and fire.

reading: From the clay set on his wheel the potter shapes whatever is in his mind; like the potter, if our lord Nandi wills it, the unmoving world becomes this or that.
nuance: The potter image makes the world the Lord's to shape at will. அசைவில் உலகம் (the world without motion) suggests inert matter that moves only by his will; the variant அயைவில் is unclear.

reading: He of wide expanse, the one unlike all others, the lord of a host of many bhutas, who by his nature has the bounty of keeping the world, whose qualities are the eight qualities, the matted-haired one, abides close to the mind.
nuance: எண்குணம், the eight qualities, is the term Kural 9 uses of the one to be worshipped. Here the eight belong to the matted-haired Siva. விரியுடையான் may mean the expansive one or the one with spread matted hair; விகிர்தன் is the one who is different, unlike the world.

reading: Gladly he made the seven worlds; gladly he made the many ages; gladly he made the five elements; gladly he made life and flesh.
nuance: உகந்து (gladly, delighting) opens every line. Placed under grace, the verse suggests that creation is itself an act of the Lord's goodwill toward souls, as tradition takes it: he makes bodies so that souls may work out their bonds.

reading: He made and owns the seven worlds of old; he made the many gods first; he made the many souls first; having made them, he stands as the Supreme.
nuance: படைத்துடையான் joins making and owning: he is maker and possessor. The verse repeats முன்னே (first, of old) for both gods and souls, so neither is prior to his making; it does not say whether souls themselves are created or only embodied, a point Siddhanta settles by holding souls to be beginningless.

reading: The First made the five great elements; the First made the many faultless ages; the First made the countless gods; and the First stands bearing all he made.
nuance: The last line adds keeping to making: தாங்கி நின்றான், he stands bearing them. The variant அனாதி (the beginningless) for ஆதி (the first) would sharpen the point that the maker has no beginning.

reading: He is vast, the seven wide realms becoming one in him; he is not easy to point to as 'this is he'; Siva himself becomes the many, many souls, and is the beloved one who spoke and came into the world.
nuance: சிவன்றான் பலபல சீவனும் ஆகி, Siva becoming the many souls, reads on its face as identity. Siddhanta tradition takes ஆகி as 'pervading as' or 'standing inseparably with', keeping Lord and soul distinct; the verse alone does not settle it. நவின்றான் (who spoke) is often taken as giving the Vedas and Agamas.

reading: The light within, the one body that stands close, the excellent thing the immortals in heaven desire, the one of holy form praised by the gods on earth, the great gem in the eye: this is the great awareness.
nuance: மண்ணின்ற வானோர், the gods who stand on earth, is usually taken as devotees or Brahmins. மாபோதம் (great awareness) and its variant மாபோதகம் (great teacher) give different endings: the Lord as knowledge itself, or as the teacher. கண்ணின்ற மாமணி may be the pupil of the eye, or a yogic light.

reading: I came to know the bliss of seeing, without slackening, how the holy form of the cosmos, which no one knows, stands rightly like milk in water within the vessel of the body, made from earth and the other elements.
nuance: கடம் (pot, vessel) is the body. Milk in water is a presence everywhere in it and inseparable from it, unseen but not absent; this answers 431, where the heart could not see the one within. The poet ends in the first person: he has found it.

title: கரு உற்பத்தி
theme: The making of the embryo (கரு உற்பத்தி): the Lord, knowing each soul's due, builds its body in the womb from the tattvas and the breaths through the union of the parents; the state of breath and seed at conception decides sex, lifespan and defects; the parents do not know what they make, and the Lord, present though unseen in the small body, shapes and protects it by grace.
structure_note: The chapter moves from the Lord forming the body from the tattvas (451 to 460), through images of its building (house 461, machines 467, kiln 468, bubble and light 472) and the senses and faculties (473, 474), to grace and the parents' love (475 to 477), the effects of breath and the mother's state at conception (478 to 484), and closing reflections on maya and the Lord within (485 to 491).
source_issues: 457 repeats 2926 except for line 2; its variants (ஆகிப்படைத்தன, விடாவிடிற், பந்தியு) are 2926's readings, and பன்றி (pig) against பந்தி (row) changes the sense of the last line.
478: தாண் and பாணவம் are obscure and may be corrupt; தாண் may stand for தாள்.
452 line 2 (செந்தாள்), 463 line 2, 464 line 4 (அக்கரம் எட்டும்) and 472 line 2 (காவுடைத் தீபம்) are obscure.

reading: The Lord, the First, our precious life, makes the twenty-five that were set apart before; staying within the globe of the womb he forms the embryo, knowing what it is to become.
nuance: இருபத்தஞ்சு (twenty-five) is traditionally taken as the tattvas from earth up to purusha that make up the soul's body. ஆவது அறிந்தே, knowing what it will become, is usually read as his knowing the soul's karma before shaping the body.

reading: Above the root he sets fire and water, joins the red foot of knowledge, and, so that the sweet life borne there may enter, he lays on it the burden of the ten.
nuance: மூலம் (the root) is taken as the muladhara, அங்கி and அப்பு as fire and water, and பத்து as the ten vital airs, though ten months is also possible. செந்தாள் (red foot) and பறிகின்ற are obscure.

reading: At the hour when the two join in pleasure, the Lord, present in the sorrowful house of bondage that went before them, fixes in that moment of love the span of time and the life on earth the child will have.
nuance: The verse puts the fixing of the lifespan (காலமும்) and the earthly life (வாழ்க்கையும்) at the moment of conception. Whose bondage the துயர்மனை is, the parents' or the soul's, is not clear.

reading: Those freed from birth have seen that the 'four and three sevens' join in the man's body, which others do not know; the form that sought and entered the womb fell as two.
nuance: நால் மூவேழ் is read either as 4 + 21 = 25, the tattvas of 451, or as some other count; I can't fix it. உருவம் இரண்டாக may mean the seed dividing, or twins, or the two parents' contributions.

reading: The seed falls and the womb opens; the first five, joined by the ten, rise, and the poured water, the elements and the faculties hide within at the brow and the crown.
nuance: லிங்கம் and யோனி are used plainly of the sexual organs here. The first five are taken as the elements and the ten as the senses or vital airs; நுதல் உச்சி (brow, crown) points to yogic centres where the faculties are said to lie latent.

reading: As the wind that has taken a flower's scent spreads it and holds it in the world, so the long subtle breath settled in the soul, at the marked moment, calls it and lets it go.
nuance: The plain image is clear: breath carries the soul as wind carries scent. What குறிக்கொண்ட போது (the marked time) and அவிழும் (opens, lets go) refer to, conception or the soul's leaving a former body, is not fixed by the verse.

reading: The eight that go out, the eighteen that come in, the freed one sunk within, the nine gates, the serpent with the eight and the four horses: if the driver does not let go, it becomes even a pig.
nuance: A list of the body's parts as a chariot team. The numbers are traditionally matched with breaths, tattvas and senses, and the last line with birth in a low body, but I can't fix any of them. The same verse stands as 2926 with a different second line.

reading: If the forces meet rising, the child will be like the Lord; if they meet reversed, like Hari; if they are kept level, of balanced understanding; and a son matching his name will rule a great kingdom.
nuance: The subject of ஏற, மாற, நேரொக்க is unstated; it is usually taken as the breath or the seed at conception. The variant அரியயன் would make the second Brahma, or Hari and Brahma together.

reading: From the mingled essence of the two, the flowing seed takes form; once the body, compounded of many things, is settled, the mind sinks into a stupor mixed with maya.
nuance: ஏயம் and சாயம் are unclear; சாயம் may be colour or essence. மனோலயம் mixed with maya is usually read as the soul losing awareness in the womb.

reading: In the womb maya joins her brood to the soul in its kevala state; turiya is broken and thought arises; karma takes firm hold and maya's bonds begin, as the word of the pure Veda says.
nuance: கேவலம் (the soul's isolated state, bound only by anava), துரியம், காமியம் (karma) and மாயேயம் (the products of maya) are Siddhanta terms; the verse seems to describe the soul passing from kevala to its embodied (sakala) state at conception. எட்டாதல் is obscure.

reading: He wove bones together, bound them with nerves like lashings, made a fitting house of red flesh, and set in it, sweetly, the seat of life; I seek that good one, the Lord who rises there.
nuance: The body is described as a house built by the Lord, bone for frame, nerve for cord, flesh for walls, and the poet seeks the builder who dwells in it. The variant நண்பால் would make the last line 'I seek him in friendship'.

reading: The milk-coloured one, bright as the sun, who brings things to ripeness, enters the whole body for its good, calms the rage of the fire below, ordains how it should be, and leaves.
nuance: பால்வண்ணன் is an epithet of Siva. The 'fire' of குதம் is read as the heat of the lower body or womb, which would harm the embryo if not checked. The verse's subject may be the Lord or the sun as his agent.

reading: When the deeds that bring many endings came due, the Lord took the embryo of bondage, which does much that is blamed, through its many turns and kept it from being burned.
nuance: Line 2 (வழிபல நீராடி வைத்தெழு வாங்கி) is obscure. The point taken is that the embryo, formed by karma, is protected in the heat of the womb by the Lord.

reading: The white seed in its channel and the womb in its order: entering eight finger-breadths and coming out four, and with the eight letters, it becomes a body of eight spans.
nuance: The body measuring eight of its own spans is an old teaching. எண்விரல், நால்விரல் (eight and four finger-breadths) are often read of the breath's reach, and அக்கரம் எட்டும் is obscure.

reading: The pure one who entered there in the act of love, whose work of giving set a body in the sheath, there in that one act made an egg of two eights and three fives.
nuance: இரண்டெட்டு மூன்றைந்து (sixteen and fifteen) is commonly matched with the kalas of the moon and sun, or other counts; I can't fix it. முட்டை (egg) names the embryo. The variant கோகத்துள் would replace கோசத்துள் (in the sheath).

reading: The five foolish senses within the body arise and die within the body; in the same way the soul within the cosmos is born and dies there, and the Lord rests in the cosmos's nada.
nuance: பிண்டம் (body) and அண்டம் (cosmos) are set side by side as microcosm and macrocosm. Who அமர்ந்திருந்தான் refers to, the Lord or the soul, is not stated.

reading: The Lord built my body like machines: raising the leaf-machine, planting the embryo with the five in the balance-machine, fixing the thirty in the standing machine, and making one thing of the nine in the forge-machine.
nuance: பொறி (machine, contrivance) repeats in every line. The numbers five, thirty and nine are matched by tradition with elements, tattvas and openings, but the verse does not say what they are.

reading: From the clay the two set in their pleasure, one alone forms the pot of sorrow; with nine water-jars and eighteen pots, the kiln fires and it is made.
nuance: A potter's image: the parents supply clay, the Lord is the potter, the womb the kiln. ஒன்பது and பதினெட்டு may be the nine openings and some count of parts.

reading: You don't know how the body came to be, you don't set apart the qualities that grow in it, you don't go into them; the body is what took shape within the ten, so that what was set within it might be known.
nuance: ஈரைந்து (ten) is usually the ten months in the womb. சித்திகள் இட்டது may be powers placed in the body or simply what was set there; the last line is compressed.

reading: The way he set the body and the way he set the life, placing the nine gates as sluices, and the Lord who set the fire at the end within the firm lotus at the head: I have joined hands with him.
nuance: The nine gates are the body's openings, here called மடை, sluices built to purpose. The lotus at the head with fire is a yogic image of the crown. The verse treats the body's design as the Lord's work and the place where the poet meets him.

reading: I have heard it: the great unfailing light everywhere is the one who kindles it; the first maker of wombs, the divine builder, joins the fluid into the embryo's form and draws it out until it comes right in the body.
nuance: மயன் is the divine architect of the Puranas, here used of the Lord as maker of wombs (முதல் யோனி). The construction of line 1 is loose.

reading: Once flower and bud have joined and opened, a light within the grove mingles and is born; like a bubble standing in water, a shadow, it spreads through the earthly body, and the eight take hold.
nuance: காவுடைத் தீபம் (the lamp of the grove) is obscure. The eight are taken in the next verse as five senses and three inner faculties, the subtle body (puriyattaka) of the tradition.

reading: Of the eight, five become the senses and three the bound inner faculties; this body-bag, which is the bond's awareness clinging to the soul, the Lord with the eye in his brow ties, unties and watches.
nuance: கரணம் மூன்று are traditionally mind, intellect and ego. Calling the body பாச உணர்வு, the awareness of the bond, makes it the means by which the soul knows while bound.

reading: Joining his name with it, the Lord with the brow eye fashions the body, and so that the soul's bond may fall away he lays out the whole range the Veda describes, starting from earth.
nuance: The body is made so that பசுபாசம் நீங்கிட, the bond may leave the soul: embodiment is for release. மண்முதலாக is read as the tattvas from earth upward. கண்ணுதல் நாமம் கலந்து is unclear.

reading: There is nothing but grace, and no grace apart from Hara; so when he gives a soul he also arranges the love that comes to it from its two mothers.
nuance: இருகைத் தாயர் is taken as the mother who bears and the one who nurses, or the mother and the divine mother; I can't fix it. The point is that a child's being loved is itself the Lord's grace.

reading: The birth so arranged is the greatness of the good Lady and of the Light who gathered and removed the darkness: they set out all the many beings given discernment and stand within them too.
nuance: மாது நல்லாள் is Shakti and சோதியவன் Siva. பகுத்துணர்வாக்கிய (made to discern) may refer to giving beings the faculties to know.

reading: The fire that grows into greatness, the fashioning seen as male, female or neither, and the likeness borne down the mother's and father's line: all these were brought about by the Light's power.
nuance: வன்னி (fire) is unclear: the vital heat of the embryo, or the Lord as fire. The variant வன்னியைக் makes it an object. கற்பனை here seems to mean form or fashioning, not fancy.

reading: If the male part prevails it becomes a male, if the female part a female, and if the two are equal neither; if the strength is great the child will rule the whole earth, and if the force is excessive nothing takes at all.
nuance: The first two lines state an old belief about sex determination. தாண் and பாணவம் are obscure; தாண் may be a misreading of தாள் (strength).

reading: If after the flow the breath runs five, life will be a hundred years; if four, eighty on earth; the yogi who discerns the flowing breath this way can also direct its flow.
nuance: Five and four are usually taken as the reach of the breath in finger-breadths at the moment of union. The last line turns the teaching toward breath control.

reading: If the flowing breath falls short the child is a dwarf, if it is twisted lame, if it is caught midway hunchbacked; and this, looked at closely, does not lie with the woman's breath.
nuance: விளைக்கின் is read as 'bends' or 'twists'. The last line is unclear: it may say that the woman's breath does not decide these things, or that women have none of this.

reading: If the mother's belly is heavy with faeces the child is dull, if with urine mute, and if both are equal blind: this for the child that has come into the mother's belly.
nuance: மலம் and சலம் here are faeces and urine, not the Siddhanta impurity. The verse states a physiological belief about the mother's condition at conception or in pregnancy.

reading: The child is male if the breath is on the right, female if on the left, two if the downward breath opposes, and neither if the breaths taken are equal.
nuance: The verse does not name its subject; tradition takes வலம், இடம் as the right and left nostril or channel. அபானன் is the downward breath of yoga physiology.

reading: If the good breath rises evenly in both, the child conceived will be fair; if it falters in both, the bangled woman conceives nothing.
nuance: The variant ஒத்தேறில் (rises together) fits the sense.

reading: The child conceived in the bangled woman's belly is a light trembling within; nourished as with milk, it grows within like the sun's golden form and takes its fitting shape.
nuance: தால்வளை (perhaps the curve of the womb) and பால் வளர்ந்து are obscure. The light image echoes 471.

reading: The form grows for ten bright months and comes into the world in its season; it grows mingled with maya, and who here knows how it comes to be without form?
nuance: அருவமதாவது may mean how the embodied one becomes formless again at death, or how the formless Lord is in it; both readings stand.

reading: He who planted the seed did not know, she who received it did not see, the smith who knew told no one, and the Supreme who tells things as they are is there too: I am lost; how low is this maya!
nuance: தட்டான், the goldsmith who shapes, is taken as Brahma the fashioner or as the Lord himself; பரமன் then is the Supreme behind him. The point is that the parents have no knowledge of what they make.

reading: Born of two who met seeking pleasure and grown within painful bondage, once born into the world one can still seek the Ancient and stand there chanting.
nuance: Lines 3 and 4 play on நாடி (seeking) and are loose; the variant சிந்தித்து (thinking) for சந்தித்து changes the first line slightly. The reading that birth from bondage still permits worship is mine.

reading: If a cuckoo's egg is put in a crow's nest, the crow raises it without suspicion; it does not go, does not leave, does not ask why: the crow raises it out of delusion.
nuance: The verse states only the image. Placed here it is taken as parents raising a child whose soul is not theirs, in the delusion that it is.

reading: As the root-tuber becomes a sprout, shoots up, becomes a bush and then fruit and gives, and in each stage is the sweetness proper to it, so the First Lord stands as each thing to each thing.
nuance: அதற்கது வாய் (being that to that) is the key phrase: the Lord is present in every stage of growth as what that stage is. The image continues the chapter's growth of the embryo.

reading: Though our Lord's greatness is beyond all others, he is mingled within the smallness of flesh; Mahadeva is beyond the measure of the gods' knowing, and is known within tapas.
nuance: தானே அறியும் may mean that he alone knows himself, or that he is known of himself within tapas. ஊனே சிறுமையுள் sets the great Lord in the small body.

reading: The subtle body that had dissolved into the Supreme takes form again so this body may grow, and by grace is shaped anew and born, as salt crystallizes out of the sea.
nuance: The salt image is of something dissolved that takes form again from the same water. பரத்திற் கரைந்து பதிந்த நற்காயம் is read as the subtle body resting in the Supreme between births.

title: மூவகைச்சீவ வர்க்கம்
theme: The three classes of souls (மூவகைச் சீவ வர்க்கம்): souls are ranked by the impurities that bind them, the Vijnanakalas by anava alone, the Pralayakalas by anava and karma, the Sakalas by all three; Shakti and Siva yoke souls to maya in their play so as to lead them to Sivahood, and those who destroy the malas become Siva.
structure_note: 492 states the purpose of embodiment; 493 to 496 and 498 set out the classes and their subdivisions, with counts that do not agree (ten in 493, nine in 498); 497, 499 and 500 turn to those who pass beyond the malas.
source_issues: 493 counts ten kinds of soul and 498 nine.
498 line 2 repeats விஞ்ஞானர் where the Pralayakalas are expected.
500 line 4 ends with a stray வரன்றே, apparently repeated from line 3 (ரவரன்றே); the verse's syntax is broken.
496 line 1 and 499 lines 2 and 3 are obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: Shakti and Siva in their play make souls, yoke them within the joining of the two mayas, have them enter the pure turiya, enter their minds and make them full of Siva.
nuance: இருமாயை is traditionally pure and impure maya. விளையாட்டு (play) names creation as the Lord's sport, and the end of the process is that the soul becomes சிவமயம், filled with Siva.

reading: The Vijnanars are four, those in Pralayakala who 'know their own' three, and the unknowing in Sakala three; ten in all, these are the divisions of the Vijnanars and the rest.
nuance: விஞ்ஞானர், தஞ்ஞானர், அஞ்ஞானர் are technical names; how the 4, 3 and 3 subdivisions are made is not stated, and 498 counts nine.

reading: The Vijnanars are those who have left the kevala state; the thanjnanars who draw near are the eight Vidyesvaras; the enjnanars are the seven crore Lords of mantra; the true knowers stand having left anava.
nuance: The eight Vidyesvaras and the seventy million Mantresvaras are classes of liberated or near-liberated souls in Siddhanta. The play on -ஞானர் through all four lines makes the classes hard to separate.

reading: In the second class all attain release; within the second are the bound with two malas, said to be the hundred and eight Rudras; the Sakalas, beset with conflict, have three malas.
nuance: இரண்டாவது, the second, is taken as the Pralayakalas, bound by anava and karma. The 108 Rudras as a class of these souls is the tradition's reading.

reading: Between the bound soul and the freed soul stand those who have become intermediate; those unable to wither the three malas, sunk in sound, are in the Sakala state.
nuance: Line 1 (பெத்தெத்த சித்தொடு பேண்முத்தச் சித்தது) and சத்தத்து அமிழ்ந்து are obscure; the verse may be corrupt.

reading: Those who have become Siva and destroyed the five firm malas will not come to nothing; these siddhas live in the three ends, end their becoming, are free of soul-bondage and bond, and have sought and seen the ninefold tattva.
nuance: The five malas are traditionally anava, karma, maya, mayeya and tirodhana. முத்தாந்தம் is taken as Vedanta, Siddhanta and Nadanta. நவமான may be 'ninefold' or 'new'; the variant நாடிக்கொண்டாரே changes little.

reading: The Vijnanars dwell in anava's kevala state; the (second) Vijnanars stay in maya with two malas; the unknowing are the Sakalas of Sakala; the Vijnanars and the rest are nine different kinds of soul.
nuance: The second line repeats விஞ்ஞானர் where the scheme needs the Pralayakalas; this may be a slip in the text. The count of nine differs from 493's ten.

reading: By karma, the Vijnanars joined to a body enter wombs of four walls, touch some knowledge and a body, pass on through what lies between, become true knowers and attain Siva: this is the truth.
nuance: Lines 2 and 3 (அனையான கன்மத்தி நால்சுவர் யோனி, எஞ்ஞான மெய்தீண்டி) are obscure and may be corrupt; the sense of a path from embodiment to Siva is clear only in outline.

reading: Those reached by anava and avidya, without waking; bindu, nada, Sakala and the rest; those who have reached anava and the others are not they; the Shakti and Siva tattvas rise far above.
nuance: The syntax is broken and the verse may be corrupt; it seems to set the pure tattvas of Shakti and Siva above the states bound by anava.

title: பாத்திரம்
theme: The worthy recipient (பாத்திரம்): a gift as small as a sesame seed to a knower of Siva yields release, powers and the highest joy, while gold as vast as the earth given to fools bears no fruit. The other verses describe those who know the Lord, and only loosely fit the title.
source_issues: 501: the line division is broken; தரும் belongs to the end of line 2 (பரபோகமும் தரும்) but is printed at the start of line 3.
504 line 3: காட்டித்துக் looks corrupt.

reading: Gold the size of a sesame seed given to a knower of Siva yields its fruit: release, siddhi and the highest enjoyment; gold the size of the earth given to fools loses its fruit, and the highest enjoyment fails.
nuance: The contrast is between திலம் (sesame) and நிலம் (earth), one letter apart. The worth of the gift lies in the recipient's knowledge, not in its size or the recipient's need.

reading: Some went and came to know the Lord who masters Death, who eats the lives of those who stand and watch, who has the power to take life, and who gives grace to those who understand rightly; they became even gods.
nuance: The first two lines are ambiguous: காலனை and குணத்தனை may describe Death or the Lord who subdued him. Placed in this chapter, these knowers are presumably the worthy recipients.

reading: I have not let go of him since I was an embryo, have not left the truth, and seek the feet of the Changeless; putting away falsehood, I seek the feet of the one with plaited matted hair, and become like a lamp that needs no ghee.
nuance: விகிர்தன் is an epithet of Siva. The last line, நெய்விட்டிலாத இடிஞ்சில், is obscure: a lamp burning without ghee (an inner light) or an empty lamp; the reading is a guess.

reading: What is to become becomes, what is to perish perishes, what is to go goes and what is to come comes; the guardian named Nandi showed this and saw it, and the young kin does as he is bidden.
nuance: The repetitions in lines 1 and 2 state that things take their course. இளங்கிளையோன் (the young kin) may be the disciple or the poet himself; காட்டித்துக் looks corrupt.

title: அபாத்திரம்
theme: The unworthy recipient (அபாத்திரம்): a gift to those without discipline, vow and love of the Lord is wasted, like milking a barren cow or a crop sown out of season, and can drag giver and receiver alike to hell; given to the Lord, the pure guru and the desireless, it saves even a great sinner.
structure_note: Two verses on the waste of giving to the unworthy (505, 506), one on the right recipients (507) and one on the penalty of giving to those who do not revere the Lord (508).
source_issues: 508 line 3: இறைஞ்சாதார்ககு, a misprint for இறைஞ்சாதார்க்கு.
506 ends with a doubled full stop.

reading: Giving to those without good conduct and vows is like stooping to feed fodder to a handsome barren cow and milking it for something to drink; it is a crop whose season has passed.
nuance: Two images of wasted effort: the barren cow (வறட்டு) gives nothing however well fed, and the late crop yields nothing however well sown. சீலம் and நோன்பு are taken as conduct and religious vows; the verse judges the recipient, not the gift.

reading: Know it as a great fault to give to anyone except those who know how to keep to yoga, yama and niyama and in whom love dwells, and not to those in whom love does not dwell though they know what profits.
nuance: ஈவது in line 1 can also be read as what is given: the teaching of yoga, yama and niyama is to be given only to those fit for it. On that reading the verse is about initiation rather than alms. Lines 2 and 3 repeat அறிந்து அன்பு தங்கு with a negation, which makes the contrast hard to fix.

reading: Even one who does not know the way and has done the five great sins, if he gives to the Lord, to the pure guru and to those who have left desire behind and has them teach him, will not enter the hell where such people go, but will learn true knowledge.
nuance: This is the reading in which புகான் (he will not enter) governs the whole: right giving outweighs even the five great sins (பஞ்ச பாதகம்). தரல்தந்து கற்பிப்போன் is compressed; it may instead mean one who gives and then presumes to teach such people, who goes to hell, but போதம் கற்கவே (so as to learn knowledge) fits the first reading better.

reading: Though one gives great wealth as large as a mountain of earth, if it goes to those who do not bow with joined palms, thinking 'this is the Lord', giver and receiver both reach the pit of the seventh hell.
nuance: ஏழா நரகம் is the seventh, lowest hell. The verse makes the giver share the fault: wealth is no excuse for an unworthy choice of recipient.

title: தீர்த்தம்
theme: Holy water (தீர்த்தம்): the true sacred waters are within the heart, where the Lord already dwells, and those of deceitful mind who wander from river to tank to wash away their deeds are seeking in a pond what they lost in the sea.
structure_note: Inner bathing against outer pilgrimage (509 to 511, 513), with one verse (512) that keeps the gods' bathing in the Ganga and one obscure verse (514) on the water within the body.
source_issues: 511 line 4 (பள்ளத்தல் இட்டதோர் பத்துள்ளாமே) is obscure and may be corrupt.
513 line 1 ends with a stray full stop.

reading: There are many holy waters within the heart; those unlearned ones with deceitful minds who do not slowly plunge into them and bathe so that their deeds are destroyed wander over hollow and height.
nuance: பள்ளமும் மேடும் (hollow and height) is the pilgrim's road over the land. கல்வியிலோர் (the unlearned) is pointed: learning here means knowing where the waters are.

reading: To those who know the temple he appears gentle; those who know only bathing cannot join him; to those who know the breath he may or may not come; he is within the minds of those whose knowledge is clear.
nuance: The verse rings on four words: தளி (temple), குளி (bathing), வளி (breath, yoga) and தெளி (clarity). It ranks them, with bathing lowest and clear knowledge highest; வாய்க்கினும் வாய்க்கும் leaves the yogi's success open.

reading: None of the deceitful, however they mingle, know the One who is felt within the heart; those who seek out the flood of the river leave their evil deeds like something cast into a pit.
nuance: The last line (பள்ளத்தல் இட்டதோர் பத்துள்ளாமே) is obscure. It may mean that river bathing only sinks the deeds where they stay, or that the deeds cling like a பற்று (attachment, read for பத்து).

reading: The gods who know the First Lord go round the dense abode where he dwells, and plunging into the speckled water of the Ganga that flows on him who holds a deer and a bangled hand, they become meritorious.
nuance: This verse seems to grant outer bathing its place, for the gods and at the Lord's own river. மறியார் வளைக்கை may be the deer in the Lord's hand and the bangled hand of Uma beside him; பொறியார் புனல் is unclear. Some read the Ganga here as an inner current, which would bring the verse in line with the chapter.
