reading: Losing it in the sea and looking for it in a pond: none match those who search by tiring the body; they do not know at all that by firm Nandi's grace he went and entered the body.
nuance: Line 1 is a proverb for searching in the wrong place. உடலுற்றுத் தேடுவார (variant உடலுற) may mean those who search with bodily toil, that is, by pilgrimage. The answer is that the Lord is already in the body.

reading: The water mixed in the body turns black, turns red, turns white; what mixed is water, fire and wind.
nuance: The three colours are not explained. They may be the body's three humours (wind, bile and phlegm) or three stages of a yogic practice; the plain point may only be that the body is itself made of the elements the pilgrim seeks outside.

title: திருக்கோயில்
theme: The sacred temple (திருக்கோயில்): moving a fixed lingam, taking a stone from a temple wall, letting its rites lapse or having them done by an unfit priest brings ruin on the king and the land: disease, failed rain, theft and famine. Each verse ends on Nandi's word or command.
structure_note: Two verses on damage to the temple's fabric (515, 516), two on lapsed worship (517, 518) and one on an unfit priest (519).
source_issues: 518: variant மாரி (rain) for வாரி.

reading: If one pulls up a fixed lingam and sets it up elsewhere, the kingdom loses its stability before the deed is done, and great disease befalls him before he dies; so Nandi the guardian declared.
nuance: தாவர லிங்கம் is the installed, immovable lingam, as against a movable one. The verse does not say whose disease is meant; it is usually taken as the one who moves it, while the king's realm suffers too.

reading: If one takes away even a single stone from the wall of a temple someone built, the command of the Lord of heaven will have even an anointed king cut down, and will have him cut down even if he is a sage or a Vedic Brahmin.
nuance: The verse spares no rank: anointed kings, sages and Brahmins alike. முட்டுவிக்கும் may mean 'brings to an end' or 'obstructs'.

reading: If the pujas ordained in all the temples of the one who kicked Death lapse, unbearable disease grows, the earth has no rain, and even praiseworthy kings lose their strength in war.
nuance: கூற்றுதைத்தான் recalls Siva kicking Death to save Markandeya. The verse makes worship a cause of rain, not merely dependent on it.

reading: If the pujas in the temple of the First One stop, harm comes to kings, the bounty of the rains declines, and housebreaking and theft increase in the land; so our rare Nandi declared.
nuance: The text reads வாரி (abundance, or the sea); the variant மாரி makes it the rains. கன்னம் is housebreaking, from the hole made in the wall.

reading: If a Brahmin who has only the name worships the Lord, it becomes a vile disease for warring kings and famine for the land; so glorious Nandi declared after due thought.
nuance: பேர்கொண்ட பார்ப்பான் can mean a Brahmin in name only, or a Brahmin of renown. Tradition takes it of one not qualified or initiated for temple worship, but the verse does not say what he lacks.

title: அதோமுக தெரிசனம்
theme: The vision of the downward face (அதோமுக தெரிசனம்): Siva's sixth face, turned downward, sent the six-faced Skanda against the asura, bears the cosmos and its quarters, and is the Lord of the aeon and the endless Shakti; his dark throat has a meaning that those who say 'he drank poison' miss.
structure_note: A narrative verse (520), three on the dark throat and the Lord's knowledge of the false (521, 522), and three dense verses that repeat அதோமுகம் (523 to 525).

reading: When the gods, their flowers blooming, cried 'Our great Lord, our God, is this just?' and told of the asura's might, the Supreme said to the six-faced one of beautiful coral body, 'go and kill their enemy.'
nuance: The chapter title links this to the downward face; tradition says Skanda was born from it. The verse itself names only the six-faced one and the command.

reading: No one knows the meaning of the darkened throat of the downward face that bears the cosmos and the eight directions; those without understanding say that what he ate was poison, of him who wears a garland of white skulls and spreading matted hair.
nuance: The verse does not deny the poison story outright; it says the story is what people without understanding tell. What the throat means instead is left unstated: tradition reads it as the Lord's holding of the world within.

reading: He who made them knows the men of the sea-girt world who praise with lies; if they spoke the truth, he of the throat dark and gleaming would make the gods worship them.
nuance: The falsehood may be false praise of the Lord or false speech in general. The reward for truth is put high: the gods themselves would bow.

reading: Nandi rising, high in the middle, mingled with the red fire, stands within as Siva; mingling first, he goes round the world; the Lord of the twilight is the downward face.
nuance: நடுவுற ஓங்கிய (rising in the middle) and செந்தீ (red fire) suggest a yogic ascent through the central channel; அந்தி (twilight) may be the juncture of day and night or of the breaths. All of this is tradition's reading.

reading: The downward face is the Ancient who is the lower cosmos; with the downward face he works everywhere; the Lord with the bright flower wreath of the hundred faces is also the downward-faced one, the Lord of the aeon.
nuance: சதோமுகம் is unclear: perhaps 'hundred-faced', or a form of சதாமுகம். ஊழித் தலைவன் (Lord of the aeon) links the face to dissolution.

reading: Hear how the downward face became the great flower: by the downward face it spread out a hundredfold; the endless Shakti that became the downward face, he became the downward face and abides.
nuance: The repetition of அதோமுகம் in every line is deliberate. The flower that opens a hundredfold may be a lotus of the body or of the cosmos; the verse identifies the face with Shakti and with Siva at once.

title: சிவ நிந்தை
theme: Reviling Siva (சிவ நிந்தை): those who scorn the Lord as easy fall as a parrot falls to a cat; gods and asuras who opposed him perished, and even Vedic Brahmins who dwell on pleasure forget him. Enmity toward him, even feigned, rebounds many times over.

reading: To those in whose minds clear knowledge has come, who melt in longing for the heavenly city, he is easy; if base people scorn the Lord for being easy, they go down like a parrot to a cat.
nuance: எளியன் (easy, accessible) is both his gift to the devoted and the excuse of the scornful. கிளியொன்று பூஞையால் may also mean that the scorned Lord is as a parrot to the cat's eyes, but the fall of the scorner fits கீழதுவாகுமே.

reading: Gods and asuras who withered have all perished, not knowing the knowledge that stands in truth; the First Lord, from whom ripe nectar wells up, cannot be borne except by those who have become calm.
nuance: தளிந்தவர் is uncertain: perhaps 'those cooled and settled' or 'those who have drawn near'. The ripe nectar may recall the churning of the sea.

reading: Through that enmity asuras and gods waged their good war and perished midway; whatever enmity they bear, they do not reach the Lord, and even a false enmity against him becomes one tenfold.
nuance: நற்பகை (good enmity) is ironic or refers to the war of gods and asuras. The last line may mean the Lord answers even a pretended hostility tenfold, or that one false enmity grows into ten.

reading: Because they dwell on pleasure and the sulking of women and have that mingled in their very bodies, even those who are Vedic Brahmins abandon thought of the Lord who abides in the rule that says 'we are Vikirta'.
nuance: விகிர்தன் (the one unlike all, a name of Siva) and நாம் என்கின்ற நீதி are hard to fix: the line may refer to the Lord as known in the Veda or to a teaching of identity with him. The verse's target is plain: learning does not save those lost in pleasure.

title: குரு நிந்தை
theme: Reviling the guru (குரு நிந்தை): those who wound the teacher who gave a single syllable of mantra are reborn as dogs and worms; troubling the devotees, the chaste and the knowers ruins life, wealth, land and even Indra's throne; and to leave the guru's knowledge for ritual is to drop a gem and carry a stone.
structure_note: 530 sets out the base and the attained; 531 to 534 name the penalties for hurting teachers and devotees; 535 the ruin of falsehood before the guru; 536 the folly of leaving the guru's knowledge.
source_issues: 531: variants பாரிடைக் for வாரிடைக் and படிகுவர், பழகுவர் (apparently for மாய்வர்).
532: variants மாய்ந்திடுஞ் for மாண்டிடும் and சொன்னோம்.

reading: The base do not honour even those who have attained, and speak words that hurt those close to them; those who keep to the path of the learned are the ones who have attained, and who but they gain the true gain?
nuance: பெற்றிருந்தார் may mean 'those who have attained' (the realised) or 'those who bore them' (parents). The verse turns on the word: the base do not honour those who have it, and only those who follow the learned get it.

reading: Those who speak so as to wound the excellent teacher who taught one syllable and its meaning so that it was understood will be born as a dog in the town for an age and then die as worms in the earth.
nuance: ஓரெழுத்து (one letter) is usually taken as a mantra syllable, often Om, but may mean any teaching however small. The variant பாரிடைக் does not change the sense.

reading: Those who cause ruin that troubles the minds of a chaste wife, of devotees and of knowers of the tattvas will lose wealth and life within a year; this is truth, by the command of Sadananda.
nuance: சதாநந்தி may be the Lord as ever-blissful Nandi. The pairing of the chaste wife with devotees and jnanis puts them in one class of the inviolable.

reading: Those who did evil so that the great ascetics who taught the one-syllable mantra grieved in mind will be born as outcast dogs and come as outcastes in a hundred forms, and die on earth.
nuance: This repeats 531 with மந்திரம் stated. நூறுரு may mean a hundred births or a hundred bodily forms.

reading: If the hearts of the Lord's devotees are troubled, country, land and their glories are destroyed; Indra's throne and the thrones of great kings come to ruin, by the command of our Nandi.
nuance: வாசவன் is Indra. The threat moves up from land to king to the king of the gods.

reading: If falsehood enters the presence of the true guru of the true path, the good path declines and knowledge does not stay; forgetting the ancient way, the many paths are ruined and famine comes too.
nuance: சந்நிதி பொய்வரின் may mean lying before the guru, or the guru's presence proving false (a false guru). சன்மார்க்கம் is the path of knowledge in Saiva usage.

reading: Like the fate of one who lets fall the great gem he held and carries a stone stuck to his body, and like one who eats bitter things while ghee, milk and curd stand at hand: such is the ritualist beside the knower.
nuance: The last words கன்மிஞானிக்கு ஒப்பே are compressed: perhaps 'such is the karmi compared with the jnani', or 'such is one who leaves the jnani for the karmi'. The images make plain that something precious at hand is exchanged for something worthless.

title: மயேசுர நிந்தை
theme: Reviling the Lord's devotees (மயேசுர நிந்தை): the devotees stand apart from everyone and live on alms, and those who speak ill of them fall into low hell; when a jnani is reviled or worshipped, the deeds are divided and he enters Siva's bliss.
source_issues: 537: variant றுண்பார் for றுண்பவர்.

reading: The Lord's devotees are at odds with everyone; the Lord's devotees eat what they receive as alms; those who speak unwanted words of the Lord's devotees fall, each of them, into low hell.
nuance: ஆர்க்கும் விரோதிகள் (opponents of all) is taken as their standing apart from worldly ways, not as hostility; it may also be read with a negative understood, 'enemies to none'. The repeated ஆண்டான் அடியவர் opens three lines.

reading: The one who reviles the jnani and the one who worships the jnani as good take away his good and his cruel deeds; the moment he has passed into the Lord's keeping, Siva's bliss enters.
nuance: This is the traditional reading: the worshipper takes the jnani's good deeds and the reviler his bad ones, leaving him free of both. The verse runs the two together (நல்வினையான கொடுவினை), so which goes to whom is inferred, not stated.

title: பொறையுடைமை
theme: Forbearance (பொறையுடைமை), on the title's word: in the attached heart lies a lizard that grips the senses, and checking it is great patience. The other verses turn to the Lord's goodness, the grace that kings and jnanis reach, and the dancer's endless rhythm; their link to forbearance is not plain.
structure_note: Only 539 speaks of forbearance (கமை, kshama) in so many words; 540 to 542 concern the Lord and his worshippers and may have been grouped here by an editor.
source_issues: 540: variants மேனி பணிந்தடியேன் தொழ, ஒப்புநீ and ஞாலத்து நம்மடி நல்கிடென்றாலே change the speaker and the sense of the last line; line 3 ends with a full stop mid-verse.
541: variant வளைந்தருள் for விளைந்தருள்.
539: variant நாவியும் for நாவையும்.
540 to 542 do not obviously concern forbearance; the chapter grouping may be editorial.

reading: In the heart of those who cling there is a lizard; grown full, it lies tangled about the nose and tongue, and to keep it from flourishing in the mind it ravages is great forbearance.
nuance: கமை is forbearance (Sanskrit kshama). The lizard is not named: it may be desire or anger, and the nose and tongue may be the senses, or breath and speech in a yogic reading. The variant நாவியும் for நாவையும் changes tongue to musk.

reading: The countless gods ringed by their court, bowing at the feet of him whose body is like milk so that they might be saved, said: 'King even of Vishnu and of first Brahma, in the world this one is truly good.'
nuance: The variants rewrite the verse: மேனி பணிந்தடியேன் தொழ makes the poet the worshipper, and ஞாலத்து நம்மடி நல்கிடென்றாலே makes the last line a plea, 'grant us your feet in the world'. Forbearance enters only if the Lord's goodness to supplicants is meant.

reading: Those in whom knowledge has ripened are kings at our side, worshipped with joined hands by armies ringed round from every quarter; they can reach the grace of the First of the gods, who makes the flesh grow.
nuance: ஊனை விளைத்திடும் (who makes the flesh grow) may be the Lord as maker of bodies. ஏனை விளைந்தருள் (variant வளைந்தருள்) is unclear. The verse may also mean that kings with armies worship the jnanis.

reading: By strong ways and many ways, at home and in the hall, practising and setting the steps, the dancer who leaps from the field has a rhythm without limit.
nuance: கூத்தன் is Siva the dancer and மன்று his hall, but மனையிலும் மன்றிலும் may also be the body and the inner space. கொல்லை (field, cremation ground) and இலயம் (rhythm, absorption) both carry yogic readings.

title: பெரியாரைத் துணைகோடல்
theme: Taking the great as one's support (பெரியாரைத் துணைகோடல்): the poet resolves to keep company with those who run, sing, seek and join the Lord, bids his faltering heart come with him, and tells how, going with the devotees' devotees, he was announced at the Lord's gate and called in. Joining the great is supreme bliss.
structure_note: First-person resolve (543, 544), the general claim (545, 546), a short narrative of arrival (547) and a closing resolve (548).
source_issues: 544: மாமனதது and இருநது, misprints for மாமனத்து and இருந்து.
546: தேர்வார்ககு, a misprint for தேர்வார்க்கு; போர புகழா may be corrupt.
548: variant ஞாலத்துள் for ஞானத்துள்; the verse ends with a doubled full stop.
545: variant சிவதத்துவத்தை for சிலர்தத்துவத்தை.

reading: I will go along with those able to run to him and their kin; I will live on earth in the light of those able to sing; with the Lord of gods who grants grace to those able to seek, and with those able to join him, I will reach his feet.
nuance: வல்லார் (those able to) ends each verb: run, sing, seek, join. ஓட may also be 'to run away', from the world; the sense of eager devotion seems more likely.

reading: Though they suffer and tremble like tender leaves, they have set no love in the great mind there; O heart, what will you do, staying in distress? When I go, come with me.
nuance: The first two lines are obscure: it is not clear who suffers and whose mind is meant. The last two are an address to the heart, a device known from love poetry and the bhakti hymns.

reading: Seeking the Lord of the immortals, a few who draw near gain the reality; the great ones who stand ever more firmly in the path give grace, and to join with them is supreme bliss.
nuance: தத்துவம் (variant சிவதத்துவம்) here seems to mean the true reality rather than the 36 tattvas. பேரின்பம் is the bliss of release.

reading: Becoming in the world the kin of him whose matted hair bears a garland, praising him, they reach our father's golden feet; coming to the King who grants grace to those who search the heart without shutting the mouth, one can join that path.
nuance: வாயடையா உள்ளம் தேர்வார் is unclear: perhaps those who search their heart while still praising aloud. போர புகழா may be corrupt.

reading: I went with the devotees of the Lord's devotees and entered the city of him whose body is fire bearing weapons; those standing at the gate saw me and made me known, and the cry went up: 'The Lord says, let him come.'
nuance: The poet gains entry not alone but in the company of devotees of devotees, the humblest rank. ஓலம் is the call announcing an arrival or answering one.

reading: The one rare in skill appears in the knowledge of the arts; the one great in skill swims the whirlpool of births; the one with the rightful skill, understanding, abides for an aeon; I have joined those strong in holiness.
nuance: The verse plays on வல்லோன் with அருமை, பெருமை, உரிமை and திருமை. The variant ஞாலத்துள் for ஞானத்துள் would make the first line 'appears in the world of the arts'.

title: அட்டாங்க யோகம்
theme: The eightfold yoga (அட்டாங்க யோகம்): Nandi set out yama and niyama and the rest; the poet will teach the way from them to samadhi with its rites of armour, placement and gesture. Without wavering between paths, one should follow the eight limbs into samadhi, for the path of sacrifice leads nowhere.
structure_note: Two introductory verses (549, 550), an exhortation (551) and the list of the eight limbs (552) that the following chapters take one by one.
source_issues: 549 line 1: variant உரைத்த நவாக்கிரி for உரைத்தன வற்கரி; line 3: variant பிரைச்சதம். The verse may be corrupt.
551: variant யாக்கத்திற் for யாகத்திற் changes the object of the last line.
552: variant நண்பிரத்தி for நயமுறு பிராணாயாமம் பிரத்தி.

reading: Nandi, having counted in order the arranged signs and spoken the eight, set out yama and niyama.
nuance: The first line (உரைத்தன வற்கரி ஒன்று மூடிய, variant உரைத்த நவாக்கிரி) and பிரச்சதம் (variant பிரைச்சதம்) cannot be fixed. Only the last line is clear: Nandi taught yama and niyama, the first of the eight limbs.

reading: I will tell, so that it is reached, this state: going by the practised yama and niyama to samadhi, and for deliverance Parashakti, the north and east, the true armour, the placings and the gestures.
nuance: கவசம், நியாசம் and முத்திரை are mantra rites: protective formulas, placing mantras on the body and hand gestures. உத்தர பூருவ (north and east) may be directions to face or the latter and former parts of a practice.

reading: Without saying 'that path, this path', go by the path of the eight limbs and stand in samadhi; those who go the good path can enter knowledge, but in the mean path of sacrifice there is no way through.
nuance: The last line depends on யாகத்திற் (in sacrifice); the variant யாக்கத்திற் would point to the body instead. On the text as printed the verse ranks the eight limbs above the Vedic rite.

reading: Yama, niyama, the countless postures, good breath control, withdrawal of the senses, victorious concentration, meditation and samadhi: these make up the eight limbs.
nuance: The list is the standard one of the yoga tradition. எண்ணிலா ஆதனம் (countless postures) is Tirumular's touch; அயமுறும் in the last line is unclear.

title: இயமம்
theme: Yama (இயமம்), the first limb: the Lord taught the four sages to keep the yamas in every direction even if the waters rise, and the man of yama is one who does not kill, lie or steal, is good and restrained, acts justly, shares his food, is stainless and free of drink and lust.

reading: 'Even if the waters rise and pour, in all eight directions keep the rich, cool yamas,' said the Lord with the cool coral-red matted hair, granting grace to the four who were absorbed in him.
nuance: The four (நால்வர்) are traditionally the sages Sanaka and the others taught by Siva as Dakshinamurti. எழுந்துநீர் பெய்யினும் may mean 'even if the flood comes', that is, whatever happens.

reading: One who does not kill, does not lie, does not steal, has good qualities, is good, has restraint, can act justly, shares before he eats, is stainless and has neither drink nor lust: he stands in yama.
nuance: The list gives ten marks, matching the ten yamas of the yoga texts. எண்குணன் may be 'one of eight qualities' or 'one of esteemed qualities'; in the Kural the same word names the Lord. நடுச்செய்ய வல்லான் is fairness, and பகுந்துண்பான் sharing one's food.

title: நியமம்
theme: Niyama (நியமம்), the second limb: the man of niyama knows the First, the meaning of the Veda, the light and the fire, with Parashakti in his half; he keeps ten disciplines of conduct, and ten of practice: austerity, mantra repetition, contentment, faith, giving, Siva's vow, hearing Siddhanta, sacrifice, Siva puja and clear mind.
structure_note: One verse on what the man of niyama knows (555) and two lists of ten (556, 557).
source_issues: 555: variant யுணர்ந்த for யுணர்ந்து.
556: variant அருளுண் for அருளூண்.
557: நிவம்பல is obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: He who knows what is right, together with the First, the one who is the meaning of the Veda, the Light, the fire that burns there, and Parashakti who abides in his half, is a man of niyama.
nuance: பாதியுள் மன்னும் பரசக்தி is Shakti as the left half of Siva. The verse makes knowledge of the Lord, not only conduct, the ground of niyama. The variant யுணர்ந்த makes the line adjectival without changing the sense.

reading: Purity, compassion, little food, forbearance, uprightness, truthfulness and steadiness, cultivating these, and seeing lust, theft and killing for what they are: one who keeps these ten rules is a man of niyama.
nuance: நேமி ஈரைந்து is read as 'ten rules'. Several of these (truthfulness, forbearance, uprightness, little food, purity) are counted among the yamas in the yoga texts, and avoiding lust, theft and killing repeats 554; tradition reads this verse as yama and the next as niyama, or the reverse. The variant அருளுண் would make it 'food of grace'.

reading: Austerity, mantra repetition, contentment, faith, giving, Siva's vow, hearing the Siddhanta, sacrifice, Siva puja and clear mind: say these ten; one who does them many times is a man of niyama.
nuance: ஆத்திகம் is faith in the scriptures and the Lord; சித்தாந்தக் கேள்வி is hearing the Saiva Siddhanta. நிவம்பல is obscure; 'many times' is a guess.

title: ஆதனம்
theme: Asana (ஆதனம்): of the many postures, a few are named and described, the lotus, the auspicious, the cock and the lion, with svastika as the steady seat in which one becomes master; the closing verse lists the chief seven and counts the postures in the hundreds.
structure_note: An opening verse on the many postures and svastika (558), four descriptions of single postures (559 to 562), and a closing list and count (563).
source_issues: 563: a variant reads முத்த மயூரமுது for முத்தம மாமுது, putting the peacock posture (மயூரம்) in the list in place of உத்தமம் (best), which changes what the seven are.
563: சொத்திரம் is not a known posture name; it may be a corruption of சொத்திகம் (svastika), named in 558.

reading: Of the many postures that spread out from the lotus, eight are chief; among them, one who sits firmly in svastika without strain becomes master.
nuance: இரு நாலும் (two fours) gives eight. சொங்கு is taken as flaw or strain; தலைவன் may mean master of the posture or of yoga itself. The verse names svastika (சுவத்திகம்) as the seat to settle in, though it then describes others.

reading: Setting one foot upon the opposite thigh, drawing the other firmly over it, and laying the hands beautifully upon them: this is called padmasana.
nuance: ஓரணையப் பதம் is a compressed phrase, read as one foot set against the other thigh; the hands resting on the feet is one reading of அதனைத்தன் மேல்வைக்க.

reading: Placing the right foot clearly over the other, stretching the hands out on the knees and holding the body upright with ease: that is bhadrasana.
nuance: உருசியொடு (with relish) suggests the posture is held with ease, not strain. Which foot goes under is implied, not stated.

reading: Setting both feet together on the thighs and lifting the body to rest upon the elbows, holding still without wavering: that is the cock posture.
nuance: முக்கி (straining) and தொக்க அறிந்து are unclear; the description matches the cock posture of later manuals, where the arms pass through the crossed legs, but the verse doesn't say so.

reading: Stretching the hands to the knees over the feet, opening the mouth wide and fixing the clear eyes on the tip of the nose: that is called the lion posture.
nuance: The open mouth and the gaze at the nose-tip (கொடிமூக்கு) are the marks of the posture; the placing of the feet is compressed.

reading: Bhadra, gomukha, the lotus, the lion, sothiram, vira and sukhasana are the seven best; the postures are many, counted as eight and eight, ten and a hundred.
nuance: எட்டெட்டுப் பத்தொடு நூறு is traditionally summed as 126 postures (8 + 8 + 10 + 100), but it can also be read as 64 and 110; I can't fix the count. சொத்திரம் is taken as svastika (சொத்திகம்). The variant மயூரம் would add the peacock posture to the list.

title: பிராணாயாமம்
theme: Pranayama (பிராணாயாமம்): the breath is a horse that throws the false and carries the true, mastered only by the guru's grace; held with the mind and measured in inhaling, holding and exhaling, it stops birth and death, keeps the body young, keeps Siva within and kicks away Death.
structure_note: Images of the breath as a horse (564 to 566), the claim for breath held with the mind (567), the measures of puraka, kumbhaka and recaka (568, 570 to 574), the fruits in the body (569, 575), and two riddles of the twelve finger-breadths (576, 577).
source_issues: 569: a variant reads வயிற்றில் (in the belly) for வயத்தில் (under control), which changes where the breath is held.
567: a variant reads தடக்கிப் for தடங்கிப்; the sense is close.
568: a variant reads கும்பகம் for கும்பம்; the sense is the same.

reading: The lord of the five, chief of that town, has another horse to ride to salvation; it gives a hold to the true but leaps and throws the false.
nuance: The horse is traditionally the breath, the five the senses and the town the body, with the soul as their lord; none of this is named. மெய்யர் and பொய்யர் may be the truthful and the false, or those firm and unfirm in practice.

reading: There are two horses, though one is no noble rider, and none knows the skill to cast and catch them; if one gains the grace of the keen lord, the guru, they come under control.
nuance: The two horses are traditionally the breaths of the left and right nostril (ida and pingala). ஆரியன் அல்லன் is obscure: it may say the rider is not skilled, or that no master is at hand.

reading: If you ride the horse swifter than a bird, it gives intoxication without drinking toddy, makes one move lightly and drives off sloth; we have told the truth to those who understand.
nuance: Toddy (கள்) stands for a joy that needs nothing outside the body. The horse is the controlled breath, as in 564; the last line marks the teaching as for the prepared.

reading: If the breath stays with the mind without moving, there is no birth or death; the breath, turned in its channel, makes speech known, and you have gained the gift of the breath.
nuance: மடைமாறி (changing course, as water at a sluice) and பேச்சறிவித்து are unclear: the line may mean the breath turned within gives knowledge of the inner sound or of mantra. The first two lines are the plain claim.

reading: Drawing in is puraka, sixteen measures by the left; holding is kumbhaka, sixty-four; letting out is recaka, thirty-two; to change the order in one of these is deceit.
nuance: The ratio 16:64:32 is the standard one. வஞ்சகம் in the last line is unclear: it may condemn changing the measures, or name the alternation of nostrils as the 'clever' method.

reading: If one draws in the air and holds it under control, a ripened body becomes unripe and clear as crystal; if one clearly gains the guru's grace, one becomes swifter than the wind.
nuance: பழுக்கினும் பிஞ்சாம் (though ripe, it becomes unripe) promises a return to youth. வளியினும் வேட்டு வளியனும் is obscure; it may mean master of the wind. The variant வயிற்றில் (in the belly) places the holding in the abdomen.

reading: Wherever you are, fill the breath on the left; doing it there, the body does not decay; holding it there and releasing it in measure, one becomes master as the conch signals.
nuance: இடம் may be 'the left' or 'the place'. சங்கே குறிக்க is unclear: the conch may be an inner sound heard in practice, or a sign of the master.

reading: No one knows the measure of holding the breath that one draws in and lets out through both nostrils; for those who know it, it is the means to kick Death.
nuance: இருகால் may mean the two breaths or the two nostrils. Kicking Death (கூற்றை உதைக்கும்) echoes the story of Siva kicking Death for Markandeya; whether the verse promises a long life or release from death is left open.

reading: Filling the breath fully above, below, in the middle and at the sides, settling it within by recaka, and holding it in the navel, one may gain the grace of the one who drank the poison.
nuance: ஆலாலம் உண்டான் is Siva, who drank the halahala poison. பாலாம் இரேசகம் and மாலாகி are unclear: மால் may mean fullness, delight or Vishnu.

reading: Fill sixteen measures through the left, let out thirty-two gladly with pingala as the eye, and hold sixty-four between the two: this is the truth.
nuance: It repeats the measures of 568 and adds that exhaling is through pingala, the right channel. ஓமத்தால் is unclear: it may mean 'in between' or 'as an offering'.

reading: Without loosening the seat one has set, breathe out, fill all ten nadis, and hold prana and apana together; if one stays still, there is no Yama for us.
nuance: இட்ட அவ்வீடு (that house one set) may be the posture or the body. நட்டம் may mean steadiness or dance. நமனில்லை (no Yama) can be read as long life or as freedom from death.

reading: If the breath that wanders out and in is guided within and made pure, the limbs grow ruddy, the hair turns black, and the one with matted locks will not leave.
nuance: The bodily signs are stated plainly: ruddy limbs and black hair, the marks of youth. புரிசடையோன் is Siva; the verse puts him in the purified body. The same last line returns in 586.

reading: The women who built a house and moved in run out and come back twelve finger-breadths; they reach out eight fingers and cut back four; if gathered in, they become the five letters.
nuance: The women are traditionally the breaths and the house the body; the breath goes out twelve finger-breadths, eight return and four are lost. அஞ்செழுத்து is the five-syllable mantra of Siva, so the held breath becomes mantra. All of this rests on a symbolic reading.

reading: Twelve elephants have day and night; the mahout does not know them; once the mahout knows the twelve elephants, they have no day and night.
nuance: The twelve are traditionally the twelve finger-breadths of the breath (as in 576), the mahout the soul, and day and night the right and left breaths (sun and moon). Once the breath is known it no longer alternates. The riddle has other readings, such as the twelve signs.

title: பிரத்தியாகாரம்
theme: Pratyahara (பிரத்தியாகாரம்): drawing the mind inward from the senses, the yogi sees within the one the Vedas searched for; the chapter locates the inner places, below the navel, between the lower openings, where kundalini and the light stand, and defines withdrawal as separating the light from what limits it.
structure_note: Turning inward (578), the locations of the mantra, kundalini and the light (579 to 581, 583, 584), the signs of light and bliss (582), a definition (585), and the fruits (586, 587).
source_issues: 579: a variant reads நாலிரண்டண்-குலம் for பன்னிரெண் டங்குலம், which changes the measure below the navel.
587: நங்கி is not a known word; it may be a corruption of நீங்கி (gone).

reading: If one draws the mind within, looking again and again, one may see many qualities inside, and see here, today, and stay with the one the ancient Veda gladly searched for everywhere.
nuance: The contrast is between பண்டு (long ago), எங்கும் (everywhere) and இன்று, இங்கே (today, here): what scripture searched for outside is found within. The one sought is Siva, though not named.

reading: They don't know the mantra set twelve finger-breadths below the navel; once they know it, the Lord, called, came and dwelt there.
nuance: தாபிக்கும் மந்திரம் (the mantra that is established) is unnamed. The variant நாலிரண்டு (four and two, or eight) changes the measure; the variant குடிபுகுந்தானே (moved in) is close in sense.

reading: Two fingers above the root and two fingers below the yoni stands the coiled kundalini, with seven red flames within it; it lies four fingers below the navel.
nuance: மூலம் is the base of the spine or the anus, and யோனி the genital place; the seven red flames are not explained and may be the seven centres or seven bodily elements. The two measures of the place do not obviously agree.

reading: If you can fix the mind and meditate twelve finger-breadths down from the nose, the great yoga comes to its height and the body never decays.
nuance: நாசிக்கு அதோமுகம் may mean below the nose or the downward breath from the nose. மாசித்த is read as மா சித்த (great perfected). The variants யாகுமே and தானே don't change the sense.

reading: If a radiant light appears like a line, take it as flawless supreme bliss; if moonlight reaches the throat, the body that recites becomes ecstatic.
nuance: The line of light and the moonlight at the throat are signs of practice I can't fix. உன்மத்தம் may be madness, ecstasy or the yogic state unmani; ஓதுவது உன்னுடல் may mean your body, as it recites.

reading: Close the lower door firmly, set the mind upon the upper door, keep the spear-like eyes open to the void: this is the way to conquer time.
nuance: The lower door is traditionally the anus and the upper the crown of the head. வெளி may be the outer world or the inner void. காலத்தை வெல்லும் may mean conquering death, as in 571.

reading: For those who can meditate on the light that gives form, two fingers above the door that lets out excrement and two below the door that lets out the embryo, the light that gives birth stays mingled with them.
nuance: The place is the one given in 580 for kundalini, though this verse names only a light. கருவிடும் சோதி may be the light that ends births (கரு விடும், lets the womb go) as well as the light that gives birth; both readings stand.

reading: To distinguish at once the bright light from its limiting adjuncts, to dissolve the separation those adjuncts brought, to meditate, to melt and to look within: that is the greatness of pratyahara.
nuance: உபாதி (upadhi) is a philosophical term for what limits or conditions the self. The verse defines pratyahara as discrimination and inward looking, not only as drawing in the senses.

reading: If one keeps the breath that has gone out from re-entering, becomes skilled and stays firm in certainty, and the mind too is fixed there, the great one will not leave.
nuance: புறப்பட்ட வாயுப் புகவிடா is odd as read: it may mean keeping the breath out, or not letting it wander in and out. The last line repeats 575's with பெருந்தகை for புரிசடையோன்.

reading: Within one's intention the world appears; with the darkness of aversion gone, one seeks the transcendent one; if one grasps firmly the excellent mind, the vision of knowing makes one equal to the gods.
nuance: குறிப்பு is intention, or the fixed point of meditation. விகிர்தன் is a name of Siva as the one beyond change. நங்கி is obscure; I read it as நீங்கி (gone).

title: தாரணை
theme: Dharana (தாரணை): fixing the mind and breath within, through the spine to the head, the yogi sees the dance and the light of bliss, rouses the power at the base, and holds life, body and time still; since all who came before have died, the work is now, and its end is holding the dissolved tattvas in the Supreme.
structure_note: Methods of fixing mind and breath (588, 591 to 595), visions and the rousing of the power (589, 590), a warning that the body will not last (596), and a definition of dharana as the involution of the tattvas (597).
source_issues: 590: a variant reads பார்நந்தி for பராநந்தி.
595: a variant reads கோட்டைப் (fort) for கொட்டை, which changes the image of confining the monkey.
597: சத்தாதி appears in lines 2 and 3 for what seem to be two different levels; one may be a corruption.

reading: For those who fix the unwavering mind, bind it below, look up through the spine into the space above and stay as eyes that do not see and ears that do not hear, this is the way that stops the days of life from running out.
nuance: வீணாத்தண்டு (the vina's stem) is traditionally the spine. கோணா மனம் may be the mind that does not bend, or the crooked mind to be bound. வாணாள் அடைக்கும் can mean closing off lifespan, so the verse may promise long life or the end of embodied life.

reading: A heavenly waterfall flows steadily from the mountain's peak through the long nadi; in the hall the holy dance goes on, and I saw the light of unending bliss.
nuance: The plain landscape and the symbolic body both stand: the mountain-top as the head, the waterfall as the nectar of the yogis, the hall (பொது) as the dance-hall of Siva. சிலையார் may mean of stone or of the bow.

reading: The girl of the upper region, the transmuting maiden, rouses the form that rises from the root region; when he meets her, he becomes a youth: this is Paranandi's command.
nuance: Usually kundalini is the female power that rises from the base to Siva above; here the girl is above and the form rising from the root is male, so the roles may be reversed or my reading wrong. வேதகம் is alchemical transmutation. பாலனும் ஆவான் may mean he becomes a child, as in the return to youth of 569.

reading: Those who bind the last door, rouse the breath, look to the middle door, settle sweetly within and wait like a heron at the sluice-mouth may stay unbroken for an aeon.
nuance: The last and middle doors are traditionally the anus and the central channel (sushumna). The heron at the sluice (மடைவாய்க் கொக்கு) waits motionless for its moment.

reading: If the life joined with the body knows time, the life so joined is the pressure of the breath; if that breath is bound, the life, body and time of the one so joined stand still.
nuance: The verse plays on கால், which means both breath and time (காலம்). Each line begins with கலந்த உயிர் (the joined life). The reading is tentative.

reading: Those who don't open the mouth have a treasure in the mind; those who open it drive it out with breath; those who keep it closed kindle it with the moon; if the inner door is not opened, one becomes weak.
nuance: Nearly every key word is unclear. மாடு may be wealth or an ox; மதி may be the moon or the mind; கோய் is obscure; கோழை may be phlegm or a coward. The verse seems to praise silence and inner practice, and I can't do more than that.

reading: One may live for many ages if the breath that splits within the mind is driven inward without escaping; the body has seven windows and two great doors, a large cave and a bedchamber.
nuance: The second half is a riddle of the body as a house: seven openings in the head and two below, perhaps. பாழி and பள்ளியறை may be the inner space where Siva rests. எழுசாலேகம் is read as seven lattice windows.

reading: When five of the full ten have gone, what will you do, fool, waking and lamenting? For those who mark out a boundary and make a way, it is possible to bag the monkey.
nuance: The ten are traditionally the ten vital airs, five of which leave at death. The monkey is the restless mind. கொட்டை பொதியலும் is obscure; the variant கோட்டை (fort) gives 'shut the monkey in a fort'.

reading: All who came before have ended; what assurance is there for those who came after? If one talks of crores of states to come, what a trick: will a crumbling bank stand?
nuance: The crumbling bank (இடிகரை) is the body. உறுகதி may be states or destinies hoped for after death, which the verse mocks as reasons to wait. The verse's place in the chapter suggests it urges the practice now.

reading: Placing the dissolved body in the five elements, the five elements going into sound and the other subtle elements, and the mind and the rest going into what lies beyond them: dharana is holding it all with the Supreme.
nuance: The verse runs the tattvas backward, each into its cause. சத்தாதி appears twice, for the subtle elements and for something higher; the repetition may be a corruption. தற்பரம் is the Supreme.

title: தியானம்
theme: Meditation (தியானம்), the seventh limb: the gaze turned inward to the light at the palate, between the brows or at the tip of the nose, the ten inner sounds heard only by the devoted, and Siva found at the end of nada. Done rightly it steadies mind and breath, keeps the body and, by grace, takes the devotee past the tattvas and maya.
structure_note: After a definition (598), the chapter treats meditation on inner light (599 to 605), on inner sound (606 to 610), on the chambers and mandalas of the yogic body (611 to 616), and ends with grace beyond the tattvas (617).
source_issues: 599: variant பிண்ணாக்கி for புண்ணாக்கி changes the image (oil-cake against wounding).
610: variant ஐவர் அருள்நாதமோடும் for ஐவருள் நாதம் ஒடுங்க changes the syntax of line 3.
611 line 3 (ஒள்ளி தறியிலோ ரோசனை நீளிது) and 616 (நடலித்த, மடலித்த, கடலித்து) are obscure and may be corrupt.
617: variant அறியா யசந்தென்னு ('unknowing, unreal') for அறிவாய சத்தென்னு ('real to knowledge') reverses the description of the 36 tattvas.

reading: Meditation, which comes among the limbs counted from the first, is the unwavering intellect's dealing with the senses' enjoyment; meditation on Shakti in form, on the Supreme, and on Siva who comes as guru are the parts of yoga.
nuance: ஈரெட்டு (two eights, sixteen) is unclear: it may count the limbs or a larger list of disciplines. புலன்போக மேவல் can be split to mean either settling in the senses' objects or the intellect not going after them; the second fits the chapter better.

reading: Within the gathering of eye, tongue, nose, ear and knowing there is one ancient Being who tunes them; showing an unbroken light within the palate, he wore us down and so saved us.
nuance: The verse rhymes கண்ணாக்கு, பண்ணாக்கி, அண்ணாக்கு, புண்ணாக்கி. புண்ணாக்கி may mean 'wounding' us or, with the variant பிண்ணாக்கி, crushing us like oil-cake; either way the saving comes through being broken. The palate (அண்ணாக்கு) as a seat of inner light is a yogic teaching.

reading: If one looks to the full at the light in the eye that cannot be reached and stays merged there, the way of the sky opens, runs on until the open space is seen, and what stands unmade can be seen.
nuance: ஒண்ணா நயனம் (the eye one cannot attain) is commonly taken as the inner or third eye. விண்ணாறு (sky-river or sky-path) and வெளி (open space) are yogic terms whose exact sense I can't fix.

reading: Not once do people contemplate the life within the body, not once Siva within the life, not once the mind where Siva dwells, not once the moon-flower.
nuance: The four lines step inward, from body to life to Siva to the mind that holds him. சந்திரப் பூ (moon-flower) is traditionally the moon region at the crown of the head; it cannot be fixed from the verse.

reading: Light the lamp of the mind to its full, press the lamp of anger until it goes out, and trim every lamp's wick alike: then the lamp of the mind becomes a lamp that does not die.
nuance: மாயா விளக்கு means 'an undying lamp', and may also play on மாயை. Anger is itself called a lamp, one burning the wrong way, so meditation needs a moral step as well as a technique.

reading: Though one sit in yoga eight thousand years, no one sees and knows the nectar in the eye; if one looks within the inner channel until light comes, he stands merged in it as in a mirror.
nuance: உண்ணாடி can be உள் நாடி (the inner nadi) or 'seeking within'. The verse sets long practice against the right inward look: duration alone yields nothing. Sengalvaraya cites Kandar Alangaram 85 as a parallel.

reading: If both gazes are set at the middle of the nose, there is no withering, no ruin for the house, no running, no feeling, no self, no seeking: we become Siva.
nuance: மனை (house) is usually taken as the body. The run of 'no' clauses describes the stilling of breath, sense and ego; சிவனவ நாமே (we are he, Siva) states identity outright. The variant வேட்டமும் (desire) for தேட்டமும் (seeking) is close in sense.

reading: Setting both eyes on the nose and holding within the breath that does not rise, for those who can rest in absorption, seeking the end of sorrow, this is the fruit: the body is without fear.
nuance: தூங்க (to sleep) is taken in the yogic sense of absorbed stillness, as often in Tirumular. நாடியே can be 'seeking' or 'by the nadi'. உயர்வெழா வாயு is unclear: breath that is not let rise, or held so it rises within.

reading: Bell, sea, elephant, long flute, cloud, the bee, the humming beetle, conch, drum and lute: these ten softened inner sounds cannot be perceived except by those who have bowed.
nuance: The list is the yogic ten sounds (dasa nada) heard in meditation. The condition the verse sets is humility or devotion (பணிந்தவர்), not technique.

reading: The sound of sea and clouds and elephant, the vina rising in the world of the gods, the flute with abiding light, and the curling conch: none but the yogi who knows steadiness can know them.
nuance: A second list of inner sounds, this time conditioned on the yogi's firmness (திடம்), where 606 asked for humility. சுடர்மன்னு வேணு (flute with abiding light) has variants சுடர்மனு and சுடர்மணி and is unclear.

reading: The Lord's nature, the host of the gods and the working of the bonds all stand in sound; for those able to perceive it, the Lord is a sound that spreads like its own fragrance.
nuance: Lines 2 and 3 are compressed and the syntax is uncertain. The comparison of sound to fragrance suggests a presence that pervades without being seen; the reading that all three stand in nada is the usual one, not the only one.

reading: At the end of nada the good lady dwells, at the end of nada is good yoga, at the end of nada is the aim, at the end of nada is the one whose throat held the poison.
nuance: நாத முடிவு (nadanta, the end or limit of sound) is where sound subsides into its source. நல்லாள் is traditionally Shakti and நஞ்சுண்ட கண்டன் is Siva, so the verse places both beyond sound. நாட்டம் can be 'the gaze' or 'the goal'.

reading: When, among the six that rise and the five inner fires, the deep darkness lifts and nada subsides among the five that oppress, one can reach the anklets of the Lord of the konrai, the goal.
nuance: ஆறு (six) is commonly taken as the six centres, அங்கி ஐந்து as five fires and ஐவர் as the senses, but none is fixed by the verse. The variant ஐவர் அருள்நாதமோடும் gives a different syntax for line 3.

reading: In the bedchamber it is day and there is no darkness; in the chamber of fire one can keep it from blazing; in the bright pillar the way is a yojana long; in the silver chamber there is no dawn.
nuance: The four chambers are taken as places in the yogic body, perhaps the heart, the fire at the base, the spinal channel and the moon region at the crown. ஒள்ளி தறியிலோ ரோசனை is obscure and the whole verse rests on symbols I can't fix.

reading: For the yogi who keeps his vow undiminished, becomes one, runs up the spine and reaches the head, once he has grown alike in all three mandalas, the body too stays an aeon without parting.
nuance: தண்டு (staff) is usually the spinal channel and the three mandalas are traditionally fire, sun and moon. பிண்டமும் (the body too) implies the life stays with it. ஊழி may be literal (an aeon) or a way of saying 'very long'.

reading: There is a way in which each one's mandala comes; in each one's mandala are that one's gods; when each one's mandala comes to that one, each one's mandala is illusion to others.
nuance: மாயமற் றோர்க்கே can be split as மாயம் மற்றோர்க்கு (illusion to others) or மாயம் அற்றோர்க்கு (for those free of illusion). On the first, inner attainment is private; on the second, it belongs only to the undeluded. Who அவ்வவர் (each of them) are, practitioners or deities, is also open.

reading: If, inside the dark chamber of the weakening heart, one unites with the three mandalas that spring up there and pierces the great bond of the passage, the ascent comes without weariness.
nuance: துளைப் பெரும் பாசம் (the great bond with an opening, or of the passage) and மார்க்கழி ஏற்றம் are obscure; மார்க்கழி may be the month or a form of மார்க்கம் (the way). The heart is called dark and weakening before the practice.

reading: To end the covering of the three gunas, close the breath firmly at the base, turn it and hold it, and master the right and left by the measure of time: then the King of the gods grants the high state.
nuance: வலமிடம் (right and left) is taken as the two nostrils or the two channels, and நாழிகை as a timed measure of breath. வானவர் கோன் here is presumably Siva, not Indra.

reading: Those who can stay four fingers above the navel and two fingers within the seat of speech, deep as the sea, and contemplate there have known the Lord of the body.
nuance: நடலித்த, மடலித்த and கடலித்து are rare forms and may be corrupt; வாணி (speech, or its goddess) is usually taken as the throat. The finger measures locate centres in the yogic body. சடலத் தலைவன் (lord of the body) is Siva as indweller.

reading: Going beyond the thirty-six that are called real to knowledge, and shattering dense maya by grace, the devotees on the path have known the state in which great grace stays unparted.
nuance: ஆறாறு (six sixes) is the 36 tattvas. The variant அறியா யசந்தென்னு would call them 'unknowing, unreal' (asat), which fits Siddhanta teaching better than 'real to knowledge'. The verse gives the last step to grace and to the devotee (அன்பர்), not to technique.

title: சமாதி
theme: Samadhi (சமாதி), the eighth limb, is reached through the limbs from yama on: mind and breath dissolve together, bindu and nada rise, the gaze is turned back, and the yogi joins the Supreme in a cool absorption where Siva is the soul within. Yet for one who goes with the Lord no samadhi is needed.
structure_note: The chapter opens (618) and closes (631) with verses that turn on the word சமாதி: the first makes samadhi the fruit of the limbs, the last says union with the Lord makes it unnecessary. Between them are verses on mind and breath (620), the yogic body (621 to 627) and the state itself (628 to 630).
source_issues: 622: variant முக்கடல் for முகட்டு (line 1) changes the image.
625 line 4 (திருவரை யாமனந் தீர்ந்தற்ற வாறே) and 623 line 4 (ஓடும் பதத்தையே) are obscure and may be corrupt.
630: variant முன்நின்ற (standing before) for உள்நின்ற (standing within) changes whether Siva is identified with the soul.

reading: Samadhi can be reached by going through yama and the limbs that follow; in them lie the eight siddhis; to those who abide in yama and the rest, samadhi comes of itself.
nuance: Each line turns on சமாதி யமாதி, a chime of samadhi with yama-adi (yama and the rest). The verse binds the highest limb to the first, the ethical one: there is no samadhi without yama.

reading: If bindu and nada rise high in Meru, they join in the samadhi where there is no juncture, and the rare substance of endless knowledge and a beautiful light appear.
nuance: மேரு is traditionally the spine or the crown of the head. சந்தி இல்லாத (without juncture) may mean a state with no meeting of opposites, or one beyond the junctures of time. Both bindu and nada are technical terms here.

reading: Where the abiding mind is, there the breath is; where the mind is not, the breath is not; for those who rejoice within the abiding mind, within it comes the dissolving of mind.
nuance: The verse states the yogic teaching that mind and breath move together, so stilling one stills the other. மன்மனம் may be 'the abiding mind' or simply a doubled மனம். மனோலயம் (the mind's dissolving) is the goal, reached inside the mind and not by force.

reading: They contemplate the opened well and the dense forest until they know them by seeing; in the open space of the ball, between the rich hills, they reined the horse with the bridle.
nuance: Every image is symbolic: the horse is commonly taken as the breath or mind and the rein as its control. கூபம் (well), விஞ்சத் தடவி (Vindhya forest, or dense wood) and செண்டு வெளி (open ground of the ball) are places in the yogic body that I can't fix.

reading: You who stay in the middle of the four doors at the summit of the root channel: once you have seen the upper door open onto space, Death's word will not reach you even in dreams.
nuance: மூல நாடி (root nadi) is usually the central channel and மேலை வாசல் (upper door) the opening at the crown. The last line can be read literally, that the yogi escapes death, or as freedom from fear of it; the variant முக்கடல் for முகட்டு changes line 1.

reading: Five mandalas, twelve bounds and forty-eight dwellers holding them, with the aim seen in the middle: there the moon shines and flows on the moving step.
nuance: The numbers (5, 12, six eights) map the yogic body in a way the verse does not explain; tradition takes the moon as the nectar flowing from the crown. ஓடும் பதம் is obscure. A short reading is all the Tamil supports.

reading: For those who lock the breath that stirs in the body as with a bolt, settle it in that ground where seeking ends, and turn the gaze back to rest within the eye, the mango in the garden hangs within reach.
nuance: The ripe mango hanging in one's own garden is the fruit of practice, near at hand. தேட்டற்ற நிலம் (ground without seeking) echoes 604's தேட்டமும் இல்லை. Which bodily ground is meant is not said.

reading: There is a way to know the form: the gods seized the dark mountain, churned and drank the nectar, but they will not climb the rare mountain and drink the nectar there; so the mind that is the holy mountain ended and ceased.
nuance: The contrast is between the gods' outer churning of the ocean with Mount Mandara and the inner mountain, taken as the crown of the head, where the yogi drinks nectar. Line 4 (திருவரை யாமனந் தீர்ந்தற்ற வாறே) is obscure and its word division uncertain.

reading: Making love the means and subduing desire, they went to the Trusted One, the First, the chanter of the four Vedas, the light shining within red gold, climbed the branch, worshipped and gathered there.
nuance: கொம்பேறி (having climbed the branch) is traditionally the ascent to the crown. அருத்தி may be desire (subdued) or a form of 'feeding'. The verse joins yogic ascent and devotional worship.

reading: Above the base is the three-sided form; at the juncture where the paths of time meet, at the upper crescent standing level with the forehead, the form takes many different forms.
nuance: முச்சதுரம் may be a triangle or a figure of three squares, traditionally the seat of kundalini above the base. மேலைப் பிறை (upper crescent) is the moon at the brow or crown. The verse is a map I can't fix.

reading: Free of imagining, going by the path of fire, seeking the splendour of the great light that made all forms and meeting it with the joined moon, one becomes the Supreme: that is cool samadhi.
nuance: கனல் வழி (path of fire) and புணர் மதி (the moon joined) are traditionally the rising power meeting the moon at the crown. Samadhi is called தண் (cool) after the fire of the ascent. தற்பரம் is the Supreme, or the state of being it.

reading: For those able to rest in absorption, when they reach the summit the tattvas gather, the fair good lady is caught as in a net, anger is broken and goes, and they stay in balance.
nuance: மாதுநல்லாள் may be Shakti, held within the yogi, or worldly woman, no longer a snare; the verse does not say. துலை (balance, scales) gives the image of equanimity.

reading: The God who stood as the single flame of light becomes both the First and the soul that stands within; the first Brahma and the one coloured like the great sea bow at the First's feet and gain love.
nuance: The verse identifies the light seen in samadhi with the soul within (சீவன்), a strong claim on its face. The variant முன்நின்ற (standing before) for உள்நின்ற (standing within) would weaken it. Brahma and Vishnu are shown as Siva's worshippers.

reading: Many yogas suit those who practise samadhi; if one goes with the Lord, no samadhis are needed; if one becomes him, there is no samadhi at all; yet in samadhi all sixty-four siddhis are attained.
nuance: The verse ranks three states: practising samadhi, going with the Lord, and becoming him, where samadhi has no meaning. எட்டெட்டு (eight eights) is read as sixty-four; it could also mean the eight siddhis in each of their kinds. The last line restores samadhi's worth after relativizing it.

title: அட்டாங்கயோகப் பேறு
theme: The attainment of eight-limbed yoga (அட்டாங்கயோகப் பேறு): those who love Siva's feet and practise reach the Siva-state, where the gods come out to meet them, hail them as their lord or as Hara himself, and they dwell in bliss by the Lord's grace. The chapter ends by defining samadhi as joining the Supreme beyond all limiting adjuncts.
structure_note: Four verses (633 to 636) describe the welcome by the gods, framed by a verse of grace to the devotee (632) and closing with verses on who reaches what (637, 638) and a definition of samadhi (639).
source_issues: 635: கும்பத் தமரர் is unclear and may be corrupt.
639: the seven causes (காரணம் ஏழும்) are unexplained and தாரியல் is unclear.

reading: Those who delight in the feet of the matted-haired one who gladly rises into the flower will go to Amaravati; the one on the great bull, who dances with the lady, will grant grace, asking 'what did this one desire?'
nuance: போது உகந்து ஏறும் (who delights to mount the flower) is traditionally the Lord rising in the heart's lotus; Sengalvaraya parallels Kural 3. அமராபதி is Indra's heaven, a lower goal than release, which the next verses go beyond. ஏதுகந்தான் இவன் may be 'what does he want?', a gracious question, as read here.

reading: For those who hold to his feet with love, learn the Supreme's praise and contemplate him where they are, sages come to meet them as they rise, and they can reach the clear Siva-state.
nuance: The means named here are devotional (love, learning his praise, contemplation), though the chapter is the fruit of yoga. முற்றெழுந்தாங்கே may be 'as they rise in full' or 'as they rise at the end'.

reading: Having worshipped and done austerity and become king of the gods, they are hailed as the lord of Amaravati, and with cool drums and flutes sounding they dwell in bliss: this is the Lord's grace.
nuance: Whether the yogi literally becomes Indra or is welcomed like a king of the gods is open. The last words credit the bliss to grace, not to the austerity.

reading: At the time they go and reach the red-gold Siva-way, hosts of gods come out to meet them, saying 'this is our golden lord', and they may dwell in blissful union.
nuance: கும்பத்து அமரர் is unclear: the gods of the dome of heaven, or of the summit in the body. இன்பக் கலவி (blissful union) is union with Siva. The gods now call the yogi their lord, a step beyond 634.

reading: When he arrives, the gods of the directions ask 'who is this?', are told 'this is Hara', and all the splendid gods come to meet him: so he truly saw the dark-throated one.
nuance: The yogi is taken for Siva himself, which the verse gives as the proof that he truly saw Siva. மெய்கண்ட (truly saw) may also echo the name of the Siddhanta's Meykandar, but nothing in the verse requires it.

reading: Those of the true word who seek the good way and turn aside Death's way, and householders whose great giving never shrinks, though they reach the gods' many ways in the eight directions, find it becomes the way of the earth.
nuance: பார்வழி யாகுமே is the crux. Read as 'it leads back to the earth', the verse says merit wins heavens but not release, against the yogi's attainment. Read as 'it becomes the way for the world', it praises such people as a model. Both stand.

reading: For those able to rest in absorption, and those able to draw in the seven worlds, it stands as strength; for those able to store it, it is nectar to revel in; for those able to bear it, it becomes their own dwelling.
nuance: The subject is not stated; it may be the Lord, the attainment or the yogic power. Each line names a capacity (வல்லார்க்கு, those able to) and a matching gift. The variants alter case endings but not the sense.

reading: Going beyond the limiting adjunct that is effect, so that the seven noble causes come to oneself, and in the austerity that is the noble cause joining the Supreme: that is samadhi.
nuance: உபாதி (upadhi, limiting adjunct) and காரியம், காரணம் (effect, cause) are technical; the seven causes are not identified in the verse. தாரியல் may be 'garlanded' or a form of 'bearing'. The definition parallels 597's for dharana and 628's for samadhi.

title: அட்டமா சித்தி
theme: The eight great siddhis (அட்டமா சித்தி): powers such as becoming minute, light, heavy or all-pervading, and entering another body, said to come by eightfold yoga, by holding the breath in the central channel and by a year's union with a form of Shakti. The chapter frames them with grace: the siddhis come when Shakti grants them, the Lord who cuts off birth gives them, and walking the world finds nothing that love does not.
structure_note: The verses fall into loose groups: the siddhis as the Lord's gift (640 to 643); powers listed by years of practice (644 to 652); the ten vital airs, chiefly dhananjaya, and the diseases of their disorder (653 to 658); the central channel, nada and the Lady in the lotus stalk (659 to 667); the eight siddhis one by one, each reached in a year with a named Lady (668 to 693); breath counts for each Lady (694 to 703); and a close on samadhi, a list of twenty-one powers, love over pilgrimage, and freedom from death (704 to 711).
source_issues: 678 line 1 is garbled (ஞ்aனமும்), apparently ஞானமும்.

650 and 662: variants are garbled (கோண்-கிய வாமுத்தி; தளண்-களி W\டுபோய்ப்), and 664 (ஓண்-கே), 679 (படையானவையெலாண்-), 705 (சிணண்-குற்ற ... சித்திதாண்-) and 711 (கலந்தெண்-குந்) show the same encoding damage.
693: வேட்டை (hunt) makes little sense; the variant வெட்டை (open space) is likely the better reading.
644: the variant அருமிரு for அருமிகு changes 'four' to possibly 'two'.
666: the variant கூத்தனை நாடுகின்றேனே reverses who seeks whom.
694 to 703: breath counts are given without a key and may be corrupt in places.

reading: Bowing and seeking the Supreme in all eight directions, worshipping our Lord there with resolve, the eight great siddhis were established in the eight directions.
nuance: எண் திசை (eight directions) repeats in every line, matching the eight siddhis. Who established them, and what தணிந்து (calmed, subdued) qualifies, is unclear; the verse may be the poet's own account of how he received them.

reading: Seeking without fault the feet of the Lord whose nature the gods know, I saw the pure space; the eight great siddhis are not hard for me, for he gave great grace and cut off my birth.
nuance: தூவெளி (pure space) is a yogic term for the open expanse of awareness, as tradition takes it. The verse sets the siddhis beside the cutting of birth, and credits both to grace rather than to technique.

reading: By the guru's grace, Mular, following the sign, looked to the fragrant ... of Parai; with the shambhavi and khechari seals joined, the great Siva-state is the gain of the eight siddhis.
nuance: சாம்பவி and கேசரி are names of yogic seals (mudras), traditionally the inward gaze and the tongue turned back. சங்கட்டம் is obscure; a variant reads சக்கட்டம், perhaps the wheel or circle. The verse names the author, Mular.

reading: If the one beginningless knowledge, which body, elements, kala, time and maya cannot reach, joins the truth of the unceasing Lord, entering another's body becomes possible.
nuance: காயாதி பூதம் கலை காலம் மாயை lists tattvas from the body up to maya. பரகாயம் is usually entering another's body; it can also be read as the supreme body. ஆயாது அகல is unclear: 'parting without being examined' or 'separating without being caught'.

reading: The twenty thousand eight hundred kinds of karma, mantra and yoga only give the body toil; for siddhi they come down to four.
nuance: The number and the four (a variant has அருமிரு, two) are not explained. The plain point is that many practices reduce to a few that matter.

reading: Of the kalas that abide as twelve in the moon, when the rising of four is gone and eight remain, if one looks without attachment for twelve years, twelve firm siddhis arise.
nuance: The moon's kalas are a figure for the breath and the inner moon in yogic reading; the arithmetic of twelve, four and eight is obscure. The twelve years open the sequence of powers by year in 646 to 648.

reading: Powers that come in order with the years: freedom when disease and poison surround, arts and learning, long intellect and keen wisdom, ... and hearing from afar, ending at the twelfth.
nuance: The verse is a compressed list and its grammar is hard to follow; பீடொன்றினால் வாயா is unclear. The list overlaps with the powers in 705 and 706.

reading: In the seventh year one has the speed of a storm wind, an untiring pace that covers many yojanas; in the eighth grey hair and wrinkles do not appear; in the ninth comes entering another's body.
nuance: The years are supplied from the ordinals (ஏழு, எட்டு, ஒன்பது) and the context of 645; they may count stages rather than years. நரைதிரை, grey hair and wrinkles, is the standard pair for old age.

reading: In the tenth one is filled and becomes Rudra in meditation; in the eleventh the eight siddhis; and going through the seven worlds above and seven below, standing all-pervading, comes in the twelfth.
nuance: The first word of lines 2 to 4 varies across copies (ஏர்வொன்று, நேரொன்று, ஓரொன்று), and the line division of years is uncertain.

reading: The eight are: becoming atomic, lightness in the world, unyielding heaviness, the body entering another body, becoming whatever one wills, the nature of joining the supreme body, unfailing truth, and pervading all.
nuance: The standard eight are anima, mahima, laghima, garima, prapti, prakamya, ishitva and vashitva. The verse's list does not map onto them cleanly, and variants (நோன்மையும், ககனமும்) change two items.

reading: Holding all things, becoming atomic, drawing many lives in, there is no further lack; rising within those from which we rose and growing high is how the boon of release came first.
nuance: The syntax is loose and the variant கோண்கிய வாமுத்தி is garbled. One reading is that the powers rest on release; another that release is reached through them.

reading: The former three hundred and sixty measures of time came as nazhigai beginning from space; as one meditates again and again, discerning from earth upward, it rises from the navel.
nuance: முந்நூற்றறுபது (360) may count days, breaths or units of time; நாழிகை is a unit of twenty-four minutes. மண்முதல் (from earth) suggests meditating the elements in order, and உந்தி (navel) the seat from which the breath rises.

reading: Those whose mind turns and becomes full of Siva, who have discerned release and reached silence, are freed in Siva; free of the five bonds they gain purity, their mind in the Supreme, in the holy dance.
nuance: சிவமுத்தர் (those freed in Siva) and மோனர் (the silent) name a state beyond the powers just listed. ஐந்தில் தொடக்கு, bond in the five, may be the five senses or a fivefold count of malas; the verse does not say.

reading: These nine vital airs are in accord; above them is dhananjaya; while it stays in accord within the nine, body and life stay together.
nuance: The tradition counts ten airs (prana, apana, vyana, udana, samana, naga, kurma, krikara, devadatta, dhananjaya). The verse makes dhananjaya the tenth and the one on which body and life hold together.

reading: Dhananjaya stays in the nine airs, as two hundred and twenty-three; if it does not stay in the body, the body swells and bursts.
nuance: இருநூற்றிருபத்து மூன்று (223) is not explained. Dhananjaya is traditionally the air that swells the corpse after death; here its failure in the living body causes swelling.

reading: Swellings, tumours, scabies and leprosy, many swelling diseases and anaemia, swollen wind-disease, hunchback and lameness, and diseases settling in the eye.
nuance: The verse continues 654: these are the diseases of a disordered dhananjaya. வீங்கு (swell) opens every line.

reading: Eye disease comes from dhananjaya, cough does not; because kurma is not mixed in the eye, the light is not mixed in the eye either.
nuance: Kurma is traditionally the air that moves the eyelids. இவ்வாணிகள் is obscure, and the logic of the last two lines (no kurma, so no light) is unclear.

reading: Isa among the gods, Tirumal and Brahma stood there without ceasing and knew the radiant light that reaches through the sound in the channel, the eye and the heart.
nuance: நாடியின் ஓசை (the sound in the channel) and தூடி அளவு are obscure; தூடி may be a measure or a misreading. The point seems to be that even the gods reached this inner light by stillness.

reading: In the body with nine gates is one place with nine channels; for those who can still the nine channels, the nine visions ... become many.
nuance: The nine gates are the body's openings. The last line, ஒன்பது காட்சி இலை பல ஆமே, can be read 'the nine visions are not; many come', and a variant has உலைநலம் ஆமே. I can't fix it.

reading: When the bright sushumna runs below the rising fire, drawing in, and the sun and moon run their way, holding up and bearing the seven worlds: this we told to those on the rare path.
nuance: இரவி மதி (sun and moon) are taken in yoga as the right and left channels, pingala and ida; the fire below as the fire at the root where kundalini lies. The seven worlds may be the body's centres.

reading: As the Lord, meeting her, sought the Lady, like a doe caught in a net of bonds, if one makes the balanced channel a pure path it becomes a seed set aside to be sold.
nuance: துலைப்பட்ட நாடி, the channel that is balanced like a scale, is taken as the central channel between ida and pingala. The doe in the net and the seed kept for sale are images I can't place with confidence.

reading: Those who ran there and saw the one thing raise nada within the channel; seeking there, they scoop up honey and drink it, and bind the enemies who stood in the camp.
nuance: பாடி (camp) is taken as the body, the enemies as the senses or passions, and the honey as the inner nectar. The plain image is of a raid that ends in a feast and a binding.

reading: In the stalk of the bound lotus nine adorned maidens joined the Lady; standing bound, passing through the dark fruit and standing at the brow-mark, it became full.
nuance: The lotus stalk is taken as the central channel and the nine maidens as nine shaktis. களங்கனி (the dark kalam fruit) and பொட்டு (the brow-mark) may be centres at the throat or palate and the brow. The variants in line 3 are garbled.

reading: The full Shakti, divided as seven and three, and the beautiful maidens who made seven hundred and five, became the cause of the five beginning with Narayana and Brahma, and mingled and spread.
nuance: The five gods are traditionally the agents of the five acts. The numbers (ஏழுமூன்று, எழுநூற்றஞ்சு) are not explained.

reading: If this Lady, who expanded, contracted and ripened, rises hidden within and stays hidden there, the elements from earth that spread out are drawn in, and the roaring breath subsides in its place.
nuance: The Lady (மங்கை) may be Shakti as kundalini. விரிந்து குவிந்து (expanding and contracting) suits both the cosmos and the breath.

reading: The two airs called ida and pingala, flowing through their channels, stand reversed; their hindrances, six and seven, subside in the lightning creeper that grows in the cool light.
nuance: மின்கொடி, the lightning creeper, is a common figure for kundalini or the central channel. ஆறேழு may be six and seven, or forty-two; a variant reads ஆறு எழும், the six that rise.

reading: If one stills and gathers oneself and stays aware there, the breath folds and subsides within; folding within the abiding life, the dancer who took up the dance seeks him.
nuance: In the text the dancer (Siva) seeks the stilled one; the variant கூத்தனை நாடுகின்றேனே reverses this to 'I seek the dancer'. The reversal changes who moves first.

reading: Seeking within the channel with the sound of nada, going and taking hold of that sacred one, binding the enemies in the camp, it became a jewelled lamp in one hand.
nuance: Line 3 repeats 661. திரு (the sacred, Shri) may be Shakti. மாடி ஒருகை is obscure; the lamp in the hand suggests a light that is now one's own.

reading: To name the siddhis beginning with anima: being an atom within the atom, greatness, lightness, unbending weight, entering another body, and being everywhere though an atom: these are the eight.
nuance: This list is closer to the standard eight than 649's, but the mapping of each phrase is still uncertain: நேர்மை and இணுகாத ஏகார் are hard to fix.

reading: The eight siddhis come through eightfold yoga, by mastering the prana that is hard to master; when the fire at the root of the central channel drives the sun and lets the moon drink, the higher ones come too.
nuance: எட்டி யோகம, eightfold yoga, is the limbs of yoga from restraints to samadhi. The fire, sun and moon are the usual yogic figures for the root fire and the right and left channels.

reading: Through eightfold yoga, beyond the eight siddhis, all kinds of understanding become clear; the siddhis, the eight, come into being when Shakti Tripurai grants grace.
nuance: The verse puts the siddhis under Shakti's grace, not under the practice alone, and places understanding (புத்தி) above them.

reading: Those who have gained these eight with the beautiful Supreme are siddhas, since they reach the supreme world; holding firm within what they love is the supreme vision, and the eight boundaries reach to where he stands.
nuance: சித்தர் is defined here by reaching the supreme world, not by the powers alone. The last line is obscure; the variant இருக்கல் (staying) for இறுக்கல் (holding tight) changes little.

reading: For those who can reverse the moon and sun that climb the mountain and be free of dross in the pit like a bulb, the good world of desire is reached without effort; that world is anima and the rest.
nuance: மந்தரம் (the mountain) may be the spine; குழி (the pit) the root centre; கந்து, a bulb or post. The variant காய மிய for கா மிய changes 'world of desire' to something about the body.

reading: Binding it and practising for a year, he becomes the anima he puts on; lighter than carded cotton, he stays thin and cannot be overcome.
nuance: The lightness of cotton suits laghima more than anima. முடிந்திட்டு வைத்து (binding and setting) is taken as holding the breath.

reading: With that singular Lady who arises, the tattvas that go everywhere become a refuge; if the times of dying stay in one's own control, in five years comes great lightness.
nuance: மாலகு is taken as great lightness (laghima). மாய்கின்றது ஐயாண்டின் might also mean 'what dies in five years'. The formula 'with the Lady' recurs through 694 to 702.

reading: After seeing the wondrous one who has become great lightness, he stays flourishing as light; it stood spread everywhere as milk-white light, and he sees the true thing that is the higher light.
nuance: மாயன் can mean Vishnu, the wondrous one, or the illusory; who becomes light (the yogi or the seen) is unclear.

reading: When one's own tattva joins the gentle Lady who spoke the truth and mingles with it like a thing held in the hand, in a year one becomes the dark thing, mahima.
nuance: மகிமா (greatness) is one of the eight. மைப்பொருள் (the dark or black thing) is obscure.

reading: After seeing the light of the breath that rises, the passing times no longer pass; the time above stood open in space, and the times that remain go one's own way.
nuance: கால் means both breath and time, and the verse plays on the two: mastering the breath is mastering time. 680 repeats much of it.

reading: Knowledge flourishes as his way, the world flourishes as his way, all things flourish as his way; he stands as his own way, as his own grace.
nuance: தான் may be the Lord or the yogi who has gained the powers; the second fits the chapter, the first the closing words தன்னருள். Line 1 is garbled in the source (ஞ்aனமும், read as ஞானமும்).

reading: If one stays a year with the Lady of the tattvas, holding all the hosts of elements one has seen, what opens is good prapti.
nuance: பிராத்தி is prapti, the power of reaching anything. The formula of a year with a Lady recurs in 682 and 684.

reading: After seeing the light of lightning that rises, one can see the spreading worlds in the ripening flower; the moving time stood open in space, and the passing times do not pass.
nuance: Lines 3 and 4 repeat 677. The flower (பூ) may be a lotus centre or the earth.

reading: For those who know, there is nothing that goes, nothing that comes, nothing that dies, nothing that grows, no delay, and no light at all in the inner cave.
nuance: தமரகம் is the small inner cavity, traditionally of the heart or head. After the verses on seeing lights, this one denies even light: the knower's state is beyond change, and beyond the visions too.

reading: If one dwells within the known Parashakti, the hosts of elements fall away; if one stays a year with them gathered, entering another's body becomes possible.
nuance: The formula follows 679 and 684. பரகாயம் மேவல் recurs from 643.

reading: People do not know what the lamp's light is; for those who already have the light of the root lamp and see the light of the lamp that is seen, the light of the higher lamp makes release easy.
nuance: The four lamps (ஆன, மூல, கான, மேலை) may be stages of an inner light rising from the root centre to the crown, as tradition takes them. கான may be 'seen' or 'of the forest'.

reading: If one stays a year with the Lady of Sadasiva, gathering all the hosts of elements one has seen, one becomes the ancient Lord's tattva.
nuance: ஈசன் தத்துவம், the Lord's tattva, is taken as ishitva, lordship, one of the eight.

reading: He becomes the light of the rising moon and its coolness; if the moon's kala joins, he becomes the moon itself.
