nuance: The moon is a yogic figure for the cool nectar in the head. ஆகின்ற சந்திரன் opens every line. A variant reads தண்ணளி, cool grace.

reading: He becomes able to create, able to protect, and lord of destruction; he becomes one of whom it is said, he is himself the one.
nuance: In context the subject is the yogi who has gained ishitva, taking on the Lord's acts. The verse names three acts, not the five, and does not say whether the yogi becomes the Lord or only acts like him.

reading: If, within the kala that flourished in its nature, one firmly turns back the five elements spread out in many forms, in a year one sees the subtle true thing.
nuance: மறித்திடில் (turning back) suggests withdrawing the elements into their source. The verse plays on தன்மை, பன்மை, வன்மை, மென்மை.

reading: If you ask what ripened as the true thing, it is the good vashitva; he becomes the very self of all lives, mingled with them like a thing in hand.
nuance: வசித்துவம் is vashitva, the power of bringing beings under one's will. The verse turns it into being the self of all lives, a gentler sense than control.

reading: If the sun that flourished in its nature sees the subtle true thing, and the senses become golden and go, one sees the good creeper.
nuance: The creeper (கொடி) is a figure for Shakti or kundalini, and the sun for the right channel. பொன்மையதாக (becoming golden) is obscure.

reading: If one knows the body of that creeper with the Lady who is the good creeper, in a year one goes to the golden worlds and returns, and becomes the lover of the stone creeper.
nuance: காமுகன் (lover, one who desires) may point to the power of having one's desires fulfilled (prakamya). கற்கொடி, the stone creeper, is obscure.

reading: After the lovely tattva comes, the fragrance of the flower becomes the world; ... the light where the tongue dwells becomes lordship.
nuance: Line 3 is obscure, and a variant reads உன்னிடம் எய்திடு, 'reaching your place'. நா (the tongue) may refer to the tongue turned back in khechari.

reading: After seeing the good light that is lordship, it stays flourishing as a mother's home; after seeing the worlds that went within, one sees the great light.
nuance: பேயகம் is obscure, perhaps the cremation ground where Siva dances, or the great void.

reading: He who has seen with trembling that great ... which is the great light, as the light of the earth, sees the light of the breath, the one light that is the whole earth as a garland of light.
nuance: வேட்டை (hunt) does not fit; the variant வெட்டை (open space, void) fits better. காலொளி, the breath's light, recurs from 677.

reading: To tell how breath and life mingle: the breath is with that creeper Lady, and it is wanted in five hundred and thirteen, in this way.
nuance: 694 to 703 give breath counts for a series of Ladies or kalas. The numbers are not explained, and a variant in line 4 (பெண்மண்டி) is garbled.

reading: Six is in the head of nectar; six is a thousand three hundred and five; six becomes a thousand on the rare path; what grows as six is two.
nuance: ஆறு means both six and path, and the verse may play on both. The counts are obscure.

reading: Above the two is the Lady of Sadasiva; to tell how the two rise taking breath, two thousand and fifty-one gathered, and the time taken is five.
nuance: The numbers are not explained; கால் is again both breath and time.

reading: The Lady with five and five faces: five with five is ayuta; besides that five, two thousand; the time taken is one.
nuance: அஞ்சுடன் அஞ்சு முகம் (five and five faces) may be the ten faces of a goddess. ஆயுதம் may be ayuta (ten thousand) or 'weapon'.

reading: The Lady of the tattva that is one: to tell how the one moves taking breath, the one wins thousands upon thousands, and the time taken is before.
nuance: ஒன்று opens every line; the counts are obscure.

reading: With the Lady of that kala who rises first, the measure where the breath ends is fifty-one with five.
nuance: Fifty-one may be the letters of the Sanskrit alphabet, which mantra theory links to the kalas; the verse doesn't say so.

reading: With that singular Lady hard to fathom, the measure of breath is five hundred and thirty-nine, and the breath stayed within its measure.
nuance: ஆய்வரும் (hard to examine) opens each line. மாய்வரு வாயு may be 'the breath that ends' or 'the wondrous breath'.

reading: In the Father who is the twofold treasure, the way the breath moves is two hundred and thirty-three with five: these are the letters in which the breath moves.
nuance: இருநிதி (twofold treasure) is obscure; எழுத்து (letter) suggests the counts are of syllables in a mantra or breaths matched to letters.

reading: With the Lady in the rising light, the place of the breath is seven hundred and twenty-nine and four, and the fire rose and stayed with it in this way.
nuance: The fire (அங்கி) may be the root fire of 659 and 669. The counts are obscure.

reading: Taking six breaths it produces essence; taking seven it doubles and brings it down; taking eight the places come into accord; and with nine the breath is even across the great ground.
nuance: இரதம் may be rasa, the bodily essence or nectar. The verse reads like a practice of breath counts, but its terms can't be fixed.

reading: The yogi of the light of samadhi sees at the juncture how the moon meets sun, Supreme and Sthanu, and becomes one with the world.
nuance: சந்தி (juncture) may be the meeting of the channels or the twilight hour. தாணு (the pillar) is a name of Siva. சகமுகத்து உந்தி is obscure.

reading: A list of powers: freedom from afflicting spirits, removing poison, learning that is revered and great wisdom, ... hearing from afar, becoming invisible, and moving with the speed of wind.
nuance: அணங்கு is an afflicting spirit or goddess; அருஞ்சனம் may be poison or a rare collyrium. Line 3 is garbled in a variant. The list repeats much of 646.

reading: Escaping death and old age, entering another's body, giving the earth of battle to the dead, and gaining the form of Hara: one who has learned the count knows these as three sevens.
nuance: மூவேழ் (three sevens, twenty-one) closes the list begun in 705. சரைவிடல் (leaving old age) has a variant சிறைவிடல் (release from prison). Line 2 is obscure.

reading: Circling the world where the sea roars and walking till the feet ache is of no use; those sweet ones who see the Lord in love know the city where the Lord dwells.
nuance: The verse sets love (காதல்) against pilgrimage. The city (நகர்) is not named; tradition reads it as the body or the heart. Placed in a chapter on powers, it may also say that travel to the worlds, a siddhi, is not the point.

reading: With the root, the first one, Brahma, Vishnu and Hara before him, as the five-faced one declares: supreme bindu, ample supreme nada, bindu, the single nada, the sheltering Shakti and Parai are the feet of the Supreme.
nuance: The five-faced one is Sadasiva. The list of bindu, nada, Shakti and Parai follows the stages of Saiva cosmology, as in chapter 140; how they divide is unclear.

reading: Going with the deity of adhara yoga, with Parai above, joining the Supreme, as the sixteen kalas from medha rise, the light above, unspoken and unthinkable, is the yoga of bliss.
nuance: ஆதார யோகம் is yoga through the body's centres. மேதாதி ஈரெண் கலை, the sixteen kalas beginning with medha, are a mantra-theory series. ஆனந்த யோகம், the yoga of bliss, is the chapter's goal beyond the powers.

reading: When moon and sun come and join, the ancient gods praise; to the true devotees who do what is ordained, the Supreme stands and shows the Lord.
nuance: பதி may be the Lord, the Pati of Siddhanta, or the place (abode). Moon and sun meeting is again the joining of the side channels.

reading: Those who pierce till the brow-spot rises, plant the staff till sparks rise, and know, have no Yama; those who can bind become hidden and are everywhere, wedded within the honey-opening lotus.
nuance: பொட்டு (brow-spot), தண்டு (staff, taken as the spine) and பொறி (sparks) are yogic figures. நமனில்லை (no Yama) can mean freedom from death or from death's power over the soul, and the two readings differ greatly.

title: கலை நிலை
theme: The state of the kalas (கலை நிலை): by love turned toward Siva and by breath held steady along the kalas, the yogi can guard the inner faculties and the body, find the Lord and his Shakti dwelling within so that the body becomes Siva's temple, and by tests of the breath know when the body's end approaches and how to put it off.
structure_note: The verses are chained: each begins with a word from the end of the one before (காக்கலும் 712 to 713, நிலை 713 to 714, சாதகன் 716 to 717, கிடக்குமே 717 to 718). 721 and 723 share the refrain of the day the Lord and the Lady part (தன்னில் பிரியுநாள்), traditionally the day of death foreseen by the breath.
source_issues: 713: கலைபதி நாறையும் is a wrong word split for கலை பதினாறையும் (the sixteen kalas).
719: line 1 begins தனே, which breaks the rhyme with ஊனே, வானோர், தேனே; read தானே.

reading: If one makes love the way and looks with the eye at the forehead-eyed Lord who made love the way, by love he opens the way of the Ganga, and by love one can guard oneself.
nuance: காதல் வழிசெய்து is repeated in every line. கங்கை வழிதரும் is the obscure line: plainly the Lord who bears the Ganga, it is traditionally taken in yoga as a flow of nectar from the crown, or as a channel of breath. What is guarded (காக்கலும்) is not named; the next verse lists it.

reading: One can guard the four inner instruments, the sixteen kalas and the good breath mingled within; one can guard them all if one stands with the mind fixed.
nuance: கரணங்கள் நான்கு are traditionally manas, buddhi, chitta and ahankara. கலைபதி நாறையும் is read here as கலை பதினாறையும், the sixteen kalas (traditionally of the moon, matched with the breath); the printed word split hides this.

reading: The breath that comes evenly stands steady, still like a lamp that does not flicker; if one knows the union that stands along the path of the kalas, this is the way to be free of wavering.
nuance: சிலைபெற may mean 'firm as stone' or simply 'steady'. கலப்பு (union) is taken as the joining of the breaths or of breath and mind; the verse does not say which. The variant மலைவறி would give 'free of confusion' for அலைவற, a small change.

reading: The Lord of the elements who stays close at one's side, and the way found by holding the breath as a sluice holds water: Sankara with matted hair sits enthroned upon the bull.
nuance: மடையொன்றி (joined like a sluice-gate) is read as the breath held and released; the verse does not say breath. The last two lines are a plain image of Siva, and their link to the first two is left to the reader: perhaps the Lord who is reached by that way.

reading: People do not know how much time remains to them; one who looks to how that time can be lengthened and holds the gathered breath so that it shines stands firm, and he is the true practitioner.
nuance: பெருக்கின்ற காலப் பெருமை is taken as the lengthening of life by breath control, a common claim of the yogic tantra. தருக்கு usually means pride; here it seems to mean firmness or strength.

reading: Seeing what that practice is, one performs worship that is great austerity; if it is directed as knowledge into the place of refuge, it ripens and lies there as a transmutation.
nuance: வேதகம் is the alchemist's transmuting agent that turns base metal to gold; the image is traditionally of the body or soul transformed. போதகம் (instruction, knowledge) and புகலுற (into the refuge) are compressed and I can't fix what is being 'directed' (பாய்ச்சினால்), though breath is likely.

reading: Of itself it lies there with its three rising fruits; of itself it moves, looking into the inner nadi; of itself it spreads out as a lotus; of itself it goes on, standing within that light.
nuance: The subject of தானே is unnamed: it continues the 'transmutation' of 717, and may be the breath, the kundalini or the practice. The three fruits (பயன் மூன்று) are not named. The lotus (பங்கயம்) is traditionally a chakra and the light (சோதி) the vision at the crown.

reading: The Lady of the tattvas, who rose of herself, makes her way through the flesh and dwells within us; when the Mother who bore the world of the gods regards us, the body drinks honey and becomes Siva's temple.
nuance: The verse gives the body (ஊன்) a positive end: it becomes சிவாலயம் through Shakti, the claim 725 makes in the first person. தேனே பருகி (drinking honey) is traditionally the nectar of yoga; whether it is the body or the yogi that drinks is not stated.

reading: No one knows how the breath, which packs in so as to make one shine, is wasted away; once one knows how it is wasted, one can join with the breath in which Nandi shines.
nuance: அழியும் படி is 'the way it perishes', of the breath and by implication of life. நந்தி is Siva (or Tirumular's guru); the verse can be read as joining the breath to Nandi or as reaching the breath in which he shines.

reading: By testing you can see the flaw, the day when the Lord parts from the Lady; worship the guru, who is the means, and value him as great wealth.
nuance: சோதனை is traditionally the testing of the breath to foretell the day of death, and the parting of நாதன் and நாயகி is taken as death, the separation of Siva and Shakti (or of life and body) in the person. The verse does not name the breath; the reading rests on the chapter. The variant gives சாதகமாகும் குருவழி பட்டு, 'following the guru's way that makes the practice', with much the same sense.

reading: If you can tie fast, so that it does not escape, the horse that rose with twelve legs, and drink deeply, the body will not leave for a thousand years of water and a thousand of earth; this is the Lord Nandi's command.
nuance: The horse with twelve legs (ஈராறு கால்) is traditionally the breath, whose outward reach is reckoned as twelve finger-breadths; கால் means both leg and wind. நீர் ஆயிரமும் நிலம் ஆயிரத்து ஆண்டும் may be read as a huge span of years or as surviving through flood and the earth's ages; the sense is long life, the measure is unclear.

reading: Seven in sound, five in sight here, three in the nose and two on the tongue: on the day the shining Lady and the shining Lord part, he has set out the stainless light.
nuance: The numbers attached to hearing, sight, smell and taste are traditionally read as signs, counted in days, by which the failing senses foretell death; the verse names no days. தேசி and தேசன் (the radiant one, female and male) echo நாயகி and நாதன் in 721. The last line can be read as the Lord fixing the light the soul goes to, or fixing these signs.

title: காயசித்தி உபாயம்
theme: The means of perfecting the body (காயசித்தி உபாயம்): since the body is the ground of life and of true knowledge, and the Lord has made it his temple, it is to be nurtured, not despised; breath control, mantra, the raising of the vital airs, restraint of food and union with Shakti are given as the means by which the body is cleansed, made young and kept from death.
structure_note: Two opening verses in the first person state the turn from despising the body to cherishing it (724, 725). The rest gives the means: cleansing by breath and the humours (726, 727), a set of yogic diagrams and counts (728, 729), inner sound, mantra and the raising of prana and apana (730 to 733), Shakti and the reversal of age (734 to 736), and the defeat of Death (737 to 739). Several verses close with an oath on Nandi (ஆணையே).
source_issues: 732: the variant list holds the garbled entry Wடனே, a stray Latin letter in place of a Tamil one.
738: the variant வாயுவுன்ய் சரீர is garbled.
739: சனவேத in line 1 is obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: If the body perishes, the life perishes, and one cannot firmly attain true knowledge; so, having learned the means of nurturing the body, I nurtured the body and with it nurtured life.
nuance: The argument is practical: the body is kept because knowledge (மெய்ஞ்ஞானம்) needs time and a living frame to be won. உபாயம் is left unnamed here; the chapter supplies it.

reading: I once held the body to be a thing of shame; then within the body I saw the true substance, and knowing that the Highest has made the body his temple, I now cherish it.
nuance: The verse narrates a change of mind: இழுக்கு (a fault, something base) is the view Tirumular says he held first, the ascetic contempt for the body. உத்தமன் கோயில் கொண்டான் makes the body a temple, and ஓம்புதல் is the word for caring for something precious.

reading: Turning the breath round cleanses and drives out; for those who know the means of loosening the impurity, filling the lotus and circulating it, the heat ceases and the body becomes like collyrium.
nuance: Breath is not named; சுழற்றி (whirling) and கமலத்துப் பூரித்து (filling at the lotus) are traditionally taken as the inhalation (puraka) and circulation of breath. மலம் here may be bodily waste or the soul's impurity. அஞ்சனம் (black eye-salve) is unclear as an image: a dark, lustrous, unaging body is one reading, an invisible one (the salve of the magicians) another. The variant சுழித்து changes little.

reading: With the body like collyrium, practice in the evening removes phlegm, at midday the treacherous wind, and in the early morning bile; we have spoken so that the poison goes, and grey hair and wrinkles are destroyed.
nuance: ஐ, வாதம் and பித்தம் are the three humours of Tamil medicine (kapha, vata, pitta), each matched to a time of day. What is to be done at those times (செய்திடில்) is not named; the chapter suggests breath practice. நரைதிரை (greying and wrinkling) are the marks of age the chapter promises to undo, as again in 734.

reading: The serpents of three coils, the two and the eight, the yantra that holds, the twelve finger-breadths, and the two hanging eggs tied there: whoever stays fixed so will not lose the body.
nuance: Almost every term is technical. The coiled serpent is traditionally kundalini, twelve finger-breadths the measure of the breath, and the two hanging eggs (முட்டை இரண்டு) are taken by some as the testes, tied in a yogic lock; பாம்பு இரண்டு எட்டு may be nadis or the eight-petalled lotus. I can't fix the diagram. The variant நான்றவிழ் (hanging loose) for நான்றவிம் may be the better reading.

reading: A hundred and sixty-six go round to the right, a hundred and sixty-six to the left, a hundred and sixty-six face each other, and a hundred and sixty-six enter.
nuance: நூறும் அறுபதும் ஆறும் may be one number (166) or three counts (a hundred, sixty, six). The subject is unnamed; breaths through the right and left channels, meeting and entering the central channel, is the likely sense in this chapter, but it is a guess.

reading: One who has mastered the left and right in Shakti's temple can hear music at midday; the sweet dance and Siva himself appear; we have spoken truth, by Sadananda's command.
nuance: Shakti's temple is taken as the body, and left and right (இடம் வலம்) as the left and right breaths (ida and pingala). The music (வாத்தியம்) is traditionally the inner nada heard in yoga, and கூத்து Siva's dance. The variant வாக்கியம் (speech) for வாத்தியம் would change what is heard.

reading: Bindu shining in its many forms as the letter ma, the letter sa recited in thought until it is attained, the mantra that turns back, and the abiding nada: when these are fully gained, they are the yogi's path of dharma.
nuance: மகாரம் and சகாரம் are letters of a mantra, traditionally of the five-syllable mantra, and are matched here with bindu and nada; their roles are not explained. மறிப்பது (that which turns back or blocks) and the last line's division (நாதம் அறப்பெற or நாத மறப்பு) are uncertain.

reading: Raising by contemplation the prana that stands straight with the whorl of the navel, fixing it first at the summit with Siva's mantra, and raising the apana by contemplation, one becomes Siva.
nuance: பிராணன் and அபானன் are the upward and downward vital airs; உந்திச் சுழி (the navel whorl) and முகடு (the summit, the crown) are their stations. சிவன் அவன் ஆமே, he becomes Siva, is the strongest claim in the chapter, and it rests on the technical practice.

reading: Mark the place two finger-breadths above the anus and below the linga; in this body the Lord too is there; see that this is the instruction that is not to be spoken.
nuance: The place is traditionally the muladhara, the base of the yogic body. ஆறா உடம்பு (the body that does not cool, or does not rest) is unclear. கூறா உபதேசம் can be 'instruction not to be told' (secret, from a guru) or 'instruction that cannot be told'.

reading: Those who closely embrace the blue-hued lady with fine jewels and hold to her as lasting will, as the world can see, lose their grey hair and wrinkles and become young again; by the supreme Nandi's command.
nuance: The plain reading is of union with a woman; the blue lady (நீல நிறனுடை நேரிழையாள்) is traditionally Shakti, or kundalini, and the embrace a yogic union. Both readings stand in the text. சதம் may mean 'lasting' or 'a hundred (years)'.

reading: If the cosmos contracts there is no ruin for it; if the body contracts the breath stays firm; if food is reduced there are many means; and one becomes the dark-throated Kapali.
nuance: அண்டம் and பிண்டம் are the cosmos and the body, the macrocosm and microcosm of yoga. 'Contracting' is unexplained: shrinking, withdrawal or restraint. The last line names Siva as Kapali (the skull-bearer with the dark throat); the yogi becoming him is the sense taken, though it could be the means being his.

reading: If one goes step by step through the cosmos to the back door set in the body, women with flower-decked hair that bees seek will look at it with desire: it becomes a fine body.
nuance: பிழக்கடை வாசல் (the back gate) is traditionally a passage of the yogic body, perhaps the rear channel up the spine; I can't fix it. The reward is outward beauty, desirable to women, which runs against the ascetic strain elsewhere in Tamil didactic verse.

reading: Before the torment of great, whirling Death rages, if you would see the anklet-bearing holy feet of the Lord who is in the burning blood and in the fire, there you can stand in the shade and in the clear.
nuance: அழலும் இரத்தம் and அங்கி (fire) are taken as the inner fire of the yogic body, where the Lord is seen. நிழலுளும் தெற்றுளும் is obscure: perhaps standing untouched in shade and in clear (light), or in any condition.

reading: The fire I saw, the four and seven kalas, the breath he saw with the whole body, and the awareness gained by seeing the flesh, taken as medicine: this is how the mango sapling stands and grows.
nuance: The list is compressed and its grammar uncertain. The mango sapling (மாங்கன்று) is an image of the body tended to grow, but how fire, kalas and breath make the medicine is not explained.

reading: If you take with love the Shakti of the arising Veda, with the straightness of rice as it grows, divide it into many crores of portions and be absorbed by the mantra that holds what is destined.
nuance: Nearly every phrase is obscure: சனவேத சத்தி (perhaps the Shakti of the arising Veda, perhaps a corrupt word), the rice image (the variant நீர்க்கொள நெல்லின், rice taking water, suggests growth fed by water), and ஊழ்கொண்ட மந்திரம். The reading is a guess at the words, not the sense.

title: கால சக்கரம்
theme: The wheel of time (கால சக்கரம்): a life is measured out in naazhigai, days, lunar mansions and years, and most people perish without noticing the measure run out. The yogi who rises along the inner staff to the crown outlasts these measures, escapes Yama, and finds the Lord within as the syllable Om and in the seven circles.
structure_note: Counts of time and life (740 to 747); the need for ordered practice and the fate of those who neglect it (748 to 753); the Dancer seen within and the long life it brings (754 to 759); those who never see, and the unpassing thing within the passing (760 to 762); the Lord within, reached as Om and in the seven circles (763 to 769).
source_issues: 747: line 3 பாரா திகணால் is obscure and may be corrupt.
749: line 2 இட்ஞ்சில் is a misprint, probably for இடிஞ்சில் (lamp bowl).
750: line 3 மூன்றுக்குன்ய் is garbled; variants நின்றிடில் and அணைந்திடும் for நின்றிடும்.
758: the variant கூடி for கோடி changes 'a crore of yugas' to 'joined with the age'.

reading: The nadis form a circle like the moon; taking up the twelve, I set out to examine how life is sustained standing within the Lord's circle and how the nectar slips away.
nuance: மதிவட்டம் (the moon's circle), பதிவட்டம் (the Lord's circle) and மது (honey, nectar) are yogic terms I can't fix; ஈராறு (twelve) may be the twelve signs of the time wheel or a count of breath. The plain frame is the poet announcing his inquiry into how life is kept and lost.

reading: Whatever people know by the five senses, by understanding, by learning and by mixing these, they perish without noticing the many naazhigai of their life being cut away.
nuance: The numbers (ஐந்து, ஆறேழு, எட்டு, ஒன்பது, பத்து) are attached to kinds of knowing and are traditionally taken as counts of the tattvas; I can't fix them. The last line is plain: the naazhigai, units of about twenty-four minutes, run out unnoticed.

reading: The years of a perishing life are counted in spans, twenty-five and three, thirty-three, sixty-two, and the hundred that rises beyond reckoning.
nuance: ஐயைஞ்சு மூன்று can be read as twenty-five and three or as twenty-eight; what each span measures (a lifetime, a stage, a breath count) is not said.

reading: Keeping to the right day and its days, knowing the days one, two, eight and three, and rising by entering into them, one may enter the house without distress.
nuance: மனை (house) may be a house of the zodiac, the body, or the inner seat the yogi reaches; the day numbers are not explained.

reading: Those who enter the house, bathing in the midst of Magam, reckon twenty-five and twelve; by that they know themselves and climb the eight, with six signs of their own, six of karma and the shining four.
nuance: மகம் is the lunar mansion Magha, but bathing there may be literal or a yogic figure. The verse is a list of counts whose scheme I can't recover.

reading: Beyond the four, the four beings and the twenty, beyond the ten and the fifteen, beyond forms and qualities and the six years, lies the one beyond the banyan: who knows it?
nuance: Each line passes beyond (கடந்தது) a number. ஆலம் may be the banyan, under which Siva teaches, or poison, which he swallowed; பாலம் (bridge) is also unclear. The movement, counting up to what has no count, is plain.

reading: Six for the twenty, five for the three, two, twenty-six, and twenty-seven for the one moon: so he ordained the days in another station.
nuance: Twenty-seven for the moon matches the twenty-seven lunar mansions. The other numbers, and who விதித்தான் (he who ordained) is, are not given; the Lord is the usual reading.

reading: The ordained twenty-eight, with three as a half, gathered make thirty-three; the eighteen set in place, and three, two and one rising in order, are to be known.
nuance: A count whose scheme I can't recover. பாரா திகணால் in line 3 is obscure.

reading: Unless one examines these orders step by step and practises, it is hard for anyone to remain even a little while; the scripture is the ground, there is no other, so complete it humbly, without beating a drum about it.
nuance: மறை may be the Veda or simply the hidden teaching. பறையறையாது (without beating the drum) is a plain instruction against proclaiming one's practice. இருக்க (to remain) is taken here as staying in the body.

reading: Fools strive without knowing the end; but for those able to catch the flame as it kindles, like a lamp burning in its bowl, the attainment may be reached even while walking the earth.
nuance: இட்ஞ்சில் is taken as இடிஞ்சில் (lamp bowl). கடிந்தனன் மூளக் கதுவ (to seize as it blazes) is obscure; the inner flame of yoga is the usual reading.

reading: With the little finger as a cord for the three, held at the chest without moving, and the three at the head joined together, one who contemplates perceives the picture.
nuance: This seems to describe a posture or a placing of the fingers, but I can't reconstruct it. ஓவியம் (picture) is taken up in 751 as an inner awareness.

reading: Know the awareness that has become this picture; sinners do not know its use; for the three mandalas, the meritorious staff rests in the flower.
nuance: தண்டு (staff) is traditionally the spinal channel, பூ (flower) a lotus centre, and the three மண்டலம் those of fire, sun and moon. A plain reading is not available.

reading: For the yogi who has run up the staff to the head, the three mandalas gladly accord with the body; those who saw it have seen, and those who did not, the fruit of their deeds, struggle when the body parts.
nuance: பிண்டம் பிரிய (when the body separates) is death; the contrast is between the yogi whose body is held in accord and those who die struggling. The variant மகிழ்ந்துடன் changes little.

reading: Hear what that struggle and ruin bring: when the sun with the goddess spreads through the six, the life that came with honour falls apart and goes whirling on, ending as food for dogs.
nuance: அணங்குடன் ஆதித்தன் ஆறு விரியின் is obscure. சுணங்கன் (dog) is plain: the neglected body ends as carrion.

reading: Whirling so, a person never sees the paired flowers and goes into the fire with nothing within; but for those who can see the way to the anklet-feet, the Dancer stands in the channel.
nuance: துணைமலர் (paired flowers) and கழல் (anklet) are usually the Lord's feet; தழல் (fire) is the cremation fire. குழல்வழி (the tube's way) is traditionally the central channel.

reading: Those who have seen many qualities in the Dancer's sign stand at the head of the sastras; if they look within for experience, the Lord too unfolds as one with them.
nuance: ஆத்தன் (the trusted one, the Lord) may be the Dancer or the seer who becomes like him. The contrast between knowing scripture and inner experience (அனுபோகம்) is the verse's turn.

reading: Hear now the unending growth in the one: the days go well for the three, and if one stays joined as the thirty pass, the Dancer gleaming like gold on the mountain appears.
nuance: The three and the thirty may be mandalas and days of practice; குன்றிடைப் பொன் (gold on the mountain) may be the crown of the head.

reading: Knowing the fine point where the Dancer unites, they praise him there; when in ten the eight directions appear and one gazes on the lotus with delight, a hundred years may be attained.
nuance: சாத்திடு நூறு (the hundred that is fixed) is taken as a hundred years of life; பதுமரை (lotus) as an inner centre. The numbers ten and eight are not explained.

reading: Those who have reached the hundred guard the body and see it held for a thousand; those who stay joined a thousand age on into a crore of yugas.
nuance: The plain claim is the long life of the yogi's body, rising in powers of ten. The variant கூடி for கோடி would change a crore of ages to 'joined with the age'.

reading: Seeing a crore of ages, they stand unwavering, see crores within without weariness, and staying close in Siva rise to the height.
nuance: சிவங்கோடி விட்டு is hard: 'leaving crores for Siva' or 'Siva's crores'. The variant அயர்வற (without weariness) is followed here.

reading: Of those who rise, many mingle with the world and take its fruits without knowing, and some act without a mind on it; they do not see the fish-eyed one.
nuance: கயலுறு கண்ணி (she with fish-like eyes) is usually the goddess, the Lord's Shakti. Whether உயருறுவார் are failed yogis or simply people who prosper is unclear.

reading: Those who do not see run off and pass away; the shameless talk pleasantly and let it go; and for those who do not see, all that has passed passes on unseen.
nuance: The verse repeats காணகிலாதார் (those who cannot see) to make blindness to passing time its subject; நயம்பேசி (talking nicely) may mean empty talk in place of practice.

reading: Those who cannot see the thing that passes away, yet that passing thing can be seen; and looking within the passing with the mind fixed, the thing that does not pass can be seen.
nuance: The verse plays on கழிகின்ற (passing) and கழியாத (unpassing). The passing thing may be the breath, time or the body; the unpassing one is usually the Lord or the self. The turn from one to the other is plain.

reading: The unborn one with the eye, seeing within as Nandi, becomes the solitary one in whatever direction one thinks of; this firm Siva-state is the station reached by those able to seek.
nuance: கண்ணன் is not Krishna here but is taken as the one with the (third) eye; காணந்தி may be காண் நந்தி (Nandi who sees). சிவகதி (the Siva-state) is plain.

reading: For those able to seek there is no Yama and no ruin; they stand as lords among men; this is the thing the seekers have discerned, and it may be told to those able to join it.
nuance: நமன் is Yama, death. நரபதி (lord of men) may be literal kingship or mastery; the verse doesn't say.

reading: What is spoken is A and U, what is grasped while it stays in the mind; when the spoken M runs along the tube, the Lord settles in the six.
nuance: அகார, உகார, மகாரம் are the parts of Om. குழல்வழி (the tube) is the central channel and ஆறு (six) probably the six centres; ஆறு may also mean the way.

reading: No one knows where the Lord dwells; for those who search it out he stays within without decay, and whoever sees the Lord becomes him.
nuance: அவன் இவன் ஆகுமே can be 'he becomes this one' or 'this one becomes him'; the identity of seer and Lord is the point either way, but how far it goes is the reader's theology.

reading: No one knows how he becomes this one; hear it: he unites in this one's sound and light, and stands as this one's circle.
nuance: ஓசை (sound) and ஒளி (light) are taken as nada and the inner light; வட்டம் (circle) links to the seven circles of 768.

reading: Seven circles blossom within you, yet you do not know how to reach the dwelling of the excellent one; staying attached within and learning the means, you can see his dwelling held firm.
nuance: The seven circles (வட்டங்கள் ஏழு) are often taken as the bodily centres; சிட்டன் is the excellent or holy one, the Lord. கட்டி (firmly, or a lump) is unclear.

reading: One can see Brahma and Hari, the dark-throated Lord Isa, Sadasiva and Shakti, and all of them set together.
nuance: The gods are the usual five presiding deities of the inner centres; the verse may mean they are seen within, in the circles of 768. கலந்துடன் வைத்ததே (what is set mingled together) is vague.

title: ஆயுள் பரிட்சை
theme: Testing the span of life (ஆயுள் பரிட்சை): signs of the body and counts of the breath on its days are said to tell how many years, months or days remain. Around the counts stand verses on the Lord found beyond sound, on watching the failing breath, and on knowing the knower, by which the bond loosens and grace is given.
structure_note: A bodily sign and the sound within (770, 771); watching the breath and its left and right courses (772, 773); a long run of number verses linking breath counts to remaining time (774 to 784); then the Lord who stands beyond karma, the knowledge no one has, and grace (785 to 789).
source_issues: 773: line 4 reads தலைவ நிடம், a misprint for தலைவ னிடம்.
775: variants (ஐயொன்பது, ஒன்பது, அன்பது) change the number in line 2.
776: the variant எண்முன்றினாலும் changes the number in line 2.
781: variants ஈராறாகும் and ஐந்திற் change the numbers.
783: the variant வகையான்ய் சமாதியில் is garbled.
787: உலகுயி ரத்தின் is obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: If the hand placed on the head appears straight, the span is six months; if the sign is doubled in excess, it is one month, and a sound is heard daily by the life.
nuance: The verse gives a test of the remaining span, but the sign (வைத்தகை சென்னியில் நேரிதாய்), உத்தமம் and மத்தம் can't be fixed; ஓசை (sound) may be an inner sound heard before death.

reading: Sound and the Lord are alike in awareness; those who have gone beyond sound contemplate the Lord, and the Lord in their heart is the awareness that has known the sound.
nuance: ஓசை is traditionally nada, the inner sound. The variant பிறந்தவர் (those in whom sound arose) reverses 'gone beyond sound' and changes the sense.

reading: If one watches the breath that is wasting away, it gives the good of our own dwelling, the teaching that dwells on the flower comes, and one becomes a master in the world.
nuance: அழிகின்ற வாயு is the breath spent with each moment. பூமேல் உறைகின்ற போதகம் (the knowledge dwelling on the flower) may be an inner lotus or a god seated on one; போதகம் can also mean an elephant.

reading: None master the Lord's left and right; if the left and right turn, it is the woman's; if they keep to their own way, five; if they keep to their own way, a hundred.
nuance: இடம் வலம் (left and right) are traditionally the breath in the left and right nostrils, and தலைவன் the breath or the Lord. தையல் (woman) and the numbers five and a hundred (perhaps years) can't be fixed.

reading: If the breath runs in the six that has risen, eighty go; reckoned by the seven, it is better; take the two that stand at sixteen, stand clear, and understand this kind.
nuance: A count whose scheme I can't recover; ஆறொருபத்து may be sixteen or six and ten.

reading: If these eight run to their place, that kind is known as fifty; if the nine stand together, the threefold is thirty-three.
nuance: The variants (ஐயொன்பது, ஒன்பது, அன்பது) change the number in line 2, so even the count is unsettled.

reading: If three threes and one stand to the end, three eights and four stand as places; if three fives run and stand apart, three and twelve can be seen.
nuance: The variant எண்முன்றினாலும் changes the number in line 2. What is counted is not said.

reading: If the day-breath runs thirty, the span can be seen; it can be made by putting twelve within; if it is one without refuge it can be sent off; the ten set right can be stored.
nuance: பகல் (day) may be the daytime or the right breath, traditionally called the sun. The verbs (see, make, send off, store) suggest the breath can be governed, but the scheme is unclear.

reading: If the breath runs properly on two days, the two fours stand without hostility; if the three stand clear to wane, the form can be measured as six.
nuance: ஏயிரு and பாயிரு are unclear; the units (days, months, years) are not given.

reading: If the four ways of measuring run on that path, one four stands true; if the five that shake run on the pure way, it can be seen in three without stain.
nuance: A count whose scheme I can't recover.

reading: If the intended ten run, it can be seen; the two mixed can be seen; three fives without mixing can be seen; the one can be seen with the mind fixed.
nuance: The refrain காணலுமாகும் (it can be seen) carries the verse. The variant கலப்புற மூவைந்தேழ் reverses 'without mixing' and adds a seven.

reading: Considered, in twenty it is six; in twenty-five it is three; in twenty-six it can be shown as two.
nuance: Possibly breath counts against remaining days or months. The variants ஈராறு (twelve for six) and ஐந்திற் (five for twenty-five) change the numbers.

reading: In twenty-seven it can be shown as one rising mingled; in twenty-eight it can be shown as ten.
nuance: The refrain காட்டலுமாகும் (it can be shown) continues 781's series; what is shown is not said.

reading: For ten, five, six and eight, the enemy that dreads the burden is ten days; if the weekly course is six and five, it is one day.
nuance: The series seems to narrow toward a single remaining day. The variant வகையான்ய் சமாதியில் is garbled but would bring in samadhi.

reading: If the joined days become thirty-one, the four become three; if the life goes and the four eights stand together, the measure in the house is two.
nuance: மனை (house) and மன்றியல்பு are unclear; மன்று may be the hall where the Lord dances.

reading: In the house it is one and three months, Nandi declared it as one in the spring; one who rises beyond karma and opens out into the clear space becomes the Lord who stands joined with himself.
nuance: சுனை (spring, pool) may be an inner centre. The second half turns from the counts to the yogi's goal: வினையற (with karma gone) and வெளிச்செய்து (making open, or entering the void).

reading: No one knows the fire that measures, no one knows the breath that measures, no one knows the thing that perishes; but I have come to know the knowing.
nuance: வன்னி (fire) and வாயு (breath) are the measurers of life the chapter has been counting. அறிவறிந்தேனே can be 'I knew by knowledge' or 'I knew the knower'.

reading: Knowing is with the breath and the five senses; if one searches within and keeps world and life from being parted, that knowledge stands dense and shines.
nuance: உலகுயிரத்தின் is obscure, taken here as உலகு உயிர் அதன்; பிறிவுசெய்யாவகை (so as not to part) may mean keeping life in the body.

reading: That gives grace, and the world is its grace; it graces those of renown in common every day; it gives the honey, the lady of the flower; this is the Lord who grants grace.
nuance: அது (that) may be the knowledge of 787 or the Lord. மலர் மங்கையர் செல்வி (the lady among flower-women) is taken as Lakshmi or as Shakti; மது (honey) may be bliss.

reading: Nandi, the great one who ordained birth, joined to his sign the fair hut of the body; for those who work so that the bond of the old dwelling, its attachment cut, gives way, understanding widens.
nuance: குரம்பை (hut) is a common figure for the body and பழப்பதி (the old town) may be the same body or the round of births. அழப்படி and அகலும் மதியே (the mind, or the moon, widens or departs) are hard.

title: வாரசரம்
theme: The breath by weekday (வாரசரம்): on each day of the week the breath should flow through the left or the right nostril, and the yogi who knows the rule, and turns the breath that runs against it, keeps the body sound and comes to bliss.
structure_note: The rule by day (790 to 792), the sun and moon in the two channels (793), what follows when the breath runs wrong (794, 795), and a closing verse tying breath, mind and the reckoning of days and hours (796).

reading: On Friday, Monday and Wednesday the breath runs on the left; on Saturday, Sunday and Tuesday on the right; on Thursday it runs on the left in the waxing fortnight and on the right in the waning.
nuance: The days are named by their planets: வெள்ளி Venus, திங்கள் the moon, புதன் Mercury, மந்தன் Saturn, இரவி the sun, செவ்வாய் Mars, and பொன் (gold) for Jupiter. Left and right are taken as the left and right nostril, the channels இடை and பிங்கலை of 793.

reading: If on Friday, Monday and Wednesday the breath moves steadily on the left, the bright body has no flaw: so the generous one gladly told us.
nuance: வள்ளல் (the generous one) is usually taken as Nandi, Tirumular's teacher. The promise is bodily health, not release.

reading: The yogi who knows Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday in this way is a lord; for those who know how to turn the breath that does not fit the day to the right, there is bliss.
nuance: Thursday is here simply a right-hand day, while 790 splits it by fortnight. ஒவ்வாத வாயு வலத்துப் புரியவிட்டு is read as redirecting a breath that runs on the wrong side; how this is done is not said.

reading: Moon and sun, alternating over the two fortnights, rise and fall through ida and pingala; life wells up in the middle between them: understand it, discern it and be clear.
nuance: Moon and sun are the traditional names of the left and right channels, and the middle is taken as சுழுமுனை (sushumna), which the verse does not name. உயிருக்கு இரந்து in line 3 is unclear.

reading: When the breath that has risen moves from the right side to the left, there is trembling, fear and going away; if the risen breath runs strongly, understand the sign in which it rose.
nuance: Line 2 is obscure and has variants (அதிற்கஞ்சி, அதிற்றுஞ்சி) that change it; it may name the bad results of a breath on the wrong side. இராசி is taken as the zodiac sign of the moment, which ties the breath to astrological reckoning.

reading: The wise one who joins the breath that will not keep to the middle but runs left and right and does harm, and leads it as it should go so that joy is gained, said there is something before the lamp that ends it.
nuance: அந்தணன் is taken as Siva or the teacher. முடிகின்ற தீபத்தின் முன்னுண்டு is obscure: perhaps a light at the crown, reached when the breath enters the middle channel.

reading: The thing to be searched out is above the adorned flower; the kinds of breath and their sixteen strengths, and the support that wrestles with the straying mind, become the day and the hour.
nuance: Almost every phrase is technical: அணிமலர் may be a lotus of the body, பதினாறு may be sixteen measures of breath, and ஆதாரம் a support centre. The last line seems to say the breath itself is the clock, but the reading is a guess. A variant reads முகுத்தமு.

title: வாரசூலம்
theme: The trident by weekday (வாரசூலம்): each day of the week has a direction in which the inauspicious trident stands, and a journey made with it behind or to the left brings no grief, while one made with it ahead or to the right brings trouble.

reading: Telling how the trident falls by weekday: on Monday and Saturday it is in the east, on Tuesday and Wednesday in the north, and on Sunday and Friday in the west.
nuance: சேய் (the red one) names Mars, so Tuesday, and பானு the sun, so Sunday. The rule is travel lore of the kind still printed in almanacs; the verse gives no reason for it.

reading: On Thursday it is in the south; if the trident is to the left or behind, there is no grief, but if it appears to the right or in front, trouble grows on trouble.
nuance: மிக்கது மேல்வினை மேன்மேல் விளையுமே could also be read as 'further deeds grow greater and greater', a good result; the contrast with துக்கமும் இல்லை favours the bad sense, as the rule is usually given.

title: கேசரி யோகம்
theme: Khechari yoga (கேசரி யோகம்): the tongue turned up into the palate and the breath held there make nectar flow from above, so that death, age and evil deeds lose their hold; the body becomes a lit temple where the Lord and Shakti dwell, and the yogi gains powers such as far sight.
structure_note: Sealing the body and turning the tongue up (799 to 809), the body as a temple and those who dwell in it (810 to 812), Shakti and the moon's kalas pouring nectar (813 to 816), raising and holding the breath (817 to 821), and far sight and the inner lamp (822 to 824). Many verses begin with the last word of the one before.
source_issues: 813: a variant replaces lines 2 and 3 with a garbled reading (W\ற்றைம்பதோ டொன்றாய்), apparently a different count.
815: line 4 reads கொழுந்தது வாகுண்- குணமது தனே, garbled.
821: the variant for line 2 is garbled (நலண்-கிடுண்- காமத்து நாடியி Wள்ளே).
822 lines 1 and 2 and 823 line 1 are marked corrupt and carry stray f characters; 823 line 2 கடைன்யான is garbled.

reading: So that nothing comes loose and drops down, bind the eight, bank the hearth, lock the crossbeam and fasten the upper bag at its stem; when one stays firm thus, there is no Yama.
nuance: The verse is a riddle in household words. அடுப்பு (hearth) is often taken as the fire at the base of the spine, மேற்பை (upper bag) as the head or the palate cavity, and what must not drop as the breath or the bindu; none of this is stated. The last line repeats 574.

reading: On the square plank where the washerman beats clothes, bank the edges so the channels do not leak, let the sky-river flow in and fill the tank, and on looking up one is free of dirt.
nuance: The plank is taken as the palate, the sky-river as the nectar from the head, and அண்ணாந்து பார்க்க (looking upward) as the upturned gaze or tongue. அழுக்கு may be bodily or the soul's impurity. Variants read விண்ணாற்றைத் தேக்கி and நிரப்பிட்டு.

reading: Those who exchange left hand and right and eat with the trunk need not grow weary; for those who can drive out sleep and stay aware, there is no need to die: they can remain.
nuance: Left and right hand are read as the two breaths, and துதிக்கை (an elephant's trunk) as the tongue turned back to 'eat' the nectar. The promise to stay without dying may be literal or may mean freedom from birth and death.

reading: If one practises with discernment, nectar wells up and stays; it speaks fittingly when its time comes; practised further it becomes the sphere of the moon, and flowing, it nourishes.
nuance: உரை செய்யில் recurs in each line and may mean 'practise' or 'utter', perhaps a mantra. The moon's sphere (நிலாமண்டலம்) is traditionally placed in the head as the source of nectar.

reading: If the tip of the tongue is pressed up into the middle, there the soul and Siva dwell; the three gods and the thirty-three appear, and the flesh does not die for a hundred crore of years.
nuance: நடுவே is taken as the cavity above the soft palate. சதகோடி யூனே is obscure; 'a hundred crore' may qualify the flesh's life or the gods. The verse places the soul and the Lord together in the body, as 725 does.

reading: On the peak of the high mountain where the body's juices flow, no one knows how the juice of the sky flows; for those who know it there is honey to drink, and clarity.
nuance: ஊனூறல் (flesh-juice) and வானூறல் (sky-juice) set bodily secretion against the nectar from above; the mountain peak is taken as the head. தெளியலு மாமே can mean 'one gains clarity' or 'one may drink it clear'.

reading: If the two breaths are set swiftly in the upper palate, there is no Death and the door opens; as the world sees, grey hair and wrinkles change and one becomes a child: by the command of supreme Nandi.
nuance: இரு கால் is read as the two breaths, and the door that opens as the opening at the crown. The last two lines repeat 734 almost word for word, where the means is union with a woman.

reading: Raising the tongue up, beginning from Nandi, and staying joined there, one rules the whole earth; those who sit thinking of the bound sun as outside them are doers of evil.
nuance: நந்தி முதலாக may mean 'with Nandi as the first' (invoking the teacher) or name a place in the body. Lines 3 and 4 are obscure; they may fault those who seek the light outside instead of within.

reading: Those who stood bewildered while evil deeds danced, if they seek the tongue, leave Yama no room; those who sought verse and saw its fruit through became sweet cane that danced the divine dance.
nuance: The rhymes நாவினை, பாவினை, தேவினை drive the verse more than its sense. பாவினை may be verse or sin; தீங்கரும்பு (sweet cane) sets up the next verse.

reading: Those whose practice is to make it sweet cane raise the tongue fully to its shoot there, and as they straighten the bent bud, the body's water comes rising like cane.
nuance: The cane image plays on கரும்பு and அரும்பு (bud). The bent thing straightened (கோணை நிமிர்த்திட) may be the curled tongue or the coiled kundalini; the verse does not say.

reading: Raise the tongue by the way of the body's water, drink the honey-water and say Sivaya nama; the way the breath's water comes will bring the Ganga: know well the way the sky's water comes.
nuance: சிவாய நம is the five-syllable mantra, here joined to the bodily practice. கானீர் is read as கால் நீர், water of the breath, and the Ganga as the nectar descending as it falls on Siva's head.

reading: For those who know it rightly and worship within, grace pours down as purified knowledge; entering and closing one door of the steps, knowing it within, the place of his dwelling becomes a temple.
nuance: Worship is moved inside the body. காய்ந்தறிவாக may mean knowledge burnt clean of impurity. The door (படிக்கதவு) recurs in 820; a variant reads கோய்ந்தறிந்.

reading: Those who make their home inside the temple are better than a mother to the whole world, good as ripe fruit even among those who are hostile to them, and worse than fire to doers of evil.
nuance: காயினும் நல்லவர் plays on காய் (unripe fruit, or to burn with anger): they are good even when bitter, or good even to those who burn against them. The verse makes the inward yogi a moral presence in the world, gentle and severe by turns.

reading: He is on the heads of the doers of evil, the golden abode of those who worship with flowers, within the devotion of those who sing verse, and in the minds of those of great deeds.
nuance: சென்னியிலுள்ளவன் (on the head) may mean he stands over evildoers as their judge, or that he is present even in them. பாகவத்து and மதி (mind or moon) can each be read more than one way.

reading: Like rays rising from the moon he is sixteen, and in the lord's house a hundred and a hundred and twenty-four; spreading his arrows within the house of motion, he remained without opposing.
nuance: The sixteen are taken as the moon's kalas; the other numbers and the houses (பதிமனை, கதிமனை) have no fixed reading. A variant replaces lines 2 and 3 with a different count.

reading: Shakti sat with those kalas around her; the maiden sat in their midst; she sat with a deer-like face shining like the moon; she sat pouring nectar.
nuance: கன்னி (the maiden) is a name of Shakti. The kalas are those of 813, so she is the moon in the head from which nectar flows. இருந்தனள் opens every line.

reading: The two silvers poured into the golden earthen enclosure flowed down and stayed within, beginning from the sky; for those who can guard what has gone so that it does not leave, it becomes a shoot.
nuance: Silver (வெள்ளி) is traditionally read as the white bindu or the nectar, and gold as the body or Shakti, as in the alchemical language of 834. The last line is garbled.

reading: When the tender creeper who is that quality stays there gladly as fragrance, the knowledge of the tattvas, which is wealth, stays with him as kin.
nuance: கோமளவல்லி (tender creeper) is a name of Shakti. Who 'he' is in இருந்தனன் is not said: the Lord or the yogi.

reading: The breath that rested will rise within; as this staff and the cosmos above are joined, if one makes it rise with that blossomed flower, the circle blossoms and one may live.
nuance: தண்டு (staff) is taken as the spine and அண்டம் as the head; the flower and the மண்டலம் may be a centre of the body. பரிந்த and பரிய are unclear.

reading: Seeing the mind's girdle within the circle, binding it below with intent, so that daylight shines in the vessel within, the one with ear-rings ceased his dance.
nuance: ஒட்டியாணம் (girdle) may point to the abdominal lock of hatha yoga (uddiyana). குண்டலக் காதன் (the one with ear-rings) is usually Siva, and his ceasing to dance is read as the stilling of movement; it may also be the jiva.

reading: The breath that is passing away will settle within, and the breath that is going out can be guarded; when it flows, at the time it scorns the round anklet, drive off the bag.
nuance: Lines 1 and 2 are plain; lines 3 and 4 are not. வட்டக் கழல் (round anklet) may be Siva's feet, and பை (bag) the body or a sheath.

reading: If one door of the steps is closed inside the bag, light will shine within the body; if the breath rises swiftly there, the temple daubed with black becomes lit with a gem lamp.
nuance: பை (bag) and மையணி கோயில் (a temple smeared dark, perhaps with soot) are read as the body, which held breath turns into a lamp-lit shrine. Which door is closed is not said.

reading: Willing the shining breath to rise, within the navel and in the throat where it is pressed, holding it so that the revered circle is gained, one can tell of what stood withering.
nuance: கும்பி is read as கும்பகம், holding the breath. A variant replaces line 2 with one naming காமம் and நாடி. The last line is unclear.

reading: One can speak of the breath and the sky, and of the hardness of earth and water; when these five come together, one can speak of seeing far.
nuance: The five are taken as the elements (earth, water, fire implied, air, sky). தூர தெரிசனம் (far sight) is one of the yogic powers. Lines 1 and 2 are marked corrupt in the source.

reading: I shall tell of far sight, and it can be seen: placing the dark-eyed one within in meditation and setting the mind on the lovely lamp, the whole earth is before one as in daylight.
nuance: காராருங் கண்ணி (the one with dark eyes) is taken as Shakti, and கடைன்யானம் as a garbled கடை தியானம் or ஞானம். Line 1 is marked corrupt.

reading: Twelve finger-breadths below the navel that rises first there is, they say, the daylight of the many Vedas; set a good lamp in the rising nada there and one becomes lord of the temple that arises in oneself.
nuance: முந்நால் (three fours) is read as twelve; whether the place is below or above the navel depends on how முன்னெழு and கீழே are taken. The body as a temple that rises within closes the chapter.

title: பரியண்-க யோகம்
theme: Paryanka yoga (பரியங்க யோகம், the yoga of the couch): sexual union of man and woman made a discipline, in which the breath is held and the bindu, the 'silver', is not let fall, so that union yields bliss, mastery and long life; Siva himself is its first practitioner. The chapter ends in the space, the light and the rootless lotus known within.
structure_note: Preparing and entering the union (825 to 828), mastery and the five nazhigai (829 to 832), the age, the bliss and the guarded silver told in the language of planets and goldsmiths (833 to 837), the fire, the space and the light (838 to 840), and long life and the rootless lotus (841 to 844). Many verses begin with the last word of the one before.
source_issues: 825: line 2 is marked corrupt (stray f after மாலையுஞ்); the last word has variants யோகமே, போதமே, மோகமே that change the sense.
833: line 4 is garbled (சித்தமுன்ய்).
Chapter title reads பரியண்-க யோகம், a garbled பரியங்க யோகம் (the verses spell it correctly).

reading: Having anointed with all the unguents, dried and dressed her fragrant hair with garlands, uniting in embrace with the woman so that the needle's eye is reached, the enjoyment is one without sleep.
nuance: ஊசித் துளை (the needle's eye) is taken as the opening of the central channel, and தூங்காது (without sleeping, or without slackening) as the alertness of the practice. The last word has variants (யோகமே, போதமே, மோகமே) that turn the line toward yoga, knowledge or passion; line 2 is marked corrupt.

reading: When the enjoyment is willed, the breath does not leave and the silver turns back from passion at Jupiter; the woman with soft breasts like dice-boxes and the good man melted together in the essence and reached the head.
nuance: வெள்ளி (silver, also Venus) is traditionally the semen and வியாழம் (Jupiter, also gold) the point of return; the planet names do double duty as code. சூதன் may mean the man or mercury, the alchemist's metal. தலைகண்ட is read as the essence rising to the head.

reading: In the yoga where man and woman love, holding the circle, both stand out on either side; taking up the cart and rolling the sky's water, the staff and the limbs never once slacken.
nuance: வண்டி (cart), வானீர் (sky-water) and தண்டு (staff, the spine or the organ) are figures with no fixed reading. The plain claim is that the practice does not weaken the body.

reading: In the union of bodies, the tattva that forms, the bindu that comes in the enjoyment within the body: guarding it so that it is not spoiled, holding oneself and giving, one becomes lord.
nuance: பங்கப்படாமல் பரிகரித்து (guarding so it is not ruined) is taken as keeping the bindu from being lost. தங்கிக் கொடுக்க (staying and giving) is unclear: perhaps restraint on one side and pleasure given on the other.

reading: He becomes lord: knowledge goes his way, enjoyment goes his way, what is within goes his way, the five go his way.
nuance: தன்வழி can mean 'under his own control' or 'by his own path'; the five are taken as the senses. The verse makes mastery, not pleasure, the fruit of the practice.

reading: Past five nazhigai, in the sixth, when the two fall still together and the wife's heart toward her husband is so full that she says her mouth cannot hold it: the five nazhigai are paryanka yoga.
nuance: A நாழிகை is twenty-four minutes, so five is two hours. துஞ்சுவது ஒன்ற is read as the two coming to stillness together. A variant swaps மேல் and இல், which changes which nazhigai is meant.

reading: Except for those who have reached this rare yoga of the five nazhigai, no man can strip and embrace the woman with bangles on her forearm and sandal on her breasts.
nuance: ஒண்ணாதே may be 'cannot' (it is beyond them) or 'must not' (it is forbidden them). Either way the union is restricted to the adept, not offered to all.

reading: If you ask who has attained this impossible yoga: he who set the sky's Ganga in his spread locks sat steady in the five nazhigai, holding the melodious nectar in mind.
nuance: Siva, the Ganga-bearer, is made the model practitioner, joined with Shakti. எண்ணா மென எண்ணி is obscure.

reading: At the fitting ages of twenty and thirty there is bliss for the woman and for the man; as the five blossom with the woman the mind slackened, but there is no slackening of the silver.
nuance: The ages are usually taken as twenty for the woman and thirty for the man. மன்னர் (kings) stands for the men. The contrast is that the mind may give way in pleasure while the bindu is held. Line 4 is garbled (சித்தமுன்ய்).

reading: So that the silver does not melt and run off by the path of the gold, the cunning goldsmiths covered it with charcoal; as the brand was pulled away they went by the tube and held it fast in Valli's tongue.
nuance: Goldsmith's craft stands for the practice: silver as bindu, gold as the woman's part or the body, the tube (குழல்) as a channel. கள்ளத் தட்டார் (thieving goldsmiths) may praise their cunning. வள்ளியுண் ணாவில் has no settled reading; it may be the tongue of the fire.

reading: The two who set it there, rejoicing in each other with minds undisturbed, make a bliss; for the ten kinds and the eighteen hosts the burning sun stands as the master.
nuance: The ten kinds may be the ten breaths and the eighteen கணம் the classes of celestial beings. The sun (வெங்கதிரோன்) may be the right-hand breath or Siva. Line 1 is clear; the rest is not.

reading: For the man who embraced the woman standing between the hot sun and Saturn there is a bliss; before the silver sank into the gold between them, they hid Mars between them.
nuance: Planet names again stand for bodily things: செவ்வாய் (Mars, the red one) may be the red essence, sun and Saturn the channels or body points. A variant ends புதனிருந் தானே. No reading is secure.

reading: For those who keep Mercury corrected, if they stay mingled with the beauty of intent, there is no strain even for the one who shares himself with a woman, and the silver in the bellows rises without flagging.
nuance: புதன் (Mercury) may also be mercury the metal, as in alchemy. மங்கை பங்கன் (he who shares himself with a woman) is a name of Siva, here perhaps the practitioner. துருத்தி (bellows) is taken as the lungs or the body.

reading: If the rising fire is led on ahead, it truly works on the body as melting does on wax; after one knows the mother there is no more toil, and for those who know the space there is no falling.
nuance: ஔயை is read as அவ்வை, the mother, Shakti. Falling (விழுகின்றது) may be the fall of the bindu or the fall into birth; வெளி (the open space) is taken as the void known in the head or the space of awareness.

reading: Knowing the space and, in the middle of the space, knowing the light, the chisel does not break; knowing clarity through gracious Nandi, I knew the space, and beyond that I know nothing.
nuance: உளிமுறியாமே (the chisel will not break) is obscure, and a variant reads உளியை. மேலறியேனே can mean 'I know nothing more' in humility or 'there is nothing beyond to know'.

reading: If you ask who spread out in the high place: Mal, the four-faced one and great Nandi; that thing in the middle of the four grounds they explained above to the woman with a lightning-thin waist.
nuance: The four grounds (நாலா நிலம்) may be centres of the body or levels of being. மின்னிடையாள் is usually Shakti. The verse ties the teaching to the gods, but its sense is unsure.

reading: If, in the union of the lightning-waisted woman and her man, they pour it into the golden circle and can join self with self, one may live on earth for many ages.
nuance: பொன்னிடை வட்டம் (the golden circle) is unexplained. தன்னொடு தன்னை தலைப்பெய்ய (to join self with self) may be the self reaching itself or the two partners becoming one. A variant reads வல்லீரே, addressing the reader.

reading: No one knows the skill of drawing it up so that it swells, at the drawing's end; those who know that skill raised themselves on high.
nuance: வாங்கல் (drawing in) may be drawing up the bindu or the breath. உதம் is obscure; it is read here as rising. The verse is a riddle and this reading is a guess.

reading: Knowing the rising, if one is caught there in a whirl, and knowing the fury there, the skull grows dark; one woman who knows the good stays always, and knowing the moment, she drove off the world within you.
nuance: சுழி (whirl) and கபாலம் கறுக்கும் (the skull darkens) may warn of danger in the practice. ஒருத்தி (one woman) is taken as Shakti. பார்க்கடிந்தாளே may mean she removed the world or she guarded you; the reading is unsure.

reading: There is no earth and no water, yet there is a lotus; no stalk, no root, yet the lotus bloomed; there is no town, yet there is a light one sees; no below and no above: it is a flower in hearing.
nuance: A riddle of negatives: a lotus without ground, water or root, taken as the lotus of the crown or of awareness. கேள்வியிற் பூ may be 'a flower known by hearing', from the teacher, or a flower in the sound of nada. A variant reads ஒன்றில்லை.

title: அமுரிதாரணை
theme: Amuri dharana (அமுரிதாரணை): a water held within the body, called the drinking-water of strength and Siva-water, is praised as a medicine without rival. Drunk, alone or with pepper, gooseberry, turmeric and neem, it is said to make the body golden and supple, restore the hair, end grey hair and wrinkles and keep Yama away; Nandi taught it as a medicine of light that cannot be told.
structure_note: The water is introduced (845), its effects on body and mind praised (846 to 849), and its names and source in Nandi's teaching given last (850). The verses never name the water plainly; they call it குடிநீர், சிவநீர், சிவத்தின் நீர் and கானல் உவரி.

reading: The strengthening water that lies in the body is like a well-sweep set to draw from the sea; if one draws it by the one way in the body for the one purpose, life is spared distress and can seek its end.
nuance: அமுரி in the title is commonly taken as the body's own urine, and the chapter as a teaching on drinking it (amaroli); some readers take the water symbolically as the nectar of yoga. The sea and small well-sweep may mean the supply is ample beside the small draw, but the image is not explained. ஒருவழி ஒன்றுக்கு (one way, for one thing) is compressed, and உயிர் நாடலும் may mean 'life can seek' or 'one can attain life'.

reading: If one drinks this clarifying Siva-water, within a year the body shines without any defect; with breath held in the eight the mind too subsides, and the body, giving joy, becomes gold.
nuance: சிவநீர் (Siva-water) is the chapter's reverent name for the water. வளியுறும் எட்டின் is obscure: the eight may be the eight limbs of yoga or a measure of breath. காயம் கனகம் (the body as gold) is the alchemists' image of the perfected, undecaying body.

reading: Siva's water taken with a hundred peppercorns has no medicine to rival it; if people understand it and apply it to the crown of the head, the hair changes and grows anew.
nuance: மாறும் opens two lines in different senses: a rival (no medicine rivals this) and change (the hair changes). நுகரும் may mean the water is drunk with the pepper or that pepper is steeped in it; the verse doesn't say which. மறுமயிர் is read as new hair.

reading: Witless people say the salt water of the shore, near the bank, is to be avoided; for those who can drink it with the froth and scum removed, grey hair and wrinkles change, and Yama is not there either.
nuance: கானல் உவரி (brackish water of the shore) is taken as the same water under a disguising name; வரைவரை is read as 'avoid it, avoid it'. நரைதிரை (grey hair and wrinkles) and நமன் (Yama) make the promise one of youth and deathlessness, as in the body-perfecting chapters of this tantra.

reading: O you with curling hair and fair forehead, a wonder: if pepper, gooseberry, turmeric and neem are put into this water mixed with the hidden body, the body grows supple and the head grows dark.
nuance: The address to a woman (அளக நன்னுதலாய்) is taken in the tradition as Siva speaking to Shakti, or as a conventional address. களவு காயம் is obscure: காயம் may be the body or a spice such as asafoetida, and களவு 'hidden' or a corrupt word. இருளும் கபாலம் (the skull darkens) is read as the hair turning black. A variant gives இளகிடு for இளகும், with no change of sense.

reading: Nandi in his grace called it the hero's medicine, the gods' medicine and the woman's medicine; those who know it as the primal medicine know that across the wide earth this medicine of light cannot be told.
nuance: The names are given without explanation; நாரி மருந்து (woman's medicine) is unclear, perhaps tied to Shakti. The closing line can mean the medicine is too great for words or that it is not to be told openly, a secret teaching; both stand.

title: சந்திர யோகம்
theme: Moon yoga (சந்திர யோகம்): the body holds the kalas of moon, sun and fire, which with the stars make ninety-six, and the inner moon waxes and wanes as the outer one does. By knowing the fortnights, setting the breaths of sun and moon, joining moon, sun and fire, raising the power from the base through the central channel to the head and keeping bindu, the yogi gains bliss, an unharmed body and freedom from Yama.
structure_note: The kalas are counted first (851 to 860): moon sixteen, sun twelve, fire ten in 852 but sixty-four in 854 to 856, where with four of the stars they total ninety-six, and the nine of elements, lights and star are called the pranava. The middle verses join the three lights and the breaths (861 to 870), then come the serpent and moon (871), a regimen of sleep and food keyed to the moon (872 to 875), and the keeping of bindu, breath and nectar with their fruits (876 to 883). Much of the text is obscure and some lines look corrupt.
source_issues: 860 line 4 (தானான்ய்) and 872 line 4 (மேவுன்ய்) have encoding slips, read as தானாம் and மேவும்.
871 line 4 (நீண்-கல் கொடானே), 874 line 4 (தாழவல் லார்.க் இச்) and 881 lines 3 to 4 (தண்டோ ட்டி, நமன்இகில்லை, நாளனஇல்லை) are garbled in the text.
855: அனிலின் (of the wind) is read as அனலின் (of fire), to agree with 854 and 856.
852 gives fire ten kalas, while 854 to 856 give sixty-four.
853 line 2 and 868 line 4 are obscure and may be corrupt.
863: variants கருக்குழி and கழுக்குறி for கருத்துழி; 869: variants change lines 2 to 4; 883: variant மதியும் ஆதித்தனும் for the unclear மதித்திரு. Each changes the sense.

reading: As the moon's kalas rise and fall through the two fortnights, so the body, pure in its subtle and its gross form, climbs from the subtle into the gross.
nuance: மதிக்கலை (the moon's digits) sets the chapter's frame: an inner moon in the body that waxes and wanes like the outer one. How the subtle and gross bodies follow the moon is not explained. A variant reads மதிநிலை for மதிக்கலை.

reading: The kalas that arise in moon, sun and fire, sixteen, twelve and ten, all go by the middle way; this is the knowledge known to the yogi who comes to be.
nuance: இடைவழி may be 'the middle way' (the central channel) or the இடை (ida) channel. Fire is given ten kalas here, but sixty-four in 854 to 856; the two counts are not reconciled.

reading: Sun and moon have kalas that never cease; when fire joins, the unchanging sun takes in all the sixteen kalas of fulfilment through the great breath.
nuance: Line 2 (நாறா நலங்கினார் ஞாலங் கவர்க்கொள) I can't construe, and the rest is read only roughly. பெருங்கால் is taken as the great breath.

reading: The sun's high kalas are ten and two, the moon's ten and six, and fitting fire's eight eights; examine how they stand.
nuance: Twelve, sixteen and sixty-four, stated as sums and products in the manner of the chapter. The verse only counts; what the kalas are is left to the teacher.

reading: Fire's kalas are eight eights, the kalas round the sun are counted as twelve, and the moon's are bound at sixteen; these are not merged, yet each is joined with the other.
nuance: அனிலின் (of the wind) is read as அனலின் (of fire), to agree with 854 and 856. The last line, distinct yet one with another, is compressed.

reading: Fire's sixty-four, the sun's twelve and the moon's sixteen are the kalas, and with the four rays of the stars the kalas bound together number ninety-six.
nuance: 64 + 12 + 16 + 4 = 96. Ninety-six is also the number of tattvas in some Tamil Saiva lists, which may be why the total is stated, but the verse does not make that link. A variant reads ஈரெட்டுத் for ஈரெட்டும்.

reading: All the kalas run in ida and pingala, and through the unnamed middle channel between them; rousing the base and joining it with the head, the good attain the holy feet and stand there.
nuance: இடை, பிங்கலை and the சொல்லா நடுநாடி (the middle channel not named, taken as sushumna) are the three main nadis. மூலம் is the base centre; rousing it to the head is the traditional account of the kundalini's ascent, though the verse does not name the power.

reading: In fire, the two small rays, sun and moon, with the star that stays in their play, become the light of the supreme power, which dwells as the nine wheels for the world.
nuance: பரையொளி (Para's light) and நவசக்ரம் (nine wheels) are technical; the nine are perhaps those listed in 859. The syntax is loose and the reading is a guess at the joints.

reading: Earth, water, fire, air and fitting space, the guarding sun, the rare moon, fire and the contrary star: these nine become the pranava, the great way.
nuance: Five elements, three lights and the star make nine, and the nine are said to be Om. The verse names them; it does not say how they make the syllable. முரணிய (contrary, opposed) of the star is unexplained.

reading: The star shines in the fortnight when the moon wanes and does not shine in the fortnight when it waxes; the star is all the wombs on earth, and the star within the star is one's own true form.
nuance: தாரகை can mean a star, the pupil of the eye, or (as tāraka) the mantra that carries one across, traditionally Om; each fits a different line. The last line, the star of the star as one's own form (சொரூபம்), moves from the sky to the self. தானான்ய் is an encoding slip for தானாம்.

reading: In the first fifteen days it sprouts and grows, in the latter fifteen, having grown, it shrinks; for those who can know those fifteen, reaching the feet beyond words becomes possible.
nuance: Plainly the moon's two fortnights; in the chapter they are the waxing and waning of the inner moon, which the yogi must learn. The verse does not name what grows and shrinks.

reading: Rousing the fire and feeding the rare sun, with the moon that stays the garlands become five and five, and as the senses' going ceases at the swelling star, this is the yoga that joins moon, sun and fire.
nuance: தாமம் ஐந்தைந்து (five and five garlands, or abodes) is obscure. The clear claim is the last line: the yoga of the chapter is the joining of the three lights, and it stops the senses' outward going.

reading: Though they see the sixteen kalas joined and abiding in the body, the base do not think of it; once harsh Death has set them where he means, they fall into it and their bewilderment does not end.
nuance: நீதர் is read as நீசர் (base men). For கருத்துழி (the place he intends) variants give கருக்குழி (the womb's pit), which would make the fall a rebirth, and கழுக்குறி.

reading: When fire joins the moon, the sun's light arises; when fire joins the sun, the moon's light; when fire, moon and sun join, that star arises, and what abides there becomes everything.
nuance: A symmetrical riddle of the three lights; the joining of all three yields the star, which elsewhere in the chapter is one's own form (860). A variant gives சிவத்தினிற் in the last line, which would place what abides in Siva.

reading: Entering without straying, seizing the twelve female kalas and the sixteen male kalas and bringing them, if one pours them into the fire that appears straight ahead, insatiable bliss becomes bliss itself.
nuance: Twelve and sixteen are the sun's and moon's counts from 854, but here twelve are called female and sixteen male, the reverse of the common pairing of moon with the female; the verse does not explain. The pouring into fire borrows the language of the fire rite for an inner act.

reading: Set the breath of the visible sun on the left and the breath of the great moon on the right; if you do this with care and without error, the axle-pin will not shake for a thousand years.
nuance: காலை may be கால் (breath) with the object ending, or 'morning'. The sun's breath usually runs on the right and the moon's on the left, so the verse prescribes a reversal, as tradition reads it. ஆணி (the axle-pin) is taken as the body or life that holds.

reading: The nourishing heart resounds with the drum's sound in the nine; there the Supreme of the gods stands as lamplight before what is above, and for the dawn the sun itself is the conch.
nuance: The inner sounds heard in yoga are often listed as drum, conch and others. ஒன்பது may be the nine gates or nine sounds. A variant gives பரையோசை (the sound of Para) for பறையோசை (the drum's sound).

reading: Sun and moon measure time; within the covering the pouring rain stays; when it thunders and presses beyond the shell of the cosmos, that is the place of the Lord.
nuance: பொதிரவன், அதிரவன் and the last line (எதிரவ நீச நிடமது) look like puns on ரவம் (sound) and may be corrupt; ஈசன் இடம் is read from நீச நிடம். The inner rain is often taken as the nectar of yoga and the thunder as nada.

reading: No one knows the mantra that meets the light rising from the navel lotus; once they know that mantra, the son is born before the father.
nuance: அந்திக்கும் (meets, joins) also echoes அந்தி, the twilight rite. The son born before the father is a riddle of reversal that the verse doesn't solve, and I can't fix whom they stand for. Variants change lines 2 and 3 to 'they did not know by knowledge how it met' and the end to மகன் இருந்தானே (the son was there).

reading: Even when they speak they know no gain, and even having recited they are mutes who know nothing; if you can join the beginning and the end, the Lord of the Veda will appear there.
nuance: அந்திக்க plays on the twilight worship at dawn and dusk (சந்தி) and an inner joining of beginning and end, perhaps of the breaths or of the moon's course; the verse sets recitation against this inner act. வேதியன் may be the Lord of the Veda or a true Brahmin.

reading: The serpent seeks to devour the moon, and the sun's light seeks to burn the serpent; the great one, ending the enmity of serpent and moon and holding them together, will not let them part.
nuance: The eclipse serpent swallowing the moon is turned inward: the serpent is traditionally the kundalini and the moon the moon in the head. Line 2 and line 4 (நீண்-கல் கொடானே) are corrupt or obscure, and the variants (துடங்கொளின், கொடானெம்) make the great one either the Lord or the yogi who does this.
