reading: Not sleeping until what was eaten has settled, sleeping when the practised moon goes down, and carrying within the good fullness, the wondrous fullness reaches the moon.
nuance: A regimen of sleep and food. Whether the moon is the outer moon or the inner one, and பூரணை the full moon or the filling of breath, both readings stand. மேவுன்ய் is an encoding slip, read as மேவும்.

reading: Not sleeping until the moon rises; when the moon has risen, eating one's food; not sleeping while the moon moves across; and sleeping once the moon has gone down.
nuance: The rule is clear in outline, but again the moon may be outer or inner. பிங்கட்டன் in the last line is obscure; a variant reads பிங்கட் டன்றுயில்.

reading: Yogis who stay unparted through the aeon measure Yama by the nazhigai; they rise in the world as first of the aeon, and those able to humble themselves become of the moon's hue.
nuance: நாழிகையாக நமனை அளப்பர் may mean they count Death's span as a mere nazhigai (twenty-four minutes), or that they hold Death by measured time. Line 4 is corrupt (தாழவல் லார்.க் இச்); a variant reads இன் வழிச் சைவராமே, 'become Saivas of this way'.

reading: As the cool moon and the sun move over the earth, one sees the way of earth's and moon's three times; after it ripens on the day the white moon appears, there is not a moment until the cool moon sets.
nuance: The verse is too compressed for a firm reading. கணம் இன்று may mean 'not a moment is lost' or 'no moment of waking', continuing 873.

reading: Who knows how the six kalas of the growing sun and the six of the waning moon blossom, run twelve finger-breadths, and opening out, fall?
nuance: Twelve finger-breadths (பன்னிரண்டு அங்குலம்) is the traditional reach of the out-breath from the nostrils, so the verse is read of the breath, but it does not name it. A variant line 3 (மலர்ந்தேறு பன்னிரண்டோடு எட்டு நாலாம்) changes the count.

reading: Though one says the waning moon's day is life's, for the yogi bindu does not go out by its way anywhere; free of desire, it is bound at the base, through awareness of the word set within the moon of Om.
nuance: Line 1 and line 4 (ஓமதியத்துள் விட்டு உரையுணர்வாலே) are obscure; ஓமதி may be ஓம் with மதி (moon) or ஓமம் (fire rite). The clear claim is the middle: the yogi's bindu does not leave, because desire is absent and it is held at the base.

reading: Joined with the six true kalas of the red sun and the four, the endless one's kalas, with ten, stand closely joined; considered, they pass into the six inner kalas.
nuance: Nearly every word is technical or doubtful (சூறுற, ஈறிலி நங்கலை, அகலுவா); the reading only follows the numbers. No firm sense can be fixed.

reading: Knowing bindu, in union with the blood, is cast forth, and the united bindu wanes in the rays it casts; if awareness and body stand matched, awareness and body never once leave each other.
nuance: சோணி (shonita, the female blood) paired with bindu is the old account of conception. The first two lines are compressed; the last two are clear: when awareness and body are kept in balance they do not part, which is to say death does not come.

reading: The unwavering mind, joined with the breath and hooked to the sound of Siva's sounding conch, binds the five senses that no longer drive it: that is release, and they drink nectar, a joy that does not fade.
nuance: பவனம் is the breath, and the conch's sound one of the inner nadas. பருகார் may be 'those who drink' or 'they do not drink'; the second would make the last line a reproach to those who do not do this, and both readings stand.

reading: On the bank of the river where the nectar-water comes, gathering the five lights in the bubble and driving them through the staff, those able to hold them have no Yama, and their good kalas have no ending day.
nuance: தண்டு (the staff) is taken as the spine and its central channel, and the nectar as what flows from the moon in the head. குமிழி (the bubble) and the five lights are not explained. The line is garbled in the text (தண்டோ ட்டி, நமன்இகில்லை, நாளனஇல்லை).

reading: Opening the spring of nectar-water within and sending the clear water to the lotus of the two feet, settled in the samadhi of clear water, unending good goes on by the eye's stream and the breath's course changes.
nuance: இணையடித் தாமரை (the lotus of the two feet) is the Lord's feet, here perhaps placed in the head. கண்ணாற்றொடே (by the eye's stream) is obscure; கால்வழி மாறும் is read as the breath's course changing, as in yogic stilling of the breath.

reading: If the moon and its partner, unchanging and without disorder, reach the head by the staff, the body comes to no harm, the means one seeks is won, and a joy that does not decay wells up on earth.
nuance: The variant மதியும் ஆதித்தனும் மாறின்றி (moon and sun without exchange) makes the partner the sun; the printed line (மதித்திரு) is unclear. The end, joy here on earth (பார்மிசை), not only after death, fits the tantra's aim of a perfected body.

title: அசபை
theme: Under the heading Ajapa, the chapter praises the one letter and the five letters (சிவாயநம in its several orders) as the sound-form of Siva's dance in the golden hall: the dance, the letters and the mantra are one, Siva's body is mantra, and chanting the letters by the drawn chakra ends birth, removes the bonds, yields powers and turns copper to gold.
structure_note: Most verses open with the last word of the one before (அந்தாதி). After an invocation (884) and the letters as the source of the world (885), the chapter names the hall and its dance (886 to 897), counts the letters and mantras (898 to 900), returns to the dance (901 to 903), gives the chakra and the chanting with its fruits (904 to 909), and ends with seed syllables and orders of the five letters (910 to 912) and a numbered dance (913). The heading அசபை (the mantra that is not spoken aloud) is not named in any verse.
source_issues: 888 line 3: கூத்துததனிநின்ற is a misprint for கூத்துத் தனிநின்ற.
890 is obscure throughout (மூலை, வெப்பு, வாசிய, தயாவாசி); it may be corrupt.
899: the numbers (seven thousand, twenty, thirty, seven crores, seven and two) cannot be reconciled as printed.
911 line 2: மிகார விகாரியாம் is obscure and may be corrupt.
912 varies between சிவாய நம and சிவயநம and between ஈ and இ; line 1 நமமசி வாயிடும் looks like a misprint for நமசிவாய ஆயிடும். These may be scribal variants or deliberate orderings.
913 line 4: ஆடனான் is likely an error for ஆடினான்.
The heading அசபை (the unspoken mantra) is not named in these verses, which concern the dance and the five letters; the heading may belong to a section the edition's divisions have shifted.

reading: I praise and extol the knowledge I take refuge in, I settle in my mind the red feet of the Lord, I proclaim Siva-yoga, and I raise up our Lord, the one letter.
nuance: ஓர் எழுத்து (the one letter) is traditionally Om, or the syllable சி as Siva; the verse doesn't say which. அறையோ can be a call to listen ('hear this') rather than 'I proclaim'.

reading: By one letter he became everything in the world, by two letters he joined there as two, by three letters the light springs up, and by the great letter delusion came.
nuance: A traditional key: one letter is Om or சி, two letters சிவ as Siva and Shakti, three letters அ, உ, ம of Om. மாவெழுத்து (the great letter, or the letter ம) is taken as the ம of நமசிவாய, which tradition makes stand for malam, hence மயக்கம். All of this is symbolic; the verse gives only the counts.

reading: The place where the gods dwell is called Chirrambalam, Chidambaram, the holy Ambalam and the southern Podu.
nuance: Four names for the one dance-hall, with தேவர் உறைகின்ற repeated in each line. தேவர் may be the gods who attend, or an honorific plural for the Lord himself. Tradition reads the hall also as a place within the body, but the verse names only the hall.

reading: The golden hall is wonder and bliss; it is the holy dance, the unceasing dance; that dance is the dissolution of the world, the rare dances of destruction.
nuance: The verse makes one dance both bliss and destruction (பிரளயம், சங்காரம்). Destruction is one of the five acts; the dance of destruction is not presented as fearful but as rare (அரு).

reading: The dance is the single letter, the one letter; the dance is the work of grace; the dance is the Supreme who stood alone; the dance is gold itself.
nuance: அனுக்கிரகத் தொழில் (the work of grace, anugraha) is the last of the five acts; 887 named destruction, so the dance holds both. தமனியம் is gold, perhaps the golden hall, perhaps the gold that copper becomes in 903 to 907.

reading: He himself stands as the supreme light and as the tattva, himself stands as A and U, and for the tattva-dance of the supreme light he himself is the ground, ground to himself.
nuance: தராதலம் (the earth, the ground) says the dance needs no stage but the dancer. அகார உகாரம் are traditionally Siva and Shakti, or the first two parts of Om. Line 2 recurs unchanged in 901.

reading: For the ground at the root the Supreme over all is the base; that ground is the heat and is நமசிவாய; spoken, the ground becomes வாசிய, and the yoga of the ground is தயாவாசி.
nuance: Obscure throughout. மூலை may be the root centre (மூலாதாரம்), and வெப்பு its heat. வாசி is the breath in Siddha usage and is also a play on the syllables of சிவாய (வா, சி); தயா may be compassion. I can fix neither the syntax nor the reference.

reading: A and U are the Siva-forms, the supreme ones are said to be the place no one knows, the supreme consciousness is where the holy dance comes to rest, and Siva's way is bliss.
nuance: The plurals சிவங்கள் and பரங்கள் are unusual and their reference is unclear. அடங்கிய may mean the dance is contained in the supreme consciousness, or subsides into it.

reading: The three blisses and the two knowledges become one; few know that bliss is சிவாய; for those who can know it with bliss, it is caught as the dance of bliss.
nuance: Which three blisses and two knowledges are meant is not said. அறியவல்லார் கட்டு can be read 'for those able to know' or as 'the bond of those able to know'; either way, the Lord or the bliss is 'caught' (அகப்படும்) as the dance.

reading: What the masters of many arts attain is the two: Omkara and the five letters; what they attain is devotion to the dance of destruction and the angles by which it spreads.
nuance: படுவது (what befalls, what is attained) opens every line. கோணம் (angle) may point to the triangles of a drawn chakra, as in 904; this is a guess.

reading: This is the way: Sadasiva and the unchanging Agama, Siva's path, the punnai tree where bees dwell, the holy dance and the words of the Agama, and the stainless one of the hall common to all.
nuance: வாறே (thus, this is the way) opens each line and continues 893's last word. The punnai tree with bees is unexplained here; it may be a sacred tree of a shrine or a symbol. பொது (common, public) is also a name of the dance-hall.

reading: The stainless one is joined in turn to the Agama of Pati, Pasu and Pasam, to the concealing power that becomes bliss, to the impurities called anava, maya and karma, and to the place of the holy dance.
nuance: அமலம் (the stainless) opens each line, and the verse does not say how it relates to each thing it is joined to. திரோதாயி is the Lord's concealing power, which tradition holds hides the Lord only until the soul is ripe, so it can 'become bliss'. காமியம் is the karma-impurity. The three named impurities are the standard Siddhanta three; the plain sense is that where the dance is, the stainless stands against them.

reading: He is lord to himself, his own mountain, his own substance, and again lord to himself.
nuance: The first and last lines are almost the same, closing the circle of a being who depends on nothing. தன்மலை (his own mountain) may be Kailasa, or a play on மலம் that I cannot confirm.

reading: The pair of feet is the Lord: of the supreme dancer, of the worthy vessel, and of the knowledge that opens as a flower releases its pollen.
nuance: The verse builds four lines of தலைவனுமாய் நின்ற to land on தாளிணை (the two feet). சற்பாத்திரம் (a worthy vessel) is unclear here: perhaps the Lord as the fit recipient of worship, perhaps the soul fit to receive grace.

reading: The paired holy feet are the eight letters; the paired anklets are twice five, are fifty-one, are seven thousand.
nuance: The feet are identified with letters and mantras. Fifty-one is the traditional count of letters of the Sanskrit alphabet, and seven thousand the count of mantras (900). The eight letters and twice five (perhaps the five letters doubled, or the ten letters of a longer formula) are not specified.

reading: Being seven thousand, twenty and thirty, in the seven thousand becoming seven crores, the countless mantras of the seven thousand stand as seven and two.
nuance: A chain of numbers I cannot resolve. ஏழாயிரத்துயிர் may be 'the life of the seven thousand' or a misdivision. The point that survives is that the mantras multiply beyond counting and yet reduce to a few.

reading: The mantras that exist number seven thousand, there is no kind of mantra outside them, the mantra is Siva's holy body, and this is the nature of mantra.
nuance: சிவன் திருமேனி: that Siva's body is made of mantra is an Agamic teaching (the mantra-body), here stated plainly. எத்திறம் இல்லை may also mean 'there is nothing it cannot do'.

reading: He himself becomes his own fitting dance, himself stands as A and U, and for the tattva-dance of hrim he himself dances alone in the world.
nuance: The verse reworks 889: the tattva-dance there is of the supreme light, here of ரீங்காரம், the seed syllable hrim, traditionally Shakti's.

reading: The two dances are one: it becomes the lotus; the two dances are one: the dance of dissolution that Death performs; the two dances are one: the mantra that does not mock; the dance is the Sivalinga, the good copper turned gold.
nuance: Which two dances are one is not said (perhaps Siva's and Shakti's, or creation and destruction). நமன் may be Death, or a fragment of நம from the five letters. நகைசெயா is obscure. The copper turned gold, repeated through 903 to 907, is an alchemical image; tradition takes copper's tarnish as the soul's impurity removed by the mantra.

reading: If one says சிவாயநம it becomes red gold; the supreme consciousness gathered as red gold; it becomes red gold as shrim and krim; red gold is the holy hall.
nuance: ஸ்ரீ and கிரீ are taken as the seed syllables shrim and krim. The golden hall of Chidambaram and the gold of alchemy are both in play; whether the verse promises actual gold or uses gold for purity is not settled by the verse.

reading: To make the holy hall, draw the auspicious chakra by scoring twice six lines into twenty-five squares, and chant it as the holy hall: this is the way.
nuance: Six lines each way make a five-by-five grid of twenty-five cells, so the arithmetic holds. Tradition fills the cells with the five letters in rotating order (the திருவம்பலச் சக்கரம்), which fits 912's changing orders; the verse itself gives only the grid.

reading: The way is சிவாயநம, நமசிவாயநம: chant it so and no birth follows, by grace one may see the dance that grows, and copper becomes gold.
nuance: Release from birth, the vision of the dance and the alchemical gold are promised in one breath; the verse doesn't rank them. அருளால் places the vision under grace, not under the chanting alone.

reading: The golden mantra cannot be told; it is red like the kinjuka flower; for the capable who take in its smoke and are filled, the body becomes gold and they reach the golden feet.
nuance: கிஞ்சுகம் is the red palasa flower. புகையுண்டு பூரிக்கில் may be alchemical fumigation or the in-breath (பூரகம்) of breath control; பொறி may be the senses or a spark. The body turned golden is both a siddha claim and an image of the purified body.

reading: One may see the golden feet and sons will be born; by the command of the golden feet copper becomes gold; seeing the golden feet the body becomes holy; the good dance of the golden feet speaks to thought.
nuance: Worldly fruits (sons, gold) and the holy body sit side by side. சிந்தனை சொல்லுமே is unclear: the dance may speak to the mind, or be what the mind dwells on.

reading: One may enter another body and take pleasure there, good women come with liking, even by speaking it the bright serpent of bonds departs; this is the subtle secret of the holy dance.
nuance: ஒருகூட்டில் புக்கு is read as the yogic power of entering another body. The serpent of bonds (பாசச் சுடர்ப்பாம்பு) is the bond pictured as a serpent; சுடர் (bright, burning) could also suggest kundalini, but the verse calls it பாசம். Powers and liberation are again listed together.

reading: When one chants the subtle mantra eight thousand times, the subtle way can be seen above, subtle karma can be destroyed, and Siva's bliss is subtle.
nuance: சூக்குமம் (subtle) opens each line and is the last word of 908. செபித்தாலும் literally 'even if one chants', but 'when one chants' fits the promise better. மேல் may mean above, in the head, or simply 'further'.

reading: Declare bliss to be one; bliss declares ஆ ஈ ஊ ஏ ஓம்; bliss becomes the five; bliss becomes அம் ஹ்ரீம் அம் க்ஷம் ஆம்.
nuance: The vowels and seed syllables are mantra forms I can't interpret from the verse; tradition matches the five vowels with the five letters or the five faces of Sadasiva. அஞ்சு (five) may be the five letters.

reading: So that the two bodies are taken up without parting, the two bodies are change and the changeless, sounded as ஊ ஆ ஈ ஏ ஓ and as ஈ ஓ ஊ ஆ ஏ, and that is the dance.
nuance: மேனி இரண்டு (the two bodies) are commonly taken as Siva and Shakti; they may also be the gross and subtle bodies. மிகார விகாரி is obscure; I read it as விகாரி and அவிகாரி (changing and unchanging), which is a guess.

reading: The dance becomes சிவாயநம and நமசிவாய; with ஈ ஊ ஆ ஏ ஓம் it becomes சிவாயநம and சிவயநம; with இ ஊ ஆ ஏ ஓம் it becomes நமசிவாய: one way of holding it, in changed order.
nuance: The five letters are rotated (சிவாயநம, நமசிவாய, சிவயநம), as in the chakra of 904. கோளொன்று மாறே may mean 'one formula, changed in order' or 'the planet/grasp changes'. The variant spellings may be deliberate forms or copying errors.

reading: As one and two dance, one dances with them; as one, two and three dance, all seven dance in accord; as he dances in one, the nine dance with him: he who dances in the hall, the ruby dance.
nuance: The numbers carry the meaning and the verse doesn't fix them; tradition variously makes them Siva and Shakti, the three powers, the seven worlds or notes, and the nine forms of the Lord. The plain sense: everything joins the dance of the one in the hall. ஆடனான் is likely ஆடினான் or ஆடுவான்.

title: திருஅம்பலச் சக்கரம்
theme: The chakra of the holy hall (திருஅம்பலச் சக்கரம்): diagrams of crossing lines and cells are filled with the five syllables na-ma-si-va-ya, Om, bindu and nada and the fifty-one letters, and the Dancer of the hall dwells in them. The five syllables are praised as the source of the elements, the Vedas and the Agamas, as what drives out the three impurities and ends birth, and are read letter by letter as Siva, Shakti, soul and bond; the chapter ends with drawn figures used for worldly rites of fixing, enchanting, driving away, killing and attracting.
structure_note: Construction and filling of the chakra (914 to 929); the letters, Om, bindu and nada in the chakra and the body (930 to 964); the five syllables praised and interpreted, with further grids (965 to 996, grids at 987 to 991 and 995); six rites with drawn figures (997 to 1002). Many verses are technical instructions whose layout can't be recovered from the words alone.
source_issues: 946: the syllable strings (மவயரசி, வாசி மயநம) don't form clean rotations of the five syllables and include a stray ர; likely corrupt.
956: line 3 has a stray backslash (அறியவொண் ணாத\து); read as அறியவொண்ணாதது.
1002: line 2 is corrupt (பொனefனாளிf), with Latin letters in the Tamil.
970: வேரெழத்து looks like a misprint for வேரெழுத்து.
945: யாகொன்றி may be a misprint for ஆகொன்றி.
994: a variant reads சமயங்கள் for மந்திரங்கள், changing six mantras into six religious systems.
972 recurs as 1115 with different words (அயன்தனை for பயந்தனை, பெயர்ந்தனள் and அறுத்தாளே for பெயர்ந்தனன் and அறுத்தேனே), so the speaker of the last line differs between the copies.
938: Indra is set with the north, though he is usually guardian of the east; the scheme or the line may be disturbed.

reading: The circle has twelve lines, and twelve more are set across them; the houses so formed number a hundred and twenty-one, and in one of those houses he himself arrives.
nuance: ஈராறு பத்தொன்று is taken as 121, the eleven by eleven cells that twelve lines each way make. Who arrives (எய்துவன்) is left unnamed; in context it is the Lord, or the worshipper's letter.

reading: The place where he dwells is his own letter; one letter with four makes the letters of his great name, the five letters set in the square, and the one who is the one within the one is Hara.
nuance: தன் எழுத்து (his own letter) is commonly taken as சி, the one that with four others makes நமசிவாய. நாற்கோணம் is the square of the diagram.

reading: Nothing is as rare as saying 'Hara Hara'; people don't know to say it; by saying it they become as the gods, and by saying it birth is cut off.
nuance: The plainest verse of the opening: the name alone, without diagram, is enough. அமரரும் ஆவர் can mean they become immortals or become like the gods.

reading: There are eight stations where my Lord dwells; in the eight, with one, six and fourteen, and bindu and nada joined and rising, the mantra was formed by the one of milk-sweet speech.
nuance: The numbers (one, two threes, two sevens) are not explained, and பான்மொழி may name the goddess 'of milk-sweet speech' or describe the mantra's sound.

reading: People don't know the means by which he stays joined with the good lady of the opening lotus; those who unite the letter that is let go with the letter not let go can guard the precious life.
nuance: விட்ட எழுத்து and விடாத எழுத்து are traditionally taken as the outgoing and the held breath, or the spoken and the unspoken syllable of the previous chapter's ajapa. கட்டவில்லாருயிர் is obscure; read here as கட்டு அவிழ் ஆருயிர், the life whose bond is loosed, or the precious life.

reading: The five syllables are seated as a temple; when this gross temple is passed, the subtle known as temple remains, and there he sits enshrined.
nuance: தூலம் and சூக்குமம் (gross and subtle) may mean the gross and subtle body or the spoken and inner forms of the mantra; ஆலயம் (temple) carries the verse in all four lines.

reading: This circle has six lines, within them lines making five, and the cells come to twenty-five; in one of these cells the letter A takes its place.
nuance: Six lines each way give five by five, twenty-five cells, the smaller grid filled in 921 to 924.

reading: Shakti is curved in the middle of MA, O curved around it, U split and raised; A is the head, SI the two eyes, NA and VA the good legs: so the figure is sought.
nuance: The letters seem to be shaped into a figure with head, eyes and legs, traditionally taken as the form of the Dancer drawn from the syllables. The way the letter shapes are combined can't be recovered from the words.

reading: Om, the pranava, is set in the middle and on both sides; in the central face is NAMASIVAYA, and SIVAYANAMA runs in the outer circle.
nuance: ஆடும் அவர் வாய் (the mouth of the one who dances) is obscure; it may tie the diagram to the Dancer of the hall.

reading: The mantra is examined in its rotations, SIVAYANAMA, MASIVAYANA, NAMASIVAYA, YANAMASIVA, VAYANAMASI, taken in order from SI.
nuance: The five rotations of the five syllables, each beginning on a different letter, fill the rows of the grid. The last line (தொட்டநதத் தடைவிலே) is obscure.

reading: In order, the fifty letters go two to a cell in the twenty-five cells; with KSHA, the last, placed at MA, all fifty-one letters are set.
nuance: Fifty-one is the count of the Sanskrit alphabet with க்ஷ added; the verse fits the whole alphabet into the five-syllable grid.

reading: The outer circle is set with 'Hara Hara', the circle within it with 'Hari Hari', the circle within that with the ajapa, and the lines become a trident.
nuance: அசபை is the unspoken mantra of the breath, subject of the previous chapter. அரிகரி may be Hari or a variant of Hara.

reading: At the trident's head Shakti appears, around it Om, in the space between its prongs the five letters appear, and this is also the way to reach the Lord of the banyan.
nuance: ஆலப்பதி may be the Lord under the banyan or a place; the reading of the figure depends on how the trident of 925 is drawn.

reading: That is A, I, U, E and O, five; they form circle upon circle of the chakra, and in the shared space between, our name swells.
nuance: நம் பேரே may be 'our name' or the syllable நம.

reading: What received the name is the root mantra; after it, the chakra stands set straight at the junction within the circle, and this is the nature of its form.
nuance: சோர்வுற்ற (wearied, slack) of the circle is obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: The Lord makes clear the working of the way this mantra is reached; wind, water, fire, earth and sky stood before the letters that are sounded.
nuance: முயலும் எழுத்துக்கு முன்னா may mean the elements came before the letters, or stand in front of them as their places in the diagram.

reading: Above the forty-eight letters set six and fourteen, above them bindu and nada; standing fierce and saying SIVAYANAMA, the three impurities cry out and leave.
nuance: The count (6 x 8, then 6 and 14) is not explained. கூப்பிட்டுப் போமே pictures the impurities fleeing with a cry; the claim that the mantra removes the three malams is plain whatever the numbers mean.

reading: The Lord is within her letter and the good lady within the Lord's letter; those who think of the two dwelling there in accord are the virtuous who know the meaning.
nuance: Tradition takes சி as Siva's letter and வ as Shakti's; the verse says only that each is within the other's.

reading: Set A, place ARA above it, set I, and it stands as a linga; set MA, and once the breath is seen rising above, it becomes a flame-tip sealed with 'thom'.
nuance: அரவு may be the letters ர or ஹ, or the serpent. தொம் may be a seed syllable. The verse shapes letters into a linga and then a flame.

reading: There is A, there is SA, everything is there; no one knows the purpose for which SA stands; for those who know the purpose of KA, SA is Shakti and Sadasiva.
nuance: அ, ச and க are not explained; they may be letters of a seed mantra, or அ and ச Siva and Shakti as in 957.

reading: By the five letters Nandi is seated; by the five letters the pancakshara is seated; the five letters make the letter-chakra, and within the five letters he is seated.
nuance: The circling of அஞ்செழுத்து in every line makes the Lord, the mantra and the diagram one thing.

reading: Many signs are told for seeing the Dancer; those who recite the first of the Dancer's letters stand as one in creed with him, and that is the sign for seeing the Dancer.
nuance: Which letter is first is not said: ந in the usual order, சி as the Lord's own letter, or Om.

reading: If one raises the fire within that direction and recites the letter NA within that direction, the Vedic one in that direction is made to dwell within that direction.
nuance: அத்திசை (that direction) opens every line; directions of the diagram are assigned to letters and deities, but which is meant is lost. மறையன் may be Brahma, the Vedic one, or 'the hidden one'.

reading: If one looks to the lady he himself gives, he gives and places her above; when one recites the MA he gave, it becomes a gem-light he has given.
nuance: கல்லொளி (light of stone, a gem's light) links this verse to the next. The grammar of who gives and who is placed is unclear.

reading: The north stood as gem-light, Indra stood as gem-light, and he showed the letter SI, which stood as gem-light, as gem-light.
nuance: Indra is usually the guardian of the east, not the north, so either the diagram's scheme differs or the line is disturbed.

reading: He himself stands as cool light with the seven qualities, as the Vedas with them; if one recites what becomes those qualities, he becomes the self-risen Vedic one.
nuance: எழுகுணம் may be 'seven qualities' or 'the rising quality'. The last line may mean the reciter or the Lord becomes the Vedic one.

reading: Births esteemed as those of the Vedic man are seen as such, but the Vedic man in whom the five letters have come to stand becomes those five letters himself.
nuance: One reading: the true மறையவன் is made by the five syllables dwelling in him, not by the birth people esteem. The first two lines are compressed and may only say the birth is held in honour.

reading: NA stands at the feet, MA at the navel, SI and VA are seen at the shoulders, and the light above is of the nature of YA.
nuance: The syllables are placed on the body from foot to crown. சீயுரு தோள் is unclear: சி may be at the chest or with வ at the shoulders.

reading: Nandi excelled in giving the six letters of that nature their fine nature; if one looks at them alike and filled with light, he stands spread through them.
nuance: இருமூன்று எழுத்து, six letters, is commonly Om with the five syllables. ஒவ்வியல், பவ்வியல் play on the letters ஒ and ப and are obscure.

reading: The mantra spreads to all lives; it is the boon-giving mantra; take it so it fits; it is the mantra that drives away surrounding enemies, the mantra that gives strength: raise it with Om.
nuance: சூழ்பகை (surrounding enmity) may be outward enemies or inner foes; both readings stand, and the chapter's closing rites (997 to 1002) show the outward sense was also in view.

reading: Raising the excellent Nandi with Om, raising the lamp that rises in the middle with NAM, raising with AAM: those who know that way saw the great hall and rejoiced.
nuance: மாமன்று is the great hall, the அம்பலம் of the chapter's title, here seen within. நாம், ஆம் may be syllables or words ('we', 'it is').

reading: Within the chakra the five letters are poured into the steps joined part by part; with the fifty-one letters within, the Supreme beyond stands joined to it.
nuance: பாகொன்றி and வார்த்திக்கும் are obscure; யாகொன்றி may be a misprint for ஆகொன்றி.

reading: With the supreme five letters set in the middle, further orders of the syllables are given, ending in the form VASI-MAYANAMA.
nuance: The strings (நவசிவ, மவயரசி, சியநம, வாசி மயநம) do not form the clean rotations of 923 and include a stray ர; they are likely corrupt.

reading: The elements match the letters, the colours match the letters; when the letters stand matched, he stands within those letters.
nuance: Each syllable is traditionally given an element and a colour; the verse doesn't list them.

reading: The chakra stands for the whole wide earth; Nandi, as a calf, drew milk from the good Lord of the land of maya who stands as the hall, and he is one whose way is to stand on the mountain.
nuance: The calf milking its mother is a common image for drawing grace by love. Who is the calf and who is milked is not certain, and குன்று may be Kailasa or a yogic height.

reading: Within this chakra are many qualities, five signs and the Dancer's five letters, and the dance stands within it.
nuance: The dance (கூத்து) of the hall is set inside the drawn diagram; the five signs are not named.

reading: Outside a line, on the line its head, in the curl U, fire around it, the bending stroke and horn, O, bindu and nada: this clear plan is the Siva mantra.
nuance: The verse names the strokes of the written letters (கால், கொம்பு, the curl and the dot) as parts of the drawn mantra; the figure itself can't be reconstructed.

reading: With A, U and SI in the middle, VA and the six joined with the breath, and with SI contemplating Siva, the Lord of O stands pleased.
nuance: A near-variant of 976 and 982. 'The six' (ஆறும்) is unexplained.

reading: Where all ceases, A arises; where it is reached, the true object is seen; that bright light which cut away anger, the true object, is a pill like gold with its dross removed.
nuance: குளிகை is the alchemist's pill that turns base metal to gold; the image makes the realised mantra a transforming pill. அற்ற இடம் may be the place where breath or thought stops.

reading: When A is sounded with U, the release that is U melts and mingles; how shall I tell the nature of my father, Nandi, who came into me as MA?
nuance: அ, உ, ம are the parts of Om; the verse moves from the syllable to the speaker's experience of the Lord within.

reading: What the people of this world know is letters on water; no one sees and knows the one letter in the sky; and those who know this letter do not perceive the letter in the flesh.
nuance: Writing on water is the stock image of what doesn't last. The last two lines can be read as a rebuke (even knowers miss the letter in the body) or as 'who knows this letter? they do not perceive it in the flesh'.

reading: At morning the letter is centred in the body, at evening the fifty letters are; with the root spoken by the Veda centred above, he gave release.
nuance: நடுவுற (being centred) in every line suggests stages of practice through the day; மூலம் may be the root mantra or the root centre.

reading: Below the navel is one good letter; sinners don't know its use; it can't be known even by painters; the Goddess and he shine there together.
nuance: ஓவியர் may be painters (it can't be drawn) or those who have ceased (renouncers). நாவி may be the navel or musk. The centre below the navel is traditionally the base of kundalini.

reading: The mantra Hara attained is A with SA; no one knows A with SA; once someone knows it, A with SA becomes the beginningless as well.
nuance: அவ்வொடு சவ்வு is unexplained: perhaps Siva and Shakti, or the syllables of a seed mantra. அதரன் may be அ(த்)து அரன் or a variant.

reading: One mantra, springing from the flower, rises within the navel; people perform the twilight rites without knowing it, worship at dusk, and go off making noise.
nuance: A rebuke of outer ritual: சந்தி (the twilight rite) done aloud without knowing the mantra that rises within. The flower (மலர்) is the inner lotus as tradition reads it.

reading: The mantra of worship gives direction; the mantras within the life are its supports; if one looks at the mantra within the flower without letting it go, the mantra within the life is a goad.
nuance: ஆதாரம் is the yogic support-centre or simply a base. The goad (அங்குசம்) anticipates 977.

reading: In the formless is the sky, where nada rises; in the swelling drum-shaped waist is the cherished bindu; joining in the middle of YA and SI, the true mantra wells up as it takes form.
nuance: துடியிடை (the drum-shaped middle) may be the waist of the body or of Shakti. The verse places nada above and bindu below.

reading: When bindu and nada join and meet the moon, nectar comes and wells up in the inner sky, and the mantra rising there becomes the oblation.
nuance: The moon is traditionally the centre at the head from which nectar flows in yoga. The fire rite is turned inward: the mantra itself is the oblation. அங்குதி is read as அங்கு உதி(த்த).

reading: Those who recite the six letters don't know them, nor recite the six as one and understand; for those who can utter it with no other letter, by one letter life can be won.
nuance: The six letters are commonly Om with the five syllables, and the one letter Om or சி. உயிர்பெறல் may be gaining life (long life) or gaining the soul's release.

reading: With the recited letters go the soul-letters, three fives; the first letters are said to be fifty-one; in the light-letters there are ten and three more; set down the nada letter and seek.
nuance: உயிர்க்கலை மூவைஞ்சு (fifteen) and ஐயிரு மூன்று may count vowels and other letter groups; the arithmetic is not clear.

reading: As nada rises spiralling from bindu, the mistress of bonds becomes sixteen kalas; she took the beautiful letter-form with breath as her body, and without end became the fifty-one.
nuance: பந்தத் தலைவி (mistress of bonds) is Shakti as the power that binds and releases. The sixteen kalas are traditionally the vowels or the moon's digits; the fifty-one are the letters.

reading: The fifty letters are all the Vedas and all the Agamas; once one knows what the fifty letters become, the fifty go and become the five letters.
nuance: The whole of scripture is reduced to its letters, and the letters to the five syllables. The verse recurs almost word for word as 2698.

reading: By the five letters he made the five elements, by them the many wombs of birth, by them he bears this wide world, and by them he stands seated.
nuance: யோனி is the kinds of birth, traditionally 84 lakh. The five syllables are made the instrument of creation and support.

reading: To one who, falling and rising, begins the holy name of the Transcendent and does not tire and give it up, the Lord comes to take away the grief of the deeds that cling, says the one with coiled locks.
nuance: வீழ்ந்தெழல் may be falling down in worship and rising, or falling and rising in life. The final line puts the promise in the Lord's own mouth.

reading: He stands as the food one eats and the medicine, endless time, learned hearing and song; while the gods in heaven long to worship his feet, he has become the five letters, beyond reckoning.
nuance: எண்ணின்று may be 'beyond count' or 'standing in thought'. The gods worship from afar what is near in the syllables.

reading: By the greatness of the five comes the wide world, by it the temple, by it the way of the virtuous one, and by working the five in their kinds one becomes the protector.
nuance: ஐந்து (the five) is in context the five syllables, but could be the five acts or elements. பாலன் may be the protector or a child (one guarded).

reading: As the root letter he is sky and beyond; as the water letter he bears the earth too; as the fine letter he is fire; and the letter that is life, the one-letter Lord, is bright light.
nuance: Each syllable is matched to an element; the verse's assignments don't plainly match the usual scheme (ந earth, ம water, சி fire, வ air, ய sky). வேரெழத்து looks like a misprint for வேரெழுத்து.

reading: The sound of the fourth letter is the world's form; within the fourth letter the world is contained; for those who can recite the fourth letter, it is the good path.
nuance: The fourth letter is commonly taken as வ, fourth in நமசிவாய and traditionally Shakti's letter; it may also be a number for another syllable.

reading: The bejewelled lady joined, entered my heart and loved there the word NAMASIVA; she holds the step that knows the fearful, she moved, and I cut away all other babble.
nuance: The verse recurs as 1115 with அயன்தனை for பயந்தனை and with the lady, not the speaker, cutting the babble (பெயர்ந்தனள், அறுத்தாளே). பயந்தனை ஓரும் is obscure.

reading: For those who stay saying the name NAMASIVA, the lady of the rule shines: the one woman who stays sweetly in the stomach and in the fire raises up the sheath of food.
nuance: ஆமம் (the stomach, or undigested food), அன்னமயம் (the food-sheath) and ஓமம் (the fire rite) suggest Shakti as the digestive fire that turns food into the body; this is a traditional reading.

reading: Knowing the liking of the supreme five letters as is fitting, while night and day come, she takes her place in the middle where the dance is danced and stands as the substance of the eight directions.
nuance: பட்ட பரிசே and பரமஞ் செழுத்ததின் are compressed. Night and day may be the two breaths; the middle, the central channel or the hall's centre.

reading: A is the soul, U the supreme and MA the impurity in the three-part word; SI is Siva, VA the form, and YA, one may say, is the soul.
nuance: Both Om and the five syllables are read as the Siddhanta categories. Tradition takes வ as Shakti, the Lord's form (வடிவம்) of grace. A is made the soul here, where Kural 1 makes A the image of the Lord.

reading: With NA, MA and SI in the middle, the two VAs joined with the breath, beginning with O and uttered once, the first Lord MA is within the mind.
nuance: 'The two VAs' and 'Lord MA' are unexplained; the verse is a near-doublet of 982 and close to 951.

reading: Five elephants live in the forest; for the five, the five letters are the goad; for those who can hold all five together, the First beyond the five can enter within.
nuance: The five elephants are the senses, though the verse doesn't name them. அஞ்சாதி ஆதி may be 'the First before the five' or 'the fearless First'; அகம் புகல் may be his entering the heart or their entering his.

reading: In the five kalas, beginning with A, the order beginning with NA is changed to begin with MA; for those who seek Nandi at the root and join with the Supreme Shakti, there is no ritual.
nuance: சந்திசெய்வார் plays on the twilight rite (சந்தி) and joining: the inner union replaces the outer rite. மூலம் is traditionally the base centre.

reading: SIVAYA, joined, becomes the abiding soul, the precious enjoyment and knowledge; the soul that has come to clarity goes on by these, grace settles in it, and becoming that Siva is release.
nuance: சிவாய without நம is traditionally the subtle form of the mantra, with the impurity (ம) and concealment (ந) dropped, as in the ninth tantra's subtle pancakshara.

reading: Once the truth of the five letters is known, the Supreme stays firm within the heart; there is no deceit and no ruin to the house; I declare that this is refuge.
nuance: அஞ்சுக (opening) may be 'fear' (imperative) or a form of அஞ்சு, five; மனை (house) may be the household or the body.

reading: Recited clearly in the heart, SIVAYA with A becomes Siva's form; those who can see SIVAYA with A clearly stayed in that clarity.
nuance: அவ்வே may be the letter அ added to சிவாய, or simply 'that'.

reading: With SI, VA and YA, and NA and MA sought in the middle, uttered once with O, the first Lord MA stands esteemed.
nuance: A near-doublet of 976, beginning from சி rather than ந.

reading: The acts sought in the five beginning with NA, the hard deeds contained in the five beginning with A: for those who can see clearly within the first SI, Sadasiva becomes their own First.
nuance: The two groups of five (from ந and from அ) may be the five syllables and the five vowels; the point is that seeing சி first frees from deeds.

reading: NAVA and SIVA become the soul and the Supreme; what lacks tapas is only tattva; those who search, at one with Siva, in devotion reached the clarity that they are what is called Siva.
nuance: நவம் is obscure: perhaps ந and ம (soul and bond), or 'the new'. The closing claim, that the seeker becomes Siva, is the Siddhanta goal of oneness without loss of the soul, as tradition reads it.

reading: Know by gathering the eight and the two; set Nandi whom you sought within knowledge, and the five who danced become kin there; seek it and know it clearly.
nuance: In Tamil numerals அ is 8 and உ is 2, so எட்டும் இரண்டும் is traditionally read as the letters அ and உ. The five who danced are the senses, now made kin.

reading: They don't know the eight and two well; the poor who don't know them miss that the eight and two, as six and four, are the step of the true path of Siddhanta.
nuance: இருமூன்று நான்கு (two threes and four, or six and four) is unexplained. சித்தாந்த சன்மார்க்கம் names the path explicitly.

reading: Draw eight lines across eight lines, set one letter of the Lord in the middle, place the forty-eight cells within the circle, and recite the five letters quickly.
nuance: Eight lines each way make seven by seven, forty-nine cells: the centre for the Lord's letter and forty-eight around it. சிட்டஞ்செழுத்து is read as the prescribed (சிட்ட) five letters.

reading: Danavas, the Sattars, the two Chatirars, with these three the Atravar and the rest, the other fifteen, bindu and nada and the host: this is the Siva chakra.
nuance: The names are classes of beings or letter groups placed in the cells; most can't be identified.

reading: The six of great penance who suffered and the Supreme; those who gave up the self say 'to the Transcendent, nama'; however many the eight ways of the Lord, I join them and speak, I know nothing else.
nuance: The first line is obscure. விகிர்தா நம (homage to the Transcendent) is the mantra form; the last line is the speaker's humility.

reading: Siva first, with the three and the five excelling; from them twelve, one with one; from them bindu and nada rising; first of the assembly is Sankara's own name.
nuance: The counts likely place deities or letters in the 49-cell grid of 987; சவை (assembly) may be the hall.

reading: Draw lines making the world as seed, set the sixteen kalas of the conch, then twelve in each kala from the first, and recite looking to the tenth, the Brahma rite.
nuance: நத்தார் கலை (kalas of the conch, or the moon's), உத்தாரம் and பத்தாம் பிரம சடங்கு are obscure.

reading: I found the honey within the lotus flower and rose with it; at the time of joining, going by the Lord's way that never perished of old, without losing the bond, it becomes 'nama'.
nuance: கண்டெடுந்தேன் puns on 'I found and took up' and 'honey'. பதிவழி may be the way of the Lord (பதி) or the settled way.

reading: The virtuous gods stand showering flowers and meditate on the mantra of the Lord's two feet; they draw near and, saying 'nama' with the name and holding it dear as their eyes, stand merged with it.
nuance: கண்என உன்னி (thinking of it as one's eye) means holding it most dear.

reading: The six letters are six mantras; for the six, four each, twenty-four, they say; in the Savitri there is one head-letter, and those who can discern it have ended their births.
nuance: The Savitri (Gayatri) has twenty-four syllables, which the verse matches to six times four. A variant reads சமயங்கள் for மந்திரங்கள்: the six letters would then be the six religious systems.

reading: Set eight cells in eight, fill the cells so that each joined one shows as eight, mark them and surround them with Om: for lives in bondage, Umapati is there.
nuance: The filling rule may be a magic square of eights. மட்டும் உயிர்கட்டு is obscure: perhaps 'for lives bound' or 'binding lives'.

reading: Those who take NA as first with A and hold it on the tongue, reaching within the eight beginning with A, and perceive U as first: on their crown the one who is first in U comes and stays.
nuance: The play is on letters as 'firsts'. உச்சி (crown) is the traditional head centre where the Lord is met.

reading: On a pipal board, set MA in one place, draw the figure on palm-leaf, smear dense wax over it and warm it in the flame, and fixing (stambhana) is seen.
nuance: 997 to 1002 give rites for worldly ends: தம்பனம் (fixing or paralysing), மோகனம் (enchanting), உச்சாடனம் (driving away), மாரணம் (killing) and வசியம் (attracting), traditionally among the six acts (ஷட்கர்மம்) of mantra practice. The verses state technique without comment, and many words of material and direction are uncertain.

reading: Set a board of karanai wood toward Yama's quarter, write 'death', set the letter MA in the eight, smear it with the five astringents and bury it by a hearth, and enchanting (mohana) follows.
nuance: கரண இரளி may be two woods or one; மரணம் இட்டு may be writing the word or the name of the target. Yama's quarter is the south.

reading: There in the north-west, in Ayyanar's shrine, on a board of palasa wood, smear it with bitter stuff, set the bindu, and place it so it doesn't rise: this is for driving away (uchchatana).
nuance: காங்கரு மேட்டில் is obscure; கடு may be a bitter or astringent paste.

reading: At noon, in the fire-corner, spread the five astringents on a green palm-leaf and place it in a triple square in the old cremation ground, if one wants killing (marana) without fear.
nuance: The fire-corner is the south-east. முச்சதுரம் may be a triple square or triangle. அச்சமற மேலோர் may mean 'the great, without fear' or 'without fear, over the enemy'. The verse gives the rite without approving or condemning it.

reading: Smear yellow orpiment on the leaf, write the letters A and U, place it fittingly on a bilva board for attracting (vasiya), and recite eighty thousand times.
nuance: எண்பதினாயிரம் (eighty thousand) is the count of recitations, as tradition reads it.

reading: For Garuda, write U on the leaf, smear it with gold and silver, place it on a white naval-wood board facing west, and recite eight thousand times with the letters.
nuance: எண்ணாக் கருடன் is obscure: perhaps a rite against poison invoking Garuda. Line 2 is corrupt in the source.

title: அருச்சனை
theme: Archana, worship with flowers, scented pastes, food offerings and lamps: offered with love it brings everything from wealth and the eight siddhis to release. Yet those given to Siva, the Siva-yogis and the desireless need no rites, and the chapter turns inward to the Lord known within, the syllables of the mantra placed in the body, and the nectar and light of Siva.
structure_note: Outer worship and its fruits (1003 to 1006); the worshipper's fitness and those beyond rites (1007, 1008); inner knowing, the mantra in the body and the state of union (1009 to 1014).
source_issues: 1008 line 1: ஆட்பட்டோ ர் has a stray space (ஆட்பட்டோர்).
1011 line 4 (ஓராசித்த தேவரே) is obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: Offer lotus, blue lily, water lily, the fine neythal, fragrant areca blossom, madhavi, mandaram, thumbai, vakulam, surapunnai, jasmine, champak, pathiri and chrysanthemum.
nuance: The verse is only a list of flowers ending in the command சாத்திடே (offer, adorn). It sets the outward rite that 1008 will say some need not perform.

reading: Mix sandal with fragrant kunkumam, camphor and dark agil, blended properly with rosewater as part of the rite, and adorn and worship with love.
nuance: சாங்கமதாகவே is taken as 'with its proper limbs', the rite done complete; சந்தொடு is unclear. The verse closes on அன்பொடே: the materials are listed, but love is the manner required.

reading: Standing in love, offering the food offering and setting golden lamps and incense and lights in every direction, when worshippers who have put away sorrow think on him, release comes to them with joy.
nuance: துன்பம் அகற்றி can be what the worshippers do (putting sorrow aside) or what the worship does (removing their sorrow). அமுது here is the food offered (naivedya).

reading: If you come and worship there is nothing you cannot reach: first Indra's wealth, then the eight siddhis, and at last release.
nuance: Each line opens with எய்தி வழிப்படில், and the fruits climb from worldly wealth to powers to release. எய்தி may mean coming near the Lord or having attained the means.

reading: Those who have left desire for others' wives and quenched the senses, with pure food offerings, attentive contemplation, the five-limbed prostration and repetition of the mantra, have minds that settle with the breath.
nuance: அவித்தார் has no stated object; the senses are the usual reading. பஞ்சாங்கம் may be the five-limbed prostration or a five-part rite, and அனுசந்தானம் steady inner attention. மனம் பவனத்தோடு வைகும் is a yogic note: the mind abiding with the breath.

reading: Those who have become servants of the Stainless One, those who have no desire for it, the great Siva-yogis and the eminent who have searched it out do not want ritual works; they want love.
nuance: கன்மம் here is most naturally the ritual work the chapter has been prescribing, though it can also mean deeds and their fruit. The last line is compressed: ஆய்ந்து அன்பே, 'having examined, love', taken as love being what they keep.

reading: No one knows him through the knowledge that is hard to reach; people seek through the senses and lament, but if they look steadily within the house of the way, he can be found inside the struck bell.
nuance: பொறிவழி (the way of the senses) is set against looking within. நெறிமனை, the house of the path, is taken as the body; எறிமணி, the struck bell, is traditionally the inner sound heard in meditation, though it could also be the bell of temple worship.

reading: The heart is twofold, like darkness and light: delusion and ignorance, and abiding knowledge; ignorance that does not cast off these delusions stays bewildered, and only those who have broken delusion are the knowers.
nuance: The pairing of இருள் and வெளி (darkness and open light) for ignorance and knowledge in the one heart is the image. The last line is elliptical: அவர்களாம் supplies 'they are the ones' without saying what.

reading: When the self becomes He and He becomes the self, the knower of the two becomes Siva; this is the love of one who has reached the fourth way, and he becomes Him.
nuance: நாலாம் மரபு is traditionally the fourth of the four paths (charya, kriya, yoga, jnana). The verse calls union a form of love (அன்பு). ஓராசித்த தேவரே is obscure.

reading: Om always rests below the navel, the unfailing syllable va is in the long throat, na abides in the forehead, and swelling bindu and nada are above.
nuance: This is a placing of mantra syllables in the body (nyasa). Only Om, va and na are named, and why they sit where they do is not explained; the usual placings of the five syllables differ.

reading: Nama, the seat, is the soul; Sivam, the attainment, is Siva the Lord; when nama falls away there is no more seeking the First; to join the great silence that is Siva is true release.
nuance: The verse splits நமசிவாய: நம is the பசு, the bound soul, as the seat (ஆசனம்), and சிவ the பதி. Line 3 (நமவற ஆதி நாடுவது அன்றாம்) is obscure; it may mean that once the soul's part ceases, the search ends. மாமோனம் is the great silence.

reading: On the day clarity comes, Siva's nectar wells up; on the day light comes, it leaps in a single petal; if in that state the two become one, the Lord who gives the open space remains as that space.
nuance: ஓர்ஏட்டில் (in one petal or leaf) may refer to a lotus centre in yogic anatomy. ஓர் இரண்டு ஆகில் can be 'if the two become one' or 'if one becomes two'. வெளி, open space, is the Lord's own nature here.

title: நவகுண்டம்
theme: The nine fire-pits (navakundam) of the fire rite, each of its own shape, read at once as altars and as places in the body: the flame rising in them is the Lord's light, in which Siva, Shakti and Skanda are visualized in forms of fixed numbers. Those who see that fire within are freed from strong karma, live long in the guarded body and reach release.
structure_note: An announcement (1015) is followed by the kundas and the light rising in them (1016 to 1020), the forms seen in the flame, of Shakti, Siva and Skanda (1021 to 1033), and the fruit of joining the fire: release, long life, the guru's teaching and the yogi's inner practice (1034 to 1044). Much of the chapter is technical and some lines look corrupt.
source_issues: 1038 line 2 (மலர்ந்திரு குண்ட மகாரத்தார் Yமூக்கு) contains a stray Latin 'Y' and is corrupt.
1035 line 4: செற்றற்து is probably a misprint for செற்றற்று.
1022 line 4: கற்றும் வின் வாளே is split oddly and unclear; perhaps வினவாரே or a corruption.
1033: the numbers do not cohere (ten feet in line 2, two feet in line 3).
1016 line 4 and 1044 lines 2 to 3 are obscure and may be corrupt.
1030 line 4: தந்தமி லாற்கே is read as அந்தம் இலாற்கு (to the endless one), matching 1031; the division of words is uncertain.

reading: I will tell what the nine kundas are, the good flame that rises in them and all the good that rises in them.
nuance: குண்டம் is the pit for the sacred fire; nine kundas of different shapes belong to the Agamic fire rite. The chapter treats them also as places within, so a plain and an inner reading stand throughout.

reading: Within the kunda spoken of are three parts, the four-cornered pit, five good things and the hostile triple city with fire; the parts that rise beyond these we do not know.
nuance: முக்கால் (three legs, three times or three parts), நாற்கோணம் (square) and பாரங்கி (perhaps earth and fire) are unclear. முப்புரம், the three cities Siva burned, are traditionally read as the three malas. The last line may be corrupt.

reading: That which, thrown upward, made space within, the red flame that knew the breath and entered thought within, which knew the earth and stood with the cosmos unbounded: I knew it and sought it within.
nuance: கால் is taken as breath, as elsewhere in Tirumular, and the red flame as the inner fire. சிறகற (without wings or edges) is obscure.

reading: As the light rising within this kunda one can create and destroy the fourteen worlds; all the spread of the ancient Veda I have set out today as a spoken text.
nuance: The subject of ஆக்கி அழிக்கலாம் is open: the light itself, the Lord, creates and destroys, or the one who knows it gains that power. Line 4 claims this teaching restates the Veda.

reading: In the sixteen places of that kunda the kalas set there stand guarding; for those who see the fire rising within, strong karma, however it boils up, cannot join them.
nuance: பதினாறு கலை are traditionally the sixteen digits, as of the moon. உள்ளெழ (rising within) is what turns the rite inward.

reading: In the kunda rising within the triple peak, the five that dance stand within and without, and the twelve signs of the zodiac rise there; for those who seek it, it is the good flame.
nuance: கூடம் முக்கூடம் (peak, three peaks) and ஆடிய ஐந்து (the five that dance: elements, senses or the five acts) are not fixed by the verse. The twelve signs may be the twelve-part breath or a diagram.

reading: The good flame forms the circle of head and face, flames are the hands held in thought, the body is flame and the linga stands unshaken; she rises as the good flame and is the Good.
nuance: This begins the visualization of a deity's form in the fire. நல்லதென்றாள் is read as 'she who is called the Good', the goddess, which 1022 takes up.

reading: She who is called the Good is the sovereign who has come to us; she who is called the Word, is she the flame-crowned head or the feet? Those who do not ask her who stands gently think her stone, even though they have learned.
nuance: The last line (கல்லதென் றாளையும் கற்றும் வின் வாளே) is unclear and may be corrupt; read here as the learned taking the goddess for stone, the image only.

reading: In the kunda shaped like the young crescent of the sky, two flaming serpents point to the directions, many serpents spread, and the supreme flame took its place within my body.
nuance: விளம்பிறை names the crescent-shaped kunda, one of the nine shapes. The serpents (நாகம்) may be ornaments of the form or the coiled power; பன்னாலு (fourteen, or many fours) is unclear.

reading: The feet that took their place are a single beautiful flame, the feet are those that took up the dance, two hands and six flourish in ease, and the red flame of the face belongs to the three-eyed Lord.
nuance: A form of Siva in the fire, given by parts. நண்ணீர் அதற்கு (approach it) and கையிரண்டு ஆறும் (two hands and six, or two and the six) are unclear.

reading: The three-eyed one is himself the whole flame; that one swallowed all the world; with eyes in every direction he saw the eight quarters; to every god of whatever eyes he is our father and Lord.
nuance: The verse plays on கணன் (the eyed one): முக்கணன், அக்கணன், திக்கணன், எக்கணன். 'Swallowing the world' is usually said of Vishnu; here it is Siva's, and எக்கணன் may glance at the many-eyed gods, Brahma and Indra.

reading: For our father the Lord there are six circles, and because the six-faced one appears before his father and Lord Skanda stays joined there, hold him fast as the son.
nuance: The six-sided kunda is matched with six-faced Murugan. மாட்டிக்கொள்ளீரே (fix, hold fast) is read as a command to the meditator.

reading: In the Veda rising within the kunda, one foot moving and two unfolding, two bent hands and one rising trembling: these gods set there are good light.
nuance: The verse lists limbs of forms seen in the fire, but whose forms and how they are counted is not clear.

reading: As good light she moves through all the world, as the light of a gem she stays mingled within, as the light of the word she follows all lives, and as the gem's light she stands in the eye.
nuance: கல்லொளி (light of stone, a gem's light) is repeated; it may be the inner light seen in meditation. The feminine நின்றாளே makes the subject Shakti.

reading: This kunda does not stay fixed but becomes angled; in the ancient circle the six sixes rise, and as these tattvas mingle within it can be raised, like a heart of space.
nuance: மாறாறும் is read as ஆறாறு, the thirty-six tattvas. விண்ணுளம் (sky-heart, or 'as if the heart of the sky') and the last line are obscure.

reading: Three lifting feet, the letter, two fierce faces with six eyes, a tongue that reads and counts, four horns, and eyes rising close by: these belong to the one without end.
nuance: Another numbered form. கொம்பு and தந்தம் can mean horn or tusk, which might suggest an elephant form, but தந்தமிலாற்கே is read with 1031 as அந்தம் இலாற்கு, the endless one.

reading: The endless one has no place wide enough, no one to measure him and no word to reach him; know the endless one through devotion.
nuance: பத்தே may be devotion (பத்தி) or the number ten, which 1032 opens with. Lines 1 to 3 are the chapter's clearest statement that no form contains the Lord the other verses describe.

reading: In the kunda measured out with ten, eight, six and four, the lotus blooms; bound there it stands as the mingled truth, and settled on Parvati's side.
nuance: The petal counts may be those of lotus centres in the body or of the kunda's drawing. மெய் may be truth or body.

reading: Parvati's partner has twenty hands spread, ten feet, ten faces with their eyes, two flower feet, a flaming crown, forty ears and a good twenty-five.
nuance: The counts do not cohere as given: ten feet (காற்பதி பத்து) then two feet. சோத்திரம் may be ears (srotra) or hymns (stotra); இருபத்தஞ்சு may be the twenty-five tattvas.

reading: The form of five measures five fives; because the kunda blooms there, the supreme flame spreads as light, and to join the cooing fire is release.
nuance: ஐஐந்து (twenty-five) may be the tattvas. மஞ்சிட்ட (cloud-laid) and பஞ்சிட்ட (cotton-laid, or five-laid) are obscure. வன்னி, fire, is named as what one joins for release.

reading: He who is the whole flame, the good light of release, abides in the thought of those who stand beyond learning; those who seek without attachment, pass through the spreading light and are free of hostility have joined him.
nuance: கற்றற்று is read as 'with learning ended' but may hide another word; செற்றற்து in line 4 is taken as செற்றற்று, 'without enmity'.

reading: The five kalas joined, this kunda and all the directions settle there; those who have kindled the fire that the five elements watch are ever joined with it.
nuance: The five kalas are traditionally nivritti, pratishtha, vidya, shanti and shantyatita. காய்ந்தவர் may be those who kindled or heated the fire, or those who overcame it.

reading: Join the One who made the seven worlds of the wide waters a region of truth and of rescue; the gods made perfect by knowledge seen in practice have mingled with the reality that has no false part.
nuance: The verse plays on கண்டம் (region, part): மெய்கண்டம், உய்கண்டம், செய்கண்ட, பொய்கண்டம்.

reading: The two feet joined become two hands, the kunda opens at the syllable ma as the nose, the red face blooms with the other eye and forehead, and the tuft of hair is there for the Supreme.
nuance: Line 2 is corrupt (a stray Latin Y). The verse seems to map a form, and perhaps mantra syllables, onto the kunda, but the mapping cannot be fixed.

reading: The Supreme's light is there as a child on one side, blooms as one in the middle, spreads to the west and hollows, and flourishes as the creeper, Shakti.
nuance: பாலன், மத்திமன் (child, middle one) may be stages of the Lord's form or positions. பச்சிம திக்கு, the west, in yogic usage can mean the back channel. கொடி (creeper) is a common image for Shakti.

reading: The kunda where the creeper ran its six courses and played is two-angled at the base and alike at the end; those who see unfailingly the flame spread through the seven worlds become a great treasure.
nuance: கொடியாறு (six courses of the creeper, or the creeper's river) may be the six centres of the body. மாதனம் (great wealth) is taken up in 1041.

reading: Taking as his means the fire that grows as great wealth, the guru stands perfected and teaches it fittingly, and the feet that rule the world, seeing it, are moved with love.
nuance: The verse rhymes on -தனம்: மாதனம், சாதனம், போதனம், பாதனம். Who sees and is moved in the last line, the Lord or the guru, is not certain.

reading: No one examines and knows as their own the light that spreads wherever one looks; those who guarded the body and dwelt in thought within it have grown old in that body and seen a crore of ages.
nuance: ஆத்தம் (one's own, or trustworthy) is unclear. The claim of long life in the guarded body is plain and fits Tirumular's teaching of nurturing the body.

reading: The nine kundas known over the ages are alike; the yogi who has seen within raises them in the nadi, and as the womb conceives on union, seeing the world through this is the practice.
nuance: The verse makes the nine kundas inner and raised through the channels. The third line (பகங்கண்டு கொண்டஇப் பாய்கரு) is read as an image of conception; சகம் கண்டு may be seeing or creating the world.

reading: Four practices, three fires, the bilva, the circle of pain, six that grow, the flower-stage, teaching, five flowers, the false elephant: seeking the Lord in these is nine crore.
nuance: The verse is a compressed list whose items cannot be fixed; தழல் மூன்று are traditionally the three sacred fires. நவகோடி may be nine crore or nine kinds. Some words may be corrupt.

title: சத்தி பேதம் - திரிபுரை சக்கரம்
theme: The distinctions of Shakti (சத்தி பேதம்): the Goddess Tripura, under many names (Tripurasundari, Manonmani, Parashakti, Abhirami, Bhuvanapati, Varahi, Omkari), is the source of the worlds, the tattvas, nada and bindu, speech and mantra, never apart from Siva; worshipped, she enters the poet's heart, clears his deluded mind and shows him the way to Siva.
structure_note: Each verse begins with the last word of the one before (அந்தாதி). Verses on her cosmic nature (1045 to 1048, 1052 to 1056, 1059, 1065, 1070, 1074) alternate with iconographic portraits (1049 to 1051, 1067, 1072, 1073) and with the poet's own experience of her entering him (1058, 1060, 1061, 1064, 1066). Despite the title, the verses do not describe the diagram of the Tripura chakra itself.
source_issues: 1063: line 1 reads நிறகும், a misprint for நிற்கும்.
1065: line 4 மண்டல முன்றுற is probably மூன்றுற (three); read so here.
1046 (மாமது), 1051 line 3 (நாற்கால் கரீடணி), 1056 (உராசத்தி), 1068 lines 3 and 4 and 1072 line 2 (ஈன வராகம்) are obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: Mahamaya, maya, the bindu-born, the spoken word, the Om-maya and the inner light, and the mantras that are herself among the six crores, are the forms of Shakti; being and not being, there is Tripura.
nuance: வயிந்தவம் (baindava, born of bindu) and வைகரி (vaikhari, speech at its spoken level) are terms of Saiva cosmology and mantra theory; ஓமாயை and ஓராறு கோடி (six crores, taken of the mantras) are obscure. ஆமாய் அலவாம் can be read 'she is and is not' or 'she is all and none of these'.

reading: Tripura, Sundari, Antari, the vermilion one, Paripurai, Narani, the one of many colours, Isi who removes darkness, Manonmani: by these names the great one stands as many.
nuance: A string of the Goddess's names; several (அந்தரி, of the sky; நாரணி, the female Narayana; மனோன்மனி, she who lifts the mind beyond mind) carry traditional meanings, others (பரிபுரை) are unclear. மாமது in the last line is obscure: 'the great one' or 'great honey'.

reading: In the three cities she formed herself, three forms of one nature, she who is gold, red and white is learning, and she herself grants enjoyment and release.
nuance: The three colours are traditionally matched with three goddesses (gold with Lakshmi, red with Durga or Shakti, white with Sarasvati) who are one Tripura; the verse only says three forms are one. Granting both போகம் and முத்தி, worldly enjoyment and release, is the claim Srividya makes for this goddess.

reading: Tripura grants nada and nada's end; the supreme bindu, which multiplies, becomes the earth and the worlds; Parai, Abhirami, she who is beyond the senses, embraces, gives grace, gives that wisdom and rules.
nuance: நாதாந்தம் (the end of nada) and பரவிந்து (supreme bindu) are stages of manifestation in Saiva cosmology. அகோசரி is 'she who is not an object of the senses'. போதம் is taken as wisdom; the last line is compressed.

reading: Anklets on her feet, red silk her garment, breasts bound with a band, the sugarcane bow and flower arrows, the goad and the noose, a fine crown, and earrings of dark great gems: such is she.
nuance: A portrait of Tripurasundari with her standard emblems. Tradition reads the noose as desire or attachment, the goad as restraint, the sugarcane bow as the mind and the five flower arrows as the senses; the verse gives the emblems without their meanings.

reading: She with earrings, with brows like a killing bow, with a form of lasting blood-red colour, with beads and necklace, rayed crown and the great moon, Chandika stands holding up the four directions.
nuance: The gentle portrait of 1049 turns fierce here: கொலைவில் (killing bow) and சண்டிகை (Chandika, the fierce goddess) show the same goddess in her terrible aspect. கண்டிகை is usually a bead string, often rudraksha.

reading: Tripura who stands, the ancient one who extends, the undiminishing Mohini, the one of the crest, who knows the good, who wears beads, Karidani of four limbs, the pure one of the pure lotus.
nuance: Another list of names. மாதிருக்கும் சிகை and நாற்கால் கரீடணி are obscure; the second may be a corrupt form of a Sanskrit name. Only புராதனி (the ancient), மோகினி (the enchantress) and சுத்தை (the pure) are clear.

reading: She is the tattvas, the heavy-breasted, the rising of bliss; as the substance she rules, the great Shakti, the great Parai; all those things, and the smaller than the atom, she is, and she is the mind of the form she set up.
nuance: பாரத தனத்தி is taken as பார தனத்தி (of heavy breasts); சுகோதயள் is 'rising of bliss' and வத்துவம் is vastu, substance or reality. அணோரணி echoes the Upanishadic 'smaller than the small'. The last line (கோல மதியவள்) can also mean she is the moon of that form.

reading: There are no gods who do not know her, no rare austerity done without her, nothing the five can achieve without her, and without her I know no way of entering the city.
nuance: The plainest verse of the chapter, built on the repeated அவளன்றி (without her). ஐவர் (the five) are traditionally the five gods who perform the five acts, but may be the five senses; ஊர் (the town) is traditionally the city of release or Siva's realm.

reading: The knowers say Parashakti is bliss; they say she is both formless and with form; they say action is her will; and the knowers say the Supreme too is in her.
nuance: The verse reports what knowers (அறிவார்) say rather than asserting it in the poet's voice. பரனும் அவளிடத்தான் can mean the Supreme is within her or is on her side, as in the half-woman form; either way Siva and Shakti are not apart.

reading: Wherever he is, there is the lady Mahadevi; wherever there is flesh, he is there as the breath of the life within; wherever the sky is, he is there and beyond it: see the many signs of the king who stands everywhere.
nuance: உள்ளுயிர்க் காலவன் is taken as கால் (wind, breath) of the inner life; it could also be read with காலம் (time). The verse moves from his inseparability from the Goddess to his presence in bodies and beyond the sky.

reading: You do not grasp how Parashakti, Mahashakti, stands in many ways as the power of the earth, as the strong power through every age; Parashakti is the enjoyment that is merit.
nuance: தராசத்தி (the earth's power) is fairly clear; உராசத்தி is obscure, taken as 'strong power' or 'the power in the breast'. The last line makes the Goddess herself the fruit of merit (புண்ணியம்) enjoyed.

reading: Sharing half his body with the curl-haired Shakti who brings enjoyment, he stands there as Parashakti; taking a body there, she is the branch along which the knowledge that ripens devotees spreads each day.
nuance: பாகஞ்செய்து is read first as sharing a half (the half-woman form) and then, in பாகஞ்செய் ஞானம், as ripening; the pun is the verse's hinge. கொம்பு (branch, creeper's support) prepares the next verse's கொம்பனையாள. Who is subject of the first two lines, Siva or Shakti, is not fixed.

reading: Trusting, I desired and placed within me the one like a creeper, the maiden of full breasts with a fragrant opening garland, the one of the channel shining to the sky, the little girl whose holy body is red coral.
nuance: The love lyric's vocabulary turned on the Goddess. வானவிர் நாடி is taken as the nadi that shines up to the sky, traditionally the central channel; a plain reading is less clear. நம்பி may be 'trusting' or an address to a man ('O Nambi').

reading: The things set in place, the many lives that join bodies, the ten faces, Parai and Paraparai, the workings of the mind and its instruments, and the Shakti who makes them act: of all these she is the head of knowledge.
nuance: பத்து முகம் (ten faces) may be the ten directions or ten forms of the Goddess. வித்தைத் தலையவள் is read as the head of vidya (knowledge), and is a name in Srividya; it may also be the head of all the listed things.

reading: The leader, the lady of broad breasts, the peacock of the pure path who does unending austerity, the maiden who conquers many arts, has filled my heart and stands here so that it is steady.
nuance: தொலைவில் தவம் is read as தொலைவு இல், austerity without end; it could also be austerity done far off. The Goddess as one who herself does tapas is a well-known image (Parvati's penance for Siva). The verse's point is the last line: her filling the heart makes it stable.

reading: She who stood, the finely jewelled one, joined with the long kala, settled into my inner self while the seven worlds worship her; at one with the hall, Manonmani the auspicious became one with me and, matching me, closed it.
nuance: நீள்கலை (the long kala) is technical and unclear. மன்று (the hall) may be the hall of Siva's dance at Tillai or its inner counterpart. ஒத்து அடைத்தாள் ('matching, she closed') may mean she shut the doors of the senses or closed the way of return; the verse does not say.

reading: People do not discern how Manonmani, the auspicious, the jewelled one in the lotus where all subsides alike, who does all this as the great Lord, closes off the mind that churns.
nuance: The word order is compressed and the reading is tentative. மத்து (churning stick) is taken of the agitated mind; சித்தடைக்கும் வழி is read as the way she stops the mind (சித்தம்), in keeping with மனோன்மனி, she who lifts beyond mind.

reading: Knowing, she stands at once as the inner light; when the lady of fragrant flower-hair and he stand joined, she grants the goal to those who rise, ripened.
nuance: கணிந்தெழுவார் is taken as கனிந்து எழுவார், those who rise ripened; it could also be 'those who reckon and rise'. The union of Siva and Shakti is the condition of grace in this reading.

reading: The girl gentle as grace, Ananda Sundari, looked at my inner self, like a mean fruit gone sour, made it clear, showed me the way to Siva, set me in light and took me into herself so that I would be saved.
nuance: அளி is grace or the bee; 'bee-like girl' is also possible. The fruit image runs to the end: the sour fruit is made clear and sweet, and உண்டாள் (she ate) completes it, the soul consumed by the Goddess as its rescue.

reading: What was called 'is' and 'is not' took form and stood, settled and filled the hall of rich Tillai; they have not seen it: with the cause and she who causes, she stands settled so the three spheres are joined.
nuance: தில்லை மன்று is the hall at Chidambaram where Siva dances. காரண காரணி may be 'the cause and the causing one', Siva and Shakti. மண்டலம் முன்றுற is read as மூன்று, the three spheres traditionally of sun, moon and fire; the line is uncertain.

reading: She stood as his body and life; Parashakti, who joins the way to Siva, went in and, entering me as one, became my awareness; the supreme light stood with her whose hand holds the leaf.
nuance: சென்றான் and நின்றான் are masculine while the subject seems to be Shakti; the verse may move between the two as one. ஏடங்கையாள் is taken as 'she with the palm-leaf book in her hand', a Sarasvati attribute; ஏடு may also be a petal.

reading: The lady with the leaf in her hand, our sovereign, the three-eyed one, whose guise is crystal, who loves the white lotus: wear Parvati's feet, sung in the holy hymns, on your head, and let your mouth speak her praise.
nuance: Crystal, the white lotus and the book are Sarasvati's marks, given here to Parvati, so the verse makes the goddesses one. திருமுறை may mean the sacred hymns generally or the Saiva canon by name.

reading: Praising and worshipping her paired feet so that they are gained, the way of worship is set; she who looks out with goad, noose and green sugarcane, the flower-child, is everything to the Primal One.
nuance: Lines 3 and 4 repeat பார்த்திடும் and are obscure; பசுங்கரும்பு may be the green sugarcane bow of 1049. வழிபடு மாறிடும் may mean 'the way of worship' or 'worship changes (one)'.

reading: Placing in the middle the name of the jewelled one on the flower, the younger sister of Mal who in many ways made the world, and practising it many times on the fingers, light grows and all three times appear.
nuance: The Goddess as Vishnu's (மால்) sister is a common Saiva identification. The practice looks like repeating her name or mantra counted on the fingers, with knowledge of past, present and future (முக்காலம்) as its fruit; பாதியில் வைத்து (placing in the half or middle) and நீதி மலர் are unclear.

reading: The gentle one who is the sixteen beginning with Medha, Paraparai who shines in the texts beginning with the Veda, she who is the support and spreads as the examined expanse, is the good grace of nada and what precedes nada.
nuance: மேதாதி ஈரெட்டும் (sixteen beginning with Medha) is traditionally taken of sixteen kalas or powers; the list is not given. ஆதாரம் may be the bodily centres (ādhāras) as well as 'support'.

reading: Come, you people, and hear it from those who have received grace: I praise the red feet, which hold the rare true thing, of Bhuvanapati, who turns the deluded mind into a mind that has found the true thing.
nuance: The verse turns on பொருள (the true thing, meaning) and மருள் (delusion). Read this way, பொருள்பெற்ற சிந்தை describes the mind she gives, not her own; the line also allows 'Bhuvanapati of the mind that holds the truth'.

reading: She of the boar's face and her station, with the pestle that pounds the base boar and holding the other weapon, the plough, the white-smiling one rises high in the hearts of those who know her without flaw.
nuance: A portrait of Varahi, the boar-faced goddess, whose traditional weapons are the pestle and plough. ஈன வராகம் (the base boar) in line 2 is obscure; it may be a boar-demon or a corruption.

reading: She is called Omkari, a girl of unfading green; becoming Ahankari she bore the five, and she sits sweetly within Hrinkara.
