nuance: ஓங்காரி (she who is Om), ஆங்காரி (she who is ahamkara, the sense of I) and ரீங்காரம் (the seed syllable hrim, sacred to the Goddess) play on one sound. ஐவர் may be the five gods or the five elements, which in Samkhya arise through ahamkara.

reading: Tatparai, who stood as the leader herself, herself sowed lives and gave the fourteen worlds, the place of the gods, the mind and good intellect; she herself is also the nature of the way to Siva.
nuance: The repeated தானே (she herself) gathers the chapter: creation, the inner faculties and the path to release are all hers. பதினாலும் is taken as the fourteen worlds, which the verse doesn't name.

title: வயிரவி மந்திரம்
theme: The Bhairavi mantra (வயிரவி மந்திரம்): the goddess Bhairavi, also called Tripura and Manonmani, is a mantra of twelve kalas to be laid out, worshipped and recited with its rites, and she is the Shakti in whom the gods have their cause, who enters the devotee's heart, wakes him, takes away his deeds and births, and reveals Siva.
structure_note: The mantra's count of kalas and the lunar days of practice (1075 to 1080); her form and her worship in the lotus (1081 to 1087); the rites of the mantra, with breath, finger-placing, the limbs of the mantra, mudras and seed-letters (1088 to 1096); then a hymn of praise in which she enters the poet's heart (1097 to 1124). Each verse opens with the closing word of the one before, and the last verse returns to the twelve of the first.
source_issues: 1082: line 3 reads ஒப்fபது, with a stray Latin f; the line is probably corrupt beyond that.
1113: line 3 reads ஒன்fறி, a stray f for ஒன்றி.
1118: line 2 reads துன்னியங fகைவரை, a stray f; probably துன்னியங்கு ஐவரை.
1101: line 4 reads உய்ய்க்கொண்டாளே, probably a misprint for உய்யக்கொண்டாளே.
1115: line 1 reads மேலி, probably a misprint for மேவி (cf. 1113 மேவி).
1077 lines 2 and 3, 1079 line 3 (பரிபிடி அந்தம்), 1090 line 3 (பிரைச்சதம்) and 1117 are obscure and may be corrupt.
1075 spells the goddess பயிரவி; the chapter heading and later verses have வயிரவி.

reading: Take Bhairavi as the first, with twelve kalas, conceive in her the letter A and maya, and with the twelve from the start and the fourteen at the end recite the place of speech as the end of sixteen.
nuance: The numbers (பன்னிரண்டு, பதினாலு, சோடம் for sixteen) belong to the arrangement of the mantra and are not explained. ஆகாரம் may be the long vowel ஆ or 'form'. The verse spells the name பயிரவி; the heading has வயிரவி.

reading: The fourteen at the end is Bhairavi herself; the great Shakti who rises in the lotus of the mind, as beginning, middle and end, becomes both the end and the beginning.
nuance: சிந்தை கமலம், the lotus of the mind, is usually taken as the heart-lotus of meditation. The point that she is end and beginning at once is plain; what the fourteen count is not.

reading: The three who come into being are absorbed in her there; Tripura goes with those of merit so that they gain light, while the ancient ones who cling to the passing elements and those who do not reach the refuge do not.
nuance: ஆகின்ற மூவர் are traditionally Brahma, Vishnu and Rudra. Lines 2 and 3 (புராதரர், சாரவுழிச் சாரார்) are obscure, and the contrast between them and the புண்ணியத்தோர் is my reading of the syntax.

reading: Nandi, holy and pure, becomes the goddess; with the moon that circles through the reckoned twenty-seven days, and the fire, the sun and the moon's end that were set, the one of firm mind becomes the Southern one too.
nuance: திரு may be the goddess, Sri or simply holiness. The twenty-seven days are the lunar asterisms, so the verse seems to set the practice by the moon. தென்னன், the Southerner or the Pandya, is taken as a name of Siva; the whole verse is obscure.

reading: For the one who stands reciting Tripura, the earth on the golden mountain praises the Southern one, holy Nandi, with his attendant, and with the Lord at the end of the mantra.
nuance: பரிபிடி அந்தம் is obscure; it may name the closing of the mantra or a seat of worship. பொன்னங்கிரி, the golden mountain, is usually Meru or Kailasa.

reading: Nandi who taught knows grace and declares it rightly by the way of the Veda: when the knowing joined with the moon runs twenty-seven days, the trident of radiant Bhairavi comes to rule.
nuance: The twenty-seven days again tie the practice to the lunar month. The trident's 'ruling' is commonly taken as her protection or possession of the practiser; the verse does not say which.

reading: The trident-bearer who holds trident and skull has a fourth pair of hands holding noose and goad; she is the gentle one who stands as the upper limb of the form that Vishnu and Brahma could not know.
nuance: The form Vishnu and Brahma could not know is Siva's column of fire; the goddess is placed as part of it (மேல்அங்கம்), which is read as her being half of Siva's body. நாலாங் கரம் can also be read as four hands in all.

reading: The gentle vine-like one, knower of the kalas and of wisdom, jewelled and of the colour of the kinjuka flower, has a holy body like stone and wears garments of many kinds and many gems.
nuance: கிஞ்சுகம், the palasa flower, makes her red. விடமி (she of poison?) is obscure, and line 3 is corrupt in the text, so 'like stone' is a guess at கல்லியல் ஒப்பது.

reading: Her crown has many gems, like ten million moons; she wears gem earrings and has a doe's eyes; her good gem-eyes are sun and moon, and she brims with golden gems and with fire.
nuance: சூரிய சோம நயனம் with வன்னி gives the three eyes of sun, moon and fire, the third eye shared with Siva. The verse is a description for visualising her, as 1082 is.

reading: Within the eight petals of the full-blown flower there is a noble lady; there are eight maidens there, and the sixty-four women spread around came near and saw the Shakti.
nuance: The eight-petalled lotus is a worship diagram. The eight maidens and sixty-four women are traditionally her attendant powers (the eight mothers and sixty-four yoginis), but the verse names none of them.

reading: With anklets, bangles, conch and discus seen on her, the yogini of the eight directions, the Goddess, Parashakti, the gracious one who bears the cosmos and the eight directions, is worshipped within the lotus.
nuance: Conch and discus are Vishnu's emblems; here they are hers, as the verses after say that the gods are forms of her.

reading: With worship, scent, adorned flowers and great banners, in contemplation the sound of the five comes and speaks; in the gem-mantra yoga that needs no dwelling, see Tripura shining in her radiance.
nuance: பஞ்சத்து ஒலி, the sound of the five, may be the five-syllable mantra or five inner sounds. வாசம் இலாத may mean without scent or without abode. The verse moves from outer worship to inner hearing and sight.

reading: The many gods one sees are each different, just as the many ornaments worn appear many though they are gold; see that the Mistress is the good cause of Siva, Brahma and Vishnu whom people honour.
nuance: The gold and ornaments image is the classic one for one substance in many forms. Here even Siva is among the forms caused by her, which the hymn later balances by calling him her husband and the light (1119, 1123).

reading: The Karani mantra recited in the lotus, joined with filling, holding and emptying the breath, and Narani, set in the middle as Nandi taught, are the end of the Vedic books too.
nuance: பூரண கும்ப விரேசம் is read as பூரகம், கும்பகம், இரேசகம், the three phases of breath control. காரணி and நாரணி are names of the goddess. ஆரண வேதநூல் அந்தம் may simply mean Vedanta.

reading: From the end, the middle finger, to the beginning, the little finger, recite reversing the order in which it came; understand clearly the start of fine Tamil and worship: Nandi taught this as new.
nuance: The verse describes placing the mantra's syllables on the fingers. செந்தமிழ் ஆதி may be the Tamil letters from அ, or Tamil as the first speech. நவம் can mean new or nine; 1090 begins with நவசத்தி, the nine Shaktis.

reading: When the nine Shaktis spoken of are finished one by one, counting the long order of the zodiac signs, Nandi, who earlier spoke of the eight, set them in order and fixed rule and observance.
nuance: பிரைச்சதம் எட்டு is obscure. நியதி நியமம் may be the rule of practice or the second limb of yoga. The verse seems to tie the nine powers to the cycle of signs.

reading: She of garlanded tresses and merciful eyes, the young vine who stands within and scatters the darkness of the night: see the fine smoke rise inside the great flame of the fire rite, mingle and return with nectar.
nuance: அழுதொடு is read as அமுதொடு, with nectar; as written it could mean 'with weeping'. ஏமத்து இருள் may be the darkness of night or of delusion. The fire rite may be outward or the inner fire.

reading: Seeing the heart mantra, say 'nama' in honour; upon the head the oblation set in the middle; and the end said to be worn in the middle is for the topknot.
nuance: The verse runs through the limbs of the mantra placed on the body (அங்க நியாசம்): heart with namah, head with the oblation word (ஆகுதி, svaha), topknot (சிகை) with its ending. Lines 3 and 4 are compressed and the endings are the tradition's, not named.

reading: With the armour at the end of the topknot, then turning to look at the limb that stands as enemy, and then the eye, the mudras, the trident, and the yoni in its kind can be formed.
nuance: கவசம் (armour), நேத்திரம் (eye) and the limb 'that stands as enemy' continue the limbs of the mantra; the last is commonly taken as the weapon (astra). Then the hand-seals: trident and yoni.

reading: Crossing the two little fingers, joining them, pointing and holding with the ring fingers, pressing them together and setting the two thumbs within the middle, speak.
nuance: A hand-seal described finger by finger, taken as the yoni mudra of 1093. வருத்தம் இரண்டும் is obscure, and which fingers அணிவிரல் and பெருத்த விரல் are is the usual reading, not certain.

reading: Recite the spoken mantra dividing it by its sounds; taking the sa-letter first without hesitation, for the teaching of the breath and prana, take it with the shrinking bindu and call.
nuance: சகாரம் and the bindu (the nasal dot) build a seed-syllable. இராகம் may be tone or the mantra's parts; வாசி is the breath. The exact syllable is not recoverable from the verse.

reading: With the soul that was called and prana first, with the spread 'sau' and the ya-letter made, with maya joined and the wide conch mudra, the Goddess shone in the middle.
nuance: சவ் and யகாரம் are seed-letters; சவ் is the familiar bija of Tripura worship. The verse ends the rite with the goddess present in the middle of the diagram or of the body.

reading: Bhairavi who stands, the dark one, the night-walker, the Lady who goes in grace into the heart where one and two have joined, for the Lord of the gods: seek her, proclaiming her in the world she graces well.
nuance: நீலி and நிசாசரி are fierce names. ஒன்றும் இரண்டும் ஒருங்கிய உள்ளம் may be the heart where the soul and the Lord, or Siva and Shakti, are one. From here the chapter becomes a hymn.

reading: The first mother stands with her power as the Veda that was proclaimed, the moving and unmoving, the five elements, the four directions, the three-eyed one, darkness and open space, the many lives that appear, the light and Parapara.
nuance: A list identifying her with everything, from scripture and the elements to Siva himself (முக்கண்ணி can be she of three eyes) and the supreme (பராபரை).

reading: If one recites and realises primal Bhairavi abiding at the virgin's shore, body and life become the Lord, births in this foolish world are destroyed, and an unending form becomes one.
nuance: கன்னித்துறை is often taken as Kanyakumari, where the goddess is a virgin; it may also be an inner place. உடலுயிர் ஈசனாம் can mean body and soul become the Lord, or that the Lord is the soul of the body.

reading: The lovely girl, with eyes like the blue water-lily under curving brows, Ananda Sundari, the sweet nectar that delights, revealed the Siva above.
nuance: Shakti reveals Siva: the hymn's recurring claim that the way to Siva is through her. மேலைச் சிவம் may be Siva beyond, or Siva at the crown of the head.

reading: She revealed, made me know the fruit, made it clear within my mind, made me rejoice, made the rayed light shine, and took me so that I was saved.
nuance: Five lines of the causative -வித்து (made to) give a sequence: revelation, understanding, clarity, joy, light, rescue. The poet speaks in the first person, as through most of the hymn.

reading: She took countless millions of forms, she saw the garlands in the eye of the sixty-four kalas, and she opened the three wide rays above: the fine woman who stands above the head.
nuance: எண்ணெண் கலை are the sixty-four arts or kalas. The three rays are traditionally sun, moon and fire. தண்டலை may be the top of the spine (தண்டு) or a grove; the yogic sense is likely but not fixed.

reading: Stand and praise slowly and bow to the fine woman, the leader of austerity, Manonmani who looks on delusion; once you have bowed, cruel births will not come again.
nuance: மையலை நோக்கும் can be 'who looks upon (and so ends) delusion'. Bowing as the end of births is an old pattern; here it is to the goddess.

reading: She of bamboo-like shoulders, with tresses set with fragrant soft flowers, wearing the young crescent, the beautiful trident-bearer with the pure crown of hair, has sat sweetly in my heart.
nuance: The crescent and trident are Siva's marks, worn by her. The verse turns from description to her dwelling in the poet, which the following verses develop.

reading: The maiden who dwells in the sweet southern corner, the sole lady and leader herself, set me apart, brought me to refuge, filled me, and stands seeking my heart.
nuance: தென் மூலை is the southern corner, perhaps Kanyakumari again (1099); மூலை may also hint at மூலம், the base of the spine. தனிப்படுவித்தனள் may be 'made me single' or 'made me unique'.

reading: The maiden of the clan, joined with wisdom where the three channels rise through the middle, sleeps within, the fresh gold anklets on her small feet sounding.
nuance: The sleeping maiden in the middle of the three channels is traditionally kundalini, coiled until woken. The verse does not use the word; குலக்கன்னி may echo kula, the base. Why she sleeps while the channels rise is unclear.

reading: While I slept, Manonmani came, embraced my neck with her jingling bangled arms, spat her shining betel into my mouth, said 'Do not sleep, sir', and gave me the means.
nuance: உறங்கும் அளவில் may be the poet's sleep or follow on from her sleep in 1106. Giving her chewed betel is an image of intimate grace known from devotional legend. உபாயம், the means, is taken as the yogic method of waking.

reading: The one who gives the means rooted out all danger from my heart, made love grow, held craving down inside the whirl that lights the breath, and said 'Fear not'.
nuance: சுவா is read as the breath (சுவாசம்), and சுழி as a whirl or centre in the body; both are uncertain. அஞ்சல் is the gesture and word of reassurance.

reading: They say that she of sweet speech, the girl of rare austerity, of true and gentle words, richly jewelled, is the goddess who gives sweet words to those who praise her red feet, thinking her their refuge.
nuance: The verse repeats sweet speech in her and as her gift. என்றாரே, 'they said', presents it as the word of others, not the poet's own.

reading: The girl of rare austerity who is dear life, Karani and Narani within the dark-tressed one, the fierce one who withdraws towns, lives and worlds, plays in my heart.
nuance: ஒடுக்கிடும், withdraws, gives her the act of dissolution, one of the five acts. Fierce and tender names sit together through the hymn.

reading: The lovely maiden who played shone in my heart, joined it for many days, moved there and came to know it, and is the one at the head of the kalas who mingles within the crown of the head.
nuance: The movement from heart to crown (உச்சி) suggests the yogic rising of Shakti. கலைத்தலை may be the summit of the kalas or of the moon's digits at the head.

reading: In the eye of the forehead that has one eye, at the head of the kalas, the breasted woman stays embraced; looking to the discernment at the bow's head, the swaying flower-branch stayed there.
nuance: The forehead eye and சிலைத்தலை (the head of the bow, the brow) point to the place between the eyebrows. Whom she embraces is left unsaid; it is usually taken as Siva.

reading: The jewelled one sat, entering my heart; she entered the four fingers' space and embraced, joined with the perfected pillar and became one with it, and the primal one attained rare austerity.
nuance: தாணு, the pillar, is a name of Siva. நால்விரல் may be a measure of four finger-breadths in the body. Line 3 is corrupt in the text; ஒன்றி is read.

reading: The beginning and the beginningless, the causeless and the cause, the light of light, Sundari of supreme bliss, the woman, samadhi, Manonmani, the auspicious one, recited, joined my heart.
nuance: A string of names held together in paradox: beginning and beginningless, causeless and cause. Line 3 recurs in 1120, and line 1 in 1124.

reading: The jewelled one joined my heart and raised it; she desired there the words 'namasiva'; she grasps the state that knows Brahma; she moved and cut away all my other babble.
nuance: நமசிவ is the five-syllable mantra. அயன்தனை ஓரும் பதம் is obscure: perhaps the word that knows the creator, or the state beyond him. பிதற்று, babble, is the idle speech the mantra replaces. மேலி is probably மேவி.

reading: Foolish people babbled and passed away; before those whose effort is complete stand the first mother who grants grace, her three fish-bright eyes, her red mouth that speaks, and the gracious look of her face.
nuance: முயற்றியின் முற்றி may mean 'when effort is complete' or 'complete in effort'. கம்பலை (clamour, sound) with செவ்வாய் is unusual.

reading: Within the three, mind, heart and breast, a child's path was born as it was spoken; in the womb of the bountiful Tiru, the virgin is the intent of the stealthy light of Mahamaya.
nuance: The verse is obscure throughout. உள்ளம், இதயம், நெஞ்சம் are three inner seats. கள்ள ஒளி, stealthy light, fits maya as what both shows and hides. It prepares the virgin mother of 1118.

reading: The virgin, and the virgin undone, the beloved of pure words, bore the five; the lords of the well-made books are there too: what is this? This maya is darkness itself.
nuance: The paradox of a virgin who is mother. ஐவர, the five, are traditionally the five gods of the five acts. Line 2 is corrupt in the text. Whether 'this maya is darkness' rebukes those who cannot grasp the paradox or names her as maya is open.

reading: Darkness is Shakti and light is our Lord; the substance is the joy in the enjoyment of the meritorious; if one, in clarity, thinks of the mind as god, our primal Lord grants grace.
nuance: Shakti as darkness and Siva as light can be read as concealing and revealing, two of the five acts. Line 4 may also be read 'if one thinks of god with a clear mind'.

reading: Parashakti, who is beginning and beginningless, the green-bangled one dwelling above as Parapara and as the half, the woman, samadhi, Manonmani, the auspicious one, blossomed together in my reciting heart.
nuance: பாதி, the half, is her place as the left half of Siva. The verse repeats 1114 nearly line for line but ends 'blossomed' (முகிழ்த்தாள்) instead of 'joined'.

reading: As it is recited, people do not know that the highest of the kalas is the Veda from the beginning; the mistress of the cow declared that he stands as caste, difference and the tattvas, and is the first.
nuance: ஆவின் கிழத்தி, mistress of the cow, also reads as mistress of souls, since ஆ (cow) and pasu are one word; 1122 ties her to Tiruvavaduturai. Who 'stands as caste and difference' is unclear; perhaps the Lord, perhaps her.

reading: The mistress of the cow, the mistress of the cool shore of good Avaduturai, the mistress of speech whom they praise, the mistress of the gods, Siva's woman who is Tiru, the mistress who abides, drove out my deeds.
nuance: ஆவடுதண்துறை is Tiruvavaduturai, where tradition places Tirumular's life and his entering the cowherd's body; the cow names gain local weight here. நாவின் கிழத்தி may be Sarasvati as a form of her.

reading: Abiding as the inner light in the hearts of those whose deeds are driven out, she stands as the tattva for all who reach her; the jewelled one who made me her servant becomes the beginningless too, so that one may see the Lord her husband.
nuance: Picking up வினைகடிந்தாள் from 1122. Line 4 is compressed: she is the way to seeing Siva, and is called beginningless as he is.

reading: The beginning and the beginningless, the causeless and the cause, she searched out the Veda; the light that stood for the Vedic ones, standing in the form of a lone flame, is Parapara, the half, the first of the twelve.
nuance: பன்னிரண்டு ஆதி returns to the twelve kalas of the opening verse, closing the chapter as a ring. Line 1 repeats 1114.

title: பூரண சக்தி
theme: Full Shakti (பூரண சக்தி): the goddess, Parashakti, is the Lord's own power and consort, mother of all within the bonds, the powers of knowledge, will and action, bindu and nada, and the light that rises through the lotuses of the yogic body. The chapter ends in praise of her names and a complaint that people speak of the Lord without knowing her.
structure_note: The verses are linked end to beginning (அந்தாதி: கும்பகம் closes 1126 and opens 1127, பாலன் closes 1134 and opens 1135, and so on). Roughly: Shakti and Siva in union and as the soul's parents (1125 to 1137); Shakti as bindu, nada and the light in the yogic lotuses (1138 to 1146); a run of praise verses naming her (1147 to 1153); and a closing reproach (1154).
source_issues: 1129: line 3 reads உரைசெய்Yயும் with a stray Latin Y; read உரைசெய்யும்.
1147: line 4 reads றா\ளே with a stray backslash; read றாளே.
1149: line 3 மண் லடத்தொளி is probably மண்டலத்து ஒளி, split wrongly.
1144: line 3 மத்தகச் தேசெல is malformed, perhaps மத்தகத்தே செல.
1146: line 2 (பரந்தன வாயு திசை தோறும்) is short by a foot; a word may be lost.
1141: பழினெட்டு is not a standard form (perhaps பதினெட்டு); 1130 and 1141 look like variants of one verse.
1131 and 1153: the -ஐயமாய் compounds of 1131 and the opening தாவித of 1153 are obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: Tirumular says he has measured the bounds of the wide world, its first Lord, and male and female in it, and that he measured them by examining and coming to know the Lord's grace.
nuance: அளந்தேன் (I measured) opens all four lines. ஆணொடு பெண் may be the male and female of the world or Siva and Shakti; in a chapter on Shakti the second is likely, and the grace (அருள்) by which he measured is traditionally Shakti herself.

reading: People have not known the Lord; the Shakti who brings about the ages joined him and that is fullness, and by the path the maiden who graces the companies of the meritorious brings, breath retention comes.
nuance: பூரணம் (fullness) gives the chapter its title and is also the yogic term for drawing the breath in; with கும்பகம் (holding it) at the end, the verse seems to play on the stages of pranayama. கன்னி, the maiden, is a name of Shakti, ever virgin though consort. How the clauses connect is not clear from the verse.

reading: The five elephants, their mahout with his goad, the jewel-crowned Lord and the lady who dwells sweetly in blissful union all merge and are lost in the union of love.
nuance: கும்பக் களிறு ஐந்து, five elephants with swelling temples, are traditionally the five senses and the mahout the mind or the soul; கும்பம் picks up கும்பகம் from 1126. ஆயொழிந்தாரே, they became and ended, is read as absorption. The image is symbolic and the verse does not name its terms.

reading: Our father can enter only into the love set in blissful union, and within the bond where people suffer in a mire of sorrow, Parashakti, my mother, is there in the very bones.
nuance: The verse divides the parents: the father reached through love, the mother present inside bondage. என்பிற் is read here as 'in the bone', the body; it could also be a form of என்பது. The rhyme of அன்பு and என்பு is old in Tamil.

reading: Once the conceit of saying 'my mother, my father' is gone, your mother and the Lord of the ages are both there; the great Nandi, joined with her as the abiding mother, stands as the mother after.
nuance: The first line is clear: claiming the divine parents as one's own is a pride (செருக்கு) to be cut. The rest is obscure: பின்னம்மை may be 'the later mother' or பின்னம் (division) with அம்மை, and the subject of the last two lines may be Nandi or Shakti. The point the tradition draws is that the Lord is both father and mother.

reading: The four-faced Brahma of the cool flower, the hundred on the earth and the teacher who dwells on the flower all come by the command of the lady who dwells on the tongue.
nuance: நாமேல் உறைகின்ற நாயகி, the lady on the tongue, is the goddess of speech, here taken as Shakti. போதகம் may be 'teaching' or a 'teacher', and ஒரு நூறு (a hundred) is unexplained. The verse is nearly repeated as 1141.

reading: Those who stay within, gathering the deluding mind into one and then knowing the Supreme, become that one themselves.
nuance: Each line turns on a compound ending in -ஐயமாய் (ஆணையம், மாணையம், பாணையம், தாணையம்) whose senses are obscure; ஆணையம் picks up ஆணை from 1130. Only the outline (one-pointed mind, knowing the Supreme, becoming it) is fairly clear.

reading: The mistress of the tattvas, arising of herself, lit the moon as the gods rose; with the light of a lamp that wells with honey, know the hall of the dance.
nuance: மதியை விளக்கினள் can mean she lit the moon or she made the mind clear. மன்று is the hall where Siva dances, outward at Chidambaram or inward in the yogi's heart or head. மானே (O deer) addresses a woman, or names the goddess.

reading: When the grace of the lady who is knowledge, within maya and within the five senses, comes to one, she stays filling the mind of those who know the knowledge that does not part, as their path.
nuance: The verse makes Shakti knowledge both in maya and in the senses, so even bound knowing is hers. பிரியா அறிவு, knowledge that does not part, is traditionally knowledge inseparable from the Lord.

reading: One who seeks out the long-haired lady dancing in the place where there is neither night nor day, and sleeps there with grace in silence, becomes a child that age does not touch.
nuance: இரவும் பகலும் இலாத இடம் is traditionally the state beyond waking and sleep, or where the breaths called sun and moon cease. அரவம் is 'noise' but also 'serpent', so a reading in terms of kundalini is possible. பருவம் செய்யாத பாலன், a child that does not age, is the yogi's youth; பாலன் opens 1135.

reading: He becomes a child, and with Parashakti, leaving bindu and nada behind, he stands as the Supreme itself, meeting the release that is the root.
nuance: Bindu and nada are passed beyond, not reached, so they are here stages below release. தற்பரம் is the Supreme in itself. Whether the subject is the yogi of 1134 or the Lord is not settled by the verse.

reading: Parashakti, standing with the Supreme, becomes the power of knowledge and the power of will, and when the power of action arrives she enters into all the rest.
nuance: ஞானம், இச்சை and கிரியா are the three Shaktis of Saiva doctrine: knowing, willing and acting. The verse gives them an order, action last, through which she reaches everything else.

reading: No one perceives that the lady, like fragrance in a flower, and he stand together in one form; when they mingled, like an embryo forming, our father stood with his thought set on her as on fortune.
nuance: மருவொத்த can be 'like fragrance' (inseparable from the flower) or 'fitting'. கருவொத்து may be 'like an embryo' or 'in accord with the cause'. திரு may be Lakshmi, fortune or simply the sacred. The plain point, that Siva and Shakti are one form, is clear.

reading: The Siva-Shakti who moves within thought spread out as bindu and nada; she is the moon-ground, the one with matted hair, the pure one, of the nature of both end and beginning.
nuance: சந்திர பூமி, சடாதரி and சாத்தவி are names of the goddess; சாத்தவி may be 'the sattvic one' or a form of Shambhavi. சிந்தையின் உள்ளே places the cosmic bindu and nada in the mind.

reading: No one knows the reversed way of the nectar-breasted lady who stays quiet; steady, with the light of a good lamp, she wells up for those who have the inner sight.
nuance: அமுத பயோதரி, she whose breasts are nectar, is a name of the goddess. மாறி இருந்த வழி, the turned-back way, is traditionally the reversed course of breath or kundalini. உள்ளுடையார் may be those with inner vision or those who hold her within.

reading: The Lord who owns all, the fire, the light of Rudra, rides the bull and shines; the base fall away, and the practitioners who see him become his dwelling place in their hearts.
nuance: சாதகர் are practitioners of a discipline (sadhakas). The last two lines are compressed and the relation of கடையவர் போயிடும் to what follows is unclear.

reading: Her dwelling above is the six-petalled lotus; above the earth the petals number in hundreds; the merit that dwells on the flower has come, the lady of fresh bangles who dwells above the earth.
nuance: The petalled lotuses are traditionally the chakras of the yogic body; the counts (ஆறிதழ், பழினெட்டு, இருநூறு) can't be fixed from this text. The verse repeats the frame of 1130 almost line for line, with petals in place of Brahma.

reading: Because the lady of fresh bangles stays where the Supreme is, as his firm banner and holy light, and comes shining as a creeper across the sky, the world moves on as the woman's creeper.
nuance: கொடி means banner, creeper and, of a woman, slenderness; the verse plays on all three. The claim is that the world runs by her, as the creeper grows from its root in the Lord.

reading: The flower moved as four and five, the maidens sat as eight and one, it spread its own way inside the lotus and followed the inner way, close to the light.
nuance: Both pairs make nine; the maidens are commonly taken as the nine Shaktis seated in the heart lotus, eight round one. What the subject of படர்ந்தது and தொடர்ந்தது is (the flower, the light, the breath) is left open.

reading: The stacked lotuses are the seat of the Primal one: one rises within the house of the body, one goes up to the crown of the head, and one presses upward in the triple square.
nuance: முச்சதுரம் (triple square) is traditionally the base centre, drawn as a square; மத்தகம் is the head. The four kinds of lotus (அடுக்கும், எடுக்கும், மடுக்கும், முடுக்கும்) are a sound pattern whose technical sense is uncertain.

reading: The sprouting flame that rose in the triple square ran until it had a place in every square, and passing the square of the hand to gain the inner light, she stayed in all of them.
nuance: முளைச்சுடர், the sprout-flame, rising from the base square is traditionally kundalini. கைச்சதுரம் (square of the hand) is obscure. சதுரம் closes every line, picking up முச்சதுரம் from 1144.

reading: She stayed with faces six and four; the breaths spread to every quarter, drew together to look at the pearl-bright face, and the nectar flowed down.
nuance: ஆறொடு நாலாய் may be ten faces, one to each quarter, or six and four. தேறல் (honey, nectar) flowing அதோமுகம் (face downward) is traditionally the nectar from the crown. The final அம்பே may be 'arrow', 'water' or 'mother'.

reading: Manonmani, with eyes like arrows and a waist slender as a twig, garlanded, her body like worked red gold and fragrant, speaks every day with her eyes on the Lord.
nuance: மனோன்மணி is a name of Shakti in Saiva tantra, the power beyond mind. நவிலுகின்றாள் is 'speaks' or 'recites'; what she says is not given. The praise of her beauty follows the conventions of love poetry.

reading: The great goddess of whom the four Vedas speak, clothed in garments, her feet covering the ground, stands in majesty over the world and the whole cosmos, adorned with the three lights.
nuance: முச்சோதி, the three lights, are traditionally sun, moon and fire. நான்மறைச் சத்தி may mean the Shakti of whom the Vedas speak or the Shakti who is the Vedas. The second line's sense is unclear.

reading: I say praise to her who can adorn our Lord of the worlds, who can shape the countless cosmic eggs within, and who can adorn the light of the mandala.
nuance: புனைதல் (to adorn, compose) and வனைதல் (to shape, as a potter shapes clay) carry the verse: she is both the Lord's ornament and the maker of worlds.

reading: I hail the mother, mistress of the worlds, the young girl of rare penance who stands within my strength, the jewelled one of fair brow who put away anger, the one of fresh bangles who drives Death away.
nuance: அருந்தவப் பெண்பிள்ளை recalls the goddess as a girl doing penance to win Siva. என் ஆற்றலுள் நிற்கும, standing within my strength, makes her the poet's own power. சீற்றங் கடிந்த can mean she has put away anger or that she quells it.

reading: The bangled beauty from whom joy rises, the lady Tripura of fair form, Ganga, destroys the deeds of her devotees, thick as brushwood, and is also the Primal one.
nuance: சுகோதய சுந்தரி and திரிபுரை are names of the goddess. செடியார் வினை may be deeds thick as a bush or sinful deeds (செடி, sin). The third line (சேர்வரை என்றென்) is obscure.

reading: She of soft sound, a tender creeper of the sky, she of many sounds, a fruitful creeper, drove out the doll of mean sound and entered the mind as the doll of mighty sound.
nuance: இசை is sound and also fame, and பாவை a doll or a woman. The four kinds of sound may be the levels of speech from subtle to gross, as tradition reads such lists; புல்லிசை may equally be ill repute driven out of the mind. புகுந்தானே has a masculine ending where புகுந்தாளே would be expected.

reading: Our Lord is himself the goal of penance; when he conceives and makes the world, Parashakti joins him and runs through it above and below, and that very one becomes the life of all.
nuance: பாவித்து, conceiving or contemplating, makes creation an act of the Lord's thought, with Shakti as its extension. ஆவிக்கும் may be 'for the soul' or 'that gives life'. The opening word தாவித is obscure.

reading: Not knowing him, people call him this or that; they do not see the cause that stands for release to come, and they neither consider the constancy of the great lady with flowered tresses nor examine and know.
nuance: The chapter closes with a reproach: speaking of the Lord without knowing his Shakti is to miss the cause through which release (கதி) comes. திதம் is steadiness or standing.

title: சுத்த சைவம்
theme: Pure Saivism (சுத்த சைவம்): the Lord who makes all things includes the four kinds of Saivism, and the pure Saiva is one who has discerned the real and the unreal, learned and practised in order, and passed through Vedanta and Siddhanta to the end of nada and the Supreme.
structure_note: 1419 introduces the four kinds of Saivism treated in this chapter and the next three; 1420 to 1422 describe the pure Saiva and the Siddhantin.
source_issues: 1419: line 3 (மூவுல காளி யிலங்கெழுந்) is obscure and may be corrupt.
1422: line 3 (புதாந்த போதாந்த மாதுப் புனஞ்செய்ய) is obscure; புதாந்த is probably பூதாந்த.

reading: To consider the greatness of the all-knowing one who makes town and world alike is to see that Meru, the three worlds and the earth are his, and so are the four kinds of Saivism.
nuance: நால்வகைச் சைவம், the four kinds of Saivism, are taken as the subjects of this chapter and the next three (pure, impure, path and severe pure). Line 3 (மூவுலகாளி யிலங்கெழுந்) is obscure, and how Meru and the worlds bear on the four kinds is unclear.

reading: Pure Saivas, having discerned the real, the unreal and what is both, keeping clear of the sentient and the insentient and untouched by pure and impure, hold the eternal Supreme dear.
nuance: சத்து, அசத்து and சதசத்து are in Siddhanta usually the Lord (real), the bonds (unreal) and the soul (real-unreal), and சித்து, அசித்து the sentient and insentient; that is the tradition's mapping, which the verse does not spell out. The pure Saiva is defined by discernment and by not being touched, not by outward marks.

reading: Those who learn what is to be learned, go step by step through the true yoga in which the kalas abide and the knowledge of the earlier stages, reach the stage of the word and, rid of fault, see the Supreme beyond: they are the Saiva Siddhantins.
nuance: முறைமுறை (in due order) makes the way a sequence: learning, yoga, knowledge, then the Supreme. முற்பத ஞானம் and சொற்பதம் are technical and can't be fixed here; சொற்பதம் may be the stage of the word or mantra, or the stage words can reach.

reading: Those who have seen pure Vedanta, the clear Siddhanta and the end of nada have unwavering sight; those full in the end of nada, past the ends of the elements and of knowing, are lovers of knowledge.
nuance: The verse is built on -அந்தம் (end): Vedanta, Siddhanta, Nadanta, Bhutanta, Bodhanta, traditionally a series of limits each passed in turn. Here Vedanta and Siddhanta stand together, not opposed. மாதுப் புனஞ்செய்ய is obscure.

title: அசுத்த சைவம்
theme: Impure Saivism (அசுத்த சைவம்): Saivas of service and rite, known by outward signs such as earrings, seals and rudraksha beads and by recitation; the chapter then turns to those who see further, the severe pure Saiva and the jnani.
structure_note: 1423 and 1424 describe the Saiva of outward signs; 1425 and 1426 move beyond them to the severe pure Saiva and the jnani, which sits oddly under this heading.
source_issues: 1425 names கடுஞ்சுத்த சைவர் and 1426 the ஞானி, though the chapter heading is impure Saivism; the verses may be misplaced or the headings arranged later.

reading: For those on the paths of service and rite it is fitting to praise the paired holy feet and, without lapse, to wear the signs: paired earrings, the two seals and the paired rudraksha garland at the neck.
nuance: சரியை and கிரியை are the first two of the four Saiva paths (with yoga and jnana): temple service and ritual worship. The signs are outward, which is why this is called impure Saivism, meaning mixed with form rather than wrong. தினையார், ஈரணை முத்திரை and இணைக்கண்ட மாலை are taken by tradition as earrings, seals and a rudraksha garland; the exact objects are uncertain.

reading: One who wears two gold earrings, keeps the two inner bonds on the body, tests himself, follows the twelvefold way and keeps reciting is one kind of Saiva.
nuance: துவாதச மார்க்கம் (the twelvefold way) may be the breath's reach of twelve finger-breadths beyond the head, or a twelve-syllable mantra; the verse doesn't say. உட்கட்டு இரண்டு (two inner bindings) is obscure. ஒருசைவர், 'one kind of Saiva', places such a person within Saivism without praise.

reading: Those who have seen the nine divisions have seen the rare thing, and those who see the divisions are the severely pure Saivas.
nuance: கண்டம் is a division or region (the nine regions of the earth) and also the throat, and the verse puns on it and கண்ட (saw) in every line. What the nine divisions are, in the world or in the body, can't be fixed from the verse. It names the severe pure Saiva of chapter 90, not the impure one.

reading: The jnani is one who comes to see all the good books of the earth, the way of silence, all sixty-four attainments, the other planes, the end of the unwritten Veda, and himself together with the Lord.
nuance: எழுதா மறை, the unwritten scripture, is the Veda kept by mouth, and its end (ஈறு) Vedanta. எண்ணெண் is sixty-four. The list climbs from books to silence to seeing oneself with the Lord (கோனொடு தன்னையும்), which is the last and highest item.

title: மார்க்க சைவம்
theme: Path Saivism (மார்க்க சைவம்): the means and the vision of the pure Saiva, who holds Vedanta and Siddhanta as one, reflects on the Lord, the soul, the bond and release, and by the feet of the Supreme power becomes Siva, while soul and bond cannot of themselves reach the Lord.
structure_note: Means and marks of the pure Saiva (1427 to 1429); the Supreme power and the state beyond real and unreal (1430, 1431); what the pure Saiva contemplates and sees (1432 to 1434); the schools compared (1435); the limit of soul and bond (1436); and the attainment of Siddhanta (1437). Despite the heading, most verses speak of the pure Saiva.
source_issues: 1431: line 1 reads அசுத்து where 1420 and 1430 have அசத்து; probably a misprint, though அசுத்தம் (impure) would also make sense.
1433: lines 2 and 3 (மாரண மந்த மதித்தானந் தத்தோடு / நேரென ஈராறு நீதி நெடும் போகங்) are obscure and may be corrupt.
Chapter 89 is headed மார்க்க சைவம் but most of its verses describe the pure Saiva (சுத்த சைவர்).

reading: For pure Saivas the means are Siva's emblem of gold, the sacred ash, the good path, great knowledge, the means by which the wrong path does not arise, and the true path.
nuance: சாதனம் is both a means of practice and an emblem worn, and the verse may mean either or both. பூதி is sacred ash. சன்மார்க்கம், the true path, is in Siddhanta the path of knowledge. பொன்னாற் சிவசாதனம் may be a gold emblem or Siva's emblem made precious.

reading: The faultless knower, lord of rising knowledge, in whom knowledge dawns within the joined portion of Vedanta and Siddhanta, who has true release, is the eternal devotee of pure Saivism.
nuance: வேதாந்த சித்தாந்த, written as one compound, treats the two as a single body of teaching. சத்தசைவம் is read as சுத்த சைவம்; சத்த could also be 'true'.

reading: The Agamas are nine, and within them the twenty-eight, free of delusion, in their three divisions; pure Saivism is the rare whole in which they and the calm truth of Vedanta and Siddhanta end as one.
nuance: Twenty-eight (நாலேழு, four sevens) is the standard count of Saiva Agamas; the nine are those Tirumular names in his preface (63). The two நாலேழு and the three divisions (முப்பேதம்) are not clear, and the counting may be compressed.

reading: The Supreme power who stands apart from the pure and the impure, the seven turiya states, the real and the unreal, she who impels and she who is within, is the Father's power of grace and is everywhere.
nuance: பராபரை is the feminine of பராபரன், the Supreme as Shakti; it is repeated three times with different qualifiers. துரியங்கள் ஓரேழு, seven turiyas, can't be fixed from the verse. அருட்சத்தி names grace as the Lord's own power.

reading: Those who have passed beyond the real and the unreal become that very one, in the state of 'I am Siva' where sentient and insentient are no longer told apart, and sink into the power of bliss in release; attainment too is at its height there.
nuance: சிவோகம் (I am Siva) is a contemplative formula; Siddhanta tradition takes it as union in which the soul does not cease, a reading the verse alone does not settle. தானாகி may mean they become themselves or become Him.

reading: What pure Saivas are to reflect on is the self, the Supreme called Sadasiva, the abiding triad of Lord, soul and bond, the ancient stainless-making impurity and the bondage from before, and release.
nuance: The list is the syllabus of Siddhanta: self, Lord, the three categories, impurity, bondage and release. மாசற்ற may qualify what follows (the soul made stainless) or the whole list; பழமலம், the ancient impurity, is traditionally anava, beginningless as 115 says.

reading: For pure Saivas the vision is this: when all is set in the fullness and cut away, death comes to its end, and with bliss there is the long enjoyment of the twelve.
nuance: மாரணம் may be 'death' or 'great death'; ஈராறு (twelve) and நீதி are unexplained, and the second and third lines are obscure. Only the frame, a vision of fullness and bliss, is fairly sure.

reading: To hold to unchanging knowledge and great yoga without pride, settle the unsettled mind and make it Siva, and keep to the path by cherishing the contemplation one has gained: that, marked out, is the jnani's charya.
nuance: சரிதை is சரியை, service, here named as the service proper to the jnani: tradition nests each of the four paths within the others. மதிப்பற may be 'without pride' or 'beyond measure'. பாவனை, contemplation, is what the jnani keeps up as his service.

reading: Those who have seen Vedanta hold that Brahman alone is real and the world false; those who have seen the end of nada are yogis who do not waver; and the Siddhanta that is not other than Vedanta is the way Saivas share.
nuance: பிரமமித்தியாதரர் is read as those who hold Brahman (பிரமம்) and falsity (மித்யா), the Advaita thesis that the world is false; that division is the tradition's. வேதாந்தம் அல்லாத சித்தாந்தம் can mean a Siddhanta not other than Vedanta or one that is not Vedanta, and the two readings pull opposite ways. சாதாரணமன்ன is likewise 'common' or 'like the common'.

reading: As clouds do not reach the sky and the many sights do not reach the eye, the Lord, who is thought of yet beyond the reach of thought, is not reached by soul and bond.
nuance: The images make the relation one-way: the sky holds the clouds, the eye takes in the sights, and neither is reached by what it holds. The last line repeats 115's பதியினைச் சென்றணுகா பசு பாசம் with அண்ணல் for பதி.

reading: To be neither one nor two nor nothing, yet one; to leave the sects and the formless; and to go by her feet to the love of the Supreme power and so become Siva: that is the attainment of Siddhanta.
nuance: ஒன்றும் இரண்டும் இலதுமாய் is the Siddhanta formula of non-duality, neither simple oneness nor two, as tradition reads it. நிராகாரம் may be the formless as a doctrine held by some sect. பாதத்தால் may be by her feet or on foot.

title: கடுஞ் சுத்த சைவம்
theme: Severe pure Saivism (கடுஞ் சுத்த சைவம்): beyond outward signs, the severe pure Saiva destroys desire, bond and the state of a bound soul, strips away the tattvas and maya, and becomes pure Siva, until 'I' and 'He' can no longer be said and the senses are stilled in union.
structure_note: Two verses define the severe pure Saiva and the Siddhanta path by what is removed (1438, 1439), one by what is reached (1440), and two speak in the first person and of the result (1441, 1442), linked end to beginning by சாற்று.
source_issues: 1440: line 1 (சுத்தச் சிவனுரை தானத்தில் தோயாமல்) is obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: Those who go beyond outward garb to Siva's side without show, crush the bonds of desire and lay waste bondage and the state of a bound soul, are the pure Saivas who know Siva.
nuance: வேடம், garb, is the outward dress and signs of a sect, such as those of 1423 and 1424. பசுத்துவம் is the soul's state of being bound, not the soul itself. விகிர்தன், a name of Siva, is the one unlike all others. சிவபோதகர் may be those who know Siva or those who teach him.

reading: To strip away the five that make the body, the six and the five, great maya in its layers and the rest, wipe away the bond of the isolated state and firmly reach oneself: that is the path of Siddhanta.
nuance: ஐந்து, ஆறு and ஐந்து are traditionally groups of tattvas (elements, and the higher categories), stripped from the grossest upward. கேவலம் is in Siddhanta the soul's state wrapped in anava alone, before it takes a body; tradition supplies that sense. தனையுறல் may be reaching oneself or reaching Him.

reading: Those who, without dwelling on words about pure Siva, reach the root that is the seed of release and the goal of the freed, and as souls so reach Hara that the separate self is gone, become pure Siva: they are the pure Saivas.
nuance: அற்றால் (when it ceases) is read of the soul's separateness; tradition holds that the soul is not destroyed, and the verse does not say. Line 1 (சுத்தச் சிவனுரை தானத்தில் தோயாமல்) is obscure.

reading: Searching out what 'I' is and what 'He' is, I came to the state of That where there are not two, He and I; since that truth was granted, I can no longer speak of He and I.
nuance: The verse is a report of experience in the first person. தான் is the Lord here, and தற்பதம் may be 'the That-state' (tat) or 'his own state'. நல்கலால் (because it was given) makes the knowledge a gift, not an achievement.

reading: When the truth beyond speech is attained, the five that are hard to curb subside, knowledge shines above as the light of a lamp, and union with the Supreme becomes one's station.
nuance: சாற்றரிதாகிய (hard to speak of) picks up சாற்றகில்லேன் from 1441. The five are traditionally the senses. சாயுச்சியம் is union, the last of the four stations (salokya, samipya, sarupya, sayujya); பதி may be 'station' or 'the Lord'.

title: சரியை
theme: Chariyai (சரியை), the first of the four Saiva paths: seeking out temples and towns, singing and bowing to Siva until he takes the heart as his temple. The chapter sets chariyai in the ladder of chariyai, kiriyai, yoga and jnana, matches each to a kind of worship and a kind of devotee, and ends with the four grades of initiation.
structure_note: An opening that names the teachers of the root chariyai (1443), a verse ranking four kinds of puja (1444), the one verse on chariyai practice itself (1445), two verses matching the four paths to four kinds of people (1446, 1447), worship by form and formless (1448), Nandi's giving of the paths (1449) and the four initiations (1450). The same fourfold scheme of samaya, visesha, nirvana and abhisheka closes chapters 93 and 94.
source_issues: 1443: the teachers' names (காலாங்கி, கஞ்ச மலையமான், கந்துரு) are divided differently in different readings; கந்துரு is uncertain.
1446: வியமாதி is probably a scribal form of இயமாதி.
1447: வெண் யோகத்தர் probably stands for எண்யோகத்தர் (eight-limbed yoga) after the preceding சேர்ந்த.

reading: This is the way of the root chariyai, as Kalangi, Kanjamalaiyan and Kandhuru examined it; listen: on earth it is the life of pure Saivam.
nuance: காலாங்கி, கஞ்சமலையமான் and கந்துரு are taken as disciples of Tirumular named in the lineage verses; the readings of the names, especially கந்துரு, are not secure. மூல சரியை may mean the root or first chariyai, or the chariyai of Mulan.

reading: Standing as the life of life is the bright jnana-puja; looking at the light in the life is the great yoga-puja; invoking the deity into a form is outer puja; love at the end of all fault is Siva-puja.
nuance: ஆவாகனம் is the ritual invocation of the deity into an image, the work of kiriyai. செயிற்கடை நேசம் (love at the end of fault, or love free of fault) is obscure; it is usually taken as the devotee's pure love, the puja of chariyai. The verse ranks inner over outer worship without dismissing the outer.

reading: Seek through lands, towns and holy temples, and sing 'Siva Peruman'; having sung, bow; and when you have bowed, he will take your joined heart as his temple.
nuance: The outward wandering of chariyai ends inward: the temple sought outside becomes the heart. கூடிய நெஞ்சம் may be the heart that has come together in devotion, or the heart joined to him.

reading: The devotees are those in chariyai; those of kiriyai are servants who take the garb of grace; the practisers of pure yama and the rest are pure yogis; the siddhas are those who go and reach Siva-jnana.
nuance: The verse matches the four paths to four kinds of people: பத்தர், தொண்டர், யோகர், சித்தர். வியமாதி is read as இயமாதி (yama and the other limbs); அருள்வேடம் (the garb of grace) may be holy ash and rudraksha or the guise of devotees.

reading: Those of true jnana who have become Him, those of the eightfold yoga, the siddhas in samadhi, those of kiriyai who never fail in archana, and those of chariyai: all are of this wide earth.
nuance: The list runs down from jnana to chariyai, the reverse of 1446. வெண் யோகம் is read as எண் யோகம், eight-limbed yoga. நீள்நிலத்தோர் (those of the wide earth) may honour all four as living on earth, or may mark them all as still within the world.

reading: Kiriyai, the yogas and the rising jnana-puja; the rare form of Siva and the formless in which he dwells; the puja chosen at the stage when one can discern: these are the high puja of love.
nuance: Tradition matches kiriyai to worship of Siva in form (உரு), yoga to form-and-formless, and jnana to the formless (அரூபம்); the verse names form and formless but doesn't spell out the match. தெரியும் பருவம் (the stage of discerning) suggests worship fitted to one's ripeness.

reading: The four paths beginning with chariyai, the four jnanas they give, and the six of wide Vedanta and Siddhanta: Nandi, who is their meaning, came to the golden city and set them for deluded men to worship.
nuance: தருஞான நான்கும் is taken as the four fruits of the paths, or the fourfold division of each path. ஆறும் (the six) is unclear: six schools, or six divisions of Vedanta-Siddhanta. பொன்னகர் (the golden city) may be Tillai, Kailasa or the world. Nandi is both teacher and the meaning taught.

reading: Samaya initiation is purity of many kinds in which one's own action ceases; visesha is purification by Hara's mantra; nirvana is purification of the kalas; abhisheka is the path of settled jnana.
nuance: சமயம், விசேடம், நிருவாணம் and அபிடேகம் are the four grades of Saiva initiation (தீட்சை) in the Agamas, though the verse does not use the word தீட்சை. Here சமயம் is the first initiation, not a sect. கலாசுத்தி, the purifying of the kalas, is a technical rite.

title: கிரியை
theme: Kiriyai (கிரியை), worship of the Lord by rite and service: refuge at the feet of the one God of all directions frees from the sea of deeds, but rich offerings reach him only from those who have given up flesh. Service done by humans is service to the Lord, and kiriyai with chariyai leads on through yoga and jnana, by the guru's grace, to becoming Siva.
structure_note: Refuge at the feet (1451), the condition of not eating flesh (1452), an obscure verse of praise built on கன்று (1453), service as devotion (1454), the ladder from kiriyai to Siva (1455) and a first-person close of love and service (1456).
source_issues: 1453: lines 1 and 2 (கோனக்கன் றாயே, நடுவே யுழிதரும்) are obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: In all ten directions there is one supreme God, and there is no direction where he is not; take refuge in the shade of the Pure One's holy feet, clustered like flowers, and the leaping sea of deeds will not reach you.
nuance: கொத்து (a cluster, of flowers) pictures the feet as a bunch of blossoms; the shade (நீழல்) is the refuge. தத்தும் (leaping, surging) makes வினை a sea with waves. எத்திக்கு இலர் இல்லை may also mean 'there is no one in any direction who is without him'.

reading: Even if one worships with crores of fragrant forest sandal and great flowers that reach the sky, none but those who eat having put away flesh can reach his flower-anklets where the honey sits.
nuance: The verse sets the scale of offering against one abstention. ஊனினை நீக்கி may also be taken as 'removing the body', but in a chapter on worship and with உண்பவர் (those who eat) it reads most naturally as giving up meat.

reading: Praise his sounding anklets as the king's calf; the Lord, calf of jnana who roams in the middle, calf of the sky whom the gods worship with joined hands, and holder of the deer's calf, is a vessel of grace.
nuance: Each line turns on கன்று (calf, young one): கோனக்கன்று, ஞானக்கன்று, வானக்கன்று, மானக்கன்று. Only the last is clear, the deer Siva holds in his hand. Whether the worshipper or the Lord is the calf in line 1, and what நடுவே உழிதரும் (roams in the middle) refers to, I can't fix. வள்ளம் may be a vessel, a boat or a measure.

reading: Bow to this: she who serves all the regions of the eight directions is a part of him; the service humans do is service to the Lord; serving the Lord is devotion.
nuance: அவள் ஒரு கூறன் is the Lord who has her (Shakti) as half his body. The words இது, அது and பணி are repeated so densely that the grammar is unclear; பதிபணி may be service to the Lord (பதி) or service at his shrine.

reading: The devotee, practising kiriyai and chariyai, moves by pure grace into flawless yoga, and through the jnana realised on the path it leads to, by the guru's grace, the mind becomes Siva.
nuance: The verse gives the whole ladder in one sentence: chariyai and kiriyai, then yoga, then jnana, then Sivam. Each step is credited to grace (சுத்த அருள், குருவருள்), not only to practice. It names kiriyai before chariyai, perhaps for metre.

reading: Melting in love, I serve him every day; standing before his body of red gold and his lotus feet, I ask him to grant me words to speak there, and he shines as a light within my bones.
nuance: The grammar of lines 2 and 3 is loose: மொழிவது எனக்கருள் may be 'grant me what to say' or 'grant me grace, I say'. என்பினுள் சோதி, the light within the bone, answers the image of bones melting in love (compare 272).

title: யோகம்
theme: Yoga as the third path: the yogi sits still as a post, unmoved by touch, and finds Siva blossoming within the soul like scent in a flower, the Lord whom Hari and Brahma sought for ages and who dwells in the crown. Learning and the arts do not end the bonds; the yogic way does, and the chapter ends with yoga's four grades.
structure_note: The yogi's stillness (1457), the Lord perceived only by those who perceive (1458 to 1460), the inner method over learning (1461), practice done with longing (1462), the inner fire (1463), the many who fell and the few who love (1464), an obscure verse on the paths within yoga (1465), and yoga's samaya, visesha, nirvana and abhisheka (1466), matching 1450 and 1476.
source_issues: 1462: மேய்த்தவர் is probably a misreading of மெய்த்தவர்.
1465: the verse is very compressed and may be corrupt; the division of paths within yoga can't be recovered with confidence.

reading: Going by the path and becoming one within rectitude, setting themselves like a planted post, for those who know the sign and do not start whether scratched or struck, union becomes possible.
nuance: தறி இருந்தாற்போல் (like a post standing) is the image of the motionless seated yogi; not flinching at scratch or blow marks withdrawal from the senses. குறி (the sign, or the goal) is a recurring yogic term in Tirumular whose exact referent the verse leaves open.

reading: He lets himself be perceived age after age only by those who perceive him; Hari who rests on the ocean and Brahma strove for ages, and he is in the crown.
nuance: ஒருச்சி is read as உச்சி, the crown of the head, where yoga places the meeting with Siva; it may also be the summit beyond the gods' reach. The verse recalls the story of Hari and Brahma seeking his foot and crown (chapter 41).

reading: As scent dwells in a flower, the fragrance of Siva has blossomed within the soul; for the knowers who perceive it steady as a painting, it is the central post joined with musk.
nuance: The first two lines are plain: Siva in the soul as scent in the flower. ஓவியம் போல (like a painting) may describe the still yogi or the stable vision. நாவி அணைந்த நடுதறி (the planted middle post joined with musk) is taken by tradition as the central channel, sushumna; that is symbolic and uncertain. Sengalvaraya notes a parallel in Tiruppugazh 239 on the soul as Siva's form.

reading: You say 'we are saved' but do not see the thing to be reached; if you see clearly in your mind Nandi who mingles in the fragrant flower, and darkness leaves, he is the root seed of your former births.
nuance: The flower and scent carry on from 1459. The last line can mean the Lord was always the root seed of one's births, or that clear seeing destroys the seed of birth; the verse doesn't say which.

reading: Letters, songs and the sixty-four arts do not remove birth bound in fetters with blame at its head; I have come to know the way of sending the moon, fire and sun up the path.
nuance: The plain point is that learning (எழுத்து, பாடல், எண்ணெண் கலை) does not end the bonds. சோமன், அங்கி, அருக்கன் (moon, fire, sun) are traditionally the three channels or the three zones of the yogic body, and வழித்தலை செய்யும் (turning them up the path) a yogic method; that reading is tradition's.

reading: If done standing in longing, one becomes a true ascetic; done in longing, it becomes true speech; done in longing, true tapas; done in longing, one becomes a dweller of heaven.
nuance: The verse does not name what is done; under the heading it is yoga. மேய்த்தவர் is probably மெய்த்தவர் (true ascetics). The fourfold repetition of விரும்பி நின்றே செயின் puts the weight on desire held steadily, not on the practice.

reading: If cherished, he grants the world of no birth; if seen, he stands within his own union; if without shame, he opens the way to the path of hell: the excellent one is the fire that burns in the flesh.
nuance: ஊனில் சுடும் அங்கி (the fire that burns in the flesh) is traditionally the inner fire of yoga, and the verse calls it உத்தமன், the Lord. நாணில் may be 'if shamed' or 'without shame', and நகர நெறி may be the path to hell (நரகம்) or to the city (of Siva). So the third line either warns or promises; I have taken it as a warning, with the plain contrast of a fire that frees or harms.

reading: Kings of just sceptre and endless great ascetics, countless thousands, have fallen; the siddhas, the gods and the three in their greatness come in love, saying 'this one is the Father'.
nuance: The two halves are not joined by any word. They may contrast the many who fell, for all their rule and austerity, with those who reached him by love; or say that even siddhas and gods only love him. மூவர் (the three) is usually Brahma, Vishnu and Rudra.

reading: For the yogi there are three, yoga and the rest, taken up; kiriyai and the rest belong to the body as chariyai; chariyai that has left thirst is one; within that one I placed my love in devotion to the Sun.
nuance: The verse seems to subdivide yoga by the four paths (chariyai within yoga and so on), as 1474 does for jnana, but the lines are too compressed to fix. ஆதித்தன் (the Sun) may be the Lord as light, or the sun of the yogic body. Reading tentative throughout.

reading: Yoga-samaya is contemplating the many yogas; yoga-visesha is eight-limbed yoga; yoga-nirvana is the rising of the Supreme that is reached; yoga-abhisheka is gaining bright siddhi.
nuance: The four stages repeat the four initiations of 1450 (samaya, visesha, nirvana, abhisheka) as grades within yoga. பரோதயம் (the rising of the Supreme) is technical. The verse makes siddhi the crown of yoga, where 1476 makes the guru's feet the crown of jnana.

title: ஞானம்
theme: Jnana, the fourth and highest path: there is no dharma, religion or release above it. Its marks are going beyond sound and the faculties, loss of 'I' and 'mine', passing beyond merit and sin, and becoming the pure, freed Siva-siddha. Like yoga, jnana has the four paths within it and four grades, ending at the good guru's feet.
structure_note: Jnana's supremacy (1467), what the knower passes beyond (1468 to 1471), an obscure symbolic verse (1472), the paths within jnana (1473, 1474), the knower described (1475) and jnana's four grades (1476), matching 1450 and 1466.
source_issues: 1476: நற்குறு பாதம் is probably நற்குரு பாதம்.
1472 is symbolic and obscure throughout (ஏனம், கூனல் மதி மண்டலம்); some words may be corrupt.

reading: There is no path of dharma in the land higher than jnana, no religion beyond jnana is good, what goes beyond jnana does not give good release, and those who excel in jnana excel among men.
nuance: ஞானத்தின் மிக்க opens every line, but its sense shifts: in the first three it is 'higher than jnana', in the last 'abounding in jnana'. The verse ranks dharma and religion below jnana without rejecting them.

reading: Sound and reflection on sound, the fitting mind, directed awareness, the ego that makes aware, and these three with the chitta, and the act of thinking itself: going beyond sound, those who pass them gain the true path.
nuance: The list looks like the inner instruments (manas, buddhi, ahankara, chitta), with சத்தம் and சத்த மனனம் perhaps standing for hearing and reflecting on teaching (sravana, manana). How the items group into 'these three' is unclear. சன்மார்க்கம் here is the path of jnana, the subject of the next chapter.

reading: That the world is in him and what is near him, and what becomes grace to me through love: those who can say these gain jnana, reach Sivoham, and receive the love that follows.
nuance: சிவோகம் (I am Siva) is a contemplative formula of identity. The first two lines are compressed and the subject of தன்பால் (in himself) may be the Lord or the knower. The verse has love both before jnana (அன்பால்) and after it (பின்பாலின் நேயம்).

reading: For those who have examined and understood the jnana without crookedness, the safe place to dwell is Brahman, all classes of being make up the moving and unmoving world, and it gives the fruit of all the proud observances.
nuance: திருக்கிலா ஞானம் is jnana without twist or crookedness. தருக்கிய ஆசாரம் may be observances that people take pride in, or observances that are reasoned out; the claim is that jnana yields what they aim at. The grammar of the first two lines is loose.

reading: The greatly gracious one dwells in the city that knowledge, restraint and love never leave; his sign, his qualities and his sounding feet do not leave it; for those who know the way, this is plain as the sound of water.
nuance: The 'city' (நகர்) is probably the knower's own heart or body. நீர்த்தொனி (the sound of water) is obscure; it may mean something clearly heard, or something heard in still water. The pairing of knowledge, restraint and love is the verse's clear teaching.

reading: In a mind where jnana ripens and rises, a boar springs up to be seen ahead at every turn; seeing the water facing the curved moon's circle, cutting off all defect, one stands as a bright flame.
nuance: ஏனம் (boar) may recall Vishnu as the boar who dug for Siva's foot, or ஏனம் may mean a vessel; கூனல் மதி மண்டலம் (the circle of the bent moon) and the water before it are traditionally the moon-region in the head and its nectar. The ending is plain: defect cut away, the knower becomes light. The rest is symbolic and I can't fix it.

reading: For the jnani the four are in jnana with its qualities; for the silent one none of these join; before that, deluded, Shakti stands above and makes knowledge grow; those of this kind are of chariyai and kiriyai.
nuance: The verse seems to grade the jnani, for whom the four paths are within jnana, above the silent one (மோனி) who is past all of them, and below both those still in chariyai and kiriyai. The middle lines (மோகித்து மேல் நிற்றல் ஆம் சத்தி வித்தை) are obscure.

reading: For the jnani the four beginning with jnana are within jnana: jnana in jnana is not saying 'I' and 'mine'; yoga in jnana is the good light at the end of nada; kiriyai in jnana is seeking good release.
nuance: Each path is said to contain all four (jnana in jnana, yoga in jnana and so on); the verse gives three of the four within jnana and leaves out chariyai. நாதாந்தம் (the end of nada) is technical. The clearest line is the first: jnana's own core is the end of 'I' and 'mine'.

reading: He who reaches jnana-in-jnana has passed beyond merit and sin, is free of strife, has seen the beloved jnana of the far shore, and is the firm, pure, Siva-freed siddha.
nuance: புண்ணிய பாவம் கடந்த says the knower is beyond both good and bad deeds, not only bad ones. கரைஞானம் (shore-jnana) may be the knowledge of the far shore or the knowledge at the limit; கண்ணிய நேயம் (the cherished, or the intended, object of love) is unclear.

reading: Jnana-samaya is seeing the self one seeks; jnana-visesha is the rising of the Supreme one seeks; jnana-nirvana is the grace of the one who knows the good; jnana-abhisheka is the good guru's feet.
nuance: நற்குறு பாதம் is read as நற்குரு பாதம், the good guru's feet. The sequence runs from seeing the self, to the Supreme rising, to grace, to the guru's feet: the summit of jnana is placed at the guru.

title: சன்மார்க்கம்
theme: Sanmarga (சன்மார்க்கம்), the true path, which in Saiva usage is the path of jnana: laid down by Nandi as a guru-path, it removes the five impurities and the bond of soul and fetter, joins the soul to the Lord, melts the unmelting heart and ends birth. Without clarity there is no knowing Siva; the lower paths serve the simple, and sanmarga is becoming Him.
structure_note: Those who conquered death on the path (1477), Nandi's guru-path and its acts of devotion to the guru (1478, 1479), the fourfold refrain on clarity (1480), and a run of definitions of sanmarga (1481 to 1487), most ending in சன்மார்க்கமே.
source_issues: 1481 line 4 reads தாவை னாயுறலான, which is not good Tamil; it is probably தானவனாய் உறலான (becoming Him oneself).
1482 lists the marks of sanmarga without giving them; the verse may be a fragment or an introduction to lost or displaced verses.

reading: Those who saw the flame of scripture that is the manifestation of the Siva-tattva, the declared sanmarga, lost their anger, became Siva-yoga siddhas, conquered death and knew the sign.
nuance: சுருதிச் சுடர் (the flame of the shruti) may be the light that scripture reveals or scripture itself as light. Losing anger (சீற்றம் ஒழிந்து) is set beside conquering death, so moral and yogic attainments stand together. குறிப்பு (the sign) is unclear.

reading: Nandi, the sole leader of Saiva greatness, has laid down one guru-path for salvation; he laid it down so that those in the world may join the divine Siva-way, the good path, and be saved.
nuance: நன்மார்க்கம் (the good path) glosses சன்மார்க்கம். The verse makes the true path a teacher's path (குருநெறி), handed down, not found alone.

reading: Seeing, worshipping and contemplating the guru, touching and praising him, wearing his sandals on the head: for those on earth who serve the guru so, sanmarga is what brings them to release.
nuance: The six acts (தெரிசித்தல், பூசித்தல், சிந்தித்தல், பரிசித்தல், கீர்த்தித்தல், பாதுகம் சூடல்) are all directed to the guru as to the Lord. The verse ties the path of knowledge to devotion to the person of the teacher.

reading: Those who do not know clarity do not know Siva, do not even become the soul, cannot become Siva, and do not end their births.
nuance: தெளிவு here is spiritual clarity, settled knowledge of what is real. சீவனும் ஆகார் (they do not become even the soul) is striking: without clarity one does not truly know oneself as soul, let alone as Siva. The four lines climb from knowing Siva to ending birth.

reading: Becoming Him, destroying the five impurities, being freed by a speech that is silence, the bliss in flawless jnana-experience, and coming to be Him oneself: this is sanmarga.
nuance: ஐந்து மலம் (five impurities) is an extended count of the usual three (anava, kanma, maya), adding maya's products and the concealing power. மோனமதாம் மொழி (speech that is silence) is the guru's silent teaching or the knower's silence. Line 4 is corrupt as printed.

reading: For those of sanmarga there are a face and a seat, a place and a deity, a class and a vision; I shall tell those of every path: listen.
nuance: The verse announces items (முகம், பீடம், இடம், தெய்வம், வருக்கம், தரிசனம்) without explaining them; they may be the marks of each path, given in verses not here. Read alone, it is only a preface.

reading: The means of sanmarga is knowledge and the known; the means of the later paths stands for the simple; those who have left the evil path and are flawless in the fourth state become Him: that is sanmarga.
nuance: ஞான ஞேயம் is knowledge and its object (jnana, jneya). பின்மார்க்கம் (the later or lower paths) are chariyai, kiriyai and yoga, said to suit பேதையர், the simple; it is a ranking, not a dismissal. துரியம் is the fourth state beyond waking, dream and sleep.

reading: If the three lower paths come naturally to the rare disciples who reach sanmarga, then the good path itself is seeking with Siva; the scriptures accept it as the path of the word.
nuance: The verse seems to say the lower three are taken up into sanmarga for the ripe disciple, but the conditional (என்றால்) makes the logic hard to fix. சொன்மார்க்கம் may be the path of the word (scripture) or a pun on சன்மார்க்கம்.

reading: Those who have seen, with themselves, the alien bond, the karma that comes, the states that follow, the root prakriti, the entwined knowledge, and difference upon difference, are of sanmarga.
nuance: அன்னிய பாசம் (the bond that is other, alien to the soul), அவத்தை (the soul's states), மூலப் பகுதி (root nature, mula-prakriti) are technical terms. தன்னொடும் கண்டவர் (who saw them along with themselves) suggests knowing the self and its bonds together, as distinct.

reading: Removing pasu and pasam and joining the soul with Pati, making the unmelting heart melt, reaching the rising of the true form that does not bend, and the stillness in which there is no moving: that is sanmarga.
nuance: The three Siddhanta categories appear together: removing the soul's bound state (பசு) and its bonds (பாசம்), and joining it to the Lord (பதி). கசியாத நெஞ்சம் கசிய puts melting love at the centre of the path of knowledge. அசைவு இல்லாமை is stillness.

reading: The path the sanmargis lay down for reaching is sanmarga and nothing else; for those who do not rest in the path called sanmarga, the path is sanmarga as siddha-yoga.
nuance: Every line opens with மார்க்கம் சன்மார்க்க and the sense turns on how the repeated words divide. The last line may mean that siddha-yoga is the sanmarga for those not yet settled in it, or that sanmarga itself is siddha-yoga; the verse leads into the next chapter on yoga.

title: சகமார்க்கம்
theme: Sahamarga (சகமார்க்கம்), the companion path, which the chapter identifies with yoga: sanmarga itself becomes sahamarga, and within yoga-samadhi are space, light and Shakti. Yoga gives the yogi both union with Siva and the enjoyments of the world; it purifies the centres and channels, cuts down the five senses with the sword of the mind, and the Lord stands within like a ripe fruit split open.
structure_note: Sanmarga as sahamarga (1488), the loss for those without the twelve-path (1489), samadhi (1490), yoga and enjoyment (1491), the purifications (1492), the five senses subdued (1493) and the ripe fruit (1494).
source_issues: 1492 line 4 reads சாதா ரணங்கெட லாஞ்ச மார்க்கமே; ஆஞ்ச மார்க்கம் is probably ஆம் சகமார்க்கம், with a syllable lost.
1488: துறதி is obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: Sanmarga itself is what became sahamarga; it is the mind-path that places release within attainment; the later path is unending birth and death and the ruin of wrong-path knowledge.
nuance: சகமார்க்கம் (the companion path) is in Saiva tradition the yoga path, standing with the Lord as a companion; the verse doesn't define it but joins it to sanmarga. பின்மார்க்கம் here seems to mean a fallen path, unlike 1483 where it is the lower paths. துறதி is obscure, perhaps துர்கதி (an evil end).

reading: For those without the twelve-path that joins, guru, Siva and religion do not come together; fearful Lakshmi will not be in their house, and they lose form and kin together.
nuance: துவாதச மார்க்கம் (the twelve-path) is unexplained; it is taken as the breath reaching the dvadasanta, twelve finger-breadths above the head, or as twelve divisions of practice. The threatened loss is worldly as well as spiritual: wealth (திருமகள்), body (உரு) and kin (கிளை).

reading: Within yoga-samadhi is the wide space, within it is light, within it is Shakti; those who delight in yoga-samadhi are siddhas.
nuance: அகலிடம் (the wide place) may be the world or the inner sky (ஆகாசம்); ஒளி and சத்தி are the light and power traditionally experienced there. The refrain யோகச் சமாதியின் உள்ளே makes samadhi a place one enters.

reading: Both yoga and enjoyment come to yogis: those whose minds reach Siva's form through yoga have, as enjoyment, the attainment of the aims of life on earth; both belong to the yogi who does not perish.
nuance: போகம் (enjoyment) is not renounced here but given to the yogi along with yoga. புருடார்த்தம் are the aims of life, traditionally dharma, wealth, pleasure and release. அழியாத யோகி may be the yogi whose body does not decay, in keeping with Tirumular's care for the body.

reading: Purifying the centres and the channels, the sky-light at the end of the sixteen kalas beginning with medha, and in the abode of awareness the ordinary working of senses, instruments and intellect ceasing: this is sahamarga.
nuance: ஆதாரம் (the centres, chakras), நாடி சுத்தி (cleansing the channels) and மேதாதி ஈரெண் கலை (the sixteen kalas from medha, in mantra-yoga the stages of the syllable up to the end of nada) are technical. சாதாரணம் கெடல் is read as the ordinary working of the faculties ending.

reading: The five that stand rebelling he will then torment and hurl down with the sharp sword of the mind; the one the eighteen hosts contemplate has come and stood in the mind of him who can bow.
nuance: The five are the senses. அயில் மன வாள் (the sharp sword of the mind) makes the mind the weapon, not the thing subdued. கணம் பதினெட்டு (the eighteen hosts) are the traditional eighteen classes of celestial beings. Who 'he' is in the first half, the yogi or the Lord, is unclear.

reading: To those of rich colour he is true like a rich ripe fruit; for those whose hearts have ripened and who hold him gladly in the heart, he, the ripe fruit, splits open and stands within.
nuance: The play is on கனி (fruit, to ripen): the Lord is the fruit, the devotee's heart ripens, and the fruit opens within. வளநிறத்தார் (those of rich colour) is obscure; it may be the radiant or the fortunate. பகுந்து (split open, or shared out) suggests the Lord giving himself.

title: சற்புத்திர மார்க்கம்
theme: The path of the good son (சற்புத்திர மார்க்கம்), traditionally kiriyai: worship, recitation, praise, chanting, truthfulness and purity offered to the Lord as a son serves a father. Bowing at Hara's feet is the fruit of birth, his feet are the shore for all souls, and he comes forth each time he is worshipped.
structure_note: 1495 places the path among the others (the saha path and sanmarga); 1496 lists its acts; 1497 rebukes those who will not take even a small step; 1498 to 1500 give the reward and the manner of worship; 1501 calls the world to hear it.

reading: The true work of the good son's path is one thing, the saha path's is another; passing beyond both, to become one with the Goddess of the saha path is the clarity of sanmarga.
nuance: சகமார்க்கம் (the companion's path) is traditionally yoga, and சன்மார்க்கம் (the true path) is jnana, so the verse ranks kiriyai, yoga and jnana. தாவிப்பதாம் and சகத்தொழில் are obscure: 'what leaps' or 'what raises', and 'the companion's work' or 'worldly work'. The union with the Goddess (தேவியோடு ஒன்றல்) as the mark of jnana is unusual and may be read of Shakti as grace.

reading: Worshipping, reciting, praising, chanting, faultless good austerity, truthfulness, freedom from impurity, offering food with love and performing the purifications: this is the faultless path of the good son.
nuance: The list mixes ritual acts (pūjā, recitation, japa, food offering, purification) with moral ones (truthfulness, purity), so kiriyai here is not ritual alone. நீசுத்தி is read as the purifications done before worship; the line is compressed.

reading: Even seeing the six-legged bee roam choosing blossoms and the grey swan gather fragrant lotus and blue lily, people do not join even a small path of virtue.
