nuance: The plain sense contrasts creatures that gather flowers with people who will not gather them for worship. மறுகா (unwavering) and குறுகா (not shrinking, unfading) are uncertain in what they qualify, and சிறுகால் may mean 'a small path' or 'even for a little while'.

reading: The rare shore is the shade of his feet, the great shore is Pinakan's command, and for all souls who come toward the shore he became the one shore, equal to the seven worlds.
nuance: கரை (shore) is said four times; the sea it implies is birth, which the verse doesn't name. பிஞ்ஞகன் is a name of Siva. Making his ஆணை (command, rule) a shore puts obedience beside refuge.

reading: Rising, bowing, taking up, embracing and marvelling, do service in due order to Hara's feet; done in awe, that is the fruit of birth, and if you part from it in fear, that nature is yours.
nuance: The first line is a string of bodily acts of devotion; முகந்து may be 'taking up' (flowers or water) or 'facing'. The last line, பயந்து பிரிக்கில் அப்பான்மை உனாமே, is obscure: perhaps a warning that whoever separates himself out of fear keeps his bound nature.

reading: Standing I worship, lying down I worship our Lord, always I worship the beautiful supreme light; worship him strewing flowers thick, and each time you worship the Lord of the gods comes forth and appears.
nuance: நின்று, கிடந்து (standing, lying) cover every posture of the day, so worship is unbroken. The promise is plain: he appears (வெளிப்படும்) at each act of worship, not only at its end.

reading: You who live in the world in bodies, hear the sariyai of the good son's path where fortune abides: worship so that the bond that fixes you in the womb shrinks, and stay in joy every day.
nuance: சற்புத்திர மார்க்கச் சரியை reflects the tradition that each path has four grades (the sariyai within kiriyai and so on). கைகூம்ப may mean the bond 'folds' or shrinks, or that one worships with hands folded. கருமன்னு பாசம் is read as the bond that keeps one returning to the womb.

title: தாச மார்க்கம்
theme: The servant's path (தாச மார்க்கம்), traditionally sariyai: the humble temple tasks of lamps, flowers, sweeping, smearing, bell and bathing the image. Seeking the Lord by the ordained way quiets the mind's 'this or that', but worship done without love leaves the mind a stone sunk in a mossy pond.
structure_note: 1502 lists the tasks; 1503 sets the ordained way against sectarian wavering; 1504 and 1505 describe daily worship and the love that holds the Lord; 1506 warns that outward acts without that love are empty.
source_issues: 1502 line 1 reads எளியனல் தீப miடல்மலர் with Latin letters 'mi' in the Tamil; perhaps எளிய நல் தீபம் இடல் மலர் (lighting good lamps, flowers).

reading: Lighting lamps, gathering flowers, smearing the floor with care, sweeping, praising, holding the bell, the many bathings of the image and the rest: doing the work of the temple is the servant's path.
nuance: தளி is the temple. These are the menial tasks of a temple servant, which tradition ranks as the first of the four paths. The first words are garbled (see source issues), but the list of tasks is clear.

reading: People wander off saying this or that is the supreme, and none bows saying 'this is the way'; go by the ordained way and seek the King: that is how the mind's 'that or this' is stilled.
nuance: அதுவிது (that-this) is used twice: first of the rival claims about the supreme, then of the wavering they leave in the mind. விதிவழி (the ordained way) is not specified; in the chapter it is the servant's worship.

reading: I worship at the twilights of the moon and then the sun, and always think on the One's close-fitting anklet; worshipping daily the God of gods whom the celestials worship, all worship is completed in its due order.
nuance: அந்திப்பன் திங்கள் அதன்பின்பு ஞாயிறு may be the twilight worship at evening and morning, or, symbolically, the moon and sun breaths of yoga. வகையின் முடிந்ததே may mean worship is complete when done by rule, or that all forms of worship end in him.

reading: The celestials call the Lord by a thousand names, think of him rejoicing within and worship his feet standing inside them; for those who hold him as their own eye, the Lord stands held by great love.
nuance: பண்ணவன் is a name for the Lord (perhaps 'master', or 'Lord of melody'). The point turns on பற்றி நின்றான்: it is the Lord who is held, caught by love, rather than the worshipper by the Lord. The thousand names are praised, but the love is what holds him.

reading: Though they recite, worship and gather great flowers, look at their mind, a stone dropped in a mossy pond: they do not know the remembrance that dwells in love for the stainless light, the Lord with the dark-gem throat.
nuance: The stone in the moss pond is the mind that sinks without being changed, or round which the moss closes again at once. The verse names the same acts the chapter commends (recitation, worship, flowers) and denies them value without நேசம் (love).

title: சாலோகம்
theme: Salokam, dwelling in the Lord's world: the states of release named salokam, samipam and sarupam are gained through sariyai and the paths after it, and in kiriyai the mind becomes the temple and the grades of initiation end in samadhi.
structure_note: 1507 matches the states to the paths; 1508 lists the stages of kiriyai through the initiations.

reading: Salokam and the rest are gained through sariyai and the rest: salokam and samipam come with sariyai, and on reaching the great world sarupam becomes the way, the form of the Supreme who is beyond the worlds.
nuance: The traditional scheme pairs sariyai with salokam (his world), kiriyai with samipam (nearness), yoga with sarupam (his form) and jnana with sayujyam (union); the verse compresses it and seems to give two states to sariyai. மாலோகம் may be 'the great world' or Mal's (Vishnu's) world, and பாலோகம் இல்லா is obscure.

reading: In kiriyai one's own mind is the temple; the samaya rule of mantra, then the special stage, then the third, coming to know the root, and the samaya consecration itself is samadhi.
nuance: சமயம், விசேடம் and the third (traditionally நிருவாணம்) are read as the three grades of Saiva initiation (diksha), with அபிடேகம் as the consecration of a teacher. The verse names only சமயம், விசேடம், மூன்றாம் and சமயாபிடேகம், so this key is the tradition's. தன்மனங் கோயில் (the mind as temple) is the plainest claim.

title: சாமீபம்
theme: Samipam, nearness to the Lord, set in a ladder of the four states by what becomes of the bond (பாசம்) in each, until in sayujyam the bond dissolves and the Lord alone remains.
source_issues: 1509: சிரமானது in line 3 is unclear and may be corrupt.

reading: In salokam the bond is still the soul's; in samipam the bond turns into grace; in sarupam the bond becomes the crown; with the bond dissolved, the Lord is sayujyam.
nuance: Each line turns on what பாசம் becomes: பசுவானது (of the soul, or the soul's own state), அருளானது (grace), சிரமானது (the head or crown; possibly 'toilsome', or a corrupt word), and கரை (dissolves, or reaches its shore). The scheme uses the three Siddhanta categories, pati, pasu and pasam, to rank the states; the exact sense of each line is the tradition's.

title: சாரூபம்
theme: Sarupam, taking the Lord's form: it is reached through the eighth limb of yoga and the true path, and as everything that comes to the golden mountain takes its colour, so one who enters the guru's abode takes on the radiant form of the Lord of Kailash.

reading: Abiding sarupam is the eighth limb of yoga and is not attained except in the abiding sanmarga; those who practise gain the body's attainment in its limbs, and here, as such, it is a yoga without fall.
nuance: எட்டாம் யோகம் is read as samadhi, the eighth limb. அங்கத்து உடல் சித்தி may be bodily perfection or powers in the limbs; இங்கிவராக இழிவற்ற யோகமே is obscure. That sarupam needs sanmarga sits awkwardly with the scheme that gives it to yoga, unless சன்மார்க்கம் here means the true path in general.

reading: As everything moving and still that comes to the golden mountain becomes that mountain's colour, so the moment one enters the abode of the guru one serves, one becomes the radiant form of the Lord of Kailash.
nuance: சயிலம் (mountain) is Meru, whose gold the old image says turns all that nears it gold; the verse needs that image but names only the mountain. சாரூபம் (taking his form) is reached here through the guru, not through practice: entry into his abode (பதி) is enough.

title: சாயுச்சியம்
theme: Sayujyam, union with Siva, the last of the four states: Saivam is relation with Siva, knowing oneself and reaching him, and its end is Siva's bliss; sayujyam is the state beyond waking, abiding in stillness and becoming Siva.
structure_note: Two verses built on anaphora: four lines on சைவம் (1512), four on சாயுச்சியம் (1513).

reading: Saivam is relation with Siva; Saivam is knowing oneself and reaching Siva; Saivam is leaving what does not reach Siva; Saivam is Siva's bliss, sayujyam.
nuance: சைவந் தனையறிந்து may be 'knowing Saivam' or 'knowing oneself (தன்னை)'. Line 3, சிவந்தன்னைச் சாராமல் நீங்குதல், can mean leaving all that is not Siva, or (less likely) parting without clinging even to Siva. The verse defines Saivam not as a sect but as a relation that ends in union.

reading: Sayujyam is reaching the state beyond waking; sayujyam is abiding in stillness; sayujyam is becoming Siva; endless sayujyam is the power of bliss in the mind.
nuance: சாக்கிராதீதம் (beyond waking) and உபசாந்தம் (complete stilling) are technical terms for the soul's highest states in Siddhanta. மனத்து ஆனந்த சத்தி may be 'the bliss-shakti in the mind' or a name of the Goddess as bliss.

title: சத்திநிபாதம்
theme: The descent of power (சத்திநிபாதம்): when the soul is ripe, the Lord's grace-power, figured as an old woman, a hill-girl or the Goddess with flowing hair, comes to the blinded soul, removes its darkness, cuts its deeds, comes as the guru and makes it Siva. Worship of the Goddess with the Lord ends birth.
structure_note: The chapter opens with the riddle of the old woman and the blind old man (1514), explained in part by 1518, which repeats its third line with the Lord as subject. Grace as light in darkness runs through 1516, 1517, 1522 and 1529; the Goddess as girl and consort through 1519 to 1528; 1527 states the doctrine plainly.
source_issues: 1516 lines 3 and 4 (மருள்நீங்கா வானவர் கோன், புலம்பயல்) are obscure and may be corrupt.
1515 is obscure throughout (தீம்புலன், தேம்புலன், கோம்புலன்).

reading: The old woman who sat in the corner of the dark room, meaning to unite with the blind old man, removed his blindness, showed him many good qualities, charmed him and married him.
nuance: A riddle verse. Tradition takes the old woman as the Lord's grace-power, hidden and ancient, the dark room as the soul's state under malam, and the blind old man as the soul blinded since beginningless time. Nothing in the verse names them; the chapter title and 1518 support the reading.

reading: If one thinks on the direction of the sweet sense, it stands as nectar to those who know it as the true sense, and for those who know the clarity of the honeyed sense it becomes the field where the senses roam.
nuance: புலன் (sense, or region) is played on in every line: தீம்புலன், ஆம்புலன், தேம்புலன், கோம்புலன். The words resist a firm reading; கோம்புலன் நாடிய கொல்லை is especially obscure. The plain thread is that grace becomes nectar to those who know.

reading: Removing darkness and carrying one past countless births, the First grants grace so that grace never leaves; joined with the Lord of the celestials, one has a joy that never leaves the true thing.
nuance: நீக்கி, நீங்கா repeats through the verse: grace removes and then does not leave. மருள்நீங்கா வானவர் கோன் is awkward ('the Lord of gods whose delusion is not removed' makes no sense of the Lord), and புலம்பயல் is obscure; the last two lines may be corrupt.

reading: As a lamp brought into a room wrapped in darkness burns and shows the things there, so into the confusion of delusion come Nandi of the great flower, the Lord wrapped in grace, and the Mother.
nuance: The dark room recalls 1514. The verse makes the coming of grace the coming of a pair, the Lord and the Mother (அம்மை), as the chapter's title, the descent of Shakti, would lead one to expect. மாமலர் நந்தி is read as Nandi (Siva) seated in the heart's lotus.

reading: Charming and uniting, removing confusion, driving off and cutting away deeds, bringing forth joy, removing blindness and showing many good qualities, he granted the knowledge that shines with grace.
nuance: Line 3 is 1514's line 3 word for word, but here the subject is masculine (புரிந்தானே), the Lord, where in 1514 it was the old woman. Together the two verses make the Lord and his power one agent. வெருட்டி (frightening, driving away) shows grace as also forceful.

reading: The men who bathed at the Kanni ford have no thought of bathing in the Kanni ford; if they had the thought of bathing in the Kanni ford, there would be no other birth after.
nuance: கன்னித் துறை is the sacred bathing place of the Virgin (Kanyakumari) and, by the verse's turn, an inner ford of the Goddess as Kanni. Those who bathe outwardly miss the bathing that ends birth. What the inner bathing is, yogic or devotional, the verse doesn't say.

reading: He is red, dark, white and good green; those who fully understand will reach the Lord: love him, saying 'this is the one whose hand wears the hide of the huge elephant dark as kohl.'
nuance: The four colours may be the colours of Siva's faces, of the elements, or of the Lord with Shakti (green is often hers); the verse gives no key. மைவென்று may be 'outdoing kohl in blackness'. The elephant-hide is the familiar emblem of Siva who flayed the elephant demon.

reading: However many ages pass, they say the woman and he are the sole Lord; for those who worship him every day it becomes something shown, like a deed done in the hand.
nuance: தையலும் தானும் தனிநாயகம் makes the pair one sovereign. கையிற் கருமஞ்செய் காட்டது is obscure: perhaps 'as plain as a thing done in one's hand', the sense taken here.

reading: We have seen it: the light that followed both, the supreme light of the Supreme who rests from of old, the Lord with long matted locks where bees revel among flowers, stood removing darkness for those who stood and saw.
nuance: இரண்டும் (both) may be the Lord and Shakti, or the two eyes, or sun and moon; பண்டுபண்டோயும் is unclear. The verse speaks as a witness (கண்டுகொண்டோம்), and the darkness removed is for those who stood and looked.

reading: The sweet girl in her father's garden makes one know seven times seven births, and when all that stands within is gone, she becomes the ripe fruit that has beheld the First.
nuance: The girl in her father's garden is taken as the Goddess, daughter of the mountain king, or as grace growing in the Lord's own field. அண்ணிக்கும் (who is sweet, or who draws near) and எண்ணிக்கும் are uncertain forms. கனி (fruit) suggests the ripeness that 1527 calls the balance of deeds.

reading: For those who stand worshipping her with due honour, the hill-girl with rounded breasts, the tender creeper, cuts birth, grants great austerity, cuts forgetfulness and sets them to worship.
nuance: குறப்பெண் (girl of the hill tribes) is a name for the Goddess as mountain-born, though it also recalls Valli. Worship of her leads back into worship (வழிபட வைக்கும்): grace both rewards devotion and produces it.

reading: Hold fast to the Lord of the eight directions with her of flower-fragrant garland and curling hair; for those of knowledge who join there, it becomes possible to follow the steady blue light.
nuance: தூங்கொளி நீலம் (the hanging or steady blue light) is traditionally the Goddess, often described as blue, or a light seen in meditation. ஆங்கது சேரும் (who join there) leaves the place unnamed.

reading: If one draws near she gives a shoot of knowledge; even in bowing I bow strewing many flowers; the One whom nothing that approaches can know becomes the life of every world that approaches.
nuance: The subject of line 1 is unstated, and அணுகிய தொன்றறியாத ஒருவன் may be the Lord who is unknown to what approaches, or the one who knows nothing of what has come near. The verse plays on அணுகு (approach).

reading: When the two deeds stand evenly balanced, the sweet grace-power comes as the guru and removes many qualities; when one's own doing ends through the knowledge it gives, the three impurities end and one becomes Siva.
nuance: The chapter's doctrine stated plainly: இருவினை ஒப்பு (balance of good and bad deeds) is the sign of ripeness for the descent of power, the power comes in the form of the guru, and தன்செயல் அற்றால் (when one's own agency ends) the three malas go. குணம்பல நீக்கி is read as removing the soul's bound qualities. Sengalvaraya notes a parallel in Kumaraguruparar's Kandar Kalivenba.

reading: Thinking of her with flowing hair who makes fragrance in the place where there is neither night nor day, join her without a sound, and the Supreme, with no other care, will rule you.
nuance: இரவும் பகலும் இலாத இடம் (the place of no night or day) is traditionally a yogic state beyond the moon and sun breaths, or the state beyond waking and sleep. குரவம் may be the kuravam flower or a sound; அரவஞ்செய்யாமல் (without noise) may mean silently, or without the serpent (kundalini) stirring. பராபரை is the supreme Goddess.

reading: The evening lamp, the moon and the sun, and the lone flame, the Lord who lights the hall: the Lord who lit up knowledge entered me, lit up my flesh and stayed with me.
nuance: விளக்கு (lamp, to light) runs through every line, from outer lights to the light that lights the body. ஊனை விளக்கி (lit up the flesh) makes the body itself the place grace shines, not something to be left behind. Sengalvaraya notes Appar's verse beginning மாசில் வீணையும் மாலை மதியமும், which also opens with the evening moon.

title: அருசமயப் பிணக்கம்
theme: The quarrel of the six sects (அறுசமயப் பிணக்கம்): the six systems seek the Lord outside and miss the God who stands within the body; he is not the substance of any sect, and those who argue that this one or that one is good stay deluded and are born and die. The way is Siva's path, the guru's word and the light within, where no quarrel remains.
structure_note: Three movements: the sects miss the God within (1530 to 1533); Siva's path alone saves and the sects are waste (1534 to 1541); the Lord to be sought without distinction, and the inner light that ends the quarrel (1542 to 1549). The heading's word பிணக்கு appears only in 1547.
source_issues: 1535 line 3, முண்ணின் றழியு முயன்றிலராதலான், may be a misprint for உண்ணின்று.
1534: the word division யறையே சிவமாந் / தவம் is uncertain.

reading: The six sects that stand in the assembly do not see the God who stands within the body; caught in the bond of house and children, they fall writhing into the pit of maya.
nuance: ஆயத்துள் (in the assembly) is set against காயத்துள் (in the body), a near rhyme that carries the argument: the sects look in the crowd and miss the body. Which six sects are meant the verse doesn't say; tradition gives several lists.

reading: They do not know the purpose of the One who hid within the heart and stands everywhere, the generous chief, the great ascetic dwelling in the flower, the thief-chief who enters and leaves the hollow hut of the body.
nuance: பொள்ளற் குரம்பை (the hut full of holes) is the body with its nine openings. கள்ளத் தலைவன் (the thief-chief) is the Lord who comes and goes unseen. மலருறை மாதவன் may be the great ascetic in the heart's lotus or a name of Vishnu given to the one Lord; the verse doesn't settle it.

reading: For those who say he is within and without, our Lord is within and without; for those who say he is neither within nor without, he is neither within nor without.
nuance: A mirror verse. It can be read as the Lord appearing to each as each conceives him, or as an irony at the sects: what they say decides what they find. It doesn't say which view is right.

reading: Those who saw the six sects did not see him; he is not the thing the six sects hold; be clear, and having become clear, settle, and once settled you may enter the house without wavering.
nuance: தேறுமின், தேறித் தெளிமின், தெளிந்தபின் chains clarity to clarity. மனை (house, home) is read as release, the home one does not leave; it may also be plain household life lived without wavering.

reading: There is nothing but Siva, I declare; for those who reach him here there is nothing but the austerity that is Siva; the six sects are nothing but waste: cling to the feet of Nandi, strong in austerity, and be saved.
nuance: சிவம், தவம், அவம் rhyme through three lines. அறையே may be 'I proclaim' or a call. நந்தி may be Siva himself or Tirumular's teacher; the tradition uses the name for both. The line breaks are uncertain (யறையே சிவமாந் / தவம்).

reading: The six sects that sought the Lord, longing greatly to become gods, perish where they stand because they did not strive within, and so do not know the way to leave the earth.
nuance: முண்ணின் றழியு முயன்றிலர் is unclear: perhaps உண்ணின்று (within) with a misprint, as read here. விண்ணவராக (to become gods) faults the sects for seeking heaven rather than release from birth.

reading: Siva's path is the only path; all others are paths of becoming, and in them is a birth in bonds; if the path of austerity shows itself straight, the three of the wasted path are of that same kind.
nuance: சிவகதி, பவகதி, தவகதி, அவகதி play on கதி (path, end). Lines 3 and 4 are obscure: அவகதி மூவரும் may be the three gods (Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra) as ends in becoming, or three classes of the lost.

reading: Counted out, there are a hundred sects, and they fall within the six; the sects that are spoken of do not stay in the path they took; the end, the supreme path, is no path of theirs.
nuance: ஆறு சமயமவ் ஆறுட் படுவன may also read 'the six sects fall within those six' (the six inner sects of Saivism). The last line, ஈறு பரநெறி யில்லா நெறியன்றே, can be parsed as 'the supreme path is not a path without an end' or as read here; it is unclear.

reading: The wretched are like braying donkeys; pure Siva stands everywhere untouched, but not understanding the one who removes faults, takes up good qualities and cherishes, they go mad and are born and die every day.
nuance: The third line echoes Tiruvasagam (Ammanai), where குற்றங்கள் நீக்கிக் குணங்கொண்டு கோதாட்டி describes the Lord, which fixes its sense: the Lord is the one who removes faults and cherishes, and the deluded don't know him. தோய்வற்று (untouched) says Siva pervades without being stained.

reading: Whether bewildered or clear of mind, if people unite and drive the two deeds into the cave's mouth and, moving on, attain, then when the end is shown there is a supreme path for those whose fear is gone.
nuance: முழைமுகப் பாச்சி (driving into the mouth of the cave) is obscure; it may be yogic, the breath driven into an inner opening. The point that both the confused and the clear can reach the path is the plainest part.

reading: Far and near, without affliction, named Nandi, pure to those who can look without wavering: people bewildered by the deceiver do not know the purpose the body serves.
nuance: மாயன் may be Vishnu, often named the deluder, or maya personified. காயம் விளைக்குங் கருத்து (the intent the body produces) is read as the purpose for which the body is given; it may also mean the thoughts the body breeds.

reading: There is one seed for both ways: the blame of living on earth and clinging to it; those on the ruinous path do not stand before the word of the one who knows the whirl to seek the way.
nuance: வழி இரண்டு (both ways) is unexplained. சுழியறிவாளன் (the one who knows the whirl) is taken as the guru who knows the inner point (சுழி) of yoga. The verse is compressed and its grammar uncertain.

reading: All the great ascetics say Mahadeva is the Lord; Nandi is to be known as nada; if, without making distinctions, you worship with folded hands calling him Lord, the First himself stands as that path.
nuance: பேதஞ்செய்யாதே (without making distinctions) answers the chapter's quarrel: the remedy is not one sect's victory but worship that does not divide. நாதமதாக அறியப்படு (known as nada) gives the Lord a mantra-form.

reading: Hara's path, the Father, the First Lord, who became the strong path and entered the heart: if the minds of devotees who seek the supreme path do not become the Supreme's path, they are many kinds of distance away.
nuance: நெறி (path) ends every line: Hara's path, the strong path, the supreme path, the Supreme's path. The claim is that devotion itself must become the path, not merely seek it.

reading: He knows each one's nature, he is good, he is the sun; he shines in the attainment of those of great knowledge; think of him without fault, the pure gem-coloured one: rare is the path of virtue he set.
nuance: பரிசறிவான் may be 'he who knows the measure (of each)' or 'he who knows the gift'. அரிது (rare, hard) in the last line may say his path is hard to walk or precious.

reading: Give up the delusion of deluded men who say this sect or that one is good; seek the God beyond the forest, whose form is beyond all lack.
nuance: கானம் may be the forest (the wild of worldly life) or, as some take it, song; ஊனம் (lack, flaw) also means flesh, so ஊனங் கடந்த உரு may be a form beyond the flesh. The verse rejects the ranking of sects, not worship.

reading: Seeking that path, the immortals and sages saw the red path and were made Siva; those without the First's grace, who seek the earlier paths, do not go on the red path, and so are bewildered.
nuance: செந்நெறி (the red, straight path) is Siva's path. The verse makes grace the condition: those without it keep to முன்னெறி, the paths they began with. சிவனெனப் பெற்றார் (gained the state of being called Siva) anticipates sayujyam.

reading: If one knows how to reach and how to gain the light standing within, there is no quarrel at all; the poor in mind do not know how to end there, in the fire that is the way of cutting off.
nuance: பிணக்கொன்றும் இல்லை (no quarrel at all) answers the chapter's title: the sects' quarrel ends in the inner light, not in argument. வங்கி (fire, vahni) in line 3 is obscure; tradition may read it as the inner fire of yoga.

reading: There is one way to walk the path; the world listens to the fancies of those who walk astray; removing the grief that walks in whirlpools, even those who walk in blame may come to praise.
nuance: நட (walk) runs through every line. கழிநடக்குண்டவர் (those who walk to excess, or along the backwaters) and பரவல் (praise, or spreading) are uncertain; the last line may also mean that the grief spreads to those who walk in blame.

reading: When the great austerity that went the right way abides, cutting away the clinging of strong deeds that bring blame, and leaving the course of the strong deeds that follow, if one goes in due order, one stands before the Lord of the celestials.
nuance: வழி (way) is repeated, and வழிசெல்லும் வல்வினை may be 'the deeds that go with one on the way'. உழி is read as 'in due order' or 'at the right time'. The end is to stand before the Lord, not to become him.

title: நிராசாரம்
theme: Beyond sectarian observance (நிராசாரம்): those who master a sect's scriptures claim to know, but the Lord dwells with the forbearing and with those who hold his feet; sect-bound people who never turn to the Lord within weep, are reborn and perish inside the sect they could not leave.
structure_note: The chapter opens (1550) and closes (1556) on the six sects and those who stay in them. Between, verses set holding the Lord's feet against grieving neglect (1551, 1552), sort kinds of knowers (1553), and urge the mind to seek the Lord within (1554, 1555).
source_issues: 1550: இமையங்கள் and யமை (line 3) are unclear and may be corrupt; read here as இமையவர் and அமை.

reading: Those who stand as gods gained the six sects and, reciting the shastras, say 'we have understood'; but the First Lord stands mingled among those who know forbearance.
nuance: இமையங்களாய் நின்ற தேவர்கள் is obscure: இமையவர் are the unblinking gods, but இமையங்கள் may hide another word. யமை in line 3 is read as அமை (it is settled, we know); கமை is taken as Sanskrit kshama, forbearance. The contrast between scripture-learning and forbearance is the verse's point on this reading.

reading: People who bear the feet of the Lord with spreading matted hair and konrai blossom are without equal on earth; those who never think how to be freed stay in the world grieving and weeping.
nuance: நேர் ஒப்பர் can mean 'they are equal' (to the gods, or to one another) or 'they are incomparable'. நீங்கிய வண்ணம் is taken as the way of release from bonds; it could also mean the way the Lord stays apart.

reading: If those who weep and those whose nature has gone wrong take up rare austerity and think of the Lord there, the king of the gods keeps them from suffering, grants them greatness, and there is no more birth.
nuance: The verse picks up 1551's weepers and offers them a way back: even the fallen (இயல்பு கெட்டார்) are not shut out. வானவர் கோன் here is the Lord, not Indra.

reading: Those of deep knowledge do not think of any helper; those of worldly knowledge eat the fruit that falls to them; those of dark knowledge are born again, mixed in the world; those who know the water become the great tall cloud.
nuance: The four kinds of knower turn on puns I can't fix: தூர் (root, depth, or far), பார் (the earth), கார் (darkness, or the rain-season) and நீர் (water, or one's true nature, நீர்மை). The cloud of the last line may be one who, knowing, gives to all as rain does; that is a guess.

reading: Though they see the sign of the boat, called up with knowledge, spilling its load with its mast and its old home, the people of cruel deeds do not think to cling to the red feet.
nuance: The boat is commonly taken as the body that carries the soul; பறி (mast, or a fish-basket, or plunder) and பழம்பதி (the old dwelling) are unclear. The plain point stands: people see the body break up and still don't turn to the feet.

reading: If I say the one who abides is the one who dwells in the mind, people scorn it, these poor fools; mind, draw near and worship, and there you can reach even the one who has no companion.
nuance: மனோமயன், he who is made of or dwells in the mind, is the claim people scorn. துணையிலி, the one with no companion or equal, recalls the Kural's தனக்குவமை இல்லாதான். The verse turns from the scorners to address its own mind.

reading: Though the light within Om rises within them, they do not gain the experience free of the ego; before death they do not reach freedom from birth; they stood inside the sect they never left and perished.
nuance: ஓங்காரத்துள் ஒளி is a yogic term for the light seen in meditation on Om. ஆங்காரம் அற்ற அனுபவம is the experience of Siva without the 'I'. The verse's fault is not the sect as such but never moving beyond it (நீங்காச் சமயம்).

title: உட்சமயம்
theme: The inner religion (உட்சமயம்): the six sects are roads to one city and the Lord made them all, so quarrelling over which is good is a dog barking at a hill; within them Nandi set one Saiva path of the guru, Hara's path, which knowers and gods cannot reach by examining alone but which opens to those who worship his feet.
structure_note: 1557 and 1558 state the thesis about the six sects; 1559 to 1567 describe Hara's path and Nandi's Saiva way; 1568 returns to mocking those who rank penances; 1569 to 1572 turn to the Lord's faces, his inclusion of all deities and the hidden use of the body.
source_issues: 1560: பழிவழி (way of blame) may be a corruption of பழவழி (the old way).
1569: line 4 (நாமே பிரானுக்கு நரரியல் பாமே) is obscure and may be corrupt.
1565: மினற்குறி is read as மின்னல் குறி.

reading: The ancient First One who long ago shaped both the gods and us is the First Lord who moves among the six sects so that they seek his pair of feet.
nuance: அமையங்கு உழல்கின்ற is unclear: 'roams there among them' or 'is fitly there'. On either reading the six sects are his arrangement, not rivals to him.

reading: As one great city has six roads leading to it, so are the six sects; those who say 'this is good, that is bad' are like a dog that rises barking at a hill.
nuance: The hill is unmoved by the barking: the quarrel harms only the quarreller. The verse does not say every road is equally short; 1556 and 1567 show Tirumular still ranks a Saiva path.

reading: Come and reach, and be saved by, the unique Lord of Saiva greatness, Nandi the bright flame who gives life so that souls are saved, loving to those of true greatness, lord of the world who gives bliss.
nuance: சைவப் பெருமை names the Saiva path in a chapter that has just told sects not to rank one another; the inner religion is offered as fulfilment, not as a rival sect.

reading: For those able to know, by seeking the way he laid down within the divine path Siva set, that 'this one is he', he is there, and it becomes a duty.
nuance: பவன் may be Bhava, a name of Siva, and பழிவழி (the way of blame) may be a corruption of பழவழி (the old way). இவன் அவன் is often taken as recognizing the soul as one with the Lord, or the guru as the Lord; the verse does not settle which.

reading: For the six sects that teach how to become, there is no way to go except merit; for other souls, the way there is the flowering creeper of the supports.
nuance: ஆதாரப் பூங்கொடியாள், the flower-creeper lady of the ādhāras, is taken as Shakti or kundalini rising through the body's centres. The verse seems to set the sects' road of merit against an inner yogic road, but the syntax is loose.

reading: Even in the days when I knew Hara's path and still wandered searching other paths, the solitary flame stood on the strong path by which one crosses the sea of the heart and climbs.
nuance: The verse is autobiographical: the Lord was already waiting on the path while the speaker strayed. உரநெறி and தரநெறி (the strong path, the path of rank or crossing) are unclear.

reading: The Siva path that reached the discerned Hara, the great way by which those who turned away went in contemplation, the path of grace by which the fulfilled entered the beyond, coming and adorning it, becomes the path of union.
nuance: The verse piles up names for one path; பேர்ந்தவர் (those who moved away, from the world or from births) and போந்து புனைந்து are uncertain.

reading: Cast off the divided mind so that its twoness ends; recite the moving letter ச, and reciting, abide in Hara's path and contemplate; then the flame-light that fills will appear.
nuance: சகாரம், the letter ச, is traditionally the first letter of சிவாய and so stands for Siva in the five-letter mantra; ஊரும் (moving) may describe the breath carrying it. ஈரும் மனம் is the mind that splits or cuts.

reading: If you see the Lord whose sign is lightning, whose sign in the Brahmins' Veda is fire, the First Lord whose sign is thought, the dear sign at the tip of the shoot of knowledge, that is Hara's path.
nuance: The four குறி (signs) may be forms of the inner light; மினல் is read as மின்னல், lightning. நயக்குறி and ஞானக் கொழுந்து (the tip, or flame, of knowledge) are obscure.

reading: Hara's path stands so that souls, many though they are, cannot grasp it by examination; those who plunge in, worship his red feet with folded hands and, being worn away, understand, find it a bliss.
nuance: ஆன்மாச் சதுர்பல is obscure: perhaps 'souls of four and many kinds'. தேய்ந்துணர் may be 'understand as the self wears away'. The contrast between examining and plunging in is clear and recurs in 1571.

reading: Nandi, the unique Lord of the Saiva religion, laid down one guru's path for salvation: the divine Siva path, the true way, which he set out for those in the world to join and be saved.
nuance: சன்மார்க்கம், the true path, is in later Siddhanta the highest of four paths (after charya, kriya and yoga); whether Tirumular uses it in that technical sense here can't be fixed from this verse.

reading: Our great Nandi laughs when he sees madmen who give two names, 'this penance' and 'that penance'; whatever the penance, wherever one is born, those who understand alike can quickly enter the city.
nuance: ஒல்லை ஊர் is 'quickly, the city', echoing the one city of 1558. எங்குப் பிறக்கிலென் sets birth aside as well as sect.

reading: The Lord has five faces and is the precious soul; the Lord has a sixth face turned downward; for the Lord and his garland of skulls, we ourselves are the Lord's human nature.
nuance: The five faces are Sadasiva's; அதோமுகம், the downward face, is a sixth in some Agamic accounts. சிரமாலை may be a garland of heads (skulls) or a garland on his head. The last line is very obscure; I read it as the Lord taking human nature in us, but that is a guess.

reading: The First Lord who measured the seven worlds stands as the tidal sea and as all lives; Parasakti, standing undivided, is the deity of the beginning and the end.
nuance: உலகேழும் அளந்தவன், who measured the worlds, is Vishnu's epithet as Trivikrama; applied to the First Lord it fits the chapter's case that other sects' gods are his. Whether ஆதிப்பிரான் here is Vishnu, Siva or both can't be fixed.

reading: Gods and vidyadharas examine and know, yet Hara's path stands beyond their examining; I examined and knew to worship his red feet, and examining and knowing, I saw this life and the next.
nuance: ஆய்ந்தறி opens every line: the same examining that fails the gods succeeds when it ends in worship. இம்மை அம்மை is this life and the other.

reading: The use of the body, which cannot be known, he made into six unknowable kinds; in the six unknowable sheaths an unknowable cosmos is set.
nuance: அறியவொண்ணாத (cannot be known) opens every line. கோசம் is kosha, a sheath of the self; the usual count is five, so the six may be a different scheme. The point that the body holds a whole hidden cosmos is clear.

title: சிவகுரு தரிசினம்
theme: Seeing the Siva-guru (சிவகுரு தரிசனம்): the true guru is Siva himself come into the world, who tests, removes the bonds and shows the soul, the bonds and the Lord; siddhi, release and the knowledge of Vedanta cannot be known except by his grace, and fools who take him for an ordinary man miss it.
structure_note: 1573 to 1578 define the Siva-guru by what he does; 1579 to 1587 insist that every attainment comes through his grace, with 1581 as the summary 'the guru is Siva'; 1588 and 1589 close in the first person, with the speaker's own release.
source_issues: 1582: line 1 reads சித்த யாவையும், probably for சித்தம் யாவையும் as in line 3.
1583: largely obscure; the play on நந்தி and அந்தி may hide a corruption.

reading: Making one bow in devotion, giving the feet to praise, testing with pure teaching so that fault is removed, and showing the real, the unreal and the real-unreal: because he does this, the guru who is mind and Lord is the Siva-guru.
nuance: சத்து, அசத்து, சதசத்து (sat, asat, sadasat) are traditionally the Lord, the bonds and the soul, which is neither wholly real nor unreal but takes the nature of what it joins. சித்தம் இறையே is unclear: 'the mind is the Lord' or 'the guru whose mind is the Lord'.

reading: Gathering the bonds, binding them and plucking them out, freeing one from the cherished body, and directly joining one to release without shame: the faultless true guru with this aim is the hall itself.
nuance: அம்பலம், the hall, is the dance hall of Chidambaram, so the guru is equated with the place of the Lord's dance; it may also be read as the open space of consciousness. கூசற்ற முத்தி is release without shrinking or shame.

reading: The eight siddhis, the purification that makes one firmly Siva, the purity of the eight powers, the power in yoga, the knowledge of mantra practice and devotion: all are learned by the Lord's grace.
nuance: எண்சத்தி, the eight powers, may be the Lord's eight shaktis or the eight siddhis again. நாதன் here is the Lord, who in this chapter is the guru.

reading: Because he who is beyond all the worlds comes here, gives abundant grace in the hearts of the good, and takes everyone to save them and protects them, the good guru praised in words is pure Siva.
nuance: அப்பாலோன் இப்பாலாய், the one beyond becoming the one here, is the chapter's whole doctrine of the guru in four words.

reading: God, the pure guru and the means: by teaching you to see everything as these three, and removing the unaging bond of soul and fetter, the supreme guru in love gives everything that belongs to release.
nuance: தேவன், சுத்த குரு, உபாயம் (God, guru, means) is one triad; the verse may also mean seeing everything as the three categories of Pati, pasu and pasam. மூவாப் பசுபாசம் is the soul's beginningless bondage.

reading: The utter fools who do not see the grace pure Siva gives by coming as guru and purifying say 'he is one of us, with eyes that deceive'; the meritorious bow at his feet, saying 'this is the Father'.
nuance: பொய்த்தகு கண்ணான் நமர் is obscure: perhaps 'a man of ours, seen by deceived eyes', the fools mistaking the guru for an ordinary man. The verse sets two ways of seeing the same person.

reading: Removing falsehood by truth, the firmness of the world of truth, the bounty of Hara who is bright Siva, and the bewilderment of the sixty-four siddhis: who knows these except by the Lord's grace?
nuance: எட்டெட்டுச் சித்தி may be sixty-four or eight and eight. மயக்கம் may mean the siddhis' power to bewilder, a warning against them, or the bewildering wonder of them.

reading: Because Siva himself is the Siva-jnani, those who can reach his feet saying 'pure Siva' gain the good release of the new tattva; there is no more becoming, and there is the supreme world.
nuance: சிவஞானி is the guru as knower of Siva, here said to be Siva himself. நவமான தத்துவம் may be 'the new tattva' or 'the ninefold tattva'.

reading: Nandi said the guru is Siva; people do not grasp that the guru is Siva; the guru stands as Siva and as king; the guru is a king beyond word and thought.
nuance: குருவே opens every line. The teaching is given on Nandi's authority, the guru of Tirumular's own line.

reading: All that is thought abides in thinking; by grace one is made to know the meaning; when the whole mind becomes firmly Siva, the Father settles right there.
nuance: சித்த யாவையும் is unclear and may be a slip for சித்தம் யாவையும், which opens line 3. அத்தம் is 'meaning' and அத்தன் 'the Father': the verse plays on the two.

reading: No one knows the intent of Nandi, the king and our father, who set the glory met within his own glory; to one who rejoices calling him the Nandi of the sky, he becomes the solitary flame of fire at dusk.
nuance: The verse plays on நந்தி and அந்தி (dusk) and is largely opaque. அங்கித் தனிச்சுடர் (the lone flame of fire) recalls the inner light of yoga; the sense I give is a guess.

reading: The holy siddhi and release, the grace that grants glory without bewilderment, and the knowledge of Vedanta that is the truthful meaning ending delusion cannot be known unless the Lord takes form and gives grace.
nuance: நாதன் உருவாய், the Lord taking form, is the guru: knowledge of Vedanta is not reached by study alone.

reading: Devotion and the knowledge that is dispassion are the seed of the supreme siddhi; because one joins 'I am Siva', the knowledge of release sprouts; and if Shakti gives grace, that sprout grows easily.
nuance: சிவோகம், 'I am Siva', is a meditation in which the self is identified with Siva; whether this is a practice or the state reached is unclear. The seed and sprout image echoes 1932.

reading: Our Lord, the First One, who set before me the blissful birth to be attained later, reveals himself when his time comes; it is the mind he set to be held steady.
nuance: இன்பப் பிறப்பு, a blissful birth, may be the new birth given by the guru's initiation. The last line is unclear: perhaps the Lord appears as, or in, the mind made steady.

reading: Clear Siva-knowledge is bright siddhi; clear Siva-knowledge is bright release; Siva-knowledge goes as one into the supreme Siva; Siva-knowledge gives Siva's bliss.
nuance: சிவமான ஞானம் opens every line. The verse makes Siva-knowledge itself the attainments that 1575 and 1584 list separately.

reading: I have known and understood this whole wide world; understanding closely and reciting, I gained holy grace; I have forgotten and left the life of those whose wits are dead; I was born and have ended this birth.
nuance: பிறந்தொழிந்தேன் means 'I was born and am done', so this birth is the last. மதி மாண்டவர் (those whose understanding has died) are the worldly the speaker has left behind.

reading: People do not understand at all how the Lord of all the many lives he sustains is present; cutting away this dividing quarrel, I saw the Lord who holds everything as in a womb.
nuance: பிரிக்கின்ற பிணக்கு, the quarrel that divides, may be the sense of separation between soul and Lord or the sects' disputes of chapter 106. கருக்கொண்ட, having conceived, makes the Lord the womb of all.

title: திருவடிப் பேறு
theme: Attaining the holy feet (திருவடிப் பேறு): the guru, Nandi, lays his hand and his feet on the disciple's head, heart and eyes, removes the forms of the self and makes him Siva beyond words; the knowledge of the holy feet is itself Siva-hood, release and every mantra, medicine and path.
structure_note: 1590 to 1597 narrate the speaker's initiation in the first person: the touch, the feet on the head, the ending of forms and words. 1598 to 1604 generalize: what the knowledge of the feet does, what neglecting them brings, and the feet as all things.
source_issues: 1591: lines 3 and 4 (வீடந்தம் இன்றியே யாள்கென, பாடின் முடிவைத்துப் பார்வந்து தந்ததே) are obscure and may be corrupt.
1603: lines 3 and 4 are compressed and unclear.

reading: As love rose in harmony, the guru red as Siva came and placed his hand on my head, so that I went to the Lord who rises with tenderness within the bond, and the guru's joyful feet came gladly into my heart.
nuance: சென்னி கை வைக்க, placing the hand on the head, is traditionally taken as initiation by touch (hasta-diksha). பாசத்துள் ஏக is unclear: going within the bond, or the bond going.

reading: When he gave his feet, our Lord took my head; he gave me the strength of knowledge that is a sword and, leaving me with 'rule without end of release', set a crown on me in grace's glory and gave me the world.
nuance: தலைதந்த can mean the Lord gave headship or took the head (the ego) in exchange; the exchange of feet for head is a common devotional image. பாடு and பார்வந்து தந்தது are unclear.

reading: Becoming himself, coming into my true form, he removed the four forms that had arisen; good Nandi, who ruled me giving the other seal, first crowned me with his feet and established me: this is true.
nuance: சொரூபம், the self's own form, and the four சொரூபங்கள் are technical; they may be the four states preceding the true form. முத்திரை may be a ritual gesture given in initiation or a seal of identity.

reading: Word ended, feeling ended, soul and supreme ended; like water without waves, he did away even with becoming Siva and set me in the true form beyond the shoreless four beginning with being; we passed beyond words.
nuance: சிவமாதல் தீர்த்து, ending even the becoming-Siva, goes past any state still named. சத்தாதி நான்கு (the four beginning with sat) are unclear. Sengalvaraya notes a near-identical opening in Kandar Alangaram 61.

reading: The guru took the soul's three forms and took the rare reality as a seal; Nandi, the feet of the great Lord, wordless, took me there and saved me so that I melted.
nuance: உயிர் முச்சொரூபம், the soul's three forms, and பொருள் முத்திரை are technical terms I can't fix.

reading: In the great bliss beyond speech, he made me, freed of stain, Siva and made me die; the flawless light took over the three debts and, so that the fame that had come died away, gave his feet and abides.
nuance: மாள்வித்து, causing to die, is the death of the self. கடன் மூன்று (three debts) may be the three malas or the three traditional debts; வாச்ச புகழ் மாள, the fame that came dying away, is unclear.

reading: How Nandi, the supreme, who set his feet in my heart, my eyes and my head, gave me the goal, how he showed the truth and how he set the rule cannot be spoken.
nuance: Heart, eyes and head are the places of the guru's touch and gaze in initiation as tradition reads it; the verse ends, like 1593, in what cannot be said.

reading: Placing his holy feet on my head and looking with grace, I saw great Nandi who took a great form, the king, our king, in the form of the guru, so that the path to the womb was drained away.
nuance: கருவழி வாற்றிட, draining the womb-path, is ending rebirth. The guru's form and Nandi's great form are one in what the speaker saw.

reading: Knowledge of the holy feet makes one Siva; knowledge of the holy feet brings one to Sivaloka; knowledge of the holy feet frees one from the prison of impurity; knowledge of the holy feet is itself firm siddhi and release.
nuance: திருவடி ஞானம் opens every line. It may mean knowledge of the feet or the knowledge that the feet are; the verse lets both stand.

reading: If one does not do as he set above, the deeds to come will turn a mind dazed by delusion into illusion; this is how the sky-dweller of spreading light, with milk on his head, set his feet and made me bear them.
nuance: மேல்வைத்தவாறு (as he set above, or as set out above) and மேல்வினை (later karma, or karma on top) play on மேல். பால் on the head may be the moon or the Ganga. The link between the two halves is unclear.

reading: I gained the shade called the anklet-bearing lotus holy feet; the First Lord within the fire that tall Mal could not know will also break apart the nest of my life where the coil dwells.
nuance: நெடுமால் அறியா அழல் recalls the story of the column of fire whose end Vishnu could not find. குழல் சேரும் கூடு (the nest where the coil or tube joins) is taken as the body with kundalini or the central channel; breaking it may mean release from the body.

reading: Crowned kings rule the three worlds, but the bliss of those who are kings of the feet has no measure, if you ask; the gods who stood as crowned kings stood free of fault as subjects of the Lord.
nuance: முடிமன்னர் and அடிமன்னர், kings of the crown and kings of the feet, set head against feet: kingship at the Lord's feet outranks the gods' own crowns.

reading: I set his feet within my mind so as not to go by the senses that burn falsely; worn out, I turned away the two whirling deeds and knew the true honey, the end of the Veda.
nuance: இருவினை, the two deeds, are good and bad karma, both binding. புலன் வழி, the way of the senses, is the opposite of keeping the feet in mind. மெய்த்தேன் puns on true honey and 'I attained truth'.

reading: The sages of old placed on their heads the Lord's two feet, to which one may cling; this is the principle of those who stand joined to the path of those who dwell in the ancient flood of bliss on earth.
nuance: Lines 3 and 4 are compressed: படிசார்ந்த (come down to earth, or in due order) and குடிசார் நெறி (the path of the household of devotees) are uncertain.

reading: What is mantra, what is great medicine, what is tantra, what are gifts, what is beauty and what is the pure path: it is our Father Lord's pair of feet.
nuance: தானங்கள் may be gifts (dana) or holy places (sthana). The verse folds every religious means, ritual and textual, into the feet.

title: ஞாதுரு ஞான ஞேயம்
theme: Knower, knowing and known (ஞாதுரு, ஞானம், ஞேயம்): for one who stands in Siva as the known, the bonds and the ego lose their hold and the two of 'I' and 'He' become one. Tirumular speaks of Nandi as the guru who reworked his tattvas, broke his ignorance and showed him a state beyond the senses; silence and the mudras complete the knower.
structure_note: Three verses on standing in the known (1605 to 1607), three in the first person on what Nandi did (1608 to 1610, each ending நந்தியே), and three on silence, mudra and the knower (1611 to 1613).
source_issues: 1609 line 3 reads தன்aன, a Latin letter for ன; read தன்னை.
1611 line 3 (மோனங்கை வந்தூமை யாமொழி) can be split more than one way.

reading: For one who stands in the known, the unfailing bliss of Siva, the bonds that cling do not spread, and even if they spread, once the ego is gone and one holds that state, the unfailing state of nectar is reached.
nuance: ஞேயம், what is to be known, is here Siva himself as the bliss that does not leave. The verse allows that bonds may still arise (படரினும்) and makes the loss of ஆங்காரம், the ego, the condition. அமுத நிலை may be the deathless state or the yogic nectar of earlier chapters; both readings stand.

reading: For those who stand in the known, knowledge and the rest follow; the knower of the known finds release in the known, and those who reach the known of the known know the knowledge that stands in the gathering.
nuance: The verse turns ஞேயம் over five times, and the phrases (ஞேயத்தின் ஞாதுரு, ஞேயத்தின் ஞேயம்) resist a fixed sense. ஆயம் may be the assembly of the tattvas, the soul's faculties, or the company of the knowers; I cannot fix which.

reading: The reality appears as two, 'self' and 'He'; seeing both within oneself and offering the flower called 'self' at His feet, one finds that saying 'I' and 'He' is no longer right.
nuance: The self offered as a flower turns outer worship into an inner act. The last line, நல்லது ஒன்று அன்றே, can be read as 'is no good thing' (duality is wrong) or as the rhetorical 'is it not the one good thing'; the first fits the verse's movement from two to one, but the second is not ruled out.

reading: Nandi changed the thirty-six tattvas set in me and set me anew, laid the Supreme's all-pervading nature over me to be praised, made it sure, made me Siva, and through the known destroyed my fear and took me as his own.
nuance: வாறாறு is read as ஆறாறு, six sixes, the thirty-six tattvas. வியாத்துவம் is vyaptva, pervasion. Nandi is both Tirumular's guru and a name of Siva; the verse lets the two stand together.

reading: Nandi broke through the ignorance in my later knowledge, which was like that of fools who never knew, made me the Supreme so that I might know myself, and stayed, making me know myself in his own Siva-state.
nuance: The first two lines are hard: முன்னை அறிவு and பின்னை அறிவு may be the soul's knowledge before and after the guru's work, or before and after birth. தற்சிவம் is taken as Siva's own state. The third line is misprinted in the source.

reading: Nandi came and showed me, saying 'see': an eye that does not see, a hearing that does not hear, an enjoyment that does not swerve, a union that is no joining, a modesty that feels no shame, and the awareness at nada's end.
nuance: Each phrase pairs a faculty with its negation, so the state shown is one where seeing, hearing, enjoying and joining go on without the senses or a second party. நாதாந்தம், the end of nada, is a technical term for the stage beyond primal sound.

reading: For those to whom silence has come, release comes too, the powers stand before them, all speech ends in a mute word, and the five acts come forward.
nuance: மோனம் கைவந்தோர் is those for whom silence has become natural, not merely those who keep a vow of speech. Line 3 (வந்தூமை யாமொழி) is read as ஊமையாம் மொழி, a speech that is mute; it can also be split to mean they become mute and speech ends. That the five acts, the Lord's work, 'come forward' for them is a strong claim and may mean they share in it.

reading: Those who, through the three mudras, turned back the kala and breath set in the three by a fourfold measure, and cut off their bondage at the bright guru's feet in that bliss, are neither born nor die.
nuance: The three mudras, the three in which they end, and the fourfold measure (நான்மடங்கு) of kala and breath are technical and unnamed. பெத்தம் is baddha, the bound state, which the verse sets against release. Only the conclusion, freedom from birth and death at the guru's feet, is plain.

reading: The supreme knower holds the mudra nurtured by abundant Shakti, the three higher forms; entering the known, the resounding dance, he stands as the root-form, the one called the knower.
nuance: மேலைச் சொரூபங்கள் மூன்று are not named; they may be three forms of Siva or three states beyond the waking ones. ஆலித்த நட்டம் (the roaring or resounding dance) is made the known itself, so the dance is what the knower enters. மூலச் சொரூபன் may be the knower or Siva; the verse ends by naming him ஞாதுரு.

title: துறவு
theme: Renunciation (துறவு): Siva, himself a renouncer who lives in the burning ground and eats alms, cuts the births of those who renounce and becomes their light. The renouncer refuses the senses' claims for the tapas of reaching his feet, keeps to the path whose thorns hurt only those who stray, and, in a run of riddling images, turns the body's energies inward.
structure_note: Plain verses on Siva and the renouncer (1614 to 1618, 1620, 1622) alternate with symbolic ones whose sense is not fixed: the ploughman (1619), the five-hooded serpent (1621) and the nine gates (1623).
source_issues: 1623 is obscure throughout (ஆம்பற் குழலியின் கஞ்சுளி, வேம்பேறி, கூம்பேறி) and may be corrupt.
1621 line 1 (படம்ஐந்து நாலது) is unclear; நாலது may be a corruption.

reading: To those who, never forgetting, daily speak of the radiant Lord who saw the tapas of renouncing free of death, birth and the two deeds, the Lord of the immortals shows the abode of dharma.
nuance: இருமை, the two, is usually the two kinds of deed, good and bad, though it can mean this world and the next. அறப்பதி may be the abode of dharma or Siva's realm as dharma's seat. The verse joins renunciation to unforgetting speech of the Lord rather than to bodily austerity.

reading: The soul that is born and dies again through much folly, forgetting, finds that once it has renounced, at the ripe time for joining Siva's grace, its many darknesses vanish and grace becomes its blazing light.
nuance: சேர்பருவம், the season of joining, is traditionally the soul's ripeness for grace, when its malas are mature. The verse makes renunciation the soul's part and the light grace's, without saying which comes first.

reading: The righteous one, unborn, with no one of his own, dwells in the burning ground and eats alms; see, he too is a renouncer, the mad one who cuts off the births of those who renounce.
nuance: காட்டகம் is the burning ground or the wild; பிச்சை and பித்தன் are Siva's familiar epithets as beggar and madman. The verse makes Siva the model renouncer, so the renouncer imitates the Lord rather than merely obeying him.

reading: He made the path and made the thorn; if you slip from the path the thorn pierces, but for those who can walk without slipping, the path's thorns do not pierce.
nuance: நெருஞ்சில் is the caltrop, a low creeper with spiked burrs that lame the barefoot walker beside a path. The plain reading is that suffering comes from straying, not from the path itself; the verse does not say whether the Lord sends the thorn as punishment or merely set it there.

reading: The five came demanding ruin and their dues and closed in on me; I owe them nothing, for mine is the resolve of tapas that reaches the holy feet of the lord whose mount is the dancing bull.
nuance: The image is of creditors or tax-collectors: கடமை is a due or levy, and நான் கடவேன் அலேன் 'I am not a debtor'. The five (ஐவர்) are traditionally the five senses, which the verse does not name.

reading: The ploughman ploughed and the sky gave rain; a blue lily bloomed in his furrows, and saying it was like the eyes of the ploughwomen, the ploughman gave up ploughing.
nuance: A riddle with no key in the verse. Read symbolically, the ploughman is the seeker, the ploughing his discipline, the rain grace and the lily the vision that makes further effort needless. Read plainly, he is distracted by a reminder of women's eyes and abandons his work. Its place in a chapter on renunciation favours the first, but both stand.

reading: For those who renounce what is above, the Lord is a shining light; for those who renounce the day set by Death, he is a friend without desire; for those who renounce darkness, he stands as the one with an eye in his forehead; only those who renounce the earth can reach his state.
nuance: The verse grades renunciations by what is given up (heaven, death's day, darkness, the earth) and pairs each with an aspect of Siva. மேல் and கார் are not fixed: மேல் may be the heavens, கார் dark ignorance or the rain cloud. The climax puts giving up the earth highest.

reading: There is one serpent with five hoods, settled and filling the anthill of enjoyment; when its two bodies stop spreading their hoods and dancing and it makes a single hood, the body becomes its proper dwelling.
nuance: The serpent is traditionally the soul with its five senses as hoods, living in the anthill of the body; the 'two bodies' (ஆகம் இரண்டு) may be the gross and subtle bodies, or the two breaths. A yogic reading takes the serpent as kundalini. நாலது in line 1 is unclear. Either way the image is of many hoods drawn into one.

reading: The primal Lord, the source of the way of those who have left all, is not so easy that one can stand and say 'this is he'; Siva's feet become many, many souls, and we do not know the way his goodness comes.
nuance: அகன்றார் is those who have gone away, the renouncers. சிவன் தாள் பலபல சீவனும் ஆகும் is hard: it may mean that Siva's feet are present in many souls, or that many souls reach them. நயன், goodness or grace, is left unexplained, which is the verse's point.

reading: The nine gateways opened their channels and something was caught in the wallet of the one with lily-like tresses; the helmsman climbed the neem tree and looked: this is how it flowers in the temple, climbing the mast on the roof.
nuance: Only the nine gates are clear: the nine openings of the body. ஆம்பல் குழலி (one whose tresses are like the water-lily, or a pipe), கஞ்சுளி (a mendicant's bag), the helmsman (மீகாமன்) on the neem, and the mast climbing to the temple are traditionally read as the breath or the yogi's awareness rising to the crown of the head, but the verse gives no key.

title: தவம்
theme: Tapas (தவம்): those who withdraw and let go of attachment are beyond fear, death and the turn of day and night; only those with the Lord's grace know what tapas is; it ends birth where asking only wins wealth; no threat shakes the true ascetic, and the Lord comes near only to such. Yet the chapter ends by saying tapas is needed only until the samadhi of knowledge is reached.
structure_note: Praise of tapas and the tapasvin (1624 to 1630), then the inward look that replaces learned talk (1631), and a closing verse (1632) that limits tapas to a stage, leading into the next chapter.
source_issues: 1632 line 3 reads மச்ச கசமார்க்கத்தோர்க்கு, probably corrupt; perhaps for (அ)ச்ச சகமார்க்கத்தோர்க்கு.

reading: For those excellent ones who have withdrawn and become steady and let go of attachment, the heart does not tremble, Yama is not there, nor suffering, nor night and day, nor any fruit of deeds to undergo.
nuance: ஒடுங்கி is withdrawal, of the senses into the mind or the mind into stillness. The list of absences is built so that letting go of பற்று, named only in the last word, is the cause of all of them. இராப்பகல் இல்லை may also be a yogic reference to a state beyond the sun and moon breaths.

reading: None but those who have received the Lord's holy grace know the nature of this great tapas, or all the precious lives and the appearing of the wide earth, or the greatness of what true tapas does.
nuance: The verse makes grace prior to tapas: even knowing what tapas is depends on it. The first line, all lives and the appearing of the world, can be read as more things grace reveals or as the effects of tapas itself; the grammar allows both.

reading: People who ask for many things, not knowing what birth is, get the wealth they wanted with honour; those who do great tapas without forgetting win the greatness of ending birth.
nuance: பிச்சைசெய் மாந்தர் may be beggars in the plain sense or worshippers who beg favours of the Lord; the contrast is between asking for goods and the tapas that seeks no goods but an end to birth. The verse grants that asking works; it ranks it lower.

reading: Whoever comes to unsettle the great ones who sit enduring hardship in their fair tapas, even Indra himself, their minds are set right upon Siva.
nuance: Indra sending distractions to break an ascetic's tapas is a familiar puranic motif; the verse answers it by placing the ascetic's steadiness in Siva rather than in his own strength.

reading: Hidden, yet not hidden, he does not appear to the eye: he of the spreading matted hair and the colour of fresh gold, wearing the white moon, cannot be approached except by those of rare tapas, and is to be worshipped without delay.
nuance: கரந்தும் கரந்திலன், hiding yet not hidden, is a paradox common in Saiva hymns: present everywhere but not seen. The verse gives a full iconographic image while denying that the eye sees it.

reading: The First, our Lord, who set the blissful birth to be reached later and set what must come first, reveals himself when the time to reach him comes; it is the mind, set to reach him firmly, that does this.
nuance: இன்பப் பிறப்பு, a birth of joy, may be a heavenly birth or the birth in which release comes; what is 'set to come first' (முன்னெய்த வைத்த) is not named, and in this chapter may be tapas. The last line's மன் எய்த may be 'to reach firmly' or 'to reach the king'. The chain of 'set' (வைத்த) makes the Lord the arranger of the soul's sequence.

reading: Caught in the midst of the uproar when ministers, troops of elephants and kings rise in enmity, those who kept their gaze on the knowledge they had set up and on the trustworthy one, and stayed unblinking and unharmed, are the people of tapas.
nuance: ஆத்தம் is āpta, the trustworthy one or the trustworthy word, traditionally the Lord or the scripture he gives. The scene is literal war, and the claim is that the tapasvin's stillness holds even there. இமைத்தழியாது can be 'without blinking' or 'without perishing in a blink'.

reading: Leave the cleverness of reciting the shastras and, for the space of a moment, turn back and look within; that look, fixed like a nail driven into green wood, drives off the births that bind.
nuance: மாத்திரைப் போது is the length of a single measure, the shortest unit of time. பசுமரத்து ஆணி, a nail in green wood, is the proverbial image of what goes in easily and holds firm. The verse sets a moment's inward look against a lifetime of scriptural talk.

reading: Tapas is needed if one is to reach knowledge, but not needed once the samadhi of knowledge is in hand; tapas is not needed by those on the path of the companion, and they do not know the word that says 'no tapas'.
nuance: Lines 1 and 2 are clear: tapas is a means that falls away. Line 3 (மச்ச கசமார்க்கத்தோர்க்கு) is probably corrupt; if it is சகமார்க்கம், it is the 'path of the companion', traditionally the yoga stage of the Saiva fourfold path. Line 4 is obscure: it may mean they don't need tapas because they are past the debate, or that they never learned the teaching that tapas is unneeded.

title: தவ நிந்தை
theme: The limits of tapas (தவ நிந்தை): once the Life of life is within and samadhi is in hand, recitation, chant, purity rites and even tapas fall away; true tapas is knowing the outcome, cutting the senses with the sword of understanding, a single-pointed mind and the fellowship of those already in Siva's bliss. Those without tapas or learning only whirl around for food.
structure_note: The title, literally 'reproach of tapas', is not borne out as an attack: the verses list what becomes needless (1633, 1634, 1644), redefine true tapas (1635, 1638, 1639, 1641) and fault those with none (1642).
source_issues: 1636 line 4 (இவைகளைந் தூடிற் பலவுல கோரெத் தவரே) and 1643 lines 2-3 (கோணியைப் பல்காற் குழக்கன்று) are obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: Recitation is not needed if the Life of life has come within; desire is not needed if one sees the true body as its place; dying is not needed if samadhi is in hand; going about is not needed for those who do not follow the senses.
nuance: Each line pairs a practice or urge with the attainment that makes it needless. மெய்க்காயம் இடம் கண்டால் may mean seeing the body as the Lord's dwelling, in line with Tirumular's body-as-temple teaching. சாதலும் வேண்டாம் may be that death is overcome or that one need not seek death; போதல் may be pilgrimage.

reading: No need to cry out once one has grasped the meaning and grown calm; no need of sounded chant once samadhi is in hand; no need of purification for one who stands free of pollution; no need even of the mind for one who rests without action.
nuance: சத்தம் may be audible chant or sound in general. துடக்கு is ritual pollution (as from birth or death) and also attachment, so line 3 can be ritual or moral. The last line goes furthest: the mind itself is put among the things that become needless.

reading: Those who know the outcome do the true tapas of old, speak the true word of old and do the true dharma of old; those who know the outcome surpass those of heaven and of earth.
nuance: விளைவு, what grows from an act, is the fruit of deeds; to know it is to see where each act leads. பண்டை, of old, presents the right way as ancient rather than new.

reading: Doing tapas in company, I saw the sounding anklets; doing tapas in search, I saw the Siva-state; is wasting oneself away tapas? If they cast these off and quarrel, what tapas have the many worldly people?
nuance: Line 3 (வாடித் தவஞ்செய்வதே தவம்) can be read as a statement, 'tapas done in wasting is tapas', or as a question, which fits the chapter's criticism of mortification. கூடி may be 'in the company of devotees' or 'united with the Lord'. Line 4 is obscure.

reading: Those who have swum with their arms across the seven great seas of the mind come into the shelter of the people of tapas; if those still in the round of birth listen to them and serve them, they may come face to face with Nandi.
nuance: The seven seas are not explained; they may be the mind's restless states, seven births or the seven bodily centres. The verse gives a chain of mediation: the tapasvins reach shelter, and the worldly reach Nandi through serving them.

reading: Draw the sword of understanding that stands in the mind, cut yourself from the crowd, cleave it so that no two remain, and turn back the five so they do not stray into the field: then, within tapas, the light of the way becomes your own light.
nuance: புனம், the millet field, is the field of sense objects and the five are the senses, as tradition reads them. இனம் may be the senses as a band or bad company. ஆறொளி may be the light of the path or the light of the six centres; the plain sense is that discipline makes the light one's own.

reading: To speak of him who stands equal to all and beyond all gives devotion; the sage gives release to the devotees who bow and worship; to act in that state as one who is real is itself tapas.
nuance: ஒத்து மிகவும் நின்றான், one who is equal and also exceeds, is taken as the Lord who is in all and beyond all. சத்தான செய்வது (doing what is sat, real) is the verse's definition of tapas, but its sense is not fixed: it may be acting as the real self, or doing what is true.

reading: Touching leaves and plucking flowers, I gathered them thinking 'for my father', but did not see the water that comes; seeing the scripture that reaches the summit my heart bowed, and touching the summit I saw how tapas is taken up.
nuance: The verse moves from outer worship (leaves, flowers, water for the Lord's bath) to something reached at the தலை, head or summit. தலை தொட்ட நூல் may be the highest scripture, and தலை தொட்டு may be touching one's head in reverence or, yogically, reaching the crown. வரும் புனல் காணேன் may be a confession of incomplete outer worship or a hint at inner water.

reading: The Lord grants that no trouble reaches the devotees who hold to the great tapas of matted hair; looked at truly, the tapas of those who take on hardship lies in a single mind that holds the body in check.
nuance: Line 3 (இடரடை செய்தவர்) can be those who take on hardship or those who cause it; line 4's உடரடை is read as உடல் அடை, holding the body. The verse seems to move the worth of tapas from outward marks to one-pointedness of mind.

reading: Like one who, frightened by a crocodile lying in the river, runs off and meets a she-bear that has just given birth, so are those who do no tapas and do not know the books, standing and whirling around for rice.
nuance: ஈற்றுக் கரடி, a bear that has just whelped, is at its fiercest; fleeing one danger, the man meets a worse. The verse's target is a life spent chasing food, where each escape leads to a new danger.

reading: Those who can tie up in its stall the frisking young calf that keeps butting at the sack will find in the heart, without slipping, how the fruit ripens and how the fruit is eaten.
nuance: The calf is traditionally the mind and the stall the place it is held; கோணி may be a sack of fodder or something bent. The ripening and eating of the fruit is the fruit of discipline coming to fulfilment, but the verse does not name the fruit.

reading: No tapas is needed to make the mind Siva if one has kinship with those whose minds have joined Siva's bliss; when the mind becomes Siva, siddhi and release follow; the mind becoming Siva is the fruit of tapas done.
nuance: The verse gives two routes to one end: fellowship (உறவு) with those in Siva's bliss, which makes tapas unnecessary, and tapas itself, whose fruit is the same. Sengalvaraya notes a parallel in Tiruvasagam (அச்சோப் பதிகம் 1), where the Lord removes the mind's malas and makes it Siva.

title: அருளுடைமையின் ஞானம் வருதல்
theme: Knowledge comes from possessing grace (அருளுடைமையின் ஞானம் வருதல்): the Lord's grace is the source of good wealth, knowledge, greatness and divinity; it keeps deeds from clinging, removes birth and makes the soul one with Siva, and it is to be won in embodied life. Tirumular ends by vowing not to let go of Nandi until release.
structure_note: Litanies on what grace gives (1645, 1649, 1650), verses on merit and sin and the end of birth (1647, 1648), images of the soul taking on what it faces (the chariots in 1651, the sun- and moonstones in 1653), and a closing first-person vow (1654).
source_issues: 1653 line 3 (சதிகொண்ட சாக்கி) is obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: If the Lord's grace is there, good wealth is there; if the Lord's grace is there, good knowledge is there; in the Lord's grace there is greatness, and in the Lord's grace one becomes the great deity.
nuance: The last line, பெருந்தெய்வமும் ஆமே, can mean that grace makes one divine or that the great God himself is reached in it. The chapter title borrows the Kural's chapter name அருளுடைமை but means the Lord's grace, not compassion between beings.

reading: People wander the world as if spitting out the knowledge that spread across the five Tamil lands; yet the loosening mind, the knowledge of our Primal One and the five Tamil lands are all tattva.
nuance: தமிழ் மண்டலம் ஐந்து is usually taken as the five Tamil regions, where the teaching spread; some read the five mandalas yogically, as regions of the body. உமிழ்வது போல (as if spitting out) may mean rejecting the knowledge or pouring it out. The verse's claim that all of it is tattva is clear; its tone toward the wanderers is not.

reading: Merit and sin are two that come with one to the earth, and a few knowers see this when it happens; weigh them, cut both at the root, and seek out the Lord's dwelling beyond them.
nuance: The verse asks for both merit and sin to be uprooted, since both bind to birth; it does not rank merit above sin. தப்பு அப்புறத்து is read as 'beyond, escaping both'.

reading: Grace that goes before at the time of ending stands in the world as the life at the centre; grace that stays behind removes birth; standing before me, it gave me a release.
nuance: The subject, grace, is supplied from the chapter; the verse names only what 'stands before' and 'stands behind'. முடிகின்ற காலம் may be death, the dissolution of the world or the end of a soul's bonds, and நடுவுயிர் may be the life within all or the soul held between births.

reading: By Siva's grace some become gods, by Siva's grace some equal the deity, by Siva's grace deeds do not cling, and if Siva's grace is joined, that is Siva's world.
nuance: The grades (gods, equal to the deity, free of deeds, Siva's world) mount toward the last, which makes Sivaloka not a place reached after death but the state of being joined to grace.

reading: Drawing near the paired feet of the meritorious one, our father, the pure one, knowledge grew like a lamp; becoming one of earth or one of heaven happens only when one receives the Lord's grace.
nuance: விளக்கென ஞானம் விளைந்தது, knowledge grew like a lamp, ties the chapter's title to an image. The last two lines put even ordinary human and heavenly births under grace, not only release. The father (எந்தை) may be Siva or the guru.

reading: Mounting the chariot of the body, driven by the mind as charioteer, one mounts the chariot of maya and is bewildered; know these; mounting the chariot of love and receiving the stainless one's grace, one mounts the chariot of the assembly, and He becomes this one.
nuance: The image of the body as chariot and the mind as charioteer is old (it is in the Katha Upanishad). Tirumular stacks four chariots: body, maya, love (நேயம்) and ஆயம், which may be the assembly of the Lord's company or the tattvas brought under control. அவன் இவன் ஆமே, 'He becomes this one', is traditionally the soul's union with Siva.

reading: If one is born in that world with a body, it is in that world that one seeks those of rare tapas, in that world that one joins Hara's feet, and in that world that one receives grace.
nuance: அவ்வுலகம், that world, is not named; it may be this earth, stressing that grace is won in embodied life, or a higher world in which one is reborn. The repetition makes the embodied birth the condition for every step that follows.

reading: The sunstone that sees the sun takes the form of fire, the moonstone that sees the moon takes the form of clear water, the witness that holds the spark takes the form of flame, and the Lord who holds the fire takes on beautiful form.
nuance: The sunstone and moonstone each take on the nature of what they face, and tradition reads the soul as taking on Siva's form when it faces him by grace. சதிகொண்ட சாக்கி is obscure: சாக்கி may be sakshi, the witnessing soul, or a flint (as in சக்கிமுக்கி); the last line may also mean that Siva, who holds fire, shines in the soul so lit.

reading: Seeking him with all kinship, I search for our Nandi; having searched, I join him as Siva Peruman; having joined, so as to reach his sounding anklets, I do not let go until release.
nuance: நாடும் உறவும் கலந்து can be 'with seeking and kinship mixed' or 'mingling land and kin', i.e. while still living among one's people. The chain தேடுவன், தேடி; கூடுவன், கூடி links each step to the next, and the verse ends on a clinging that is itself the way to release.

title: அவ வேடம்
theme: The futile garb (அவ வேடம்): those who put on the ascetic's guise for food and show do not reach Siva's feet; the land suffers when the ignorant wear it, so the ruler should correct his people and strip the base of it; false austerity leads to hell, and garb saves only those who have come to know.
