structure_note: Two verses on the pretender and the harm he does the land (1655, 1656), two on the ruler's duty to set the land right and weed out the false (1657, 1658), and two weighing false against true austerity and garb (1659, 1660).
source_issues: 1656: line 3 reads பஞ்ச்மாம், a misprint for பஞ்சமாம்.

reading: Fools who put on guises and frighten people so as to eat their food in pomp: dance, sing, weep, wail and search as you will, you will not see Siva's feet.
nuance: வெருட்டிடும் (who frighten) suggests ascetics who overawe householders into feeding them. The dancing, singing and weeping of line 3 are the outward marks of devotion; the verse says that performed for show they find nothing.

reading: If men without knowledge wear the garb in the land, do base things and live by begging, the land's honour and good decay and famine comes; to make the base put off the garb is a joy.
nuance: The harm is public, not only the pretender's own: the land loses its standing and suffers famine. Who is to strip the garb is left unsaid; the next verses and 241 put it on the ruler.

reading: Joy and sorrow in a land come to it from the good and bad deeds of its people; so it is said that if the ruler looks into it every day and sets the people of his land right, the world will flourish.
nuance: இறை here is the king, not the Lord, though the word allows both. The verse makes the king answerable for his subjects' conduct, not only for his own; in this chapter that means dealing with false ascetics.

reading: Men of low birth put on the garb to rise, men of the right line put it on to become gods; those who became ruined, base men of a blameworthy line, the outcast ones, are to be weeded out.
nuance: Every line turns on a compound with குலம் (இழி, வழி, பழி, கழி), and their sense is unsure: வழிகுலம் may be 'those of the proper line' or 'those who follow the way', and சண்டர் may mean the fierce or the outcast. களையப்பட்டோர் (weeded out) echoes the ruler's duty of 1657; whether the verse ranks garb-wearers by birth or uses birth words for conduct can't be fixed from the Tamil.

reading: Those who practise false austerity go to hell, and if they do not become men of merit, false and true austerity alike are things to be undergone among experiences; austerities hold only through true knowledge.
nuance: Line 3, போகத்துள் போக்கியம், is obscure: it may mean that both kinds of austerity only yield experiences to be consumed, so neither frees without சத்திய ஞானம். The first line's claim is plain; the rest is my best reading.

reading: The false garb is worn for the sake of eating; those who wear the true garb receive alms; but though the false garb be worn just like the true, a garb becomes one that saves only for those who have understood and known.
nuance: மிகு பிச்சை கைக்கொள்வர் may mean the true wearers take alms as the highest thing, or simply that they live by alms rather than by feasting. The last two lines can be read as saying even an outwardly false garb saves the knower, or that no garb saves anyone but the knower; either way knowledge, not the garb, decides.

title: தவவேடம்
theme: The garb of austerity (தவ வேடம்): only those great in austerity can rightly bear the ascetic's garb, which the rest wear as hunters wear theirs; the chapter then lists the marks of the Siva-yogi, from holy ash and earrings to bowl, sandals and staff.
structure_note: One verse on who may bear the garb (1661), then three lists of the yogi's emblems (1662 to 1664), the last counting ten.
source_issues: 1663: line 3 reads நீறனி, probably for நீறணி; lines 2 to 4 are obscure and may be corrupt.
1661: line 3 கவர்வேடத் தாகாரவ் வேடந் is run together in the source; read as அவமிக்கவர் வேடத்தர் ஆகார் அவ்வேடம்.

reading: Those great in austerity are the foremost wearers of the garb; those great in futility are hunters bent on killing; those great in futility cannot bear that garb, which none but those great in austerity can carry.
nuance: வேடர் means both 'wearers of garb' and 'hunters', and the verse turns on it: the false ascetic is a hunter in disguise. தவம் and அவம் (austerity and its empty counterfeit) are set against each other as in Kural 262.

reading: Wearing holy ash is the first of the emblems; earrings of copper and the rudraksha string are Rudra's emblems for those who recite too; these are the emblems of the flawless Siva-yogi, if you examine.
nuance: சாதனம் here means an emblem or outward means, not a practice. கண்டிகை is traditionally the rudraksha string. ஓதியவர்க்கும் may mean those who recite the scriptures, or those who have been instructed.

reading: For the yogi there are the inner loincloth and the cloak, a single matted lock wound with cord, ash on the body, the skull-bowl, and the cane staff.
nuance: The list is compressed and several words are unclear: உட்கட்டு, கஞ்சுளி, தோகைக்குப் பாசத்து, சீகந்தம், மாத்திரை. I take கஞ்சுளி as a cloak and பிரம்பு as a cane staff; the line divisions of the list are guesses.

reading: Earrings, rudraksha beads, the horn, the good conch to blow, the high bowl, flawless sandals, the seat at the end of yoga, the flawless yoga band and the staff: these are the ten.
nuance: நாதம் is taken as a horn or other sounding instrument, and கட்டி may be a separate item or part of the begging bowl (கப்பரை); the count of ten depends on which. யோகபட்டம் is the band that holds the knees in a seated posture.

title: திருநீறு
theme: Holy ash (திருநீறு): wearing the ash Siva himself wears, as armour, drives off deeds and brings the Siva state; ash from the sacred fire changes the form and lineage of the pure who wear it. The chapter opens with a verse on the true sacred thread and tuft.
structure_note: The first verse (1665) is about thread and tuft, not ash, and nearly repeats 230; only 1666 and 1667 are on the ash.
source_issues: 1666: line 1 reads பூசுng, a garbled பூசுங்.
1665: a verse on thread and tuft, nearly repeating 230, stands at the head of the chapter on holy ash.

reading: Fools, you do not understand thread and tuft: the thread is Vedanta and the fine tuft is knowledge; Brahmins who keep to the one part will see the supreme soul, whether it is one or two, if they recite Om.
nuance: The first two lines restate 230 plainly. பாலொன்றும் and ஓரொன்று இரண்டெனில் are obscure: perhaps 'whether the soul and the Supreme are one or two', a question Om is said to settle. Why the verse stands under holy ash is unclear.

reading: If they wear with gladness, never letting it fade, the holy ash that is armour, which Kankala wears, deeds will not stay, the Siva state will come, and they will reach the beautiful holy feet.
nuance: கங்காளன் is Siva bearing the skeleton, and கவசம் (armour) makes the ash a protection. மங்காமல் can mean wearing it without letting it fade, or without fail.

reading: The ash from peepal, banyan and fig wood, its form changed in the spreading fire, makes the form of the pure, who have gained the feet of the partless and stainless one, into a high lineage like Brahma's.
nuance: அரசுடன் ஆலத்தி is taken as peepal (அரசு), banyan (ஆல்) and fig (அத்தி), the woods of the sacrificial fire, and அக்காரம் as the ash; both readings are tradition's guess. The last line may mean the wearer gains Brahmin status, or that his form becomes like Brahma's.

title: ஞான வேடம்
theme: The garb of knowledge (ஞான வேடம்): knowledge, not garb, decides; the ignorant in garb go to hell and the knower without it is released. For the Siva-gnani any garb serves, his own garb is Siva-yoga, and he lives as one dead while body and senses remain, silent, released and in Nandi's state.
structure_note: Garb weighed against knowledge (1668 to 1670), the gnani set against ritualists and showy knowers (1671, 1672), and the gnani's own state (1673 to 1675).
source_issues: 1675: line 4 மேனமும் is not a known word; probably மோனமும் (silence).

reading: Those without knowledge belong to hell even if they wear the garb; those with knowledge are the good released even without it; those who want knowledge go to the Naked One and stand in the garb that has knowledge.
nuance: நக்கன் (the naked one) is Siva, the ascetic beyond all garb, which sharpens the point. The verse does not reject garb: for seekers it is the garb joined to knowledge.

reading: There is no use in those of petty knowledge wearing the garb; those of good knowledge, without wearing it, attain grace; those of evil knowledge, with the stain of sect, and those of lesser knowledge, have nothing to say.
nuance: The four grades (புன், நன், துன், பின் ஞானம்) are a play on one word. பின்ஞானத்தோர் may be those whose knowledge comes later or is secondary, and the last line may mean they cannot speak of the truth at all.

reading: For Siva-gnanis and Siva-yogis the emblems are not futile, if you examine; for the others they are futile; through the four means the peerless reality can come to dwell within.
nuance: அவமாம் அவர்க்கு may refer back to the gnanis (for whom emblems are empty, being unneeded) or to others; the plain and the opposite readings both stand. சாதனம் நான்கும் may be four emblems or the four paths (சரியை, கிரியை, யோகம், ஞானம்), as Siddhanta tradition counts them.

reading: The ritual purifiers wander like a dog at the foot of the stake, the monkey-glad knowers wander pecking about, but the Siva-gnanis wander as men dead while their senses and body remain intact.
nuance: கழுவடி நாய் is read as a dog hanging about the impaling stake for scraps, though கழு may mean washing; குரக்களி ஞானிகள் as knowers with a monkey's restless glee. 'Dead while living' (செத்துத் திரிவர்) is the classic image of the released one whose attachments are gone.

reading: Devotees are devotees; those who are not cannot become devotees nor become that garb; devotees are those who have gained Siva-knowledge, and those who have not are not devotees.
nuance: The verse defines அடியார் by Siva-knowledge, not by garb or by profession of devotion; the repetition of அடியார் in every line drives it home.

reading: For the gnani even a handsome garb is fitting; the garb he has taken is itself Siva-yoga; that garb becomes a means to the knowledge of grace, and for one who is not so, nothing of it avails.
nuance: சுந்தர வேடம் (a beautiful garb) may mean that even rich, unascetic dress does not harm the gnani. The last line can also be read 'for him, whatever comes is fitting and nothing binds'.

reading: The Siva-gnani who reaches the state through knowledge holds a lone temple set in its place; being one of silence he is released and a siddha, and he may be called the other kind of ascetic.
nuance: தானத்தில் வைத்த தனி ஆலயத்தன் may mean his own body or heart is the temple in which the Lord is set, as in 1823. ஏனைத் தவசி could mark him as an ascetic of a different kind from the garb-wearers, or the verse may say only that he too can be called an ascetic.

reading: The state of not being oneself, the becoming Him, the nature that is Siva, the wearing of the seal of attainment and silence: these belong to the one who has gained release at Nandi's feet.
nuance: தான் அன்ற தன்மை and தான் அவன் ஆதல (losing the self and becoming Him) are Siddhanta terms for the soul's union. மேனமும் is unknown; I read it as மோனமும் (silence), which fits 1674.

title: சிவ வேடம்
theme: The garb of Siva (சிவ வேடம்): the true Siva garb is not worn on the body, which sheds it at death, but is the state of those who by grace become Siva's servants, are free of darkness, delusion and action, and seek the Lord within; so rein in the running horse and seek Nandi rather than garb.
structure_note: Two verses define the Siva garb as an inner state (1676, 1678), with one between on the bodily garb that dies with the body (1677), and a closing call to drop garb and seek Nandi (1679).

reading: Those who by grace become servants of Hara, seek the golden Lord in their own body as the true thing, are without darkness and have ceased from their great doings: these are of the Siva garb of clear servanthood.
nuance: பொருளாம் தனது உடல் பொற்பதி நாடி can be read as seeking the golden Lord within one's body, or as regarding one's body as His property. இருஞ்செயல் அற்றோர் (free of great action) may mean free of deeds that bind.

reading: A garb begun on the body is not for the soul; when the body falls away the garb falls with it; those who have not grasped what body and soul truly are are like a log cast adrift on the sea.
nuance: The argument is plain: garb belongs to the body and dies with it, so it cannot serve the soul. The log adrift is a common image of the soul tossed in the sea of births.

reading: Free of delusion and darkness, the great mind gone, having learned to escape the hands of carp-eyed women, being simply themselves with those free of desire, they rest without action: these are of the Siva garb.
nuance: கையிணைக் கற்று is obscure: perhaps having learned (to be free of) the embrace of women. தயலற்றவர் may be those without women (from தையல்) or those without longing. தாமே தாமாகி (being themselves alone) suggests the soul standing in its own nature.

reading: Hold the reins of the running horse firmly; people, what will you do by putting on a garb? You don't need it; seek Nandi, our great Lord, search for him, and you can go and reach the thing that is bliss.
nuance: The running horse is traditionally the mind or the senses, and some read it of the breath; the verse does not say. The closing contrast is between taking on garb and reining oneself in.

title: அபக்குவன்
theme: The unripe (அபக்குவன்): the unready choose blind teachers and fall with them, look outward, do not wake to the light or answer the Lord's call, say one thing and do another; the king should drive out the great sinners; and the unworthy disciple, who neither removes his impurities nor fears birth, is not to be given the teaching.
structure_note: The unripe seeker (1680 to 1683), the king's duty against sinners (1684), austerity, the Lord's nature and waking (1685 to 1687), and the unworthy disciple (1688, 1689).

reading: They will not take the guru who removes blindness but take one who does not; blind and blind, playing a blind game, both fall into the pit.
nuance: குருடு (blindness) is ignorance, and the repetition of குரு and குருடு makes the line a pun. The blind leading the blind into a pit is a widespread image, known also from the Upanishads and the Gospels.

reading: A magic mirror has arisen in the mind, yet they do not see even its reflection in their thought; they will not polish it so the fruit of deeds departs, but go off desiring what lies outside.
nuance: The mirror in the mind is read as the inner faculty in which the Lord or the self could be seen if it were cleaned; விளக்கியும் (polishing) supports this. புறக்கடை (the outer gate or back door) is taken as the outward world of the senses.

reading: When called they do not answer 'what is it?'; those among kin do not know the mother's breast that flows sweet when the mouth is put to it; the formless one is the one who keeps the body.
nuance: பிரசைகள் may be people, subjects or children; the verse seems to say the unripe do not answer the Lord's call nor know him as a mother's breast that gives without asking. உருவிலி (the formless one) is the Lord; ஊன்நிலை செய்யும் may mean he sustains the body. The line connections are my guess.

reading: Saying one thing with the mouth and thinking another in the mind, don't do yet a third, great one; I will know you here as you are, and once I have known you, others will not take me for a madman.
nuance: The first two lines are a plain demand that word, thought and deed agree. The last two are obscure: பேய் may mean a madman or a ghost, and who speaks to whom is unclear; it may be the teacher sizing up a would-be disciple.

reading: If the king of the faithful does not inflict hard punishment on these sinners of the five betrayals so that they fear, and drive them off this earth, the whole earth will fall into famine and lie waste.
nuance: பஞ்சத் துரோகம் is traditionally taken as the five great sins (killing, theft, liquor, adultery, and wronging the guru, in one list). அஞ்சச் சமயத்தோர் வேந்தன் may be 'the king, so that those of the sects fear' or 'the king of the faith'. பஞ்சம் (famine) puns with பஞ்ச (five).

reading: The karma that those who stand in austerity undergo rests in Siva, and even the gods do not know it; for all who stand in austerity without knowing this, it is suffering that stays in births.
nuance: The sense may be that the ascetic who knows offers his deeds to Siva and is freed, while austerity without that knowledge only adds to births. பவத்திடை நின்றதோர் பாடு (suffering that stands in birth) is my reading.

reading: Burning with anger, scheming, doing deeds, eating, relishing, doing harm, falling back, putting oneself forward and boasting of greatness: these are not the nature of one near the Lord.
nuance: இறைபால் இயற்கை அல்லவே can mean 'not the nature of the Lord' or 'not the nature of those who are with the Lord'. Placed in this chapter, the list reads as the marks of the unripe; the first reading would make it a statement about the Lord's own freedom from these.

reading: They do not know the dawning and cannot see the open space; even when it dawns they will not open their eyes in it; bind fast the strong inner eyelid and see: that is the lamp that guards against the night not ending.
nuance: விடிவு (dawn) and வெளி (open space) are traditionally read as the dawning of knowledge and the inner space seen in yoga. உண்ணிமை (inner eyelid) is obscure; it may mean closing the outer eyes to see within.

reading: One who keeps to the path that changes the soul's set bonds, then, released from bondage, wavers, and does not think his way through the tattvas to reach the goal: to such a deluded disciple the teaching is not to be given.
nuance: பெத்த மற முத்தனாகிப் பிறழ்வுற்று is hard: it may describe one who seems freed but slips back. The verse ends without naming what is not to be given; the teaching or initiation is implied.

reading: He who does not know the way to remove the five abiding impurities, does not give up dipping into lust and the rest, a tangled liar who does not fear birth and death, is an outsider: he is the unworthy disciple.
nuance: மலம் ஐந்து, five impurities, extends the usual three (ஆணவம், கன்மம், மாயை); tradition adds மாயேயம் and திரோதாயி. அசற்சீடன் (the unreal or unworthy disciple) is set against சற்சீடன் of the next chapter.

title: பக்குவன்
theme: The ripe (பக்குவன்): the worthy disciple seeks a flawless guru, gives him goods, body and life, and stays at his feet like a shadow; sattvic, fearing birth, discerning the real from the unreal and melting in devotion, he receives the guru's foot and the knowledge it brings, and the teaching is to be given to such as he alone.
structure_note: The ripe seeker and his prayer (1690 to 1695), the marks of the true disciple, each verse ending in சற்சீடன் (1696, 1697, 1702, 1703), and between them the foot-initiation and how the teacher teaches (1698 to 1701).

reading: The wise who worship, with scripture as their eye, know the flawless supreme guru; those who know the way are those who know the good way, and the others know only ruin.
nuance: கருதி is taken as ச்ருதி, the revealed scripture, so scripture is the eye by which the true guru is recognised. அழிவறிவார் may mean they come to ruin.

reading: Seeking you, Supreme One, I have stopped my trembling and given that up; from now I will join no one else; shatter the deeds of me your servant so that my thinking ends; kick me, my master, and take me gladly into your grace.
nuance: The verse is a prayer, the only one in the chapter in the first person. உதைத்து (kicking) may recall Siva's foot that kicked Death, or the guru's foot placed on the disciple in initiation (1698); the plain sense is a plea to be taken by force.

reading: Even while one trembles, the seed called the Supreme can be given to devoted singers by one who, looking from above at the sowing of the seed, sets their scattering minds straight.
nuance: பரம் என்னும் வித்தை may be read as 'the knowledge (வித்தை, vidya) called the Supreme' or 'the seed called the Supreme', and the verse may play on both. Who gives is not named; the guru is implied.

reading: If you take one, take a good guru; give him the goods you have, your body and your life; stand without break even for a sesame seed's while and know clearly: that is Siva's state itself.
nuance: உள்ள பொருள் உடல் ஆவி (goods, body, life) is the classic threefold self-offering to the guru in Saiva tradition. The verse makes unbroken attention, not the gift alone, the way to Siva's state.

reading: Jyoti, Visakha, then the two stars of the Scorpion and the Crab: to all but those who keep uprightness within justice, thinking the named day is when one comes to know, he knows neither the Primal nor anything.
nuance: The first line names lunar asterisms (சோதி is Svati) and signs, perhaps days thought fit for initiation. The verse may be setting the upright mind above the auspicious day, or prescribing those days; the grammar of lines 2 to 4 is unclear.

reading: When the Lord, for its beauty, takes his place in a mind made pure like a great jewel polished by work, deeds strong as weeds depart and one sees his anklet-bearing holy feet, and grace comes.
nuance: தொழிலார மாமணி, a gem made bright by the jeweller's work, implies effort in purifying the mind. விழலார் விறலாம் வினை (deeds with the strength of weeds) is my reading of an unclear phrase.

reading: He who, being sattvic, thinks on the supreme tattva, comes forth on the path of the faithful, fears the binding round of births, and can keep to the way of dharma: he is the true disciple.
nuance: சாத்திகன் is one in whom the quality of sattva rules. ஆத்திக பேத நெறி (the path of the distinctions of belief) is unclear: perhaps the graded paths of the believer as against the unbeliever.

reading: He who considers how the real and the unreal stand, melts his mind, bows when Siva's grace points the way so as to gain knowledge through devotion, and whose desire is fit for the Shakti of bliss: he is the true disciple.
nuance: சத்து and அசத்து are taken in Siddhanta as the Lord (real) and the bonds (unreal), with the soul between. The verse joins discernment, devotion (பத்தி) and knowledge in one disciple.

reading: 'Place your foot on me and grant grace': thinking of this, the teacher places his foot; the deceptive birth of the great head on which the foot is placed ends, and through the gracious Shakti of that body he who has received the foot becomes a knower free of fault.
nuance: அடிவைத்து (placing the foot) opens every line. It is traditionally read as the guru's initiation by touch of the foot on the head (திருவடி தீக்கை). Lines 2 and 3 are compressed and my joins are guesses; ஆசு அற்றுளோன் is read as 'free of fault'.

reading: As the desire for glorious knowledge grows and grows and a love that never came before turns to the supreme guru, he in whom the four means not yet possessed have come becomes a seeker of knowledge, fit for the foot to be placed on him.
nuance: சாதகம் நான்கு may be the four qualifications of Vedanta (discrimination, dispassion, the six virtues, longing for release) or the four Siddhanta paths; the verse does not say. அடிவைக்கவே ties the verse to the foot-initiation of 1698.

reading: Teach only those of ripe mind; setting them within the bound of the Supreme beyond, and facing east, south, north and west, teach them while meditating on the Lady of the tongue.
nuance: நாவுடையாள் may be the goddess of speech or Shakti as the power of the word. The four directions may refer to the seating for initiation or to teaching in every quarter; பராபரத்து எல்லை is unclear.

reading: When the disciple bows at the Lord's feet with the fivefold salutation, tells his want and praises with good heart, the one who shows him how to be rid of the prison of the body and makes knowledge known to the knower, together with Siva, is the follower of the true way.
nuance: ஐ வணக்கம் may be the five-limbed prostration or simply 'the salutation'. சன்மார்க்கி (one on the true way) seems to name the teacher; the verse could also be read of the disciple. சிறையுடல் makes the body a prison.

reading: Since Vedanta is the path of giving up desire, the one who turns aside the stream of worldly life and bows his head to the feet of the great Vedantin who gives up desire in Siddhanta is the true disciple.
nuance: Tirumular joins the two: the teacher is a Vedantin whose renunciation is grounded in Siddhanta (சித்தாந்தத்து). வாழ்க்கைப் புனல் (the flood of worldly life) is to be diverted, not dammed.

reading: Good quality, truth, compassion, discernment and gentleness, never leaving the true guru's feet, like a shadow, and gaining clear sight so that the supreme knowledge of consciousness is clear and wonder appears: such is the true disciple.
nuance: The list of virtues (சற்குணம், வாய்மை, தயா, விவேகம், தண்மை) is ethical before it is spiritual. The shadow at the feet is the disciple's closeness; அற்புதம் (wonder) is the dawning of the supreme knowledge.

title: ஆறு ஆதாரம்
theme: The six adharas: the lotuses of four to sixteen petals rising from the root carry the fifty letters, and purifying them cleanses the nadis and the body; above them, through the sixteen kalas to the end of nada, the supreme Shakti stands and pure knowledge turns into the bliss of Siva.
structure_note: The petal counts from the root (1704); the ascent beyond the adharas to Shakti and the Lord (1705, 1706, 1707); purification and the body (1708); the fifty letters and the six ends in every body (1709, 1710); the sixteen-petalled flower where knowledge becomes bliss (1711). The petal counts of 1704 (4, 6, 10, 12, 16 and 2) add to fifty, the number of letters in 1709 and 1710, as the tradition matches them.
source_issues: 1704: கோவிமேல் (line 2) is obscure and may be corrupt.
1705: line 3 (போதா லயத்துஅ விகாரந்தனிற்போத) is hard to divide and may be corrupt.
1707 repeats 1492 with a different last line (சாதா ரணங்கெட்டான் தான்சக மார்க்கமே against 1492's சாதா ரணங்கெட லாஞ்ச மார்க்கமே) and காலந்தத்து for கலாந்தத்து in line 2; 1492's readings look sounder.
1711 repeats 2359 with small differences in lines 1, 3 and 4.

tamil: மூலம் கண்டு ஆங்கே முடிந்து முதல் இரண்டும்
reading: Four, six, ten and twelve, the sixteen marks standing above, and the first two: seeing them from the root upward and reaching their end, one may see the feet of the one who has seen time.
nuance: The numbers (நாலும் இருமூன்றும் ஈரைந்தும் ஈராறும் ... பதினாறும்) are traditionally the petals of the lotuses from the root (மூலம்) to the throat, with முதல் இரண்டும் as the two petals at the brow. கோவிமேல் is obscure. காலம் கண்டான் may be Siva who mastered time (or Death), or a form of காலகண்டன், the dark-throated one.

reading: Beyond the twelve of nada and at the end of the sixteen, from medha up to the end of nada, the supreme Shakti stands above, and in the changeless abode of knowing is the truth that lies above the adharas.
nuance: மேதாதி நாதாந்தம் and ஈரெட்டு are taken in mantra-yoga as the sixteen kalas of the ascent above the brow, from medha to the end of nada; ஈராறு may be the twelve-finger span above the head. போதாலயம் (abode of knowing) and the third line's division are unclear, and the line may be corrupt.

reading: When one sees without the two, above and below, and without the sixfold nature of 'he' and 'I', the Supreme of supremes, spread over all the earth, stands as a wishing tree, generous as a rain cloud.
nuance: மேல், கீழ் may be the upper and lower centres or high and low in general; தன்மைகள் ஓராறு (six natures) may be the six adharas or six marks of the ego, and தான், நான் set the self against the other. கார் ஒன்று கற்பகம் joins the wishing tree to the rain cloud, both images of giving without stint.

reading: Purifying the adharas cleanses the nadis, and with the light of the sky reached beyond the sixteen kalas from medha, the senses, the instruments and the intellect lose their ordinary working in the abode of knowing: this is the companion's path.
nuance: சகமார்க்கம் (the path of the companion) is the traditional name of yoga as the third of the four Saiva paths. சாதாரணம் கெட்டான் may mean the senses lose their common working, or that the yogi loses what is common to ordinary people. The verse recurs as 1492.

reading: Rousing Om without pause from medha onward, purifying the adharas and the paths, and practising until the dross in the bodily elements is driven out, the body itself becomes the fruit the adharas yield.
nuance: அத்துவா are traditionally the six paths of Saiva cosmology (of mantra, word, letter, world, tattva and kala). தாது ஆர மாசு may be impurity filling the bodily elements or a reference to semen. The last line, ஆதாரம் செய் போகம் ஆவது காயமே, can mean the body is the fruit of the practice, in the spirit of Tirumular's teaching on perfecting the body, or that the body is what the adharas serve.

reading: The six ends meet in every body, so mark the adharas that have been taught: above the fifty letters set in them, in the adhara where it wells up, stands the one letter.
nuance: ஆறந்தம் is traditionally a set of six 'ends' (vedanta, siddhanta, nadanta and others). The fifty letters of the alphabet are distributed in tradition over the petals of the adharas, and ஓரெழுத்து (the one letter) is usually taken as Om. ஆறிய (settled, or cooled) is unclear.

reading: However the body that forms, the body that perishes and the body that departs are joined together, the fifty letters, which are tattvas, are the six ends even for the body that is coming to be.
nuance: The three bodies may be the gross, subtle and causal bodies, or the body born, the body dying and the subtle body that goes on. The verse makes the letters the stuff of every body; how its two halves connect is not clear from the Tamil.

reading: On the lovely flower above the one that is sought are sixteen petals, and there pure knowledge becomes the bliss of Siva and ripens into abiding knowledge.
nuance: A sixteen-petalled lotus is traditionally the throat centre, though the sixteen may be the kalas above the brow named in 1705 and 1707. ஆயும் may mean examined, chosen or fine. The verse recurs as 2359, which ends with the Lord joining (புணர்ந்திருந்தானே) where this ends with knowledge ripening (விளைந்தது).

title: அண்டலிங்கம் (உலக சிவம்)
theme: The cosmic linga: the linga is the directions, the arts and the world itself, arising as Shakti and as Sadasiva, who gives enjoyment and release. The gods praise him without understanding; the temple, and many materials matched to each varna, can serve as the linga; and the Lord beyond all knowing makes the body his temple and the cosmos his place of worship.
structure_note: The linga as world, Shakti and Sadasiva (1712 to 1714, linked by repeated words); the gods' praise and the Supreme in all gods (1715, 1716); grace through the fixed form (1717); the temple, the materials and the varnas' lingas (1718 to 1721); the Lord in the body (1722, 1723); the cosmos as his body and as a linga being worshipped (1724, 1725).
source_issues: 1719: line 4 reads உய்த்த்தின், a misprint, perhaps for உய்த்ததின் or உய்த்தவர்; line 2 (கொத்தும்அக்கொம்பு சிலைநீறு கோமளம்) is obscure.
1720: line 4 (தென்தியங்கு ஒன்றை) is obscure and may be corrupt.
1724: சூழல் in line 1 is probably a misreading of கழல்.

reading: No one knows what the linga is: the linga is the eight directions, the linga is the sixty-four arts, and it is the world that has taken form as the linga.
nuance: எண்ணெண் கலை (eight eights) are traditionally the sixty-four arts, though கலை may also mean the kalas of cosmology. The last line can be read either way round: the world rose as the linga, or the linga took up the world.

reading: What arises in the world arises first as Shakti, in Shakti's form and with Shakti's qualities, and what so arises in the world is Sadasiva himself.
nuance: The verse picks up 1712's last word (உலகே) and repeats உலகில் எடுத்தது in every line. In Siddhanta, Sadasiva is the form of Siva where formed and formless meet, the one the linga signifies; the verse makes the world's arising Shakti's and Sadasiva's at once.

reading: Sadasiva remains giving enjoyment, release, understanding and powers, and the oneness beyond the body and the thirty-six tattvas; the six paths of the Agamas too are Siva.
nuance: ஆகமும் may be the body (ஆகம்) or the Agama, which changes what lies beyond the tattvas. ஆகம அத்துவா ஆறும் are the six paths (adhvas) of Agamic cosmology, here declared to be Siva himself.

reading: Countless gods praised our Lord and hailed him as the fragrant fresh south breeze and the bountiful one, yet for all their clamour they do not grasp that he stands beyond the worlds and guards them.
nuance: The south breeze (தென்றல்) is the gentle wind of Tamil poetry. The point is the gap between praise and understanding: the gods worship loudly (ஆர்த்தினர்) but miss what he is.

reading: The bright fire, Brahma, Vishnu, Prajapati, the shining sun and Indra, the gods who mingle everywhere as the light of the eye, are all, as a cool light everywhere, the Supreme.
nuance: ஒண்சுடரோன் may be Agni or Rudra. The play on சுடர் (flame) runs through every line, ending in தண்சுடர் (cool flame). The verse can mean the gods are the Supreme, or that the Supreme pervades them as their light.

reading: Siva can give grace from within the fixed form, yet none worship the truth of the great Supreme; and for those who do, it becomes the golden creeper standing within the flower.
nuance: தாபரம் (the fixed) is traditionally the installed linga, and மாபரம் the Supreme beyond form. பொற்கொடி (golden creeper) is a name for Shakti, and பூவகம் may be the heart lotus. One reading: grace comes through the installed form though few seek the formless, and those who do find Shakti within.

reading: To those who study Hara's state, the raised temple tower is the gross linga, Sadasiva is the fine subtle one, and the altar of offerings is the bhadra linga.
nuance: The verse reads the temple itself as linga in grades: the vimana (தூலம், gross), Sadasiva (சூக்குமம், subtle), and the bali-pitha (பத்திர லிங்கம்), whose name is technical. Its point is that the whole temple is Siva's form.

reading: Pearl, ruby and coral, sacred ash and other substances, cooked and raw rice, flowers and sand: for one who seeks to be saved, any of these can be made the linga, the Father's body.
nuance: The verse lists materials for lingas, many of them temporary ones made for a single worship in Agamic practice. கொத்தும்அக்கொம்பு and கோமளம் are obscure; அத்தன்தன் ஆகமம் may be the Father's body or his Agama. The list says the material matters less than the worship.

reading: Thick curd, ghee, milk, pure wax, refined copper, fire, mercury, water, strong brick, bilva and gold: any one of these, clearly known, can be the Sivalinga.
nuance: A second list of materials. தென்தியங்கு ஒன்றை is unclear; I take ஒன்றை as 'any one'. இரதம் is usually taken as mercury, used for lingas in later Saiva practice.

reading: For Brahmins' worship the linga is of crystal, for kings' worship of gold, for prosperous Vaishyas of komalam, and for Shudras the ancient bana linga.
nuance: The verse assigns materials by varna; it doesn't say one worship is worth more than another. கோமளம் recurs from 1719 and is unclear (perhaps a gem). The bana linga is traditionally a naturally formed stone from a river.

reading: The Lord stood where nothing could know him, even for one who knew and sought his single nature; and he who is the eight worlds of new awareness has, as I have come to know, made my body his temple.
nuance: The demonstratives அது, எது, இது in the first and last lines carry the argument and are hard to fix. புவனங்கள் எட்டும் may be the eight worlds or the eightfold form of Siva. Sengalvaraya compares the last line with Tiruvachakam's Pidiththa Paththu 10, where the Lord enters the body as a golden temple.

reading: Inside the flesh, a place made to fall away, he who is the wide world settles unknown; before the light came, the destroyer of sin, the holy one, stood there as refuge.
nuance: The verse rhymes அகலிடம் (wide place), உகலிடம் (place of falling away), பகலிடம் (place of day) and புகலிடம் (refuge). பகலிடம் ஆம் முனம் may mean before the light of knowledge dawns, or before the day ends.

reading: The earth is his flower-decked feet, the sky his crown that bears the woman, and the Lord's body stands as space: that is how he stands as the origin.
nuance: சூழல் in line 1 is read as கழல் (anklet, feet), which fits the head-to-foot pairing with முடி (crown). The woman on the crown is traditionally Ganga. நீதியுள் may mean 'in right order' or 'the Lord of justice'.

reading: The earth is Shakti as the base and the sky the linga; the wave-beaten sea is its bathing hall, the cloud water on the hills and the stars of the sky its garland, and the directions are the garment of boundless Nandi.
nuance: The cosmos is pictured as a linga in worship: Shakti as the pedestal, the sea for its bath, stars for its garland. கலை is read as garment, the directions clothing Siva, as his name திகம்பரன் says; it can also mean digit or kala.

title: பிண்டலிங்கம் (உடற் சிவம்)
theme: The body linga: the form of the human body is the Sivalinga, Chidambaram, Sadasiva and the holy dance. The Lord enters the body as his temple, the five keep its gates, and the worship he takes there is made by setting the senses behind.
source_issues: 1727: lines 1 and 2 (உலந்திலர் பின்னும் உளரென நிற்பர் / நிலந்திரு நீர்தெளி யூனவை செய்ய) are obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: The form of the human body is the Sivalinga, the form of the human body is Chidambaram, the form of the human body is Sadasiva, and the form of the human body is the holy dance.
nuance: The refrain மானுடர் ஆக்கை வடிவு claims the body's very shape (வடிவு), not only what dwells in it. Chidambaram is the hall where Siva dances, and the verse puts the hall, the dancer, the dance and the linga all in the human frame.

reading: Those who have not wasted away stand as though they live on; so, as earth, water and the rest that make the flesh become one with the five elements and the senses, worship the Lord who gives strength.
nuance: The first two lines are obscure. உலந்திலர் may be those who have not died, perhaps the perfected who keep their bodies, and நிலந்திரு நீர்தெளி ஊன் may list the elements that make the flesh. வலந்தரு may mean 'who gives strength' or 'circumambulated'. The plain thrust is that the body made of the five elements is where worship is done.

reading: When he took the body as his temple the five took up dwelling there, and keeping its gates they guide and give grace; the Master entered me as if taken into a mother, took the gate, and came to rule me.
nuance: The five (ஐவர்) may be the five deities who govern the body in Siddhanta or the five senses turned to the Lord's service. தாயில் கொண்டாற்போல் is unclear: as a child is held in its mother, or as a mother takes in her child. வாயில் (gate) recurs in 1729.

reading: Our great Nandi took the body as his temple, with the great Veda as the ground of his feet and the ten nadis as its gates, and took its worship once the five senses were put behind.
nuance: கொல்லைப் பெருமறை (the great Veda of the field) is obscure. The ten nadis are traditionally the body's main channels of breath. புலன் ஐந்தும் பிறகிட்டு (the five senses set behind) makes the worship itself an act of restraint.

title: சதாசிவ லிங்கம் (உலக முதற் சிவம்)
theme: The Sadasiva linga: Sadasiva, five-faced, fifteen-eyed and ten-armed, is the form shared by the gods, bindu, nada and Shakti; through Shakti the directions, Vedas, religions and tattvas unfold. His faces and limb-mantras are set on the body, the poet takes him into his heart, and the chapter ends with one's own body as the linga and the linga as the syllable Om.
structure_note: Sadasiva's form and what he holds in common (1730, 1731); the unfolding through Shakti, in a chain where each verse takes up the last one's closing word (1732 to 1734); the five faces, their colours and the Lord in the heart (1735, 1736); Shakti and Siva as all the tattvas (1737, 1738); devotion (1739, 1740); the faces and limb-mantras set on the body and the shapes of Shakti (1741 to 1745); the Lord in the body and heart (1746 to 1750); Om and the linga (1751, 1752).
source_issues: 1749: line 1 carries a stray Latin Y (ஆங்கவை Yமூன்றினும்), flagged as corrupt in the source.
1746: line 2 reads அஞ்கின், probably for அஞ்சின், and தனிச்சுடை ராய், probably for தனிச்சுடராய்.
1741: காற்றிடில் (line 1) may be for கூற்றிடில், and lines 3 and 4 (அத்தரு கோரம் மருடத்துஈ சானனே) are hard to divide and may be corrupt.
1747: தென்தலைக்கு (line 3) is obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: Sadasiva, a pearl of good light, stands with his two feet together on the pedestal, with arms spreading two and eight, five faces to be sought, and three fives more.
nuance: A meditation image. The two and eight arms make ten, as 1736 says; செங்கையின் மூவைந்து (three fives with the red hands) is unclear, but 1736 gives fifteen eyes, so the fifteen are probably his eyes.

reading: Brahma, tall Vishnu, Rudra, Maheshvara above them and the five-faced one above him, bindu and nada, and the supporting Shakti with Siva: Sadasiva is what is common to them all.
nuance: The list follows the traditional ascending order of the deities who govern the levels of the cosmos. சாதாரணம் (common) may mean Sadasiva is shared by all of them, or is the general form that includes them.

reading: Within the Shakti that comes to be, the kalas take their place and the rays rise; once he is seated within her, the ten directions are within that Shakti.
nuance: ஆகின்ற சத்தி opens every line. கலை may be the kalas of cosmology, and கதிர் the rays of sun and moon. Who is seated (அமர்ந்த) is not said; Sadasiva is the natural subject.

reading: Within those directions are settled the six limbs of the Veda, the four Vedas, the path of chariyai, and the religious systems.
nuance: The verse takes up 1732's last words (அத்திசை) and hands its own last word (சமயம்) to 1734. Placing the Vedas, chariyai and the religions within Shakti's directions makes them all products of her unfolding.

reading: From that religious order arise the ten states, the twelve signs of the zodiac and the forty-eight bodies, and from it arises Sadasiva himself.
nuance: சமயம் may here mean religious system, as in 1733, or appointed time and order. அவத்தை ஈரைந்து (ten states of the soul) and சரீரம் ஆறெட்டு (six eights of bodies) are technical and I can't fix them.

reading: The five faces he gave me, his servant, face the zenith, east, south, north and west, and are coloured crystal, saffron, dark collyrium, red and milk-white.
nuance: The faces are traditionally Isana, Tatpurusha, Aghora, Vamadeva and Sadyojata, matched in order with the colours. அடியேற்கு அருளிய (granted to me, the servant) turns an iconographic list into a vision given in grace.

reading: He has five faces, fifteen eyes, ten hands and ten weapons, and this Lord has entered my heart and stands filling it.
nuance: The play on அஞ்சு (five) fills three lines and gives way in the fourth to நெஞ்சு (heart), so the counted form ends inside the devotee.

reading: Shakti and Sadasiva are the earth and the cosmos; Shakti and Siva fill all that is fixed and all that moves; Shakti and Sadasiva are form and the formless; Shakti and Siva are the thirty-six tattvas.
nuance: Each line opens with சத்தி and pairs her with Siva or Sadasiva, so the verse never names one without the other.

reading: The tattvas are the formless and all that moves and does not move, they are form and the rising of joy; all tattvas stand as everything, and Sadasiva is the tattva itself.
nuance: தத்துவம் opens every line, taking up 1737's last word. சுகோதயம் (the rising of joy) is unclear here; it may name a state or the pleasures the tattvas give.

reading: Declare that Sadasiva, welling up within, is our Lord: describe him in other words and he stands beyond them; apart from the gods whose work is lofty speech, he has entered my mind.
nuance: மிகைப்பொருள் (surplus meaning) suggests he exceeds any other description. Line 3 (ஏறுரை செய்தொழில் வானவர்) is unclear: it may be the gods who make proud claims, or ஏறு may be Siva's bull. மாறுசெய்வான் may mean he opposes or he differs from them.

reading: Clear in understanding, I have held steady within me the first Lord whose mind is full of grace, with his dark throat, raised axe and bright crescent in his curling red hair.
nuance: The dark throat (from the poison he drank), the axe and the crescent are Siva's usual marks. The verse moves from seeing the form to holding it within (தெளிந்திருந்தேனே), which is meditation.

reading: Telling the five faces in which Shakti stands, the verse places Vamadeva as the highest, Tatpurusha in the east as the head, and Aghora and Isana after them.
nuance: The verse is hard to divide. காற்றிடில் may be for கூற்றிடில் (if one tells); உரையத்து, தத்துவம் பூருவம் and அத்தரு கோரம் மருடத்து do not divide clearly. The five faces are also the five Brahma mantras of Agamic worship.

reading: Isana is the crown of the head, Tatpurusha the face, Aghora the heart, Vamadeva the secret parts, and Shakti the feet.
nuance: This is the placing (nyasa) of the five faces on the worshipper's body. The feet traditionally belong to Sadyojata, so சத்தி here may name that face or the power in it. தாணுவின் தன்முகம் (Sthanu's own face) is read as the face.

reading: Heart, head, tuft, long armour and eye are the limbs; the flawless bindu is green, the crest flashes like lightning, and the ten weapons are like a red flame.
nuance: நெஞ்சு, சிரம், சிகை, கவசம், கண் are the limb-mantras (anga mantras) of Agamic worship, with the weapon (astra) completing them. The colours belong to the tradition of meditation on them; சேகரி may mean the crest or a name of Shakti.

reading: The heart is the Lord's power of knowledge, the head the supreme Shakti, the tuft and the armour his power of will, and his power of action is in the supreme eye.
nuance: The limbs of 1743 are matched with the Lord's powers of knowledge, will and action (ஞான, இச்சை, கிரியை). How சிகையாதி and வண்ணம் divide between tuft and armour is unclear.

reading: Shakti stands moving in the square, rests in the hexagon, and stays moving in the circle; Sadasiva is Shakti's form.
nuance: சலம் may be water or movement. The square, hexagon and circle may be the shapes of a linga's pedestal or the diagrams of worship. சயனம் (lying, bed) is unclear here.

reading: However long one calls on Nandi who bears the deer, he stands in the five as a single flame; rising past the navel to the lotus, Nandi stands above, in the nine.
nuance: நந்தி ends a word in every line. மான் நந்தி may be Siva holding the deer or 'great Nandi'. The five, the navel, the lotus and the nine are yogic places in the body, but which ones is not fixed; கால் நந்தி may be the breath.

reading: Our Lord stays joined with the body and always moves within it; when it rose to the head and was set right, I stood and worshipped Siva's feet within my heart.
nuance: What rises to the head (தென்தலைக்கு ஏற) is unstated; tradition takes it as the breath or kundalini. தென்தலை may be 'the fair head' or a corruption. The worship is inner: the feet are found in the heart.

reading: I came to know the bright reality in the world, brought him in and made my heart his temple on earth; I have joined the Pure One, and this is truth, not falsehood; I bowed, and the sun's song is the sound.
nuance: The verbs run in sequence: knew, brought, joined, bowed. குவலயம் கோயில் என் நெஞ்சம் can mean my heart is a temple on earth, or the earth and my heart are both his temple. The last phrase, பகலவன் பாட்டும் ஒலியே, is obscure.

reading: When fierce fire blazes through those three, the fourteen bear it, and in their midst rise the beginning and the end; these here become one's body and the moon.
nuance: The three may be the sun, moon and fire, or three nadis, and ஈரேழு (fourteen) may be the worlds or the body's regions. இந்து (moon) is traditionally the cooling nectar at the head. I can't fix the sense with any confidence.

reading: One's own body stands as one's Sivalinga, one's body stands as Sadasiva, one's body is one's own Siva and Siva-bliss, and one's body becomes the Supreme itself.
nuance: தன்மேனி (one's own body) opens every line, and தற்- (one's own) is prefixed to linga, Siva and bliss. The verse draws the chapter from Sadasiva's form to the worshipper's own body.

reading: No one knows that he is the letter A and that she, the Lady spread through the world, is U; the two together become the whole earth and rise, transformed, as sound.
nuance: தாரம் may mean consort, so the two are Siva and Shakti, or the sacred syllable (tara, Om), of which A and U are parts. Sengalvaraya compares the first line with Kural 1.

reading: In the linga, Om is the good pedestal, M fills its neck, U fills its inner circle, and A is the linga itself, filled with bindu and nada.
nuance: The syllable Om is mapped onto the parts of the linga: pedestal, neck (கண்டம்), inner circle and shaft, with bindu and nada, the dot and resonance of Om, in the shaft. இலிங்கம் opens every line.

title: ஆத்மலிங்கம் (உயிர்ச்சிவம் )
theme: The lingam of the self (ஆத்மலிங்கம்): the letters A and U, bindu as pedestal and nada as shaft, and Shakti joined with Siva make up the lingam, fixed and moving, which is Sadasiva; and the Lord who wears the moon, whom the gods seek in the eight directions, makes the devotee's mind his temple.
structure_note: Six verses (1753 to 1758) on what the lingam is made of: letters, bindu and nada, Shakti and Siva, and the tattvas mapped onto its parts. Four verses (1759 to 1762) turn to the Lord dwelling in the mind as in a temple.
source_issues: 1756: பூரேர் in line 3 is obscure and may be corrupt.
1757: கருஐந்தம் in line 4 is unclear.
1761: குரால் in line 2 is obscure.

reading: With A first he stands as everything, with U first he stands having entered the lives; if one knows both A and U, A and U are themselves the lingam.
nuance: அகாரம் and உகாரம் are the first two parts of the syllable Om, traditionally matched with Siva and Shakti, or with the Lord as all things and the Lord within souls. The verse names no subject; the reading supplies 'he'. Its first line closely echoes the Kural's first verse.

reading: Bindu, which is both the support and what it supports, and nada with medha and the rest spread out above; the supporting bindu is the first pedestal, and their union is the lingam.
nuance: ஆதாரம் and ஆதேயம் (support and supported) are technical terms; மேதாதி is taken as medha and the other kalas of the syllable above nada. போதா இலிங்கப் புணர்ச்சி is obscure; the plain sense is that the pedestal and the shaft together make the lingam.

reading: The lingam that is Shakti and Siva is the fixed one, the lingam that is Shakti and Siva is the moving one, the lingam that is Shakti and Siva is Sadasiva, and Shakti becoming Siva is itself the fixed lingam.
nuance: தாபரம் (the installed, immovable lingam) and சங்கமம் (the moving one, traditionally the devotee or the guru as a living lingam) are paired. The repetition makes one point: whatever its form, the lingam is Shakti joined with Siva.

reading: One can see the light that rises straight up of itself, the place where the fifty rising toward the sky dwell; together with the golden creeper rising in the body, what rises straight up of itself is the letter A.
nuance: ஐம்பது (fifty) is taken as the fifty letters, and பொற்கொடி (the golden creeper) as Shakti or kundalini. பூரேர் is obscure, perhaps a form of பூர் or a misreading; I take it as the body. The verse ends where 1753 began, with A as the lingam.

reading: The lingam is where bindu and nada meet: bindu is the pedestal and nada the lingam; these two, as the supporting deities, come and perform the five acts of creation, and those are five.
nuance: கருஐந்தம் is unclear; read as the five acts beginning with creation (கரு, the embryo or making). Tradition matches bindu with Shakti and nada with Siva, as the pedestal and the shaft.

reading: Shakti as the good pedestal is the soul; Shakti as the good middle part is vidya; Shakti as the good lingam is the Siva tattva; and Shakti with the good soul is Sadasiva.
nuance: The three parts of the installed lingam (base, middle and shaft) are matched with the three classes of tattvas, atma, vidya and Siva; கண்டம் is taken as the middle section. The last line, joining Shakti and soul as Sadasiva, is less clear.

reading: When he entered my mind, my life became settled, and when he entered my mind and poured down bliss, goodness entered and sought the Lord with me, and the First One entered among his own and took me over.
nuance: The subject is unstated until ஆதி (the First) in the last line. இனம்புகுந்து may mean entering the company of devotees or joining his own kind. The repeated புகுந்து (entered) carries the verse.

reading: The Supreme, my Father who wears the cool moon, the support of the world, whose temple is the minds of his devotees, the Lord who abides on the heads of the gods, the one who wears the snake, has settled and dwells in my mind.
nuance: Each line turns on a word ending in -பரன் (Lord): பராபரன், தராபரன், சிராபரன், அராபரன். The devotee's mind as the Lord's temple is the chapter's turn from the outer lingam to the inner one.

reading: If I say 'we are not the Lord's', the foolish world will call my mind a ruined thing; the Lord who has made my mind his temple, with the snake on his red matted hair where fire and water contend, is that holy one.
nuance: குரால் is obscure: it may mean something dull or faded, or a decaying thing, and the first two lines may be read differently. The image of fire and the Ganga contending on Siva's hair is a common one.

reading: The gods go about the eight directions and praise him, saying 'there he stood, there he lay'; I stand and praise my Lord at all times, and he is one with me and dwells within my heart.
nuance: நின்றான் கிடந்தான் (he stood, he lay) is often taken as the standing and reclining forms worshipped in temples, which the gods seek outwardly. The contrast is between seeking him abroad and finding him within; அன்று and என்று may also mean 'then' and 'always'.

title: ஞான லிங்கம் (உணர்வுச் சிவம் )
theme: The lingam of knowledge (ஞான லிங்கம்): the supreme Siva takes form, formlessness and form-with-formlessness, the nine forms with Sadasiva in the middle, and comes as guru to souls; with him stands Parashakti, and the whole world is the play of Shakti and Siva, which enters the mind and makes it Siva.
structure_note: The chapter moves from the Lord's forms (1763 to 1765) through worship and the Lord's oneness with Shakti (1766 to 1770) to the world and the soul as the play of Shakti and Siva (1771, 1772).
source_issues: 1766: lines 2 to 4 (காண்டகை, கன்னி, மூண்டகை) are obscure.
1769: the subject of கொழுந்து is not stated and the verse may be incomplete in sense.

reading: The supreme Siva, who takes form, formlessness and form joined with formlessness, stands for the many souls with the purpose of being their guru too, and Sadasiva gives like the wishing tree.
nuance: உருவும் அருவும் உருவோடு அருவும் (form, the formless, and form with the formless) is the Siddhanta division of the Lord's nine manifestations, set out in the next verse. தரு is taken as the wishing tree of the gods (karpaka).

reading: The four below are form, the four above are formless, and the one in the middle, standing among them, is form and formless; these are his parts, and they are the supreme Siva himself.
nuance: The verse gives only the numbers. Tradition names the four forms as Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra and Mahesvara, the four formless as bindu, nada, Shakti and Siva, and the middle as Sadasiva, who is worshipped as the lingam; 1776 lists the same nine.

reading: Those who bow to him as the lord of the gods, the lord of the four-faced one, the lord of the four, Nandi who stands in the middle, saying 'lord of whom?', find by that path that the Great One is the lord of all at whose feet they are.
nuance: நால்வர் (the four) is traditionally Sanaka and the three other sages taught by Siva as Dakshinamurti. ஏவர் பிரான் என்று is ambiguous: a question, or an exclamation ('lord of every one!').

reading: I stood longing and worshipped so that my deeds would leave me; whether the Virgin is known together with the visible one who measures out the year, the month and the day, or the kindled one changes, it is one.
nuance: The second half is obscure. The one who measures years, months and days is perhaps the sun, or the Lord as time; கன்னி (the Virgin) is taken as Shakti; மூண்டகை மாறினும் is unclear. The last words, that it is one, suggest the Lord and Shakti are one under every form.

reading: The first, supreme God, the good God of the cosmos, the great God whom the devotees of light follow, the great God within justice, the stainless one, our Lord: Parashakti abides in his half.
nuance: The list of epithets ends by placing Parashakti in the Lord's half (பாதியுள்), the image of Siva as half woman. சோதி அடியார் may be devotees who see the light, or the devotees of the one who is light.

reading: Above Shakti is Parashakti, and within her is the pure state of Siva, an untouched clear light, beyond the beyond of the Father's holy feet; this is the truth of the Lord being himself, and it is also what accords.
nuance: The grades Shakti, Parashakti and pure Siva state are technical. ஒத்தவும் ஆம் in the last line is unclear: perhaps that Siva and Shakti are equal, or that this matches the teaching.

reading: If one sees the tip, the world appears; if one sees the place where it rises, one can abide; if one sees where it spreads, it is above Parvati; the one who saw it gather and rise is in my thought.
nuance: கொழுந்து (tip, sprout or flame) has no stated subject. It may be the lingam's top, the flame of light in yoga, or kundalini rising; பார்ப்பதி மேலே may mean above Parvati or above what is seen. A symbolic reading is the only one that makes sense here.

reading: Speaking first of the union of my Father, the Supreme, and my Mother, and then telling it in order, is jnana; he set the great-eyed one above the navel at the place where they met, and dwelt there rejoicing.
nuance: பெருங் கண்ணி (the great-eyed woman, Shakti, or a great garland) and உந்தியின் மேல் (above the navel, a centre of the yogic body) are taken symbolically; tradition reads it as the Lord holding Shakti in a bodily centre.

reading: In the play of Shakti and Siva, becoming life and feeding it amid the joined two mayas, then separating out the pure turiya, it enters the mind and makes the self Siva.
nuance: இருமாயா is taken as pure and impure maya; துரியம் is the fourth state of consciousness. The subject that becomes life and enters the mind is unstated: the play, or Shakti and Siva.

reading: The earth is the play of Shakti and Siva; Shakti becomes Siva and Siva becomes Shakti; there is no fixed thing other than Shakti and Siva, and it is always Shakti who takes shape as form.
nuance: தாபரம் here can mean the fixed world or the installed lingam, as in 1755; both readings say the same: nothing stands apart from Shakti and Siva. The last line gives form to Shakti, leaving Siva formless.

title: சிவலிங்கம் ( சிவகுரு )
theme: The Siva lingam (சிவலிங்கம்): the Lord pervades sea, wind and fire too widely to be walked round, yet there is a way to circle him, by water, flowers and his name; the nine forms together are the lingam, and restraining the breath through the inner flame leads to the supreme state.
structure_note: A question and its answer (1773, 1774), a verse of worship (1775), the lingam as the nine forms (1776) and a yogic verse (1777). The alternative title சிவகுரு is not developed in the verses.
source_issues: 1777: lines 2 and 3 are hard to construe and may be corrupt.

reading: The roaring sea, the water of the earth, the spreading wind and the fire that dwells in things: he stretches long and wide in their ordered array, and I do not know how to bound him and walk round him.
nuance: வலம்செய்தல் is circumambulation, walking round a shrine in worship. The difficulty is that the Lord is the elements themselves, so there is no outside from which to circle him.

reading: There is one way here to bound him and walk round him: for those who bear the flowing Ganga water and flowers and can utter his name and know him, the one with twisted matted hair does not go off anywhere and hide.
nuance: The answer to 1773 is worship with water, flowers and the name, joined to knowing (உணரவல்லார்). புரைத்து எங்கும் போகான் may also mean that he does not slip away through any gap.

reading: We have seen the Lord as one alone; as I worship his pair of feet as the good, the First Lord gives grace then and there, so that the five senses are conquered and lie subdued and one rejoices.
nuance: அன்று என்று is unclear: 'on that day', or 'saying it is not so'. மிகக்கிடந்து may describe the senses lying overcome or the devotee lying prostrate.

reading: Brahma who blossomed, Vishnu, Rudra, Mahesa, the five-faced one who gives fruit, supreme bindu and nada, Shakti who gives good and Siva: taking these forms, the lingam that gives fruit is the supreme Nandi.
nuance: These are the nine forms of 1764, named. ஐம்முகன் (the five-faced) is Sadasiva. Calling the lingam பராநந்தி makes the guru's name, Nandi, the name of the whole.

reading: Going through the red flame that rises, while the breath rises only as far as the body allows, if one contemplates what is to be joined and what goes on leaving it, and restrains it, that is the supreme state.
nuance: செஞ்சுடர் (red flame) is taken as the inner fire or kundalini, and ஆவி as the breath. The second and third lines are hard to construe: they may contrast the breath that is held with the breath that goes out.

title: சம்பிரதாயம் ( பண்டை முறை )
theme: The ancient way of initiation (சம்பிரதாயம்): the guru takes the disciple's body, wealth and life with water, places hand and feet on him, cuts the clinging of deeds and births, and shows the Lord within; the disciple, exchanged for the guru himself, comes to know no difference between I and you, Siva and soul, as body and life are one.
structure_note: The rite and its effects (1778 to 1785), in which the giving of body, wealth and life recurs (1778, 1783, 1784); then the fruit of it, awareness and grace (1786, 1787), and the non-difference of the soul and the Lord (1788 to 1791).
source_issues: 1781: பிட்டடித்து in line 1 is obscure and may be corrupt.
1783: பாடல் in line 3 and குளிக்கொண்டே in line 4 are obscure.
1786: lines 3 and 4 are circular as written; a word may be corrupt.

reading: Taking body, wealth and life with water, looking so that the clinging of spreading deeds is cut, placing his hand, setting his feet in an instant and making the awareness subtle, Nandi showed the way that cuts off birth.
nuance: உதகத்தால் கொண்டு (taking with water) is the gesture of a gift sealed by pouring water; the disciple's body, wealth and life (tanu, artha, prana) are given over to the guru. The look, the hand and the feet are traditionally the initiations by sight, touch and the feet.

reading: Life and body as the bright possession, the wondrous Supreme, the breath that follows after, Siva who acts and Chit-Shakti: the supreme guru took me, unable to save myself, so that I might be saved for the First One.
nuance: The list in the first three lines is hard to construe; it may name what the guru took over or the levels through which he raised the disciple. உயலார் (those who cannot save themselves) is read as the disciple.

reading: The thing the teacher set in the western direction and told me to think on every day lies below the crown and above the uvula; this is the state he set, with the mouth not opened.
nuance: பச்சிம திக்கு (the western direction) is taken as the back of the head or the hidden rear path of the breath. The place between crown and palate and the closed mouth point to a yogic practice, but the verse does not spell it out.

reading: Me, who wandered babbling everywhere, he swept clean, drew out all the dirt that sat within, and exchanged himself and me as on a balance: the rate matched and the trade turned out well.
nuance: The image is a merchant's: தட்டொக்க (the scale pans level), வட்டம் (the rate or commission in an exchange), வாணிபம் (trade). The guru takes the disciple and gives himself. பிட்டடித்து is obscure; it may mean beating about, or be corrupt.

reading: People do not know at all how the Lord of all the many lives that are borne abides; cutting through the strife of the dividing bindu, I have found the Lord who holds everything as in a womb.
nuance: பிரிக்கின்ற விந்து (the bindu that divides) is taken as maya, which sets things apart; பிணக்கு is the conflict or tangle it makes. கருக்கொண்ட may mean holding all as a womb holds, or holding the seed of all.

reading: Taking note of the body, wealth and life that come together, seeking and setting his feet, with the power of grace and jnana he removed all clinging to the body of suffering, and became one with what he had joined, having plunged into it.
nuance: This repeats the rite of 1778. பாடல் உடல் is read as பாடு (suffering) with the body; குளிக்கொண்டே (having plunged, or having immersed) is obscure, perhaps the disciple immersed in the Lord.

reading: He took my servitude as his own, he took my throng of life, wealth and body, and since he who gave all fruit has taken them, there is nothing I can say he took.
nuance: கொண்டான் (he took) opens every line. The turn is that what he took was his own gift, so it cannot be counted as taken; the disciple's surrender gives nothing the guru did not already hold.

reading: Those who do not come to know the truth of how the body and the one in the body join, the breath that guides, the soul that stays firm, and what holds the body that is taken away, are like ghosts.
nuance: தேகம் and தேகி (body and the embodied one) are a pair; பறிக்கின்ற காயம் may be the body that is snatched away at death. The comparison with ghosts is that they have form without understanding.

reading: To those with awareness the world appears as it is; those with awareness have no suffering that befalls them; the time when those with awareness came to know, those with awareness knew it and saw.
nuance: உணர்வுடையார் (those who have awareness) opens every line. The last two lines are circular as written and their point is unclear; perhaps that the moment of knowing is known only by the knower.

reading: What can I say to Nandi, who gave pure grace to those who wandered in the expanse of the body, spread out and then contracted in turiya and in the sakala state, and roamed through the thirty-six?
nuance: ஆறாறு (six sixes) is the thirty-six tattvas; துரியம் and சகலம் are states of the soul (the fourth state, and the state of full embodiment). The movement described is the soul's wandering through the states and the tattvas before grace.

reading: Nearing him, there is no difference such as I and you, standing together as flesh and the life in the flesh; as the gods abide in heaven, humans revel in bliss as in honey.
nuance: The image of body and life (ஊன், ஊனுயிர்) for the union recurs in 1790 and 1791. The verse claims non-difference while keeping the image of two that live together.

reading: He and he do not know him; if one knows him, there is no knower left; if he and he know him, he and he become this one.
nuance: A riddle built on அவன் (he) and இவன் (this one). It is traditionally read as the soul and the bond (or the soul and its awareness) that do not know the Lord, and the knower lost in knowing him; the referents are not fixed by the verse.

reading: He who stood saying 'I am this' every day is there as the awareness within, as life in this flesh; he is there pouring like the great cloud of the sky; and I become the Lord of the space as well.
nuance: நான் இது தான் is unclear: the Lord identifying with the soul, or the soul with the Lord. அம்பர நாதன் may be the Lord of the sky or of the hall (அம்பலம்); the last line claims the speaker becomes him.

reading: The great Lord's nature and mine were never separate as 'he' and 'I', and the Lord knows it; Uma is truly joined as body and life, and the lord of the gods makes it right beforehand.
nuance: The last two lines are unclear: உமை மெய்யே may mean Uma is the body (மெய்) while Siva is life, or 'Uma, truly'. திருந்த முன் செய்கின்ற may be the Lord preparing the soul beforehand.

title: திருவருள் வைப்பு
theme: The placing of grace (திருவருள் வைப்பு): grace is what binds the soul and what frees it, the whole course of a life from birth to dissolution, and the five acts by which the Lord makes and pervades the worlds. The Lord cannot be reached by one's own knowing; he enters the heart of those he graces, and is unseen by those without grace.
structure_note: Verses 1792 to 1797 set the Lord beyond knowing; 1798 to 1804 sing grace as bond, release and indwelling, with the refrain அருள் and அகம்புகுந்தான்; 1805 to 1813 turn to cosmology: grace as the five acts, the nine forms (1807, 1810), and bindu ripening into maya and the worlds (1812, 1813).
source_issues: 1794 line 3: சிந்தையைக் சிக்கென should be சிந்தையைச் சிக்கென (sandhi misprint).
1801 line 3 (அருளானஆனந்தந்து) is a misprint for அருளான ஆனந்தத்து, as in 1800; line 4 அதும்புகுந் தானே is probably a misprint for அகம்புகுந் தானே.
1792 and 1806 line 4 are obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: The two states are night and day, form is soul and body, grace is virtue and austerity, and what stands within matching them is enjoyment.
nuance: The verse is a list of pairs and its key words are unclear: இருபதம் may be 'two states' or 'two feet', and பொருவது may mean 'what matches' or 'what contends'. Read as a whole it seems to set grace among the pairs that shape embodied life, but I can't fix the last line.

reading: Nandi is hard to see and beyond thought, and appears far off to those who would touch or approach him; but when the heart lies longing and gathered there, as the light of a lamp, the darkness ends.
nuance: விளக்கொளி யான்நெஞ்சம் can be split as 'my heart, a lamp's light' or read with விளக்கொளியான் as the Lord who is the lamp's light, coming into the heart. Either way the darkness ends inside, not by reaching out.

reading: Within the inner intent the world appears; if the darkness of aversion goes, the Lord stands there; if one searches the gathered mind steadily, one gains a knowing vision and becomes like the immortals.
nuance: குறிப்பு (sign, intent, focus) and விகிர்தன் (the one who is other, a name of Siva) carry the verse. குறிப்பு may be the meditator's point of focus or the Lord's own will; the world 'appearing' in it is open to both.

reading: Ages went by in not discerning; our Lord Pinnakan knows apart from us, and as the one who knows that knowledge is the companion of those who know fully, he draws near and knows, master of great nature.
nuance: The play on அறி (know) runs through every line. Who knows what is hard to fix in lines 2 to 4; the plain point is that our ages of not knowing are met by a Lord who knows and comes near.

reading: Once the deeds that run of themselves are destroyed, I no longer know; perhaps Nandi knows. When the flesh melts and one perceives awareness itself, our Lord of the gods is like honey.
nuance: நானே அறிகிலன் may be humility or the claim that the 'I' as knower is gone once karma ends. ஊனே உருகி, the flesh melting, is the devotional image of the melting body found across Saiva hymns.

reading: The Lord does not exist because I know him; those who knew the heavens were bewildered and did not know him; if the bright flame that knows the flesh and breathes within does not know him, who else will?
nuance: The flame within (ஒண்சுடர்) may be the soul or the Lord himself. On the first reading only the soul's inner light can know him; on the second, only he knows himself.

reading: People do not know how far grace reaches everywhere, do not discern that grace is nectar to be enjoyed, do not consider grace's great subtlety in the five acts; who knows that grace is the eye everywhere?
nuance: Each line opens with அருள். The five acts (ஐங்கருமம்) are named here as grace's work, not only as power, which the chapter goes on to say outright (1805, 1809).

reading: He grants knowledge so that the soul may draw near by knowing, lets desire in through the senses and joins with it, turns it into knowledge and gives the grace of his feet; those who stood close to him became Siva.
nuance: அணு (the atom) is a Siddhanta name for the bound soul. The verse seems to say that even desire through the senses is used by grace, but who 'joins' (புணர்ந்திட்டு) is unclear.

reading: Born in grace, grown in grace, wearing out, resting and vanishing in grace, fed the full nectar of bliss that is grace, by grace my Nandi entered my heart.
nuance: The whole course of a life, birth, growth, decay, rest and disappearance, is set inside grace. இளைப்பாறி (resting) may point to the rest the soul has in dissolution before the next creation.

reading: By grace he bathed me in the great sea of nectar, by grace joined me to his feet and gave me longing, fed me the full nectar of bliss that is grace, and by grace my Nandi entered there.
nuance: Lines 3 and 4 nearly repeat 1800. அடிபுணைந்து can be 'joined to his feet' or 'his feet became my raft' (புணை), which suits the sea of line 1.

reading: It was grace that put the soul into bonds, grace that let go its love of those bonds, grace that gives release without shame in that love, and grace is the state that does not appear in the love of that union.
nuance: The striking claim is that binding too is grace. Siddhanta tradition reads it so: the soul is joined to bonds so that its root impurity may ripen and fall. Line 4 is compressed and I can't fix it.

reading: The great gracious one who gave the way of no birth, the great ascetic Nandi who gave grace that does not forget, the Brahmin who is a sea of virtue, the first Supreme, came as kin and entered my heart.
nuance: அறவாழி அந்தணன் is the Kural's own phrase for the Lord (Kural 8). மாதவன் here is 'great ascetic', not Vishnu. Nandi in Tirumular is both the Lord and the first guru, so the verse may also speak of the teacher.

reading: By grace he entered the heart of me, his servant; though within, he is not seen by those without grace; entering, making bliss and becoming Siva, Nandi entered as the blissful one.
nuance: அகம்புகுந்தான் opens every line, carried over from the end of 1800. Line 2 says the same indwelling Lord is in everyone but is not perceived without grace.

reading: Great maya, which does not know, with the knowing soul; the instruments it makes, the five elements and the many senses with them: all these are the fivefold work of grace.
nuance: ஆயும் அறிவோடு அறியாத மாமாயை is taken here as the soul (which knows) beside maya (which does not), the sentient and insentient. Calling the whole apparatus of body and senses grace's work follows 1802.

reading: Grace is all the elemental world, grace is the Pure one become the moving and unmoving; the Lord who is called darkness and open space, everywhere, is grace, and there is none apart from embodied form.
nuance: சகளம் is the Lord's form with parts, as against the formless. Line 4 (அருளே சகளத்தின் அன்றிஇன் றாமே) is unclear: it may mean grace is known only through form, or that nothing exists apart from it.

reading: Siva with Shakti, shining nada, bindu, the five-faced Sadasiva of austerity, Isa, Hara, Mal who enters births and the lotus-born at the end: he dances, having become these nine.
nuance: These are the nine forms (நவந்தரு பேதம்) of Siva in Siddhanta. Placing Vishnu (மால்) and Brahma among Siva's own forms ranks them under him. பவமுறும், 'who meets birth', may refer to Vishnu's avatars.

reading: To those without the eye of grace the rare thing does not appear; to those with it Hara appears before them. To the dark-eyed even the sun does not appear; to the clear-eyed it is glorious light everywhere.
nuance: The sun is visible to all but the blind; so the Lord is present to all but seen only with grace's eye. The fault lies in the seer, not in the light.

reading: He himself creates, protects, destroys and conceals; doing these he himself grants release; he himself pervades and is the head.
nuance: The five acts, with release (முத்தி) taking the place of the fifth, grace. தானே (he himself) opens every line: no other agent is involved.

reading: The upper four are his formless forms; Sadasiva, unwavering, is form and formless; the lower four are lasting forms; the Lord, beyond measure, is all of them and yet one.
nuance: This sorts the nine of 1807: Siva, Shakti, nada and bindu formless; Sadasiva both; Maheswara, Rudra, Vishnu and Brahma with form. துலையா (unweighable, or unfailing) and the last phrase அல்லது ஒன்றே are not fully clear.

reading: Being one, he is the imperishable; standing as if he were the soul, he is the life of life; pressing close, he is also not those things, as a companion; his play stands in me as love.
nuance: The verse seems to state the Siddhanta relation of Lord and soul: one with it, other than it, and with it as companion. The syntax is compressed and the reading is tentative.

reading: The Spotless one, standing in love with Shakti, reaching kutila and nada, joining to become many kalas, ripens as a bindu that cannot be lost.
nuance: குடிலை (kutila, the curved power), நாதம் and கலை are technical terms of the cosmology chapter 140 develops. வீயத்தகா, 'not fit to perish', may describe bindu as imperishable or as not to be spent.

reading: The supreme bindu that ripens is itself all-pervading; from it ripen pure maya and the vast great maya, the branch of the gods, the rising mantras and Veda, and countless crores of worlds.
nuance: தனிமாயை may be சுத்தமாயை (pure maya) and மாமாயை the great maya, the two levels of maya in Siddhanta; மனு here is mantra. The chain (1812 to 1813) links back to grace: what grace places is the whole cosmos.

title: அருள் ஒளி
theme: The light of grace (அருள் ஒளி): those who stand in grace are freed of the bonds, and the poet tells how, seeking with song and tears, he was given Siva's feet, made spotless and fed nectar. Grace is a lamp that turns its bearer into light, and when light and darkness both pass the soul becomes Siva.
structure_note: A verse on standing in grace (1814) is followed by first-person testimony of what Nandi gave (1815 to 1817, 1820), verses on the lamp and the light (1818, 1819), and two closing verses on grace as refuge (1821) and a challenge about birth and death (1822).
source_issues: 1819 line 3: ஒளியுருள் may be a misprint for ஒளியிருள்; the line is obscure.
1822 lines 2 and 4 (மெய்ப்பொருள் நீக்கிடும், தேறுஅணிவோம்) are obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: Those who stand first in grace know and do not sink; those who do not stand in grace do not leave the five bonds, know not grace's greatness and do not draw near; born in grace, they know by knowing.
nuance: ஐம்பாசம் (the five bonds) is traditionally anava, karma, maya, mayeya and the concealing power; the verse does not list them. Who is 'born in grace' in line 4 is unclear: perhaps those of line 1, perhaps everyone, as in 1800.

reading: Great Nandi gave the way of no return; Nandi the blissful gave nectar that never sates; the Lord of a thousand names said, in a single name, 'Bathe in the insatiable sea of grace.'
