nuance: வாரா வழி, the road from which one does not come back, is release from rebirth. பேர் ஒன்றினில் may mean 'by one of his names' or that the thousand names are summed in one, which tradition may take as the five-letter mantra.

reading: Dancing, singing, weeping and crying out, seeking, I found Siva's great nature; as he joined me he gave me a sign that is no sign and stood within me, and I gained his grace.
nuance: The first line is the vocabulary of ecstatic devotion. குறியாக் குறி, 'a sign that is not a sign', is traditionally the Lord beyond form given in a form, or the guru's teaching; the verse leaves it open.

reading: Treating the birth I came into and the impurity that came with it as a film of maya I had clung to, I set my feet on your way saying 'you are my father', great Nandi; I left what I had learned and bowed at your anklet.
nuance: அத்தனை நீயென்று may be 'you are the father' (அத்தன்) or 'you are all that' (அத்தனை); அடிவைத்தேன் may be 'I stepped forward' or 'I placed myself at your feet'. கற்றன விட்டேன் is a strong phrase: learning is put down, not completed.

reading: Light the lamp and know the open space; before the lamp suffering changes; those who hold the lamp that lights the lamp become themselves the lamp that shines in the lamp.
nuance: விளக்கு (lamp) occurs in every line, and விளக்கும் also means 'explains' or 'makes clear'. வெளி (open space) may be the yogic inner sky. Tradition reads the lamp that lights the lamp as grace or the guru kindling knowledge.

reading: Light and darkness never end once and for all; only for those in the light does the light not fail; light and darkness are as different as an eye that has seen them; when both light and darkness go, the soul becomes Siva.
nuance: Line 3 is obscure. The last line goes past the usual image: release is not light defeating darkness but both passing, which tradition may read as going beyond knowledge and ignorance alike.

reading: Me, who wandered outside, he crowned with his golden anklets, entered my very nature and made me spotless, entered as dharma and gave me nectar; I sat dazed, wondering how he did it.
nuance: பொற்கழல் சூட்டி, crowning with the anklets, is placing the feet on the head, the gesture tradition calls திருவடி தீட்சை. நிறமே may be 'my colour' or 'my very being'.

reading: There is one wide place called grace and one refuge called the true thing; when the one who entered the mind to remove delusion is grasped with clarity, the way to Siva follows.
nuance: மருள் (delusion) and தெருள் (clarity) are paired. Grace and the true thing may be two names of one refuge or two stages, grace leading to the real.

reading: Tell us how you were born before and died here; another god's version of the truth is set aside; casting off the body that vultures adorn, we shall clothe the precious soul in clarity: can you say this?
nuance: The verse reads as a challenge to those who cannot account for their own births and deaths. Line 2 (வேறொரு தெய்வத்தின் மெய்ப்பொருள் நீக்கிடும்) and தேறுஅணிவோம் are obscure, and the reading is a guess.

title: சிவபூசை
theme: Worship of Siva (சிவபூசை): the body is the temple and the soul the linga; outer worship with flowers and water is open to anyone and the Lord answers it with grace, but rite without inner knowing does not reach him. The chapter moves between praise of offering, the inner rite of mantra and the heart, and the stages of initiation.
structure_note: It opens with the inner temple (1823 to 1825), then praises flowers-and-water worship and its fruit (1826 to 1840), with warnings that praise and rite alone do not bring knowing (1837, 1841, 1842); it closes on the jewel within the body (1843, 1844), the grades of initiation (1845) and the Lord beyond the ages (1846).
source_issues: 1835 lines 1 and 2, 1840 line 1 and 1844 lines 1 and 2 are obscure and may be corrupt.
1841 lines 3 and 4 (ஆத்தி மலக்கிட்டு அகத்துஇழுக்கு அற்றக்கான் மாத்திக்கே) are obscure; அற்றக்கான் may be a misprint for அற்றக்கால்.
1825 line 4: சீன்முகம் is not a known word; it may be a misprint (perhaps for சின்முகம்).
1836 line 4: வயனங்கள் may be a variant or misprint of நயனங்கள், echoing line 3.

reading: For the generous Lord the heart is the great temple, the body of flesh the shrine and the mouth the tower gate; for those clear through and through, the soul is the Sivalinga, and the five thieving senses are the bright lamps.
nuance: Each part of the temple is matched to the person. The senses, called thieves (கள்ளப் புலன்), become its lamps, which implies they are mastered rather than cut off. காளாமணி is unclear, perhaps 'unflickering jewel'. Only 'for those clear through' (தெள்ளத் தெளிந்தார்க்கு) is the soul the linga.

reading: We have nothing to show, morning and evening, to Nandi of spreading matted hair who eats the oblation of sacrifice; as the food offering we offer the song that cools the heart, and that is our milk offering.
nuance: The verse plays on அவி (oblation): வேட்டவி of the fire rite, ஊட்டவி fed to the deity, பாட்டவி of song and பால்அவி of milk. It seems to put sung praise in the place of the sacrificial offering, but the first two lines are compressed.

reading: Invoking Sadasiva, who is the Supreme with the sweet-spoken goddess as his half, and taking the upper face as Isana, when the gesture is made, he becomes Siva.
nuance: ஆவாகித்து is avahana, invoking the deity into the image; ஈசானம் is the upward face of five-faced Sadasiva. சீன்முகம் is obscure, perhaps a mudra. 'He becomes Siva' may mean the image becomes Siva or the worshipper does.

reading: Without right thought and truthful speech it is hard to see the Lord of the sounding anklets; those who can see him are the ones who can truly praise him with flowers and water.
nuance: The order matters: inner truth comes first, and only then is outer offering real praise. நினைவதும் may be 'thinking of him' or 'thinking rightly'.

reading: The reason the Lord stays fixed in the hearts of the gods who bathe and garland him is that they worshipped him with the five nectars, the services eight and eight, and joined palms.
nuance: அஞ்சமுது is the five nectars of temple ablution (panchamrita), not the yogic amudham. உபசாரம் எட்டு எட்டு may be sixteen services (the usual count) or sixty-four.

reading: For those who would do good there are flowers and there is water; the Lord sees it and goes on granting grace; countless sinners slip away without knowing how to approach our Lord.
nuance: The point is how little worship needs: flowers and water are always to hand, so failing to worship is not lack of means. நழுவுகின்றார் (they slip away) makes the failure an evasion.

reading: Hear how the Father bathes in the nine holy waters: washing clean and sprinkling the feet of those raised high in true knowledge is release, so our Mulan said.
nuance: The nine sacred waters are relocated to the water that washes a jnani's feet, and the Lord is said to bathe in that. Tirumular names himself (நம்மூலன்) as the authority.

reading: Lord of the gods, even if I remain on this path forgetful, grant that I may hold flowers and water rightly before you and worship you fully, without forgetting.
nuance: A prayer, not a teaching: the worshipper asks for the unforgetting worship that he admits he cannot keep by himself. மறப்பு opens and returns in line 3.

reading: Worship, the hosts of gods, the endless sea and all on the land stand as yours; the thousand names and the Lord's holy name are a way that never sates, our first Lord.
nuance: The syntax is loose: ஆரா வழி may be 'the insatiable way' or 'the way no one completes'. The verse seems to make worship, the cosmos and the names all the Lord's own.

reading: Bathed in the five products of the cow while the hosts of gods worship, the endless Lord's grace, clear within the great flower that drips honey, stands having made the five qualities of the earth.
nuance: ஆன்ஐந்து is the panchagavya used in ablution. பார் ஐங்குணம் are the five qualities of earth (sound, touch, form, taste, smell). The honeyed flower may be a temple flower or the lotus of the heart.

reading: Holding together flowers and water gathered with toil, the gods, going above the rain clouds, praise him, wavering with their bonds still thick on them; our Lord's grace comes without fail.
nuance: உழைக்கொண்ட may be 'gathered with toil' or 'held at one's side'. If the gods worship with their bonds still on them, the verse says grace answers worship even before the bonds fall.

reading: Those who will not enter the sea of the heart, carry loads of flowers to Nandi of spreading matted hair in the flood-sea, leave the sea of deceit and join hands in worship sink in the sea that drags them down.
nuance: Four seas: the flood-sea (perhaps the Ganga in his hair or the cosmic deluge), the sea of the heart, the sea of deceit (the senses) and the sea that swallows, taken as the sea of births. The syntax of line 2 is unclear.

reading: The cool sea of the backwaters is full of uproar; those who go by the way do not know the flower bud; while the many who earn blame fall into blame, he stands at the crown of those who come into the open.
nuance: The first two lines are obscure. வெளிப்படுவோர் may be those who become manifest in knowledge, and உச்சி the crown of the head as in yoga; neither can be fixed.

reading: There is one knowledge of the fruit: to those who strew many flowers knowing that fruit, Hara himself keeps near; so that they may reach the feet of the three-eyed one, he has come and stands for ever by his own ways.
nuance: பயனறிவு (knowing the fruit) separates worship that understands what it seeks from mere strewing of flowers. வயனங்கள் is unclear: perhaps 'means' or 'ways', perhaps a variant of நயனங்கள் (eyes).

reading: They praise, strewing great flowers and standing in worship, crying 'our Lord's gracious red feet'; yet none of them, though they praise, come to know the holy one who stands as form and as the unageing first.
nuance: The last line turns against the first: praise and offering do not by themselves bring knowing. தீர்த்தன் may be 'the holy one' or 'the one who ends' (births).

reading: With the gods, music comes down and joins the earth; carrying flowers and water, they praise the Pure one; who can conceive the nature of his grace, standing as the first among the three and in many forms?
nuance: மூவரிற் பன்மை முதல்வன் is taken as first of the three gods (Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra) and present in many; the syntax allows other readings.

reading: You who can labour, holding water and flowers between your hands, keeping the Lord's great austerity without fault, strewing flowers of every kind on the jewelled feet, stand firm like the rain cloud.
nuance: The rain cloud (மழைக்கொண்டல்) may stand for unfailing, generous giving, matched to the steady showering of flowers. ஈசன் பெருந்தவம் may be austerity done for the Lord rather than his own.

reading: They said: overcome, hurry, serve with fragrance; if, standing fittingly as the Lord's service comes right, you strew dense water and flowers and worship, he will accept it every day, as was said.
nuance: Line 1 (வென்று விரைந்து விரைப்பணி) is obscure, with a pun on விரை (hurry; fragrance). The second half is clearer: daily offering is accepted.

reading: Adorning him, setting him up, praising him as Svayambhu and praising him every day, they do not know the Lord; when one removes the impurity and the inner stain is gone, that is the way that leads to the great goal.
nuance: சயம்பு is the self-manifest linga. Lines 3 and 4 (ஆத்தி மலக்கிட்டு அகத்துஇழுக்கு அற்றக்கான் மாத்திக்கே) are obscure; ஆத்தி may be the Bauhinia flower sacred to Siva. The contrast of outer rite and inner purity seems clear.

reading: They do not know the mantra by which to call on, contemplate and lead Nandi of spreading hair, who roams in delight beyond the lotus of the breath, and establish him in Siva.
nuance: ஆவிக் கமலம் may be the lotus of the soul or of the breath, the heart-lotus of inner worship. கூவி, கருதி, தாவிக்கும் echo the outer rite's invoking, meditating and establishing (avahana, sthapana) done inwardly.

reading: Until they see the ruby sunk within the visible body, no one knows its worth; to those who cherish him and swell their thought of him again and again, the one who is a ruby garland enters the mind.
nuance: The jewel is hidden in the body, not outside it, as in 1823. காண் ஆகம் may be 'the body that is seen' or 'look: within the body'.

reading: Nandi of great nature, a wheel against the clinging dark, by his two natures took my heart as his place; the gods held fast to the one whose nature is to come and whose nature is to give.
nuance: பிணங்கிருள் நேமி and இருந்தன்மை are obscure; இருந்தன்மை may be 'two natures' or 'a great nature'. The reading is tentative.

reading: Samaya initiation purifies impurity and one's own acting ceases; vishesha that follows is purification by mantra; nirvana initiation is purification of the kalas; for those become knowledge in the hall there is abhisheka.
nuance: The four are traditionally the grades of Saiva initiation given by a guru: samaya, vishesha, nirvana and acharya abhisheka. The verse does not name தீட்சை. The match of each grade to a purification is the verse's own, but its grammar is compressed.

reading: Except to those who have perceived him age after age, he does not let the soul in its fate know him; beyond the ages, beyond those called Hari of the ocean and Ayan, he is at the one summit.
nuance: ஊழி (aeon) and ஊழ் (fate) are played against each other. Hari and Brahma failing to find the summit recalls the myth of the column of fire. ஓர் உச்சி may be that summit or the crown of the head in yoga.

title: குருபூசை
theme: Worship of the guru, Nandi: outer worship with sandal and flowers does not reach the Lord, while inner worship in knowledge, in the place beyond sun and moon and beyond day and night, is the great worship.
structure_note: Praise of Nandi's feet opens (1847); outer offerings are set against inner knowing (1848, 1849); a verse on the daily name (1850) and one on the ranking of offerings (1851); then the place beyond sun and moon (1852, 1853), the yogic inner worship (1854) and the worship beyond day and night (1855, 1856).
source_issues: 1851: பூசைநா றாகுமாம் is presumably பூசை நூறு ஆகுமாம்.
1847: போகின்றுபதேசம் is read as போகின்ற உபதேசம்; the division is uncertain.

reading: Holding to the lotus feet of Nandi, I praise the worship that honours the teaching he gives, and the splendour that rises above the six-and-six supports.
nuance: போகின்றுபதேசம் is read as போகின்ற உபதேசம், the teaching that goes forth. ஆதாரம் ஆறாறு can be the six bodily supports (adharas) or six times six, the thirty-six tattvas; either way the splendour is above them.

reading: Though one worships with ten million loads of fragrant forest sandal and great flowers heaped to the sky, the one with honey-filled flowered tresses cannot be reached except by those who put away the flesh and perceive.
nuance: தேனமர் பூங்குழல் names the goddess by her hair; whether she stands here for Shakti alone or for the Lord with her is not said. ஊனினை நீக்கி is usually taken as leaving identification with the body rather than abstaining from meat. Sengalvaraya cites Appar's 'ஊனையே கழிக்கவேண்டில்' for the same thought.

reading: If one rises high in the knowledge one has reached, the true Supreme is there; standing in the path of knowledge is the true offering, ceaseless inner worship is the best, and reaching the red feet is the ceasing of one's own acts.
nuance: The verse redefines archana (அர்ச்சனை) as standing in knowledge, not as an outer rite. செயலறல், the end of acting, is traditionally the stillness in which the soul no longer claims its acts.

reading: Long for the Lord at noon, morning and evening; longing, sow his name with 'nama'; sow it, and long for him in the three spreading lights, and Nandi, the great one, will become your master.
nuance: நச்சுமின் (long for) and விச்சுமின் (sow, from வித்து) alternate through the verse. Naming the Lord with நம is taken as the five-letter mantra. The three lights are usually sun, moon and fire, which yogic readings place in the body.

reading: Worship in a holy mandala counts a hundredfold, worship of a fashioned image a thousandfold, and alms given to the countless ten-millionfold; but food prepared for a jnani, if you consider it, is beyond all these.
nuance: பூசைநா றாகுமாம் is read as பூசை நூறு. எண்ணிலிக்கு ஐயம் may be alms to countless people or to one of countless worth. The verse ranks offerings by merit and puts feeding a knower of Siva at the top, as the next chapter will at length.

reading: All worship offered in the place where moon and sun shine goes to the asuras as their share; worship in the place where moon and sun do not shine is the great worship of Nandi.
nuance: Plainly read, worship done in the light of day and night is lost and worship beyond them is true. In yogic tradition moon and sun are the left and right breath channels, and the place where they do not shine is the central channel or the crown above them. Both readings stand.

reading: What rises as moon and sun becomes bindu and nada in the canopy above; there, with thought gone beyond waking, worship Nandi, and that is good worship.
nuance: மீதானம் (the canopy above) is traditionally the space at the crown of the head. சாக்கிராதீதம் is the state beyond waking in Siddhanta's scheme of states. The verse turns the moon and sun of 1852 into bindu and nada.

reading: Turning mind and breath back at the root, making the impermanent body into its elements and setting it aside, entering the Pure One's grace and staying in bliss: this solitary worship is Sadasiva's.
nuance: மனபவனம் is mind and breath, and மூலம் the root support at the base of the spine. உடல் பூதமாக்கி அகற்றி is taken as the rite of purifying the elements, in which the body is dissolved in thought before worship.

reading: Worship practised by day and night becomes paired flowers for the Lord as he is by nature; worship not practised by day and night the one of hanging matted hair takes wholly.
nuance: The second half may mean worship that is not bound to times, or worship in the state where day and night (the two breaths, or waking and sleep) have ceased. இணைமலர் may also be the Lord's paired feet.

reading: Staying in the place where night and day are not, drinking without distraction the clear honey of bliss, in the joy of the Lord's feet where there is no night or day, I have set the night and day of maya in their two places.
nuance: இராப்பகல் அற்ற இடம் is the place beyond the alternation of states. The last line is obscure: it may mean the speaker has left maya's day and night behind, or holds them apart while staying between.

title: மகேசுவர பூசை
theme: Worship of Siva in his devotees (மகேசுவர பூசை): what is given to the devotee, the walking temple, reaches the god, and feeding one knower of Siva outweighs gifts to thousands of Brahmins and the building of temples.
structure_note: The thesis comes first (1857): gifts to the living devotee reach the god in the temple, not the reverse. The rest ranks feeding the devotee above ritual gifts (1858 to 1861, 1866), praises the ash-wearing devotees (1862, 1864), turns briefly to the poet's own devotion (1863) and to false worshippers (1865), and ends on charity to ascetics as the end of karma (1867).
source_issues: 1864: line 2 reads தூfங்கிருள், with a stray Latin letter; read தூங்கிருள். தொழுகை may be a misprint for தொழுக.
1865: the verse is obscure and its last line (ஆய்ந்தொழிந் தா ரே) is split oddly; the text may be corrupt.

reading: If you give something to the god of the temple of images, it does not reach the Lord in the walking temple; if you give something to the Lord in the walking temple, it reaches the god of the temple of images.
nuance: படமாடக் கோயில் is the built temple with its images (படம் may also be its banners); நடமாடக் கோயில் is the living devotee, whose body houses the Lord. The verse does not forbid temple offerings; it says they flow one way only.

reading: What the ascetics of steady mind eat with delight, the three worlds have eaten, and what they receive, the three worlds have received: so Nandi of the eight directions declared.
nuance: தண்டு அறு சிந்தை is a mind without obstruction or wavering. The claim is that feeding one such ascetic feeds the whole world, and it is given Nandi's authority.

reading: A rare gift made to the realised one who stays settled in a single measure becomes holy water for the three gods and for the thrice seven elders; understand this.
nuance: ஆத்தன் is taken as the trustworthy, realised one. மாத்திரை ஒன்றினில் may be one moment, one measure of breath, or one syllable. மூவேழ் குரவர் is commonly read as twenty-one generations of forebears whom the gift sanctifies.

reading: What if one gives a thousand villages to Brahmins, what if one builds a thousand temple towers? Nothing equals the merit of giving a midday meal to a jnani; that is certain.
nuance: அகரம் is the agraharam, a village granted to Brahmins, and சிகரம் the tower of a temple: the two great religious gifts of a king, both set below one meal.

reading: Feeding ten million Brahmins learned in the rare Veda who perform the six duties does not bring the fruit of thinking of the ash-wearing servant of the Lord; if it is gain one wants, a single handful given to him is the gain.
nuance: ஆறிடும் வேள்வி is taken as the Brahmin's six duties (studying and teaching, sacrificing and having sacrifice done, giving and receiving). The syntax of line 3 is compressed; the sense of comparison is clear but the exact construction is not.

reading: Those who wear the ash crying 'Lord who rides the bull, our master' are devotees, gods walking on earth; those who honour them apart, saying 'this is the Lord with the river on his red locks', have no karma.
nuance: வேறு அணிவார் is unclear: those who honour the devotees specially, or who adorn them as the Lord. Either way the verse treats seeing the Lord in his devotees as what frees from karma.

reading: Glorious Nandi took me and sent me as his holy word; until I come back, though I ache and ache, I will not stop babbling 'Great Nandi' of the one with shining matted hair.
nuance: திருமுகம் can be a royal letter or the holy face. On the first reading Tirumular is Nandi's message sent into the world, which fits the tradition that he was sent south from Kailasa.

reading: By worshipping Hara's devotees, who know no decline, the world's thick darkness leaves; seeking the gracious one so as not to fall short, and rising after worship, there is a joy unlike any on earth.
nuance: பண்பன் (the one of goodness) may be the Lord or the devotee; the verse moves from honouring devotees to seeking him without a break.

reading: Those who worship the Lord without the fitting disposition, entering as if possessed and matching only in outward face, stay deluded within age after age and, for all their inquiry, come to nothing.
nuance: The verse plays on மத்தர் (the frenzied): புகுமத்தர், முகமத்து, அகமத்தர். Its target may be worshippers of the temple image who neglect the devotees, given the chapter's argument, but the verse does not say so.

reading: The food eaten by those in the wise guise of devotees is as if the Father, Brahma and Vishnu had eaten it; if the clear-minded drink what they leave, it is release: so our Mulan has said.
nuance: ஊன் here is food, not flesh. சேடம் is the remnant of the devotee's meal, which tradition treats as sanctified. Tirumular names himself (நம் மூலன்) as the authority.

reading: Those who never fall still strive at rare austerity; charity done to them alone sinks deep karma, removes it along with hard and cleaving karma, and becomes the golden world.
nuance: The kinds of karma (ஆழ்வினை, அருவினை, போழ்வினை) are not clearly distinguished; the repetition may be for sound. The subject of தீர்க்கும் may be the charity or the ascetics.

title: அடியார் பெருமை
theme: The greatness of the Lord's devotees: where one lives the land prospers and rain falls, they attain the Lord in this body and this world, all things are held in their sight, and they are bound to Siva by a deed written before birth.
structure_note: The chapter opens and nearly closes on the land blessed by a devotee's presence (1868, 1869, 1881, 1882). Between them come verses in the devotee's own voice, on holding all in the hand and the eye (1870, 1871), on the Lord beyond sex and sense (1872), on the inner chamber (1874, 1877) and on the deed of servitude (1876). 1883 ends with the devotees at the top of a ladder of knowers.
source_issues: 1869: line 1 reads உடலோணடும், a misprint for உடலோடும்.
1883: line 4 reads மேலுணுர், a misprint for மேலுணர்.
1868: ஒரு வாது இருக்கில் is probably a misdivision of ஒருவன் இருக்கில்.

reading: If there is one who seeks the god of all directions in the fitting way, there are no enemies, rain falls on the earth, and that world suffers no inner want or ruin.
nuance: ஒரு வாது இருக்கில் is odd; it is probably ஒருவன் இருக்கில், 'if there is one'. On the plain sense a single seeker of the Lord brings peace and rain to his whole land.

reading: Born in that world, with that very body they seek rare austerity in that world, join Hara's feet in that world and gain grace in that world.
nuance: அவ்வுலகம் may be the land of 1868 where the devotee lives, or this world as against another. Either way the stress falls on attaining in the same body and the same world one is born in, not after death.

reading: If the sign I have taken, the summit of the great mountain, the gods, the immortals of the cosmos, the Primal one and those of the eight directions all come into the palm of my hand, then we are saved for good.
nuance: கொண்ட குறி (the sign taken) may be the linga or the form of the Lord meditated on, and குலவரை உச்சி Kailasa. The verse may be a condition or a claim: the devotee who holds the Lord holds everything.

reading: The seven worlds, the undivided, the soul, all the moving and unmoving, the qualities, the ancient Veda, creation, protection and the rest, and Siva who beholds them: none is apart from my eye.
nuance: என் கண் can be the eye of knowledge that sees all, or the devotee's eye in which all is contained. கண்ட சிவன் may also mean 'the Siva I have seen'.

reading: The light within the dark, neither woman nor man nor neuter, cannot be known by anyone; he sees without eyes and hears without ears, and to have searched out the Lord's greatness is true maturity.
nuance: மூடத்துள் may be the body, ignorance, or the hidden heart. மூப்பு (age, seniority) is taken as ripeness of wisdom; the line could also mean that inquiring into his greatness only ends in old age.

reading: In this moving world the Lord's devotees go by the undeluded way and rule the world of the sky; their arms are the eight directions, their feet the netherworld, and their great crown the outer cosmos.
nuance: The second half gives the devotee the cosmic body usually given to the Lord. போது பாதாளம் is read as 'the feet reach the netherworld'; பகிரண்டம் is the outer cosmos.

reading: Contemplate our Lord who dwells in the inner chamber; those who have seen the inner chamber will not come to grief; the heart that enters within and knows, seeing the inner chamber, can destroy the eight.
nuance: அகம்படி is the inner apartment of a palace and those who serve in it, and also simply 'within'; the verse uses it in every line. The eight (எட்டு) to be destroyed are not named; the eight bodily constituents or eight bonds are possible.

reading: The first Lord, who stood as end and beginning, as love's companion and as destruction, has taken my soul as his field to plough; blame and praise and all that befalls me now fall away.
nuance: உழவு கொண்டான் pictures the Lord tilling the soul. Taking கழிவும் முதலும் as end and beginning is the usual reading; காதல் துணை may also be his consort.

reading: For my mother, my father and seven times seven births, a deed of bond to Siva was written that very day; he who alone created the world wrote it, and the cloud-coloured one stood as witness.
nuance: ஆவணம் is a legal deed, here a deed of servitude, and நேர்எழுத்து the attesting signature, so Brahma writes it and Vishnu witnesses it. The image of hereditary bondage to Siva by deed resembles the story told of Sundarar. Sengalvaraya cites Appar's 'முந்தி உலகம் படைத்தான்'.

reading: He dwells close within the resolute, flows like milk within the humble, and stands as the Primal Lord within those who wear his signs; for one who has reckoned him so, can he be let go?
nuance: The last line is unclear: it may ask whether such a devotee could ever be abandoned, or whether he could ever give the Lord up. அணிந்தார் may be those who wear ash and rudraksha, or those who adorn the Lord.

reading: Nandi of the hanging locks, above the heads of the gods, placed his devotees on his head as a garland so that they might do true service; the one of spreading locks rules the golden world free of baseness and grants its fruit.
nuance: மிலை is a garland worn on the head; who is placed there is not said, and some take it as the Lord placing his feet on the devotee's head. The golden world (பொன்னுலகு) recurs from 1867.

reading: To recognise Hara's devotees by their signs and delight in them even at an age that does not yet understand is true servitude; those who walk with the matted crown of his sign, bathing in wave-filled waters, make great austerity.
nuance: அறியாப் பருவம் is childhood, the time before understanding; the verse may be thinking of child saints like Sambandar. மறியார் புனல் may also be the waters of the Ganga in the locks of the one who holds the deer (மறி).

reading: Those who approach him and love him are able to approach Siva too; for the devotees who draw near and seek him, greatness in him becomes absorption.
nuance: அவன் is most likely the devotee or the guru, so that approaching him is approaching Siva; இலயம் is absorption. The referents of அவன் and இவன் are not fixed by the verse.

reading: The eight classes of gods who were there before come in countless numbers with love to this wide earth, and across the directions and the sky alike the land for twelve leagues around is made fit.
nuance: The verse continues the theme of the place where a devotee lives. எண்இரு நாலு திசை and பன்னிரு காதம் are numbers whose exact sense is unclear; பதஞ்செய்யும் may mean 'becomes ripe' or 'becomes a holy station'.

reading: The land where a Siva-yogi and jnani dwell will have knowers free of false yoga; the ninefold yoga will be gained, good order will be seen, and without the yoga of births it becomes the higher world.
nuance: அவயோகம் (bad yoga), நவயோகம் (nine yogas or new yoga) and பவயோகம் (union with birth) form a play on யோகம். The nine yogas are not specified.

reading: He who created the vast world knows from above; he who transcends the vast world knows from above; the immortals of the vast world know from above; and Siva's true devotees know from above.
nuance: The four lines repeat மேலுணர், so the devotees end a ladder beginning with the Creator and Siva. மேலுணர்வான் may also mean 'the one known as highest', which would make the verse a list of who is supreme.

title: போசன விதி
theme: The rule of eating: devotees are welcomed and fed everywhere as if with nectar, and those who know the grace within Siva beg at noon for the Lord in the inner temple, eat without distinction and sit apart, free of desire.

reading: In all eight directions people welcome the Lord's devotees with prepared food, calling it nectar; those who cling to ruling a piece of land would not know desire for it if they left it lying.
nuance: கட்ட அடிசில் may be food made ready or food bundled for the road. The second half is obscure; it may contrast the devotee, fed everywhere, with the king who clings to his land, or say that a king who gave up his land for this life would not miss it.

reading: Those who know the grace standing within Siva beg alms at noon for the Lord in the temple within, eat, think of all without distinction, give up desire and sit raised in solitude.
nuance: உள்ளமர் கோவில் is the temple within, the heart where the Lord dwells, so the alms are begged for him and eating is an offering. பேதம் அற நினைந்து may mean without distinguishing donors or without the sense of self and other.

title: பிட்சா விதி
theme: The rule of begging: Siva himself begged with Brahma's skull and made begging the devotee's way to his feet; begging from desire is faulted, while the true ascetic is free of hunger, craving and anger and the world comes to him.
structure_note: A riddle verse faults begging from desire (1886); three verses on Siva the beggar (1887 to 1889); then the devotee's freedom from hunger and anger (1890) and the two ways of the ascetic, going to doors or staying put (1891).

reading: There is a seed pot and there is one fenced field, and the ploughing was finished before noon; those who cannot lose their fear, reap that crop and eat, go begging alms for their desires.
nuance: The seed pot and the fenced field are symbolic; tradition takes them as bindu and the body, or as the grace and the soul, with the work already done for the devotee. The plain point is that those who do not use what they have beg out of desire.

reading: He took alms in Brahma's skull; he took alms to do unfailing dharma; he took alms showing Brahma's head; he took alms so that Brahma might become supreme.
nuance: The verse draws on the story of Siva as the divine beggar who cut off Brahma's fifth head and begged with its skull. பிரமன் பரமாகவே may mean to raise Brahma, to show Brahma's pride humbled, or to show himself as the supreme beyond Brahma; it is unclear.

reading: People call the Lord who spread out and created the seven worlds a beggar; why does he beg? For the devotees who think of him without end, he begged so that by begging and eating they might reach his feet.
nuance: The verse makes Siva's begging a model: by begging himself he made begging a path for his devotees. இரந்துண்டு may describe the Lord or the devotees; both readings lead to the same point.

reading: The Lord who stands on the way waits ready to come, waits ready to give himself as joy to the good, waits to contend as their only refuge; yet if he waits to come, they say he does not know.
nuance: The verse repeats இருந்தான் (he stayed, he waited). Its last line is obscure; it may mean that people think the Lord is unaware while he only waits for them to turn to him.

reading: Fiery hunger, craving and anger do not stay in the bodies of Siva's devotees; those who reach Siva do not stay even in the abundant worlds or the worlds of merit.
nuance: The verse pairs two kinds of not staying: the passions do not stay in the devotee, and the devotee does not stay in any heaven earned by merit. Hunger stands with the passions here, which suits a chapter on living by alms.

reading: Even those very clear in true inner knowledge go with outstretched hand to the doorstep; the ascetics who stayed without going for alms found the whole world coming to them.
nuance: ஐயம் is alms, but also doubt, so ஐயம் புகாமல் may mean 'without entering for alms' or 'without doubt entering'. On the first reading the verse allows two ways for the ascetic and gives the higher place to staying put.

title: முத்திரை பேதம்
theme: The kinds of mudra: shambhavi, khechari, the grace-hand and the knowledge-mudra are distinguished, and the highest seal is the mudra of silence, in which speech and mind both cease and release is gained; the chapter ends by placing Vedanta and Siddhanta together in pure Saivam.
structure_note: Silence and release open the chapter (1892). The named mudras are listed and glossed (1893, 1894, 1897), silence is defined (1895, 1896), the yogi's attainments gathered (1898), pure Saivam defined (1899), and the mudras assigned to kinds of people (1900). 1901 closes on coloured paths.
source_issues: 1896: line 4 reads சுத்த்ததை, with a doubled consonant; read சுத்தத்தை.
1893: உரைத்தாரம் and சொருகுஇடன் are obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: When the four-sevens cease, the mudra attained is fixed in the speech of silence, and saved at the holy feet of supreme Nandi, with all tumult gone, one gains good release.
nuance: நாலேழு may be twenty-eight, or four and seven; what ceases is not said, perhaps the senses and faculties or the tattvas. பாலான மோன மொழி is the 'speech' of silence, a paradox the chapter returns to.

reading: The three turiyas become the place of closing; restraining there the hard-to-utter sound, shambhavi and khechari join, and the truth is knowledge growing: these are the distinct mudras.
nuance: துரியங்கள் மூன்று (three fourth-states), சொருகு இடம் (the place of closing or inserting) and உரைத்தாரம் are technical and obscure. Shambhavi (gaze fixed within) and khechari (the tongue turned up, moving in space) are named mudras of yoga.

reading: Shambhavi is Nandi's gracious glance; the grace-hand mudra is free of births; khechari is the truth that rises in practising Om; and the knowledge-mudra is the true knowledge of the Lord we practise.
nuance: The verse reads each mudra as an inner reality rather than a posture: the gaze becomes the Lord's glance, the gesture of the hand his grace. அருட்பாணி may be the hand gesture of grace or the grace of the Lord's hand.

reading: Within the station he becomes Sadasiva, within knowledge he is the good Sivam; so the mudra of silence, in which the form of Sivam otherwise seen is hidden, is release beyond release.
nuance: தானம் may be a yogic station or a place of worship; ஏனைச் சிவமாம் சொரூபம் is unclear. முத்தாந்த முத்தி, the release at the end of release, is a Siddhanta phrase for the final state.

reading: When speech and mind are both still, that is silence; if only speech falls silent, one is merely mute; the pure are those in whom speech and mind are silent, and who knows the purity they bring about?
nuance: The verse separates mauna from muteness (மூங்கை): silence of the tongue alone is nothing. The last line may also be read 'who can know that pure state which makes them?'

reading: The mudra of yoga is the eight siddhis; considering the mudra of knowledge that is one, Veda-khechari and shambhavi are fitting; for yoga, khechari is the yoga mudra.
nuance: The verse sorts mudras by path, yoga and knowledge, but the assignments in lines 2 and 3 are compressed and the term வேத கேசரி is unclear.

reading: The yogi, the eight siddhis, the sound of grace, the traces of past impressions, the enjoyer, his intellect, the good path of the aims of life, the good shakti and the testing of the supports: seeing them as one, he reaches the One and stands.
nuance: The verse is a list of terms (வாதனை for vasana, புருடார்த்தம் for the human aims, ஆதார சோதனை for examining the bodily supports) whose links are not stated. The point seems to be that all are gathered into one vision.

reading: The twelvefold path and the sixteenfold path, the ten kinds that end desire and the six limbs, the unfailing nature of Vedanta and Siddhanta, considered together with the nine Agamas: that is pure Saivam.
nuance: துவாதசம் (twelve) and கோடசம் (sixteen) may be the paths of breath reaching twelve and sixteen finger-breadths, or kalas. நவாஅகமோடு is read as the nine Agamas Tirumular names elsewhere, but நவ may also mean new. The verse makes pure Saivam hold Vedanta and Siddhanta together.

reading: The mudra of silence is the seal of the liberated, the mudra of knowledge the seal of the lords, the mudra that sweetens is the Siddhanta mudra, and the mudra that is displayed belongs to the religion seen outwardly.
nuance: தேனிக்கும் and கானிக்கும் are obscure; they are read here as 'makes sweet' and 'is shown', which ranks inner mudras above those seen in a sect's practice. The ranking is my reading of the sequence, not stated.

reading: The trace seen on the pure path rises in the middle; the flower path seen there stands as the golden place; the higher path seen is the white moon's land; and the one who has seen the blue path becomes the Spotless One.
nuance: The four paths, pure, flowered, higher and blue, are coloured stages of yogic ascent through the central channel, but which centres or lights they name is not fixed by the verse. நின்மலன் may be the Lord or the yogi who becomes like him.

title: பூரணக் குகை நெறிச் சமாதி
theme: What becomes of yogis and jnanis when they leave the body depends on how far they have come: the yogi passes through other worlds and returns to finish his yoga, while the faultless jnani rests in silent samadhi, becomes Siva and is not born again. To die to the three impurities while still living is the real death and the real attainment.
structure_note: The chapter climbs a ladder: the yogi's after-death course (1902 to 1904), the Siva-yogi who goes to a higher world and returns (1905), the jnani who does not return (1906), and then the jnani's state described from within: dying to the impurities (1907), acting by grace (1908) and pervading everything (1909).
source_issues: 1903 line 1 is corrupt: 'சமாதிaக' contains a Latin 'a'; probably சமாதிக்கு or சமாதியைக்.

reading: A yogi who leaves the body in the waxing fortnight goes, it seems, by the gods' way into the sun's light, rests in the realm of the fathers and comes to what lies in the moon.
nuance: வளர்பிறை (the waxing fortnight), தேவர் (gods), பானு (sun), பிதிர்பதம் (the fathers' station) and சசி (moon) recall the old teaching of two after-death paths, the gods' way through the sun and the fathers' way through the moon, and of death in the bright fortnight as auspicious. That is the traditional frame, not something the verse spells out; whether these are stages of one journey or alternatives is not clear from the Tamil.

reading: A yogi who dies without reaching a samadhi equal to these goes to a world of refuge, then returns and, practising unbroken great yoga until what remains is spent, reaches the goal by relying on grace.
nuance: The first line is corrupt, so 'without reaching samadhi' is a reconstruction. வியோகி may mean simply the yogi who has departed, or one fallen from yoga. The point that survives is that unfinished yoga is resumed in a later life rather than lost.

reading: One who keeps in this way to the path open to people on earth advances through Siva-yoga by way of the bindu; if he is still imperfect before he becomes a full Siva-yogi, powers come to him and he takes on one body.
nuance: விந்து (bindu), ஊனத்தோர் (the defective) and ஓர்காயம் (one body) are technical and unclear. Tradition takes the last line to mean that attainments short of the goal yield siddhis and a perfected or further body; it may equally mean one more embodiment. The verse places powers below full Siva-yoga.

reading: When a Siva-yogi who has knowledge leaves a worn-out body, he reaches the world of austerity, then comes back and, through the knowledge of Siva-yoga, stands united; such people of merit are honoured by the worlds.
nuance: தவலோகம் and புவலோகம் are taken as names of the upper worlds (tapoloka, bhuvarloka) in the Puranic scheme. 'Comes back' marks this as a step short of the jnani's case in the next verse.

reading: When the faultless jnani who is also a true yogi leaves the body, he rests in a silent samadhi where the self is gone, becomes That, takes no other body, and as one freed without fault does not return.
nuance: தானற ... தானவன் ஆகும் plays on self: the self ends and he becomes He. பரகாயம் usually names the siddhi of entering another's body; here the jnani needs no body at all. The verse sets this against the returns of 1903 to 1905.

reading: If asked what the dead gain, it is to join pure consciousness; those who, still living in the world, have died to the three impurities become Siva and are the true siddhas.
nuance: The verse turns on செத்தார் (the dead) used four times: bodily death in the first line, death to the three மலம் in the last two. சித்து may mean consciousness (chit) or Siva as consciousness, and the second line's syntax is loose. 'Dying while alive' is the plain point.

reading: The strong one who has left birth behind protects, by Hara's grace, a lineage of grace, and for a jnani who asks even for sons the Lord gives form to what he wills.
nuance: Most of this verse is obscure. கருவிட்டு is taken as leaving the womb, that is birth; அருட்குலம் as a lineage or community of grace, perhaps disciples; the last line as the Lord shaping things to the jnani's wish. Whether புதல்வர் means bodily sons or spiritual heirs cannot be settled from the Tamil.

reading: For the Siva-jnani in whose heart grace dwells, Siva is everywhere and the Supreme is present everywhere; having died here, he stands everywhere as the Lord.
nuance: The last line can be read with the jnani as subject (he becomes the all-pervading Lord) or with ஈசன் as subject (the Lord stands everywhere). The third line, on the sky that swallowed the world, is unclear.

title: சமாதிக் கிரியை
theme: The body of a realized jnani must not be burned or left to animals: that is like setting fire to the Lord's temple and brings drought, famine and the fall of kings. It is to be buried seated in a cave-tomb, and the chapter prescribes the tomb's measures, sites, furnishings, offerings and the shrine set over it, which brings grace to the land.
structure_note: Three warnings against burning or exposure (1910 to 1912) and one promise for burial (1913) are followed by a manual of the rite: measures (1914, 1916), sites (1915), lining and seat (1917, 1918), placing the body (1919), offerings and closing (1920, 1921), and the linga or tree set on top with the sixteen services (1922).
source_issues: 1916 line 3 (பொற்பமா ஓசமும்) and 1920 line 3 (குருத்தலம் வைத்துஓர் குழைமுகம் பார்வை) are obscure and may be corrupt.
1919 line 3: போதறு கண்ணமும் may be a corruption of சுண்ணம் (powder), which appears in 1917.

reading: If the body of a boundless jnani is burned, the whole land burns with fever; if dogs and jackals feed on it, strife comes and the world itself becomes food for dogs and jackals.
nuance: The punishment mirrors the wrong: fire for fire, dogs and jackals for dogs and jackals. நுண்செரு, read here as strife, is an unusual word.

reading: If fire touches the body of a jnani beyond reckoning, it is as if the Lord's own temple were set alight; rain fails, the world falls into famine and countless kings lose their kingdoms.
nuance: அண்ணல்தம் கோயில் makes the jnani's body the Lord's temple, a claim Tirumular makes of the body generally elsewhere. The harm is to the whole land and its rulers, not only to those who burn the body.

reading: Burying such people is an act of merit; heaping fire on them brings ruin to the land, letting the body decay in the open disgraces it, and the whole world is thrown into confusion by the spreading fire.
nuance: The third line, மண்ணில் அழியில் அலங்கார பங்கமாம், is taken as decay on open ground spoiling the body's dignity, but it could also mean harm to the land's order. The verse names burial as புண்ணியம், merit, and not just as the lesser evil.

reading: When the boundless jnani has reached grace, if that body is kept in a cave-tomb, fine kings and all who live on the ancient earth receive grace and joy without end.
nuance: This is the reverse of 1910 to 1912: where burning harms land and kings, the kept body blesses them. குகை, cave, is the chapter's word for the tomb.

reading: The pit is dug a good nine spans deep, its surround measured at five spans, the inner cave made triangular at three spans; in this birth-ending cave the body sits in the lotus posture.
nuance: The measures nine, five and three are clear, but what குவைமிகு சூழ (the surround) refers to is not. பவமறு (ending birth) gives the tomb a part in the jnani's release, or marks it as fit for one already released.

reading: One's own house, a hall, a tank bank, the land between rivers, a flower grove, good ground in a town, a forest beyond thought and a high mountain slope are the places fit for the cave-tomb.
nuance: The list runs from the household to the wilderness, so the tomb is not confined to remote or sacred ground.

reading: The verse gives further proportions for the cave: a fourfold enclosure, a base of five parts and of nine set true, and an arrangement three by three, done exactly by those who perform the rite.
nuance: பஞ்சாங்க பாதம், நவபாதம் and பொற்பமா ஓசமும் are obscure, and the arithmetic cannot be fixed from the Tamil. Only the stress on exact measure is clear.

reading: Five metals and nine gems are spread out abundantly, a seat placed over them, munja grass laid on it and white ash on that, and a pouch of fine gold powder may also be set there.
nuance: பஞ்ச லோகம் and நவமணி are the standard five metals and nine gems of temple consecration, which treats the tomb like a shrine.

reading: With the fourfold enclosure laid in the cave, put on it a garland dripping honey, sandal paste, musk, clear sandal, civet and rose water, and offer bright incense gladly.
The body is dusted with sacred ash and clothed, set on the seat, adorned with fragrant powder, seated on top, and then things are spread over it.
nuance: போதறு கண்ணமும் is unclear: perhaps powder free of buds, or a corrupt form of சுண்ணம். What is spread in the last line, flowers or cloth, is not said.

reading: After spreading, the four sides are filled in, fried vegetables, cooked rice and tender coconut set down, and after a further act the cover above is closed.
nuance: குருத்தலம் வைத்துஓர் குழைமுகம் பார்வை தரித்தபின் is obscure: it may refer to a guru's place, a face with ear-rings or a ritual gaze. The food offerings echo those made to a deity.

reading: White ash, powder, many flowers, darbha grass and bilva are strewn over it, it is bathed with water of the feet, and the ground above is laid out three by three.
nuance: பாத உதகம் is usually water that has washed a holy person's or deity's feet; whose feet is not said. The three-by-three ground repeats 1916.

reading: On the platform above, install one of two, a peepal tree or a Siva linga, with the shrine facing north or east, and perform with love the sixteen services.
nuance: அரசு here is the peepal tree, not kingship. சோடச உபசாரம் is the standard sixteenfold worship of a deity, so the tomb becomes a temple.

title: விந்துற்பனம்
theme: Bindu is both the cosmic seed, from which with nada the tattvas, the powers of speech and the worlds unfold as Mahamaya, and the bodily seed, distilled from food through the seven bodily elements. The Lord stands in the seed as a sprout in its seed; those who do not know how bindu is lost, or how to guard it, perish with the perishing body.
structure_note: The chapter moves from bindu as cosmic source (1923 to 1930), through the seed and sprout image for the Lord in the world (1931, 1932), to bindu in the body: its making from food (1933, 1934), its becoming mind (1935) and its loss (1936).
source_issues: 1924: the numbers (25, 6, two twos) do not obviously total the stated 36; the grouping or a number may be lost.
1923 line 4 (கலைவை கரியே) and 1931 line 3 (மதுவித்திலே மலர் அன்னம்) are obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: From bindu as it arises come kundalini and, in order, the nine bindu-born powers, the gods beginning with Brahma, the shaktis, the instruments, the kalas and speech.
nuance: குடில் (kutila, the curved one), வயிந்தவம் (baindava, born of bindu), கரணம் and கலை are technical terms of Saiva cosmology, and கலைவை கரியே is taken as கலை, வைகரி (the spoken level of speech). The list order is the tradition's and the verse is compressed.

reading: The distinctions of bindu give twenty-five, those of nada six, and the rest come in twos and twos; together they make the thirty-six tattvas.
nuance: ஐ ஐந்தும் (five fives), ஆறும் (six) and ஈர்இரண்டில் (two twos) do not simply add to ஆறுஆறு (six sixes, 36) as read here; the grouping may be different, or a number may have dropped. The standard Siddhanta count is 36 tattvas.

reading: All the distinctions that arise rest above the supreme bindu; Mahamaya, the goddess of speech, the supreme power and kundalini with kutila, these four shine within bindu.
nuance: மாமாயை, வாகேசி, தற்பரை and குண்டலி are traditionally taken as names of bindu or of powers in it. Whether குடிலை is a fifth name or one with குண்டலி is unclear.

reading: The kalas beginning with nivritti, the letters A and U and M with bindu within M, and the spotless end of nada reached in the eye extend through the mind and its faculties to their end.
nuance: அகர, உகாரம், மகாரம் with விந்து and நாதாந்தம் are the parts of the syllable Om as analysed in mantra theory. கண்ணினுள் (in the eye) and மனாதியுள் அந்தமும் are obscure.

reading: As end and beginning, the Supreme who pervades all is the seed, the root of cause and effect, and performs the five acts.
nuance: வீயம் (seed, bija) and கந்தம் (root, bulb) can be read of the Lord or of bindu as his instrument; the verse runs them together. ஐங்கருமம் are traditionally creation, preservation, dissolution, concealment and grace.

reading: By the power of bindu, which is the seed, the undivided and the cosmos spread out; when the five elements of the body arise in maya as effect, bindu is both inside and outside.
nuance: அகண்டம் (the undivided) and காரிய மாயை (maya as effect) are technical. The verse links cosmic and bodily bindu, which the chapter later treats as one.

reading: Bindu enters and shines through everything within and without; its colour is white and nada's red, and joined with Shakti and Siva it has power over life and grants release.
nuance: White bindu and red nada are traditionally matched with Siva and Shakti and, in the body, with semen and female blood. சிவபாதம் and ஆயுள் may also be taken as Siva's feet and length of life.

reading: This bindu, flawless like the Supreme, stays in its effects as thread stays in cloth and clay in a pot, and as cause and effect of the kalas and the rest becomes all the worlds: it is Mahamaya.
nuance: படம், கடம் (cloth, pot) are the classic examples of a material cause present in its effect. The verse makes bindu the material cause of the worlds, distinct from the Supreme it resembles.

reading: Nandi stands in that seed and is sweet there, but people do not perceive how he is in this seed; the holy one stands in the seed common to all, as flower and swan in the seed of honey.
nuance: The play on வித்து (seed) runs through every line. மதுவித்திலே மலர் அன்னம் அதாகி is obscure: மலர் and அன்னம் may be the lotus and swan of Brahma, or அன்னம் may mean food. The plain sense is that the Lord is in the seed of things unseen.

reading: There is no sprout without the seed, no way for the sprout to appear except from the seed, and seed and sprout exist only together; those who see this see Hara's way.
nuance: The verse does not say what seed and sprout stand for. They are commonly taken as Siva and the world, or Siva and Shakti: cause and effect inseparable. Placed here, it may also bear on bodily bindu and the body.

reading: Food eaten divides into three parts, the body's, the mind's and the waste that leaves; the body's and the mind's parts join, and what was there before becomes chyle.
nuance: The threefold division of food into body, mind and waste is an old physiological teaching. இருந்தன முன்னாள் is unclear: perhaps what lay in the stomach the day before.

reading: Of the seven bodily elements beginning with chyle, each forming in three days, a rare drop of bindu arises like dew on a single blade of grass, and over seven threes of days the gathered bindu grows in the body.
nuance: ஏழ் மூன்றின் is read as seven times three, twenty-one days. The dew on a grass blade marks smallness and rarity. Sengalvaraya notes a parallel in Tiruppugazh 862, where a drop like dew on a grass tip grows into a body.

reading: Within three days it mingles in the body and the kala-bindu becomes one's own mind; for those who hold steady it is not lost, but those who follow illusion perish with their mind.
nuance: கலாவிந்து and நேயத்தே நின்றோர் (those who stand in love, or in what is fitting) are unclear. The claim that bindu becomes mind ties bodily continence to mental steadiness, as tradition reads it.

reading: People do not know how much bindu is being lost, nor how to guard within themselves what is leaving; worn out in a perishing body, they perish, knowing the perishing yet not stopping it.
nuance: அழி (perish) opens three lines and the last, so the verse sounds what it describes. அறிந்தொழியாரே can mean 'they do not know and desist' or 'they do not stop though they know'. Unlike the poets who answer the body's perishing by turning from it, Tirumular calls for guarding it.

title: விந்து ஜயம் - போக சரவோட்டம்
theme: Conquest of bindu (விந்து ஜயம்) and the practice of union governed by the breath (போக சரவோட்டம்): the yogi turns desire back to the root and, raising the inner fire, drinks the nectar of the moon instead of losing bindu; where union with a woman happens, it is timed by the lunar days and the breath and held so that bindu is not spilled. Kept bindu gives breath, strength, siddhi and the state of Sivoham.
structure_note: Turning from women and the need for grace (1937, 1938); the rite of union, its days, breath and conception (1939 to 1945); the seed and its sower (1946, 1947); bindu kept, burnt upward and turned to nectar (1948 to 1966, with 1953 on seeing women as death and 1955, 1960, 1961 on union without loss); the teaching, mantra and Sivoham (1967 to 1971); the place of knowing and the elements in the body (1972 to 1974).
source_issues: 1970: line 4 repeats the end of line 3 (அப் பொல்லா வினையை) and the verse has no main verb; the closing line seems lost.
1939, 1940: the day counts (மேல்பனி மூன்றிரண்டு, ஆறுஐந்து பன்னொன்றும்) are obscure and may be corrupt.
1946 line 4 (மத்தில் இருந்ததோர் மாங்கனி) and all of 1972 are obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: The yogi who leaves without looking at the women he sees, kindles a fire so the reflecting heart melts, lays waste the eye's desire and joins it at the root, is the Siva-yogi.
nuance: பார்க்கின்ற opens lines 1 and 3: the women seen and the eye that sees. மூலத்தே சேர்க்கின்ற is taken as turning the force of desire back to the muladhara, the root centre, rather than suppressing it; the verse does not name what is joined.

reading: Without grace Siva-yoga does not stay; one who harbours lust and its kin lives in fear; if the will to rule stays, the body is ruined, and in the flesh, if the life is not tended among these, it dies.
nuance: தானே opens three lines. அதிகாரம் may be worldly power, the ego's claim to command, or in Siddhanta the stage of the soul's bondage; சடம் is the inert body. The verse puts grace before technique in a chapter mostly of technique.

reading: If they wish to go into a woman's power, then of the two fortnights, in the waxing one, eight days are for pleasure; and in the waning one it is the sixth from the first day.
nuance: மாயாள் may simply be 'the woman' or carry the sense of maya, the one who deludes. மேல்பனி மூன்றிரண்டு and the day counts are obscure; the verse fixes lunar days for union, as in the traditional rules for conception, but the exact days cannot be fixed from the text.

reading: Apart from the sixth, fifth and eleventh, those who want a love other than the common way should, after the woman's flowering, take the twenty-one days in which it rises, and do it at the time when the sixth rises highest.
nuance: பூவரில் is taken as the woman's menses. சகமார்க்கம் (the common way) and the numbers are obscure; the verse continues 1939's calendar.

reading: When it is done, the holy fourth muhurta, the time when the kala shoots, when the moon and sun breaths weaken, run there and act by the treatise's good way; leaving right and left, release.
nuance: இந்து பருதிகால் are the moon and sun breaths, the left and right channels. வலம் இடம் தீர்ந்து (leaving right and left) is taken as the breath moving in the central channel. What is released (விடுக்க) is not said; the next verses suggest it is not bindu itself.

reading: Release, and see: one who stays unshaken as the senses strain, as the five-times-five draw near, letting go all clinging to the woman of desire, holding the fierce breath and the faculties to the mind.
nuance: ஐஐந்து may be the twenty-five tattvas or five times the five senses. கடுங்கால் (fierce wind) is taken as the breath held hard. The verse asks for detachment in the very act, not abstention from it.

reading: With words like 'nature I have taken, goodness, tender one, form of old, coral-lipped, firm-breasted', when the moment of close release comes, see the faculty you have seen go within, then release.
nuance: The first lines are a lover's endearments. கண்ட கரணம் உட் செல்ல (the faculty seen going within) is taken as the breath or the bindu drawn inward before release; the sense is that the yogi keeps the inner turning even at the climax.

reading: After release, in the rules of conception, consider the times that came into play and look to the life span bound, the day of death, low qualities and high, thinking 'this is the way it went'.
nuance: The verse seems to say that the time of union fixes the child's length of life, death day and character, as in the astrological lore of conception. சீர்ப்பட்ட நெறி may be 'the proper way' or 'the way it turned out'.

reading: Having looked to this, free of the world's spread and gaining form, keeping away from the woman, and even if one parts and keeps apart for two months after union, in later days of age all will remain.
nuance: The verse is obscure. உருப்பெற்று may mean gaining a firm body. One reading: restraint after union keeps strength into old age. Another: the effects of the union remain even if one later abstains.

reading: There is no harvest for the high except for those who sow, no knowledge for the eminent except for those who sow; if they come to know the seed within the seed, it is a mango in the churning-stick.
nuance: வித்து (seed) is bindu, so 'those who sow' may be those who give bindu its proper end, or those who plant it upward in yoga. வித்தினில் வித்து (the seed in the seed) is the Lord, as in 1931. மத்தில் இருந்ததோர் மாங்கனி is obscure; it may mean something sweet hidden in an unlikely place.

reading: In thought are letters, life span and everything; the Lord is in thought with the womb and the life; thought becomes seed, cause and effect; and when thought is cut off, all these are imagination.
nuance: கருத்து (thought, intention) puns on கரு (womb, embryo) in every line. The last line makes the world of seed and birth a construct of thought, which ends when thought ends; this is a reading, not the only one.

reading: When bindu stays unspent, there stay the undying breath, great strength, power, unfailing intellect, tapas, japa and silence; and when bindu is dried up within, undying siddhi comes.
nuance: ஒழியாத and அழியா alternate down the lines. விந்து வற்றிலே may mean 'when bindu is dried up', burnt within as 1949 describes, not 'when it runs dry' by loss; the first reading fits the chapter.

reading: To dry it, kindling the fire, turning it back and raising it, plugging the whirling fire and reaching the light, those who drink, step by step, the nectar of the full moon are the Siva-yogis.
nuance: The fire at the root is raised (மறித்தேற்றி), the whirl (சுழி) is sealed, and the moon at the head yields nectar: the standard sequence of Tirumular's kundalini yoga as tradition reads it.

reading: Yogi, jnani, excellent siddha, the yogi who is lord of jnana, and one who, though passion comes, drinks the nectar in due order: such is the noble one whose bindu does not perish.
nuance: மோகம் உறினும் (even if passion arises) includes the householder who unites but keeps bindu by method, alongside the yogi and the jnani.

reading: With the Lord as the body, the fire-bindu and the breath-bindu that dies in the earth, bound and mixed in the fire with the eye and burnt, become nectar when eaten and knowledge to the yogi.
nuance: The two bindus are named again in 1965 and 1966 as food and breath. மண்ணிடை மாய்க்கும் may mean the breath that dies in the earth element at the root, or the bindu lost on the ground; கண்ணும் is unclear.

reading: Because they perish without knowing, daily they are ruined through the senses and lament; as knowledge, staying gathered in waking so as to reach the beyond, union will come.
nuance: நனவில் அதீதம் (the beyond-state in waking) is the Siddhanta turiyatita reached while awake. வாயுமே may be the breath or the verb 'it will be attained'; both are possible.

reading: If one thinks of women as Death come to kill, the desire that grew from love falls away; there is no dying even in a hundred crore years, and within the light comes the time free of fault.
nuance: The verse prescribes a way of seeing, not a judgment on women as such: the meditation turns desire off. Sengalvaraya notes a Tiruppugazh parallel where young women's charms take lives as Death does.

reading: The one who has mastered bindu, see, has passed beyond time; the one who wasted bindu passed through time and perished; those who waste bindu through the ages do not know the mingling that came by the breath.
nuance: செற்றவன் means both 'one who subdued' and 'one who destroyed'; the verse uses the same word for the yogi and the waster, and the reading depends on the contrast. காரிகை (woman) and காலின்கண் (by the breath, or at the feet) are unclear.

reading: If you want love's good on the day before union, first clear the woman's belly of waste, cold and bile by fitting remedies, and then embrace.
nuance: A medical prescription in the humoral terms of Siddha medicine: சீதம் (phlegm, cold) and பித்தம் (bile). Tirumular addresses the man and treats the woman's health as part of the rite.

reading: Driving bindu and nada, rising to the upper place, with the rod along the marked path, drinking the nectar that is milk, if you hold on without clinging, the pride of delusion dies, and that bindu too.
nuance: கோல் (rod) is taken as the spine or the central channel. பற்றறப் பற்றினால் (holding without holding) is a paradox. The last line can also mean that bindu dies to its ordinary course.

reading: Bindu's growth, the full fruit of that growth, its end and loss, the increase that comes by restraint, its gladdening loss and its division by nada: to those who grasp these, bindu becomes victory.
nuance: The verse gives the chapter's title term சயம் (victory) its sense: bindu is conquered by knowing its whole course, not only by holding it. நந்திய நாசம் (a gladdening loss) is unclear.

reading: Bindu, the seed in the root centre, knowing its way by the fire there, raising the endless sun above the throat, becomes cool nectar when it reaches the moon.
nuance: வீசம் is bija, seed. பானு (sun) and சந்திரன் (moon) are the hot and cool poles of the yogic body, and the cool nectar is the moon's. அதிகண்டம் is taken as above the throat.

reading: When bindu, the moon of nectar, is consumed, the stream of nectar runs like fire; since this is the Siva-yoga of nectar, siddhi follows, and the jackfruit grove of nectar comes to the yogi.
nuance: அமுதம் opens every line. அங்கியின் மான (like fire, or the fire's measure) is unclear. பலாவனம் (jackfruit grove) is an image of abundant sweetness.

reading: Knowing the yoga by which bindu does not leave, even when two bodies mingle, the pleasure that does not go there is Siva's pleasure, the true pleasure of the enjoyer; fools embrace women but not so that infatuation dies.
nuance: சிவபோகம் (Siva's enjoyment) is the verse's claim: union in which bindu is kept is itself a spiritual bliss. The last line is compressed; it may also be read 'fools do not embrace with infatuation ended'.

reading: Those joined in yoga, though they turn to women, do not release bindu out of love; those who take hold of women's craving for life waste away, though they seem lovers there, their love a matter of juice.
nuance: உயிராசை (craving of life) may be the woman's desire or the man's lust for her. சாற்றிலே (in the juice) is unclear; it may be the bodily fluids, or a pun on சாற்று (declare).

reading: The bindu spoken of becomes victory by Shakti: kindling the fire raised at the root, with nada through the middle channel that does not run in four directions, holding it, drinking the nectar, one becomes the seed.
nuance: நடுநாடி is the central channel. The last word may be read அருந்த வித்தாம் (drinking it becomes seed) or அருந்தவம் (rare tapas); both fit.

reading: Bindu and nada above, the fire at the root: when the fire that came settles in every hair-root, thought changes and Sivam becomes the self, and bindu dies into seed in the true body.
nuance: மயிர்க்கால் தோறும் (in every hair-root) pictures the fire pervading the whole body. சிவம் அகமாக may be 'Sivam as the self' or 'Sivam within'. மெய்க்காயம் (true body) is taken as the body made imperishable.

reading: One who pounds the seed and eats it does not know the harvest; one who, without pounding it, roasts the seed and eats is no different from him in the end; one who, not pounding and eating, sowed the seed is the other.
nuance: A riddle on வித்து. Plainly: to eat the seed is to lose the crop. Symbolically, spending bindu in pleasure or burning it without method both waste it, while the sower turns it to growth. Which practice each figure stands for cannot be fixed.

reading: Seeing how bindu is contained in food, turning back the bindu that is the abiding breath, releasing the lightning-like bindu into the end of nada, the coloured holy bindu dies in the body.
nuance: அன்னம் may mean food or the swan (the breath, hamsa); with பிராணன் it gives the two bindus of 1966. நாதாந்தம் is the end of nada. 'Dies in the body' is taken as being absorbed, not lost.

reading: For those who know the two bindus called food and breath, take them in and can practise, a golden form appears with the eight siddhis, and all such stand beyond destruction.
nuance: சொன்னமாம் உரு (a golden form) is the perfected body of the siddhas. எண்சித்தி are the eight great powers. As in 1965, அன்னம் may be food or the hamsa breath.

reading: The letter Si standing as the breath one thinks on, the letter Ma joining, these one with the three, go to Parashakti; to tell how to join with bindu's victory is the teaching.
nuance: சிகாரம் and மகாரம் are letters of the five-syllable mantra. ஒருமூன்றோடு ஒன்ற (one with the three) may be the three remaining letters or the three bodies. உபதேசம் is the guru's teaching.

reading: It is itself the teaching, and there is nothing apart from it; when the fourteen that came from bindu, high as the sky, subside like deer, then intellect and the nature of the Siva-state come.
nuance: பதினான்கு (fourteen) may be the fourteen worlds or the fourteen instruments (ten senses and four inner faculties). மானேர் (like deer) is unclear.

reading: As bindu and nada bore fruit, these many lives came forth; for all abiding lives the end and the beginning, and the mantras too, are that; when bindu is contained, Sivoham grows.
nuance: சிவோகம் (I am Siva) is the experience of identity with Siva. The verse joins the cosmic bindu that brings forth lives (1923) to the bodily bindu whose containment brings Sivoham.

reading: The way of roasting, the way of weighing the mind's victory, the way of sticking to that long mountain and sealing it, and the way of cutting that evil karma.
nuance: Line 4 repeats the end of line 3 and the verse has no main verb, so the conclusion is lost. வறுக்கின்ற (roasting) echoes 1964's roasted seed; நீள்வரை (the long mountain) may be the spine.

reading: If bindu and nada join together and meet the moon, the nectar of the beautiful sky will spring there, and the mantra uttered there becomes the oblation.
nuance: சுந்தர வானம் (the beautiful sky) is taken as the space in the head. The last line turns the inner act into the fire rite: mantra and oblation happen within.

reading: Mind with its essence, mind and ear: those of one kind rise and agree in the channel; the word rising in the mind is speech, and if one seeks that desire, it is heavy juice.
nuance: The verse is obscure. It may trace sound from mind to speech, and then say that desire turns this power into gross fluid (இரதம்).

reading: They do not know the place where sound, the mind of sound and the mind's thought agree and know; for those who know truly the place where knowing happens, that very place is the Father's abode.
nuance: அத்தன் (Father) is the Lord. The verse places the Lord at the point where knowing itself takes place, not in an outer object of knowledge.

reading: From chest to feet is earth, at the navel water, below the breast fire, below the hands above the dark mountain air, and the beauty mingled above is space.
nuance: The five elements are placed in regions of the body. The boundaries (உரம் அடி, கருமலை, கைக்கீழ்) are not clear, and the order of regions in the verse may be disturbed.

title: ஆதித்த நிலை - அண்டாதித்தன்
theme: The sun of the cosmos (அண்டாதித்தன்): the sun and the gods circle Meru in worship of the Lord's feet, and the Lord himself stands as the sun, the source of all lives, figured in a diagram of circles and petals; the way the sun travels beneath the earth is hidden from all but those who know.
structure_note: Praise of the sun as worshipper and as the Lord (1975 to 1978), the sun's diagram of triangles, circles and petals (1979, 1980), and the hidden way of the sun beneath the earth (1981 to 1984). The next chapter turns to the sun in the body.
source_issues: 1979: வவைய is probably a misprint, perhaps for வளைய.
1980 line 3 (கேத முறுங்கேணி) is obscure and may be corrupt.
1983: line 1 (மண்ணை இடந்துஅதின் கீழொடும்) seems a foot short.

reading: The reason the gods, the red-rayed sun first among them, circle cloud-topped Meru is their tapas of bowing to the twin feet of the Lord, light of all lights, as their own light.
nuance: The sun's daily round of Meru, an astronomical fact in Puranic cosmology, is read as circumambulation in worship. எஞ்சுடர் may be 'all lights' or 'the light that remains'; either way the sun's light is borrowed from the Lord's.

reading: The sun, the holy Lord who stands as refuge for all lives, rising so that the seven worlds flourish without strife, is the origin of all lives.
nuance: பகலவன் மாலவன் may name the sun and Vishnu side by side, or call the sun 'the great one'. The verse does not say plainly whether the புண்ணிய நாதன் is the sun or the Lord who stands as the sun; the chapter's drift favours the second.

reading: The sun, with love and a thousand names, stands as the radiant light within the light; whatever the Vedic priests ask and the gods say, this is how love ripens toward the First One.
nuance: ஆயிர நாமமும் (a thousand names) recalls the hymns of a thousand names. The last two lines can be read as 'whatever they ask, it is love that ripens', setting love above ritual request, but the syntax is loose.

reading: He himself stands to the world as its principle, as the woman, as Shambhu, and as the cool light.
nuance: தானே opens every line. தையல் (the woman) is Shakti and சம்பு is Siva, so the one who stands as the sun holds both. தண்சுடர் (cool light) is the moon, a surprise in a sun chapter: the Lord is both lights.

reading: Triangle, circle, hexagon, two balanced circles, the pure eight, and in the outer circle sixteen petals: the sun rose in this distinct order.
nuance: The verse describes a diagram (yantra) for the sun, or the centres of the body in yogic reading. வவைய is probably a misprint, perhaps for வளைய; துலை and மலைவுற்று are unclear.

reading: Within the sun, in the triangle, the good sun shines as four; the sun is in the eight; and in the light's spreading it is sixteen.
nuance: The numbers continue 1979's diagram and are often taken as the sun's kalas. கேத முறுங்கேணி is obscure: கேணி (well) and கேதம் (grief) give no clear sense here.

reading: With the sun the earth went dark; the four that were divided babbled and passed away; you do not see the Vedic truth that stands within the light and beats like a drum.
nuance: பேதித்த நாலும் may be the four Vedas, the four religions or the four states; துடியிடை (drum-waisted) is also an epithet of a woman. The plain sense is a reproach: the truth is in the light, and talk misses it.

reading: The way the sun comes beneath the earth is a rare thing no one can see; the one who rises between water and fire is the sun beyond everyone's reach.
nuance: Plainly the sun's passage under the earth at night. Symbolically the earth, water and fire are taken as centres of the body, so the hidden sun is the inner light rising in yoga. Both readings stand.

reading: Cleaving the earth and what is below it, cleaving the sky and making space, cleaving the eye and giving bliss, he stood suited to the reckoned day.
nuance: இடந்து (cleaving, digging through) repeats. கிழமை may be the day of the week, named after the sun, or 'what is rightfully his'. Line 1 is a foot short.

reading: No one knows the way the sun comes cleaving the earth; those of the rare final texts say it circles the holy mountain where the brave one sits; those who knew the town knew and remained.
nuance: அருங்கடை நூலவர் (those of the rare final books) may be Vedantins or Agama teachers. The mountain is Meru, or in yogic reading the head. ஊர் (the town) may be the Lord's abode or the body.

title: பிண்டாதித்தன்
theme: The sun in the body (பிண்டாதித்தன்): when the malams are destroyed and the inner current runs up the channel, a wide light shines; those who find where that sun settles know themselves and fall silent, and the poet's love melts toward those who know where it lies hidden.
source_issues: 1985: மலங்கன் is likely a misprint for மலங்கள்.
1986: the line break falls inside ஆதித்தனோடே, so line 3 runs long and line 4 is short.

reading: Standing, sitting, lying and walking, he kept within the thought of Nandi; when the malams are destroyed and the current runs up the channel, the wide light is seen shining in victory.
nuance: The four postures say the practice is constant, not set to a seat. கன்றாய is unclear (become a calf, or worn); மலங்கன் is likely மலங்கள். குழல்வழி (the tube's way) is traditionally the central channel, and the spreading light the inner sun the chapter is named for.

reading: Those who have found the place where the sun runs and settles and can practise it know themselves; all the babble the divided world utters, they put to rest with that sun.
nuance: ஆதித்தன் ஓடி அடங்கும் இடம் is taken as the point where the solar breath (the right channel) comes to rest. The last line can also mean that the babblers themselves subside with the setting sun, that is, die.

reading: No one knows the ford where it lies plugged after drawing out, going forth and circling the world; for those who know that ford, my inmost love lies melting.
nuance: The subject is not named: in this chapter it is the inner sun, and many take it as the breath, which goes out, ranges and is then locked in (சொருகி). உருகிக் கிடக்கும் echoes சொருகிக் கிடக்கும்: the light lies locked, the poet's love lies melted, for those who know.

title: மன ஆதித்தன்
theme: The sun of the mind (மன ஆதித்தன்): sun, moon and fire are taken as the lights and breaths within. When the two rays become one the life-breath stops wandering and the clear-minded become Siva; beyond these lights shines one that the bounded cannot perceive, and without the First One's grace there is only darkness.
source_issues: 1988 line 1: மின்பனி may be மின் பனி (glittering dew) or a corruption; the sense of சோரும் (droops, melts) is clear.
