reading: As the glittering dew melts before the darting rays of the sun and the moon shines facing it, my life-breath, moving within the spreading rays, will stop wandering once it becomes a single ray.
nuance: Sun and moon are traditionally the right and left breaths (pingala and ida), and the 'single ray' their union in the central channel. ஆவி may be breath or life; உலாஅது is 'will not roam'. A plain reading of dawn and moonlight also stands, but the last two lines push toward the yogic one.

reading: Worship when moon and sun come together, in the way the moon comes to meet the sun that went before; those whose minds grow clear in the place of the two become Siva.
nuance: பானு (sun) and இந்து (moon) may be the new-moon conjunction or, as tradition takes it, the two breaths meeting. உபய நிலம் ('the ground of both') is commonly placed between the brows or in the central channel; the verse does not say where.

reading: Sun, fire and moon come with their kalas, and between the kalas, they say, there are four; know that when the sun joins fire and moon, that is the fullness.
nuance: அருக்கன் அனல் மதி are the three lights, traditionally matched with three breaths or regions of the body. What the 'four' between the kalas are is not stated. பூரணை is the full moon and, figuratively, fullness or completion.

reading: That light which moves beyond the two spheres is an awareness that those of a single sphere cannot perceive; it stands shining through the great sphere, and only those fit to approach it are fit to know it.
nuance: அண்டம் is the cosmic egg or world-sphere; ஈர் அண்டம், ஓர் அண்டம் and பேர் அண்டம் are not explained and may be read cosmically or of regions in the body. The last line plays on அண்டு (approach) and அண்டம் (sphere).

reading: Dwelling in the nine it circles the world, yet no one knows the nature of the Lord in the nine; those who dwelt in it before but lack the First One's grace are without bliss and stand surrounded by darkness.
nuance: ஒன்பது is unexplained: the nine planets that circle the world fit the chapter's suns and moons, and the body's nine gates are another traditional reading. The contrast between dwelling in it and having grace is the clear point.

title: ஞானாதித்தன்
theme: The sun of knowledge (ஞானாதித்தன்): bindu and nada dawn within the heart as the source of the kalas and of speech, and the Lord is a light beyond sun, moon and fire, travelling through all the worlds, shining at centres in the body, and removing a darkness the outer lights cannot.
structure_note: Two verses on bindu and nada as an inner dawn (1993, 1994), one on the Lord's titles (1995), then verses on his light within (1996 to 2000).

reading: Bindu spread into two, lower and higher; the lower became the higher nada, and with the higher kala and the rest set within them they rise in the heart like the dawn.
nuance: அபரம், பரம் (lower, higher) and பரநாதம் are terms of Siddhanta cosmology. அருணோதயம் (sunrise) gives the chapter its sun: the unfolding of bindu is pictured as an inner dawn.

reading: The sound that rises at that inner dawn is the working of clear higher nada, so the bounteous higher bindu and the speech that begins with vaikhari are one rising for the five kalas.
nuance: வைகரி is the spoken level of speech, traditionally the last of four (with madhyama, pashyanti and sukshma). ஐங்கலை are taken as the five kalas beginning with nivritti. The verse ties sound and speech back to one source.

reading: The celestials say he is the Lord of the gods who rises in the ten directions, who of old was called Lord of the three, the Lord of the four who goes on teaching from the centre, the Lord who abides.
nuance: மூவர் are traditionally Brahma, Vishnu and Rudra, and நால்வர் the four sages taught by Siva as Dakshinamurti; நடுவாய் உரையாநிற்கும் may refer to that teaching. Neither identification is in the verse.

reading: My father, without falsehood and true, lord of the worlds: moon, fire and sun remove the black darkness, but Nandi, holy one who removes the darkness that deeds make, rose mingled in me so that the darkness close at hand left.
nuance: The contrast is between outer lights and the inner one. செய்யிருள் (darkness of deeds, or dense darkness) and கையிருள் (darkness at hand, or within one's grasp) are both open; tradition takes the inner darkness as the soul's impurity.

reading: Lighting the single flame so that the wavering darkness leaves, the juice of the rare fruit above comes near; and that is also the form of the great flame the Lord of Kailash, who stands as a ripened flame, took on above.
nuance: மேலை அருங்கனி ஊறல் (the juice of the rare fruit above) is commonly read as the nectar said to flow from the head in yoga, and கயிலை as the crown of the head. அனித்திடும் is obscure. The verse is compressed and the reading is a guess at its order.

reading: The great light that fills as true knowledge goes to and returns from the worlds without strife, and becomes the light of a quarter no chariot knows; who knows this? It is the Lord.
nuance: தேரறியாத may be 'that no chariot knows', the sun's chariot not reaching it, so a light beyond the sun; or 'that inquiry cannot know', from தேர் (to examine). Both readings stand.

reading: The sun that blossoms within the circle becomes the light of rays within the region; going out it travels to all eight directions, and for those who know rightly it stays in its place.
nuance: மண்டலம் and கண்டிதம் are probably regions of the yogic body (கண்டம் may be the throat), but the verse does not fix them. The contrast is between the light going out everywhere and standing still for the one who knows.

reading: They perceived the flame that shines in five places, the navel, the nose, the eyes, their middle and the crown, as the three: the Lord of the gods, Tirumal and Brahma.
nuance: The five places are centres of contemplation; நாசி நயன நடுவு may be one place, between nose and eyes, and தூபி the crown of the head. Who perceives (the gods, or the sages) is not clear in the verse.

title: சிவாதித்தன்
theme: Siva as the sun (சிவாதித்தன்): his light of knowledge ends the darkness of bond and ignorance; he is in every body like the sun reflected in many pots, yet not confined by them; and he himself is the three lights, the gods, body and soul, and the elements.
source_issues: 2004 line 4 (ஐவர்க்கு இடம்இடை ஆறங்கம்) is obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: The darkness of bond and the ignorance that stood against me vanished through the supreme light of Siva which is knowledge, as dense darkness leaves at the dawn where two lights become one.
nuance: ஒன்றும் இருசுடர் ('the two lights that join') may be sun and moon at dawn or, as in chapter 144, the two breaths united. The main claim, that knowledge as Siva's light ends bond and ignorance, is plain.

reading: When the sun appears in pot after pot, closing them does not shut him in; the poison-throated Lord who stands as though confined in the body he dwells in is of the same kind.
nuance: The sun reflected in water-filled pots is a classic image for one presence in many bodies. Here the point is that Siva is in each body without being held by it; விடங்கொண்ட கண்டன் is Siva who swallowed the poison.

reading: He himself is the spreading light that stands as the three lights in one; he himself establishes things, standing as Brahma and Vishnu; he himself stands not other than body and soul; he himself is open space, light and darkness.
nuance: The fourfold தானே insists on one agent behind all. உடலுயிர் வேறன்றி ('not other than body and soul') states Siva's presence in them; how far it means identity is left open.

reading: The divine lights, fire, sun and moon, the earth, water, fire, wind and sky, and the many souls the great Lord of the Saivas bears: these are the six limbs and the place, in between, for the five.
nuance: The first three lines name Siva's traditional eight forms (the five elements, sun, moon and the soul), though fire is named twice. The last line, ஐவர்க்கு இடம் இடை ஆறங்கம், is obscure: ஐவர் may be the five deities and ஆறங்கம் six limbs (of the Veda, or six paths).

title: பசு இலக்கணம்
theme: The marks of the soul (பசு இலக்கணம்), given through the swan (அன்னம்): the Lord is known within as an unfading lamp, and soul and Lord are two swans that never part; the swan that holds itself a separate one does not reach its gain.
structure_note: The title is about the soul, but the two verses speak of the swan; the swan (hamsa) as an image of the soul is the link.

reading: The One who is perceived as far as one contemplates him, the Supreme whom the recited Vedas study, the unfading lamp within me: I came to know him as of the nature of the swan.
nuance: அன்ன மயம் may be 'of the swan' (hamsa, the soul and the breath in yogic usage) or 'made of food' (annamaya, the body's sheath). The next verse's swans favour the first; the second would mean he is known in the body.

reading: There are two swans on the river bank; the two keep close and never leave each other; if a swan holds that its state is a single one apart, that deluded, separated swan will not reach the gain.
nuance: The two swans are commonly taken as the soul and the Lord, like the two birds on one tree of the Upanishads; they may also be read as the two breaths. பின்ன மட அன்னம் is the swan that is foolishly divided off, or that thinks itself apart.

title: புருடன்
theme: The soul as purusha and as anu (அணு, the atom): the Lord made speech, bonds and the tattvas from beginningless time; he is the atom within the atom and is in the soul as the soul is in him; the tiny soul, like a banyan seed, can be cleared of the dark of bonds and set on the good path.
source_issues: 2009 line 4: நடர்கொண்ட is obscure; it may be a corruption of நடைகொண்ட.

reading: Speech beginning with vaikhari, the impurities beginning with maya, the distinctions beginning with purusha that bear false witness, and the particular workings of knowledge and action that bear true witness: the Lord who acts made all these from beginningless time.
nuance: கரி (witness) closes three compounds, பொய்கரி, மெய்கரி, செய்கரி, a word game hard to fix. புருடாதி பேதம் are the tattvas from purusha down. The claim that the Lord made even the bonds 'without beginning' (அனாதியே) is central to Siddhanta, as tradition reads it.

reading: The first Lord is the atom within the atom; for those able to approach the atom within the atom, by dividing that atom of atoms into a thousand parts, approaching the atom within the atom becomes possible.
nuance: அணு is both 'atom' and, in Siddhanta, the soul (anu), so 'the atom within the atom' may be the Lord within the soul. The verse repeats அணுவில் அணுவினை in every line; the thousand parts mark extreme subtlety.

reading: If one makes the soul pure by the light, as with the seed of the spreading banyan, driving out the painful darkness of bonds, one can seek the good path that leads on.
nuance: The banyan seed is tiny but holds a great tree, a traditional image for the soul's hidden capacity. சுடர் (the light) is unnamed; it is commonly taken as grace or knowledge. நடர்கொண்ட is obscure.

reading: People do not perceive the seamless mingling in which he is in the soul and the soul is in him; the peerless Lord, being everywhere, stood without lessening as all that moves and does not move.
nuance: கணு அற (without joint or seam) stresses that the mingling has no join; the verse holds both indwelling (he in the soul) and containment (the soul in him).

title: சீவன்
theme: The individual soul (சீவன்): it is unimaginably small, yet the Lord, greater than all, dwells within its flesh; bound by maya's adjuncts, it is stirred by the guru's grace, leaves them, enters the fourth state and becomes knowledge, and takes Siva's form within.
source_issues: 2011 line 4: நாறாயிரத்து is read as நூறாயிரத்து (a hundred thousand).

reading: To tell the form of the soul: split a cow's hair into a hundred and each part into a thousand, and the soul's part is one in a hundred thousand.
nuance: A similar measure of the soul by dividing a hair-tip is found in Upanishadic texts. The point is the soul's subtlety, not a literal size.

reading: Though our Lord is greater than all others, he is mingled within the flesh in smallness and is there; Mahadeva is not of a measure the gods can know; his measure is known by tapas.
nuance: The last line can be 'he alone knows the measure of tapas' or 'his measure is known only by tapas'. The verse balances greatness and smallness, answering 2011's tiny soul with the Lord who dwells in it.

reading: He is, and he is clear; to speak of it, though souls lack the quality of practising separation, the souls who practised of old will later see and take Siva's form within their thought.
nuance: வியோகம் (separation, or detachment) and the syntax of the first two lines are unclear; உண்டு தெளிவன் may also be 'having experienced, I am clear'. The last line, taking Siva's form in thought, is the firm part.

tamil: ஓயும் உபாதியோடு ஒன்றின் ஒன் றாது உயிர்
reading: The conscious soul is under the sway of maya's adjuncts; when it is stirred there by the grace of the guru, the adjuncts cease, and the soul, not becoming one with them, enters turiya and becomes knowledge.
nuance: உபாதி (limiting adjunct) and துரியம் (the fourth state, beyond waking, dream and deep sleep) are technical terms. ஒன்றின் ஒன்றாது may be 'not merging with what it joined'. The guru's grace as the trigger is plain.

title: பசு
theme: Souls as cattle (பசு, the bound soul): learned or powerful souls may bellow and graze, but only ripened ones give milk; and souls grazing in the field of the senses will not grasp the meaning until they are led past the boundary to the Lord's feet.

reading: Though the learned cows wander bellowing and the mighty cows graze tethered to a mark, the ripened cows are like a pot full of milk; the other cows are dry cows.
nuance: பசு is both cow and the bound soul, so the verse sorts souls. கற்ற (learned) and கொற்ற (mighty, ruling) souls make noise or keep to marks, perhaps rites or sectarian signs; முற்ற (ripened) is traditionally read as souls whose impurity has ripened for grace. The categories are the reader's to fill.

reading: What can be done with cows that graze in the field? Unless they are led across the boundary, joined to the Lord's feet, made strong and come to value it, the heart that makes its field will not know the sign.
nuance: Who leads the cows across is not named: the Lord, or the guru. கொல்லை (field, cleared land) is commonly taken as the field of the senses, and குறிப்பு as the hidden meaning or goal.

title: போதன் (அறிஞன்)
theme: The knower (போதன்): soul and Siva are not two, and once the soul knows Siva it remains as Siva; the knower, taught the thirty-six tattvas by Nandi's grace, passes beyond them, while those who do not know the impurities pursue hair-tearing austerities, and those busy only in the Lord's daily work miss his daily grace.
source_issues: 2021 line 4: நவமான is ambiguous between 'new' and 'ninefold'.

reading: There is no difference called soul and Siva; souls do not know Siva, and once souls know Siva, souls remain as Siva.
nuance: One of the best-known verses of the Tirumanthiram. It can be read as identity (the soul is Siva, unaware of it) or, as Siddhanta reads it, as non-separation in which the freed soul becomes Siva-like without ceasing to be; the verse uses both வேறில்லை and ஆயிட்டு இருப்பர், which pull in each direction.

reading: The dancing Lord, the lamp of qualities, is the overseeing witness, a lamp in the eye, for all abiding souls whose lamp is the mind, as the many-headed serpent's lamp is the jewel in its hood.
nuance: The verse stacks four lamps (குண, மன, பண, கண விளக்கு), and how they relate is not fixed. பணவிளக்கு is the jewel the serpent is said to carry in its hood. கண்காணி is an overseer or witness.

reading: The knower who, being knowledge, is freed of ignorance, whose sense-doors are closed and who is himself everywhere, knows as knowledge within them all, and is also that soul which stood gathered in.
nuance: போதன் may be the freed soul or the Lord, and the verse's subject shifts; பொறிவாய் ஒழிந்து (the doors of the senses ceasing) and செறிவாகி (concentrated, or densely present) carry the sense.

reading: To me, who did not know the nature of the thirty-six, Nandi made known the nature of the thirty-six; after I knew it by his grace, he stood beyond the thirty-six.
nuance: ஆறாறு (six sixes) is the thirty-six tattvas. நின்றானே is third person, so the one beyond them is Nandi; some take it of the knower, who passes beyond them with him.

reading: Those who do not stand in and know the grace that is Siva, and do not know what the five ruinous impurities are, perform austerities and tear out their hair; they never seek the new truth.
nuance: தலைப்பறிகின்றார் (they pluck the hair from their heads) is traditionally taken as aimed at Jain ascetics. மலம் ஐந்து is a fivefold count of impurities; நவமான தத்துவம் may be 'new', 'excellent' or 'ninefold' tattva.

reading: Those who live daily in the work the Lord carries on do not daily seek the Lord's loving nourishment; since the Lord gives grace daily to the good, those who do not seek it daily are mere day-labourers.
nuance: Every line begins நாடோறும் (daily), and நாடிடார், நாடார் play on நாடு (seek). நாள்வினையாளர் may be day-labourers or those bound to each day's deeds. Who 'lives in the Lord's work' is unclear: all beings, or ritual workers.

title: ஐந்து இந்திரியம் அடக்கும் அருமை
theme: How hard it is to restrain the five senses (ஐந்து இந்திரியம் அடக்கும் அருமை): the senses are rutting elephants that tire the mahout, a horse no learning can steer, birds and lions feeding in five fields; the poet confesses he cannot conquer them, though cutting their claws and teeth would bring one to the Lord.
structure_note: A sequence of animal images for the senses (elephants, a leaping horse, birds, lions), the five as rulers with ninety-six ministers, a personal confession (2028), and a closing verse on great powers that stands apart.
source_issues: 2029 is obscure throughout (எண்ணிலி இல்லி, இல்லதோடு) and may be corrupt.
2027 line 4: சிறைஇறுத்து may be read as 'paying tribute' or 'breaking prison', with opposite senses.

reading: There are five elephants in rut within the body; they do not come to the post of the Agamas' teaching; once the mahout is spent and they too have weakened, we do not know how to set yoga right by uniting.
nuance: ஆக மதத்தன puns on ஆகம் (body) and மதம் (rut), and ஆக மதத் தறி on ஆகமம் (scripture) and தறி (tethering post). The mahout is commonly taken as the mind or the self. The last line admits defeat rather than prescribing.

reading: Though the mahout has learned good books in his mind and jabs with his foot to correct it, the leaping beast only leaps in confusion; even if he climbs onto its neck and sits there and goads it, that beast will not keep to the road.
nuance: பாய்மா (the leaping beast) is usually a horse; எருத்து (neck) suits an elephant or bull, so the beast may continue 2023's elephants. The point is that book learning does not tame the senses.

reading: Five fields, five birds, and the birds go and feed there; five lands, five waters, five natures; one family, and one herdsman tends them with a staff; and the ways by which they come and go are nine.
nuance: The fives are traditionally the senses, their objects and their qualities, and the nine ways the body's nine openings. The herdsman may be the soul or the Lord. The verse lays out the scheme without stating a moral.

reading: Five lions live in the forest; the five go out to feed and come back into their five dens; if the claws and teeth of the five are cut, reaching the Lord fully becomes possible.
nuance: The lions are the senses and their dens the sense organs, as the image is usually read. Cutting claws and teeth disarms the senses without killing them.

reading: Under the five ministers are ninety-six; the five and their sons mean to rule; if the five stand with their anger, we cannot pay the tribute to the five.
nuance: தொண்ணூற்று அறுவர் is traditionally the ninety-six tattvas of an extended count. சிறை இறுத்து may be 'paying the levy' or 'breaking the prison'; the second would reverse the sense of the last line.

reading: Day after day I cannot speak of the radiant light, nor of the holy lady who is there too; I cannot conquer the five senses and myself; I have become like a horse that bolts when one stands to strike it.
nuance: திருமங்கை (the holy lady) is commonly taken as Shakti, with the light as Siva. கொல்ல நின்று ஓடும் குதிரை may also be a horse that runs on to its death. A rare first-person confession of failure.

reading: Shut that pot of countless holes in the dark room; going along with it brings error; if one guards against going along with it, there is bliss.
nuance: எண்ணிலி இல்லி is read here as a pot pierced with countless holes, an old image for the leaking body or mind; this is a guess. The verse repeats எண்ணிலி இல்லி in every line and the last line (இல்லதோடு) may mean 'with the one who has no holes'.

reading: The great strength of fate is the sea-girt earth; the great strength of praise is the ancient heaven; the great strength of the mind is human life; the great strength of wealth is the strength of water.
nuance: Each line pairs a power with its domain, but the logic is unclear, and மதி may be mind or the moon. The verse seems to stand apart from the chapter's senses.

title: ஐந்து இந்திரியம் அடக்கும் முறைமை
theme: The way of restraining the five senses (ஐந்து இந்திரியம் அடக்கும் முறைமை): the senses are fish, elephants and gnawing thieves, and the fort of knowledge alone does not hold them; yet Tirumular mocks those who only cry 'curb the five', since full suppression leaves one inert. What works is letting the senses subside as the mind settles on Nandi, is drawn in by worship and song, and is caught by the Lord's grace.
structure_note: Images of the senses caught or escaping (2031, 2034), a sharp turn against bare suppression (2033) set beside praise of subsiding in the five (2035), the mind as seed of all (2036), and then means: grace, meditation on Nandi, worship and song (2038 to 2043).
source_issues: 2032 line 3: விடக்கிண்டு is obscure and may be corrupt.
2037 and 2042: the syntax is loose and the second halves are obscure; the text may be damaged.

reading: In a round pool a cubit deep, holding half a cubit of water, the many fish that lived there have been caught; the fisherman brought his gear and cast it, and now we are free of harm.
nuance: The verse names no meaning for its image. Placed here, the pool is usually taken as the body or the heart, the fish as the senses or desires, and the fisherman (பரவன்) as the Lord or the guru who catches them. The measures (ஒருமுழம், அரைமுழம்) may be symbolic and I can't fix them.

reading: He who sets about curbing the restless senses of this lying body is himself immortal; the mind that goes to the flesh for pleasure runs only as far as it is let run.
nuance: விடக்கு is flesh; விடக்கிண்டு is unclear and may be corrupt. The last line (நடக்கின் நடக்கும் நடக்கும் அளவே) can also mean that the mind goes wherever it is allowed to go, so the curbing lies in not allowing it.

reading: The ignorant say 'curb all five, curb them'; even among the immortals none has curbed all five; knowing that to curb all five is to become inert, I learned the knowledge that does not curb them.
nuance: அசேதனம் is the insentient: a mind with all five senses shut down is no better than matter. The verse is commonly taken as rejecting forced suppression, not restraint itself, since the same chapter praises the senses subsiding (2035) and the senses caught by grace (2031). The word அடக்கு is the one the Kural uses for self-restraint.

reading: Elephants in triple rut rise trumpeting; I built a fort called knowledge to hold them, but they broke out and ran, rushed into great ruin, and that is how the fattened elephants wreck everything.
nuance: The elephants are usually taken as the senses, as in 977; மும்மதம், rut flowing from three places, is sometimes read as the three malas. The point is that knowledge by itself, as a wall, does not hold them.

reading: If one subsides within the five, that is the wide world; if one subsides within the five, that is rare tapas; if one subsides within the five, that is Hara's state; those who subside within the five are the ones who have grace.
nuance: ஒடுங்குதல் is to draw in or subside, not to beat down (அடக்குதல்), and the chapter seems to set the one against the other. ஐந்தில் ஒடுங்கில் can mean the senses settling within their five, or the self drawing back from them. அகலிடம் (the wide place) may be the world or the vast inner space.

reading: What use in babbling at length, what use in thinking of a mirage? The mind is the seed of everything that spreads out; enlarge it and it grows, shrink it and it shrinks; for those who examine, that is all the meaning there is.
nuance: பேய்த்தேர், literally the demon's chariot, is the ordinary word for a mirage. The verse makes the mind, not the senses, the root: whatever world one lives in grows or shrinks with it.

reading: The Lord of unfailing fame, who knows how life wanes and is one with the kin in whom he set the sweet life, makes the five's dancing subside; the serpent that has slain its bonds takes the opening and rests in that path.
nuance: The syntax is loose and the reading is a guess. நாகம் (serpent) and துளை (hole, opening) may be kundalini entering the central channel, as yogic readings take it, with அஞ்சாடல் ஒடுக்க as the stilling of the five senses' play.

reading: Tie the five elements that leapt about to the post of knowledge where the spreading light rests; if grace grants what is called bliss, that becomes the higher destiny that covers one over.
nuance: பூதங்கள் ஐந்தும் are the five elements, here probably standing for the senses built from them, tied like cattle to a post (தறி). வேய்ந்துகொள் (to roof, to cover) and மேலை விதி (the higher rule or fate) are unclear.

reading: If you think daily on Nandi who moves within, gently drawing in the spreading thought, and the mind fixed on its mark looks along the mark's path, north and south become the temple of the mind.
nuance: பைய (gently) again sets drawing in against forcing. குறி (mark, sign) is a yogic term for the point of concentration. வடக்கொடு தெற்கு may mean the whole world or, in the body, the line from crown to base; either way the shrine is the mind.

reading: Some many nazhigais and days have gone; the wealth that seemed lasting is like writing on water; conquer the senses and let them go at once, and even if a mountain falls you can bear it.
nuance: நீள்பொருள் may be lasting wealth or the long-lived body. விடுமின்கள் can mean 'let the senses go' or 'free yourselves'. The last line promises steadiness, not escape: the mountain still falls.

reading: Praise and sing the holy form of the Pure One and worship it; then, turning back the five senses with the intellect, pour into the heart the Lord of the four directions and of all who come after, and gathering into one becomes possible.
nuance: The order is worship first, then the senses turned back by புத்தி (intellect), then the Lord poured (ஊற்றுக) into the heart. ஒருங்கல் is the mind gathered into one.

reading: No one perceives the five who gnaw within the embodied state where the heart is held; if one speaks of many things as if in jest, it becomes a mountain wrapped in streaked darkness.
nuance: சகளம் is the state with form, the embodied soul or the Lord in form. The second half is obscure: மைசூழ் வரை, a mountain surrounded by black, may be delusion piling up from idle talk.

reading: There is nothing one must give up; reaching him in your thought, praise him with song; the senses that arose from the craving of the five false ones are only five.
nuance: The first line seems to answer the call to renounce: nothing needs abandoning if the Lord is held within and sung. The last two lines are unclear; ஐந்தே may belittle the senses (they are only five) once their root, craving, is seen.

title: அசற்குரு நெறி
theme: The way of the false guru (அசற்குரு நெறி): the false guru lacks inner feeling and true knowledge, does not see the Veda-Agama path, reviles others, is ruled by lust, and teaches for his food what he has only looked at. Such teaching harms the teacher, the king and the land, and teacher and pupil fall together like the blind leading the blind.
structure_note: Three portraits of the false guru (2044 to 2046), the harm of his teaching to self, king and realm (2047), and the image of the blind (2048).

reading: A fool without inner feeling, who does not ascertain the truth, never sees even a part of the Veda-Agama path, does no service, reviles others and has the nature of a bound soul: he is a false guru.
nuance: பரநிந்தை can be reviling others or reviling the Supreme. அணுவின் குணத்தோன், one with the quality of the anu, is taken as one still in the bound soul's state, who cannot free others. கணுவின்றி is read as 'not even a joint's length'.

reading: Those who have looked over mantra, tantra, great yoga and jnana, bondage and release, yet do not reflect on them or make others clear, and go blind for the sake of food: they are false gurus.
nuance: தரிசித்துப் பார்ப்பவர் suggests acquaintance by sight, without having thought it through (சிந்தனை செய்யா). ஊண்பொருட்டு names the motive: teaching as a living.

reading: He who does not know what is, a fool and a great fool, a wretch not free of lust and the rest, who teaches the unreal to wretches as the way, is without knowledge: he is no master but an unreal teacher.
nuance: அசத்து (the unreal) is a Siddhanta term for what is not abiding; the unreal teacher passes on the unreal. கலதி (wretch, the luckless) is applied to both teacher and pupils.

reading: If one teaches without removing the fancies that pose as learning, one's own state declines and one becomes one's own enemy; it is ruin to the good king and to the land, as Nandi said of old.
nuance: கற்பாய கற்பங்கள் is unclear: கற்பம் may be kalpana (imaginings), ritual prescriptions (kalpa), or a play on கற்பு (learning). தற்பாவம் may be one's own condition or the state of becoming That. The claim that bad teaching ruins king and realm echoes the first tantra's concern with rule.

reading: The blind who go showing the stick to the blind fall, front and back, into the old pit in their way; the blind leader falls, front and back, altogether; the blind fall together with the blind.
nuance: குருடு repeats in every line, so the verse stumbles as its walkers do. The guru who is himself blind is meant, not the pupil alone.

title: சற்குரு நெறி
theme: The way of the true guru (சற்குரு நெறி): the true guru gives his feet, makes one know oneself, lifts the soul beyond the tattvas and quells its bonds; like alchemy turning iron to gold for good, his grace ends birth. He shows the real, the unreal and the real-unreal, burns away the malas, and is finally the Supreme himself acting through the five acts.
structure_note: What the true guru gives (2049 to 2051), the true guru set against the false (2052, 2053), alchemical images (2051, 2054), the guru's path and teaching (2055 to 2058), the soul freed of the malas (2059, 2060), the Lord's play and five acts (2061 to 2063, 2065), nectar (2064), and a closing definition: the Supreme is the guru (2066).
source_issues: 2060: வலலார் (line 2) and செலலா (line 4) are misprints for வல்லார் and செல்லா.
2061 line 1: மீட்டுட்டி is obscure, perhaps for மீட்டு ஊட்டி.
2063 and 2065 are syntactically obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: The true guru is the lord who gives his feet and protects; giving his feet he can grant self-knowledge; giving his feet he brings the soul beyond the tattvas; giving his feet he quells the bonds: he is the Real.
nuance: தாள்தந்து opens every line: the gift of the feet, a form of initiation, is the guru's single act with four effects. சத்து (the Real) in the last word makes the true guru (சற்குரு) one with the Real he shows.

reading: He ended the deeds and the afflictions that seize his devotees; he set his feet upon their heads; he kept away the band of Yama's messengers; he ended the sorrow of birth.
nuance: தவிரவைத்தான் (he made it cease) opens each line; in the second it seems to mean he placed the feet without fail, so the refrain bends in sense. கோள் may be the planets' evil influence or anything that seizes.

reading: As black iron, once turned to gold, does not turn back into iron, so one who has received the guru's grace at the very moment marked will not come near birth again.
nuance: The alchemical image stresses that the change is final. குறித்த அப்போதே, the appointed moment, may be the moment of initiation or the time ripe for grace.

reading: Those who remove the bond, seek with love the Supreme and themselves, and drive out impurity completely are faultless true gurus; those who, lacking knowledge, are moved by clamour are not gurus who give understanding.
nuance: பூசற்கு இரங்குவோர் is unclear: பூசல் is clamour or strife, so it may be teachers stirred by quarrels and show; a reading as பூசை (ritual worship) is possible. போதக் குரு is a guru who teaches understanding.

reading: The stainless one who stands in love, able to give a love free of impurity, eternal and pure, is the lasting guru who gives to the loving ones who have grasped the tattvas as they are and are freed of them.
nuance: நேயம் (love) repeats in three lines. The opening phrase matches Tiruvachakam, Sivapuranam 13 (நேயத்தே நின்ற நிமலன்), as Sengalvaraya notes. Line 3 (ஆயத்தவர் தத்துவம் உணர்ந்து ஆங்கு அற்ற) is compressed and my reading of it is tentative.

reading: As everything the philosopher's stone touches becomes gold of rank, so all the world the guru touches is rid of the three malas and reaches the Siva-state.
nuance: பரிசன வேதி is the stone that transmutes by touch; பரிசித்த (touched) ties the image to initiation by the guru's touch (ஸ்பர்ச தீக்ஷை in later manuals). திரிமலம் are traditionally anava, karma and maya.

reading: When the presence of the true guru who stands as the very self, and that nature of being the self, are revealed, the self must win itself; to gain this, consider within you that the body is only flesh.
nuance: தானே என நின்ற can be 'standing as oneself' or 'standing as He alone'. சதுர் may be skill or the fourth state (turiya). ஊனே என நினைந்து may be 'thinking it is mere flesh' or 'thinking of him as intimate as one's flesh'.

reading: The path of coming and going, the path of maya, the path that those who saw the womb's path do not see, the great path Nandi speaks of: going by the guru's path one can reach it.
nuance: வழி ends every half-line. The first two paths are birth and death under maya; the last two are the path of release, unseen by those who know only birth, and taught by Nandi. The guru's path joins them.

reading: The guru is the one of supreme bliss whom the Veda and Agama describe, who practises Siva-yoga, has no thought of his own and removes the soul's bonds; one may place oneself with such a good guru when he comes.
nuance: ஒருசிந்தையின்றி may mean 'without any other thought' or 'without a separate thought of his own'. வைக்கலும் ஆமே leaves unclear who is placed: the pupil entrusting himself, or the soul set with the guru.

reading: Showing the real, the unreal and the real-unreal, setting the sentient and the insentient in Siva the Supreme, speaking the word that is bliss beyond pure and impure: when he speaks, he is the Father's grace-guru.
nuance: சத்து, அசத்து and சதசத்து are traditionally the Lord, the bonds, and the soul that can turn to either; the verse lists them without assigning them. சித்து and அசித்து are the sentient and the insentient.

reading: By bowing at the feet of the Lord who is free of attachment, those who wither the five malas that well up and the awareness of bondage, scorch the surrounding divisions by the three turiyas, and reach the Supreme are the true adepts.
nuance: ஐம்மலம் are traditionally anava, karma, maya, mayeya and tirodhana. துரியம் மூன்று (three turiyas) is a technical term I can't fix; it may be the fourth state in the three avasthas of soul, Shakti and Siva. சாதகர் are practitioners who have reached the goal.

reading: All is the Lord's bliss with the Lady; when the strong senses come, the soul appears; the five unspoken malas subside, and rising to reach the Siva-state that does not pass is play.
nuance: விளையாட்டு (play) is read of the Lord: the soul's embodiment and release are his sport with the Lady. சொல்லா மலம் may be malas beyond words or ones not to be named. செல்லா may mean 'not passing away' or 'where none goes'.

reading: Drawing back the soul he had placed in a lowly birth, setting it in its place and feeding it, humbling it, recovering it by knowledge, establishing it, and placing it in silence once it reaches release: these are the doings of the Freed One.
nuance: The list may map onto the Lord's acts toward the soul, ending in grace. மீட்டுட்டி is obscure, perhaps மீட்டு ஊட்டி. முத்தன் (the Freed One) is the Lord, or the guru in whom he acts.

reading: The insentient world is the playground of the Father's grace; the soul he has made discern the sentient from the insentient he makes pure, wipes away its mala and sets with the Real: such is the way of his five acts.
nuance: சடம் (insentient matter) is not illusion here but the field where grace works. The five acts are presented as all serving the soul's purification.

reading: Our stainless Lord, who stood in love for those who pass beyond the Isa tattva and say there is nothing beyond, and for those who, still in bondage, ever contemplate him, has made all the realms clear.
nuance: ஈசத்துவம் is the Isvara tattva, one of the pure tattvas. The first two lines are obscure; பாவியும் may be 'contemplating' (பாவித்தல்) or 'even the sinner'.

reading: In the mandala that rises blossoming like a garland of rubies, pure gold stood and nectar ripened there; those who guarded it and drank lived free of birth, and the brutes who did not perceive it lived for the flesh.
nuance: The mandala, the rubies and the pure gold (ஆணிப்பொன்) are symbolic and taken in yogic readings as a region of the head where nectar forms. மாக்கள் (brutes) is the word for those who live only for the body.

reading: So that the real with the unreal and the real-unreal are set apart and the clinging attachment of bondage is cut here, the Lord moves the two mayas and the soul there and makes the one thing known.
nuance: இரு மாயை are traditionally pure and impure maya, and அணு is the bound soul. The syntax is hard and my reading is a guess.

reading: Because he burns mala by the ascending path, cuts away darkness by the endless word and withers the soul's bond so that release comes, the Supreme himself, if you would name him, is the guru.
nuance: The chapter ends by collapsing the distinction: the guru's three acts (burning, cutting, withering) are the Supreme's, so the true guru is the Supreme. ஈறில் உரை (the endless word) may be the teaching or the mantra.

title: கூடா ஒழுக்கம்
theme: Conduct that does not fit (கூடா ஒழுக்கம்): those who do wrong in secret forget that the Lord is an overseer present everywhere, and those who seek him in the north or across the land forget that he is within the body; those who see him give up their stealth. The later verses turn to grace that clears the mind, to the soul and its awareness, and to knowing oneself as the chief work.
structure_note: The Lord as overseer (கண்காணி) before whom hidden wrong is futile (2067, 2068, 2072, 2074); against seeking him outside (2070, 2071) and against sects that do not know him (2073); then a run of compressed verses on grace, the soul, awareness and the tattvas (2075 to 2083) whose tie to the title is loose.
source_issues: 2078 and 2082 are compressed to the point of obscurity and may be corrupt.
The chapter title (கூடா ஒழுக்கம்) fits 2067 to 2074 only loosely and 2075 to 2083 hardly at all; the grouping of these verses may be editorial.

reading: Saying there is no overseer, people commit many thefts; when you look, there is no place without an overseer; those who saw the one who stands mingled everywhere as overseer have given up stealth.
nuance: கண்காணி, a supervisor or watchman, opens every line. கள்ளம் and களவு cover hidden wrongdoing generally, not only theft. The cure is not fear of being caught but seeing the overseer, after which stealth simply ends.

reading: He knows what was done; the men of this sea-girt world who cry out great falsehoods, if they speak truth, will be made worshipped by the gods by the one whose throat glows dark.
nuance: செய்தான் அறியும் may also mean 'the doer himself knows'. The dark throat (மைதாழ்ந்து இலங்கும் மிடறு) is Siva's, from swallowing the poison.

reading: Rebirth is for the drunken who pass the day selling ten and eating; for the madmen who pound the seed-grain, eat it and lay waste the field, there is never any birth.
nuance: A riddle. பத்து (ten) may be the ten organs of sense and action, spent for daily living. The 'madmen' who eat the seed and ruin the field are taken as those who destroy the seed of karma, so nothing grows into a new birth; பித்தர் is also a word for Siva's devotees.

reading: They say 'north, north', but nothing has been placed there; those without knowledge set out to walk; all the world contained in the north is contained within, for those who know.
nuance: Going north may be pilgrimage to Kailas or the vow of facing north until death (வடக்கிருத்தல்). The verse does not say which; its point is that what is sought there lies within.

reading: They wander everywhere in the land seeking Nandi, the one who stirs the body, the lord of the body's good land, who is fragrant within the body; they do not know the purpose that stands in the body.
nuance: காயம் (body) recurs in every line. காயக் குழப்பன் is unclear: one who kneads or works the body, or one who stirs within it. Against the poets who scorn the body, Tirumular makes it the land where the Lord lives.

reading: As overseer he rises in the hand; as overseer he stays in the mind; as overseer he mingles and makes the way; the beloved who has become overseer is he.
nuance: கையகத்தே எழும் may echo the proverbial gooseberry in the palm: present and plain. The last line turns the watchman into the lover (காதலன்), so the overseer of 2067 is not a threat.

reading: Virgins in one enclosure, the learned in another, those doing great tapas in another, those who have known their own nature by contemplation in another: what is this? They do not know the Lord's nature.
nuance: சிறை may be an enclosure, a side or a prison: each group shut in its own discipline. கன்னி is unclear here; it may be the celibate. The verse faults division rather than any one practice.

reading: In the eye that cannot see, the film is what hides the eye's light; that light is unseen too by those who do not see; those who have seen, without seeing, the great Eye that is eye even to the unseeing have given up stealth.
nuance: படலம் is a cataract or film over the eye, traditionally read as mala. காணாது கண்டார், seeing without seeing, is seeing not with the eye. The last words repeat 2067's ending (களவொழிந்தாரே).

reading: As a madman cleared by medicine returns to his nature, and as an eye regains its own light, so when Nandi gave grace I, clear in mind, ceased from doing.
nuance: பிரகிருதி here is one's natural state. செயல் ஒழிந்தேன், I ceased from action, is the end of acting from one's own will, not idleness.

reading: The eight moved as the Lord's power; not knowing them to be filled with the Supreme, people do not wake; the schemers intent on intoxication gave up thinking of the One free of ill.
nuance: The eight (எட்டும்) are traditionally Siva's eight forms: the five elements, sun, moon and the soul. சுராமயம் may be 'full of liquor' or 'of the gods (sura)'. பள்ளியுணரார் may be 'they do not wake from sleep'. நிராமயம் (free of disease) is an epithet of the Lord.

reading: For those who were one and two and have become one by uniting, one and two never come together; for all who keep saying 'one or two', the One that has become one with one stands as one and two.
nuance: The verse plays on the debate whether soul and Lord are one or two. It seems to say those who have united no longer think in those terms, while for the debaters the truth appears as both; the Siddhanta term for this is advaita as inseparable union.

reading: If the soul stands still, where will awareness stand? Without knowing, the body falls; soul and food lie together, and people do not know how the crop lies within.
nuance: அயர் அறிவு may be weary or absent knowing. பயிர் (crop) may be the body that grows from food, or what grows in the soul. The verse is compressed and may be damaged.

reading: When the soul is seen as distinct, awareness spreads everywhere; if one knows the soul, awareness becomes knowledge; people do not know the great Being that then swallows body and awareness.
nuance: உணர்வு (awareness) and அறிவு (knowledge) are set apart. Line 3 (உயிர் அன்று உடலை விழுங்கும் உணர்வை) is hard; அன்று may be 'then' or 'not'.

reading: The linchpin of the world, the bright flame, the highest Siddha, stands to be known as the linchpin of the land in the five; the chief work toward the Lord of the gods is knowing oneself.
nuance: ஆணி (linchpin, nail, also the finest gold) plays through the verse: உலகாணி, நிலவாணி, சிலவாணி, தலைவாணி. Only the last line is clear: self-knowledge is the principal thing.

reading: The lone flame that stands as 'He is the end', the bright flame that stands as the end of the body and as the world, standing as the fullness of sweetness: give up petty pleasure; this is the grace of the King of endless qualities.
nuance: அந்தம் recurs: end, limit, and in தேன்அந்தம் perhaps 'beauty' or 'fullness'. சிற்றின்பம் (petty pleasure), usually sensual pleasure, is set against the Lord's sweetness.

reading: None knows the purpose of the Lord, first in all from stone up, who says the flesh and life that are yours exist; if one stands so that the name that rose upon the good First is gone, one becomes the tattva that is one's own first.
nuance: கல்முதல் and நாமம் அற நின்றால் are obscure. The drift may be that when name and identity drop away one reaches one's source; I can't fix more than that.

reading: The senses and the inner organs came to the soul as the subtle body, not the gross; through the five kinds they give, the Purusha too abides in the heart at the end of the thirty-six.
nuance: சூக்கும உடல் (the subtle body), அந்தக்கரணம் (inner organs) and ஆறாறு (36, the tattvas) are technical. ஐவிதம் may be the five kanchukas; the verse is a compressed tattva statement.

title: கேடு கண்டு இரங்கல்
theme: Grieving at people's ruin (கேடு கண்டு இரங்கல்): they spend a rare human birth, their youth and their days in toil, argument, lust and want, and fail to worship the Lord who is near them as light and honey, while death comes running.
structure_note: Laments over wasted lives (2084 to 2093, 2095 to 2098) alternate with exhortations to worship (2094) and warnings that time is short (2099, 2100); the chapter closes on people who set the Lord apart as a god without knowing him (2101).
source_issues: 2086 line 1 (கையரை) and 2096 line 4 (நாதியே வைத்தது) are obscure and may be corrupt.
2099 line 3 (விதிர்திருந்து) is unclear in form.

reading: Sinners who store seed, sow it and plant out seedlings, not knowing that their span of life is running out, know nothing of the suffering their deeds bring; they are like those scorched in a full-blazing fire.
nuance: The plain reading is of people absorbed in the farming year; வித்து (seed) could also bear the yogic sense of bindu, as in chapter 140, but nothing in the verse forces it. முனிகின்ற in the last line (be angry, or be consumed) is unclear.

reading: Though they see time slipping away in a moment, what do people gain by arguing? They cannot stand in right conduct, bow at the feet of the Stainless one and know the First in love.
nuance: வாது (disputation) is set against அன்பு: knowing the Lord is said to come through love and bowing, not argument.

reading: Those who borrow, pound paddy and tend the body as if it were their life end up lying in their place, bodies mounted on a pyre of rough logs on a wide slope.
nuance: கையரை in line 1 is obscure (perhaps the wretched, or the hands at work). The irony is that labour spent only on keeping the body ends on the cremation ground.

reading: People of blameworthy speech, who do not grasp the Supreme that the holy one under the banyan's shade taught the four long ago, stand gathered together as if that were strength.
nuance: கல்லால் நிழல் புண்ணியன் teaching நால்வர் is traditionally Siva as Dakshinamurti teaching the four sages. உரந்தன்மையாக ஒருங்கி நின்றார் is unclear: perhaps they band together in obstinacy.

reading: Lasting fame and the truth of full austerity our Lord always gives to his devotees; but the world, saying 'that god, this god', has come to loss by its own diminishing.
nuance: அது இது தேவு என்று points at running from one god to another; the verse contrasts it with steady devotion to one Lord rather than condemning a named sect.

reading: Born in joy, grown in joy, forgetting the joy that is there to think on, some cry out for food and clothing and, standing in sorrow, sleep in sorrow.
nuance: The repeated இன்பத்துளே and துன்பத்துளே frame the verse. The joy may be the bliss of Siva in which beings are held, as tradition reads it, or simply the good of life; either way the fault is forgetting it.

reading: Having gained a birth that is hard to gain, they do not cherish the Lord's feet, hard to gain; all these creatures, hard to come by, have lost a gain that is hard to gain.
nuance: பெறுதற்கு அரிய opens every line. Sengalvaraya notes Arunagirinathar's Kandar Alangaram 67 takes up the same first line.

reading: With eager minds, boundless youth and a kindness they think good, in the time of pleasure they stand in the work of lust that soon runs out and forget the joy of the great ascetic.
nuance: மாதவன் is read here as the great ascetic, Siva; it can also name Vishnu, or mean great austerity. தீர வருவது may mean lust that ends, or that exhausts the one who follows it.

reading: He is in this way a form like the young sun, in that way the Lord dwelling within fire, in this way the Lord dwelling in the lotus; yet in truth we sat arguing over deeds.
nuance: Sun, fire and lotus may be the sun, fire and moon regions of the yogic body with the heart lotus, or outward forms of worship. வினைவாது is read as dispute about deeds or ritual; the last line is compressed.

reading: They cannot reach the sign the guru set, nor seek it; they wander making pleasant talk; they cannot sing, knowing what he has done; what gain is there for them?
nuance: குறி (sign, mark) the guru set is not specified. ஆடவல்லார் may be the Lord who dances, whose deeds they do not sing, or the people themselves, able only to dance; the question at the end is rhetorical.

reading: Worship daily, until you sleep in death, the tall flame that has filled your heart, the Lord, calling him 'our red Lord'; if you do not, you become like an elephant that has thrown off its fear and broken loose.
nuance: அஞ்சு அற்று may be 'free of fear', an elephant no longer held by the goad, or 'free of the five', a pun on the senses. Either way worship is what keeps the self in check.

reading: Beasts, humans, the great and birds: there is nothing the One made and set his love on that he does not think of; those who joined the great austerity where grace abides and came to know drink, run and take the fruit of the earth.
nuance: The syntax is loose. Line 3 may describe the freedom of the realized, or the ordinary acts of every creature that the Lord sustains. திருமருவு may mean where Lakshmi (fortune) abides or where grace abides.

reading: Like gold that the unjust have got, the Lord is not known by those without the light, and none follows him to know him; I seek the refuge who set him as the first fruit, the Lord of the immortals.
nuance: The gold of the unjust is perhaps hidden away and of no use, as the Lord is for those without inner light. நாதியே வைத்தது is obscure.

reading: They do not grasp how the bee, delighting among flowers full of honey, builds a great store of honey; and no one knows the honey that enters the mouth unsought, to be drunk without toil.
nuance: தேன் (honey) plays through every line, with வருந்தேன் (I do not toil) inside it. The honey is commonly read as the bliss of Siva, or in yogic terms the nectar (அமுதம்) that flows within; the verse names neither.

reading: Time has passed without their knowing the purpose; the Lord of Amaravati is full of longing for them, there is One for every life in the world, yet not striving and standing firm, they slip.
nuance: அருத்தியுள்ளான் can mean he has desire (for them) or is one to be desired. அமராபதி நாதன் is the lord of the gods' city, here an epithet of Siva.

reading: Death comes leaping and running close, and the days allotted have fallen away; what will you do, trembling? If you mean to be at peace, stir the porridge while it boils.
nuance: The proverb in line 4 is read here as 'act now, while there is heat and time'; it may instead mean that the effort must be made in the thick of things. விதிர் திருந்து is unclear.

reading: Before the waves reach the field that the river curves around near its bank, join and gain joy; if you look to the great austerity that springs near the mountain, the days left before grey hair are few.
nuance: திரை means both a wave and a wrinkle, and நரை is grey hair, so the field before the flood is youth before age. The mountain may be Kailasa or a yogic centre; that is not fixed.

reading: The One who knows coming, who knows the night in this dark, bewildered world, the rising radiant light: before those who know the serpent, people set him above as one god, without knowing him as mingled with them.
nuance: அரவு அறிவார் may be yogis who know the serpent power, or those who know Siva who wears the snake. விரவு அறியாமலே is read as not knowing his union with the soul; the verse seems to fault worship that keeps him apart.

title: இதோபதேசம்
theme: Salutary teaching (இதோபதேசம்): leave the passing birth behind, hold the Lord in mind even at death, keep to the Siva way with truth and love, and worship the guru who shows how to reach him; for those who do, deeds and births end.
structure_note: Direct exhortations in the second person (2102 to 2113), then verses on whom the Lord rewards and whom he punishes (2114 to 2118), and a close on the guru as the way to the Lord (2119, 2120).
source_issues: 2110: சிவனார் in line 1 may be a slip for சீவனார் (the soul).
2118: சற்குறுபால் is probably for சற்குரு; the verse is doubtful throughout and may be corrupt.
2109 line 4 (ஈற்றுப் பசுவது) and 2121 lines 3 and 4 are obscure.

reading: Forget and leave the birth that does not last on this earth; even at the time of dying, think of the Lord; contemplate the excellent Siva way that ends the suffering of fluttering in distress.
nuance: இறந்தொழி காலத்தும் ஈசனை உள்கும் returns almost word for word in 2108: the thought held at death matters for what follows.

reading: Direct your mind as far as it will go; speak the truth as well as you can; even if you have nothing, our Lord is there in fullness; seek the good way of Hara.
nuance: இல்லை எனினும் can be 'even if you lack means' or 'even if some say he is not'; both readings make the Lord's presence independent of the seeker's state.

reading: Kin is one and God is one; think only good; then there is no death for you and no shame; there is no refuge to go to outside your own mind; stand there, think of him firmly and be saved.
nuance: ஒன்றே குலம் is now usually read as the one kinship of all people; it may also mean all souls are of one kind. நமன் இல்லை நாணாமே can be 'there is no Yama, without shame', or 'there is no Yama, be unashamed'; line 3 may be 'there is no state you will enter' rather than 'no refuge outside the mind'.

reading: Praise the lord of the cool Kailasa mountain, the Nambi who is the centre of the four directions, and, taking up the body that wafts its fragrance to the winds, stand telling the nature of the one who kicked Death, and be saved.
nuance: கூற்று உதைத்தான் is Siva who kicked Yama to save Markandeya. Line 3 (காற்றிசைக்கும் கமழ் ஆக்கை) is obscure: perhaps the body made fragrant by worship, or the body of breath.

reading: Seek the way to go so that, leaving this body, you do not enter another body and be born; if you think on that time, asking when this body came to be ours, grace may be gained.
nuance: அக்காலம் உன்ன may be reflecting on the body's origin, or holding the Lord in mind at the time of leaving it, as in 2102 and 2108.

reading: Hara is there as knower of that thing that enters as it leaves, even as it comes to be; even when dying, seek the Lord, and that thing which comes to be will reach the farther shore.
nuance: அப்பொருள் (that thing) is read as the soul, which passes from body to body; அக்கரை (the other shore) is release from that passing.

reading: If the one that flies is to reach its goal, think of the Lord even at the time of dying; then the state of Siva joins with distinction, and after it comes freedom from all birth, the great world.
nuance: பறக்கின்ற ஒன்று (the thing that flies) is the soul, as a bird leaving its nest.

reading: Gathering and standing, worship our Lord; singing, stand within and bow at his feet; for those who stand within the mirror and come to know, he becomes like a cow long in milk after calving.
nuance: ஆடி (mirror) may also be read as 'dancing'. பசு is both cow and the soul; the image of the milch cow is usually taken as the Lord giving freely, but whether the soul or the Lord is the cow is not fixed.

reading: When the releasing one rises upward, stand in the middle and seek the Lord's feet; the one of unfailing fame, by whom strong deeds perish, will place you among the celestials.
nuance: விடுகின்ற சிவனார் may be a slip for சீவனார், the soul leaving the body; நடுநின்று may be the middle channel of yoga or the space between the brows. Read either as death or as yogic ascent.

reading: Those who wear the holy ash, crying 'you who ride the bull, our Lord, our master', are devotees and living gods; those who wear as their ornament the holy feet of the great one with the river in his red locks have no deeds left to bind them.
nuance: வேறு அணிவார் may mean they wear the feet as a distinct ornament, or wear nothing else.

reading: You who would have joy, know our Lord and be loving, take on the quality of the true knowledge that austerity yields; standing in the work of birth, you have toiled in the bond that brings pain and been ruined.
nuance: The verse moves from what one may become to what one has been: the same addressees, offered love and knowledge, are told they have so far only laboured in பாசம்.

reading: There is one true austerity to take up, one true foot to take hold of, one true path to take up, for those who stand wishing to take them up.
nuance: மெய்த்தாள் is read as the Lord's true feet. The last line puts the condition on the seeker's wanting: the way exists for whoever desires it.

reading: The fire-coloured one gives joy to those who come to him and painful birth to those who turn away; to the keen he shows his ringing anklets there, and those who join him come to know the God.
nuance: The verse states a simple reciprocity: drawing near gives joy, turning away gives birth again.

reading: They praise for all time release, knowledge, the sound of threefold Tamil and the Lord; the Stainless one is there as ghee within milk, yet they do not desire that light.
nuance: The ghee in milk is the Lord present throughout but not seen until churned out. The last line may fault those who praise but do not seek the light, or (taking விரும்பார் as 'want nothing else') praise them; the reading here takes the first.

reading: No one can tell how many ages the Stainless one, lord of order, has set; except that they come and plunge into birth, they cannot understand anything of Siva.
nuance: நியமத்தன் may be the lord of cosmic order or the one who keeps the observances. பவமத்து and சிவமத்து are unusual forms.

reading: Whatever the life here and whatever its ills, at the time like sleep, none but those free of venom can seek you, pure gem-coloured one, the Vikirta dwelling in excellence.
nuance: துஞ்சு ஒத்த காலம் is read as death, likened to sleep. நஞ்சு அற்றவர் (those without poison) may be those free of malice or of the soul's impurity. The verse is obscure and the reading tentative.

reading: If deceivers stay in the land before the true guru, famine comes to it; the Lord fears them and casts them into hard hell, while for those with upright hearts, attainment is there to be seen.
nuance: The text is doubtful throughout: சற்குறுபால் is probably சற்குரு, அஞ்சுவன் (he fears) is odd for the Lord, and தெரிசிக்க சித்தியே may mean seeing them is itself an attainment. Only the broad contrast of deceivers and the upright is secure.

reading: Countless gods worshipped Siva, yet by worshipping him there is no way to become him there; if one worships the guru who shows how to become him by that worship, union is possible.
nuance: ஆமாறு (the way of becoming) is the hinge: worship of Siva alone gave the gods no way to become one with him; the guru shows it. The verse makes the guru the means, not a rival object of worship.

reading: Seeing that men and gods, held by soul and bond, pass away through their deeds, if the one called guru is a knower without flaw, there is nothing to call him but the Supreme.
nuance: The condition matters: only the flawless jnani is to be named பரம். Men and gods both fall under பசு and பாசம், so neither can be the guru by status alone.

reading: The sole Lord who took them as his servants, so that love may grow and the deeds of those who took him up may go day by day, has ended them, not as one who took on the form of the tall one with water in his red locks.
nuance: Lines 3 and 4 are obscure. They may mean the Lord destroys his servants' deeds through the guru rather than in his own form, which would continue 2119 and 2120, but that is a guess.

title: உடலிற் பஞ்சபேதம்
theme: The kinds of body (உடலிற் பஞ்சபேதம்): the soul lives in a gross body of the seven bodily elements, a subtle body of eight tattvas and finer bodies still; the subtle body carries it from birth to birth to taste its deeds, while for the knower the body becomes Siva, so the body is not to be despised.
structure_note: The body as nested bags (2122), the subtle eightfold body (2123, 2124), the gross body (2125), the bodies and their measure (2126 to 2130), the subtle body's passage between births (2131 to 2134), the body according to the kind of soul (2135, 2136), and a defence of the body (2137, 2138).
source_issues: 2124 nearly repeats 473 (473 has எட்டினுள், ஆய்விடும், பாச உணர்வென்னுங் காயப்பை, கட்டி அவிழ்த்திடுங்).
2132 line 2 (மாக நனாவில் கானாமறந் தல்லது) is obscure; கானா may be for கனா (dream).
2138 is obscure throughout and may be corrupt.
2136: எஞ்ஞானத் தோர்க்கு is an unusual name for the pralayakalas, matching 494's எஞ்ஞானர்.

reading: There is one bag of a body with many wares in it; there is one bag of maya and another bag besides; when the thief who stood inside the body-bag goes out, the maya-bag turns to earth: such is the bewilderment.
nuance: The three bags are traditionally the gross, subtle and causal bodies, and the thief the soul, which slips out unseen. The verse names only the body-bag and the maya-bag clearly.

reading: Of the body the Father fashioned in two parts, the pure subtle one, when spoken of, is sound, touch, form, taste, smell, intellect, mind and ego: the eightfold body.
nuance: புரியட்டகம் (puryashtaka) is the subtle body of eight in Siddhanta: the five subtle elements with buddhi, manas and ahankara. The two parts are the gross and the subtle body.

reading: Within the eight, the five senses and the three bound instruments arise; as the clinging bond becomes awareness, the one with the eye in his forehead binds and unbinds.
nuance: This verse nearly repeats 473. The eight are the eight of 2123; the three கரணம் are traditionally mind, intellect and ego. Siva both binds the soul in the body and releases it.

reading: Chyle, blood, flesh, skin, fat, bone with its grease, marrow and the semen that spreads: this is the perishing adjunct, and but for its form, the body may be called one.
nuance: The list is the seven or more bodily elements (dhatus) of the gross body. உபாதி (adjunct) marks the gross body as something laid over the soul. The last line is unclear: perhaps the body is one thing, differing only in form.

reading: Who knows the greatness of the feet? Who knows where they stood? Who knows the sixty-eight bodies? Who knows what became the guard of the feet?
nuance: அறுபத்தெட்டு ஆக்கை (sixty-eight bodies) has no settled meaning; it may be a count of bodily parts or of kinds of body. அடி may be the Lord's feet or the base of the body.

tamil: நண்பால் உடம்பு தன் னால் உடம் பாமே.
reading: In the body built to eight spans, in eye, foot and body and in the hands that flow, the sixty-eight bodies join, and by that union the body becomes a body of itself.
nuance: எண்சாண் (eight spans) is the traditional measure of the human body, each by its own hand. புண்கால் and the sixty-eight are obscure, and the reading is tentative.

reading: The soul that is life to the body and the four inner faculties subsides into the Supreme; Brahman, showing the measure that stands in each pot, is stilled and gone: who knows this?
nuance: கடந்தொறும் (in each pot) recalls the Vedanta image of one space in many pots, the one Brahman in many bodies. நாலு is read as the four inner instruments. How the lines fit together is unclear.

reading: When the six ends join with the middle, the clear three sixes hold firm; the eighteen kalas spoken of join together, and the life counts the welling body as its own body.
nuance: ஆறு அந்தம் may be the six ends (the antas of Saiva doctrine) or 'the six as end'; மூவாறு and the eighteen kalas are counts whose content the verse does not give.

reading: The body whose gross face abounds in flesh, the body in which the subtle sits in what is unreal, the body that shows the finest as if in the hand: all are bodies held within the Lord's feet.
nuance: தூலம், சூக்கம், துல்லியம் name gross, subtle and finest bodies. மெய் and பொய் pun on body and truth, falsehood; the sense of the middle lines is uncertain.

reading: As a fierce galloping horse sets down one foot and lifts another, the body can go far and near; leaving one coat of flesh and putting on another there, it fits itself to whoever it becomes.
nuance: The subject is read as the subtle body, which passes from one gross body to the next. The coat image (போர்வை) is the gross body worn and shed.

reading: Like a snake leaving its slough, it may go, and by Hara's grace it goes to the place it must go and eats the two fruits.
nuance: The two fruits are good and bad deeds' results, as tradition reads them. Line 2 (நனாவில் கானா மறந்து) seems to speak of waking and dream but is obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: Having eaten what is in hell and heaven, the subtle body leaves and goes on as the cause; with its old deeds following, like a yogi who enters another's body, it takes up a body and meets birth and death.
nuance: பரகாய யோகி is the yogi with the power to enter another body, one of the attainments in the siddhi chapter; here it is a simile for the subtle body taking a new birth.

reading: One who has borne the Supreme and become Him changes what has come and reaches the highest; other souls go to the place their deeds bring them and suffer, entering sky and earth.
nuance: தான் அவன் ஆகிய (he who became He) states union plainly. ஆனவை மாற்றி may mean undoing the bodies and deeds that came to him.

reading: For the knower, the body, once established, becomes Siva; for the knower the body itself becomes That; for the yogi it is bindu and nada; for the silent sage the body is release in which the three voids are destroyed.
nuance: மேனி in line 3 may be another class of seeker or simply 'body'; முப்பாழ் (the three voids) is a technical term, traditionally taken as maya, the soul's state and the void beyond, but this is not fixed.

reading: For the vijnanakalas the body is anava itself; for those of the next kind, maya, it is said, is the body; for those without knowledge, karma becomes the body; those of true knowledge take on a body of Siva.
nuance: The classes follow 494: விஞ்ஞானர் (bound by anava alone), எஞ்ஞானர் (taken as the pralayakalas), அஞ்ஞானர் (the sakalas, bound by all three malas). Each one's 'body' is the impurity that holds it.

reading: See the dull ones who, calling the body filth, do not value it and hold some other place to be sacred; if one seeks and holds to this body as good, one grasps this whole cosmos in the strong body.
nuance: மலம் may be filth or the soul's impurity; தலம் என்று வேறு தரித்தமை is read as taking another place (a shrine, or another body) as holy. The last line rests on the body as microcosm (அண்டம்).

reading: Speech, mind and the rest, in good utterance, play gently within the Stainless; the others, the ear, sound and the rest and the mind as well, those who have gently held them see Him, hungering.
nuance: The verse is obscure and the reading a guess. It seems to set the faculties at play in the Lord against the senses gently held in check; முகத்தார் பசித்தே is unclear.

title: உடல்விடல்
theme: Leaving the body (உடல்விடல்): the desires, speech, breath-sound, senses and mind that tie a person to the body fall away, and nothing, not even vows and gifts, is a sure support for the perishing flesh; the mind made firm stands before Siva.
structure_note: Two verses list what ends with the body (2139, 2140); the third sets the desire-driven wandering mind against the steadied mind before Siva (2141).

reading: The desire that shapes a person, the speech one keeps up, the sound that shines in the breath, and the mind that clings to the sore-like body: when one looks upward, the body perishes.
nuance: அண்ணாந்து பார்க்க carries the verse. Plainly it is the upturned gaze of the dying; in the yogic tradition it is taken as turning attention up to the crown, at which the body-bound faculties fall away. Both readings stand. பண்ணாக்கும் may mean 'that makes song' or 'that fashions'; புண்ணாம் உடல் calls the body a wound.

reading: The ears of the perishing body, the vows and gifts of passing time, the speech that is spoken and the nadis that come to their end: none of these is a sure support for the flesh that is passing away.
nuance: The participles அழிகின்ற, கழிகின்ற, மொழிகின்ற, முடிகின்ற, ஒழிகின்ற march the verse toward its end. The verse says vows and gifts do not hold up the body (ஊன்); it does not say whether they help the soul.

reading: Desire rising at the leaf-slender waist and a mind sunk at the breast send one wandering, carrying a body brief as lightning; but the mind made firm as stone stands before Siva.
nuance: மின்னுடல் may be the lightning-brief body or, in yogic reading, a body of light. சிலையாய சித்தம் may be a mind steady as stone or bent like a bow (சிலை is both), and சிவமுன் இடைக்கே is obscure, so the contrast drawn here is one reading.

title: அவத்தை பேதம் - கீழால் அவத்தை
theme: The descending states of the soul (கீழால் அவத்தை): waking, dream, deep sleep, turiya and the beyond are placed at centres of the body from the brow downward, each with fewer instruments; bound by the five malas the soul is born and dies without end, yet the Lord rouses it from the stupor of anava through maya, and one who sees the malas plainly in full waking stands with the Supreme.
structure_note: Places and instruments of the states (2142 to 2147); an interlude on ignorance of the life in the body and on yogic mastery of breath and elements (2148 to 2153); the states one by one from dream to the beyond (2154 to 2159); the malas, the kevala state and the Lord's awakening of the soul (2160 to 2166).
source_issues: 2158: line 1 begins with a stray Latin 'Y' (Yஊமை); the tool flags it as corrupt.
2155: கழுத்தியது looks like a misprint for சுழுத்தியது (deep sleep).
2145: பசுமை in line 1 is not matched to any element and may be a slip.
2164: line 4 (அஞ்சணும் மன்னன்) is obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: Waking, with its twenty-five, is at the middle place; dream, with its fourteen, they say is at the throat; deep sleep is in the heart of the purusha who sees no falsehood; and turiya is at the navel of the one who has seen the truth.
nuance: மத்திமை is traditionally the brow. ஐஐந்து may be twenty-five or five and five, and the usual Siddhanta count for waking is thirty-five; சுழுனை here seems to stand for deep sleep (சுழுத்தி) rather than the channel sushumna.

reading: Counting from the thirty-six, the states run from first waking as five, then four, then two and one; understand them as reaching from niyati up to Siva.
nuance: The numbers (ஐந்து, நான்கு, இரண்டு, ஒன்று) are compressed and their objects are not named; நியதி and சிவம் are the ends of the tattva list, so the verse seems to map the states onto the tattvas. அப்பதி is unclear.

reading: The ten senses, their ten objects, the ten vital airs that stand as mantra, the four inner instruments and the soul make up the bound state of waking.
nuance: The sum is thirty-five, the traditional count of waking's instruments. மந்திரமாய் நின்ற மாருதம் (breath standing as mantra) is usually linked to the unspoken mantra of the breath. பந்த names waking itself as bondage.

reading: Earth is golden, water white, fire red, air black and the sky smoke-coloured, and those who stand in them remain hidden.
nuance: பசுமை (green) in line 1 has no clear element of its own; it may qualify earth or be a slip. The ones who stand hidden (மறைந்துநின்றார்) are traditionally the deities presiding over the elements.

reading: The five elements, the five senses, the outer tattvas that work harm, the malas, the gunas and the adharas: the instruments of the first state number ninety-six.
nuance: Ninety-six is the larger Siddhanta count of the tattvas and their sub-parts (2179 calls it common to all). ஏதம் படஞ்செய்து is obscure; it may say the instruments cause harm or that they spread out.

reading: Told by their places: twenty-five elephants, a great army, five leaping horses, the lord in the middle with four who dwell within, and at the long gate five with four.
nuance: The body is pictured as a king's camp. Tradition takes the elephants as the tattvas, the horses as the senses or breaths, the lord as the soul and the four as the inner instruments; the closing five with four is unclear.

reading: People cling to body after body and do not know the life that stands within the body; not knowing the bond between body and life, they wander bewildered like a dog that has strayed into a monastery.
nuance: உடம்பும் உடம்பும் உடம்பைத் தழுவி may be bodies embracing in desire or the soul taking body after body. The phrase உடம்பொடு உயிரிடை நட்பு is the Kural's (338). The dog in the மடம் is a stray in a place not meant for it.

reading: Fools do not know the one way things stand: if one turns back the ajapa breath, draws it up, holds it as a seed and turns toward Siva the foe of Kama, the body that has taken form will not perish.
nuance: அசபை is the mantra said by the breath without utterance; மாற்றி (reversing) is taken as turning it back inward. மருக்கும் and கருக்கொண்டு are unclear. The promise that the body will not perish is the yogic claim of 724, not a statement about the soul.

reading: The noble teacher who gave the fourteen came within me, and by the kalas he grants he hid away the sixty and set my mind in stillness.
nuance: ஆரியன் is the guru. The fourteen may be the instruments of dream (2154); அறுபத்து (sixty) and ஒடுங்கிய சித்து are not explained in the verse.

reading: Earth, water, fire, air and sky, and the abiding mind, intellect and ego, each contemplated one by one: so mastery of the elements is won.
nuance: பூதசயம் is bhuta-jaya, mastery of the elements, a yogic attainment. The words linked to each element (மலர், பொன்) may name their colours or seats; their exact sense is unclear.

reading: One son to the first, two to the form, three to fire, four to the marriage, five children to the maiden, none before; and the maiden loved the maiden.
nuance: A riddle. The counts one to five are traditionally taken as the qualities of the elements, from sky (sound alone) to earth (all five). The last line, a maiden loving a maiden, is obscure; it may speak of Shakti turning to herself.

reading: Once the five senses, the five objects they mingle with and the four inner instruments are understood together, he becomes as he was of old and abides spread out as the whole cosmos.
nuance: It is unclear whether the subject is the soul regaining its original state or the Lord. வியாக்கிரத்து is obscure, perhaps for வியாபகம் (pervasion).

reading: As ten of the fourteen fall away and the four inner instruments remain, the soul at the throat sees dream, made from the impressions of household life.
nuance: The ten that leave are taken as the outer senses, so dream works with the inner instruments alone. வாதனை (impressions) makes dream the replay of waking life. மன்று கலந்த is unclear.

reading: Leaving its place and entering the heart alone, its self-regard gone, its understanding gone and dazed, in the unmanifest where it knows nothing spread out, the body forgotten, it is deep sleep.
nuance: அவ்வியத்தம் is the unmanifest. கழுத்தியது, read here as deep sleep, looks like a misprint for சுழுத்தியது; it could also be read with கழுத்து (throat), which would not fit the heart of line 1.

reading: In deep sleep three remain, the chitta, the breath and the soul's own seeing; dwelling within the lotus, the soul stands joined with the excellent reality.
nuance: கழுமுனை may be deep sleep, as in 2142, or the channel sushumna. The lotus is traditionally the heart. விழுமப் பொருள் (the excellent thing) may be the Lord, present even in deep sleep.

reading: Rising from its place into the sky of turiya and leaving the world behind, at the summit of thought the soul casts off the ignorance of the flesh and stands silent as a mute.
nuance: ஊமன் (the mute) gives the silence of the state beyond speech. கானத்து எழுந்த (risen in the forest, or in song) is unclear.

reading: When the silent letter meets the spoken letter, the five draw in as a tortoise draws in its limbs; reaching Om it gains an inner light, and it is beyond names, beyond our knowing.
nuance: ஊமை எழுத்து and பேசும் எழுத்து are traditionally the unspoken and spoken parts of a mantra, or bindu and nada. The tortoise is the Kural's image (126) for restraint of the senses; here the drawing-in follows the mantra rather than effort.

reading: Turiya lies within waking itself; the fourteen jackals ate poison and died, the great horse bolted and was gone, and where turiya ends cannot be told.
nuance: The fourteen jackals are taken as the fourteen instruments and the horse as the breath or mind. The first line makes turiya a state reached awake, not a separate sleep.

reading: Held in the states by the five unyielding malas and given body and instruments from maya that are other than itself, every soul is born and dies without end and is beaten by strong deeds that do not abate.
