nuance: Tirumular counts five malas (2183 names anava first); tradition lists anava, karma, maya, the concealing power and mayeya. வேறாய stresses that body and instruments are not the soul.

reading: Maya makes the soul eat the fruit of its deeds without itself being part of the soul, and release comes by the Lord's grace: the soul, born through knowledge, reaches release directly through the knowledge it contemplates.
nuance: Line 1 and நண்ணல் இலா உயிர் (the soul that does not approach, or the soul not yet near) are compressed. The verse joins grace and knowledge as the means of release without saying how they relate.

reading: In the kevala state anava is a sleep of utter stupor; as it gives way, the knowing soul, prompted by its karma, leaves that steady kevala and, not yet the Supreme, falls into the five states.
nuance: கேவலம் is the soul's state alone with anava, before embodiment. நந்த can mean to wane or to flourish, so whether anava weakens or prevails here is open; the reading takes it as waning.

reading: As a teacher wakes with a shining rod the pupils sleeping in front of him, so the loving Lord wakes those long sunk in anava through blameless Maya.
nuance: The simile makes maya the Lord's instrument of grace, not a fault: embodiment wakes the soul from the deeper sleep of anava. ஏசாத (blameless) defends maya against the charge the word often carries.

reading: As the undiscerning speak of the moon seen in the clouds and in a pot of Ganga water as though it were many, though the great moon is one and undiminished, so with this body: its king departs on the day it goes.
nuance: The moon reflected in many vessels is an old image for one reality seen in many bodies. The reading of line 4 (அஞ்சணும் மன்னன் அன்றே போம் அளவே) is a guess; whether the one is the soul or the Lord is unclear.

reading: When the king of the land rides his leaping horse into his fair city, the five who serve him and all who live there take to the drum-house and fall asleep.
nuance: Traditionally the king is the soul, the horse the breath, the city the body and the five the senses, so the verse pictures the senses falling still as the soul withdraws inward. துடியில்லம் (house of the drum, or of the pulse) is unclear.

reading: Considering how the five stubborn malas work through the five long states, one who sees all five plainly while fully awake stands always with the Supreme.
nuance: நேர் (straight, direct, facing) opens every line: the stubborn (நேரா) malas, seen directly (நேரே) in waking, give way to the true (நேராம்) Supreme. The verse places release in waking, not in withdrawal from it.

title: மத்திய சாக்கிர அவத்தை
theme: The middle states within waking (மத்திய சாக்கிர அவத்தை): waking itself holds all five states, each tied to a mala or power, and the tattvas are counted differently by each school (96, 36, 28, 24 and 25). The soul in the sakala state gropes like a blind man, but by grace and Nandi's teaching it learns that it is the knower beyond the inert tattvas, sheds states, malas and tattvas, and stands as one.
structure_note: The states within waking and their powers (2167 to 2170); grace beyond the tattvas (2171); counts of the tattvas and the yogic body (2172 to 2178), with the schools' counts set side by side (2179); the knower and release from tattvas and malas (2180 to 2182); the malas graded by the rank of beings (2183).
source_issues: 2167 line 3: அழுத்தி is obscure, perhaps a misprint for சுழுத்தி.
2178: the number in lines 1 and 2 cannot be fixed (நாற்பத்தொண் may be forty-one or forty-nine).
2183 line 1: அவரோனுக்கு is obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: Within waking, waking-of-waking belongs to the concealing power, waking-dream to Mahamaya, the pressing stage of waking to one's karma, and waking-turiya to maya.
nuance: திரோதாயி (the concealing power), மாமாயை, காமியம் (karma) and மாயை are four of the five malas or bonds; the verse names four sub-states. அழுத்தி is obscure, perhaps for deep sleep (சுழுத்தி) within waking.

reading: Maya rouses kala and the tattvas after it, among them raga; passing through turiya, deep sleep, dream and waking, the soul comes to be in the sakala state.
nuance: கலாதி and இராகாதி are the impure tattvas of kala, vidya, raga and the rest, which maya produces to rouse the soul. சகலம் is the embodied state between kevala and suddha.

reading: Like a blind man whose eyes are open, who sees only the step ahead and goes feeling with a stick, the soul in its three states strives by its deeds.
nuance: The image makes the embodied soul partly sighted: instruments let it see the next step only. சொல்லும் விழிபெற (to gain the eye that is spoken of) may hint at the guru's word as the cure; மூவயின் (three places) is unclear.

reading: As a spider sits at the centre of its web and feeds on the life it catches, so the master sits in the golden house of the five senses and consumes the five beginning with sound.
nuance: அத்தன் usually names the Lord, but the one who enjoys sense objects is in Siddhanta the soul; the verse can be read of either, or of the Lord as the soul's inner ruler.

reading: Beyond the twenty-five tattvas set each in its place there is One who reaches to the summit; calling him the mad one, the great one, the unborn, and longing for him, I was saved by his grace.
nuance: பிச்சன் (the mad one) is a loving epithet of Siva, the wandering beggar. The verse breaks the run of counting with personal devotion: the tattvas are named, but grace saves.

reading: Twenty-four with purusha and its true tattva, twenty-five again with the true purusha and the Supreme, and taking the undivided void as the Supreme: so are counted the twenty-eight tattvas of Vedanta.
nuance: The arithmetic is compressed; the verse seems to build the Vedanta count of twenty-eight from the Samkhya twenty-four and twenty-five by adding purusha, the Supreme and the void (வியோமம்).

reading: Taking up ida and pingala, entering with the gunas, and twisting at the root in the triangle, one may see the feet of the Lord who holds time.
nuance: இடை and பிங்கலை are the left and right channels; மூலம் and முக்கோண் are the root centre and its triangle. ஏலம் is obscure, and காலம் கொண்டான் may be the master of time or the one who holds the breath (கால்).

reading: The ten nadis and the vital airs settle in the running breath, and desire, the fluid that bathes, and the mind that seeks the good all lie within the body.
nuance: இரதம் may be the body's essential fluid, often taken as bindu. The verse places breath, desire and mind together in the body, which the yogic chapters treat as the field of practice.

reading: What is to come comes, what is to perish perishes, what is to go goes and what is to enter enters; Nandi, the guardian, showed this and saw it, and the one with shining ornaments does as he bids.
nuance: The doubled verbs state that things run their course. இலங்கிழையோன் (one with shining ornaments) may be Shakti or the soul; ஏவன செய்யும் (does what is commanded) is open as to who commands whom.

reading: Twenty-three with prakriti, turiya, the time known within, the true void and the higher turiya: so the twenty-eight tattvas are to be counted.
nuance: This is a second reckoning of the twenty-eight of 2172; the added items differ. பத்தொடு பத்துமோர் மூன்றும் (ten and ten and three) with பகுதி gives twenty-four.

reading: If the breath runs in the measure of three hundred and thirty and ten, doubled in its seats, the five malas bow, the breath rises, and in that way the tattvas stand clear.
nuance: The numbers are a breath count whose total is unclear; தளங்கொள் இரட்டியது ஆறு may be the six centres doubled. Only the claim that measured breath subdues the malas is plain.

reading: The countless tattvas, numbered in crores and thousands and hundreds, are contained in the ninety-six, and those, when examined, in the twenty-five.
nuance: The exact figure (நாலொரு கோடியே நாற்பத்தொண்ணாயிரம் மேலுமோர் ஐந்நூறு) cannot be fixed; நாற்பத்தொண் may be forty-one or forty-nine. The point is that the many reduce to the few.

reading: The ninety-six are called common to all; the thirty-six are the tattvas of the Saivas; the twenty-eight are for the Vedantins and Vaishnavas; the twenty-four and twenty-five are for the Mayavadins.
nuance: The verse sets the schools' counts side by side without condemning any; அருஞ்சைவர் (the rare Saivas) marks the Saiva count as the one it values. The twenty-four and twenty-five are usually Samkhya numbers, here given to the Mayavadins.

reading: If the tattvas stay in their own course one may live wise and shining, and the false ones fall away; the tattva that is real is the letter A.
nuance: பொய்த்துவம் plays on தத்துவம்: the false against the real. The letter A (அகாரம்) is traditionally Siva, as the first sound in all letters and in Om.

reading: The thirty-five and one are without knowledge; I sat not knowing myself, the one who knows, until Nandi graciously said 'you are the one who knows', and I came to know that I am the knower.
nuance: ஐஏழும் ஒன்றும் (five sevens and one) are the thirty-six tattvas, inert (அறிவொன்றிலாதன). The verse repeats அறி in every line: the soul is set apart from the tattvas as the knower, and learns it only from the guru's word.

reading: Putting away the five states from waking-of-waking, the five mala-states from waking that they produce, and with them the false thirty-six, keeping to the path, the soul stands as one.
nuance: ஒன்றாகியே நிற்கும் (stands having become one) is read here as union; the verse does not name with what.

reading: The five malas from anava belong to the lowest beings, four to Mal, three to Haran, two to the Isvaras, and anava alone to Sadasiva.
nuance: அவரோனுக்கு is obscure (perhaps the lowest, or a slip for Brahma), and நான்காம் மாற்கு is read as நான்கு ஆம் மாற்கு. The grading makes the gods themselves bound souls of higher rank, as Siddhanta holds.

title: அத்துவாக்கள்
theme: The six adhvas (அத்துவாக்கள்), the paths of tattvas, mantras, letters, worlds, words and kalas through which the soul is bound: counting and searching them leaves seekers bewildered, but rising through the states to Siva's dance makes them all Sivaya.
structure_note: The count of the six adhvas (2184), seekers lost among them (2185), and their passing into Siva through the states and the dance (2186).

reading: Thirty-six tattvas, seven crore mantras, fifty-one letters, two hundred and twenty-four worlds, eighty-one words and five kalas: so the paths came to be.
nuance: The numbers match the six adhvas of Saiva Agamic tradition: tattva, mantra (மனு), varna (வன்னம்), bhuvana (மேதினி), pada (பதம்) and kala. The verse lists them without the word அத்துவா, which is the chapter title.

reading: Those who study the three regions well, run along with the twenty-five within, gather together and follow the path by its marks are left bewildered after all their searching.
nuance: மண்டலம் மூன்றும் is traditionally taken as the regions of fire, sun and moon in the body, and இருபத்துஐஞ்சு as the twenty-five tattvas. Whether the bewilderment is failure or the stunned arrival of the search is not plain; திகைத்திருந்தார் allows both.

reading: Beginning from waking-within-waking and taking the gross body as the measure, one passes into the beyond and reaches the dance of love, becoming Siva, and then all five are Sivaya.
nuance: ஐந்தும் சிவாயவே is traditionally taken as the five letters நமசிவாய losing ந and ம (taken as the malas) so that only சிவாய remains; the five may also be the five states. தாக்கிய (that strikes) with தாண்டவம் is unclear.

title: சுத்த நனவாதி பருவம்
theme: The pure states beginning with waking (சுத்த நனவாதி): waking, dream, deep sleep, turiya and the beyond are matched to the tattvas, the malas and places in the body, and each state is divided into all the others, as the soul drops its instruments and passes inward to turiya and the beyond where it becomes Siva. Among these sit verses on the malas that hide the soul (rice and husk), the one herdsman of the many cows, and knowledge that knows itself.
structure_note: The chapter opens with bindu and the states (2187, 2188), lists the tattvas (2189 to 2191) and the malas and bound soul (2192 to 2195), then maps the states onto tattvas and the subtle body (2196 to 2201). 2202 to 2206 divide each state into the others. The rest mixes the soul's rise through the states (2207, 2212, 2216 to 2218), knowledge knowing itself (2209, 2224), the malas and their cure (2210, 2211, 2213), symbolic verses on the mind (2214, 2215), yogic verses (2219 to 2223), and a close (2225, 2226).
source_issues: 2205 line 4: கோன்றிடும் is a misprint for தோன்றிடும்.

2200 is a variant of 2142 with different counts (ஐஐந்தில் for பன்னான்கில், ஐஐந்து பத்துடன் for ஐஐந்து மத்திமை) and a different third line (பொய்கண்ட மூவர் புருடன் சுழுனையின் against பொய்கண் டிலாத புருடன்இத யம் சுழுனை); one or both may be corrupt.
Obscure words that may be corrupt: 2196 தனலுண் பகுதி, 2198 சேயதே வலவித்துடன் (perhaps கேவல வித்துடன்), 2216 முனவகத்தே, 2225 அரியன தூடணம் அந்தண வாதி.

reading: The gross states beginning with waking and subtle prakriti, the twenty-five, are the power of bindu; the soul's own bindu stands and goes forth, and in this way dream mingles into waking.
nuance: நனவாதி (waking and the rest) opens the chapter's subject. ஐஐந்து (five fives) is taken as the twenty-five lower tattvas; how bindu, the soul and the states fit together here is not clear from the verse.

reading: Within waking, those in the beyond-state are like the newborn lying still, those in turiya like infants crawling, those in deep sleep like children walking and growing; when dream runs within waking, the work is done well.
nuance: The verse seems to match the states within waking to a child's growth, lying, crawling, walking. The direction of the comparison, and what நன்செய்தி (good affair) means in the last line, are uncertain.

reading: Close-knit ritual is the Siva tattva; with it come undivided blissful yoga, great grace and learning, the sacred form one fixes on with its many qualities, and in knowledge all that moves and stays, as far as the cosmos.
nuance: The verse lists without connecting words, so how கிரியை, சுகயோகம், பேரருள் and கல்வி relate is a guess. It may describe what the pure (சுத்த) states open on to.

reading: From the first, the Lord set the tattvas in place: supreme Siva, Shakti, Sadasiva, flawless Isa, pure vidya, then bodha, kala, time, niyati and mahamaya, down to the last.
nuance: The list runs from the five pure tattvas (Siva, Shakti, Sadasiva, Isvara, Suddhavidya) to the impure ones begun by maya. போதம் and நீதி are not standard names in this list; நீதி ஈறாக may mean 'down to the end, in order'. என்னே may be wonder or 'what is this'.

reading: Siva shining in radiance, Shakti, Sadasiva, Isa, the fiery vidya, raga, kala, time, stainless vidya, niyati, mahamaya, and the flawless purusha and the rest, with the soul at the end, make thirty-six.
nuance: ஆறாறு (six sixes) is the standard count of thirty-six tattvas. The order differs from 2190 and from the usual Siddhanta order, and அனல்வித்தை and மாசகல் வித்தை look like two vidyas, pure and impure; ஆன்மா ஈறு may be the soul at the end of the list or the atma tattvas.

reading: Anava, maya and karma are the malas; as bran and husk cover the sprouting grain, the soul stands as the rice, unlike Sthanu who has none: cherish it by separating your bonds.
nuance: The rice image is a classic of Siddhanta: the husk and bran are with the grain from the start, as the malas are with the soul, yet are not the grain and can be removed. தாணுவை ஒவ்வாமல் sets the bound soul apart from Siva, who is free of them.

reading: The cows are of many colours but their milk is of one colour, and the herdsman who grazes them is one; if the herdsman lays down his staff, the cows will not let go of their master.
nuance: பசு means both cattle and the bound soul, so the verse is read of souls, many in form and one in nature, and of the one Lord who tends them. கோல் போடில் may mean laying the staff aside or striking with it; traditionally it is the Lord's act of grace, after which the souls cling to him.

reading: Body, senses, mind, bright intellect, chitta, the mighty ego and ignorance remaining, that soul perishes; and if its delusion branches further, it reaches the seven hells.
nuance: The list is the soul's instruments, ending in அறியாமை, which here stands for the mala of ignorance. மயல் (delusion) that grows is what leads down; the verse does not say the instruments themselves are bad.

reading: The beyond-state that does not know itself is anava; turiya, where words are known, is karma; deep sleep that follows is the desire spoken of; and the rest, of food, is dream and waking.
nuance: The verse seems to match the states to the malas: atita to anava, turiya to காமியம் (karma), sushupti to desire, and dream and waking to the grosser bonds. உண்டி (food) in the last line is obscure; the matching is the tradition's reading.

reading: In waking there is no dream; in the five of waking, the subtle without dream is seen as deep sleep; prakriti that eats fire, and maya that gathers itself; in waking, turiya and atita come to the fore.
nuance: Each line is compressed and the syntax uncertain. தனலுண் பகுதி (prakriti that eats fire) is obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: When twenty-five of the thirty-six withdraw, there is waking in waking; when six more leave, waking in dream; when the other five also go, at the end of waking is deep sleep; in this, there is maya alone.
nuance: The counts follow the tradition that each state is marked by fewer tattvas in play. The arithmetic and which tattvas are meant are not stated, and the states named may be read differently.

reading: The purusha who came in maya, in turiya, leaving the order that arose and becoming not even that, goes far off with the kevala seed; then the body that was taken has no use.
nuance: சேயதே வலவித்துடன் is obscure; read as கேவல வித்து, the seed of the kevala state, it fits the next chapter's subject, but the reading is a guess.

reading: The soul is the knower in atita and turiya; if it practises atita-turiya by that, the one who rose in atita and became knowledge is completed in turiya, in the ripe fire.
nuance: மானன் and முதிய அனல் (ripe fire) are obscure. The verse seems to say the soul, as knower, matures through the higher states.

reading: Waking has twenty-five with ten; dream, with the twenty-five at hand, is in the throat, they say; the three who saw falsehood, with purusha, are deep sleep; the one who saw the truth, settled in the navel, is two.
nuance: This is a variant of 2142: the states descend through places in the body (brow, throat, heart, navel) with fewer instruments in each. சுழுனையின் may be சுழுத்தி (deep sleep) or சுழுமுனை (the central channel). The counts differ from 2142.

reading: Union with the eightfold subtle body is waking; three in it is dream; two in it is deep sleep; entering one in it is turiya.
nuance: புரியட்டகம் is the subtle body of eight (the five subtle elements with mind, intellect and ego, as tradition counts it). The numbers mark how much of it stays active in each state.

reading: Waking in waking is the ordinary run of things, like flowing water; dream in waking is remembering and forgetting; deep sleep in waking is not searching within; turiya in waking is Nandi in the beyond.
nuance: From here to 2206 each state is divided into the states within it. புனலில் வழக்கம் may mean the habitual flow of life or of the waters of the body; the reading is uncertain.

reading: Seeing in dream as if awake is waking in dream; seeing in dream and forgetting is dream in dream; seeing not-seeing is deep sleep in dream; and turiya comes in inferring and the like.
nuance: அனுமாதி (inference and the other means of knowing) attached to turiya is unexpected; the line may be corrupt or mean that judging what was dreamt is the highest level within dream.

reading: Waking in deep sleep is the appearing that nothing appears; dream in deep sleep is its truth in deep sleep; deep sleep in deep sleep is knowledge destroyed by knowledge; turiya in deep sleep is a void beyond words.
nuance: பாழ் (void, waste) is a term Tirumular uses for states beyond form. The lines read as pointers rather than definitions.

reading: Waking in turiya is the awareness that knows what is good; dream in turiya is the awareness that knows the inner; deep sleep in turiya is the void; turiya in turiya appears itself as the supreme.
nuance: இதம் may be 'the good' or 'this, the present'. வியோமம் (space, void) is a technical term for the pure expanse. தோன்றிடும் is printed கோன்றிடும்.

reading: Knowledge knowing knowledge is waking; knowledge reaching unknowing is dream; that unknowing of knowledge is deep sleep; knowledge becoming knowledge of knowledge is turiya.
nuance: The verse plays on அறிவு and அறியாமை in every line, so the sense rests on wordplay. It reads as the four states seen as states of the soul's knowing.

reading: He who is everywhere, having left the five malas, with knowledge as his form, after delighting in it, leaves even the way of being everywhere and rises above, beyond the subtle and its hues.
nuance: ஐம்மலம் (five malas) extends the usual three. Whether தான் is the freed soul or the Lord is unclear; read here of the soul whose pervasiveness was hidden by the malas.

reading: Twenty-five, six and five more are in waking, aimed at as waking, dream and deep sleep; body, then the subtle, true prakriti, maya and doubt: he is one in that turiya.
nuance: The counts echo 2197. அவன் அத்துரியத்தன் may say that the soul beyond these is in turiya, or that the Lord is; the verse does not settle it.

reading: All this time he did not know what this is; after knowing it he knew nothing else; after knowing the knowledge that knows 'this is it', he is one whose nature is to know it.
nuance: ஈதென்று (as 'this') opens every line. The verse moves from first person (அறிந்திலேன்) to third (இயல்புடையோனே), which may be the speaker describing himself or the knower in general. Knowing it ends other knowing: the knower becomes what knows.

reading: As life of life, with form and without, as union with others, as knowledge and as fullness, the loving Shakti and the Lord are the world and all; without them, all is the delusion of darkness.
nuance: இருண்மூடம் (dark delusion) is read as the soul's state under anava without the Lord's presence. இயற்பின்றி may mean 'without their nature' or 'without their working'.

reading: Making the soul good through the power in raga, the Lord fashioned the fitting bonds, the five malas and the thirty-six distinctions of tattva, and set the instruments, so that the malas may be cut.
nuance: The second half states a Siddhanta teaching: bodies and instruments are given not as further bondage but so that, working through them, the soul can be rid of mala. The first line, சத்தி இராகத்தில், is obscure.

reading: In waking-atita anava is in its own truth; when waking-atita reaches turiya, and anava does not leave in waking-atita, the truth of the Supreme abides in waking-atita.
nuance: சாக்கிராதீதம் opens every line. Tradition distinguishes the atita of the bound soul, a blank under anava, from the atita of the freed, the Supreme's presence. The third line (ஆணவம் தான்விடா) seems to contradict this reading and may be meant as 'when anava has gone'.

reading: By the mixing of mala, Shakti was hidden, knowledge was hidden, Sthanu was hidden; when the mixing of mala ends, there is the light of the moon.
nuance: மலக்கலப்பு (mixture with mala) opens three lines, each naming something hidden. மதியொளி is the moon's light, or the light of understanding; both readings stand.

reading: In the bewildered mind are three lions, in the mocking heart four fox cubs, in the dividing heart five elephant calves, and to the hostile heart the milk is two.
nuance: The animals are symbolic and the verse does not gloss them. Commonly the three lions are taken as the three malas, the four foxes as the four inner instruments, and the five elephant calves as the five senses. பாலிரண்டு (milk, or share, of two) is obscure.

reading: Before the mind, scattering and rising as the eighteen roaring eyes leave, is shaken, if you stand in the true way, there will be an elephant coming with a roar.
nuance: பதினெட்டுக் கண்கள் (eighteen eyes) is unexplained; it may be a count of faculties or of sects. ஆனையும் ஆமே can mean that one becomes like a charging elephant in strength, or that the elephant (the senses or mind) is won; both readings stand.

reading: In waking, twenty fall away; in dream, with the inner instruments; standing at the front, he shook them off and entered within, and without thought stood in deep sleep.
nuance: நாலைந்து (four fives) is the twenty, presumably tattvas. முனவகம் is obscure and may be corrupt. The verse describes the soul passing inward through the states as it drops its instruments.

reading: He who stood so, the teacher, being in turiya, united, taking on the world's rules of discipline, went to the turiya-atita and staying there a while became the Supreme, the stainless one.
nuance: ஆசான் may be the soul as master of itself or the guru; நியமாதி is the yogic niyama and the limbs after it. சிலகாலம் (a while) suggests a stage rather than an end.

reading: That Isa, as vidya in the atita, swallows the world; leaving Sadasiva, the great Shakti and the five forms, he becomes Siva, reaches silence, and is the light of the root.
nuance: The verse may describe the soul rising through the pure tattvas (vidya, Isvara, Sadasiva, Shakti) to Siva. உலகுஉண்டு (having eaten the world) and மூலத்தன் are read here as absorbing the world and being at the source.

reading: Those who have seen within the three regions the good lord of the realm of maya, and pass on contemplating him inwardly, open out; on the lotus, the one above is below, and the cosmos itself is within.
nuance: மண்டலம் மூன்று are traditionally the regions of fire, sun and moon in the body. The syntax of the second and third lines is uncertain.

reading: The flock of birds cried, not knowing the time; women stood confused, not knowing; our Lord stood so that none could know him; those who know the secret wear him on their crown.
nuance: The birds and women may stand for the senses and their objects, or be plain images of not-knowing. வேதுஅறியா may be வேதம் அறியா (the Vedas not knowing). சூது (secret, subtlety) and உச்சி (crown) may point to the crown of the head in yoga.

reading: Knowing the intent, I saw the nine regions fit together there; seeking the Lord of the worlds I knew the great Lord of the gods truly, knew him in his fullness, and stood with mind fixed.
nuance: ஒன்பது கண்டம் may be the nine parts of the earth or nine places in the body. The verse is a first-person testimony, its repeated அறிந்தேன் building to the mind standing still.

reading: As he who kindles the lamp's flame, the lamp's flame is the root practice; in the place of the root, by the rule there, that lamp burns, taking the other, the moon region.
nuance: மூல சாதனம் and மூலத்தானம் point to the muladhara. The lamp lit at the root and fed from the moon region above is traditionally read as the fire of kundalini meeting the moon's nectar; that reading is the tradition's.

reading: If you ask about the open space where the skull of the five who seek inward is gathered, he said: look upward, and at the junction where the five meet the eye's glass sees; that is the intent.
nuance: The five (ஐவர்) are probably the senses drawn inward. அண்ணாந்து பார்த்து (looking up) and the சந்தி (junction) are read as the gaze to the point between or above the brows. கண்நாடி may be the eye as a mirror or a seeking eye.

reading: The knower knows what is not known; one who does not know is not the knower of himself; who can know the knower who knows without knowing, joining the unknowing state to the knower?
nuance: Built on அறி in every phrase, like 2206 and 2209. அறியாதவத்தை may be அறியாத அவத்தை (the unknowing state) or அறியாத தவத்தை. The last line ends in a question that tradition reads as the knower known only by being it.

reading: We have told the vision of turiya: the void, the rare faults, the Brahmin and the rest; beyond great time is turiya, and the rare atita is in the atita itself.
nuance: தூடணம் (faults) and அந்தணவாதி are obscure here; the line may be corrupt. The verse reads as a closing summary of the turiya teaching.

reading: The sentient one in maya is bound to prakriti; removing that other part of maya is itself maya; it becomes kevala; in the womb of sakala maya, the jiva of men immersed there is in turiya.
nuance: கேவலம் and சகலம், the soul's isolated and embodied states, lead into the next chapter (கேவல சகல சுத்தம்). The syntax is uncertain and the last line may mean that even immersed souls have a turiya.

title: கேவல சகல சுத்தம்
theme: The three states of the soul: kevala, alone with anava and knowing nothing; sakala, joined to body, maya and karma; and suddha, purified by grace. The chapter sorts beings by their impurities, subdivides each state into three and maps them onto waking, dream, deep sleep, turiya and the beyond, and holds that bondage and release alike are Hara's grace, by which the soul, with maya as nurse and Siva as father, comes to purity.
structure_note: 2227 to 2236 introduce the three states and the beings in them; 2237 to 2239 the suddha state as the tattvas subside; 2240 to 2248 the classes of soul by their impurities; 2249 to 2254 the ninefold division and the waking states; 2255 to 2257 bondage and release as grace; 2258 to 2261 the states in the body and birth; 2262 to 2265 the way to purity; 2266 to 2268 a riddle, the tattva count and the closing family image.
source_issues: 2230: சீடம் is probably a misprint for கீடம் (worm, insect), as in 2244 (கீடாந்தத்து).
2233: ஒம்மயமாகி is probably ஓம்மயமாகி.
2250: line 3 reads கேவத் திறசுத்தம், apparently corrupt for கேவலத்தில் சுத்தம்.
2258: கழுனை is probably a misprint for சுழுனை (compare 2260).
2262: line 1 reads இருவிடை; the Sengalvaraya parallel and 1527 read இருவினை.
2237, 2246, 2248 and 2260 are obscure throughout and may be corrupt; 2239's நாலேழ் fits no count I can fix.

reading: The pure soul that knows itself, the kevala soul that is alone in itself, and the sakala soul that stands in division and difference are each joined to the real, the unreal and the real-unreal, according to their own work.
nuance: The chapter's three names arrive at once: கேவலன் (alone, with anava only), சகலன் (joined to body and world) and சுத்தன் (pure). சத்து, அசத்து and சதசத்து are traditionally the Lord, the bonds and the soul between them, but line 3 is compressed and I can't fix how each soul is paired with each.

reading: A person is his own enemy and his own friend, his own next world and this one, the one who eats the fruit of the deeds he did, and his own master.
nuance: The fourfold தானே makes the soul answerable for its own state. Placed in a chapter that later says bondage and release both come by Hara's grace (2256), the last line (தனக்குத் தலைவனும்) reads as the soul's responsibility within its bound state, not as a denial of the Lord; that is my reading.

reading: The soul in kevala moves into mahamaya; as maya lights it, it comes to knowledge, and as karma-born and maya-born impurity mingle with it, the bonds it takes on make the sakala state.
nuance: காமியம் and மாமேயம் are taken as காமிய மலம் (the impurity of deeds) and மாயேய மலம் (the impurity of maya's products), which with anava make the three malas. எறிப்ப (strikes, or shines on) leaves open whether maya wakes the soul or wounds it; tradition takes maya as a lamp that gives the soul limited knowledge.

reading: Those who enter the sakala state are the sakalas, joined to all three named impurities: the matchless lotus-born Brahma, Vishnu, the many long-lived gods, humans and everything down to the worm.
nuance: The verse puts the high gods among bound souls with men and insects; status in the cosmos does not lift the three impurities. சீடம் is read as கீடம் (worm, insect), as in 2244.

reading: Those who stay in all-spreading maya are the pralayakalas; of those in the other condition, with bodies, the ones of unfailing marks are Srikantha and, with him, the hundred and eight Rudras.
nuance: பிரளயம் is taken as பிரளயாகலர், souls with two impurities. Srikantha and the 108 Rudras as a class of such beings is a Siddhanta teaching; line 2 (மேவிய மற்றது உடம்பாய்மிக் குள்ளன) is obscure.

reading: Those in kevala who have anava alone are the vidyesvaras, Ananta and the others, the eight, the seventy million mantra beings and the many lords.
nuance: These are the விஞ்ஞானகலர், souls with only anava left. எழுகோடி மந்திரர் are mantras as beings, not formulas. The repeated ஆகின்ற (that become) keeps the list a list of states, not of persons.

reading: Among them, those who have received Siva's grace leave behind the praised bindu and nada as their impurity departs, become one with Om and are absorbed; being stainless, that is the work of the flawless suddha state.
nuance: Bindu and nada, elsewhere the source of manifestation, are here something to be left behind. ஒம்மயம் is read as ஓம்மயம் (made of Om); ஒடுங்கல் is absorption or subsidence.

reading: On inquiry there are three kinds and four kinds; these are kevala, maya and joined desire, which by their nature depart, and the Lord, gathering them up and setting them aside, cut away the impurity.
nuance: மூவகை நால்வகை and சேர்இச்சை are obscure: perhaps three classes of souls and four impurities, with இச்சை standing for karma. The last line is clear: the Lord removes the impurity.

reading: Leaving the false end of knowing and the thirty-six behind, so that ignorance departs, becoming the one he reached, entering the space that is the real moving and unmoving world, reaching without reaching: that is called the suddha state.
nuance: ஆறாறு is the thirty-six tattvas. பொய்யான போதாந்தம் (the false end of knowing) may be knowledge that ends in the instruments, as against Siva-knowledge. எய்தாமல் எய்தும் is a deliberate paradox: union without arriving anywhere.

reading: This soul, beginningless and bound, is driven by the five impurities that came without beginning; from beginningless kevala it is placed in sakala, and through beginningless births it comes into the suddha state.
nuance: அனாதி begins every line: soul, impurities, kevala and births are all without beginning, yet the movement ends in purity. The five impurities are counted again in 2253 and 2257; tradition adds மாயேயம் and திரோதாயி to the three. பசுவியாத்தி is unclear.

reading: Within the suddha state, beyond the kevala, as knowledge arises in the midst of turiya toward the supreme, one knows oneself by oneself, and that is the reality.
nuance: Lines 1 and 2 (அந்தரம் ... தற்பரத்தின்பால்) are obscure and I have kept only their drift. தத்துவம் here seems to mean the truth itself, not a tattva in the list.

reading: The twenty-five subside in the soul, and the soul too, seeing the truth, finds release in the suddha state; the three pure tattvas beginning with vidya, the ancient Shakti and the lord Siva appear in that order.
nuance: ஐஐந்து (five fives) is taken as twenty-five lower tattvas. The pure tattvas are traditionally suddha vidya, isvara, sadakhya, shakti and siva, which fits வித்தை முதன்மூன்றும் with Shakti and Siva.

reading: The twenty-five and the six subside into the soul, the three above are reached in true yoga, and seeing the Shakti held in Siva's portion, one subsides as one reaches the four-sevens.
nuance: 25 + 6 + 3 approaches the thirty-six with Shakti and Siva, but நாலேழ் (four sevens, twenty-eight, or four and seven) does not fit any count I can fix. சிவபாகம் may be Siva's half, the Shakti who is his left side.

reading: Those with anava alone, who know nothing, are the kevalas; those who hold maya are the pralayakalas; and those who take on all three bonds are the sakalas, who have visible form and see without seeing.
nuance: காணும் உருவினர் காணாமை காண்பவே may mean the sakalas see only with bodily eyes and so do not truly see. The verse is a key to the chapter's classes.

reading: For the vijnanakalas the impurity is anava; for the pralayakalas, maya; for the sakalas, anava, maya and karma, all three, are the impurities shown.
nuance: Later Siddhanta texts give the pralayakalas anava and karma, without maya, since maya is dissolved at pralaya. This verse, with 2240 and 2243, ties them to maya instead. Whether that is an older scheme or a looser use of மாயை I can't say.

reading: The vijnanakalas rise within kevala by the power of bindu that rises there, and the mantra beings who pass from kevala into sakala in the world have mahamaya as their truth.
nuance: பூவயின் (in the world, or in the flower) and the syntax of lines 3 and 4 are unclear. The tradition makes mahamaya (pure maya, bindu) the field of the higher beings, as impure maya is of the sakalas.

reading: The pralayakalas who dwell in maya come so that maya does not appear, and those in the maya-sakala of anava, karma and mahamaya are called the hundred and eight Rudras.
nuance: ஏயமன் is obscure, and the relation of the 108 Rudras to 2231 is not settled by the verse.

reading: Those whom the three impurities join, embrace and bewilder are the sakalas of that body: gods, devas and men, and truly, from Brahma down to the many insects, sakalas enter wombs in due order and are bound.
nuance: யோனிபுக்கு (entering the womb) makes sakala the state of birth itself. The list from வேதா to கீடம் matches 2230.

reading: Those steeped in the suddha state become pure when the three impurities, real and unreal, run off, and each bond in turn, the maddening darkness, is let go entirely by the ray that is Siva.
nuance: மத்த இருள் (intoxicating darkness) is traditionally anava, and சிவனான கதிர் the light of grace. சத்துஅசத்து may name the impurities as both real and unreal, or the soul's two sides.

reading: Tat-kevala is release, solitude itself; afterward sakala is separation from kala and the rest; the suddha-kevala named in words is waking, and what one does within oneself is one's own purity.
nuance: Each line pairs a technical name with a gloss I can't fix. The verse seems to begin the subdivision of each state that 2249 to 2252 set out.

reading: Kevala is the soul without knowledge, not joined to raga and the other tattvas, without any mark, eternal, unjoined to kala, without action, and pervaded by impurity.
nuance: முத்தன் (freed) at the start seems ironic: the kevala soul is 'free' of the tattvas only because it has nothing. தினங்கற்ற வல்லோன் கிறியன் is obscure.

reading: Bindu and maya, the kriya that comes with them, the ever-present supreme power of knowledge and the purifying of the body; the pralayakalas who gain the true knowledge of bindu; and the sakala and suddha souls who come into the world.
nuance: The verse is a list without a main verb, and I can't tell how its items relate. It may be naming what belongs to each class of soul.

reading: If the divisions of kevala and the others are told, the three kevalas rise within sakala, and there the three of suddha too, so that the unceasing nine are known to those who perceive them.
nuance: The next three verses set out the nine: kevala, sakala and suddha, each within each. Line 3 (மதிசுத்த மூடவே) is obscure.

reading: Kevala within kevala is the beyond-beyond; sakala within kevala is the bindu-born state; suddha within kevala belongs to the faultless vijnanakalas, and there the Lord is the form of grace.
nuance: அதீதாதீதம் and வயிந்தவம் are technical. Line 3 reads கேவத் திறசுத்தம், taken as கேவலத்தில் சுத்தம்.

reading: Kevala within sakala is the state beyond waking; sakala within sakala is waking within waking; suddha within sakala is the state of the supreme; these three natures are within sakala.
nuance: Here the three states meet the five of waking, dream, deep sleep, turiya and beyond. சாக்கிரசாக்கிரம் (waking in waking) is ordinary bound life at its fullest.

reading: Suddha within suddha is becoming the ancient Siva; kevala within suddha is the ancient stillness; sakala within suddha is the play of turiya; these three too can be told within suddha.
nuance: உபசாந்தம் (stillness) and துரிய விலாசம் (turiya's play) are technical. The highest of the nine is becoming Siva, which I have marked as union.

reading: Within waking-in-waking there is also dream; within waking there is deep sleep and turiya; in the state beyond waking there is easeful bliss; and the five impurity-bonds, concealment and the rest, make these.
nuance: The waking states are nested inside waking, which is the jagrat-avastha scheme of Siddhanta as tradition gives it. மறையாதி (concealing and the rest) is taken as the concealing power, திரோதாயி, among the five.

reading: In the state beyond waking, anava itself is cut off; that state does not remain in the para state; the stillness it brings, transcending, looks on the impurities and qualities and sees them.
nuance: Lines 2 to 4 are obscure. பரோபதி may be 'beyond adjuncts'. The sense may be that the freed state witnesses the impurities without being bound by them.

reading: Once one knows by grace that it is the Father's grace that, unseen, consumes bondage and release, the turiya that holds them and pure atita, there is no mind of one's own and no action of one's own.
nuance: தோன்றாமல் தானுணும் (consumes them unseen) makes even the states of the soul the working of grace. அருளால் அறிந்தபின்: the knowing too is by grace. The end of mind and action is the sign, not the means.

reading: Bondage and release, as they are called, both come by Hara's grace, as play and as the way that brings the soul to purity; so the soul comes to know in the Lord.
nuance: The verse calls bondage itself grace (அருளே) and play (விளையாட்டு). In Siddhanta the impurities are bound to the soul so that they may ripen and fall; that is the tradition's account of why bondage could be called grace.

reading: Those with five impurities are the sakalas reckoned; those with five impurities are bound by hard deeds; those with five impurities go on the path to heaven; those with five impurities are those who know Hara.
nuance: The repeated ஐம்மலத்தார் places even heaven-goers under the impurities. The last line can mean that those still bound come to know Hara, or that they are known to him; neither reading is settled by the verse.

reading: In the womb maya mixes in the beyond state; rare turiya and the desire that feeds in it, the sushumna and the first eight in the subtle body, and rare dream and the gross body are those.
nuance: The verse maps the states onto the embryo and the body. கழுனை is read as சுழுனை (sushumna, or deep sleep), and எட்டும் சூக்கத்து as the eight of the subtle body; the last line is obscure.

reading: Anava is in the beyond state; above it maya is borne in turiya; deep sleep has false karma; dream holds mahamaya; and the concealing power is seen in waking, where the impurities mix.
nuance: Each of the five states is matched with one of five impurities. Where திரோதாயி belongs, with dream or with waking, depends on how line 3 is divided.

reading: The knower beginning from Hara is in the beyond state; maya, from Hara on, stays in deep sleep; those who knew karma and took up mahamaya, and those who tell of grace, are in sakala.
nuance: I can't make the syntax of this verse sure. It seems to place kinds of knowers and impurities across the states, as 2258 and 2259 do.

reading: In sakala the soul takes a body, meets experience and what is experienced, settles among the elements, mind and the rest, holds to their working, dwells among sound and the other objects, and comes into the womb.
nuance: போகம் and போக்கியம் are the enjoying and the enjoyed. The verse lists the sakala soul's equipment in order, ending at birth.

reading: When the two deeds balance and sweet grace-power enters, establishing a seat in knowledge and taking the guru, grace-power joins one to itself, the great impurity goes, and purity is non-birth.
nuance: இருவினை ஒப்பு (balance of the two deeds) and the descent of grace-power (சத்திநிபாதம்) are traditionally the conditions for the guru's coming. The verse nearly repeats 1527. Line 1 reads இருவிடை, taken as இருவினை.

reading: When the soul reaches the end, the beyond-turiya, past the thirty-six, the six and the twenty-five with their states, the five who were his gain fade in the light, and ash-adorned supreme Siva comes to dwell in him.
nuance: ஐவர் are traditionally the five deities presiding over the states, who withdraw. ஆதேயம் (what is held or placed in something) is taken as Siva becoming the content of the soul; the numbers in line 1 are uncertain.

reading: Not knowing himself, he first took the body as himself; when he first saw himself, he saw turiya; but if the turiya he contemplates is not made one with the Lord, he will be born again.
nuance: Three steps: body taken for self, self seen as turiya, turiya joined to the Lord. The verse warns that self-knowledge stopped at the second step still leads to birth.

reading: If the beyond state is reached within waking, the bindu-born state it brings is bliss; looming birth is cut off, firm release is attained, and speech and mind do not reach it.
nuance: சாக்கிராதீதம் (beyond in waking) is traditionally taken as release while living in the body. வயிந்தவம் (bindu-born) here seems to name a pure state, not a bond.

reading: Water and fire come within the breast; water and fire do not come within the breast; if you ask what water and fire are within the breast, they are water and fire mingled, that way.
nuance: A riddle. அகலம் is breast or expanse, and அகல் a lamp, which holds oil and flame. Water and fire are taken symbolically as moon and sun, Shakti and Siva, or white bindu and red nada (compare 1929); none of these is stated.

reading: Twenty-four are impure, seven pure-impure belong with maya, and five are pure; divided in these three parts, they are maya, mahamaya and what goes with the soul.
nuance: The count 24 + 7 + 5 = 36 is the standard Siddhanta grouping of the tattvas. Which group line 4 assigns to the soul is not clear.

reading: With maya as foster mother, mahamaya giving birth, and supreme Siva standing as father, the soul passes through kevala and sakala, and the purity it seeks comes to it of itself.
nuance: கைத்தாய் is the nurse or foster mother. The family image gathers the chapter: the soul is raised through impure maya, born of pure maya and fathered by Siva, and the bound states are its upbringing. தான்வந்து அடையுமே: purity comes, it is not seized.

title: பராவத்தை
theme: The supreme states (பராவத்தை): the soul's states of waking, dream, deep sleep and turiya are traced up through grades to Siva's own turiya, where, beyond the thirty-six tattvas and by grace, the bonds fall away and the soul becomes one with Siva. Images of gold and ornament, wood and elephant show how the Supreme and the world each hide the other.
structure_note: The Lord beyond the five and the thirty-six (2269 to 2271); the grades of turiya, from the soul's to Siva's, with the union they lead to (2272 to 2285); the Lord's descending order (2286); self-knowledge and mutual concealment (2287 to 2290); the five-letter mantra and the pure supreme state in which the malas end (2291 to 2295).
source_issues: 2290: line 4 reads பரத்தை மறைந்தது, where the pattern of line 2 and of 2289 needs பரத்தின் (or பரத்தில்) மறைந்தது.
2272: நஞ்சுற (so that poison enters) fits the image poorly and may be corrupt, perhaps for நெஞ்சுற.

reading: I came to know how the beginningless supreme God beyond the five, the stainless unborn one who became the heart, stayed hidden so as to set the body and the soul apart.
nuance: அஞ்சும் கடந்த (beyond the five) is not explained: the five senses, the five states or the five malas are all possible. வஞ்சத்து இருந்த (stayed in concealment) suggests the Lord's hiding act, but the verse doesn't name it.

reading: The verse lists Shakti in her grades, as Paraparai, in peace (சாந்தி), in supreme bliss, as radiant bindu, as true maya and with the body's five powers, and the soul that receives Shakti makes the sixth in the limbs.
nuance: The line divisions and the count (ஐந்துடன், ஆறுமே) are obscure; சாந்தி may be one of the kalas and சத்திய மாயை is perhaps pure maya. Only the general sense, Shakti descending in grades to the embodied soul, is secure.

reading: Those who know are beyond the thirty-six; those who receive grace are beyond it; for them knowledge is beyond it, and beyond it Hara is sweet.
nuance: ஆறாறு (six sixes) is the usual way of naming the thirty-six tattvas. The refrain makes the point by repetition: knowing, grace and the sweetness of Siva all lie past the constituents of body and world.

reading: Passing the five and the four and entering within, the king of the vidyadharas, asleep on his soft bed, seeks out the gentle woman with longing and takes his pleasure.
nuance: A plain erotic image with a symbolic sense: the five and the four are usually taken as the five senses and the four inner instruments, the sleeping king as the soul in the yogic sleep of turiya, and the woman as Shakti. நஞ்சுற (so that poison enters) is hard to fit; it may be a corruption, perhaps of நெஞ்சுற (with the heart).

reading: In the waking proper to turiya she (Shakti) is present; across waking and the two after it lies the rare turiya; in the vast para-turiya is the Supreme; and in the turiya reached by turning back, Siva.
nuance: நனாத்துரியம், பரதுரியம் and the turiya reached by turning (திரிய) are technical grades of the states, assigned here to Shakti, the Supreme and Siva. How the second line fits the scheme is unclear.

reading: The Supreme, the state beyond (அதீதம்), is grasped as attachment ends and becomes one's own as one practises it again and again; ascetics who don't practise it don't become the Supreme, since not one of their bonds and attachments ends.
nuance: பற்றறப் பற்ற plays on பற்று: one grasps the Supreme by letting go of grasping. The verse is aimed at ascetics (தபோதனர்) whose austerity lacks this practice.

reading: False maya, which one examines, stands inside and outside; if one passes beyond breath and mind and that confusion ends, pure knowledge becomes the bliss of Siva and itself grows into the reality that covers all.
nuance: வேயும் பொருள் (the thing that covers or roofs) is obscure; it may mean the reality that pervades everything. வாயு is the breath, stilled with the mind in yoga.

reading: The Lord set the soul that rode the horse of turiya inside the great tiger and drove the jackals running, and the deeds bound to that soul stood there and wailed.
nuance: Wholly symbolic: the jackals are usually taken as the senses or the malas, the tiger as Siva or his grace, and the wailing deeds as karma left without a hold. The verse does not name any of these.

reading: In this waking that stands in long turiya, the Lord of the hall stands ready to marry; when he marries, maya vanishes, and that day this soul takes his form.
nuance: மன்றன் is Siva of the hall (அம்பலம்) where he dances. Marriage stands for the soul's union with him, and அவன்வடிவாமே for the soul taking Siva's form. சாக்கிர நீள்துரியம் is a technical state.

reading: When waking spreads out it becomes like a lamp; where it stays, maya stands to match it; the turiya one enters becomes one's own working, and in the turiya one comes to know, evil does not remain.
nuance: The last words தீதுஅகலாதே can mean 'evil does not leave' as easily as 'evil leaves without fail', and the two give opposite senses; the context of the chapter favours the second, but the text does not decide it. ஈடான and புரியல்தானாகும் are also obscure.

reading: Not knowing you, I once took myself to be one with the body; knowing you, you stood with me in turiya; and since birth does not end merely by knowing oneself, know that the one who pervades is the Stainless.
nuance: The verse separates knowing oneself, which does not end rebirth, from knowing the pervading Lord (வியாத்தன்). The shifts of person (I, you, oneself) make the speaker and addressee hard to fix.

reading: While the body, bounded by the womb, and turiya are two, the two pass through birth and death; once those who have the guru's boon unite, there are no longer two, and they stand as one.
nuance: இருவரும் (the two) is read here as the body and turiya, but it can also be the soul and the Lord, which makes the last line a statement of union. Either way the guru's grace (குருவரம்) is what ends the duality.

reading: In the soul's turiya there is waking, in the soul's stirring there is dream, in its stillness the para-atita as deep sleep, and in service para-turiya is the Supreme.
nuance: அணு is the soul as atom-like, the bound soul. The verse maps the ordinary states onto higher ones, and பணியில் (in service, or in humility) is obscure.

reading: In para-turiya there is a waking that spreads, a dream that has swallowed the wide world, a true peace and a deep sleep that takes form; as these cease, one is seen to be in Siva's turiya.
nuance: The verse sets out the four states again at the higher level of para-turiya. Each name (சாந்தி, சுழுத்தி) is technical, and the exact grades are the tradition's.

reading: After the supreme waking come the steady dream that has eaten the world, the excellent deep sleep and the strong upasanta calm; to reach these is renunciation, and one becomes the bearer of Siva's turiya.
nuance: A near-variant of 2282. உபசாந்தம் is a technical name for a state of calm; துறவே may mean renunciation itself or 'by renouncing'.

reading: From the soul's turiya up to Siva's turiya-end, the ten states cease in their order; dwelling in the truth of supreme Nandi, he stood having freed the soul from the twenty-eight.
nuance: அவத்தைபத்தும் (the ten states) and நாலேழ் (four sevens, twenty-eight, or four and seven) are counts from the tradition's scheme that the verse doesn't spell out.

reading: Above Paramasiva is the Paramam; in that Para, Paramasiva above becomes the supreme waking; the sushumna that ends the distress of the spreading dream gives strength: this is the truth of great Nandi.
nuance: கழுமுனை is the sushumna, the central channel of yoga. The ordering of Paramasiva and Paramam is the tradition's and the syntax of the verse is loose.

reading: When seen, the order runs: Paramasiva who is the support, Shakti, supreme nada, bindu above it and Sadasiva rising high, then below them Brahma, Hari, the god of the immortals' city, Rudra and Isa.
nuance: A list of Siva's descending forms in Siddhanta. பாலாய் may mean 'below' or 'as milk'; அமராபதி தேவாம் (the god of Amaravati) would usually be Indra, an odd entry here, so it may describe one of the others.

reading: Those who don't know the union, nor the end of the seven sea-girt worlds, nor how the soul stands with the body, and cannot rule here having understood the turmoil, aim only at outward show and force.
nuance: கலப்பு (mingling) may be the soul's union with Siva or the mixing of soul and body. அலப்பு, அரசாளகிலாதார் and the last line (குறிப்பது கோலம் அடலது வாமே) are obscure; this reading is a guess.

reading: If one knows oneself through the truth of great austerity that is known afterwards, the compassionate Supreme is our Lord; and when former knowledge comes to its end, I set out to know myself and so came to joy.
nuance: The traditional saying that one who knows oneself knows the Lord fits this verse, but the first line is hard to construe. முன்னை அறிவு (former knowledge) may be the bound soul's ordinary knowing.

reading: The gold ornament hides the gold, and the gold ornament disappears into the gold; one's own instruments hide oneself, and one's instruments disappear into oneself.
nuance: Seen as an ornament, the gold is not noticed; seen as gold, the ornament is not. So too the soul and its faculties (கரணங்கள்): attention to one hides the other. தன் is usually taken as the soul.

reading: The great rutting elephant hides the wood, and the elephant disappears into the wood; the elements beginning with earth hide the Supreme, and the elements disappear into the Supreme.
nuance: The image is a wooden elephant: one who sees the elephant doesn't see the wood, and one who sees the wood doesn't see the elephant. Seeing the world hides the Lord in it; seeing the Lord, the world vanishes into him.

reading: Passing beyond the thirty-six and leaving 'na-ma', the soul becomes knowledge and, standing apart, rises as 'ya'; reaching the Tatpara free of darkness beyond Para, release follows, gathered in 'Si-va-ya'.
nuance: The verse reads the five-letter mantra (நமசிவாய) as a path: dropping நம, traditionally the syllables of the bonds, leaves சிவாய, in which ய is the soul. The letter symbolism is the tradition's and the syntax is compressed.

reading: In turiya the five are the letters beginning with A; in Para spreading out, nada and its end prevail; in Para there is the awareness of the supreme state, and as it turns, the supreme turiya becomes clear.
nuance: அகராதி (the letters from A) may be the five letters of the mantra or the parts of Om. பராவத்தா போதம் names the chapter's subject, but the verse gives no clear account of it.

reading: By grace the five states in the sakala condition cease to work; in the stirring of the pure state, as one seeks Nandi's supreme state, the five malas leave like evening darkness before a flame.
nuance: சகலம் (the embodied condition) and சுத்தம் (the pure) are two of the soul's three conditions in Siddhanta. ஐம்மலம் counts five malas, where the tradition often counts three. The darkness-and-light simile is plain.

reading: When the purusha sees through the twenty-five, measured prakriti, maya and the great maya seen to be false, and becomes all of them and none of them, the saving supreme state is reached: to contemplate it is purity.
nuance: ஐஐந்து (five fives) is taken as the twenty-five lower tattvas. எய்யும் படியாய் (so as to shoot through, or to attain) is obscure.

reading: The Lord of nada in good knowledge is the one in whom his grace, the Supreme and the love that came first become one, in whom form and limiting adjunct merge, and who left me and went there yet did not go.
nuance: உபாதி (limiting adjunct) is a technical term. The paradox of going and not going (சென்றான், செல்லாமை) may be the Lord's transcendence and immanence; the verse's construction is loose.

title: முக்குண நிர்க்குணம்
theme: The three gunas and the gunaless (முக்குண நிர்க்குணம்): the states of the soul are matched with the gunas, sattva with waking, rajas with dream, tamas with deep sleep, while turiya is the stainless state beyond all three.

reading: When sattva is said to belong to waking, rajas is held to be dream and tamas deep sleep; the gunaless state that puts an end to them is stainless turiya.
nuance: The mapping of the gunas onto the states is the verse's own. ஒய்த்திடும் is an unusual form, perhaps 'that wears down' or 'that stills', and மாய்த்திடும் (that destroys) can belong either to the gunaless state or to turiya.

title: அண்டாதி பேதம்
theme: The divisions of the cosmic eggs (அண்டாதி பேதம்): the world-spheres are as many as the sands of the seven seas, all under the Lord seated on them, and the tattvas spread through them in fixed multiples.
source_issues: 2298: line 2 reads பத்தாறாய்க், with a stray க் before தான்.

reading: The outer cosmic egg and the eggs divided within it, as many as the grains of sand of the seven wave-tossed seas, shine like sparks of light and gold ornaments, and the Lord of the gods sits on them as his seat.
nuance: பகிரண்டம் is the outer egg enclosing the worlds. அண்டாசனம் (the egg as seat) is taken here as the Lord enthroned over the cosmos; the sand of the seas is a conventional figure for numberless worlds.

reading: Above the cosmic mountain the bliss tattva, with five bodies, pervades as the thirty-six; the endless tattvas it becomes are eightfold in the flawless egg.
nuance: ஆனந்த தத்துவம், அண்டாசலம் (cosmic mountain, or perhaps அண்டாசனம் again), the five bodies and the eightfold multiple are cosmological terms the verse doesn't explain.

title: பதினோராம் தானமும் அவத்தையெனக் காணல்
theme: The eleventh station seen as a state (பதினோராம் தானமும் அவத்தையெனக் காணல்): counted centres in the body yield nectar, bliss and Om, and the eleven stations are themselves states of the soul; held firmly, they leave nothing but Nandi.
source_issues: 2299: line 4 reads கிஞ்சுகக் செவ்வாய், a misprint for கிஞ்சுகச் செவ்வாய்.

reading: In the fifth there is nectar, in the seventh bliss, in the ninth Om, and in the eleventh, if one sets it and holds it there by craft, it becomes the body: listen, you with lips red as kinchuka flowers and the speech of a parrot.
nuance: The numbers are taken as stations or centres in the yogic body, which the verse does not name. முஞ்சில் is obscure, and வஞ்சகமே நின்று (standing by guile, or by craft) and காயமாம் (becomes the body, or becomes firm) are uncertain. The addressee is a woman, often taken as Shakti.

reading: The mind joined with purusha, the formless with the six, turiya beyond, and the eight that abound in spreading deep sleep: these are the rare eleven states.
nuance: The verse names the eleven stations as states, but how its items add up to eleven is not clear from the text.

reading: When the eleven that are shown come together and one fixes and presses the body down, there is nothing but Nandi; think on that rule which does not waver: what it gathers is firmness, and thought becomes possible.
nuance: உடல் நாட்டி அழுத்திடின் (fixing and pressing the body) sounds like a yogic posture or lock. The last line is loose; ஈட்டும் அது திடம் may mean the practice gains steadiness.

title: கலவு செலவு
theme: Joining and going (கலவு செலவு): the soul's passage from the kevala condition, through the sakala, to removal of the bonds ends in the pure state beyond waking; give up anger, direct the mind, and rest in grace, and even stone splits into open space.
source_issues: 2303: line 2 reads செலுத்துமிஹ், a misprint for செலுத்துமின்.

reading: Joining in the kevala condition, going in the sakala, and the removal that comes as they leave: when one sees oneself spread through these, the three cease to spread, and in the faultless waking-beyond there is purity.
nuance: கேவலம், சகலம் and சுத்தம் are the soul's three conditions in Siddhanta: alone with its mala, embodied, and pure. Whether மூன்றும் is these three conditions or the three malas is not settled by the verse.

reading: While you can still win, let go of anger; as far as it will go, direct this mind; if night and day you rest in grace, even stone will split open and become the vast space.
nuance: வெல்லும் அளவில் (while you can prevail) puts the test of giving up anger where it has power, as the Kural does. தூங்கினால் (if you sleep, or rest, or hang on) may point to yogic sleep in grace. கல் may be the hard heart, and கடுவெளி the open space taken as Siva's. Sengalvaraya notes a near-parallel line in Kandar Alankaram 15.

title: நின்மல அவத்தை
theme: The pure states (நின்மல அவத்தை): when waking, dream and deep sleep subside into turiya and beyond, and grace removes malam, the soul knows itself as the knower, beyond the inert tattvas, and becomes one with Siva. The soul knows only as grace illumines it; one Shakti feeds desire and then withers it; the freed leave heaven and hell behind, and even what is vain, known through grace, is grace.
structure_note: Withdrawal and passing beyond the elements (2304 to 2306); the states, turiya and what survives it (2307 to 2314); the Lord within and self-knowledge given by the guru (2315 to 2331); Shakti and grace in bondage and release (2332 to 2344); the reaching of Siva and those who reach (2345 to 2354). The grouping is mine; many verses are built on a repeated opening word (2312, 2319, 2321, 2330, 2336, 2339, 2340).
source_issues: 2310 line 4: ஆன மாலதீதம் is obscure; possibly a form of மலாதீதம் (beyond malam).
2314 line 4: பலராவே does not give the expected sense (fade) and may be corrupt.
2347 line 3: தலைப்ட்ட is a misprint for தலைப்பட்ட.
2353 line 2: குறிஅறி யார்கடம் may be divided wrongly (யார்கள் தம் or யார் கடம்).
2335 line 2: இல்லதம் is likely a misprint for இல்லதும்.

reading: Inside a silent well lives a tortoise with five hollows within it; if it withdraws into truth without slipping, it lives a thousand years beyond a tortoise's span.
nuance: ஊமைக் கிணறு (the dumb or silent well) is commonly taken as the body or its inner cavity, and the tortoise drawing in its five as the soul withdrawing the five senses. அழுவைகள் is obscure (hollows, depths). The last line may promise long life to the yogi; the plain and the symbolic readings both stand.

reading: For those who can run past the five above, the elements of air, fire, water and earth with space and the gods Mal, Isan, Brahma and Sadasivan, and mingle beyond them, there is no Death and no thought of their own.
nuance: The gods are traditionally the rulers of the five elements; அங்கி (fire) in line 2 may be a god's name or the element repeated. மேலஞ்சும் ஓடி (running over the five) is taken as passing through the centres of the elements in the body. கருத்தில்லை may mean freedom from the thinking mind or simply 'no concern'.

reading: People do not grasp what the great Veda declares in saying the self became the son; if the self is called Hara's son, then the self as separate is gone and so are the twenty-five.
nuance: The first line seems to echo the Vedic saying that the self is born as one's son. ஐஐந்து (five fives) is taken as the twenty-five tattvas. The argument is compressed and I can't fix whether it affirms or refutes the Vedic claim.

reading: When rising ceases, the three states of waking, dream and deep sleep subside; the conscious soul, held by the Lord in turiya, becomes supremely auspicious and endless at its close.
nuance: சாக்கிரம் (waking), கனவு (dream), சுழுத்தி (deep sleep) and துரியம் (the fourth) are the standard states of the soul. உதயம் அழுங்கில் (when rising is checked) and அந்தி (the close, or twilight) are unclear; பதிதரு சேதனன் may be 'the conscious one given by the Lord' or 'the conscious one who attains the Lord'.

reading: When everything enters into oneself and one becomes all, and one dwells in good turiya, the good soul does not go into the evil thirty-six but becomes awareness and reaches Siva's state, from which there is no going.
nuance: ஆறாறு is the thirty-six tattvas, called பொல்லாத (evil) as what binds. செல்லாச் சிவகதி may be 'the Siva-state not reached by going' or 'from which one does not leave'.

reading: As heated iron, even after the fire is taken away, keeps a heat like fire, so in turiya, where the instruments have died away, the stain of karma steeped in does not leave.
nuance: வாதனை (vasana) is the impression a deed leaves behind. The verse warns that reaching turiya does not by itself remove karma's residue; I read it as a check on the confidence of 2308.

reading: Nandi, whose form is the Veda and the rest, came and gave grace in the clear waking state; when the states as they came are closed and let go, that state beyond delusion is the Supreme.
nuance: தெரிநனா அவத்தை (the clear or discerning waking state) is taken as the waking state of the freed soul. ஆன மாலதீதம் is obscure: மால் அதீதம் (beyond delusion) or a form of மலாதீதம் (beyond malam).

reading: If the pure state beyond touches the embodied state, the Father's grace does not leave; there, being oneself, practising a samadhi that does not touch the mind's pleasure, grace becomes the first step to being one with the Father.
nuance: சுத்த அதீதம் (the pure beyond) and சகலம் (the soul's embodied state) are technical terms. சித்த சுகம் is taken as the pleasure of the mind, which this samadhi does not seek.

reading: He divided the whole of the body into two halves, set me apart and sent me everywhere; then, leaving me in kevala with a grace that does not divide, the Father who makes no division came and stayed joined with me.
nuance: வேறுசெய் opens every line: twice the Lord separates, twice he does not. இரு பாதியின் மெய்த்தொகை may be the body's two halves or the two kinds of bond. கேவலம் is the soul's isolated state, bound only by anava.

reading: Like a whirling leaf-wheel, a firebrand swung in a circle, waves on the sea or a churning stick in curds, the soul stays in its malam and is turned through heaven, hell and earth according to its deeds; by grace it is freed of these.
nuance: All four images are of endless turning in one place. அறங்காண் (seen by deeds) and கிரங்கா (perhaps 'not grieving' or 'unsteady') are unclear, so who is freed and how exactly is not fixed.

reading: When the state of oneself becoming Siva is reached, malam, the kinds of bond, the gunas and the soul's limiting adjuncts fade like the moon before the sun.
nuance: உபாதி is the limiting adjunct. The last word பலராவே is unclear; the sun and moon image needs a sense like 'grow faint', and I take it so.

reading: Fire, water and air are there; the sun and the moon dwell there; worthy Mal, four-faced Brahma and Rudra's light are all within the heart.
nuance: Plainly, the elements, the lights and the gods are within. Tradition also reads the sun and moon as the right and left breath channels and the gods as rulers of centres in the body; that reading is symbolic and not fixed by the verse.

reading: For one who tames the five elephants, lights the wick of knowledge, enters it and looks at the flesh until its darkness is gone, the way to climb to the sky is easy.
nuance: The five elephants are the senses. The flesh (ஊன்) is not despised but looked into until it is lit. வானகம் may be heaven, release, or the space at the crown of the head of yogic practice.

reading: The breath that sways the dancing foot, the sound of the damaru rising as it is struck, and the Vedas and Agamas rising in song: this is how I saw them within the nadi.
nuance: Siva's dance with its drum and the scriptures it sounds are placed within the body's channel. Whether this is a vision in practice or an image for the dance in the body is not fixed.

reading: The ancient austerity done in an earlier understanding can be known once the later understanding is gained; knowing oneself is knowledge, and anything else known afterwards is a ghoul's knowledge.
nuance: முன்னை அறிவு and பின்னை அறிவு play on earlier and later knowing; one reading is that tapas of past lives bears fruit as present insight. பேயறிவு (a ghoul's knowledge) is blunt contempt for knowing that leaves out the self.

reading: Being without action is Siva's bliss; those who rest without action do not seek Siva-yoga, do not mingle with the world, and only they have the work done.
nuance: செயலற்றிருத்தல் is traditionally taken as giving up one's own agency to the Lord, not idleness. செய்தியுண்டாம் is open: 'there is achievement' or 'there are tidings'. Even seeking Siva-yoga is counted as action.

reading: If the samadhi in which oneself becomes Him is reached, malam is cut off and that bound-soul nature goes; for those who remove the eight defects and become one, the flawless body stays on the great earth.
nuance: The body staying on earth after malam is cut is read as release while living (jivanmukti). ஊனங்கள் எட்டு (eight defects) are not named; they may be the eightfold subtle body or eight bonds.

reading: Hara's unfailing feet and his Shakti, unfailing darkness and light, the soul that appears, and unfailing action and knowledge meet from of old, and the soul is steeped between unfailing bondage and release.
nuance: தொலையா (unfailing, unending) opens every line. அணு (the atom) is the Siddhanta name for the soul; பெத்தம் is bondage. The grammar is loose and the reading is a guess at the joints.

reading: Through the Shakti who encompasses bondage and release as they arise, the soul is now bewildered and now clear; the knowledge she gives becomes the means to her, and a light to the unsupported light within.
nuance: மான்றும் தெருண்டும் (bewildered and cleared) is the soul's state in bondage and in release, both under the same Shakti. ஊன்றல் இல்லா உள்ளொளி may be the soul's own light, which has no footing of its own.

reading: The thirty-five and the one do not know, and I did not know myself, the one who knows; Nandi graced me, saying 'You are the one who knows', and I came to know that I am the knower.
nuance: ஐஏழும் ஒன்றும் (five sevens and one) is taken as the thirty-six tattvas, which in Siddhanta are inert. The guru does not give the soul knowledge but shows it that it is the knower.

reading: What was seen within the flesh: the lord of the knowledge in which oneself becomes Him, first of the gods, the light of a great gem, and the flawless Shakti of sweet grace in faultless knowledge.
nuance: The verse is a list of objects with one verb at the end, கண்டதே (it was seen). Siva and Shakti are both seen within the flesh (ஊனிடை).

reading: Light and darkness and Parai, and what is called tender regard within Parai, are apart from the soul; passing beyond tenderness, grace and clarity, the grace that makes clear is Siva's bliss.
nuance: பரை is the supreme Shakti; அளி (tender regard), அருள் and தெருள் are close words, and the distinctions between them are not explained. The verse seems to rank stages of grace below a final one.

reading: In Hara's grace-Shakti, which is bliss, the soul that has come to its end does samadhi itself; if the flesh ends and one feels within as awareness, the Lord's end is reached: this is the great saying.
nuance: The verse plays on அந்தம் (end): ஆனந்தம், தான் அந்தம், ஊன் அந்தம், கோன் அந்தம். மகாவாக்கியம் (the great saying) is the Vedantic term for the identity statements, here given a Saiva sense; which saying is meant is not stated.

reading: There is no need to teach those who are sunk without knowledge, nor those who are full of knowledge; the wise who know teach only those who, having gained knowledge, stand in unknowing.
nuance: The third group is the fit disciple. அறிவுற்று அறியாமை எய்தி may mean those who have learned enough to know they do not know, or those who have passed through knowledge into a higher unknowing.

reading: Sat, asat and sadasat come together; the conscious and the inert stand as Siva's consciousness; in turiya, where pure and impure do not begin, the pure with the three are beyond words.
nuance: In Siddhanta சத்து (the real) is the Lord, அசத்து the bond and சதசத்து the soul, which takes the nature of what it joins. மூன்றுடன் (with the three) may be these three or three states.

reading: The soul does not know by itself, yet it is not without knowing; it knows, and its knowing is sadasat; so when both stand as Hara's grace, it knows of itself and abides with Siva.
nuance: This is the Siddhanta account of the soul as சதசத்து: it can know, but only when something illumines it. The verse places that illumining in grace.

reading: Only for those who have reached tattva-knowledge does tattva-knowledge stand reached; in tattva-knowledge, as oneself becomes Him, the bliss of tattva-knowledge begins.
nuance: தத்துவ ஞானம் opens every line. It may mean knowledge of the tattvas or knowledge of the real; the verse moves from attaining it to its bliss.

reading: When one knows oneself and becomes oneself with Siva, the abiding malam and gunas die and birth ends; then follows true release, the great light of sanmarga, and the good seal of knowledge is reached.
nuance: சன்முத்தி is taken as true release. ஞானத்து முத்திரை may be a literal hand-seal of the jnani or the sealing of knowledge.

reading: Knowledge is his body, action his middle limbs and the will that reaches him his life; since the Supreme takes this form and is the seed of the five acts, the silent ones obtained the seal of knowledge.
nuance: Jnana, kriya and iccha (knowledge, action, will) are the Lord's three Shaktis; here they are his body, limbs and life. மோனிகள் are the silent sages.

reading: Knowledge is the soul's truth, will its measure, action the soul's, and maya the subtle for the soul; he who feeds these to the soul is the feeder, and he is within that mind, not within the soul's word.
nuance: மானம் (measure) and சூக்கம் (the subtle) are unclear here. The plain point is that the Lord gives the soul its powers and is within it beyond what the soul can say.

reading: The action, will and knowledge of the ancient Siva and of the souls arise from undying Mahamaya and maya; leaving the void of flawless cause and effect, Siva is beyond the undying Santa.
nuance: சாந்தாதீதன் (beyond Santa) names Siva above the highest kala, சாந்தி. That Siva's own powers should come from maya is surprising, and the line may mean only that their workings appear through maya.

reading: The Lord becomes all, what is not and what is, yet is neither not-being nor being; whatever one says of him, he is far beyond far; but understood quickly, he becomes the life of life.
nuance: The verse turns on the gap between saying and understanding: in speech the Lord is ever farther, in understanding the nearest.

reading: Shakti feeds the soul's desire and wanders with it; knowledge withers the soul's desire and ends it; because she feeds it and stays with it, by withering the soul's desire she brings it to the high state.
nuance: உயிரிச்சை (the soul's desire) opens every line. The same Shakti first feeds desire and then withers it; tradition reads this as concealment followed by grace.

reading: Those freed of the five malams become Siva and join him; those not at one remain in the darkness of the five malams, of the kind that go from earth to heaven and hell; no one sees that these too are grace.
nuance: ஐம்மலம் (five malams) is traditionally anava, karma, maya, mayeya and tirodhayi. The last line is taken to say that heaven and hell are themselves grace, a ripening, but the grammar is unsure.

reading: What those who have reached do through the great maya-Shakti, through the great Shakti of knowledge and through the great Shakti of the world: all of it is the Lord's grace.
nuance: இருமாயா may be 'great maya' or 'the two mayas', pure and impure. எய்தினர் (those who have reached) are the freed, whose acts are counted as the Lord's.

reading: The reformed have left wretched hell, left splendid heaven, left the gathering of crowded flowers, and, becoming Siva, left what is vain.
nuance: திருந்தினர் (those set right) opens every line. செறிமலர் கூட்டம் is obscure: the pleasures of the senses, the company of women adorned with flowers, or the world of births. அவம் (the vain) answers சிவம் in sound.

reading: Those who do not know the vain and Siva do not know; those who know the vain and Siva know; if they know the vain and Siva through grace, both the vain and Siva become his grace.
nuance: அவமும் சிவமும் opens every line, pairing the futile with the auspicious. The final claim is that even what is vain, known through grace, is his grace.

reading: Grace-Shakti is like heat in fire; with the substance being He, it joins awareness; darkness turned to light returns as the three malams; the holy grace, the blissful one, is the true substance.
nuance: Heat in fire is the classic image for Shakti inseparable from Siva. Line 3 is unclear: perhaps light can fall back into the three malams, or grace works even through them.

reading: When the sun rises, the lotus and the rest differ in what they do by their deeds; the sun with its rays sets them moving; that it divides without dividing is the distinction of grace.
nuance: One sun opens some flowers and closes others; tradition reads this as one grace working differently on souls by their karma. பதுமாதிகள் is taken as 'lotuses and others'.
