reading: Difference, non-difference and shifting difference-in-non-difference, awareness and joined awareness, awareness and nada, and nada with naga-nada and the nadas that follow: all are the will of the Lord's grace.
nuance: பேதம், அபேதம், பேதாபேதம் are the three ways of relating soul and Lord argued among the schools. நாகநாதம் and the other nadas are technical and I can't fix them. ஆதன் may be the Lord or the soul.

reading: Like the deed that makes a false puppet dance, he makes the elements he spread dance, creating and the rest; through the gathering of earthly things he brings awareness and settles the soul: that is Hara's grace.
nuance: பொய்க்கரி may be a puppet elephant or a false image moved by strings. பூவியல் கூட்டம் is taken as the assembly of earthly things.

reading: He who knew himself, going off without stopping, becoming the end, reaching in himself all that is and is not, separate and entering space, gained release; that confusion reaching a clarity not yet clear, at the touch becomes Siva.
nuance: The grammar is very loose. அம்மருள் தேறாத் தெளிவுற்று (that confusion gaining a clarity not reached by reasoning) is a guess.

reading: Turning again to love of the rare holy feet that are worthy to touch, going by grace along the ordained way, spurring and mounting the great horse of Siva-knowledge and leaping across, one can reach Siva.
nuance: மா here is taken as horse, so Siva-knowledge is a mount one rides across. விதிவழி (the ordained way) may be scriptural rule or the course set by grace.

reading: Those who have reached him are the charanas, the siddhas and those in samadhi; those who achieve true knowledge of the tattvas; the blissful in whom love comes first; and those whose nature is pure grace.
nuance: சாரணர் are heavenly wanderers, சித்தர் the perfected. சத்த அருள் may be 'pure grace' (சுத்த) or 'the grace of sound'.

reading: The tattvas speak of two, oneself and He; in the state where self and He are not two, those in kevala do not think 'I'; to become oneself without a self is the purity of the tattva.
nuance: தான் and அவன் open three lines. கேவலத்தானவர் may be those in the soul's isolated state, who cannot think at all, or those in a pure solitude; the verse seems to set duality, non-duality and a selfless self in order.

reading: The chief who knows himself within himself sets out to know his Lord within himself; if he does not rest in himself, his Lord within him is hard to reach as well.
nuance: தன் ஐ (his master) is taken as the Lord, or the guru; ஐ also suggests the five senses, but 'lord' fits better. Self-knowledge is the way to the Lord, not a rival to him.

reading: Do not cry 'I cannot know'; once you have gone the way of the path and met him face to face, he who can work as the two lights comes as one light within my heart.
nuance: இருசுடர் (two lights) is traditionally the sun and moon, and in yoga the two breaths. The shift from 'you' to 'my heart' is the poet speaking from his own case.

reading: One clay becomes many fine vessels, and in all the wombs one thinks of there is one; one eye sees many things but does not see itself; the Lord stands in just that way.
nuance: Two images: the clay present in all its pots, and the eye that sees all but itself. ஒருவனே may be the Lord in all wombs or the one soul passing through them.

reading: He guards the seven worlds from within; some close up and speak of him through qualities; those who do not think of Siva waste away; those who do not close up can come and receive him.
nuance: கூம்பு is to close like a flower, or to fold the hands in worship. Whether closing is narrowing the mind or worshipping is unclear, and the verse's contrast depends on it.

reading: Those who do not know the mark cannot see the mark; for those who do not know it, union is a great matter; unite in a way the mark is not known, and having united, stay without knowing knowledge, and you become the swan too.
nuance: குறி (mark, sign, target) is unexplained; it may be the object of meditation or the Lord's form. அன்னம் may be the swan (hamsa, the breath or the freed soul) or food. கூடல் may be union or yogic joining.

reading: Is it the flesh or the life that has the joy? While the Lady of the gods stands bewildering them, people who say 'we know, it is we who are great' do not know birth and death themselves.
nuance: வானோர் தலைவி (Lady of the gods) is taken as Shakti in her veiling work, or as maya. The question in line 1 is left for the reader.

title: அறிவுதயம்
theme: The dawning of knowledge (அறிவுதயம்): to know oneself is to come to no harm, and the self so known is knowledge in form, taught by Nandi's grace. Knowledge has no birth and no death and knows itself; passing beyond the world's knowing and not-knowing, the knower finds the Lord in the heart, ends the search for the distant lamp and, the malam removed, abides as Siva with no more birth.
structure_note: Self-knowledge frames the chapter (2355, 2366, 2369). Between them run the verses on அறிவு, most built on one repeated word: knowledge as one's form (2357), as unborn and self-knowing (2358), as passing beyond knowing and not-knowing (2361 to 2363), and as the heart of the wise where the Lord stays (2364). 2367 and 2368 are linked end to beginning by தேடுகின்றேன்.
source_issues: 2358 line 1 reads அழிவில்aல with a stray Latin letter; read அழிவில்லை.
2357 line 4 ends அருந்திருந்தானே, which gives no clear sense; perhaps அமர்ந்திருந்தானே or அறிந்திருந்தானே.
2368 line 4 குறையாமனைத்தாலே is probably குறையா மனத்தாலே.
2360 lines 1 and 2 (மன்னிநின் றாரிடை வந்தருள் மாயத்து முன்னிநின் றாமை) are obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: Knowing oneself, one comes to no harm; not knowing oneself, one ruins oneself; once one knows the knowledge by which one knows oneself, one stays worshipping oneself.
nuance: தன்னை (oneself) opens every line. தன்னையே அர்ச்சிக்க, worshipping oneself, is traditionally taken as worshipping the Lord found as or within one's own self, not as self-regard; the verse does not name the Lord, so that reading comes from the rest of the chapter.

reading: There, as all the mighty great gods bowed, saying that Siva sat on the lion throne, she of the full, rich hair, her conch bangles and anklets sounding at once, said 'Praise'.
nuance: அங்கே (there) does not say where. Placed after 2355 it is taken as the inner scene that opens once the self is known, Siva enthroned and Shakti (பொங்குஆர் குழலி) praising him; read plainly it is a picture of the Lord's court.

reading: Nandi graciously taught me, who did not know it, that knowledge is my form; realising through grace that knowledge is my form, I remained as one whose form is knowledge.
nuance: அறிவு வடிவு (knowledge as form) opens every line. Whose form it is goes unsaid: the self's, as Siddhanta takes the soul to be of the nature of knowing, or the Lord's. Sengalvaraya cites Tiruppugazh 1019, which speaks of knowledge as a holy body beyond knowing and not-knowing. The last word அருந்திருந்தானே is odd (see source issues).

reading: Knowledge has no destruction and no making; knowledge has no support but knowledge; the ends of the Vedas proclaim that knowledge itself knows knowledge.
nuance: ஆதாரம் here is the plain word 'support', not the bodily centres. மறை ஈறுகள் (the ends of the Vedas) are taken as the Upanishads, so the verse claims their authority for knowledge that is self-luminous.

reading: Above the fine flower of the flower one examines there are sixteen spreading petals; there, pure knowledge became Siva's bliss and, as knowledge that had gone beyond, he stayed in union.
nuance: The sixteen-petalled flower is usually taken as a lotus of the yogic body, commonly placed at the throat, though 'above the flower' may point higher. போய அறிவு (knowledge that has gone) is read as knowledge whose separate knowing has ceased. Who is joined (புணர்ந்திருந்தான்) is not said.

reading: Among those who stood firm I spoke of how I had stood intent in the wondrous grace that came; the First One came like gold, I clung to his praised holy form, and he said, 'You are great.'
nuance: The syntax is compressed and முன்னிநின்றாமை and மாயத்து (wondrous, or of maya) are unclear. The scene is taken as the Lord coming in a golden form, perhaps as guru, and acknowledging the devotee; the plain sense of the last two lines is fairly sure, the first two are not.

reading: Know knowledge as knowledge and love; this is how knowledge is known as knowledge; when knowledge is known as knowledge the powers beginning with anima come; Nandi knew knowledge as knowledge.
nuance: அறிவுஅறிவாக opens every line and can mean knowing the knower as knowledge, or knowing (the Lord) as knowledge through knowledge. The command to love (அன்பு செய்மின்) sits beside knowing, not after it. அறிந்தணன் may be அறிந்தனன் (knew) or contain அணன் (one who is near).

reading: The world cries 'knowledge, knowledge', yet no one knows what knowledge and ignorance are; if one passes beyond knowledge and ignorance and becomes knowledge, that is the fine way of knowledge and ignorance.
nuance: The last line, அறிவுஅறியாமை அழகியவாறே, may be plain ('that is the fine way') or ironic ('how fine, this knowing and not-knowing'). The verse's point is that true knowledge is not the opposite of ignorance but lies past both the world's knowledge and its ignorance.

reading: He who removes knowing and not-knowing, when the senses cease and he becomes himself everywhere, stands as knowledge within them, as knowledge made dense; he is Siva too.
nuance: The subject can be Siva, who clears away the soul's knowing and not-knowing, or the freed soul, who, the senses ceased, becomes everywhere and so is Siva too. சிவனும் ஆமே (is Siva as well) leans toward the second, but the verse allows both.

reading: The heart of those with knowledge is the wide world; the heart of those with knowledge is rare austerity; and the first Lord stays there, with the heart of those with knowledge and in it.
nuance: அறிவுடையார் நெஞ்சு opens every line. அகலிடம் (the wide earth) makes the knower's heart as large as the world, holding all; the verse then makes it the place of austerity and of the Lord.

reading: Being Vishnu and the Lord of the flower too, the first cause of the womb in the good land of the body, far and near, he stands as sweet sugarcane and nectar and tastes sweet.
nuance: மாயன் and மலரோன் are Vishnu and Brahma: the one Lord takes their roles. காயநன்னாட்டுக் கருமுதல் may be the first cause of every embryo in the body, or the root seed within the body. Sengalvaraya cites Tiruvasagam and Appar for Siva as sweeter than cane juice; the sugarcane image is shared Saiva devotional language.

reading: All this time I did not know myself; once I knew myself I knew nothing else; knowing myself and never letting go of that abiding, he questions me through myself.
nuance: ஏதும் அறிந்திலேன் can mean that nothing else remained to be known, or that the knower no longer knows objects at all. The last line, என்னையிட்டு என்னை உசாவுகின்றானே, is obscure: 'he' is taken as the Lord within, who inquires of the self by the self.

reading: The lamp of maya stays a while and goes out; the pure lamp stays and sends out its flame; the lamp of the body stays and smoulders; I am the one who seeks the distant lamp.
nuance: Three lamps are set against a fourth. The pure lamp is taken as knowledge and the distant lamp (சேய விளக்கு) as Siva, but the verse does not say so. The last word தேடுகின்றேனை (me who seeks) hangs and is completed by 2368, which opens with தேடுகின்றேன்.

reading: I search the eight directions and the two besides; I look for the feet of the one who owns all good; I sing that the Supreme is my aid; I join him with a mind that never fails.
nuance: The two beyond the eight directions are taken as above and below, so the search is everywhere. Four verbs ending in -கின்றேன் give the stages: search, look, sing, join. குறையாமனைத்தாலே is read as குறையா மனத்தாலே, with an unfailing mind.

reading: Those who came forth first in the Lord's first play, to whom afterwards the great malam came, remove it, know themselves, abide in their ancient Lord and become Siva, and birth does not come again.
nuance: விளையாட்டு (play) is the Lord's sport of creation. பின்னை பெருமலம் வந்தவர் reads as if the malam came after the souls; Siddhanta, as in 2401 (தன் ஆதி மலம்), holds the soul's malam to be beginningless, so பின்னை may mean 'then' rather than 'later'. The close draws the chapter back to its start: knowing oneself ends birth.

title: ஆறு அந்தம்
theme: The six ends (ஆறு அந்தம்): Vedanta, Siddhanta, the end of nada, the end of knowing, the end of yoga and the end of the kalas. Each is defined, and all subside into the one known where knower and knowing vanish in silence and Siva's bliss. Vedanta and Siddhanta are one; the Veda and the Agama are both the Lord's word; and tat tvam asi is read in Saiva terms as the bound soul, the Lord and their union, sayujya.
structure_note: 2370 names the six ends and 2371 praises those who know them. 2372 to 2380 define them in turn: Vedanta and Siddhanta (2372, 2373), nadanta (2374), bodhanta (2375), yoganta (2376) and kalanta with its further kalas (2377 to 2380). 2381 to 2383 gather them into the known and into silence. 2384 to 2391 turn to the Lord who taught them and works through Shakti. 2392 to 2404 argue the unity of Vedanta and Siddhanta, of Veda and Agama, and read tat tvam asi (2387, 2392, 2402). 2399 and 2400 count the ends as five, with Vedanta and Siddhanta as one.
source_issues: 2375 line 3 reads ஓர்iஉணர் with a stray Latin letter; read ஓர் உணர்வு.
2384 line 4 கூளி gives no fitting sense; perhaps கூறி.
2401 line 4 வினாவுநீர் may be a misprint for விரவுநீர் (mixed water).
2383: the numbers of kalas and ends (six in five, two with five making seven) do not resolve into a clear scheme; the verse may be corrupt.
2378: mantra, tantra, upadesa and jnana make four, though the verse says five.
2394 lines 1 and 2 (சித்தித்திலால், சித்தித்திவர்) and 2404 line 4 (அதிகாதி) are obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: The end of the Veda, the excellent Siddhanta, the end of nada, the good end of knowing, the end of the bliss of the eightfold yoga that is worth reciting, and the end of the primal kalas: these are the six ends.
nuance: The list gives the chapter's six terms: வேதாந்தம், சித்தாந்தம், நாதாந்தம், போதாந்தம், யோகாந்தம், கலாந்தம். Calling Siddhanta an அந்தம் beside Vedanta puts the two on a level, which the chapter goes on to argue.

reading: Those who know the six ends are the most pure; those who know the six ends are free of malam; those who do not know the six ends cannot know the end and the beginning.
nuance: The last line plays on அந்தம்: not knowing the ends, one cannot know 'end and beginning', taken as the Lord who is both.

reading: Vedanta, which has become the self, and Siddhanta, which says it is the self: seeing the soul in unending turiya and joining the honeyed Supreme as Siva-yoga, the malam that does not end is removed and one comes to the rare attainment.
nuance: தானான and தான்என்னும் separate the two only slightly: Vedanta as having become the self, Siddhanta as declaring it. துரியம் is the fourth state beyond waking, dream and sleep, and அணுவன் the soul as anu, both technical. ஆனா மலம் may be 'the malam that does not end of itself'.

reading: Siddhanta is this: the soul ever joined with the Supreme, the restless mind and the five beginning with sound removed by knowing the tattvas, holding in thought that neither pure nor impure follows it, and reaching the Father, the Supreme.
nuance: சத்தம் முதல் ஐந்து are the five subtle elements beginning with sound. சுத்தம் அசுத்தம் may be pure and impure maya, or good and bad deeds; the verse does not say.

reading: Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra, the acting Isa, Sadasiva, and beyond them the supreme bindu and nada: when the thirty-six that do not leave cease, the soul alone remains.
nuance: The five deities and bindu and nada are the ascending ranks of the tattvas; ஆறாறு is the thirty-six. அணு is the Siddhanta term for the soul. Placed after 2373, this is taken as the account of nadanta, though the verse does not name it.

reading: Sifting away the adjunct of the thirty-six that the living soul bears, going past the end of nada, when the darkness above is removed it becomes one awareness: that is the knowing reached at the end of nada.
nuance: The closing போதம் suggests this is bodhanta, the end of knowing. உபாதி (limiting adjunct) is a Vedanta term. செற்று (having destroyed, or pressed past) and எள்ளலின் in the last line are unclear.

reading: Passing beyond yama, niyama and the rest that are sought, entering samadhi, Siva spreading through, the soul becoming the Supreme with attachment gone, the union in perfect calm: that is the doctrine of yoganta.
nuance: இயம நியமாதி are the first limbs of eightfold yoga, so the end of yoga is reached by going beyond its steps. உபசாந்தம் is a technical term for complete stillness. படர்சிவன் பாடுற is unclear.

reading: If one marks kalanta in this doctrine: it is bindu, which belongs to the kalas beginning with nivritti and medha that appear as things unfold, withdrawing within, and clearly discerning it.
nuance: நிவிர்த்தாதி names the five kalas from nivritti, a standard Siddhanta set; மேதாதி is less clear and may be a set of kalas of the syllable Om. விள்கை (unfolding) and ஒடுங்கல் (withdrawing) make kalanta the reversal of the kalas back into bindu.

reading: Besides these discerned kalas there are five other kalas, set within light, for those able to examine: given by the gracious one, they are mantra, tantra, clear teaching and knowledge, five in all.
nuance: The count is unclear: mantra, tantra, upadesa and jnana make four, and the fifth may be the gracious one (அளியவன்) himself or something the text has lost. 2379 goes on to define them.

reading: The beginningless kala is the Agama and the Veda; tantra is standing in the way those scriptures lay down; mantra is the beginningless one who is not body; upadesa is the teaching that is knowledge of Siva.
nuance: The verse defines the five of 2378 in Tirumular's own terms: tantra is practice according to scripture, not a separate text. உடல்அல்லா மந்திரம் may mean mantra as the bodiless Lord, or the Lord whose body is mantra, as the Agamas say.

reading: The kala of one's own knowledge that becomes radiant Siva, and conduct, love and the Veda too, end in kalanta; the great one beyond speech, word and feeling, beyond speech and mind, is great Nandi himself.
nuance: வாசாமகோசரம் is taken as the Sanskrit phrase for what speech and mind cannot reach. ஆசார நேய மறையும் may mean conduct, love and Veda all end there, or that conduct and love 'disappear' (மறையும்) in kalanta.

reading: If one reaches the samadhi in which oneself becomes He, kalanta, nadanta and yoganta, and the others, bodhanta and Siddhanta, become knowledge, the known and the knower.
nuance: ஞானம், ஞேயம், ஞாதுரு are the triad of knowing, known and knower. The verse does not say which end becomes which, and Vedanta is not named, perhaps because it is one with Siddhanta.

reading: The six ends all go and subside in that known; the knower too subsides in the known of the six ends; when even the stated mark of knowledge departs, the clear silence becomes Siva's bliss.
nuance: The triad of 2381 collapses in order: the ends into the known, the knower into the known, then knowledge itself. What remains is மோனம், silence, as a state, and it is named as bliss.

reading: The true kalas, six, are held in one five; true kalanta is two with five, seven ends; and in nadanta, the end within one kala, to speak the true kala is one end.
nuance: The verse is a count of kalas and ends whose scheme I can't recover; உண்மைக் கலை (true kala) opens every line. The numbers are given as read, not reconciled.

reading: After Hara came and took hold of the one who has the soul, our glorious divine Nandi gave his feet; think on the king who taught, unfailing, the greatness of Vedanta and Siddhanta.
nuance: ஆவுடையான் is unclear: ஆ (cow) is a Saiva figure for the soul, so 'the one who owns the soul', but it may also echo ஆவுடையார, the lingam's pedestal. கூளி in line 4 gives no fitting sense and may be கூறி (having told).

reading: In the Agama that Hara spoke and gave in grace to fit the thought of those who think on him lies the truth of Vedanta and Siddhanta, which passes through the outer sects, maya and great maya.
nuance: Line 1 says the Lord's teaching is shaped to its hearers. உருவிய can mean 'piercing through' or 'drawn out from', so the truth either goes beyond the outer sects and the two mayas or is drawn out of them.

reading: Vedanta and Siddhanta are a seal without difference; the knowledge of bodhanta, yoganta, the shared known of nadanta and bliss become a rising of glory when one sinks into the silence of the seal of the ancient end.
nuance: முத்திரை here is a seal or mark of identity more than a hand gesture; மூதாந்த முத்திரை, the seal of the ancient end, is unclear. The verse gathers the ends again and ends them in silence, as 2382 does.

reading: In Vedanta, when the seven adjuncts are left, the good 'thou' is what leaves the bond at the end of nada; beyond, with the seven causal adjuncts gone, the true Supreme is the 'that' of bodhanta; and their joining, they say, is 'art'.
nuance: தொம்பதம், தற்பதம் and அசி are the three words of tat tvam asi ('that thou art'). The verse assigns 'thou' to the soul freed at nadanta and 'that' to the Lord at bodhanta. The two sets of seven adjuncts are not identified, and போமசி may be போம் அசி (the joining is asi).

reading: Beyond the seven worlds and further, within the great light said to be there, is an inner light called the ancient Parashakti; and our King stood there as the one who holds her, yet not as her.
nuance: கொண்டவன் அன்றி நின்றான் can mean he stood as the one who holds her, or stood apart from what he holds; Siddhanta's Lord is one with his Shakti yet not reduced to her. Sengalvaraya cites Appar 6-97-1 on what lies beyond the worlds.

reading: The King knows through Shakti and, setting the aim, has the acts done that make the gods know; creating all that is imagined and spreading worship, he is the One who is in all and never ceases.
nuance: The syntax is broken into odd units (கோஉணர்ந் தும், ஓஅனைத் துண்டு), which makes the reading tentative. அனைத்துண்டு may be 'is in all' or 'has consumed all', the latter pointing to dissolution.

reading: They do not think of the One, nor of the soul, nor of the two kinds of deed, nor of the two mayas; yet the One alone, knowing within, stands and feeds them, the formless one who is their support.
nuance: Line 1 names the categories: the Lord, the soul, deeds and maya. Whether it faults the ignorant who ignore them or describes the freed who no longer think of them is open. ஊட்டி (feeding) is taken as making souls experience the fruit of their deeds.

reading: Hara becomes the place of his devotees; setting out first the powers that arise in Siva so that his mighty presence acts, he is ever the steady one of Siva's bliss whom nothing touches.
nuance: தானம் may be 'place' or 'gift'. சந்நிதி சேட்டிப்ப (the presence acting) and தோயா (untouched, not soaked) are taken in the Siddhanta sense that the Lord acts through his powers by mere presence and is not stained by the acts. The verse is compressed.

reading: They say the 'thou' of Vedanta is the bound soul; the good Lord is what stands when the bond at the end of nada is let go, the 'that' of bodhanta; going on, the union of the two, held in common, is Siva-sayujya.
nuance: The verse maps tat tvam asi onto the Siddhanta categories: 'thou' is pasu, 'that' is pati, 'art' is sayujya. சாதாரணம் (common) is unclear: perhaps the union shared by both schools, or the state common to soul and Lord.

reading: Becoming Siva is Vedanta and Siddhanta; apart from that, each of the two is in vain; if Sadasiva, who is Siva, made them one, the new Vedanta is the Siddhanta of knowledge.
nuance: அவம் அவம் ஆகும் அவ்வவ் இரண்டும் may mean either is futile unless it leads to becoming Siva, or that the two taken apart are futile. நவமான may be 'new' or 'ninefold'.

reading: Since in Siddhanta the soul attains release while living, those who stand in Siddhanta attain release and siddhi; since Siddhanta and Vedanta are the perfect meaning, Siddhanta and Vedanta show Siva.
nuance: Lines 1 and 2 (சித்தித்திலால், சித்தித்திவர்) are a play on சித்தி whose exact form is unclear; சீவன் முத்தி is release while living. செம்பொருள் (the perfect meaning) is the Kural's word in 358.

reading: If Vedanta and Siddhanta, free of waste, show Siva within the Supreme and within the soul, then knowledge, made new in the states, becomes Siva; those who have realised this, rich in austerity, are the people of truth.
nuance: அவத்தை are the states of the soul (waking, dream and the rest), a Siddhanta term. நவமுற்று may be 'made new' or 'reaching the ninth'. தத்துவத்தார் plays forward into 2396, which opens with தத்துவம்.

reading: Tattva is the formed and the formless; tattva is bindu, nada and Sadasiva; tattva is the soul and its Supreme; tattva is Siva-sayujya.
nuance: தத்துவம் opens every line. It can be the tattvas as constituents of the world, which fits bindu and nada, or 'truth, reality', which fits the soul, the Supreme and sayujya; the verse seems to use both. சகளம், அகளம் are the Lord with parts and without.

reading: The Veda and the Agama are the scriptures of the true Lord; what they teach is called the general and the special; examined, both are the Lord's word; people call the two ends different, but for the great they are not different.
nuance: The Veda as பொது (general, for all) and the Agama as சிறப்பு (special, for the qualified) is a well-known Saiva position, and this verse is often cited for it. The 'two ends' are taken as Vedanta and Siddhanta.

reading: All the bliss of Siva in which Paranandi abides: the supreme bliss, the three above, the bliss that never goes to waste, the bliss of the seal of rest, the bliss of the true dance; the heart that stands without strife swells with them.
nuance: The verse lists kinds of bliss whose number and order are unclear; விராமுத்திரானந்தம் is read as the bliss of the mudra of cessation (விராம). பொராநின்ற உள்ளம் may be 'the heart that does not contend' or 'the heart that strives'.

reading: Kalanta, the two ends and nadanta: when they come about, the kalas are five; so Hara is the Lord of the five ends, as he said in the Veda and the Agama.
nuance: Here the ends are counted as five (பஞ்சாந்தம்), not six; 2400 suggests why, taking Vedanta and Siddhanta as one. இரண்டந்தம் (the two ends) may be those two, as in 2397.

reading: Not rejecting the five kinds of end, and holding them together with Vedanta and Siddhanta made one, yoganta comes right; when it comes right, one reaches the feet of the dancer in the hall.
nuance: அன்றாகும் என்னாது is read as 'without saying it is not so'. அன்னை (mother) after ஐவகை அந்தம் is unclear: the Shakti, or a misreading. மன்றாடி is the dancer in the hall at Chidambaram.

reading: The beginningless soul, free of the five malas and gone beyond, restraining what is beginningless, sees itself, becomes Hara, its own primal malam destroyed, beyond the tattvas, as water becomes milk: this is the truth of Vedanta.
nuance: ஐம்மலம் is traditionally the five bonds (anava, karma, maya, mayeya, tirodhana). Water mixed into milk is a classic image of union in which the two can no longer be told apart. That the verse calls this Vedanta's truth matches the chapter's claim that Vedanta and Siddhanta agree. வினாவு (asking) in line 4 is unclear and may be a misprint for விரவு (mixing).

reading: Knowing without weariness the soul and the Supreme, the soul and Siva, is 'thou art that'; so, action ceasing, becoming knowledge and going to subside there, is the unwearying Vedanta and Siddhanta.
nuance: தொந்தத்தசி is tvam tat asi, the great saying with its words in this order. Line 3 gives the sequence: action ends, the soul becomes knowledge, then subsides in Siva.

reading: The abiding 'So'ham' is the crowning Siva-yoga of those who know the great Veda; and that same thing, as the meaning of the great scripture of Siddhanta, appears as the Agama joined with it.
nuance: சோகம் (so'ham, 'I am He') is a meditation formula. The verse makes one teaching appear as Siva-yoga for Veda-knowers and as Agama for Siddhantins; the syntax of lines 3 and 4 is loose.

reading: The Veda that comes first and the whole Agama are the two that Isa, the Lord within, spoke; the ancient Veda, set in its due order, they become the foremost Vedanta and Siddhanta.
nuance: அகப் பதி may be the Lord within, or பதி alone as the Siddhanta Lord. அதிகாதி in line 4 is unclear: perhaps 'foremost' or அதிகாரி (one qualified).

title: பதி பசு பாசம் வேறின்மை
theme: Pati, pasu and pasam (the Lord, the soul and the bond) are all three beginningless; the bond is three, and when it is cut the soul clings to the Lord. The Lord sets the bond and maya to work through his five acts, so that the bond itself becomes the grace by which the soul is cleansed and reaches his feet.
structure_note: The title, பதி பசு பாசம் வேறின்மை, reads literally as 'the non-difference of pati, pasu and pasam'; how that is meant is unclear, since most verses treat them as three. The chapter moves from the three as beginningless (2405 to 2413), through the Lord's creation and five acts in the subtle and gross orders (2414 to 2419), to the bond as the means of grace (2420 to 2423), and ends on the guru's hand (2424).
source_issues: 2419: line 2 reads மாயைil with a stray Latin letter (மாயைiல்); probably மாயையில்.
2420: நரசு in line 3 is probably a misprint for நரகு (hell).
2414: lines 1 and 2 are almost identical (ஆகும் / ஆக), which may be a copying error.

reading: The knowing soul is beginningless, the Lord who is knowledge to that knowledge is beginningless, the bond that binds the knowing soul is beginningless, and when the soul rests in the Lord, birth is cut off.
nuance: அறிவு (knowledge) names the soul itself, and அறிவுக்கு அறிவு the Lord as the one by whom the soul knows. The three beginningless realities stated line by line are the Siddhanta position in its plainest form.

reading: Souls are many crores, from Brahma down, and the bonds that bind them are three; if their soul-state is removed and the bond is cut, the souls hold to their Lord and do not let go.
nuance: The three bonds are traditionally anava, karma and maya. Brahma is counted among the bound souls, which places the gods below Siva. பசுத்தன்மை (the state of being pasu) is what goes, not the soul.

reading: As things lie there are three stirring fruits; look every day to the knowledge that moves, and worship without any entanglement, for when you worship it becomes like a lamp set on the western hill.
nuance: கிளர்பயன் மூன்று (three stirring fruits) is obscure; it may mean the three categories as they are, or three results. குடக்குன்றில் இட்ட விளக்கு, a lamp on the western hill, suggests a light seen from far off; whether the western hill has a further sense is unclear.

reading: People love Nandi of the spreading matted hair, who made the bond, and think of him there; yet even thinking of him, how could they shrink back and hold him in their aim, so does he keep them within the bond they live in.
nuance: பாசம்செய்தான், 'he who made the bond', makes the Lord the author of bondage; in Siddhanta he does not create malam but sets maya and karma working on it. கூசம் செய்து உன்னி (thinking with shrinking) and the turn of the last line are hard to construe.

reading: As poison once drawn out does not rise again, the one who has seen the truth does not return to the soul-state and bond he has left; the kevala state pointed to sees the sakala, and burning that away, he appears in the state beyond while still awake.
nuance: கேவலம் and சகலம் are Siddhanta's states of the soul: alone with anava and inert, and embodied with maya and karma. நனவில் அதீதம், the beyond-state in waking, is taken as the condition of one freed while living. மெய்கண்டோன் means 'one who saw the truth'; it is also the name of the later Siddhanta teacher Meykandar, but nothing in the verse requires that.

reading: The Lord who is sought, and the good soul and the bond, all endure; none knows the state of the Eternal, and that lasting eternity and the removal of soul-state and bond Nandi gave to the Saivas who sought them.
nuance: நீடுமாம் says all three endure, but the last line speaks of removing pasu and pasam; the verse holds both together, as Siddhanta does, by taking removal as of the soul's bound state rather than of the soul.

reading: The Lord is the lingam of Siva's grace, the soul stands as the mighty bull, and the good bond is the altar of offerings: this is Hara's state, for those who examine it.
nuance: The verse reads the temple's axis as the three categories: the lingam in the sanctum, the Nandi bull facing it, and the balipitha nearest the entrance. Calling the bond நற்பாசம், the good bond, anticipates 2422.

reading: Pati, pasu and pasam are eternal and not taught into being; to those who speak of them they become a path; that knowledge removes them so clinging ends; and when they are practised they do not stay.
nuance: Each line opens with பதிபசு பாசம், so the formula itself is the subject. பயில்வியா (unlearnt, not brought about) and நிலாவே (do not stay, or shine like the moon) are both open; the reading above is one way to make the lines cohere.

reading: Showing the Lord with soul and bond, the higher goal and the removal of soul-state and bond, great Nandi of bliss, who gave understanding, set them with praise in true Saivism.
nuance: சத்தசைவம் may be சத்த (sat, true) or a variant of சுத்தசைவம் (pure Saivism), a kind of Saivism named elsewhere in Tirumular. துதிதந்து (giving praise) is loose in the line.

reading: The three kinds of souls are known to be everywhere, and so the knowing, beginningless Lord pervades them, and as knowing Pati he creates for them there.
nuance: அணு மூன்று is taken as the three classes of souls in Siddhanta (bound by one, two or three malas), but it could be read otherwise. Lines 1 and 2 are nearly the same words.

reading: Creation and the other acts belong to Parasiva and Shakti and are closed off from the souls between; the Supreme performs creation in its subtle form, and that beginning of creation, pure maya, lies in the Supreme.
nuance: தூய மலம் (pure malam) is taken as suddha maya, the pure material of the higher worlds. இடைப்பால உயிர்கட்கு அடைத்துஇவை தூங்கல் is hard to construe; it may instead say the acts are fitted to the souls.

reading: In that subtle order, through bindu and nada, Shakti, Siva and the Supreme, these five, the one who performs the five acts in the subtle is also the pure Isana.
nuance: ஈசானன் is one of Siva's five faces; here it may name the Lord of the pure order. The five through which he acts are listed, but their roles are not.

reading: Parasiva, and above Shakti and nada, the supreme bindu, the five-faced one, the Lord as distinct, Rudra, Vishnu, Brahma and the earth: the one who creates so that all these come to be is Hara.
nuance: ஐம்முகன் (the five-faced) is traditionally Sadasiva and வேறு ஈசன் Maheshvara; the list runs down the pure order to the three gods and the earth. The verse makes all of them Hara's creation.

reading: Creation, protection, the removal that gives rest, concealment, and the grace that comes forth, the grace that frees from inert matter: the beginningless one who shut souls in the embodied state may be called by these five.
nuance: இளைப்பாற்றும் துடைப்பு, removal that gives rest, frames dissolution as relief for weary souls rather than destruction. The last act is grace that frees from சடம், inert matter. The five are named by what they do for souls.

reading: Setting the thirty-six tattvas within kundalini, increasing maya's three parts, and dividing them through the instruments down to the last, pati, pasu and pasam stand distinct, and that is release.
nuance: ஆறாறு (six sixes) is the 36 tattvas; முப்பால் (three parts) of maya may be pure, mixed and impure maya. Whether the last line means that knowing the three as distinct is release, or something else, is unclear.

reading: With pati, pasu and pasam set above, the two kinds of deeds that govern a person are known through them; he is placed in hell and in heaven, and for his allotted days the good bond in which the 'I' dwells comes to him.
nuance: இருவினை are good and bad deeds. வீட்கும் at the start and நான்தங்கு near the end are obscure; the 'I' that dwells in the bond leads into 2421, where saying 'I' is named anava.

reading: In the bond that comes, saying 'I' is anava; through the maya he set working the Lord kindly feeds the soul its experience; and the great grace that comes into the sentient soul's sight is the means of reaching the Lord's feet.
nuance: The verse names ஆணவம் as the sense of 'I'. ஊட்டல், feeding, is the making of souls experience the fruit of deeds through maya, and பரிந்தனன் (in kindness) makes that an act of care. கண்ணிய and கண்வந்த are not fully clear.

reading: More than a means, it is the root by which the soul, its dirt gone and its delusion ended, becomes pure; as a washer loads dirt on cloth to clean it, all that comes to the soul is the bond of grace.
nuance: அறுவை அழுக்கேற்றி ஏற்றல் is taken as the washer applying fuller's earth or dung to cloth to draw out its dirt; tradition reads maya and karma as given to remove anava in the same way. அருட்பாசம், the bond of grace, is the chapter's turn. மோசு is obscure.

reading: The soul that undergoes the bond is called pasu and is itself, the verse says, the supreme first; and since through the bond's working the Lord is supreme, through that working Lord and soul become one, or the Lord becomes as the soul.
nuance: பதிபசு வாகுமே can mean 'the Lord becomes pasu' or 'pati and pasu become (one)'; either may explain the chapter title, வேறின்மை, non-difference. The verse is built on four repetitions of பாசம் பயில, and the readings above are guesses at its logic.

reading: The rare ascetics who heard the answer in the hand found the answer was the body of grace in the hand, and held close by that hand, they reached themselves within it and stood.
nuance: அத்தம் can be hand (hasta), meaning (artha) or half, and உத்தரம் answer or north. A traditional reading takes it as the guru's touch in initiation, or the teaching gesture of the silent Siva; a plainer reading, that the answer lay in the meaning itself, also stands.

title: அடிதலை அறியும் திறங்கூறல்
theme: Knowing the Lord's foot and head: the foot is his grace, which shows the soul knowledge, and in the body foot and head lie at the root and the crown. The poet tells how Nandi's feet came onto his head, cut his bonds and took him, and how the Lord, like a parent, deals with each soul by its ripeness.
structure_note: Two verses define foot and head (2425, 2426); the rest speak in the first person of the feet placed on the head (2427, 2429, 2433), in the heart (2428, 2431), and in the body's lotus (2432), and end on the Lord's care for each soul (2434).
source_issues: 2425: line 4 reads ஞானத்கைக், a misprint for ஞானத்தைக்.
2433: line 3 reads என்ணைப், a misprint for என்னைப்.

reading: The wretched do not know foot and head: the foot is Shakti, grace and the cause, the head is knowledge, and when the foot shows the soul that knowledge, release comes.
nuance: The equation of the foot with Shakti as grace is stated; பாலொன்று ஞானமே பண்பார் தலைஉயிர் is hard to divide, and may make the soul the head, or place it under knowledge. கலதிகள் (the wretched, the ill-fated) is sharp.

reading: People do not know what head and foot are; in the body they are at the crown and at the root, and those who know the knowledge that is head and foot remain as head and foot themselves.
nuance: உச்சி (crown) and மூலம் (root) are taken in the yogic sense as the top of the head and the lowest centre; தலைஅடி can also mean the foot placed on the head, as in 2427. The last line says the knower becomes what he knows.

reading: Nandi, who stood so that the whole earth and the cosmos rose up, so that the strong-footed asuras and the gods were saved, and who afterwards created the world: his pair of feet came upon my head.
nuance: நின்றான் ... மேலுற may recall Siva standing as the column whose head and foot Brahma and Vishnu could not find, which fits a chapter on head and foot; the verse does not name the story. The feet on the head are traditionally the guru's initiation by the feet (திருவடி தீட்சை).

reading: My father's holy feet are within my mind, and my mind is beneath my father's holy feet; if my father cannot know me, I cannot know my father either.
nuance: Lines 1 and 2 reverse each other: the feet in the mind and the mind under the feet. The last two lines make the soul's knowing of the Lord depend on his knowing it first. Sengalvaraya notes a close parallel in Appar's Tevaram (5.91.8).

reading: Beyond the unspoken light of the world and beyond that, where my Lord consented to dwell, he told me the light that cannot be thought and the mantra that cannot be spoken, and I stand wearing his anklet feet.
nuance: உரைசெய்யா மந்திரம் is a mantra not spoken aloud or one beyond speech, yet he 'told' it: the verse holds the paradox of teaching the unsayable. சூடி, wearing as a garland, is the feet on the head again.

reading: Set in yourselves the feet that reveal the Lord, make your understanding steady and recite the flower-feet, and see the times when the one with the river in his matted hair and the woman as his half grants the goal.
nuance: மதியது செய்து may be 'use your understanding' or, in the yogic sense, 'make the moon', the inner lunar breath. கதிசெயும் காலங்கள் (times he grants the goal) is unexplained.

reading: The one who sustains stood with his feet in my heart; the lord of the gods' city stood sustaining; he stood scorching the minds of those who do not think of him, and he stood bearing souls according to their ripeness.
nuance: பரிபாகம் is the soul's ripeness, a Siddhanta term for readiness to receive grace. கரித்து may be 'burning, blackening' or 'witnessing'; its sense against those who do not think of him is unclear. அமராபதி நாதன் uses the name of Indra's city for Siva as lord over the gods.

reading: There is one lotus with three bright flowers, and one's father's feet, two, are in the body; for those who can heat it well and bring it to the right state, it is possible to go today and reach the Lord.
nuance: காய்ச்சிப் பதஞ்செய is a cooking image, boiling down to the right consistency, taken as yogic heat or the ripening of the soul; பதம் also means foot and state. The lotus and its three flowers are not identified; tradition reads them as centres of the yogic body.

reading: He set his foot on my head so that my bonds were cut and cut, so that the confusion of my bewildered heart's delusion was cut, and he sought to take me, who was his portion; what my state became after he took me cannot be told.
nuance: கட்டறக் கட்டற doubles the cutting of bonds. பால்கொண்ட என்னை may be 'me, who belonged to his side' or 'me, who had taken a side'. The verse ends in the ineffable (விளம்ப ஒண்ணாதே).

reading: Like a parent who has seen both the tendencies and the faults of the sons he begot, the Lord who holds to souls deals with each by its nature, doing without anger what fits.
nuance: நாற்றம் is usually smell; here perhaps disposition, or நாற்று (seedling) as what has been raised. குணங்குறை செய்ய (to make up for virtues and lacks) and the third line are loosely built. The point that the Lord's dealings are without hatred (செற்றமிலா) is clear.

title: முக்குற்றம்
theme: The three faults: they afflict wholly and keep souls dazed in darkness, and those who do not leave them perish in them. With lust, anger and delusion driven out, the poet reached the abode within the sound Om.

reading: There are three faults that afflict wholly; dazed, they lay sleeping in darkness and bewildered; those who left the three have removed them, and those who did not are caught in the three and perish.
nuance: The verse does not name the three. 2436 names lust, anger and delusion, the Kural's three; the darkness and sleep here could also suit the three malas. நீங்கினர் நீக்கினர் (they left, they removed) pairs leaving and removing.

reading: Having driven off lust, anger and delusion and held fast to safety, I reached the abode that dwells within the sound Om, as of a struck bell.
nuance: The first line is nearly Kural 360's. எறிமணி (a struck bell) and ஓமெனும் ஓசை (the sound Om) are taken as an inner sound heard in yoga, and தாமம் as the abode or light within it; that yogic reading is the tradition's.

title: முப்பதம்
theme: The three words of the great saying tat tvam asi, 'that thou art': 'thou' is the soul known apart from the tattvas, 'that' is Siva, and 'art', the word that joins them, is Shakti. When they mingle the soul becomes Siva in a joy beyond words, and the joining word is matched to the turiya state.
structure_note: The chapter defines the three words (2437 to 2441), gives a breath-yoga way into them (2442), and maps them onto the states of waking, dream and turiya (2443, 2444).
source_issues: 2442: உம்பனை and தம்பரயோகம் (perhaps தற்பரயோகம்) are obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: One who reaches 'thou' as it appears, 'that' surrounding it, and 'art' that receives them, becomes the transcendent-immanent so that birth ends, and as the self that took this on dies away, stays as Siva.
nuance: தொம்பதம், தற்பதம், அசிபதம் are the Sanskrit tvam, tat and asi. பராபரம் is the Lord as beyond and within. ஏன்றனன் மாள, 'he who accepted dying', is hard to construe; it may mean the individual self ends in Siva.

reading: Contemplating awareness, and letting go, in the way of nada's end, the distinctions of the elements and the ninety-six instruments that are spoken of, to become the 'thou' that the Veda speaks of is the truth.
nuance: தொண்ணூறுடன் ஓராறு (ninety with six) is the count of 96 tattvas common in Tamil Siddha writing, beside the 36 used elsewhere in the Tirumanthiram. 'Thou' is the soul known in itself once the instruments are set aside.

reading: Whether called 'that' or 'thou', what stands in 'art' is the station of the finely jewelled lady, and Siva, whom no word can follow, stood mingled there without any fancy.
nuance: The verse makes the joining word, asi, Shakti (நேரிழையாள், the woman of fine jewels): the bond between soul and Lord is his power. கற்பனை யின்றி (without imagining) says the mingling is real, not a construct of thought.

reading: When the soul and the Supreme, joined in 'art', mingle with Siva who has no seam, it appears, once words cease, as a joy without equal, like milk, honey and nectar.
nuance: அணு is the soul. கணு ஒன்று இலாத, without a single node (as on a cane), is an image of seamless wholeness. உரையற்றிட, when speech ends, is the condition for the joy to appear.

reading: With 'thou', 'that' and 'art' appearing, the trusting soul stands as the Supreme and as Siva; that word is the saying whose form is the highest, and glorious Nandi rules and gives its true meaning.
nuance: சீவன் பரன் சிவன் may be read as matching the three words to soul, Supreme and Siva. வாக்கியம் (the saying) is the Upanishadic great saying; Tirumular makes Nandi, his guru, the one who gives its sense.

reading: Even some who do not know the fifty letters, seeking the Highest within the three-word teaching and driving the breath that is the true Supreme, become, by that supreme yoga, He himself.
nuance: ஐம்பது (the fifty) is taken as the fifty letters of the mantra alphabet, or learning in general; வாசி is the breath in Siddha yoga. உம்பனை is obscure, perhaps 'the one on high'. The verse opens the way to those without learning.

reading: When knowledge, extinguished, slips away it is the state beyond; when the senses and sound and the rest are let go it becomes vast; and the beginningless one sets going the states of waking and the rest, the three, two, one and five.
nuance: நந்தி may be the Lord's name or the verb 'extinguished' (நந்துதல்), and நந்திய in line 3 likewise; the reading changes with it. The numbers மூன்றுஇரண்டு ஒன்று ஐந்து are traditionally the instruments active in each state, but the verse does not say which.

reading: In the supreme turiya, waking is absorbed; in its spreading is dream; in its stilling is turiya, with the sushumna, and cessation at Siva; and that rare turiya is 'art'.
nuance: கழுமுனை is the sushumna, the central channel. The verse maps the joining word asi onto the turiya state, so the three words and the states of consciousness become one scheme. Its step-by-step order is compressed.

title: முப்பரம்
theme: The three supremes: Siva as the Supreme, the supreme beyond the supreme, and the Supreme in oneself (tatpara), reached beyond the thirty-six tattvas and the states of the soul. He comes to the soul like a mother to her calf, and is reached by a clinging that ends clinging, in a bliss that knowledge makes.
structure_note: The verses name the supremes in turn: சிவபரம் (2447), பரம்பரம் (2448, 2449) and தற்பரம் (2450, 2451); 2445 and 2446 describe the Lord rising within and filling the hall.
source_issues: 2451: lines 1 to 3 (தற்கண்ட தூயமும், பிற்காணும் தூடணம், கால பரமும்) are obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: Having reached the First One of the three-tiered circle, who appeared within me and rises whirling, and dwelling there in joy, the young creeper hangs down and does good: this is how good is given.
nuance: மூன்று படி மண்டலம் is traditionally the three circles of fire, sun and moon in the yogic body. இளங்கொடி (the young creeper) is taken as Shakti, perhaps kundalini. The verse is built on images that can't be fixed from it.

reading: What filled the hall became the great Supreme, and Nandi stood filling it and came face to face; once he came like a mother rising at the thought of her calf, he became a lamp of virtue filling the hill.
nuance: மன்று is the hall of the dance. The cow who rises at the very thought of her calf (கன்று நினைந்தெழு தாய்) makes grace come unbidden. குன்று நிறைந்த விளக்கு, a lamp filling the hill, echoes 2407.

reading: Beyond the thirty-six tattvas and beyond that is the teaching that cannot be told, and if told, it is Siva the Supreme; the Lord of the Veda appeared as distinct, so that bliss and attainment grow.
nuance: கூறா உபதேசம் கூறில் (if the untellable teaching is told) is the familiar paradox. வேதப் பசுவனார் is obscure: perhaps the Lord of souls (Pasupati) of the Veda, or the Veda as a cow.

reading: If one clings so that clinging ends, that is the supreme Lord; the knowledge of the Supreme is the Supreme; and for those who can cling in that clinging so that clinging ends, it is the supreme beyond the supreme.
nuance: பற்றறப் பற்றில் opens every line: 'if one clings so that clinging ends', or 'in the clinging free of clinging'. பரம்பரம் is the supreme above the supreme, the second of the chapter's three.

reading: The supreme beyond the supreme, which Lord and bond do not hold, becomes Parasiva to be reached; and the bliss of Parasiva, the supreme beyond the supreme, is made as such by knowledge.
nuance: பதிபாசம் பற்றா, which pati and pasam do not hold, sets the highest beyond even the category of Lord. The last line makes knowledge the maker of the bliss; that may mean realisation is the knowing itself.

reading: In waking, leaving the five beginning with kala, becoming itself in the lone kevala state, going beyond thought into the state beyond, and reaching what is known there, the soul itself is the Supreme within.
nuance: கலாதி நாலொன்று (kala and the rest, four and one) is taken as the five sheaths that limit the soul (kala, vidya, raga, niyati, kala). நேயம் may be the object of knowing (jneya) or love. தற்பரம் is the third supreme, the Supreme as one's own.

reading: The purity one sees in oneself, the vastness in oneself, the fault seen afterwards, all falter, and tatpara and the supreme of time mingle and end; that good state beyond the Supreme is to be sought through the letters beginning with A.
nuance: தூடணம் is dushana (fault), and கால பரம் perhaps the supreme as time. அகராதி, the letters beginning with A, may mean the parts of Om or the mantra letters. The verse is compressed and its steps are not clear.

title: பரலட்சணம்
theme: The marks of the Supreme (பரலட்சணம்): Siva stands beyond the states and the tattvas and is not bound by adjuncts, yet with Shakti as his body and form he pervades the five elements and the worlds. The soul that leaves its darkness becomes one with him, and Nandi as guru cuts away fear and gives himself.
structure_note: The chapter alternates the Supreme in himself (2452 to 2455, 2462 to 2464) with Nandi's grace to the speaker (2456, 2457) and Shakti as his body (2459, 2464), and ends with the yogi for whom tapas becomes grace (2465).
source_issues: 2458: line 1 lists வாயு and line 2 வளி, both air, and fire is missing from the elements; one word may be corrupt.
2462: தொற்பதம் is not a known form; probably தொம்பதம் or தொல்பதம்.

reading: Nandi, in the state beyond, stands apart from all; the soul in that beyond-state is without knowing; the abiding soul that gains understanding and leaves its darkness becomes one, and as the supreme soul it settles in the Lord.
nuance: அதீதம் (the state beyond) is said of both: for Nandi it is transcendence, for the soul it is traditionally taken as its state of utter unknowing before grace. பதியிற் பதியும் plays on பதி, the Lord, and பதிதல, to settle or be imprinted.

reading: The rare Lord without beginning or end, the supreme flame of light, appears and yet does not appear, and stands as the right order; those who have known that long supreme knowledge are the blessed.
nuance: தோன்றத் தோன்றாமையின் can be read as his appearing without appearing, or as the world not appearing once his light appears. நீதி is order or justice; புண்ணியத்தோர் are those whose merit has ripened.

reading: For those who can enter the well of Om and reach the great Lord who dances in the hall, in the state beyond turiya where turiya itself is contained, by a rare yoga, there is no flaw.
nuance: துரியாதீதம் is the state beyond turiya. வியோகம் can be viyoga, separation from the bonds, or a heightened yoga. துரிய in the last line chimes with turiya and is taken as 'to enter or plunge'; துரிசு is fault.

reading: As whiteness changes when red stands before it, so the soul, coming within that true Supreme, in the empty void of knowledge that has swallowed the false world, becomes the flag that joins the red Siva-Meru.
nuance: The image is the crystal that takes the colour of what is near it, a classic Siddhanta figure for the soul taking on what it stands beside. மேரு is traditionally the crown of the yogic body; கொடி may be flag or creeper.

reading: So that the tattvas from kala onward that were set on me perish, cutting at the root the two mayas as things apart, so that I become one with the truth that is the highest Parasiva, Nandi cut away my fear and took me as his own.
nuance: இருமாயை are traditionally pure and impure maya. The verse credits release to Nandi's act, not to the speaker's effort: ஆண்டவன், he who ruled me.

reading: My Nandi, who made me fit to know myself, knew me and led me to the place beyond knowing, then came forth in light as his own form and gave himself to me as the Supreme beyond.
nuance: என்னை அறிந்து may be Nandi knowing me or me knowing myself under him; அறியாத இடம், the place not known, is the state beyond ordinary knowing. தன்னை அளித்தான், he gave himself, is the climax.

reading: Expanding and contracting, he becomes earth, water and air, the unceasing wind, the sun and the moon, and the way of dharma, and stands bearing the one sky.
nuance: The list should run through the five elements, but வாயு and வளி both mean air and fire is missing; one may be a corruption. அரந்த may be Hara's, or what removes sorrow.

reading: Shakti, who in the state of being became one with him, stands as Tatpara; as the body of the Supreme who is himself, she takes on the distinctions of will, knowledge and the rest that she brings forth, and daily moves and dances in great love.
nuance: That Shakti is Siva's body (உடல்) is a Siddhanta teaching; இச்சை, ஞானம் and the unstated கிரியை are her three powers. நடத்தும் நடிக்கும் may be 'conducts and dances' or one act said twice.

reading: Bindu, nursed within Para as Para, reaches above, below and the sides, and the body, mouth, eyes and nose; the bindu that brings the knowing of taste becomes the doing of the undisciplined soul.
nuance: The verse is obscure. நான்சுவை may be 'four tastes' or 'I-taste', and சீலமிலா அணு, the soul without discipline, may mean the bound soul in general. The plain sense is that bindu, born in Shakti, runs through the senses and so into the soul's acts.

reading: In this body, as with that separate nature, the adjuncts become all the tattvas; maya, lit as brightness by the supreme light that stirs it, becomes sensation, breathes, eats and sleeps.
nuance: ஆறாம் may be 'sixth' or 'that becomes'. The point, as tradition reads it, is that maya is inert and acts only as lit by Siva's light, so the body's breathing, eating and sleeping belong to maya.

reading: The great light, sole and first, abiding as Tatpara, is itself Chitpara; the knowledge that swallowed the world enters the beautiful light in the void where the pada ends, and beyond that there is nothing here to compare it with.
nuance: தற்பரம் and சிற்பரம் are the Supreme as itself and as pure consciousness. தொற்பதம் is probably தொம்பதம் (the soul's pada) or தொல்பதம் (the ancient pada).

reading: The ancient Vedas speak of the supreme space as his body; even one who has seen the turiyatita of the crescent-wearer, if he clings to that causal adjunct, is not pure, if you ask.
nuance: Who is meant by பரனும் is unclear: the Supreme himself, said to be impure if bound to a causal adjunct, or the seer who has reached the Supreme. மிண்டின், if he clings or presses, is read either way.

reading: See him as the lone Tatpara standing within space, wind, fire, water and earth; and the Shakti that is the open space standing in those same five is his form.
nuance: Lines 1 and 3 are the same, so the verse places Siva and Shakti in the same five elements: he as what stands alone within them, she as the form they take.

reading: For the yogi of rare austerity who thinks fully on Meru and the disc of spreading rays, if he does glorious tapas, Siva's grace becomes his own; he need not go elsewhere, for there is nothing other.
nuance: Meru and the rayed disc are traditionally the crown of the yogic body and the inner sun. சிவனருள் தானாகும் may mean grace comes of itself or the yogi becomes grace. பேரவும் வேண்டாம்: no need to move or leave.

title: முத்திரியம்
theme: The three turiyas: the soul's turiya, the Supreme's turiya and Siva's turiya, each traced through waking and the states below it, answer to the three words of tvam tat asi. Standing in turiya the soul reaches the Lord beyond reach, leaves the thirty-six tattvas and maya by grace, and Nandi gives the true reality.
structure_note: 2466 sets out the three turiyas and their match with the three padas; 2467 to 2469 and 2472 to 2473 work through the states in each; 2470 and 2471 turn from the scheme to the practice and its fruit.
source_issues: Chapter title reads முத்திரியம், probably for முத்துரியம் (the three turiyas), which is what the verses treat.
2472: தெம்பதம் for தொம்பதம்.
2467 line 3 (ஆனாப் பரபதம் அற்றது அருநனா) is obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: In the three states from waking is the soul's turiya; in the three from his own is the Supreme's turiya; in the three from waking is Siva's turiya; these together match the padas of tvam tat asi.
nuance: The scheme is technical: each turiya is reached through its own triad of waking, dream and sleep, and the three are traditionally matched with தொம் (the soul), தத் (the Supreme) and அசி (their union).

reading: Turiya in one's own waking is one's tvam-pada; the same turiya runs through waking and the other two; the unending supreme pada is beyond; and in the three higher states, like the sky, Siva's turiya draws near.
nuance: ஆனாப் பரபதம் அற்றது அருநனா is obscure and the reading of line 3 is a guess. வானான மேல் மூன்று, the upper three that are sky, are taken as the higher grades of the states.

reading: The four states in the soul's turiya, and the four practised in the Supreme's turiya, ripening into the Supreme that does not abate, meet at the node of turiya, and combined they make five.
nuance: The arithmetic (four, four, five) depends on how the states are counted; கணு, node or joint, is taken as the point where the soul's states meet the Supreme's. The sense is unclear.

reading: Go straight along the path through the ten states within the three turiyas to their end, and in the union with the Supreme that is the end of all, join the two halves into one end.
nuance: ஈர்ஐந்து அவத்தை, ten states, are traditionally the five lower and five pure states. இரு பாதி, the two halves, may be the soul and the Supreme or the tvam and tat of the saying.

reading: Hold fast to the ground of turiya; though the Lord seems out of reach, standing there you reach him, and when he is known as he truly is, the lips no longer meet to recite: that is the truth of it.
nuance: பன்னா உதடுகள் தட்டாது, lips that do not strike together, is read as silence or as the mantra repeated without the lips moving. எட்டாது எனின் நின்று எட்டும் plays on reaching what does not reach.

reading: Those devotees on the path who knew the thirty-six as unreal before knowledge and left them, and broke dense maya by grace, came to know the state that becomes the great grace never parted.
nuance: அசத்து is the Siddhanta term for what is inert and passing, set against the conscious soul. Here the breaking of maya is by grace, and the knowers are அன்பர், those who love.

reading: As the fourth, turiya, becoming the waking within waking, is the soul's tvam-pada, so for the soul freed of deeds, becoming waking and the rest, the Supreme's turiya is the tat-pada.
nuance: தெம்பதம் is read as தொம்பதம். The verse makes the two padas parallel grades of the same scheme: the soul's turiya for tvam, the Supreme's for tat, reached by the soul freed of deeds.

reading: As tvam-pada and tat-pada are named as turiyas, the good name belongs to the trusted third turiya; beyond the moon and beyond the very subtle, glorious Nandi, the true reality, took me and gave grace.
nuance: The third turiya is the asi of the saying, the union. அம்புலி உன்னா, not thinking the moon, is taken as beyond the moon of the yogic body. செம்பொருள், the true reality, is a word the Kural also uses.

title: மும்முத்தி
theme: The three releases: the soul's release, the release in the Supreme and the release in Siva, which are the state beyond, stilled calm and bliss. Souls that do not know what truly is go to birth, those who know go to grace, and release is to leave all and become one with Siva, who is attainment, release and samadhi.
source_issues: 2474: line 3 begins with a stray 'Y' (Yமூவயின்), flagged as corrupt in the source.

reading: Release of the soul is the state beyond, release in the Supreme is the stilled calm, release in Siva is bliss; these three releases of three forms dwell within Om, at the end of nada.
nuance: அதீதம், உபசாந்தம், ஆனந்தம் name the three releases. தாரம் is taken as Om and நாதாந்தம் as the end of nada. Line 3 is printed with a stray letter.

reading: Souls that do not know what truly is go to birth; souls that know it go to grace; seeing that nothing inside or outside is anything in itself, and leaving it, to become one with Siva beyond is release.
nuance: ஆவது, 'what is' or 'what avails', opens three lines. ஓவு is cessation, and ஓவு சிவன் may be Siva who is the ceasing or Siva beyond.

reading: To those who become Siva, destroying the three impurities and three gunas, and say 'I am he' on the path of union with the three releases, the stainless one, Siva, stands forth.
nuance: சோகம் is so'ham, 'I am he'; it also means sorrow, but the context fixes the first sense. தவமான, which is tapas, may qualify the three releases or the path.

reading: The great Lord who cut away bondage becomes attainment, release, the purity that is firm Siva, the Shakti of bliss that ends the three fires, and the highest samadhi.
nuance: பெத்தம் (baddha) is the bound state, opposite of release. முத்தீ, three fires, are taken as the three impurities or the three torments; the ritual three fires are another reading.

title: முச்சொரூபம்
theme: The three forms (முச்சொரூபம்): the soul rises past the impurities into the knowledge of 'I am Siva' and release in three forms, while the Lord, beyond measure, becomes formless, form and both, comes as Shakti and guru, and holds the three forms as a gem holds its lustre.
structure_note: 2478 to 2481 describe the three forms and the Lord in and beyond them; 2482 and 2483 use the gem and its light; 2484 turns to a yogic instruction.
source_issues: 2483 line 2 (நாடிஒண் முப்பதும்) is obscure; முப்பதும் may be a misreading of முப்பதம்.

reading: Rising stage by stage past the five impurities, reaching the stilled knowledge of 'I am Siva', and gaining release in the three forms as if they were separate, at the end the ancient Supreme makes the truth plain.
nuance: மலம் ஐந்து are traditionally anava, karma, maya, mayeya and tirodhana. வேறும் என, 'as if separate', suggests the three forms are distinguished only on the way.

reading: Three mansions are the seat of the three; in the three the thirty-six arise; on seeing the light that sprouts and rises within the three, the body's reckoning ceases.
nuance: The three mansions may be the three bodies (gross, subtle, causal) or three regions of the yogic body; the three who dwell there are traditionally Brahma, Vishnu and Rudra. காயக் கணக்கு, the body's account, may be its debts of deeds.

reading: When the world is moved from its place and the ages are gone, and the three abiding lights become one, who can know the measure and greatness of the Lord within the many things and their natures?
nuance: The three lights are traditionally sun, moon and fire. The verse sets the Lord against dissolution: when all else merges, he remains past measure.

reading: Dividing the distinctions that start from the great one, the Lord becomes formless, form and form-and-formless; comes as Shakti, as guru, as the many souls; and dwelling with them in form, is one with them and not one.
nuance: பெருவாய் may be mahat, the great principle, or something else. ஒன்றாய் அன்றாம், one and not one, states the relation of Lord and souls as Siddhanta takes it.

reading: As a gem's light and lustre are its own marks and it stands as the gem, so the gentle three forms and the Shaktis rest in him: hold to the feet of great Nandi who made them serve.
nuance: The gem and its light is the classic image of a quality inseparable from what has it. பணிவித்த, who made them bow or serve, may also mean who made me bow.

reading: As one good gem holds its stone-light, colour, lustre and the strike of its rays, so in the three voids where words cease, speaking the great word beyond speech, is the experience at the end of the three, free of darkness.
nuance: நாடி ஒண் முப்பதும் is obscure (perhaps the bright thirty, or a misreading of முப்பதம், the three padas), as is முத்திராந்தம், the end of the mudras or of the three. The gem image continues 2482.

reading: Restrain the nada of the moving red lotus that holds a light within, and open from above the doorway that she who holds the waters has sealed shut.
nuance: The red lotus is a centre of the yogic body. பயோதரி, she who holds water or milk, is taken as kundalini or a nadi that blocks the way up; விடம் may be 'place' or 'poison'. A plain reading is not available.

title: முக்கரணம்
theme: The three instruments (முக்கரணம்): as one man appears in three roles, so the difference of Siva, the Supreme and the soul may be called one; and when Om, breath and space are raised and the stupor of the three instruments is cleared, Nandi gives the inner samadhi of unmani.
source_issues: 2487 line 2 (அக்கைக்காரணம்) is obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: As one man, joined to three places, is seen in a different form as each duty requires, so the difference among Siva, the Supreme and the soul, spoken of together, may be called one.
nuance: The image is one person in three roles. ஒன்றெனலாம், 'may be called one', is guarded: it allows the difference while naming it one.

reading: Make the light shine and raise it as Om, make the breath breath and draw it in fittingly, make space space and set it rising upward, and as clarity grows, Siva's state grows clear.
nuance: Each line doubles its noun (ஒளியை ஒளிசெய்து, வளியை வளிசெய்து, வெளியை வெளிசெய்து), so each is made purely itself. The three are traditionally taken as the mantra, the breath and the inner space of the yogic practice.

reading: Nandi gave, as a thing held in the hand, what comes when the stupor of the three instruments is cleared; great Manonmani then goes on alone, and that unmani is the inner samadhi.
nuance: முக்கரணம் are traditionally mind, speech and body, or the inner instruments. மனோன்மணி is a name of Shakti and a stage of yoga; உன்மணி (unmani) is the state beyond the mind. அக்கைக்காரணம் is obscure.

title: முச்சூனிய தொந்தத்தசி
theme: The three voids and tvam tat asi: the soul, the Supreme and their union, the three words of the saying, appear in turiya and are matched with maya, the beyond and peace, and with the letters of Om; when the impurities and qualities die Siva appears as darkness leaves before the moon, and the soul is known as Parasiva.
structure_note: 2488 sets out the three padas; 2489 and 2494 tie them to the impurities and the letters of Om; 2490 and 2491 give a practice of recitation and its fruit; 2492 and 2493 place the padas and give the Devadatta example.
source_issues: Chapter title முச்சூனிய தொந்தத்தசி: the verses use தொந்தத்தசி (tvam tat asi) throughout.
2489 line 2: காமதம் may be an error for தாமதம், as in 2494.
2492: அம்புரை is obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: Tat-pada, tvam-pada and asi-pada, which is itself: these three ancient padas appear in turiya; what stands in them is the soul, the Supreme and Siva who comes forth, and in these three threes the word-padas become tvam tat asi.
nuance: The verse names the three words of the saying and matches them with soul, Supreme and Siva. Which pada goes with which is the tradition's reading of a compressed line.

reading: In the three of tvam tat asi lie the old impurities beginning with kamya and the old qualities, and when these impurities and qualities die and Siva appears, it is like darkness going before the moon.
nuance: காமியம் is the impurity of desire-born deeds. காமதம் in line 2 is doubtful; 2494 has தாமதம், and line 2 may name the qualities beginning with tamas. இந்து is the moon.

reading: Bring forth tvam tat asi in the breath, reckon its order as tenfold, and recite the saying with its endless states before Siva in the order that moves it.
nuance: வாசி may be the breath, as in the yoga of that name, or the utterance. ஈர்ஐந்து, ten, recalls the ten states of 2469. The practice described cannot be fixed from the verse.

reading: Setting Siva within the bliss of one's own nature, and letting the teaching that is Om sink into a true heart, he knew the truth and stood, having become the Father's servant.
nuance: மதி may be 'the mind' or 'the moon'. The verse ends in servitude (அடிமை), not in identity, which is worth noticing in a chapter on the soul becoming Parasiva.

reading: Tvam-pada appears within maya, tat-pada rises in the beyond, asi-pada is reached in trusted peace: this is the saying tvam tat asi, spoken by the heavenly ones.
nuance: அம்புரை is obscure; it is read here as the beyond. உம்பர் உரை may be the word of the gods or the word from above.

reading: As in 'this is that Devadatta' the qualities that came between are let go, so when the body and its material cause are set aside, the true knowledge called tvam tat asi is that the soul is Parasiva.
nuance: அச்சோயம் தேவதத்தன் is so'yam devadattah, 'this is that Devadatta', the standard example by which the saying's identity is explained: the same man seen in another time and place. Tirumular uses the Vedanta example within a Saiva frame.

reading: The three great impurities, tamas, kamya and the dark quality, go with A, U and the vanishing M through the three bodies, and the turiya in which they are themselves is tvam tat asi.
nuance: ஆசித்த குணம் is unclear. அகார, உகார, மகாரம் are the letters of Om; ஆம் அறும் மவ்வும், 'M that ends', and உடல் மூன்று, the three bodies, follow the mantra analysis. The line-by-line pairing is the tradition's.

title: முப்பாழ்
theme: The three voids (முப்பாழ்): letting go of the seven effects gives the void of maya, of the seven causes the void of knowledge, and of their traces the void of calm; these voids are the soul, the Supreme and Siva-Shakti, where speech ends. The speaker crosses the void to Nandi's feet, and at the last even void, heart and form are gone.
structure_note: 2495 and 2496 define the three voids; 2497 is the speaker's own crossing; 2498 and 2499 warn that the void is named more than known; 2500 dissolves the void itself.
source_issues: 2499 line 2 (வேறா கயபரை யா) is obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: Seeing and leaving the seven effects, the void of maya; seeing and leaving the seven causes, the void of knowledge; seeing and ending the traces of effect and cause, the bond ends in the glorious void of calm.
nuance: The seven effects and seven causes recur in 2501 and 2505 and are not listed. வாதனை are the latent traces (vasana). உபசாந்தம் is the stilled calm named in 2474.

reading: The void of maya is the soul, the void of space is the abiding Supreme, and the far third void is the soul pervaded in Siva-Shakti; in that pure form speech comes to its end.
nuance: The three voids are matched to soul, Supreme and union, as the padas were in 2488. வியாப்தம் is pervasion; சொல் முடிவு, the end of words, fits the wordless void of 2498.

reading: To join the feet of Nandi, the Lord who rides his bull gladly every day and has no rival, I take the void as my way, cross it, and come to rest in the void that has shaken off even that imagining.
nuance: There are two voids here: the one crossed, and the one beyond imagining where the speaker comes to rest. The bull-rider gives a personal Lord in a chapter otherwise abstract.

reading: The wordless void in which turiya subsides, the foolish call the rare Paramparam; but who knows the rare ground they praise by that name?
nuance: ஆதர் usually means the ignorant, which makes the verse a rebuke to those who name it without knowing; if it is taken as 'those who love', the last line is a wondering question instead.

reading: When the thirty-six are gone and 'nama' with the rest has withdrawn, the true Supreme, standing apart, joins one in the final breath; is this not what comes when one comes clear in 'Sivayanama', which the unclear cannot grasp?
nuance: In the five letters tradition reads ந and ம as concealment and impurity, so dropping நம leaves சிவாய, Siva, grace and soul. Line 2 (வேறா கயபரை யா) is obscure, and வாசி may be breath or utterance.

reading: For those who know the true nature, that the heart is form and form is the heart, there is no hollow, no mound, no void, no heart and no form.
nuance: The verse closes a chapter on voids by denying the void too. பள்ளம், திடர் (hollow, mound) are the uneven ground of distinctions.

title: காரிய காரண உபாதி
theme: The adjuncts of effect and cause (காரிய காரண உபாதி): the soul is bound by seven adjuncts and the Supreme by seven more; when these, with effect and cause, are cut off, the soul becomes Siva. The letters of Om and of சிவாய are matched with soul, Supreme and Siva, and anava leaves only through the Lord who is the life of life.

reading: When the seven powers of the soul's adjuncts that must be destroyed, and the seven adjuncts of the Supreme that cling, are cut off together with effect and cause, the soul becomes that Siva.
nuance: The seven and seven are not listed. That the Supreme too has adjuncts (பரோபாதி) recalls 2463, where even the Supreme clinging to a causal adjunct is called impure.

reading: When the thirty-six effect-adjuncts have gone, the soul, passing apart through waking, the dream within waking and the deep sleep beyond the thirty-six, and standing in a ground it has not yet reached, is what is called tvam-pada.
nuance: பேறா நிலம் may be 'the ground not yet gained' or 'the ground of gain'. கனாநனா is dream within waking, one of the graded states.

reading: A is the soul, U is the Supreme, M is Siva in the three padas; one may also say SI is Siva, VA is the Supreme and YA is the soul.
nuance: The verse matches the letters of Om and of சிவாய with the same three. The order reverses: in Om the soul comes first, in சிவாய Siva does.

reading: The Lord is the life of life, unceasing and undying, and lives in the doubt-free distinction from the causal adjunct; except through him, the anava that wearies will not leave.
nuance: ஆணவம் is the root impurity of Siddhanta. விதிரேகம் (vyatireka, distinction) and உபமிதம் (comparison, or what is shown by likeness) are technical terms of logic, and the second line's sense is uncertain.

reading: The harsh bound soul mixes in the seven effects, Parasiva mixes in the seven causes; in the void beyond the world of imagined effect and cause and of word and pada, he is the Supreme beyond the supreme.
nuance: கடும்பசு, the harsh or tightly bound soul. பராபரம் is the Supreme beyond the supreme. The verse returns to the voids of 2495 to place the Supreme beyond both effect and cause.

title: உபசாந்தம்
theme: Upasantam (உபசாந்தம்), the stilling: the quiet that comes when the tendencies left by cause and effect fall away, beyond waking and turiya, as the soul is purified, pervaded by the Lord and steeped in Siva's bliss. It ends in union, like water settling clear after waves.
structure_note: 2506 places upasantam among the seeds of release, devotion and attainment; 2507 to 2509 define it through the falling away of maya's effects and causes and the states beyond waking; 2510 and 2511 give its fruit, Siva-bliss, silence and union.
source_issues: 2507 line 4 (பாரண வும்) is obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: The seed of release is the Lord's own knowledge, the seed of devotion is bowing and clinging to him, the seed of attainment is becoming supreme Siva oneself, and the seed of power is one's own stilling.
nuance: The four lines are built alike on வித்து (seed). சத்தி in the last line can be the Lord's Shakti or simply strength; read either way, upasantam is put last, as the ground of the others' power.

reading: The seven effects hide within maya and the seven causes are hidden in the fierce void; when attachment to the traces left by effect and cause is cut away, that is the nature of upasantam.
nuance: Which seven effects and seven causes are meant is not said; tradition reads them as groups of tattvas. வாதனை (vasana) is the trace or tendency that remains after action. கடுவெளி (the fierce void) and பாரணவும் are obscure.

reading: That turiya is the purifying of the soul; the state beyond waking that it reaches, the lasting vision of the Supreme that comes with it, and upasantam lie in the Lord's pervading of oneself.
