nuance: சாக்கிராதீதம் (beyond waking) and ஆத்தும சுத்தி (purifying of the soul) are Siddhanta terms for the higher states. தன்னின் வியாத்தி may be the Lord's pervading of the self or the self's pervading; the syntax is loose.

reading: Removing anava from the states, knowing oneself as the thing to be gained, then complete purity, the unspoken state beyond waking, the guru-Supreme, and the pervasion that is gained: this is upasantam.
nuance: The verse lists stages without connecting words. ஆணவம் is the root mala. ஆறாது அமைந்து (settled, without cooling, or without six) and பிறழ் (flashing, or swerving) in the last line are unclear.

reading: When the traces of upasantam leave the heart, one has become Siva, steeped in Siva's bliss with the joy of silence, and what is settled in it after inquiry is the ten.
nuance: ஈர்ஐந்து (two fives) is taken by tradition as the ten stages of Siddhanta practice (seeing, purifying and knowing the tattvas, the self and Siva), but the verse does not name them. Even the trace of stillness is said to go.

reading: Made one with the Supreme beyond Parai, settled like clear water that had been in waves, he who has known the word and fully tasted the rare nectar has seen the shore, in a reckoning beyond words.
nuance: The water image carries the chapter: waves are the soul's movement, clear water its stilled state, and the water was never other than the sea. பரையின் பரம் is taken as Siva beyond his Shakti. கரைகண்டான் (one who has seen the shore) is the one who has crossed.

title: புறங்கூறாமை
theme: Under the title 'not speaking ill' (புறங்கூறாமை), the verses rebuke those who claim full knowledge without seeing the Lord, tell the heart to drop its boasting and to stop quarrelling over who is God, and praise those who contemplate him within: they see him, are loved by the knowers, and become Siva-siddhas who set aside the lesser releases.
structure_note: Only the opening verses (2512 to 2515) touch the title, as rebukes of boasting and quarrelling; 2516 to 2524 turn to contemplating the Lord within, and 2525 and 2526 define the Siva-siddhas.
source_issues: The chapter title புறங்கூறாமை (not backbiting) does not fit most of the verses; only 2512 to 2515, against boasting and quarrelling, touch it loosely.
2515 line 4: வணங்ககெழு looks like a misprint for வணங்கஎழு.
2522 line 4: உலகேழுங்க்ண் டேனே is a misprint for உலகேழுங் கண்டேனே.
2523 lines 2 and 3 (சிறுவரை யொன்றுடண் / டூனமொன் றின்றி) are garbled, probably for ஒன்றுண்டு ஊனம் ஒன்றின்றி.
2526 line 2: சுத்தாசுக் தத்துடன் is a misprint for சுத்தாசுத்தத்துடன்.

reading: Like men who take up a ringing, jewelled sword to strike the hare that lies in the crescent moon, the heartless who cannot see the one with the stained, jewelled throat say, 'We know it fully.'
nuance: The hare is the mark on the moon, out of reach of any sword; the claim to full knowledge without sight of Siva is as idle. கறைமணி கண்டன் is Siva, his throat dark with the poison he held. நெஞ்சிலர் (without heart) may mean without feeling or without understanding.

reading: As the black-legged eagle passes through the sky and the black snake leaves the dark-bottomed pool, O heart, give up your talk of your greatness; when you reach the rare, wave-tossed sea it will grow calm.
nuance: The eagle's passing that makes the snake leave may stand for the Lord's coming driving off the bonds, or simply for a lesser power giving way to a greater. The last line is obscure; ஆற may mean 'to grow calm' or 'like a river'.

reading: To stand at the gate of the womb and fight so that one's foes may die is petty knowledge; if it matched the great penance that the unfriendly do, the one who asked the giver would become a lone celestial.
nuance: புல்லறிவாண்மை is the Kural's own chapter title, here applied to hostile striving bound to birth (கருவாயில், the womb's gate). The second half is obscure: தருவலர் கேட்ட and தனியும்பர் admit several readings, perhaps of a celestial gift-tree.

reading: There is no need to quarrel: if the whole wide world agrees in thinking 'our Lord is the Lord', the eighteen hosts seek to bow and see his anklet-bound feet, and there love can be had.
nuance: The verse is closest to the title: the quarrel is over whose god is God. கணம் பதினெட்டு are the eighteen classes of celestial beings. The point is that agreement, not dispute, brings even the gods to his feet.

reading: If you think on the Lord who is my life more than I am, the pure one who is a great gem more than gold, the changeless one who is the life of all shining lives, he will come in the very way you think of him.
nuance: The comparisons (more than myself, more than gold) rank him above what one values most. உன்னும் உறும் வகையாலே says he is reached in the form one contemplates.

reading: Though many speak of the things to join with the Pure One, standing, sitting or lying, the one who conquers the five senses, quickly ends dispute and comes to know him as one becomes the one.
nuance: நின்றும் இருந்தும் கிடந்தும் may be postures of practice or 'at all times'. The last line can mean that the knower becomes one with him or that such a knower is rare, only one.

reading: Those who meditate on our father and Lord, who stands as subtle knowledge, as the world and as the knowledge that reckons the seven worlds, the knower of melody, are cherished by the knowers of heaven.
nuance: பண் அறிவாளன் (the one who knows melody) may point to Siva as lord of music or to his knowing the songs of devotees. விண் அறிவாளர் are the celestials or the wise who know the higher world.

reading: If you hold within, with eyes closed, the one whom even the celestials cannot know, and do this in the morning, with thought fixed, at all three times, your nature becomes the Parapara.
nuance: முப்போதும் is the three junctures of the day, when worship is done. எண் உற வாசம் is obscure: perhaps dwelling with thought fixed, or a reckoning of breaths. The claim is that the contemplator takes the nature of the Supreme.

reading: He who spread as one with the seven worlds, the lord of great grace who gave grace afterward, good within the learning of those whose minds are unsoured, is adorned with praise in a time that does not perish.
nuance: கன்றா மனத்தார் (those of unsoured mind) makes goodness of heart, not learning alone, the place where he is found. பொன்றாத போது may mean 'in the time that does not end' or 'when one does not perish'.

reading: I said 'Praise!' and raised my father's golden red feet on my head for ever; the ringing bell is the lamp of the inner breath, the body falls into a daze, I heard the sound and saw the hall.
nuance: The bell (எறிமணி) and the inner breath's lamp are traditionally read as the inner sound and light heard and seen in yoga, and மன்று as the hall of Siva's dance within. அற்றலும் is obscure; it may be a misreading of அரற்றலும் (the outcry).

reading: None who have entered within truly know Nandi, who comes before me when sought within me; I entered the nest and climbed, closed my eyes and saw his form, and I saw the seven worlds.
nuance: கூடு (nest) is commonly the body, and climbing within it the yogic ascent. Seeing the seven worlds with eyes closed claims that the inner vision holds the whole.

reading: To those who without flaw contemplate the fame that has come, the settled knowledge, and a little hill where honey is, he becomes the hunter who makes heaven.
nuance: The small hill with honey may be an inner place (the head, where nectar is held to flow) and மறவன் (hunter) Siva as the Kirata who hunts and wins the soul. The text of lines 2 and 3 is run together and partly garbled.

reading: The great ascetics whose mind became the great moon, whose pure mind is the radiant supreme bliss, entered peace that swallows the world and, their malas gone, reached rest.
nuance: மாமதி plays on மதி as moon and as mind; the moon is often the cool inner light of yoga. சகம் உண (to swallow the world) is read as the world ceasing to appear. சாந்தி links this verse to the stilling of chapter 187.

reading: Those who cast off the three graded releases as flawed, drive out the darkness of the bonds that had seemed pleasant, lose their pride, change 'mine' and 'I' right there and stand firm are the Siva-siddhas.
nuance: பதமுத்தி மூன்றும் are the three releases short of union (dwelling in his world, nearness, his form). இதம் உற்ற (agreeable) is a sharp touch: the bonds are dark yet pleasant. எனது யான் is the pair 'mine' and 'I'.

reading: The siddhas are those who have seen Siva; with excellence they are steeped in the pure and impure yet unsteeped, freed ones rooted at the root of release, powerful in that root, of the nature of Sadasiva.
nuance: தோய்ந்தும் தோயாதவர் (steeped yet unsteeped) is the jivanmukta who lives among pure and impure things untouched by them. மூலம் (root) may also point to the muladhara, the root centre of yoga.

title: எட்டிதழ்க் கமல முக்குண அவத்தை
theme: The eight-petalled lotus and the states of the three gunas: the eight directions with their guardian gods are set as the petals of an inner lotus, through whose stalk the sushumna rises to a light; the Lord stands in the eight, in the grades beyond them and in the ages, and is reached at the summit, where a tank fills without a river and a lotus blooms without mud.
structure_note: 2527 and 2531 name the eight directions and their gods; 2528 and 2529 make them the petals of the inner lotus; 2532 to 2534 rank the grades beyond the eight and the ages; 2530 and 2535 give the tank and lotus at the summit; 2536 closes with those who seek him. The three gunas of the title are named in no verse.
source_issues: The chapter title names the three gunas, but no verse in the chapter names them.
2527 line 4: நிதித்தெண் டிசையு is unclear, perhaps for நிதித்து எண்டிசையும்.
2533 line 3: அண்டத்துக் சென்ற is a misprint for அண்டத்துச் சென்ற.
2530 line 3: கொண்பனை யாள் is obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: Indra in the east where the sun rises, Agni, Yama, the praised Nirriti, Varuna, good Vayu, honoured Kubera and Isana of the north stand filling the eight directions.
nuance: The list is the standard eight guardians of the quarters, in order round the compass. Placed here, they are traditionally read as presiding over the eight petals of the heart lotus. நிதித்து (keeping guard?) is unclear.

reading: The gathered flower has eight petals, and close within it is the city of maya; through the sushumna inside the narrowed stalk, perceive the gathered light and rise, and be saved.
nuance: The eight-petalled lotus is traditionally placed at the heart; தண்டு (stalk) is the spinal column and சுழுனை the central channel. மாயாபுரி (city of maya) may be the body or the lotus itself.

reading: There are three lotuses in bud, and in all three the light, a spreading flame, opens them; if one enters two petals within the eight, an old thing blooms and is a dream.
nuance: The three lotuses may be the three gunas or three centres; the title suggests the gunas. The last line seems to tie entering two of the petals to the dream state, but what பண்டம் (old thing) is cannot be fixed.

reading: There is a river, and a tank within; Siva's way is a hundred, its colour subtle; the precious Thing stays apart, with her of full breasts as his share.
nuance: The river and inner tank are read as the flow of nectar to a reservoir in the head, as in 2535. நூறே (a hundred) and கொண்பனையாள் are obscure. கூறு (share) recalls Shakti as half of Siva's body, yet he is said to stay apart (வேறே).

reading: The first Lord, who stands as the eight directions, the eight chariots, the eight deities and the eight kinds, fills there the eight and the four, and this is how he rises within the eight buds.
nuance: The verse multiplies eights to place the Lord in every petal. தேர் எட்டும் (eight chariots) and வகை எட்டு நான்கும் (eight and four, or eight fours) are unclear.

reading: Seven are with form; passing what is spoken, in the eighth lives the Supreme; passing that, in the ninth the Parapara of the ages; in the high tenth, the lone nature that descends as the sky.
nuance: சகளம் (with parts, with form) set against higher, formless grades is Siddhanta language, but which seven, and what the eighth to tenth are, the verse does not say. தாழ்வது வான may also be read 'that is lower than the sky' or 'that bows'.

reading: The one of many ages, the sun, the Lord; the ages within the five good ages, the age that passes into the cosmos; in that age, at its summit, in the One, is Bhagavan.
nuance: ஊழி (aeon) repeats in every line. The five ages may be cosmic cycles or the five states; the summit of the age may be the end of dissolution or the top of the head. The reading is a guess.

reading: The eight elephants that bear the world, the roaming tusker with the throngs of gods, fire, rain and the moving air all have their hold in the vast space.
nuance: The eight elephants are those of the quarters, and the tusker Indra's Airavata. பரியும் ஆகாசம் may be the vast space or the space that bears; tradition may read it as the inner space where the Lord is.

reading: On the summit of a high hill where springs rise there is a rare tank that fills without a river; the one with twisted locks wears the rich lotus that bloomed without mud, without a flower.
nuance: Each line holds a paradox: a tank with no river, a lotus with no mud, a flower worn with no flower. The hill is commonly the head, the tank the nectar there and the lotus the thousand-petalled one; plainly, the verse says the Lord's things need none of the world's causes.

reading: When one and two have joined, though people stand and sit and talk of many lands, those who conquer and stay seeking the changeless one, going or staying, are the ones who reach the sacred.
nuance: ஒன்றும் இரண்டும் (one and two) may be the soul with Siva and Shakti, or the breath and mind, or the two side channels with the central one. திருவடையோர் may be 'those who reach the sacred' or 'those who reach the holy feet'.

title: ஒன்பான் அவத்தை - ஒன்பான் அபிமானி
theme: The nine states and their nine presiding selves (ஒன்பான் அவத்தை, ஒன்பான் அபிமானி): waking, dream and sleep, each taken at three levels, have each a presiding self; passing through them, cut from mala and the gunas, the soul reaches turiya as its true form, and to become Siva beyond the three turiyas is the attainment of Siddhanta.
structure_note: 2537 names the nine presiding selves; 2538 and 2539 describe passing beyond the nine states; 2540 and 2543 count tattvas; 2541, 2542 and 2544 turn to the Lord who orders states, worlds and births; 2545 sums up.
source_issues: 2537: the names of the third group of presiding selves (சொலிதையன், பிரசா பத்தியன், விசாந்தன்) are garbled.
2543 line 3 (ஓதுங் கமைமாயே யோரிரண் டோ ரமுத்தி) is corrupt.
2539 line 4 (தவமான மவையாகி) is obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: Under the first word are Visva, Taijasa and Prajna; under the good word Virat, Hiranyagarbha and Avyakrita; under the last word the one called Ojita(?), Prajapatya and Visanta: these are the presiding selves.
nuance: தொற்பதம், நற்பதம், பிற்பதம் are taken as the three words of 'tat tvam asi' (tvam, tat, asi). Visva, Taijasa and Prajna are the Vedantic selves of waking, dream and sleep, Virat, Hiranyagarbha and Avyakrita their cosmic counterparts; the third group's names are garbled and the reading is a guess.

reading: When the nine states beginning with waking are let go, unattached to the birth-bound malas and gunas, in the common ground of penance, truth and knowledge the twofold turiya becomes the true form.
nuance: பற்றில் may be 'if one holds' or 'when one releases'; the reading follows the second. துவமார் துரியம் (twofold turiya?) and சொருபம் (svarupa, true form) are technical and unclear.

reading: In a mind become Siva, the self as jiva breaks up and the three birth-bound malas scatter and are uprooted; at the end of the nine, good Siva-knowledge takes their place, and the self becomes itself and not itself.
nuance: சீவன் சிதைய (the jiva breaks up) is the end of the bound self, not of the soul. தான் அல்லவாகுமே may be the soul being neither itself nor other than Siva, the Siddhanta 'not one, not two'. தவமான மவை is obscure.

reading: Before the nine already told there are tattvas, and nine others not to be counted in his word; these two nines can be told later, and setting them aside, the one who rules his own doing excels.
nuance: Which two sets of nine are meant is not said. The last line may praise the Lord as sovereign over his acts or the knower who is master of himself.

reading: Seeking the nature of the Lord who spoke the nine and the five and the world, I say 'my Lord' within, night and day, and he cut away the strong karma and removed it.
nuance: ஒன்பதும் ஐந்தும் may be the nine states and five states, or fourteen worlds. The plain claim is that constant inward remembrance of the Lord cuts karma.

reading: Over many long ages he gathered goods; with many clans and colours and marks he joins; with many fruits and twelve times he thinks; with many lands and ways, he is the one whose nature is in them.
nuance: The verse is a list of manifolds (பல, many, in every line) of which the Lord is the nature. பன்னிரு காலம் (twelve times) may be the twelve months or twelve breaths; much of the verse cannot be fixed.

reading: The first Parapara becomes Parapara the Shakti; light, the Supreme, the soul and the good tattva that is spoken, maya and the two, and release: with the nine distinctions in order, he is the first.
nuance: The verse seems to list nine grades from Siva and Shakti down through soul and maya. Line 3 (ஓதுங் கமைமாயே யோரிரண் டோ ரமுத்தி) is corrupt, and the count cannot be checked.

reading: Making the unclear mind clear, he set by grace for souls hell and heaven, not different from the earth, and endless births; those who do not see clearly what is separate are the souls that took on karma.
nuance: The verse makes even hell and births the work of grace, set for the soul's clarifying, a Siddhanta claim. வேறாத (not different) and வேறாத் தெளியார் (who do not see as separate) play on one word and admit several readings.

reading: In the nine states are the nine presiding selves, with the nine tattvas practised in good measure; to pass beyond the three turiyas that stand in the nine and become Siva in the fair part is the attainment of Siddhanta.
nuance: முத்துரியம் (three turiyas) is taken as the turiya of each of the three levels in 2537. செம்பால் (the fair part) may mean rightly, or in the red (Shakti's) part.

title: சுத்தாஅசுத்தம்
theme: Pure and impure (சுத்தாஅசுத்தம்): what is truly hidden and what truly defiles are not where people look. The Lord sits a few fingers from the nose tip and within the body, yet is sought in far places; ritual impurity does not touch the disciplined, the worshipper, the fire-keeper or the knower; and true purity is the Lord's way, name and feet, while those bound to karma never learn its fruit.
structure_note: 2546 to 2550 on the hidden Lord, maya and karma and the inner search; 2551 to 2555 on impurity and purity; 2556 and 2557 contrast devotees with those deluded by karma.
source_issues: 2550 repeats 2071 almost word for word (யெங்கும் for எங்கும்).
2553 line 1: அவர்ககுச் is a misprint for அவர்க்குச்.
2554: தூரறி வாரில்லை is unclear; it may be தூர் அறிவார் (who know the root) or a corruption.
2549 is obscure throughout (மோழை, முழை, கோழை) and may be corrupt.

reading: No one knows the Lord's dwelling, between four and three finger-breadths from the tip of the nose; the great Veda that speaks of him shrinks back before it: such is its nature.
nuance: The measure from the nose is a yogic placement for meditation; whether it points outward from the nose or inward is not said. கூசியிருக்கும் (shrinks, is abashed) puts the Lord beyond what scripture can say.

reading: Deeds are one; the claim on the deed one intends, the karma, and the seed of earlier births: once one sees these and departs from them, what one does after enters the destruction of karma.
nuance: கன்மக் கயம் is taken as karma-kshaya, the wearing out of karma. The first two lines are compressed; they may distinguish the deed, the agency claimed in it, and inherited karma. The claim is that after seeing, action no longer binds.

reading: The hidden Thing is hidden because maya hides it; when maya is hidden, that Thing appears; for those able to hide maya away there is no body and no thought.
nuance: The verse turns on மறை, to hide, and on மறைப்பொருள, which can also mean the Veda's meaning. Hiding the hider reverses the concealment. 'No body, no thought' is taken as freedom from the sense of being the body and mind, not their end.

reading: Closing the blunt one, opening the cave and entering within, at the sign of the cool one where phlegm collects, reaching deep there, putting it outside in the fire and shutting it down is one's own strength.
nuance: A technical yogic verse. மோழை, முழை (cave), கோழை (phlegm) and அனல் (fire) are traditionally read of closing the lower opening, opening the passage at the head, the cool region of the palate and the fire of kundalini, but none is fixed by the verse.

reading: People wander searching everywhere in the land for the one who stirs the body, the good lord of the body, Nandi who is fragrant within the body; they do not know the meaning that stands within the body.
nuance: காயம் (body) comes four times, closing every turn back on the body. கருத்து may be the meaning, the intent, or the Lord himself as the thought within. Sengalvaraya notes a parallel in Appar's Tevaram, 'I searched and found him within me'.

reading: The ignorant cry 'impurity, impurity', but no one knows where impurity lies; once one knows where impurity lies, the place of impurity is itself what is impure.
nuance: ஆசூசம் is ritual impurity, as from birth or death. The last line is circular; it is commonly taken to say the impurity is in the mind or in the body's bonds, not in the events people avoid. Another division of the words is possible.

reading: There is no impurity for those who keep strict discipline, none for those who worship Hara, none for those who tend the sacred fire, and none for the knower of the rare Veda.
nuance: The four are the disciplined (நியமத்தர்), the worshipper, the fire-ritualist and the jnani. Tirumular does not abolish ritual purity but exempts those whose practice already purifies; the fire rite itself is among them.

reading: For those who stand in worship and bow, a purity bound in the whorl begins; those who stand in the pit cannot join it, and its signs cannot be seen except by those who are freed.
nuance: சுழி (whorl) may be a yogic place, such as the point between the brows, or the turning of worship itself; குழி (pit) is perhaps the pit of births or of sense. கழிபட்டவர் (those who have passed out) are read as the freed.

reading: The pure gem and the pure fire send out pure light; none know the root of the pure gem and pure fire; for those who know the root, the pure gem and pure fire become pure indeed.
nuance: The gem and fire may be the inner light of yoga, or Siva and Shakti, or the soul and the Lord. தூர் (root, base) is a guess for தூரறிவார்; it could also be தூய் அறிவார், 'those who know purely'.

reading: What is pure is the pure way he set freely, the Lord's holy name, the eight great attainments, and the word of the pure feet.
nuance: வாளா (freely, without cause) recurs in every line, which the reading takes as 'what is pure of itself'. அட்டமா சித்தி are the eight great powers of yoga. தூயடிச் சொல் may be the word of the Lord's feet or the pure word of scripture.

reading: Apart from the devotees who praise the grace of our father, the holy one who stands as the true Thing, others' minds are bewildered by delusion in the coiled whirl of suffering.
nuance: The four lines rhyme on பொருள், அருள், சுருள், மருள் (the Real, grace, coil, delusion), setting the Real and grace against the coil and delusion of the rest.

reading: They do not know what grows from karma, which is unreal; they do not see release through the knowledge of karma; they do not recite the Veda that says release is when karma leaves; the servants of karma do not know its great fruit.
nuance: அசத்து (asat, the unreal) is the Siddhanta term for what does not endure. வினைஞானம் may be knowledge of karma's working or a knowledge that is itself action; the line is unclear. வினை opens every line.

title: முத்திநிந்தை
theme: Reviling release (முத்திநிந்தை): those who deny a higher state, ignore the guru's sign, or take their own mind for God wander outside, unable to see the way shown them, while the Lord stands within and the short way is mantra and the inner fire.
structure_note: Most verses describe the deniers and the deluded (2558 to 2560, 2562, 2565); between them, 2561 and 2563 set the Lord who stays and pervades against them, and 2564 names the way.
source_issues: 2560: line 2 reads சிந்தையைப் தெய்வம், a misprint for சிந்தையைத் தெய்வம்.
2563: line 4 reads உன்னிகிலாரே, probably for உன்னகிலாரே.
2558: இரகதி and துரகதி are obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: The world knows that those who say there is no higher state go the way of hell; going from door to door, they begin to taste an evil end.
nuance: பரகதி (the higher state) is set against நரகதி (the way to hell). Line 1 can be read of those who say 'there is' and those who say 'there is not', that is of all who argue over it, or only of the deniers. இரகதி and துரகதி are obscure: இரகதி is taken here with இரத்தல் (begging), துரகதி as துர்கதி (an evil end).

reading: Those who cannot join the mark the guru set, and do not seek it, wander about talking fine words; they cannot sing of what he gave, so what gain can they have beside those who know it and can dance?
nuance: குறி (the mark, the sign) is what the guru points to, taken as the goal of practice. The last two lines are compressed: they may contrast the talkers with those who know the gift and dance, or ask what gain either has.

reading: Something goes out and comes into my heart; taking the opened mind for God, I called it that other Lord beyond all, and 'I am free of death; what is this here?' he says.
nuance: In this chapter the verse reads most naturally as the self-deluded seeker who mistakes his own mind (சிந்தை) for God and declares himself deathless, and the speaker's 'I' as dramatic. அறப்பட்ட may mean 'beyond dharma' or 'cut off'; the voice of the last line is unclear.

reading: As water does not stay on raised ground and a ship does not stay at sea but comes to harbour, the mighty Lord, showing the real thing that does not stay in the body, stood there.
nuance: Both images are of things that move on to where they belong. உறுபொருள் (the real thing) that does not stay in the body may be the soul or the truth, and அடலிடை வண்ணன் (the one of mighty form) is taken as Siva.

reading: Their hindrance is as weak as lotus thread, yet it spreads; wanting a way out they wander outside, and the wretched, shown the way to see, cannot see, and so wander on the evil path.
nuance: தாமரை நூல்போல் தடுப்பார் may mean those who would hold back the Supreme with a lotus fibre, a futile effort, or a bond as fine as lotus fibre that still holds them. கலதி (the wretched) and காணாக் (unseeing) are plain.

reading: People who reach their end without concealment join Nandi by fixing on him; the others cannot conceive the form that runs through forest, hill, field and every place.
nuance: மூடுதல் இன்றி (without covering) is taken as without the veil of ignorance; the contrast in the last two lines is supplied, since the verse does not name the second group.

reading: While the gods go south and north, west and east, the short way is to hold the mantra on the tongue and burn the fire in the centre, and so you will shine.
nuance: குறுவழி (the short way) is set against the gods' journeys in all directions. நடு அங்கி (the fire in the middle) is traditionally taken as the inner fire of yoga in the central channel; it may also be the fire of a rite.

reading: Though they look on in bewilderment they do no great tapas, and they do not hold to the concentration taught for their good; the evildoers who speak to provoke anger stood bearing heavy karma for themselves.
nuance: தாரணை (dharana, fixing the mind) is the sixth limb of yoga. The verse turns the scorners' words back on them: what they say in anger becomes their own load of deeds.

title: இலக்கணாத் திரயம்
theme: The three kinds of implication (இலக்கணாத் திரயம்), the Vedantic modes by which a word points beyond its literal sense, are placed in the states of the soul, and what lies beyond all implication is one's own true form; the senses fall like elephants to a well-aimed arrow.

reading: Implication that leaves the literal sense goes into the void; implication that touches it without leaving gathers in the stilled state; implication that both leaves and keeps reaches as far as sat and the rest; what is pointed to beyond implication is the true form.
nuance: விட்ட இலக்கணை, விடாத இலக்கணை and விட்டுவிடாத இலக்கணை are taken as the three lakshanas of Vedantic exegesis (jahat, ajahat and jahad-ajahat). வியோமம் (space, void), உபசாந்தம் (the stilled state) and சத்தாதி are taken as stages of the soul's ascent; where each mode is placed is the verse's own scheme and is not clear to me. இலக்கணாதீதம் சொரூபம் is the true form beyond them all.

reading: When the arrow, fitted to the string and driven by the bow, struck its mark, the five killing elephants fell with the shaft; for the one who sits in the bow and shoots keenly, the light rises to meet him like a jewel set in stone.
nuance: The five elephants are traditionally the five senses, and the arrow the aimed mind or the mantra; the reading is symbolic throughout. கல்கலன் என்னக் கதிர் எதிர் ஆமே is obscure: கல்கலன் may be a jewel of stone or a stone vessel. How the verse bears on the three implications is not stated.

title: தத்துவமசி வாக்கியம்
theme: The great saying 'that you are' (தத்துவமசி): its three words, 'you', 'that' and 'are', are placed in three turiyas, of the soul, of the Supreme and of Siva, and read by implication until the soul, its bonds and instruments left behind, becomes Siva. Tirumular calls this Vedanta's saying and Siddhanta's conclusion at once, and ends with the Lord's grace making the speaker spotless and every soul dancing as he makes it dance.
structure_note: 2568 to 2579 expound the saying through the turiyas, implication and the states; 2580 to 2582 turn to knowing, which the soul has only as Siva makes it know; 2583 to 2585 are the speaker's own experience of grace; 2586 closes on the Lord as the one who moves all.
source_issues: 2580: line 1 reads அகற்றிப் செறிவு, a misprint for அகற்றிச் செறிவு.
2586: line 2 reads அகில்மும், probably for அகிலமும், and line 3 எவ்வா யியுரும், which Sengalvaraya's citation gives as எவ்வா யுயிரும்.
2568: line 4 is printed மோவி விடும், probably ஓவி விடும் run on from the previous word.
2571 line 2 (அவைமன்னா வந்து வயத்தேகமான), 2578 line 3 (இரியிலும்) and 2583 line 4 (கடிதொழ காணன்னும்) are obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: The word 'you' is the soul in the soul's turiya, the word 'that' is in the supreme turiya to which it leaps, and the true word 'are' is in Siva's turiya; the truth of 'that you are' is that these fall away.
nuance: தொம்பதம், தற்பதம் and அசிபதம் are the three words of tat tvam asi (tvam, tat, asi). சீவதுரியம், பரதுரியம் and சிவதுரியம் are the three turiyas of Tirumular's scheme. ஓவி விடும் (cease, fall away) is read as the three distinctions dissolving into one.

reading: The soul beyond the thirty-six tattvas is the pure 'you'; 'that' is the end it reaches in the stilled state; when the soul that has gained this departs, in grace the glorious union of 'you', 'that' and 'are' is 'that you are'.
nuance: ஆறாறு (six sixes) is taken as the thirty-six tattvas and அணு as the soul. உபசாந்தம் and பிரசாதம் (grace) are technical stages; the order of the steps is compressed.

reading: As in 'this is that Devadatta', the implication that both leaves and keeps applies; they call the stilled state 'you, that, are', and the soul so reached becomes the Supreme, Siva.
nuance: அச்சோயம் தேவகத்தன் is read as sa ayam devadattah, the Vedantic example: the man seen now is the man seen before, so 'this' and 'that' keep the person and drop the time and place. The same mode is applied to 'that you are'. The reading of தேவகத்தன் as Devadatta is an inference.

reading: 'You, that, are' becoming one is the 'that you are' of Vedanta, reached by tapas; it is Siva, and that is Siddhanta-Vedanta.
nuance: The last line joins சித்தாந்தம் and வேதாந்தம் into one word, a claim that the two conclusions meet. Line 2 (அவைமன்னா வந்து வயத்தேகமான) is obscure; the reading of துவந்தத்தசி and தொந்தத்தசி as forms of 'you-that-are' is the usual one.

reading: They call the wordless void in which turiya subsides the rare Supreme, and do not deny it form; but who knows the rare ground where the one, the highest of the high, arises?
nuance: பாழ் (void, waste) for the highest state is a recurring term in Tirumular. ஆகாரி தன்று என்னார் may mean 'they do not say it is formless' or the reverse; the verse may be correcting those who stop at the void.

reading: If one seeks the words 'you', 'that' and 'are' above the three trusted turiyas, that state becomes the state where soul and Supreme can be called Siva, the true thing.
nuance: முத்துரியம் recalls the three turiyas of 2568. உம்பதம் உம்பதம் ஆகும் is obscure; it may mean 'that state becomes your state'.

reading: In the turiya so placed, in the bliss of one's own form, he took the teaching of Om he had received, released it in the true heart, and stood having reached true awareness just as it was given.
nuance: சொரூபானந்தம் (bliss of one's own form) and பிரணவ உபதேசம் (the teaching of Om) are technical; who 'he' is, the disciple or the Lord, is not stated.

reading: Place the five states beginning with waking in nada and the rest, put the corpse-like mala behind, and then seek the king who is beyond mind and speech, the pure Siva-state of being and peace.
nuance: நனவாதி ஐந்து are waking, dream, deep sleep, turiya and the beyond. பிணமா மலம் (mala like a corpse) is taken as anava, inert and binding. சத்தாதி சாந்தி may be a list of states (being, and the rest, peace) rather than one phrase.

reading: It is not filled up, since nothing is outside it; it takes no name, since no speech reaches it; it joins nothing, since there is nothing else; without any cause it shows itself, such is its nature.
nuance: The verse is built as three negations each with its reason (இலாமையின்), then a positive. பூரணியாது and பேரணியாது are uncertain forms; 'not filled' and 'not named' are guesses from the reasons given.

reading: The great saying that stood as 'you are that', once it ripens into 'I have become that', is the great grace of glorious Nandi that makes one Siva; then bliss itself becomes Nandi.
nuance: The verse turns the second-person saying (நீ அது ஆனாய்) into a first-person realization (அது நான் ஆனேன்) and credits the change to Nandi's grace, not to understanding alone. The last line is uncertain: அனந்தான் may be ஆனந்தம் or அனந்தன் (the endless).

reading: The soul becoming the Supreme, the high supreme soul becoming rare Siva, as the Siva-Veda calls him the highest of the high, is the form of Om beyond any fitting word.
nuance: இரியிலும் in line 3 is obscure. ஓமயம் is taken as 'made of Om'; it may also be read as 'Om-pervaded'.

reading: Mouth, nose, the crown of the head and the top: they stand as the first places; nadi and the rest, speech and the rest, sakala and the rest, and the far-reaching light are the five Siva-states.
nuance: The verse lists places in the head and categories (நாடி, வாக்கு, சகலம்) in the compressed manner of the yogic chapters; the five Siva-states (சிவகதி ஐந்து) are not named, and I can't fix how the lists map onto each other.

reading: Those who do not know the sign of putting away both knowing and not-knowing, and tending as Lord, without knowing separation, the Siva who stands everywhere as dense knowledge, cannot grasp him.
nuance: அறிவு அறியாமை இரண்டும் அகற்றி: both the soul's limited knowledge and its ignorance are to be set aside, since Siva is செறிவு அறிவு, knowledge itself. பிறிவு அறியாது (not knowing separation) is the condition of worship here. Sengalvaraya marks a parallel for line 1.

reading: The knowers know water and fire, and know water and its mixing; but unless the Knower who is there makes us know, we do not know the knowledge the Knower knows.
nuance: The repeated அறிவு makes the point by sound: the soul can know the elements, but knowledge of the Lord comes only as he makes it known (அறிவிக்கின்). This is the Siddhanta claim that the soul knows only with the Lord's help, as tradition takes it. அப்புங் கலப்பும் is unclear.

reading: Nandi is within the beyond-state and yet transcends it; the soul within the beyond-state is without knowledge; the abiding soul that gains understanding and leaves its rolling becomes one, the supreme soul settling into the Lord.
nuance: அதீதம் is the state beyond turiya. The contrast is between the Lord, who is in it and beyond it, and the soul, which in it is knowledgeless until it gains மதி. உருள் (rolling) is taken as the round of births. பதியிற் பதியும் plays on பதி as Lord and as 'settle'.

reading: As the gods stood before him to worship his feet, the Lord stood before me in grace so that I could worship his crown, and the brow-eyed one said: see now all that you once imagined in worship on earth.
nuance: The contrast of feet for the gods and crown for the speaker is a reading; பண்டு பாவித்தது (what you imagined before) suggests that earlier worship in imagination is now fulfilled in sight. கடிதொழ காணன்னும் is obscure.

reading: The spotless one with a spotless body, the unborn, came into my heart and said 'this one is my servant'; the gold-bodied one whom the gods praise could take away my impurity, saying 'be spotless'.
nuance: நின்மலம் opens the verse and returns in the Lord's command, so the Lord's purity becomes the speaker's. The Lord claims the speaker as his servant (அடியான்) before he cleanses him.

reading: Renouncing, I entered and saw the light that holds the flame; my heart flew up and lay prostrate, and the king of the heavens, whom I had never forgotten, set me here so that I would not die and be born again.
nuance: பறந்தது என் உள்ளம் பணிந்து கிடந்தே joins rapture and surrender in one line. இறந்து பிறவாமல் ஈங்கு வைத்தான் places release here, in this life, which suits the chapter's claim that the soul becomes Siva.

reading: Body, mouth, eyes, nose and ears, the inner instruments and all else: since every soul dances as the Lord makes it dance, the fullness without hands or mouth is seen everywhere as truth.
nuance: இறை ஆட்ட ஆடலால் (dancing as the Lord makes it dance) makes all the soul's action his. Sengalvaraya notes the parallel in Appar's Thevaram, ஆட்டுவித்தால் ஆரொருவர் ஆடாதாரே. கைவாயிலா நிறை (fullness with no hands or mouth) is the Lord who acts through all without organs of his own.

title: விசுவக் கிராசம்
theme: The swallowing of the universe (விசுவக் கிராசம்): the body dissolves into the Supreme like a bubble or camphor in fire, and Siva, who spreads through all and eats and spits out the world, draws soul, Supreme, turiya and cosmos into himself, as heated iron draws in water or a wood-apple is emptied while its shell stays whole.
source_issues: 2589: மனம் ஆதிகள் ஐந்தும் is unusual, since the inner instruments are usually four; a word may be lost or the count is Tirumular's own.

reading: Like the shadow-man who vanishes, like a bubble on flowing water, like camphor in a rising flame, this streaming body goes into that Supreme.
nuance: The three images are of disappearance without remainder: camphor in fire leaves no ash. சாயாபுருடன் (shadow-man) is taken as one's shadow, or as the shadow-figure some yogic texts describe; the plain sense holds either way. The body's ending is framed as merging into the Supreme, not as mere loss.

reading: When body and soul become wholly one, Siva-Shakti spreading through them is itself the Supreme; the soul, leaving the body, becomes everywhere, and end and beginning vanish in Siva.
nuance: ஒழிவற ஒன்றில் (become one without remainder) may describe the union of body and soul in the yogi or their joint absorption. கடையுந் தலையும் (end and head) may be the ends of time or the soul's lowest and highest states.

reading: The senses joined in ear, body, mouth, eyes and nose, and the five beginning with mind, unextinguished, without contracting, expanding and contracting, are themselves the moving and unmoving world without end.
nuance: The verse seems to say that the soul's senses and inner faculties, in the swallowed state, are no longer its own but the whole world (சராசரம்). மனம் ஆதிகள் ஐந்து is unusual; the inner instruments are usually counted four. The reading is a guess.

reading: The Supreme stands spread fully everywhere, strong everywhere and dense everywhere; mighty everywhere, he eats the world and spits it out; this is how I saw the gift and came to live.
nuance: உலகு உண்டு உமிழ்க்கும் (eats and spits out the world) gives dissolution and emanation as one act, the chapter's swallowing. The last line turns to the speaker's experience.

reading: Measuring and drawing in the knowledge that is in turiya, discarding the world the mind had taken in, if one reaches the risen Supreme Siva, one becomes the open space itself.
nuance: வெட்டவெளி (open space) is a term for the formless Supreme. பரஞ்சகம் உண்டது may mean 'what the world has eaten' or 'the world eaten by the mind'; the sense of discarding the world is clear.

reading: Drawing me in as heated iron draws in water, going beyond even the highest Supreme, swallowing the light of the three voids to gain strength, my Nandi stayed in my heart.
nuance: இரும்பிடை நீர் (water on hot iron) is a classic image of total absorption: the water vanishes into the iron. முப்பாழ் (the three voids) is a technical term, traditionally the voids of maya, of the soul and of the Supreme, but the verse does not say.

reading: Like the wood-apple fruit eaten by the elephant, Lord Siva swallows, so that they spin, the soul, the Supreme, the Siva spoken of before, the rare turiya and the world above, all of it.
nuance: கரியுண் விளவின் கனி is the wood-apple that keeps its shell while its inside is gone, said to happen when an elephant swallows it whole or when a blight called கரி strikes it. Sengalvaraya notes the image in Civaka Cintamani 1122 and Tiruppugazh 57. The point is that all remains in outward form while its substance is taken into Siva. திரிய (whirling) is unclear.

reading: The highest of the high, who is end and beginning, the supreme beyond the supreme in himself, with the Supreme, swallowed us, and Nandi stayed at the end of what is known in true knowledge; we do not know it.
nuance: நேயாந்தம் is taken as jneya-anta, the end of the knowable. நாம் அறியோமே (we do not know) may mean that the swallowed self no longer knows as a separate knower, or simply that the state is beyond knowing.

title: வாய்மை
theme: Truth (வாய்மை), taken as the true as against the false in the whole person: the Lord mingles with those who are mingled with truth and does not enter before the false; knowledge without the all-knowing is no gain; those who leave falsehood and the bewildering senses and follow the one who cut away confusion reach the Siva-state.
structure_note: 2600, 2601 and 2604 repeat one formula (மெய்கலந்தாரொடு மெய்கலந்தான், பொய்கலந்தார் முன் புகுதா) with variations; around them are verses on grace, on knowledge, and on cutting the senses' hold (2603, 2607, 2608).
source_issues: 2609: lines 2 and 3 (கினமெனக் கூறு மிருங்காய மேவற் றனிவினி னாதன்பால்) are obscure and possibly corrupt.
2605: கத்தாள் in line 4 is unclear and may be corrupt for கைத்தாள்.
2604: line 4 lacks the closing full stop the other verses have; no change in sense.

reading: Put plainly, the teachings of grace are like gold refined of its flaw in fire: if one holds to them until all is cut away, without the least loss of fineness, one becomes a bright flame with enmity cut off.
nuance: மாற்று is the fineness of gold as tested on the touchstone, so இறை மாற்று அற is read as 'without the slightest loss of fineness'; it might instead mean 'with the Lord's change' or 'with no exchange'. அற்றது உரைக்கில் may mean 'if one speaks of what is detached'.

reading: Leaving aside the knowledge that knows everything, even knowing everything there is no gain; if I say that the knowledge that knows everything is 'I', it can be called the all-knowing Lord.
nuance: எல்லாம் opens every line. Lines 1 and 2 are clear: all knowledge apart from the all-knowing is fruitless. Lines 3 and 4 may say that one who takes that knowledge as oneself is one with the Lord, or warn against claiming it; I read the first, in keeping with the neighbouring chapters on 'that you are'.

reading: Doing tapas on the high mountain, I too passed beyond the base, wretched cycle of birth and found the form known to the goddess, the thief who stands in the kalas.
nuance: முலைநின்ற மாது is taken as Uma, and கலைநின்ற கள்வன் (the thief who stands in the kalas) as Siva, hidden in the phases of the moon or of the breath, or in the arts. கள்வன் for the Lord who steals the heart is an old devotional usage.

reading: He alone is fit to be called lord in the world; he alone stands as the principle of the world; as the sky pours rain, the great Veda abounds; and the heart whose flesh has melted becomes one with him.
nuance: Line 3 is compressed: வானே மழைபொழி மாமறை கூர்ந்திடும் may compare the Lord's gift of the Veda to rain, or name him as sky, rain and Veda. ஊனே உருகிய உள்ளம் (a heart melted to the flesh) is the language of devotional love.

reading: What is the cause of their gaining grace? It is that, with minds free of darkness, they seek the Lord, change their deluded minds, and praise the red feet that hold the rare substance.
nuance: The verse answers its own question. அமரில் in line 1 is unclear: it may mean 'in desire', 'among the gods' or 'in the struggle'.

reading: The one who mingles in truth with those who mingle in truth and does not enter before those mingled with falsehood stands as the saving Lord of the ages, and for the true, joy grows from mingling in truth.
nuance: மெய் means truth and also the body, so மெய்கலந்தார் can be those joined in truth or those in whom the Lord has entered bodily; the chapter title favours truth. The Lord's presence follows the person's truthfulness: he goes in where there is truth and not where there is falsehood.

reading: The pure one who mingles in truth with those who mingle in truth and does not go in among those mingled with falsehood: only those who have joined hands with him can fix that Lord in their thought when the breath rises to leave.
nuance: ஆவி எழும்பொழுது (when the breath rises) is taken as the moment of death, when only those already joined to the Lord can hold him in mind. கைகலந்தார் (those who joined hands) may also mean those who joined him in worship with folded hands.

reading: If, when the time comes, one performs Siva's truth at both times of day, it stands as the higher rule; if one gives up falsehood and the senses as refuge, the Lord himself becomes that way.
nuance: இருபொழுதும் (both times) is taken as morning and evening worship. மெய்செயின் may be 'do truth' or 'do Siva's worship with the body'; புகல் ஒன்று நீத்திடில் is read as giving up the refuge one takes in falsehood and the senses.

reading: What comes and what fails to come: this is grace; the excellent, glorious Nandi gave grace so that one may be saved; if one masters the nine paths of the lying senses, one can mount the horse called truth.
nuance: நெறி ஒன்பது (nine paths) may be the nine openings of the body; புரவி (horse) is the vehicle of ascent. மெய் என் புரவி may mean 'the horse called truth' or 'the horse called the body'; both suit Tirumular.

reading: The one who joined hands with me, Nandi in my thought, the one who mingled in truth, the first of the Veda, the pure one who does not enter before the false, is a refuge only to those who have cast off falsehood.
nuance: The verse gathers the chapter's epithets and ends where 2600 and 2601 point: the Lord is refuge (புகலிடம்) to those who have left falsehood, not to all.

reading: No one knows how to open, with their own hand, the bolt of Nandi who dwells in the inner shrine of the true feet; if you put away the false bolt of suffering so that falsehood ends, the opening of the bolt is the rare gain.
nuance: தாள் means both foot and door-bolt, and the verse plays on both: மெய்த்தாள் (true feet, or true bolt), கைத்தாள் (hand-bolt), பொய்த்தாள் (false bolt), கத்தாள் (perhaps a corruption). The Lord is pictured behind a locked inner door that effort cannot open but the ending of falsehood can.

reading: Praise him in your awareness, in the way that saves; the true path of Hara stands firm above; in the midst of those who shine without any falsehood, the Lord sits and stands.
nuance: புறம் பொலிவார் (those who shine outward) suggests people whose outward life shows their inner truth; the Lord's seat is among them.

reading: There is a fruit of the fragrant flower; he does not let the bird that comes to it enter and eat; if you shoot an arrow and drive the bird far away, you can reach the red-gold Siva-state.
nuance: The image is symbolic and not explained. The fruit may be the bliss or nectar of yoga, and the bird the senses or the ego that would consume it; the arrow, as in 2567, the aimed mind. Who 'he' is in line 2 is unclear.

reading: Cut the bond of the five bewildering senses and follow the one who cut away confusion; when I followed, Siva our Lord, without wavering, made my mind one, saying 'go and be saved'.
nuance: ஐம்புலப் பாசம் names the senses as a பாசம், a bond in the Siddhanta sense. துயக்கறுத்தான் (the one who cut away confusion) may be the guru or Siva himself; the verse moves from the first to the second.

reading: For those who can think with the mind alone, if they do what is fitting toward the Lord in solitude, the body called a heavy burden becomes the act of the pure one, knowledge for the world.
nuance: Lines 2 and 3 (கினமெனக் கூறு மிருங்காய மேவற் றனிவினி) are obscure and the word division is uncertain; இருங்காயம் (the great body) and தனி (alone) are the clearest words. The reading is a guess.

title: ஞானி செயல்
theme: The jnani's action (ஞானி செயல்): the knowers of tattva who know themselves exhaust past karma by living it out and stop future karma from forming, by Siva's grace placed on their head; karma arises through mind, speech and body and does not last when mind and speech stand straight.
source_issues: 2610: line 3 reads தததுவ, a misprint for தத்துவ (as in 2611).

reading: When former karma arrives, the knowers of tattva who know themselves experience it first and are rid of it; later karma they watch closely so as to drive it off, because they direct the five senses toward the good.
nuance: முன்னை வினை and பின்னை வினை are taken as karma already made, which must be lived out (உண்டே நீங்குவர், 'having eaten it they are free'), and karma not yet made, which can be prevented. The verse does not say the jnani escapes former karma, only that he exhausts it.

reading: The knowers of tattva who know themselves untie the knot of former karma and seize and crush later karma, by the grace of Siva placed on their head.
nuance: The verse repeats 2610's first line and adds the cause: சென்னியில் வைத்த சிவனருள், grace placed on the head, recalling the guru placing the Lord's feet on the disciple's head. முடிச்சை அவிழ் (untie the knot) may mean that former karma loses its binding power rather than that it is not experienced.

reading: Strong karma kindles through mind, speech and body; if mind and speech stand straight, strong karma does not last; the jnani is the one fit to change himself and act, free of the latent tendencies of those whose mind and speech have gone astray.
nuance: The first two lines are clear and set mind, speech and body as the three doors of karma. The last two are compressed: மனவாக்கு கெட்டவர் may be those whose mind and speech are corrupt or those in whom mind and speech have ceased, and வாதனை (vasana, latent impressions) may be what the jnani escapes or what he works through.

title: அவா அறுத்தல்
theme: Cutting off craving (அவா அறுத்தல்): talk of yogic technique is useless while desire remains; the Lord is found not in buildings or garb but in the heart freed of longing, and desire must be cut even where it reaches toward the Lord, for desire multiplies sorrow and its loss is bliss.
structure_note: The opening verses (2613 to 2616) give the command and its reasons; 2617 sets the ocean of desire against the Lord who holds the unfailing sea; the rest (2618 to 2622) describe the purity and attainments of those freed from desire and warn those who think themselves already saved.
source_issues: 2617: துவாக்கடல் is obscure and may be corrupt.
2618: துந்தொழில் is unclear; it may be a misreading of துன்தொழில் (evil acts).

reading: There is no use sitting and babbling in all manner of ways about the breath and the needle; cut away desire and attachment, and once they are cut, the place where the Lord dwells becomes easy to reach.
nuance: வாசி is traditionally the controlled breath of yoga; ஊசி (needle) is obscure, taken as the needle-fine central channel or the needle-point of concentration. அன்பு here, paired with ஆசை, is attachment to people and things rather than the love of the Lord Tirumular praises elsewhere.

reading: He is not in the mansion, not in the hall, not in the courtyard, not in the temple, not in the holy garb; standing within the hidden place in the heart of those who have given up longing, he granted release.
nuance: The list sweeps away both secular and sacred buildings and the ascetic's garb (வேடம்). மூடத்துள்ளே is unusual: மூடம் can mean dullness or a covered place, and is usually taken as the hidden inner space of the heart.

reading: Cut off desire, cut off desire; cut off desire even if it is for the Lord; the more desire grows, the more sorrows come, and the more desire is let go, the more it becomes bliss.
nuance: ஈசனோடாயினும் (even with the Lord) is the striking phrase. It is often taken as desire for gains or powers from the Lord, or even desire to be joined with him, which still keeps the self that wants; the verse itself doesn't narrow it.

reading: Fling away the attachment that, together with the five oppressing elements, makes the path of suffering; letting go of longing is the knowledge that stands in truth, and what it reaches is the following of one's own self.
nuance: அடுவன பூதங்கள் ஐந்தும் (the five elements that oppress) echoes Appar's அடுவன அஞ்சு பூதம், as Sengalvaraya notes. The last line, தொடுவது தம்மைத் தொடர்தலும் ஆமே, is compressed; it may mean that true knowledge turns one toward the self, or that what one clings to then follows one.

reading: The ages, like the swelling sea at full moon, have passed; the gods slept, caught in one sea, and the people of the earth sank, caught in the sea of desire; the Lord stands holding the sea that never fails.
nuance: The verse plays on four seas: உவா (the full-moon swell), துவா, அவா (desire) and தவா (unfailing). துவாக்கடல் is obscure; it may be the sea of duality or of the twofold deeds, or a corrupt word. Even the gods drown, only differently from humans.

reading: The remaining deeds, disease and long labours ceasing and becoming pure, then even the five acts being turned back and grace gained directly, pressing close and sinking in: this is the purity of the knowers.
nuance: நின்ற வினை may be the deeds still to be lived out (prarabdha). பின்றைங் கருமமும் is read as பின் ஐங்கருமமும், the five acts, perhaps the Lord's five acts or the soul's own five; பேர்த்து may mean they are reversed or set aside. துந்தொழில் is unclear.

reading: Realising and attaining truth, the bright attainment is release; when infatuation with women is destroyed, the gain is the eight powers; if the firm knower gives up the Siva-body, after he reaches bountiful grace he comes to rest.
nuance: The verse ranks attainments: the eight siddhis follow from mastering desire for women, but release follows only from truth. சிவகாயம் may be the body made Siva's through yoga, which the knower lays down; ஆறுமே may mean he is stilled or that his way is made.

reading: Seeking in love, saying 'that one is the Lord', they do not grasp the truth that Siva here within is the Lord; this one of becoming is this birth of many kinds, and this one's world goes when its falseness is seen.
nuance: The verse is built on a chain of pronouns and names: அவன், இவன், சிவன், பவன், புவன். The contrast between அவன் (that one, far off) and இவன் (this one, near) is the plainest point: people look for the Lord out there. பவன் and புவன் may be names of Siva or plays on becoming (bhava) and world (bhuvana).

reading: The way things boil and the way they cool, the way they are set across this whole earth: the world does not seek the five who ordain it, and in this fermenting body there is a single thread.
nuance: விதிக்கின்ற ஐவர் may be the five deities of the five acts or the five senses that command the body; நூல் ஒன்று may be one thread, one rule or one scripture. How the verse bears on desire is not clear from the Tamil.

reading: You say 'we are saved' yet do not see the thing to be reached; if you set Nandi, who mingles in the fragrant flower, in your thought and join him with clarity, he is the root seed even before birth.
nuance: கந்த மலர் (the fragrant flower) is traditionally the heart-lotus. முந்தைப் பிறவிக்கு மூலவித்து can mean the Lord is the primal seed prior to all birth, or that joining him reaches the root seed of births and so ends them.

title: பக்தியுடைமை
theme: Having devotion (பக்தியுடைமை): the Lord, whom the seven worlds cannot know, is known only through the devotion of his devotees; the poet takes on servitude to the servants of his servants, calls to the Lord as a calf calls, and finds that in bondage and release alike the devotee has no task of his own, for grace does all.
source_issues: 2624: line 2 reads அடினையும், probably a misprint for அடிமையும்.
2626: line 2 begins ற்த்தன், a garbled division of என்றத்தன் (என்று அத்தன்).
2628: line 4 reads பத்திப்பட் டோ ர்க்குப் with a stray space inside டோர்.
2629: line 1 ends யாகப் before குறவஞ், where the sandhi should give யாகக்; line 1 is obscure.

reading: The devotees praise as Pasupati the Father who stands as the knowledge that grants release and as what is heard, the undying Lord of the immortals, the pure one, the light that stands as the pure path.
nuance: பசுபதி (Lord of the pasus, the bound souls) names the Siddhanta relation of Pati to pasu. கேள்வி is learning by hearing, here the teaching heard from the guru or scripture.

reading: I took on the servitude of being servant to the servants of the servants of his servants; by the grace of the devotees, so that I might reach his feet, he took me as his servant, saying 'this one is my servant'.
nuance: The repeated அடியார் stacks degrees of humility, a common form in Tamil Saiva hymns. The grace that brings the poet to the Lord comes through the devotees (அடியார் அருளால்), not directly.

reading: He is cool in water and burns in fire; who can know Nandi? He is subtler than anyone one could find in the world, and he stands in the town as Uma's consort.
nuance: Line 2, ஆரிக் கடனந்தி யாமா ரறிபவர், is hard to divide; it may be ஆர் இக்கடன் (who [knows] this duty) or a question about who can know Nandi. நேரியர் may mean subtle or upright. The verse sets the Lord's pervading power beside his form with Uma.

reading: Who can say where the Father dwells, the One whom all seven worlds together cannot know? Unless one comes to share in the devotion of his devotees, who could speak of that pearl? Those who did stood first.
nuance: முத்து (pearl) is a name for the Lord. The last phrase, முந்துநின்றாரே, may mean the devotees stand ahead of all others, or that they alone came forward to speak.

reading: As a cow seeks and calls its calf, I, as a calf, sought and called my Lord; and the hidden meaning of the Vedas, who stood beyond the heavens, sought me out, came and entered into this body of flesh.
nuance: The image turns: the poet calls as a calf, but the Lord comes searching like the cow. வான்கன்றுக்கு அப்பால் and ஊன்கன்றால் are unclear; கன்று may be repeated for the wordplay, the second perhaps 'the calf in flesh', the poet.

reading: In bondage there is no task of one's own, since one is born into it; in release there is no task of one's own, by its nature; since the Father gives both through grace, those caught in devotion have nothing to do.
nuance: பெத்தம் and முத்தம் are the Siddhanta terms for the soul's bound and released states. தன்பணி (one's own work) is traditionally taken to mean that the soul is not the agent of either; whether this rules out effort or only claims of merit is not settled by the verse.

reading: Climbing the cool mountain where the hill-folk shout, with honey-laden flowers, my mind will praise none as God but Nandi, whose body bears the serpent.
nuance: Line 1, பறவையிற் கற்பமும் பாம்புமெய் யாக, is obscure: கற்பம் may be the kalpa tree, an elixir or an age, and பாம்பு மெய்யாக may mean the serpent on his body or the body as serpent in a yogic reading. The mountain may be Kailasa or a hill shrine.

reading: Make Nandi, the close companion, the Lord of the gods, your support and cut off birth and be saved; when one makes him close support and thinks on Siva's feet, he stands as one's support, as fire.
nuance: The verse runs on துணை (support, companion) four times. அங்கியாகி (as fire) may be the inner fire of yoga or the fire that burns away bonds.

reading: The Lord who destroyed the three cities of the demons who oppressed the gods: calling him the forest-dweller and the one of the dark mountain, thinking of him within the flesh, they became one with him.
nuance: The famous deed (the burning of the three cities) and the homely names (கானவன், கருவரையான்) are both ways of naming him; the union comes from thinking of him inside the body (ஊனதனுள்).

reading: My heart wavers as it seeks the Leader who first made both what endures and what perishes; in the mountain, in the sky, outside, in the forge and in the heart, I stood immersed.
nuance: தயங்கும் can mean wavers or shines. The list of places may be where the poet searched or where he finds himself immersed in the Lord; உலை (forge) is unexpected and may be the body's inner fire.

title: முத்தியுடைமை
theme: Having release (முத்தியுடைமை): those in release have the Father's full grace, purified tattvas and a devotion in which their deeds have fallen away, and know the supreme bliss; a second, obscure verse pictures the search for the heart's fruit.

reading: Those who, in release, have received the Father's full grace, reached the purification of the tattvas, and come into true devotion, in which their own service, true penance and action have left deeds behind, are knowers of the supreme bliss.
nuance: தத்துவ சுத்தி (purification of the tattvas) is a Siddhanta stage in which the soul sees the constituents of its world as not itself. The syntax of line 3 is loose; வினைவிட்ட may qualify the devotion or the people. பரானந்த போதர் may also be 'those awakened to supreme bliss'.

reading: When the strong-legged bird that sought rich fruit wanders seeking the fruit of the heart, the four who have gained the good light a lamp in their hand in the fire of the throat-fruit and search.
nuance: The verse is symbolic and its key terms can't be fixed from the Tamil. The bird may be the soul; களங்கனி may be the dark kala fruit or the 'fruit in the throat', a yogic centre; நால்வர் may be the followers of the four paths or four sages. I give only the surface.

title: சோதனை
theme: The test (சோதனை): the seeker's search is completed when, having bathed in the ocean of grace and left all maya, he simply stays still; the Lord pervades all as ghee in milk, takes the heart as his temple, tests and leads the seeker, and gives him the sword of knowledge with which nothing can turn him aside.
structure_note: The chapter moves from the stillness that is the test (2635 to 2638), through the Lord's pervading and indwelling presence (2639 to 2642), to his testing and leading (2643, 2644) and the sword of knowledge given by him (2645 to 2648).
source_issues: 2640: line 1 reads விகிர்த்னை, a misprint for விகிர்தனை.
2645: line 2 reads அறிவது னோடேயவ், probably அறிவதனோடே அவ் with a dropped or misplaced syllable.
2646: line 1 reads வாள்ங்கைக்கொண்டபின், a misprint for வாளங்கைக் கொண்டபின்.

reading: Our Lord, great Nandi, danced in the great bliss beyond speech, and we bathed in the ocean of grace; leaving every maya and hiding ourselves away, to stay simply still is the test.
nuance: சோதனை can mean testing or searching, and some take it with சோதி (light). சும்மா இருத்தல் (simply being still) is a phrase of Tamil mystical tradition for the end of striving. அம்மா may be an exclamation or address the Mother.

reading: I will join with the one who has all knowledge, who dwells close within the rare great Veda, the god of the gods, who holds the senses and has the mark beyond the five senses.
nuance: பொறியுடையான் may mean master of the sense organs or the one with the spark or mark; குறி (mark, sign) beyond the senses may be his formless sign or a yogic object of meditation.

reading: The world cries 'knowledge, knowledge', yet no one knows what knowledge and ignorance are; when knowledge goes beyond both knowledge and ignorance, how fine knowledge and ignorance then become!
nuance: The verse plays on அறிவு and அறியாமை six times. The last line may be admiring (once both are transcended they are seen rightly) or ironic (how strange that is); the tone isn't fixed.

reading: In the sign that is no sign, in the union that does not join, in the knowledge that does not know, loosened into a single mind, the path is supreme Nandi; his long grace is one; that close union which is no union may be called Sivam.
nuance: The verse defines its goal only by negations (குறியாக் குறி, கூடாத கூட்டம், அறியா அறிவு, செறியாச் செறிவு). ஏகசித்தம் is the one-pointed or single mind. சிவமெனலாம் (may be called Sivam) is guarded: a name, not a description.

reading: Like what moves in the wind, jaggery in the sugarcane, ghee in milk, juice in fruit and fragrance in the flower, so is our Lord; the guardian stands mingled everywhere.
nuance: Each image is of something present throughout a thing but not visible in it. காலினில் ஊரும் is unclear: it may be scent carried on the wind, or the wind itself. Sengalvaraya notes Appar's பாலின் நெய்யாம் பழத்தின் இரதமாம் as a parallel.

reading: Like a golden creeper that, joined with longing and seeking the Transcendent, reaches up a mountain, our Lord dwells in the mind, appearing as a form of fire.
nuance: The creeper may be the devoted soul climbing toward the Lord, or Uma, the mountain's daughter, reaching Siva; the verse's subject shifts from the creeper to the Lord. விருப்பொடு கூடி (joined with longing) treats longing for the Lord as good.

reading: Lord Nandi came in the space at the centre and took my inner self as his temple; as he did so I rose up saying 'my Father has come', and as I rose, Siva was within my thought.
nuance: நடுவுள் வியோமம் (the space at the centre) is traditionally the space of the heart or the space between the brows; the verse doesn't say which. அகம்படி may be the inner self or the inner precinct of a temple, kept as a pun.

reading: Without meanness or falsehood, seek the pure one, master of his nature, the good within penance, the one able in goodness, Nandi who dwells at the centre; he will shape you in many ways.
nuance: பரிசுசெய்வான் may mean he will fit you, form you or reward you; பன்மையில் (in manyness) may be 'in many ways' or 'out of the many', marking the seeker out.

reading: When he tested me he stood close behind me, and yet the Lord did not stand following there; spreading through all, the First, the Supreme beyond the supreme, my Father, stands beyond and shows that path.
nuance: The first two lines seem to say opposite things (he followed me; he did not follow), which may contrast the Lord as near guide and as transcendent, or the guru and the Lord. சோதிக்கும் (tests) gives the chapter its title.

reading: The thing rare even for the gods, who shows that path, is on this path like father, mother and kin; he sets those on the right path in Siva's world; this way is the nature of Nandi.
nuance: சிவலோகம் (Siva's world) is the first of the graded states of release (salokam) in Siddhanta, though the verse may use it loosely for release. செவ்வழி (the straight or right path) can be read either with the seekers or with Siva's world.

reading: Drawing and striking with the sword of the ford of knowledge, knowing that noble one by it and joining the Lord of the gods of gods, is what those who do not give up attachment to the many hosts have torn from them.
nuance: The first three lines describe the work of knowledge; the last line, பறிவது பல்கணப் பற்றுவிடாரே, is hard to join to them: it may say that those who do not let go of the many (senses, people, or goblin hosts) lose all this, or that what is cut away is that attachment. துறை may be ford, path or field.

reading: Once I took in hand the sword the First Lord gave, no one can pierce me or turn me aside; I will test there so that no trace is left; the God of the beginning has become this one.
nuance: The sword is traditionally knowledge given by the Lord or guru; Sengalvaraya compares Arunagirinathar's sword of knowledge-flame in Kandar Alankaram. அவன் இவன் ஆமே may mean the Lord has become the speaker, or simply that this is the primal god. வேதித்து may mean piercing or transforming.

reading: Wasting away that embryo and the formless, the bond of making deeds, fearful servitude and the many births, and setting the mind right: for the skilled who meet that test, it becomes the Supreme itself.
nuance: அந்தக் கருவை யருவை may be 'that embryo, the formless' or a play on கரு and அரு (form and formless). பணியச்சம் may be servitude and fear, or fear that makes one bow. தற்பரம் is the Supreme in itself.

reading: He told me the one thing beyond telling; cutting off the craving for the arts that rose without bound, keeping my wave-like body from leaving me and setting it right, the Supreme entered into me, now flawless.
nuance: கலைவேட்டு may be craving for learning and the arts, or for the kalas, the phases of the yogic breath. திரையொத்த உடல் (body like a wave, or wrinkled) is kept, not discarded: the Lord enters the embodied person.

title: குருமட தரிசனம்
theme: Seeing the guru's matha (குருமட தரிசனம்): those who see the guru's seat, where all offerings are understood as the Lord's, reach his feet; and the matha is turned inward, so that the Lord's only house is the person, and the seat, mountain, cave and forest of the yogi are found in the body's centres and the inward-turned face.
structure_note: 2649 to 2651 speak of the matha and the Lord's dwelling; 2652 announces a teaching on the seat, mountain, cave, centres and forest, which 2653 and 2654 give as inner correspondences; 2655 ends with the silent knowers who see the supreme light in their own form.

reading: Those who have seen the guru's matha, where people gather knowing that the offerings, the oblations, the spreading smoke and the sounds are all for the Lord, went on and stood joined to his feet, tender as young leaves and flowers.
nuance: பலி, அவி, புகை and ஒலி are the offerings, oblations, incense and chanting of ritual worship; the matha is valued because there they are known to be the Lord's. குவியும் may be the gathering of people or the folding of hands and minds.

reading: Apart from this one's house he has no house there; if one asks whether he has some other house, they know again and again that this one's house is his, and yet they wail that he is outside.
nuance: அவன் is the Lord and இவன் the person; இல்லம் (house) is usually read as the body or the heart. Line 2 can also be a statement: if one knows, he has no other house.

reading: After I found the great ford that all seek, Siva's red feet, like freshly picked flowers, come to me; our Lord, hard to search out, who has no special mark, stands as the life of the moving world.
nuance: பெருந்துறை (the great ford) may be the shrine of Tirupperunturai or a figure for the place of crossing, the guru or his matha; the verse doesn't settle it. சிறப்பிலி may mean the one without distinguishing marks or without equal.

reading: I will tell of the seat and the mountain, of the cave of the mind and the place, of the centres and the forest, to the people of the twelve great lands.
nuance: The places a yogi might seek outside (seat, mountain, cave, forest) are matched with inner ones (சித்தக் குகை, ஆதாரம்). ஈராறு இருநிலத்தோர் may be the people of the twelve lands, the wide earth, or those at the twelfth centre above the head; it can't be fixed.

reading: The face is the seat, the great matha and the land one seeks; the inner self is the supreme order and the faultless vision; the inner self is the supreme seat and the sixty-four rites; Chidambaram, the cave of the self, is the centre itself.
nuance: Each outward thing of a matha (its seat, building, land, rites) is set equal to something in the person. எண்எண் கிரியை may be sixty-four rites or eight-and-eight. சிதம்பரம் is both the shrine and, by its meaning 'space of consciousness', the inner space; தற்குகை is the cave of the self.

reading: For the knowing who have examined the inward face, the inward face is the seat and the centre; the world-ward face is Shakti's seat; and the face toward the world, the deity, is Siva.
nuance: The verse plays on அகமுகம் (face turned inward), சகமுகம் and செகமுகம் (both read as face turned to the world, from ஜகம்); the difference between the second and third is unclear and one may be a variant. The general sense is that the inward turn is the true seat.

reading: When the two mayas veil and are themselves veiled, and the five bodies pass away and one becomes oneself, and the pure supreme flame appears, those who search within their own form are the silent ones who begin from knowledge.
nuance: மாயை இரண்டும் are traditionally pure and impure maya; காயம் ஓர் ஐந்தும் may be the five sheaths or the five bodies of Siddhanta. ஞானாதி மோனத்தர் may be 'silent ones with knowledge first' or 'silent ones of knowledge and the rest'.

title: ஞானகுரு தரிசனம்
theme: Seeing the guru of knowledge (ஞானகுரு தரிசனம்): the guru's state lies beyond the tattvas and the turiyas and cannot be spoken, yet to fix the mind on his form clears the three malams, as the thought of Garuda clears poison. Nandi as guru takes the seeker's head, mouth, eyes and mind, enters the heart, cuts the bonds and makes even the smallest great, until the disciple no longer bows to gods but becomes what others bow to.
structure_note: The guru's state beyond tattvas and turiyas (2656, 2657, 2661); what seeing him does (2658 to 2660, 2665); where and how he is found within (2662 to 2664, 2666 to 2671); the Lord's rule and grace in the world (2672, 2673); and Tirumular's own transformation (2674). The grouping is mine.
source_issues: 2657: line 1 is identical to 2940 line 1, and line 3 is close to 2940 line 3; one of the two may be a borrowing or a repeat.
2663 and 2664 are obscure throughout and may be corrupt; 2669 நகழ்வு is an unusual word.

reading: When the thirty-six subside there, the supreme guru grants what is to be worshipped, gives Siva's state above all else, and bliss swells and is kept as the gain.
nuance: ஆறொடு முப்பதும் (six with thirty) is taken as the thirty-six tattvas. கும்பிடு தந்திடும் is unclear: the guru may give the act of worship, or give himself as the one to be worshipped.

reading: The light that shines beyond the three turiyas, rare Parasiva, having become all things, in the ground left where expanding and contracting have ceased: the great guru's state cannot be spoken.
nuance: துரியங்கள் மூன்றும் (the three turiyas) is traditionally the turiya of the soul, of the Shakti and of Siva, but the verse does not say. விரிவு குவிவு (expanding and contracting) may be the outward and inward movement of the mind or of the world.

reading: I received my head for the feet of Nandi, my mouth to praise him, my eyes to see him, and my mind for him.
nuance: Each line gives a part of the body its use. The epithets ஆயன, வாயன, காயன, சேயன rhyme and are hard to fix: perhaps 'who has become', 'who is in speech', 'who has a body' (the guru in visible form) and 'who is far'. The point is that the faculties were given for him.

reading: As the heavy poison clears and fear ends as soon as one thinks of Garuda's form, so the moment one fixes on the guru's form the three malams clear and he becomes Siva.
nuance: The image is of the snake-bite cure in which Garuda, the snakes' enemy, is held in mind. சிவன் அவன் ஆமே can mean the disciple becomes Siva, or that the guru is Siva; both readings are made.

reading: No one knows where the Lord dwells; for those who search out his dwelling he settles within, never perishing, and if one sees the Lord, he becomes this one.
nuance: அண்ணல் opens all four lines. அவன் இவன் ஆமே (he becomes this one) is the same turn as the close of 2659: the seer and the seen become one, which can be read either way round.

reading: Knowing as things appear, appearing and not appearing, deluded knowledge, and the waking and the other states: these three go, and when the three turiyas end, Nandi stands fixed in the high silence.
nuance: Which three are meant by மூன்றவை is unclear: the three kinds of knowing in lines 1 and 2, or waking, dream and sleep. மறி நனவாதிகள் may be the waking and the rest turned back. மோனம் here is the silent state of the guru.

reading: In the land of the moon, between one's brows, in a fragrant flower, is the maiden of two petals, crystal-formed and free of bond; she is the hold of the supreme guru who cut the bonds.
nuance: The two-petalled flower between the brows is traditionally the ajna centre, and the maiden there is taken as Shakti. சந்திர பூமி (the land of the moon) is a yogic term I can't fix. பற்று may mean that she is what the guru holds, or the refuge he gives.

reading: He entered the mind so the seven worlds rejoiced, entered the earth bearing up the long sky, entered into wrath so the eight directions shook, and entered the forest: this is what is meant by 'his town is to the north'.
nuance: The verse is obscure. The wrath may allude to Siva's angry deeds, the forest to the ascetic's retreat, and the northern town to Kailasa, or in a yogic reading to the crown of the head. Who 'he' is (the Lord or the guru) is not said.

reading: The colours and the sheaths that are oneself draw near, bird and forest are fit to be called oneself, and if one stands in the sixteen-fold path, the ten parts that seemed oneself become something other.
nuance: கோசம் is taken as the five sheaths of the self, சோடச மார்க்கம் as the path through sixteen kalas, and தசாங்கம் as ten parts or limbs. The bird and forest may be the soul in the body. I can't fix the argument; the verse seems to say that what one took for oneself is seen as other on the path.

reading: Our great Nandi, who joins and knows no parting, stays and melts one within when his form is thought of; for those who can see the heart hidden in its source, hard karma swoons away here, within those who dissolve.
