nuance: கருவில் கரந்து may mean hidden in the source, or hidden in the womb, that is, in the body. அழிவார் அகத்தே is unclear: 'within those who are undone' or 'they perish within'.

reading: One can reach our Lord of the tattvas: cutting and cutting the many bonds, seeking to stand firm and contemplating him beyond thought, one reaches him, and he himself is dharma.
nuance: தத்துவன் is the Lord as the real, or as master of the tattvas. நினைப்பற உள்கில் (if one contemplates with thought gone) holds a paradox the chapter returns to. The last line may also mean that reaching him is itself dharma.

reading: He thinks of those who think of him, he of the light of the flower that grows in the spring; even those as small as a split millet seed, if they reach him with a weighty mind, become high.
nuance: The flower in the spring (சுனை) is commonly taken as the heart lotus. கனத்த மனம் may be a full, firm or devoted mind. The verse sets the measure of greatness in the mind's turning to him, not in one's station.

reading: At the time of reaching him, if one sets aside the tattvas, take that too as the rule of attaining; those who think of the first Lord who stands as all the worlds will seek and find devotion.
nuance: மேவை விதி is obscure, perhaps 'the rule for reaching'. பத்தி may be devotion, or, less likely, order. The verse seems to make letting go of the tattvas part of the method, not its failure.

reading: Contemplating the Lord they ceased to waver; joined with our Lord they ceased from what happens; within their own minds they ceased from display; and he entered and stayed, showing the way of glory.
nuance: The three ceasings are built on நகழ்வு, நிகழ்வு and திகழ்வு. நகழ்வு is an unusual word, taken here as wavering; திகழ்வு may be shining or display. The plain sense is a growing stillness ended by the Lord's entry.

reading: Like a line of emerald and ruby that appears, the true path of the true guru of the great word joins; this line, at the root of the forehead, becomes the light within the beautiful light.
nuance: இலாடம் is the forehead, and the line of green and red there is taken as a light seen between the brows in meditation, perhaps the meeting of Shakti and Siva. சந்திடு (joins) may describe the colours meeting or the disciple joining the path.

reading: The yogic god dwells as the mouth that eats, the body, the life and the eye; he is earth, water, fire, air and sky, and the form of those who have become the open expanse is beyond even the sky.
nuance: யோகக் கடவுள் may be Siva as yogi or the realised guru. The last line, வெளியானோர் மேனி, seems to say that the body of those who have become the void is no longer bound to the elements; the syntax is loose.

reading: Proclaiming him Pasupati, Parasiva's command runs through the whole earth by its half; having made the great seat, he made the earth too a fitting seat for the devotees who come after.
nuance: The verse plays on பதி as Lord and as dwelling place. பாதியால் (by the half) may refer to Shakti as Siva's half, through whom his command works. பின்னாம் அடியார் may be later devotees or those who follow.

reading: Of the Lord of space, the wide earth and its long groves, they say: we know nothing but that they are his; the gods in heaven and the asuras did not see him, but those who received our Lord's grace remained in it.
nuance: Line 2 is compressed: தம்பரம் அல்லது may be 'other than his supremacy' or 'other than his own'. The contrast between the gods who did not see and the graced who did is a common Saiva turn.

reading: Taking the loincloth so that kings would bow, and then by Nandi's grace so that tongues would bow too, we will bow to gods no more: our mind is clear, and we have become what others go to worship.
nuance: The verse puns: கோ வணங்கும் (kings bow) and கோவணம் (the loincloth), நா வணங்கும் (tongues bow), தே வணங்கோம் (we will not bow to gods). Whether the loincloth is Nandi's or the speaker's own renunciant garb is not said. The boast that the graced become an object of worship is strong and is offered as the fruit of the guru's grace.

title: பிரணவ சமாதி
theme: The samadhi of the pranava (பிரணவ சமாதி): Om, gross and subtle, holds within it the one word, form and the formless and all distinctions; the elements, the moving and unmoving and the souls arise from it, and it is the form of both soul and Parasiva. Those on the true path pass beyond its measures and rest at the end of knowing and the known.
structure_note: The gross and higher pranava (2675); what is within Om (2676, 2677); its body and supports (2678); and the teaching and goal of the sanmargis (2679, 2680).
source_issues: 2675 line 2 reads மேலைப் சொரூபப்பெண், a sandhi error, probably for மேலைச் சொரூபப்பெண்.
2678 (வருக்கம், அருக்கம்) and 2679 line 1 are obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: The gross pranava is the great word of the bliss of one's own form; the subtle that sustains it is the woman of the higher form; the seal she bore is its cause there; and the higher pranava is the street of Vedanta.
nuance: தூல (gross), சூக்கும (subtle) and மேலை (higher) pranava are grades of Om in mantra theory. The woman (பெண்) is taken as Shakti and சூலித்த முத்திரை (the seal she conceived) is obscure. The verse ends by placing the highest Om on the road of Vedanta.

reading: Within the omkara called Om is the one word; within it are form and the formless; within it are many distinctions; and the omkara called Om is bright release and attainment.
nuance: ஓம்எனும் ஓங்காரம் opens every line. ஒருமொழி (the one word) may be Om itself as the single source of speech, or the great saying of identity. உருஅரு (form and the formless) is a standard pair for the manifest and unmanifest Lord.

reading: The five elements arose within omkara, the moving and unmoving arose within it, beyond omkara the three kinds of souls came to be, and omkara is the form of both soul and Parasiva.
nuance: உயிர் மூன்று is traditionally the three classes of souls by their malams (vijnanakala, pralayakala, sakala). ஓங்காரா தீதத்து (beyond omkara) sits oddly between lines that place everything within it; it may mean the souls stand at Om's further edge.

reading: The classes of letters become bliss and Brahman, the sun becomes the moving and unmoving in the world, and all the supports reasoned out are his body: so those who gathered and grasped knowledge without lack have known.
nuance: வருக்கம் (class of letters) and அருக்கம் (the sun, or the small) are obscure here, and சுகமாம் may be 'is bliss' or a name. I take the verse as listing what Om becomes; the reading is tentative.

reading: The mountain-like confusions born of the mind, the steady vision that is the way of the lamp, the holy place, lineage and austerity made one's own, and the good: all this is the teaching of the true path.
nuance: மனோபவம் (mind-born) can also be a name of Kama, and மலையும் may be 'mountain' or 'that confuse'. தீப நெறி (the way of the lamp) may be the inner light of meditation. The list is loosely joined, and whether the confusions are to be taught or removed is not said.

reading: For the sanmargis, who speak of the sixteen-fold path, passing beyond the end of the twelve that moves, the end joined in the fourteen, and the bow, they climb and abide at the end of knowledge and the known.
nuance: ஈராறு (twelve) and ஈரேழ் (fourteen) are numbered stages, perhaps kalas of the moon and sun or finger-breadths of breath; கோதண்டம் (the bow) is traditionally the brow region in the yogic body. ஞானஞேயாந்தம் is the end where knowledge and its object no longer differ.

title: ஒளி
theme: Light (ஒளி): the Lord is light, the source of the light of sun, moon and fire, which are his eyes, and of the five elements; he stays within the body and mind as an inner light that gives life and drives out the darkness of maya and bonds. To know the light is to find form and light one, and those it reaches are joined to him as fragrance to a flower.
structure_note: The verses play on ஒளி in nearly every line, often with the rhyming pair விளங்கொளி, துளங்கொளி, வளங்கொளி, களங்கொளி. Knowing the light (2681); the Lord's light in the cosmos, its lamps and elements (2682 to 2686); the light within body, soul and mind (2687 to 2691); the removal of darkness (2692 to 2696); and the Lord who alone is (2697). The grouping is mine.
source_issues: 2689: line 4 ends ஒருங்கிகின் றானே, probably a misprint for ஒருங்கிநின் றானே.
2690 line 1 (உலங்கொளி) may be a misreading of உளங்கொளி; 2692 is obscure throughout and may be corrupt.

reading: If one knows the light, there are form and light; if one knows light as form, it is form; if one knows the form of the light, it is light alone; and he stayed with one as the light itself melted.
nuance: A riddle built on ஒளி and உரு (form). It is commonly taken to say that the Lord is known first as form and light, then as light alone. ஒளியும் உருக (the light melting) may also be read as the light and the knower dissolving together.

reading: The eight worlds become easy to reach, the wide light spreads so that darkness leaves without trace, and making the light of day in that lotus, our Lord stayed there shining with a light that outdoes all.
nuance: அத்தாமரை (that lotus) is commonly taken as the heart lotus, so the light of the worlds is also the light within. இகல் ஒளி is a light that rivals or surpasses.

reading: Fire with its bright light, the sun of spreading rays and the moon received their wavering light by the grace of that light; the rich light they received is the great light, which is other, and making light in the throat he stayed mingled with them.
nuance: விரிகதிர் சோமன் may be 'the sun with spreading rays and the moon' or only 'the moon of spreading rays'. களங்கொளி may be the light of Siva's dark throat or simply 'light in its place'. The verse distinguishes the great light from the lights it lends.

reading: Isan of young light has no birth at all; the wavering-lit sun and moon are his eyes, the rich-lit fire is the other eye in his forehead, and this is the true body that makes light shine.
nuance: Sun, moon and fire as Siva's three eyes is standard Saiva iconography. மெய்காயம் (the true body) may be the Lord's body of light, or the yogi's body in which sun, moon and fire are the breaths and the inner fire.

reading: Light above, and below it the wind that dwells there; fire of milky light; space spread out as light; water making light; in the one long sky the five lights above become one light.
nuance: The five are the elements, each called a light, gathered into one; earth is not named unless மேல் ஒளி (light above) stands for it. The order and grouping are unclear.

reading: The flashing pure light, the excellent red light, knowledge spoken of spreading as the supreme light, the six lights joined: by pure words said daily, the light matches the way one has contemplated it.
nuance: The six lights (ஆறு ஒளி) may be the lights of the six adharas or the colours named in the verse; they are not listed. தூய்மொழி (pure word) is taken as mantra. The last line says the light answers to meditation.

reading: The shining light, hiding itself as the light of lightning, the wavering light, always speaks of Isan; the light in the heart, standing in the flesh, gives life, and as that rich light he pervades everything.
nuance: The rhyming light-words make the syntax loose: whether விளங்கொளி, துளங்கொளி and வளங்கொளி are three lights or one under three names is not clear. The verse places the life-giving light inside the body.

reading: That shining light and that darkness both abide in him; he is the wavering light and the light even of those who worship; to take as nectar the poison that came from the salt sea is the intent of Isan with the shining throat.
nuance: The last two lines recall Siva swallowing the poison from the churned sea, which stayed in his throat. அளங்கொளி ஆரமுதாக நஞ்சு ஆரும் can be read in several ways; I take அளம் as the salt sea. That light and darkness both abide in him is said, not explained.

reading: Whatever light moves is the light of Isan; what is like a shining light is the abiding Shakti of grace; three shining lights appear as spreading flames, and within the heart's light he gathers into one.
nuance: The three lights are taken as sun, moon and fire, as in 2684. தூங்கருட் சத்தி may be the grace-Shakti who abides or who hangs over all. The last word ஒருங்கிகின்றானே looks corrupt (see source_issues).

reading: The light within me is the soul that stands there; the great gem's flame that stood as rich light, flashing as shining light and subsiding into the sky, he stood as rich light in the gathering.
nuance: உலங்கொளி is unclear: perhaps உளங்கொளி, the heart's light, as in 2689. மாமணிச் சோதி (the great gem's flame) is the Lord. ஆயத்துள் (in the gathering, or in what has come to be) is unclear.

reading: The strange one who stands as shining light dwells where the hanging darkness does not reach within the wavering light and its bonds; as the brow-eyed one dances the dance of darkness, he stands as one with the shining light in the inner mind.
nuance: விகிர்தன் (the strange or different one) and கண்ணுதல் (forehead-eyed) are names of Siva. களங்கிருள் நட்டம் may be the dance in the dark of dissolution. The syntax of line 2 is loose.

reading: In the message carried to her of the flowered dark tresses, the primal supreme with the Lord of the immortals, the light and the pure light beyond the cosmic egg: this is how, rightly, the good darkness was removed.
nuance: The verse is very obscure. போனவர் தூது (the message of the one who went) and பரத்தை might recall a story of the Lord going as a messenger to a woman, but that would be a guess and I do not adopt it. நல்லிருள் (good darkness) is a puzzling phrase.

reading: Saying 'it is' and 'it is not' is the way of this world; is there a supreme goal of which it is said 'it was not before'? People have not seen it; if they come to the meaning seen, there is no gap, and within it is the lamp's light.
nuance: The verse sets the world's arguments of existence and non-existence against an inner seeing that leaves no gap. விண்டு இல்லை may be 'no split' or 'not spoken'. Who has 'seen the meaning' (கண்ட கருத்து) is not said: perhaps the sages.

reading: The bright light that rose to touch the flame is there, Isan, the sun of a vision that spreads; if the dense darkness of maya is cast off, it comes by the renunciation of the world that clings to the body.
nuance: The last line can also be read as 'it becomes the renunciant's, in this embodied world'. The sun here is an image of the Lord's light dispelling maya's darkness.

reading: The first Lord, with a holy body of shining coral and white ash, gracious coral and fine gold, of coral joy: the black darkness gone, Isan stood with me in coral light.
nuance: பவளம் (coral, red) recurs in every line for Siva's red body under white ash. The verse ends in the first person: the light stands with the speaker.

reading: Isan stood, the gods stood, and with no ground to stand on they are bewildered and wear away; when the bonds become one and old karma's hold ends, it is like a flower and its single fragrance.
nuance: பாசம் ஒன்றாக (the bonds becoming one) is unclear: perhaps the bonds gathering into one and falling away together. The flower and its single scent is an image of the soul and the Lord inseparable.

reading: He alone is, the chief among them; approach him as the one who alone is; he is like the sky, and in this vast dark world, praising him is possible as he stands as light.
nuance: பானாய் may be 'as light' (from பா, light, or பானு, the sun) or 'as a vessel'. மாயிரு ஞாலம் may be the great dark world or simply the great wide world.

title: தூல பஞ்சாக்கரம்
theme: The gross five letters (தூல பஞ்சாக்கரம்): the fifty letters that make all the Vedas and Agamas resolve into the five letters of Nandi's name, which are placed in the body and recited aloud. Said with the mouth and held in the heart, they make nectar well up, show the way of grace past rebirth, and protect the soul at death; those who ignore them whirl like splashing water.
structure_note: The letters and their reduction to five (2698 to 2700); the five set in the body (2701); their power at death and in rebirth (2702, 2705 to 2707); reciting them aloud (2703, 2704); and those who do not know their greatness (2708).
source_issues: 2698 nearly repeats 965; the last line differs (965: ஐம்பது எழுத்தும்போய் அஞ்செழுத் தாமே), which slightly changes the sense from becoming to being.
2701 lines 2 and 3 (அவ்வாய், தூயதோர் துண்டம்) and 2708 line 2 (இராமாற்றம்) are obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: The fifty letters are all the Vedas, the fifty letters are all the Agamas, and once one knows the order of the fifty letters, the fifty letters are the five letters.
nuance: ஐம்பது எழுத்து is the full alphabet of mantra theory (fifty or fifty-one letters). அடைவு (order, arrangement) suggests the letters set out in a diagram, as in the earlier chakra chapters. The claim is that all scripture reduces to the five letters.

reading: Beginning with A it becomes fifty-one, rising from U, ending in M and dying away again and again as it climbs; Nandi's name begins with Na.
nuance: A, U and M are the parts of Om, and the verse seems to trace speech from A through Om to its dying away, then to the five letters beginning with ந (நமசிவாய). மாய்ந்துமாய்ந்து ஏறி may describe the sound fading as it rises in the body.

reading: Para joined with the sixteen from A; Isan, the inner light, with his Shakti from U; Siva from Si, the Veda and the triangle; and from Na the root mantra is reached.
nuance: ஈரெண் (the sixteen) are taken as the sixteen vowels from அ. கோணம் (angle, triangle) may be a diagram in which the letters are set. மூலமந்திரம் (root mantra) is taken as the five letters beginning with ந. The correspondences are technical and I can't fix them.

reading: Mouth, throat, heart and navel, then the linga, above them that opening, a pure segment, and going to the crown of the head: these are the places, five with five, of the five letters.
nuance: The verse maps the five letters onto places in the body, some of them the adharas. இலிங்கம் here is taken as the genital centre. அவ்வாய் and தூயதோர் துண்டம் are obscure, and ஈறாம் ஐந்தோடு ஆம் may mean the five places with five more, or the five letters at the five ends.

reading: When the seven rays blaze up and the soul rises leaving its instruments, and when Death lays hand on it to change its life, it is the five letters that bring protection.
nuance: The seven rays (கிரணங்கள் ஏழும்) are unclear: perhaps the seven bodily elements burning up at death, or seven inner lights. கரணங்கள் are the instruments of the soul (mind and the rest). அரணம் is the fortress or shelter the mantra gives.

reading: At the time when sun and moon rise and are spoken of, no one knows the fitting mantra; but one can recite with the mouth and praise the holy five letters of the red-eyed one.
nuance: Sun and moon are traditionally the right and left breaths, so the first line may refer to the moments of breath rather than the sky. சேயுறு கண்ணி (she of red or distant eyes) may be Shakti, whose letters these are. The verse sets plain recitation against hidden lore.

reading: Say 'Sivaya nama' once, so that clear nectar wells up and nectar wells in the heart; those who do not wish to drink that welling flood of nectar whirl about like splashing water.
nuance: சிவாய நம is one of the orders of the five letters. The welling nectar can be read devotionally as the sweetness of the name or yogically as the amrita that flows from the head. The whirling of those who refuse is commonly taken as the round of births.

reading: For those who, standing in the qualities that are the guru's way, can cut the reckoning that is the womb's way and refuse so that the coming way dies, it is the five letters that show the way of grace.
nuance: The verse plays on வழி (way) four times: the guru's way, the womb's way, the way of coming (into birth) and the way of grace. கணக்கு (the reckoning) is the account of karma that leads to rebirth.

reading: When the soul comes, stunned by the frenzy of karma, recite Nandi's holy letters, which press close; if you dwell on what they point to, they join you to his ringing anklets, and one who knows that pointing takes the form of the king of austerity.
nuance: வெறிக்க வினைத்து is obscure: perhaps the soul dazed by karma, or coming into birth by karma. குறிப்பு (what is pointed to) is the meaning behind the letters. தவம் கோன் உரு may mean Siva's form or the form of a great ascetic.

reading: Thinking in the heart, saying 'Lord' with one's mouth, and at the time of sleep saying 'your paired feet are my refuge', one can win the grace of the Lord of the five, who dwells on the northern mountain where clouds crawl.
nuance: துஞ்சும் பொழுது may be the time of sleep or of death; in this chapter, after 2702, death is likely. அஞ்சில் இறைவன் may be the Lord in the five letters or the Lord of the five elements. The northern mountain is Kailasa.

reading: Not grasping the greatness of the five the Lord set down, will poor people go on with their empty talk? The wide earth, above and below and in every way, is wholly encircled by the serpent.
nuance: இராமாற்றம் is obscure: it may be 'talk of the night' or 'unsteady words'. The last two lines may mean that the earth is bound by the serpent (Adisesha), or by the serpent of bondage; how they answer the first two is unclear.

title: சூக்கும பஞ்சாக்கரம்
theme: The subtle five-letter mantra: the letters stand for Siva, his Shakti or grace, the soul, concealment and impurity, and chanting சிவாய, with நம (taken as the bonds) dropped, or simply சிவசிவ, removes the bonds and karma, turns the body to gold, and ends birth in becoming Siva.
structure_note: Two verses on the letters as a body of grace (2709, 2710), three on the five letters as the categories and the dropping of நம (2711 to 2713), one on the letters ending karma (2714), two on the repetition சிவசிவ (2715, 2716) and a close on fixing the name in mind and tongue to end birth (2717).
source_issues: 2714: line 4 reads தீர்fப்பதும் with a stray Latin 'f'; read தீர்ப்பதும்.
2717: நவம் may be a corruption of நம; the reading changes with it.
2711: நிரோதம் may be a variant of திரோதம் (concealment) rather than a deliberate contrast.

reading: For those whose minds melt as they contemplate the Lord as light and who clearly recite சிவாயநம, the mantra works as an alchemist's pill and he turns their bodily cage to gold.
nuance: குளிகை is the alchemist's pill that turns base metal to gold, and கூடு (the cage, the nest) is the body; the image may mean a body made immortal or simply made holy. Line 1 (எளிய வாதுசெய்வார்) is hard to place: it may set those who argue lightly about the Lord against those who melt, or say the Lord is easy for those who melt.

reading: Siva, Shakti, the soul, the choking impurity and maya: when the five bonds that bring ruin depart and the soul joins Siva with his Shakti, those bonds can no longer come near.
nuance: The verse does not name the letters, but the five it lists are traditionally the meanings of the five letters (சி Siva, வா Shakti, ய the soul, ம impurity, ந concealment or maya). பாச மலம் ஐந்து may be 'the five impure bonds' or 'the bonds and impurity of the five'; the count is unclear, since only the last two are bonds.

reading: Siva's holy name is his grace, and holds Siva, grace, the soul, concealment and impurity with maya; when Siva stands first and the rest are stilled, birth departs and the soul becomes the supreme Siva.
nuance: திரோதம் is concealment, the Lord's veiling power, and நிரோதம் restraint or cessation; the verse seems to play the two against each other. The reading of the five as the letters of the name is the tradition's; சிவன் முதலாக (with Siva first) may refer to the order beginning with சி.

reading: When the impurity called நம is wholly removed and that beginning left behind, by the power of the Lord's grace the faultless yoga of Siva-knowledge is attained; what one then chants is சிவாய, the truth free of impurity.
nuance: நம்மலம் is read as நம + மலம், the syllables நம taken as the bonds, so that dropping the opening syllables of நமசிவாய leaves the subtle form சிவாய. It could also be read 'our impurity'. அவ் ஆதி (that beginning) is most naturally those first syllables.

reading: Beginning with ந and with waking, concealment acts; when the soul stands as its own origin and reaches the end, samadhi and the fourth state become its own body, and then one may think of the syllables from ந, and samadhi, as becoming Siva.
nuance: Very compressed. நமாதி (from ந-ம) and நனாதி (from waking, நனவு) are set side by side, perhaps matching the letters to the states of consciousness; துரியம் is the fourth state. The syntax of lines 2 and 4 is my guess.

reading: The grace-giving mother and the father who together bore the one: when the maya within and the three impurities go and one chants சிவாய, it is those letters that end hard-to-remove karma.
nuance: ஆயம் is taken here as the mother (Shakti) beside அத்தன், the father (Siva), and ஒருவனை ஈன்றவர் as their bringing forth the soul or a son; the line may also mean the mother and father of the devotee. திரிமலம் is the three impurities.

reading: Those who do not come to clarity by saying Siva Siva are mutes; when the breath too, as Siva Siva, is understood and stilled within, those who stand in the clarity of Siva Siva find that Siva Siva becomes holy grace.
nuance: ஊமர் (the dumb) are those who have tongues but do not use them for the name. சிவசிவ வாயுவும் may mean chanting matched with the breath, a yogic practice, or the breath itself becoming the name; I can't fix which.

reading: Those of evil deeds do not say Siva Siva; when one says Siva Siva evil deeds die, one becomes divine, and the state of Siva itself follows.
nuance: The plainest verse of the chapter, built on fourfold repetition. It runs both ways: evil-doers do not say the name, and saying it ends evil deeds. தேவரும் ஆவர் is 'they become gods' or 'even the gods become (so)'.

reading: Hold the name நவம் still on the tongue and raise the name சிவம் in the mind, and birth ends; when even that touch is gone, the limit ends, and is not birth cut off?
nuance: நவம் may stand for நம, so that the bonds' syllables are stilled on the tongue while Siva rises in thought; it can also mean 'new'. பரிசு (touch, or manner) and அவதி (limit, or affliction) are uncertain; the sense seems to be that even the act of chanting is finally left behind.

title: அதிசூக்கும பஞ்சாக்கரம்
theme: The most subtle five letters: chanting சிவாய and சிவசிவ with a fixed mind brings bliss and a heart the Lord never leaves; the one letter of the Lord outweighs all Vedic and Agamic learning, and those who boast of knowing letters do not know the letter that masters them.
structure_note: Two verses on practice, the mind fixed by the mantra (2718) and the yogic ascent through the five (2719), then two on the one letter against book learning (2720, 2721).

reading: Fixing the mind with சிவாய நம and making oneself wholly a servant so that harm is gone, then thinking சிவாய சிவசிவ again and again, the mind stands with its harm destroyed, and that is bliss.
nuance: The verse moves from the full mantra (சிவாய நம) to its subtle forms (சிவாய, சிவசிவ). அவாயம் is apaya, harm or danger, and also echoes அவா, desire, so 'harm' may be the craving that troubles the mind.

reading: Passing through the orb of red flame and beyond it, climbing by the five in their order and taking the way, at the time he spoke of one may attain the state in which the Lord never leaves, as one's own heart.
nuance: செஞ்சுடர் மண்டலம் (the orb of red flame) is traditionally a centre in the yogic body, the sun's or fire's region; அஞ்சு அணவும் முறை may be the five letters placed in order along the body or the five states. துஞ்சும் அவன் சொன்ன காலத்து is obscure: துஞ்சு can mean sleep or death, so it may be the time of death the Lord appointed or the yogic sleep.

reading: Though one recites the Vedas with their limbs and the Agamas, what is ours lies in one letter of our Lord; master that one letter with doubt destroyed and one becomes a precious vessel that has reached the farther shore.
nuance: அங்கம் are the six limbs of the Veda. The one letter is not named; tradition takes it as சி or as the five letters held as one, or as Om. அருங்கலம் can be a rare ship or a rare jewel; with அங்கரை (that shore) the ship fits better, with the shore as the end of births.

reading: The five that ripened lie within the ancient Veda; none know the karma that wakes there and sleeps; fools say 'we know the letters', but they do not know the letter that masters the letters.
nuance: பழுத்தன ஐந்தும் பழமறையுள்ளே is traditionally taken as the five letters set at the centre of the Veda (in the Sri Rudram of the Yajur Veda). Line 2 is obscure: விழித்து அங்கு உறங்கும் வினை may be karma that seems to sleep but wakes. எழுத்தை அழுத்தும் எழுத்து (the letter that presses down the letters) plays on letters as script and as mantra.

title: திருக்கூத்து தரிசனம்
theme: The vision of the holy dance: Siva dances everywhere and as everything, with Shakti, at Tillai and beyond all worlds, and his dancing sets the scriptures, the elements, the worlds and the mind dancing. The same dance is placed in the body, in the central channel, between the brows and in the heart, is read off the dancer's hands as the five acts and the five letters, and is known by its effects on those who see it: tears, melting, the end of self, and bliss.
structure_note: The chapter has no strict order but returns to a few strands: the dance as all-pervading bliss and play (2722 to 2731, 2786 to 2792); its cosmic and sacred places, Tillai and the south (2732, 2746, 2749, 2755, 2758, 2773 to 2775); its place in the yogic body, mapped onto Meru, Lanka and the Himalaya (2735, 2736, 2747, 2748, 2754, 2764, 2770, 2771); the dancer's attributes, hands and feet read as the five acts and the five letters (2780, 2781, 2797 to 2799); and its effect on the devotee who sees it (2740 to 2745, 2760, 2778, 2779, 2796). Many verses in the second half are numerical or compressed.
source_issues: 2726 lines 2 and 3 (சமயக் களியார் பரமும் கருதுறை யந்தக்) are broken in syntax and may be corrupt.
2728: தாகாண்ட and several of the -அண்டம் compounds are obscure.
2733 lines 2 and 3 (நடம் எட்டோ டு ஐந்துஆறு, திடம்உற்று ஏழும்) are unclear.
2736: ஆன்நந்தி and கான்நந்தி are obscure and may be corrupt for forms of ஆனந்தம்.
2741: பரானநத்தத்தே looks garbled for பரானந்தத்தே.
2750: the compounds குரானந்த and புரானந்த are unclear.
2752 line 4 (உம்பரம் மோனஞா ஞானந்தத்தில்) looks garbled.
2754 lines 3 and 4 (கைகண்ட மூலம், படர்பொன்றி) are obscure.
2764 line 1 (நீரும் சிரிசிடை) looks corrupt.
2772: the petal counts do not match a standard scheme and may be corrupt.
2774: அங்கார் and மோகாய are obscure.
2782: அன்பதும் is probably a corruption of ஐம்பதும்.
2794 lines 1 and 2 are obscure.
2802: சீய is obscure.

reading: Everywhere is his holy form, everywhere Siva and Shakti, everywhere Chidambaram, everywhere the holy dance; because Siva is everywhere, the grace of Siva that abides everywhere is his own play.
nuance: The verse opens the chapter by freeing the dance from one place: Chidambaram and the dance are wherever Siva is. விளையாட்டு (play) names the whole of his grace as sport, the idea tradition calls lila.

reading: Who can know the dancer of Siva's bliss, the supreme light of consciousness, the beautiful dancer who is the state of the word, the dancer of the golden city, of golden Tillai, the wondrous dancer?
nuance: சொற்பதம் (the word-state) may be the state reached through words or the one beyond them; the verse does not settle it. பொற்பதி and பொன்தில்லை both name Chidambaram's golden hall.

reading: See the great dance of bliss, streaming honey, above the endless Shakti of eternal bliss; for the Lord who dances beyond knowledge, she became the stage for his dance of bliss.
nuance: Shakti is the stage (ஆடரங்கு) and Siva the dancer: the pair is figured as dance and floor. ஞானம் கடந்து says the dance lies beyond knowledge, even liberating knowledge. தான்அந்தம் இல்லா (without end) returns as wordplay in 2796.

reading: For the one who delights in the dance of bliss, the stage is bliss, the songs are bliss, the instruments and their music are bliss, and the whole world of moving and unmoving things is bliss.
Light, the Supreme, the Supreme that is, the Supreme of gracious Sivakami and of the joy of the creeds: the clarity that is reached in contemplation is the attainment of the dance of Siva's bliss.
nuance: Lines 2 and 3 are broken in syntax (சமயக் களியார் பரமும் கருதுறை யந்தக்), and the reading here only joins what can be joined. சிவகாமி is the name of the goddess at Chidambaram.

reading: The dances are five; the one who is without form and with form dances them as the five acts, and by grace doing the five acts, the consort of her of honeyed speech dances the holy dance.
nuance: அகள சகளத்தர் (the formless and formed one) is Siddhanta's term for Siva as both. The five dances are matched to the five acts, which 2799 assigns one by one to parts of the dancer's body. தேன்மொழி பாகன் is Siva as sharing his body with Uma.

reading: The worlds of the elements, of distinction, of enjoyment, of yoga, of the ancients, of release, of delusion, of the body, of thirst and of the five acts: beyond them, in the Supreme, is the solitary great Brahmanda, they say.
nuance: The verse is a list of compounds in -அண்டம் whose sense is mostly guessable from their first parts; தாகாண்ட (of thirst?) and the exact force of each are uncertain. The dance is not named; the verse sets the scale for the cosmic dance of the chapter.

reading: The Vedas dance, the great Agamas dance, songs dance, the seven bright worlds dance, the elements dance, the whole world dances: with nada he danced the dance at the end of knowledge.
nuance: His dance sets everything else dancing; the verb ஆட runs through the verse as a refrain, and 2751, 2756, 2789 and 2791 repeat the pattern. ஞானாந்தக் கூத்து (the dance at knowledge's end) sits beside நாதாந்தம் in 2751 as names for where the dance is.

reading: The Siddha dances joined with the five elements, the senses, the five sense-objects, the five Vedas, the great Agama, the kalas that are recited, time and the aeons, and the five knowledges of the worlds.
nuance: வேதங்கள் ஐந்து (five Vedas) is unusual, and அண்டப் போதங்கள் ஐந்து (five knowledges of the worlds) is obscure; both may follow the verse's run of fives rather than a fixed list. சித்தன் here names Siva.

reading: Gods, suras, men, siddhas, vidyadharas, the three, the thirty-three from the beginning, ascetics, Shaktas, the creeds and all moving and unmoving things dance as our Lord dances.
nuance: The creeds (சமயம்) are listed among the dancers: whatever their differences, they move by his movement.

reading: Beyond and beyond the seven worlds, above the crown of Shakti and Sadasiva who are said to be there, the dark-throated one took a holy form of compassion and delighted in the dance there for Uma to see.
nuance: The dance is placed above even Sadasiva, the highest form in the usual Siddhanta ordering, and is done so that Uma may watch: the dance as a form taken out of compassion (கருணை திருவுரு).

tamil: நடம் எட்டோ டு ஐந்துஆறு நாடியுள் நாடும்
reading: Kodukotti, Pandarangam, Kodu and Samharam, dances eight, and five and six sought within the nadis; firm and seven; the deodar forest, Tillai and the great banyan forest: he is the king of these.
nuance: கொடுகொட்டி, பாண்டரங்கம் and சங்காரம் are traditionally names of Siva's dances, known also from the Silappatikaram; தேவதாரு, தில்லை and வடம் (the banyan, taken as Tiruvalangadu) are traditionally places of his dance. The numbers and the syntax of lines 2 and 3 are unclear.

reading: Within the supreme cosmos are the feet of Parashakti, within it the Lord of spreading light, within it the spreading nada, and within it the Supreme dances.
With the path that rises like a goad in awakening and the beat of the rhythm called thonthi, Sankara dances held within the root nadi; when that time swells, there is no entering and no going.
nuance: அங்குசம் (goad), தொந்தி and மூலநாடி are yogic terms whose exact sense is not fixed by the verse; தொந்தி may be a rhythm term or a name for a bodily centre. புகும் போகல் இல்லை is commonly taken as the breath's coming and going ceasing, and may also be read as an end of birth and death.

reading: My Lord danced as Nandi, then danced the new (or nine) dances, danced as Nandi of the forest, held it in thought and danced, danced within the threefold sushumna, danced within endless knowledge, and completed it.
nuance: ஆன்நந்தி and கான்நந்தி are obscure and may be wordplay on ஆனந்தம் (bliss); நவக் கூத்து is either new or nine dances. The verse traces the dance inward, from outer forms to the central channel and then to knowledge.

reading: The five Shaktis, the five distinctions of Siva, the eight releases, the eight first states, the eight attainments, the eight states of Siva and the eight purities: the Lord dances his ancient dance through these.
nuance: The sets of five and eight are named without their members, and the traditional lists cannot be checked against the verse.

reading: The seven clouds, the seven islands of the wide sea, the bodies that surround them, the seven Siva-suns, the seven thirsts and the seven peaces: all that comes to be is contained beneath Nandi's feet.
nuance: சிவபாற்கரன் (Siva-sun) and the sevens of thirst and peace are obscure. The point that holds is the last line: the whole ordered cosmos lies under the dancer's feet.

reading: In the south, north, east, west and zenith, in the five wondrous faces, within the twofold pair of matchless great bliss, the Supreme stands and does his unique dance.
nuance: The four directions and the zenith match the five faces of Sadasiva in Saiva iconography. உபய உபயம் (twofold of the twofold) is obscure; it may mean Siva and Shakti.

reading: Those who reach his feet are his devotees; devotees are those who saw the dance in the golden hall; they are those who saw bliss at Hara's feet; those who have become devotees have received the Father's grace.
nuance: The verse plays on அடி (foot) and அடியார் (devotee, one of the foot): to be a devotee is to have reached the feet, and the feet are those of the dancer.

reading: Nandi, the dancer of good knowledge, subdued me who would not be subdued, set his foot on me, placed me in the place of supreme bliss, walked on, and settled deep within me as a picture.
nuance: அடிவைத்து (placing the foot) is traditionally the guru's initiation by the feet. படம்தான் செய்து (making a picture, or a cloth, or a hood) is unclear; the image may be of the dancer imprinted within. இடம்காண் பரானநத்தத்தே looks garbled for பரானந்தத்தே (in supreme bliss).

reading: The dancer in the heavens, the excellent dancer, the valiant dancer in the hall of red gold, the dancer of relationship, the dancer who is the Supreme: seeking him with joy, I placed him in my love.
nuance: சம்பந்தக் கூத்தன் may mean the dancer who binds himself to souls; it could also allude to the saint Sambandar, which would be out of keeping with the rest of the list.

reading: Who can describe the ruby dancer, the dancer of bountiful Tillai, the dancer with twisted locks in the adorned hall, the dancer of Siva's bliss in the far light, the dancer of pure gold?

Those who set their love on the beautiful golden flower-feet in the dance of the holy hall, perfect in its rightness, sob, tremble, fall, rise, grow faint in body, do not know themselves, and lose their cleverness.
nuance: The signs are those of devotional rapture, and the corpus records a close parallel in the Tevaram. சதுர்கெடும் (cleverness is lost) presents the loss of composure as gain.

reading: To see the drama, seeking ends, the mind's bewilderment ends, the breath in the body no longer withers, the senses that come through the intellect stop running, desire ends, and the gaze of bliss in the heart is held taut.
nuance: வாட்டறும் கால் (the breath that no longer withers) and நாட்டம் முறுக்குறும் (the gaze is twisted tight) carry a yogic sense of stilled breath and fixed gaze. The verse can be read as the effects of seeing the dance or as the conditions for seeing it; காணவே allows both.

reading: He danced with Kali, danced on the golden mountain, danced with the goblins, danced on the earth, danced amid water, fire, wind and the wide sky, and the Lord dances in the hall for all days.
nuance: The dance with Kali is traditionally the contest at Tiruvalangadu, and கனகாசலம் (golden mountain) is Meru. The verse gathers the dance's mythic sites and ends with the hall, where it goes on.

reading: Meru is the central nadi, ida and pingala are marked by the Himalaya of this sky and by Lanka, and sushumna rises through the Tillai forest and the cool Malaya: these are Siva's ground.
nuance: The verse maps the body's channels onto the land: the central channel onto Meru and onto Tillai, the side channels onto places north and south. Which channel goes with which place is not clear in the text, and 2754 gives the scheme again. இவைசிவ பூமியே makes the yogic body itself holy ground.

reading: South of Meru on the earth are, it is said, ida, pingala and the bright sushumna; the holy hall where the bearer of the half-moon dwells is the end of the boundary of the flawless world of the elements.
nuance: Chidambaram, in the south, is set at the place matching sushumna; பூதாண்டத்து எல்லையின் ஈறு (the end of the boundary of the elemental world) places the hall at the limit of the material cosmos.

reading: Taking the seven worlds as his golden city, the five ancient spaces as his city, and Shakti in the staff as his holy hall, the supreme light delighted in the dance.
nuance: தெண்டு (staff) is taken here as தண்டு, the spine or central channel, as in 2771, which ends with the same line; then the hall is Shakti within the body's central staff. The five spaces (ஆகாசங்கள் ஐந்து) are a yogic list not given.

reading: As a line of bliss and keen quality, filling the head with bliss and reaching the southern quarter, he became the enjoyer of bliss with his lady, passed beyond bliss, and danced.
nuance: The compounds குரானந்த, சிரானந்தம், புரானந்த and நிரானந்த form a chain of bliss words whose first parts are unclear; குரானந்த may be குரு + ஆனந்தம். நிரானந்தம் (bliss beyond bliss, or no-bliss) is a known term for the state past bliss.

reading: As the first Supreme dances, the fire in his palm dances, his celebrated matted hair dances, the datura dances, the half-moon dances, all above the earth and worlds dances: with nada he danced the dance at the end of nada.
nuance: உன்மத்தம் is the datura flower Siva wears and also means frenzy; both senses may be in play. நாதாந்த நட்டம் puts the dance where sound itself ends.

reading: The king's dance in the hall where we bow is the cosmic dance of the Lord of the sky; when one reaches Sivaloka, the true thing, the truth lies in the supreme silence at the end of knowledge.
nuance: Line 4 (உம்பரம் மோனஞா ஞானந்தத்தில்) looks garbled; read as silence and ஞானாந்தம் (knowledge's end). The verse moves from the dance one bows to in the hall to a silence beyond it.

reading: The worlds thrice seven, the seven spheres, the hundred and eight creeds that are means, nada with its end, the bliss of dance and the four states: with his half, the Supreme's two feet dance.
nuance: The numbers are given without their members; நாற்பதம் may be the four states of release or the four paths. பாதியோடு (with the half) is taken as with Uma, who is half his body.

reading: Ida and pingala are the Himalaya and Lanka, Meru standing in the middle is sushumna in the middle, and the Tillai forest one goes to is the root seen at hand, called the spreading one, the supreme of supremes.
nuance: The mapping of 2747 again, more plainly: the side channels to the northern and southern limits, the central one to Meru and to Tillai. Lines 3 and 4 (கைகண்ட மூலம், படர்பொன்றி) are obscure.

reading: With Kumari, the maiden at the land's end, the Kaveri, nine distinct holy waters and seven hills, and because the Vedas and Agamas, the great gain, were born there, the unchanging southern land is pure.
nuance: A praise of the south, set among verses on the southern hall (2748, 2758). பிறத்தலான் (because born there) may claim that the Vedas and Agamas were revealed in the south, which tradition says of the Agamas; it may also mean that they flourish there.

reading: Dancing in nada, dancing in the four states, dancing in the Veda, dancing above the end of fire, dancing in knowledge, the flawless Lord of the gods dances through the whole world.
nuance: நாற்பதம் (the four states) and தழல் அந்தம் (fire's end) are technical and unglossed.

reading: Dancing with the gods, dancing in the holy hall, dancing with the three, dancing with the company of sages, dancing within verse, dancing in Parashakti, the Lord of the dance dances within the king.
nuance: கோவினுள் (within the king) may mean within the ruler, within the soul as lord of the body, or within the cow (the soul as பசு); the verse does not say.

reading: In the southern holy hall the great one shines without difference, as those who have come to clarity know him: the one who says 'I am lord over the six faces' and 'I am the supreme guru of the declared creeds'.
nuance: ஆறு முகம் (six faces) is commonly taken as the six creeds, so that the dancer at Chidambaram is head and teacher of them all; it can also suggest Murugan. Who speaks the 'I am' is not fixed by the syntax.

reading: With the hall as his stage, the two lights of the two feet of our Supreme who dances on it stand as his own state within the line of the five supreme nadas, and he comes himself and grants grace.
nuance: ஐந்து நாதத்து ரேகை (the line of the five nadas) is unexplained. The two feet as two lights may be read as sun and moon, or as the two feet of the dance, one planted and one raised.

reading: The dancing foot, the sound of its anklet, the songs sung, the many dances and the form they made: as the supreme guru celebrated them, I sought, saw them within, and so came to an end of seeking.
nuance: தீர்ந்தற்றவாறு (how it ended and ceased) leaves open what ended: the search, the bonds, or the self. The dance is seen within (உளே), not in the hall.

reading: As the breath rising in the heart spreads through hands, feet and the rest, so the ruby dancer in the jewelled hall, as guru, delighted in dancing everywhere.
nuance: The breath pervading the limbs is the image for the dancer pervading all; குரவனாய் makes the pervading dancer also the teacher.

reading: The form that dances, other than the guru's form, that form-formless is the formless one itself; she who shines as Tripura is Uma, who is form and formless.
nuance: குனிக்கும் (bending) is a verb for dancing. The verse seems to distinguish the dancing form seen in the guru from the formless, and to make Uma as Tripura both; the logic is compressed.

reading: The holy way is in the small hall, in the form that dances within the guru's form; for those who have perceived it closely, the way by which the form becomes formless is the way of grace itself.
nuance: சிற்றம்பலம் (the small hall) is Chidambaram's shrine and in this chapter also a place in the body (2770). The dance is seen within the guru's form, which makes the guru the way to it.

reading: Where the life-breath rises and swells, running twelve finger-breadths, seek it: the place where our Lord of nada's end dances in delight is the holy hall itself.
nuance: பன்னிரண்டு அங்குலம் (twelve finger-breadths) is the yogic measure of the breath's reach outside the body. Line 1 (நீரும் சிரிசிடை) looks corrupt.

reading: As wind, cloud, lightning, rainbow and thunder shine clearly in the sky, so the six of joy and light mingle together and yet stay distinct; he stands as a form of light, hidden.
nuance: The sky image says the many appear in the one space without ceasing to be many. களிஒளி ஆறும் (the six of joy and light) is not glossed and may be six centres or six powers.

reading: Beyond the knowledge that examines the five beginning with fire, the eight directions, below and above, there is bliss; this is how the Lord stands and dances, for those who have passed beyond maya and great maya to see.
nuance: மாயை and மாமாயை are traditionally impure and pure maya; the dance is visible only past both. The bliss is set beyond the examining mind, not as its result.

reading: The dancer joins with her of rounded bangles, the dancer joins with flawless bliss, the dancer joins with flawless knowledge: the dancer and his dancing partner are above the dance.
nuance: கூத்தி (the female dancer) is Shakti. கூத்ததின் மேலே (above the dance) can mean that the pair are beyond the dance they perform, or simply engaged in it.

reading: I too have come to know that the Shakti who took the left side and our Father stand in dance; for all these many lives that stand with bodies, they dance, standing as the whole of them.
nuance: படங்கொடு நின்ற (standing with a படம், a cloth, picture or body) is taken here of embodied lives. The dancers in each body are Siva and Shakti.

reading: Shakti's form is all bliss; the matching bliss is Uma's body; Shakti's form rising as two in the embodied, the matched bliss becomes one dance.
nuance: சகளம் is the state with form; இரண்டு may be Siva and Shakti, whose two blisses make one dance. The verse is compressed.

reading: Gazing steadily at the space between the brows, straight from the forehead, the mantra shines out; the place where the Supreme sits as support of supports I took as Chirrambalam and joined.
nuance: A practice of fixing the gaze between the brows; the yogi names that place the small hall. பற்றுக்குப் பற்றாய் may mean the support of all supports, or the one to cling to in place of every clinging.

reading: The worlds becoming tattvas, Sadasiva, the seats called Sattvi and Sambhavi in the staff, the seven in the staff becoming Siva's seat: taking these, the supreme light delighted in the dance.
nuance: சாத்தவி and சாம்பவி are taken as names of seats or powers, and தண்டு as the spine. The last line repeats 2749's.

reading: The great flower, the lamp-light filling the hall, is good: its petals are four and a hundred; going on, there are twelve hundred; what stands is the long mandala.
nuance: The lotus with its petal-counts is traditionally a centre in the body, the thousand-petalled one at the crown, but the numbers given (நாலொடு நூறு, பத்திரு நூறு) do not match a standard list and may be corrupt.

reading: Seven crores of worlds, seven crores of bodies, seven crores of directions ringed by clear waves, seven crores of lingas ringed by the eight directions: these are the temple where he dances the cosmic dance.
nuance: அண்டம் and பிண்டம் (worlds and bodies) are paired as macrocosm and microcosm; both are his temple.

reading: Space is his body, Muyalakan lies there, the eight directions are his holy hands, the three lights are his three eyes; in the hall of the great body he dances.
nuance: முயலகன் is the dwarf under the dancer's foot, traditionally taken as ignorance (ஆணவம்). The three lights are traditionally sun, moon and fire. அங்கார் and மோகாய are obscure.

reading: The hall is the whole moving and unmoving world; the hall is the first Lord's feet; the hall is the region of water and fire; the hall is the five letters.
nuance: The hall (அம்பலம்) is given four identities, cosmic, devotional, yogic and mantric. அப்புத்தீ மண்டலம் is commonly taken as the moon and fire regions of the yogic body.

reading: Firm drums and flutes joined, sounding 'Om'; people danced crying 'the first Lord'; the good hosts who sought him, and the many goblins, sang: so it became a Pandarangam.
nuance: பாண்டரங்கம் is a named dance of Siva (see 2733); here it is the whole festive scene of music and the dancing and singing of his hosts.

reading: The gods in the world, the gods beyond it, and the gods within the earth ringed by the clear directions see and worship the dance in the golden hall on the lotus feet, and so reach their goal.
As water springs in the mouth of those who see tamarind, for all who see the joyous holy dance tears of grace drip, the faint heart melts, and the nectar of bliss in the light wells up in the heart.
nuance: The simile makes the point that the effect comes from seeing alone, as the mouth waters at the sight of tamarind. அமுது here is the bliss of the vision, without the yogic sense of nectar from the head that it has elsewhere.

reading: To stagger and fall is Siva's bliss; for those who have drunk, drinking more brings frenzy; the quality that comes to those who have seen the holy dance bending in the celebrated hall comes also to those who have heard of it.
nuance: உண்டார்க்கு உணவுண்டால் is obscure; read here as drink upon drink, the image of intoxication for the bliss. The last line extends the dance's effect from seeing to hearing.

reading: With fire, drum, rosary, noose, goad, trident, skull and knowledge, and the blue that gives both, with the woman as one half of him, he dances the great dance.
nuance: The list is of what the dancer holds in his hands, as in images of the many-armed form. உபயந்தரு நீலம் (the blue that gives both) is obscure; it may be the blue throat or Uma's colour.

reading: With the eleven parts of dance in order, the joined feet, the anklets, the drum held in the hand, and the long nada, Nandi danced in love of the beyond-supreme, outside and inside.
nuance: ஆடல் பதினோர் உறுப்பு may be the eleven parts of dance in Tamil dance theory or the eleven dances of tradition. புறம் அகம் (outside and inside) puts the dance both in the world and in the body.

reading: As the nine dance, as the sixteen dance, as the six paths of love dance with them, as in the delightful seven the seven and fifty-six dance, he danced the fifty too: the dance of bliss.
nuance: The numbers are given without their members. மார்க்கங்கள் ஆறு may be the six adhvas; அன்பதும் is probably ஐம்பதும் (the fifty letters), corrupted under the influence of அன்பு in line 2.

reading: As seven in the seven, rising as seven, as one in the seven, descending and settling as one, our supreme light, the true path in the seven, joined in the drama of the seven notes.
nuance: ஏழிசை are the seven notes of music; the other sevens are unglossed and may be the seven centres or the seven worlds.

reading: As five in the three, as three hundred and sixty, as six in the three, as the first twelve at the root, as the three lakhs at the end, he danced first in all three the dance at delusion's end.
nuance: Three hundred and sixty and twelve suggest the days and months of the year, and the three may be sun, moon and fire, which would make this the dance as time; that is a guess. மோகாந்தம் (the end of delusion) parallels நாதாந்தம் and ஞானாந்தம் elsewhere in the chapter.

reading: The great jewel that dwells on the crowns of the crowned gods, the pair of the Lord's flower feet, the fair jewel that rises in the hearts of those with love: he stands beyond the world.
nuance: The verse plays on மணி (jewel) through all four lines: the feet are the jewel on the gods' heads and in the lovers' hearts.

reading: If he who willed it dances, the worlds dance; our thought dances to the measure that he who knows dances; if he dances, the many elements dance: this is how I rejoiced seeing the dance of the fiery one.
nuance: The mind is made one of the things that move with his dance, like the worlds and the elements. எரிந்தவன் (the fiery one, or one who burned) is taken as Siva of fire.

reading: The ignorant say that the First danced; no one knows the First's dancing; once someone knows the First's dancing, the dancing of the First is the Shakti of grace.
nuance: To say that he danced, as a past event, is the ignorant view; known rightly, the dance is his gracious power at work. The verse shares its pattern with 2796.

reading: In the two states of nine and nine, as the angle of love stands at the head and dances, appearing within the Shakti that suffers, our loving Father stood and began to dance.
nuance: கோணம் (angle) suggests the triangles of a drawn diagram, and the nines may be its cells or lines; the verse cannot be pinned down. துன்புறு சத்தி (the Shakti that suffers, or that brings suffering) is unclear.

reading: As the tattvas dance, Sadasiva dances, the mind dances, Siva's Shakti dances, the placed world of moving and unmoving things dances and the Veda dances, the Father too danced the dance of bliss.
For the two to see, in the beautiful hall, as one supreme form both with form and formless, within the Shakti of holy grace, the Siddha, the blissful one, stood as a form of grace and began to dance.
nuance: இருவர் (the two) are traditionally the sages Patanjali and Vyaghrapada, for whom the dance was shown at Tillai; the verse does not name them.

reading: As Siva dances and Shakti dances, as the ruin in the world dances, as the sky that does not dance dances, as the nine tattvas and nada's end dance, Siva dances within Vedanta-Siddhanta.
nuance: வேதாந்தச் சித்தாந்தம் joins the two systems as the place of the dance, a pairing Tirumular makes elsewhere. நவமான may be nine or new. அவம் (ruin, waste) dances too: the dance takes in what is harmful.

reading: The end of nada, the end of the four knowledges, the end of the Veda, the true bliss of Siva: in the good bliss of Sadasiva, free of elements, the Nada-Brahman is Siva's dance.
nuance: நாற்போதம் (the four knowledges) and தாதற்ற (without dhatu, element or root) are not fixed. நாதப் பிரமம் (sound as Brahman) is identified with the dance.

reading: So that the struggle of the five beginning with Siva ends, and pasu and pasa stand apart there in austerity, the Supreme who is austerity dances, being himself everywhere: it is the dance of knowledge of those in Siva's bliss.
nuance: சிவமாதி ஐவர் (the five beginning with Siva) are commonly taken as the five lords who govern the five acts. தனித்து (standing apart) may mean that soul and bonds are separated. தவம் is repeated in every line and seems to name both practice and the Lord.

reading: Standing together with the gods of time, standing for release, standing to be sought under the name Vikirta, standing so that the three bright lights dance: this is how he took me as his own.
nuance: Lines 1 and 2 are obscure; விகிர்தா (the one who is other, unlike all) is a Tevaram name of Siva. The three lights are traditionally sun, moon and fire.

reading: Passing beyond nada-tattva and trusting the first scripture, they found bliss shining in the elements themselves; he wove together the 'not that' and its negation so that they are not divided.
nuance: நேதத்துவம் and நேதி echo the Upanishadic 'neti' (not this). The verse may mean that the way of negation and what it negates are held together by him, so that those beyond nada find bliss in the elements too; this is an interpretation of compressed lines.

reading: The ignorant say 'bliss, bliss'; no one knows the great dance of bliss; once someone knows the great dance of bliss, the place where the self comes to an end is bliss.
nuance: The last line puns on ஆனந்தம்: தான் அந்தம் அற்று (the self's end gone, or the self ended) is heard inside the word. Bliss is not a thing to name but the ending of the self in the dance.

reading: The hand that shook off, saying 'Si', the flower hand that embraced the ascetics, saying 'Va', the golden hand set fittingly as 'A', and the fire: the holy state is 'Ma'.
nuance: The dancer's hands are read as syllables of the five-letter mantra: the drum-hand or the shaking hand as சி, the embracing hand as வா, the protecting hand as அ (perhaps ய), and fire or the foot as ம. The exact matching is traditional and the verse does not give all five clearly.

reading: The drum, the outstretched sweeping arm, the water and the hand with fire, and the lotus foot that trod on the embryo: in this form, recite 'Sivayanama'.
nuance: Again the dancer's form spells the mantra. கருவின் மிதித்த (that trod on the embryo, or on birth) is taken as the foot crushing rebirth, or as the foot on Muyalakan; அப்பு (water) may be the Ganga in his hair.

tamil: அரன் அங்கி தன்னில் அறையிற் சங் காரம்
reading: Hara's drum is creation; the setting hand is preservation; Hara's fire is destruction; the pressing foot on which he rests is concealment; Hara's raised foot is grace for ever.
nuance: This is the classic reading of the dancer's body as the five acts. அமைத்தல் and உற்று அணைப்பு are taken as the reassuring hand and the planted foot by tradition; the verse names the drum, fire and foot plainly.

reading: The fierce one's light, the shining light, the inner light: she of tender eyes who saw the Dancer, as the first of the three murtis went between, looked on and sang the Vedas.
nuance: The tender-eyed one is most likely Uma watching the dance, as in 2732; இடைசெல்ல (going between) is obscure.

reading: How can I speak of Nandi, my Father, the Lord of knowledge, the beautiful dancer beyond and beyond the inner sky, reached by dwelling in the one mantra and passing beyond it?
nuance: The mantra is the way in and must then be passed beyond: மருவி அது கடந்து.

reading: No one knows the body to be examined of the guru Nandi in the holy hall; red like fire with white, such is the body in which one may take refuge.
nuance: சீய is obscure. Red and white together may be Siva and Shakti, or nada and bindu, as in 1929; the verse gives the colours without a key.

reading: Shakti, who is himself, stands as the Tatpara; she gives will to the Supreme who is himself and to souls; she conducts the distinctions beginning with knowledge; when she dances and grants grace, souls come to love Hara's feet.
nuance: Shakti is made the source of will (இச்சை) both in the Lord and in souls, and the dancer of the grace that turns souls to his feet. The subject of the last line is supplied.

title: ஆகாசப் பேறு
theme: The attainment of space (ஆகாசப் பேறு): the Lord who is Om, fire and right order within the heart turns the body into space; he stands as earth, cosmos and what lies beyond, and is known as light, cosmic, bodily and undivided, into which the knower's heart opens as open sky. The chapter ends by naming four spaces, outer, inner, in Siva and in the world, the last being the seat of samadhi.
structure_note: The Lord within the heart and across earth and cosmos (2804, 2805); the lights in which he is known (2806 to 2808); the sky-coloured one and the heart become space (2809 to 2811); the four spaces (2812). The grouping is mine.

reading: The one Lord who is Om within the heart, who is fire within it and who is right order within it: within the heart the body itself becomes space.
nuance: Each line opens with உள்ளத்துள் (within the heart), and the last turns from the Lord to the body: உடல் ஆகாயம் ஆமே. It can be read as the body becoming spacious or void in realisation, or as the heart-space (the inner ஆகாசம் of 2812) being where the body is known. நீதி (justice, right order) is an unusual name for the Lord here and I can't fix its sense.

reading: The Lord's nature is to stand as the great earth, as the cosmic sphere and as the ground beyond the sphere; standing as the great earth and bearing it with his feet, the first Lord stands as the rare state.
nuance: குருநிலம் (the guru-ground, or the ground of light, since குரு can mean brightness) names what lies beyond the அண்டம், and I can't fix which. தாங்கிய தாளோன் (he of the feet that bear) joins the cosmic image to the feet the devotee seeks.

reading: The light of the cosmos, with the undivided light and the light of the body, makes a greatness people babble about; hidden in light within the space that has swallowed all, it undid of itself the mark it had taken.
nuance: அண்டம் and பிண்டம் are the cosmos and the body, the large and the small worlds, here each with its light, and அகண்டம் the undivided beyond both. கொண்ட குறி (the mark taken) may be the bodily form, the soul's sense of itself, or the yogi's point of concentration; the subject of குலைத்தது is unclear.

reading: Within the enjoyment of the maidens that yields no fruit is the first supreme flame of light that gives fruit; standing beyond the knowing of Brahma and Mal, the one light becomes the high path.
nuance: பயனறு கன்னியர் போகம் is obscure: it may be the enjoyment of virgin powers (the Lord's shaktis) that produces no birth, or a yogic union without issue, set against the light that does yield fruit. Brahma and Mal failing to find the end of the light is the familiar story of the column of fire.

reading: The undivided light that is knowledge to knowledge, and the three great lights in their inseparable circuit, sink unknowing into the Father's feet; if one stays there without parting, it becomes the great time.
nuance: The three great lights (பேரொளி மூன்று) are traditionally sun, moon and fire, also matched with the channels and centres of the yogic body. பிறிவா வலம் and பெரும் காலம் (great time: long life, or timelessness) are not fixed by the verse.

reading: The sky-coloured one, the shoot of the race of the gods, who sat there wearing a great serpent as his upper cloth, settles into the hue of space, and beyond that becomes space and the one of the colour of fire.
nuance: ஆகாச வண்ணன் (sky-coloured) is usually an epithet of Mal, but ஏகாசம் (upper cloth) of மாசுணம் (great serpent) points to Siva, who wears snakes; the verse may be fusing the two or using the epithet of Siva. The movement is from a coloured form to space itself and then to fire.

reading: When the inner light that gives life to beings and to the world alike comes to join, the girl with the koel's voice frolics and roams, and my heart, taking in sunlight, becomes open space.
nuance: குயில்கொண்ட பேதை (the simple girl who has the koel's voice) may be Shakti, the kundalini, or the poet's own heart as a lovesick girl; the image is from love poetry and I can't fix its referent. வெயில்கொண்டு (taking in the sun) and வெளி (open space) carry the verse's claim that the heart becomes light and space.

reading: Approach him and the Lord does not move away; Nandi, the great Lord, spreads wide even in the atom of the world; if one bows to the space of lightning-light that has drawn near, one may drink nectar.
nuance: அணுகில் அகன்ற may be 'wide even in the atom' or 'far even when near'; both fit the paradox of the first two lines. Drinking nectar after seeing the light is the yogic sequence of the earlier tantras (nectar from the crown).

reading: The outer space is the regions and the worlds; the inner space is the knowing of our First; the space in Siva is the rich flame of light; and the space in the world is the seat of samadhi.
nuance: A scheme of four spaces (ஆகாசம்), each named with துள் (within). The last line, சகத்துளாகாசம் தானம் சமாதியே, is the least clear: தானம் may be 'place, seat' (sthana) or 'giving', and why the space within the world should be samadhi is not explained.

title: ஞானோதயம்
theme: The dawning of knowledge (ஞானோதயம்): Siva is not known by his colour or form but in knowledge he himself gives, through the path of the worthy and the guru; the seeker who searches for 'I' and 'He' is shown they are not two. Images of a lamp lit within a lamp, of gems and of nectar mark the knowledge, which is called the path of nadanta, true yoga and release.
structure_note: Bliss in the states (2813); the Lord known by service and knowledge, not sight (2814, 2815); the lamp, the tattvas, the nectar and the gems (2816 to 2819); 'I' and 'He' not two (2820); the good path of knowledge (2821 to 2824). The grouping is mine; 2821 to 2823 each repeat an opening phrase.
source_issues: 2823: line 3 reads பேணவல் லார்க்கப் பிழைப்பிலன், apparently for பேணவல்லார்க்கு அப் (or லார்க்குப்) பிழைப்பிலன்.
2821: நன்மோக in line 4 may be a corruption of நன்மோக்க (release); as printed it reads 'good delusion'.

reading: What the mind sees at its juncture is the mind's waking; seeing bliss as dream comes, and, on inquiry, the ceasing beyond it, are called bliss; Nandi, who has reached his own, says bliss is twofold.
nuance: மனசந்தி (the juncture of the mind), மனநனவு (the mind's waking) and மீதொழிவு (the ceasing above) are technical terms of the states of consciousness that I can't fix. Which two blisses are meant (perhaps the bliss seen in a state and the bliss of its ceasing) is not stated plainly; இனமுற்றான் is obscure.

reading: My Lord, whose hand killed the elephant, who holds a skull in his hand and wears the burning young crescent: I only became his servant, calling him rare and great; whether he is dark or red I cannot see.
nuance: The first two lines give Siva's familiar marks (the flayed elephant, the skull-bowl, the crescent), and the last line refuses to describe him: devotion came without knowing his colour. கரியன்கொல் சேயன்கொல் (is he dark, is he red) may also hint that he is neither Mal nor any visible form.

reading: The exalted one who drank the poison so that the great might drink nectar grants, if you enter by the path of austerity the worthy have taught, a knowledge like refined gold; seek it by the way of the Naked One's feet.
nuance: நக்கார் சுழல்வழி is obscure. I take நக்கர் as the Naked One (a name of Siva) and சுழல் as a variant of கழல் (anklet, the feet), but it may be 'the whirling way of those who laugh'. தக்கார் (the worthy) points to the guru and the line of teachers.

reading: For those who can split the lamp, light the lamp, trim the lamp within the lamp and make the lamp shine in the lamp, reaching the feet of the Lord who owns the lamp becomes possible.
nuance: The whole verse plays on விளக்கு (lamp), also 'to make clear'. It is traditionally read of the soul's light kindled by the guru's knowledge until it shows the Lord's light within; splitting the lamp may be the separation of soul from bonds. The plain riddle and the symbolic reading both stand.

reading: Where the tattvas are, the Lord of the tattvas is there; where the tattvas are not, he is not there; once one knows the nature of knowledge of the tattvas, the Lord himself appears there.
nuance: தத்துவன் may be the Lord who rules the tattvas, or 'the Real' as against தத்துவம் (the real things). The second line seems to deny the Lord where there are no tattvas, which may mean he is reached only through knowing them, or be wordplay that the last line resolves.

reading: Within the true knowledge that holds up the sky, what wells up from the spring becomes rare nectar; on his spreading matted hair, shining like fresh gold, he stands joined with the scent of the safflower.
nuance: அசும்பு (oozing, a spring) and the nectar it yields are traditionally the fluid felt to flow from the crown in yoga. விசும்பு ஒன்று தாங்கிய may be knowledge that bears the inner sky. The link between the nectar and Siva's fragrant hair is not stated.

reading: The light that dwells in the cosmos of souls, like pearl, diamond, coral of the sea, clustered fresh gold and pure-shining ruby: in what way will you call it different and divide it?
nuance: The gems are not alike, yet each shines; the question argues that the one light is not to be split by the many forms it shines in. ஒத்து உயிர் அண்டத்துள் can also be read 'matching, within soul and cosmos'.

reading: I searched, calling it 'I' and calling it 'He', and as I searched, the First of knowledge who is the 'I' granted me that 'I' and 'He' are not two; and I, the one who said 'I', ceased to think.
nuance: நான் and தான் (I and He, or I and the self) are the two terms; the knowledge that they are not two is given (நல்கினான்), not reached. The verse can be read as plain non-duality or, as Siddhanta reads such verses, as inseparability without identity; it says இரண்டில்லை and no more.

reading: The good path of knowledge is the good path of nadanta; the good path of knowledge is knowing it as 'I'; the good yoga of knowledge is standing in the good state; the good release of knowledge is the Veda of nadanta.
nuance: நாதாந்தம் (the end of nada) is one of the six ends (ஆறந்தம்). நன்மோகம் is odd: மோகம் is delusion or longing, and I read it as standing for மோக்கம் (release); the text may be corrupt. நானென்று அறிவோர்தல் echoes 2820.

reading: For those who can be saved, Siva-knowledge is their life; Siva the god is their life; Om is where they dissolve; and they become the knowing within knowing.
nuance: ஒடுக்கம் (withdrawal, dissolution) makes the syllable Om the place into which the saved are drawn back, not only a sound they recite.

reading: To those who can see, he is like the pupil of the eye; to those who can see, like nectar from the sea; to those who can cherish him, Nandi, the great name, never fails; to those who can hold fast, he becomes their support.
nuance: ஆணவல்லார் is obscure: it may mean those who can hold fast or rule themselves, or, by a pun, those free of ஆணவம் (the root impurity). The nectar of the sea recalls the churning, when Siva drank the poison (2815).

reading: Like the sound that stands within the letter Om, the excellent thing the gods above desire is the feet of our Lord, the red flame standing far off; the gods who seek them become his inner retinue.
nuance: The sound within Om is traditionally the nada beyond its letters. அகம்படி (inner retinue, palace attendants) may also mean that the feet become the seekers' inner dwelling.

title: சத்திய ஞானானந்தம்
theme: Truth, knowledge and bliss (சத்திய ஞானானந்தம்): passing beyond the three voids and the states into the turiya of 'thou' and 'that', the knower sheds malam and the thirty-six tattvas and becomes Siva. The qualities of the Supreme, truth and the rest, stand together as a water lily's form, colour, scent and beauty; the bliss floods the body like milk and honey, and even the thought of the Lord is his grace.
structure_note: Beyond the voids and the third turiya (2825, 2826); the water-lily image for the Supreme's qualities (2827 to 2829); grace and the flood of turiya (2830, 2831); the Lord beyond and the jnani's attainment (2832 to 2834). The grouping is mine.
source_issues: 2827: மாசோயை in line 1 is obscure and may be corrupt.
2834: line 4 (துவமார் துரியம் சொரூபம் தாமே) appears short and may have lost a word.

reading: Becoming every void, void and all things and yet not them, attending to the three voids and the three voids below, the one who is supreme knowledge-bliss becomes That, in a bliss where there is no saying 'this void is so'.
nuance: பாழ் (void, emptiness) and முப்பாழ் (the three voids) are technical terms in the ninth tantra; they are traditionally taken as voids of the soul, of maya and of the Supreme (or of the three padas of 'that thou art'), but the verse does not list them. கீழுள முப்பாழ் (the three voids below) suggests two sets of three.

reading: Like the turiya spoken of 'thou' and 'that', it becomes good in the trusted third turiya; beyond the beautiful earth and the unthought super-subtle is the perfect thing, glorious Nandi, who rules and gives grace.
nuance: தொம்பதம் (thou) and தற்பதம் (that) are the words of the great saying 'that thou art', each given its own turiya in the earlier chapters; the third turiya is traditionally that of அசி (art), their union. அம்புவி யுன்னா may be divided differently.

reading: To compare the lasting truth and the rest with the stainless light of a gem does not fit; rather, like the fresh water lily with its form, bright colour, fragrance and beauty, they are spoken of as six.
nuance: சத்தியாதி (truth and the rest) is taken as truth, knowledge, bliss and the qualities that go with them; the count of six (ஆறும்) is not explained. மாசோயை is obscure. The point seems to be that the qualities are distinct yet inseparable, like a flower's form, colour and scent, not one undivided glow.

reading: When Shakti, Siva and supreme knowledge are spoken of, the endless one given, Siva who is high bliss, the Shakti of his own form, the guru who comes and the body given are like the water lily.
nuance: The list is compressed and its grouping uncertain. The water lily (உற்பலம்) again stands for distinct aspects that cannot be separated; that the guru and the body are among them suggests the Lord's coming as guru in a body is one with his nature.

reading: As the water lily's form, colour, bright fragrance and beauty stand together, so when the soul merges in the Supreme, he stands so that truth and the rest appear in the very form of the great three padas called Siva.
nuance: மாமுப்பதம் (the great three padas) are taken as 'thou', 'that' and 'art'. The verse makes the water lily image explicit and applies it to the soul's union, not to the Lord alone.

reading: If one bows with a melting heart as far as one can think, and adorns him, one can hold him within; Nandi my king, joining his grace even to me, made me think as far as I think.
nuance: The verse turns on நினையும் அளவில் (as far as one thinks), used twice: first as the measure of the devotee's worship, then as the measure of what the Lord's grace made him think. Even the thinking is given. பொதியல் (to contain, to wrap) may also mean to enshrine.

reading: Like honey with milk, the juice within fruit and the sweetness of the great pure nectar, turiya, when it enters, floods the virtuous through every hair-root.
nuance: பொடிபடி is obscure: perhaps 'shattering' or 'settling like fine dust'. சீல (virtuous) may qualify the person or be part of a phrase about the body. The bliss is felt in the body, at every மயிர்க்கால், not only in the mind.

reading: Passing beyond the immortal state and beyond the cosmos, the Lord who stands alone in the beyond stood following the unwavering light of the woman with pearls in coral and cool speech.
nuance: The woman with pearl teeth in coral lips and cool words is taken as Shakti. தமரம் (sound, or a hollow) is obscure, as is whether the light is hers or his own that she follows.

reading: Changing the middle thirty-six, removing malam, becoming pure and free of flaw in turiya, losing bondage and becoming Siva, and so transformed, the jnani reaches truth, knowledge and bliss.
nuance: ஆறாறு is the thirty-six tattvas; மத்திமம் (middle) may refer to the middle state or channel. பெத்தம் is bondage (baddha), the opposite of release. பிறழ்வுற்றும் (even turning aside, changing) is unclear.

reading: Becoming Siva so that the three disgraceful malas end, holding the three voids of birth so as to cling no more, in the truth, knowledge and bliss that is austerity, the turiya full of 'thou' is the true form itself.
nuance: பவமான முப்பாழ் (the three voids that are birth) and பற்றறப் பற்ற (to hold so as to cling no more) are paradoxical and technical. துவம் is taken as tvam, 'thou'. The last line seems short of a syllable or two.

title: சொரூப உதயம்
theme: The rising of the true form (சொரூப உதயம்): the Lord pervades the elements so wholly that he cannot be marked off and circled, is beyond form and formlessness, and is reached only through the guru. Those who meditate on his form receive light; the poet sinks into the supreme light, crosses birth, and can say the First is the 'I'.
structure_note: The supreme guru in turiya and the Lord who pervades all (2835 to 2837); those beyond sect and the faults, and the soul and the Supreme (2838, 2839); form, formlessness and the guru (2840, 2841); the poet's own seeing (2842 to 2846). The grouping is mine; 2841 repeats உருவம் நினைப்பவர் in every line and 2842 பரஞ்சோதி.

reading: The supreme guru, becoming the Supreme everywhere, joining everywhere firmly and without gap, the form that endures within the all-pervading form, stood having reached rare turiya.
