nuance: சொரூபம் (own form, true nature) is used twice: the guru's own form is said to endure within the form that pervades all. Whether the guru here is the Lord as guru or the human teacher become one with him is not fixed.

reading: The water of the world in the surging sea, the tossing wind, fire and space: I do not know how to mark off the one who stretches long and wide through earth and sky and walk around him in worship.
nuance: வலம்செய்தல் (circumambulation) needs a bounded object; the verse's point is that the Lord, spread through all five elements, cannot be bounded (வரைந்து) to be circled.

reading: He stood there; the gods from Brahma and Mal on, and all who stand anywhere, praise him as Lord; our Lord, the sole master, abides, and swells forth as Lord of the worlds.
nuance: The verbs run from standing there (அங்கு நின்றான்) to dwelling (தங்கி நின்றான்) to swelling forth (பொங்கி நின்றான்): the one Lord is both settled and overflowing.

reading: Those who stand in clarity, without knowing even the trace of the sects in themselves, beyond the eight causes beginning with desire and the workings of darkness, become lords over the gods.
nuance: காமாதி காரணம் எட்டும் (the eight beginning with desire) are traditionally the faults such as desire, anger, greed, delusion, pride and envy, but the list of eight is not given. சுமையற்ற (burdenless) is unclear in its place. Sects (சமயம்) are again something to leave behind, as often in Tirumular.

reading: One of the three kinds of gods is the first form and becomes different from it; so too the soul and the Supreme; that the far-off Siva may be gloriously reached in the three turiyas is the fitting path, say the books of the Lord.
nuance: The analogy is compressed: as one god is both the source of the three gods and one of them, so the soul (அணு) and the Supreme are one and different. இறைநூல் (the Lord's books) is taken as the Agamas. The three turiyas are those of 'thou', 'that' and 'art' (2826).

reading: Standing without form, he joins himself to forms; not being a womb, he himself becomes the womb; the wondrous Lord who stands without even formlessness cannot be reached by anyone without the guru.
nuance: உரு, அரு (form, formless) and கரு (womb, embryo) rhyme through the verse. மாயப் பிரான் may be 'the wondrous Lord' or 'the Lord of maya'; Mal is also called மாயன், but here the subject is the one reached through the guru.

reading: Those who think on his form find light rising within; those who think on his form see the aeons; those who think on his form become celestials; who in the world are equal to those who think on his form?
nuance: The last line, உருவம் நினைப்பவர் உலகத்தில் யாரே, can mean 'who in the world is like them' or 'who in the world are such people' (they are rare). உருவம் may be the Lord's form or the guru's. After 2840 on the formless, the verse affirms meditation on form.

reading: As I held to the Lord who is the supreme light, the supreme light sank into me; and as I sank and sank within the supreme light, I saw the supreme light declare itself.
nuance: The movement is reciprocal: the light sinks into the poet, then the poet into the light. பறைய may be 'proclaim, speak' or 'wear away, vanish'; under the second reading the light itself fades from view in union.

reading: As form, shape and quality swallow the ancient and become the rare water lily, so the guru of the true form, who weighs the four joined to him, truth and the rest, dwells in the dawning of bliss.
nuance: The water lily image of the previous chapter (2827 to 2829). சுகோதயம் (the dawning of bliss) echoes the chapter title. தொல் விழுங்கி (swallowing the ancient) is obscure; it may refer to the old bonds.

reading: In the true form of speechless bliss and silence, if one sees truth and the rest without bound, A merges and becomes U and M, and in the speechless letter it is the inner light.
nuance: அகாரம், உகாரம், மகாரம் are the three parts of Om; உரையற்ற காரம் (the speechless letter) is taken as what lies beyond them, the point or nada. The verse ties the analysis of Om to the silence (மோனம்) of the true form.

reading: The form known to the woman with breasts who did penance on the peak of the high mountain, I too, crossing vile and wicked birth, came to see in the thief who stands in the kalas.
nuance: The woman doing penance on the mountain is taken as Uma, who won Siva by austerity on the Himalaya. கலைநின்ற கள்வன் (the thief who stands in the kalas) may be Siva hidden in the moon's digits, in the arts, or in the kalas of the yogic body; கள்வன் for the Lord who steals the heart is a devotional usage.

reading: I came to know how the rare thing within comes about, how it leaves and that this is how it enters; there is no being misled and no other place now, and the First who is ourselves can be called 'I'.
nuance: ஏமாப்பது இல்லை may mean 'there is no being deceived' or 'no other refuge is needed' (ஏமம், protection). The last line, நாமாம் முதல்வனும் நான் எனலாம், states the non-dual claim of 2820 in the poet's own voice.

title: ஊழ்
theme: Fate (ஊழ்): what befalls comes by Nandi's decree and one's own former deeds, so the knowers of truth are unchanged whether they are wounded or anointed. The devotee who has gained the Lord stays with him through thunder, fire, storm and wild beasts, ploughs the field of knowledge, and sees the loss of a body as moving to another house.
structure_note: Fate and the jnani's steadiness (2847 to 2849); the devotee unshaken by disaster (2850, 2851); the death of a body as a change of nest or house (2852).
source_issues: 2850: line 1 reads மாகடல் பொங்கிலன்; the 'what if' pattern of the verse and the editor's parallel (மாகடல் பொங்கிலென்) show it should be பொங்கிலென்.

reading: Whether they are struck or pared away, or anointed with red sandal paste, or a chisel is driven into their heads and they are thrown down, the knowers of truth, who go only by the decree of Nandi the wise, do not decline from their nature.
nuance: விதிவழி அல்லது can be read as 'except by Nandi's decree' (nothing touches them unless he wills it) or as 'going by no way but his decree'. Setting anointing beside the chisel echoes the old ideal of treating the one who wounds and the one who honours alike.

reading: Nothing was made beforehand by the heavens and laid by for one except by the way of the decree one has made oneself; going before the king by the way of the mark on the head, what I did before has become good ground.
nuance: The first two lines make the decree one's own (தான் முன்னம் செய்த விதி), not something heaven stores up. Line 3, கோன் முன்னம் சென்னி குறிவழியே சென்று, is obscure: it may be the mark written on the head (the fate written on the forehead) or the Lord's sign. The poet's former deeds are said to have become நன்னிலம், good ground for the Lord's grace.

reading: The river does not carry the fine sand it has laid down, and no one knows how to divide it up and carry it; my heart, having won Nandi of the ash-smeared body and upright matted hair, cannot part from him.
nuance: The image of the first two lines is not explained and the link to the last two is left to the reader. One possible reading: as the river leaves its sand behind and no one else can carry a share of it, each bears what his own deeds have laid down; another is that what is deposited stays, as the poet's heart stays with Nandi.

reading: What if the sky thunders, what if the great sea surges, what if the red fire of the forest mingles and the body burns, what if the wind strikes fiercely: I, at one with him, will seek the Lord.
nuance: The editor's parallel notes that the opening closely matches a verse of Appar's Thevaram (4.112.8), which uses the same 'what if' (என்) formula for the devotee's fearlessness. தான் ஒன்றி and நான் ஒன்றி both use ஒன்றி (joining): the wind joins its force, the poet joins the Lord.

reading: What if an elephant charges, what if an arrow cuts through, what if a tiger of the forest closes in around: in that other field my Lord has given, I will plough the ploughing of knowledge.
nuance: ஏனைப் பதி (the other place or field) may be the inner field as against the outer world, or the Lord's own realm. The image of ploughing knowledge turns the farmer's labour into spiritual practice.

reading: If the nest perishes, there is one who will make another nest; even if the land perishes, our people do not perish; if the house perishes, it is like entering another house: such is the state of those who know Nandi's nature.
nuance: கூடு (nest, also the body) and வீடு (house, also release) both carry a second sense; the verse's surface sense is that losing a body is like moving house, since the Lord will make another. நமர் (our people) is taken as the Lord's devotees. Whether வீடு here also hints at release is not clear.

title: சிவ தரிசனம்
theme: The vision of Siva (சிவ தரிசனம்): Siva is not other than the mind, and appears within the mind made clear; he is the subtle hidden thing in which speech and mind vanish, without going, coming or ruin; beyond the Supreme and all dispute, he gives grace in the world as Hara.
source_issues: 2854: line 4 begins யாக்கமும், which may stand for ஆக்கமும் with a glide consonant or be a misprint; the sense is unclear.

reading: There is no difference between what is called the mind and what is called Siva; Siva appears within the mind; for those who can clear the mind more and more, Siva abides within the mind.
nuance: Every line begins with சிந்தை (mind, thought). The first line states identity, the rest presence: Siva appears in, and dwells in, the mind as it is cleared. Read together, the identity may hold only of the cleared mind; the verse leaves both readings open.

reading: Look at the hidden thing in which speech and mind disappear: the thing to be seen is subtle; for those who examine and grasp it there is no going, no coming and no ruin, and even its gain is the Father.
nuance: போக்கு, வரவு, கேடு (going, coming, ruin) can describe the hidden thing itself or the knower, for whom birth and death end. The last line, யாக்கமும் அத்தனை, is obscure: it may be 'ஆக்கமும் அத்தனை' (even its growth is that much) or point to அத்தன், the Father.

reading: Being the Supreme, becoming the Supreme beyond the supreme and going further, being strength and the bright flame itself beyond all dispute, being the bearer whom no one can know as their own, he gave grace in the world as Hara.
nuance: பரன், பராபரன், உரன், தரன் and அரன் rhyme through the verse, rising to the transcendent and returning as Hara, who gives grace in the world. வழக்கற (beyond dispute, or beyond usage and speech) and தனதென ஆறு அறிவொண்ணா are compressed.

title: சிவ சொரூப தரிசனம்
theme: Seeing the form of Siva (சிவ சொரூப தரிசனம்): the Lord is consciousness, life and all things yet beyond thought, close as scent in a flower; he wakes the seeker, and what is seen is bliss and light beyond turiya, named by every title and none, beyond words.
structure_note: The chapter alternates affirmation and negation: the Lord as nectar, bliss and all things (2856, 2857), his nearness to those who think of him and his waking of the poet (2858, 2859), the bliss-light within turiya (2860), a string of denials (2861), the knowers who reach that bliss (2862), and the state beyond turiya that cannot be told (2863).
source_issues: 2856: line 1 reads மயிரக்கால், a misprint for மயிர்க்கால் (hair-root).
2857 is repeated as 3035 (chapter 223) with two variants that change the sense: புணர்வும் for புணரும் and புலனும் (the senses) for புலவி (sulking).
2862: line 4 reads யகன்றொர், probably for அகன்றோர்.

reading: Nectar wells up at every hair-root, a bliss that does not waver between difference and non-difference; the greatness of the one whose form the Veda chants lies beyond, past the three primal forms.
nuance: பேதம் அபேதம் (difference and non-difference) are the terms of the debate on how the soul stands to the Lord; the bliss here does not tip to either. ஆதி சொரூபங்கள் மூன்று (the three primal forms) is not fixed by the verse; it may be taken as the three aspects of being, knowing and bliss, or as three forms of the Lord. ஓதும் may go with the nectar ('the nectar spoken of') or simply open the verse.

reading: He is awareness and he is life; he is the union and he is the lovers' sulking; though bound up with all, he cannot be reached by thought, and he stays close as the scent stays in a cluster of flowers.
nuance: புணரும் and புலவி are the love-poetry pair of union and sulking, so the Lord is both moments of love; read so, the line borrows akam language for the soul and God. இணரும் may mean 'joined (with all)' or 'clustered', echoing இணர் (cluster) and துணர் (bunch) in the last line. The scent in the flower is Tirumular's recurrent image for a presence that pervades without being seen.

reading: Keep in mind first the one who stays close; when you think of him he will end your lack; the one of lasting scripture, the Vedic one, the great ascetic, is known through a certainty that stands within the head.
nuance: The opening துன்னிநின்றான் takes up the last word of 2857, linking the verses. மறையவன் மாதவன் can be epithets of Siva (the Vedic one, the great ascetic) or names of Brahma and Vishnu (மாதவன் is a name of Vishnu), which would change the line's sense. சென்னியுள் (within the head) is traditionally taken as the crown centre of yoga; plainly it may mean only 'in the mind'.

reading: With my mind lit as by lightning I woke, and in that waking the peerless Lord, light of himself, Nandi of golden body and coiled matted hair, opened my eyes; how am I to know what came to me?
nuance: நந்தி is both Siva and Tirumular's teacher, so the waking is at once grace and initiation. The last line is compressed: என்னுற்று அறிவன் may be 'how shall I know what befell me' or 'what shall I know of myself', and என்விழித்தான் 'he opened my eyes' or 'he looked upon me'.

reading: Truth, knowledge, the one substance, bliss; the great light of Siva's bliss that does not stay in the mind; pure Brahman, turiya; and within turiya, the great light reached in the turiya beyond it.
nuance: சத்திய ஞான ... ஆனந்தம் matches the Vedantic triad of being, knowledge and bliss, and சுத்தப் பிரம is Vedanta's word; the verse sets them beside சிவானந்தம், as Tirumular elsewhere joins Vedanta and Siddhanta. துரியத்துள் உய்த்த துரியம் (a turiya brought within turiya) is usually taken as துரியாதீதம், the state beyond turiya.

reading: It is not Para, nor the enduring Paraparan, nor strength, nor the bright flame known above, nor the bearer; being all these it is none of them; it is not even Hara, but lies beyond bliss.
nuance: A string of denials in the manner of 'not this, not this': each title of the Lord, even அரன், falls short. உரன் (strength, or knowledge) and தரன் (bearer, or one who holds a rank) are uncertain. தான் அவையாய் அல்லவாகும் keeps the denial from being a simple absence: it is all of them and not them. Even bliss (ஆனந்தம்), which 2860 named, is passed.

reading: One whose knowledge is complete, holding both release and attainment, stands within devotion and within the Supreme; those who stand within the great Shakti, as the tattvas join, pass beyond purification and become knowers of blissful joy.
nuance: முத்தியும் சித்தியும் sets release beside yogic attainment. தத்துவங் கூடலால் (because the tattvas join, or are reached) and சுத்தி யகன்றோர் (those who have left purification behind, or those beyond the purified state) are obscure; the line may mean they no longer need the purifying rites. சுகானந்த போதர் (knowers of joy-bliss) is a compound of Sanskrit terms.

reading: The state beyond turiya is the void where words cease; if one grasps the rare turiya and the beyond, how can one tell of one's own form, which spreads, contracts, does not break open, gleams and turns?
nuance: பாழ் (void, barren waste) is Tirumular's word for the state beyond form. தன் உருவும் may be the form of the self or of the Lord, and the five verbs (spread, contract, not open, shine, turn) may describe its play or simply its being past description; விள்ளா may also mean 'cannot be uttered'.

title: முத்தி பேதம், கரும நிருவாணம்
theme: Kinds of release and the nirvana of karma (முத்தி பேதம், கரும நிருவாணம்): when release is reached the soul attains Siva without distinction and the primal form becomes its own; those who cling to the one without attachments find him their kin and, gaining his light, fall silent.

reading: When the release spoken of is reached, the soul attains the Supreme, that Siva, without distinction, through turiya; the primal form becoming its own form, faultless nirvana is born.
nuance: உயிர்பர may be உயிர் பரம் (the soul, the Supreme) or உயிர் பர(ம்) எய்தும் (the soul reaches the Supreme). ஆதி சொரூபம் சொரூபத்தது ஆக is taken as the soul taking on the Lord's own nature. நிருவாணம் is both the name of the highest initiation and a word for the freed state; the chapter title (கரும நிருவாணம்) points to the ending of karma.

reading: The supreme being whom those without attachments hold to, the forehead-eyed one whom those without kin regard as kin and who stands around those with no one around them: those who have gained his light and reached him have ceased their babbling.
nuance: The verse plays on பற்று (attachment) and சுற்று (kin, surrounding): having let go of both, the renouncer finds them again in the Lord. பிதற்று (babbling) may be empty talk or the devotee's restless praise; either way, the one who has gained the light falls silent.

title: சூனிய சம்பாஷணை
theme: The discourse of the void (சூனிய சம்பாஷணை): seventy riddle verses in the images of farming, cattle, trees, birds, trade and boats, which on their surface describe impossible or puzzling things and are traditionally read as a hidden language for the body, the senses, the breath, the tattvas and the way to Siva. The few plain threads are that the senses must be herded and not let run wild, that the pure path lies overgrown and inverted, and that the sweet is left for the bitter.
structure_note: There is no argued order. Clusters recur: field and plough (2868 to 2880, 2912, 2913), cattle counted in tattva-like numbers (2874, 2875, 2883, 2884, 2903), birds and beasts (2887 to 2893, 2918, 2921), trees and flowers (2898, 2904, 2916, 2917, 2919, 2922, 2928), and trade and the boat (2915, 2929, 2930, 2935). Nearly every verse rests on a code the chapter never states.
source_issues: 2931 line 1: புலர்fந்தது contains a Latin f; read புலர்ந்தது (marked CORRUPT_LINES).
2874 line 2: ஓர்ஏழுளு ஐந்துள, probably ஓர் ஏழுள ஐந்துள.
2876 line 1: அசுத்தில் is probably அகத்தில் (compare தட்டான் அகத்தில் in 2924).
2905 line 1: ஐந்தக்து is garbled, perhaps ஐந்தகத்து.
2907 line 3: தன்மை ய்துகண்டு is garbled, probably தன்மை அது கண்டு.
2927 line 1: பாடர்ந்து is a misprint for படர்ந்து.
2928 line 3: பூவக்குள் is a misprint for பூவுக்குள்.
2884 line 4, 2892 line 1, 2915 line 3 and 2916 line 3 are obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: With the body as the board, five dice and three eyes, the game is played with the fifty-one letters; the Lord sits there and plays, and I do not know the secret of these magic dice.
nuance: ஐம்பத்தோர் அக்கரம் (fifty-one letters) is the Sanskrit alphabet as mantra theory counts it. கவறு ஐந்து may be the five senses or elements and கண் மூன்று the three lights (sun, moon, fire); these are traditional guesses. The plain sense is that life is a game the Lord plays in the body, and its rule is hidden.

reading: The pure path lies overgrown with brush and no one knows how it lies turned about; for those who do know how it lies turned about, my inner love wells up.
nuance: மாறிக் கிடக்கும் (lies reversed) is repeated and is the key: the path runs against the ordinary direction. Tradition takes it as the yogic turning inward of breath and sight, but the verse only says it is reversed. The verse could stand as a preface to the chapter's riddles.

reading: At a junction where six streets meet there are four palmyras that yield juice; setting a ladder hard to climb, I climbed that palm and saw all seven seas.
nuance: The six streets are traditionally the six adharas, the palm and ladder the central channel climbed by breath, and the seven seas what is seen at the top. None of this is stated; the verse reads as a vision report in farming-village images.

reading: I sowed brinjal and bitter gourd sprouted; I dug the dust and a pumpkin flowered; the garden-folk ran off worshipping, and the banana ripened fully.
nuance: The verse is built on harvests that do not match the sowing. I can't fix what each plant stands for; one reading is that practice yields a fruit other than the one aimed at, and that the full banana ripens after the workers have turned to worship.

reading: There is a field where an elephant grows from the seed called ஐ, and none know that field's clarity; if one gains the mind of the dark-throated Lord, that land is easy to enter without any falsehood.
nuance: ஐ may be a seed-syllable (ஐம் is a known bija), or the word for the subtle or for the master. The elephant from a tiny seed marks the vast fruit of something minute. மையணி கண்டன் is Siva of the dark throat; entry depends on his favour, not on effort.

reading: There is one low field and two high fields, and a thieving field lies mixed among them; for those who plough the field of the heart, it grew of itself into a flooded field.
nuance: The one low and two high fields are sometimes taken as the central and the two side channels, and the thief-field as what steals the yield. உள்ளச்செய், the heart's field, is the one plain term: inner cultivation brings the abundance.

reading: A plough of three yokes ploughs three measures of land and strikes deep to the stake; those who do not yoke the tongue and plough the middle field yoke the breath and plough barren soil.
nuance: நா அணை (tongue-yoke) may mean mantra or a yogic placing of the tongue, கால் அணை (breath-yoke) breath control, and நடு the central channel. களர் (saline, barren land) suggests the breath-ploughers waste their labour, but the verse could also be praising a harder way. I can't settle which.

reading: There are two water-lifts and seven wells; if the water the elder bails and the younger channels does not flow into the beds but runs to waste, it is like a hen raised by a dancing-woman.
nuance: The two lifts are commonly read as the two breaths and the wasted water as breath or vital fluid lost. கூத்தி வளர்த்த கோழி, a dancer's hen, seems proverbial for something raised to no use, but I can't fix the saying.

reading: There are twenty-four penned cows and calves of seven and five; though the calves pour pots of milk, it is the penned cow that suits the Brahmin.
nuance: 24, 7 and 5 add to 36, the Siddhanta count of tattvas, which tradition divides as 24 soul-tattvas, 7 vidya-tattvas and 5 pure tattvas; that fit makes the tattva reading likely. Why the penned cow is preferred, and who the பனவன் is, the verse does not say.

reading: There are twenty-four calving cows, and of the spring-cows one pot of milk is enough; when the wind-cows are milked and drunk, we do not know the coming of the other cows.
nuance: காற்றுப் பசுக்கள் (wind-cows) points to the breath; milking them may be breath control, after which மாற்றுப் பசுக்கள் (the other cows, perhaps births or changes) no longer come. The twenty-four again suggests the tattvas.

reading: On the top floor of the goldsmith's house a bud rose and bloomed red; wanting it round, folding away the truth, the goldsmith seized it.
nuance: The goldsmith is a stock figure of the cheat, and may be the mind; the bud at the top of the house may be a centre in the head. அசுத்தில் is probably a misreading of அகத்தில், as in 2924. I can't give a confident reading.

reading: If, in the sifting seed-bed and the field of trouble, one ties fast the turning water-lift and yokes the good striped milch cow, the cucumber seed spreads and seeds.
nuance: The images (seed-bed, field of trouble, water-lift, cow) are farm work turned to an unstated end; the field of trouble may be the body. The lines are too compressed for a confident reading.

reading: They scatter with a scoop, manure and sow, yoke the ram, stir up the sprout, yet do not cook rice in the big pot and slowly swallow it; that is how they reap red paddy with a ram.
nuance: The rhymes இடா, கிடா, மிடா (scoop, ram, pot) carry the verse. One reading is that they do all the labour and never eat the harvest; the closing line may mock reaping with the wrong tool. Both readings are guesses.

reading: The crop lies ripe, seed for what is above; it lies ripe a league above; for those who reap it again and again, the ripe crop spreads over three leagues.
nuance: விளைந்து (ripened) is repeated seven times. மேலை may be 'above' (the head, in yoga) or 'the hereafter'. காதம் is a measure of distance, and the growth from one to three leagues marks a yield that increases with repeated reaping.

reading: We do not know the intent of those who plough barren land, and they have no intent at all; the young creeper that sprouts in barren land may also wither.
nuance: This takes up களர் உழுவார் from 2872. The verse seems to blame aimless labour on soil that cannot hold a crop, so that even what sprouts dies; what the barren land stands for is not said.

reading: Placing in the fire the wedging noose for the little jackal in the shed that won't come when called, standing long and entering into good, he lived sweetly in the house with the jewelled woman.
nuance: The jackal that won't come when called may be the unruly mind, and burning the noose the ending of bonds. ஆயிழை (the jewelled woman) is often taken as Shakti. The syntax is loose and the reading tentative.

reading: When rain falls on the mountain the fawn leaps and the ripe fruit on the bunch falls; the smith set the nectar to pour onto the breast as onto a piece on the forge.
nuance: Tradition reads the mountain as the head, the rain as the nectar that flows from it in yoga, and the smith as the Lord or the yogi. The forge image (உலை) suggests heat that releases the flow. The fawn and the fruit are unexplained.

reading: In the Brahmin's house there are five milch cows that roam wild with no one to herd them; if a herdsman comes and their wildness is checked, the Brahmin's five cows will pour milk.
nuance: The five cows are widely taken as the five senses, and the closer chapter on restraining them (2025) uses the same herdsman. The point is that the senses, once herded, give milk: restraint makes them yield, not die. The herdsman may be the guru or the disciplined mind.

reading: Five wild cows, thirty lions, two sweet mangoes with nine long peppers: if one holds them as one's own monkey, they are within one's mind; if the unageing buffalo is let loose, they set it ablaze.
nuance: The numbers suggest a count of tattvas or bodily powers, but I can't map them. குரங்கொளில் and மூவாக் கடா (the unageing buffalo, perhaps death or the mind) are obscure, and the last line may be corrupt.

reading: As an unschooled maiden reads aloud the meaning of the leaves of an unwritten book, so an unborn bee drank the honey from the scent of an unopened flower.
nuance: Four negatives (எழுதாத, தெருளாத, மலராத, பிறவாத) make a knowing that comes before every means of knowing. It is commonly read as the soul's experience of Siva, beyond book, learning and sense; the verse states only the paradox.

reading: The falsehood that goes, the false seed that enters, the fruit of the naval tree that gives gruel, the green crop standing and the five who eat it: under a burning roof they prospered.
nuance: The five who eat are probably the senses, and the burning roof the body, but the first two lines (போகின்ற பொய், புகுகின்ற பொய்வித்து) may mean deeds that leave and deeds that come in as seed for birth. Very uncertain.

reading: A neem rose from a bamboo shoot; on a palm leaning on the neem there is a snake; with no one to chase the snake and eat it, the neem lies there bursting.
nuance: Tradition takes the bamboo as the spine and the snake as kundalini. The bursting neem, bitter and unfruitful, may be the body wasted when the serpent power is not roused. This is the tradition's key, not the verse's.

reading: Ten great tigers, fifteen elephants, five skilled ones, sixteen entertainers, three worthy ones, six physicians and five at the head sit and stand there.
nuance: A census of a body's or a town's inhabitants, probably standing for tattvas, breaths, senses and organs. I can't match the numbers to a known list.

reading: There are two buffaloes within this town and one service for both; if both are held fast, the two buffaloes become one.
nuance: The two are usually taken as the two breaths, or the right and left channels, which become one when held. The town is the body. The pattern of two becoming one is the clearest thing in the verse.

reading: Setting a balance within the field of the even mind and weighing cotton in the net of devotion, with pearl as the rope, the three in the town fight daily and stand full.
nuance: ஒத்த மனம் (the even mind) and பத்தி (devotion) are plain; the cotton, pearl rope and the three who fight are not. The three may be the gunas, kept in balance.

reading: The owl, the snake, the parrot and the cat, the naagai and the quail live in the middle; when the owl draws near the naagai, the rat seeing the owl cries out.
nuance: A household of creatures that prey on each other, probably faculties or passions in the body. நாகை is unclear (perhaps a bird or a cobra). I can't fix the code.

reading: He brought three white rats that stay in the laughing, scented measure; if told to leave the forge they run and they stay; that is how those born of baseness go.
nuance: The three white rats may be the three malas or the three gunas, and the forge the body or the discipline; the first line is obscure and may be corrupt. Only the three and the forge stand out.

reading: Those who have entered the forest will no longer see the space of the womb; the five horses have entered the nest and the six camels the cover; if they do not enter the cover, there are the three bonds.
nuance: கருவெளி (the womb-space) suggests that those who have gone in are free of birth. The five horses may be the senses and the six camels the six adharas or the inner organs; மூவணை (three yokes or three bonds) is unclear.

reading: Those who set their eyes on clothing and food, oil in the tube, necklace, marriage thread and bangles sink into the pit like a fluttering cloth caught on a rock.
nuance: The list is the goods of household life and of a wife's adornment, so the warning is against being taken by them. The cloth on the rock is plain enough as an image of being caught; ஆறைக் குழி (the pit, perhaps a river-pit) is unclear.

reading: On the mountain where the far shore appears within the bellows, people go three times a day to offer what they have earned; there is one woman who removes the mountain that stood within afflicting them; we do not know their town.
nuance: துருத்தி is a bellows and so the breath, and also the name of the shrine Tiruthuruthi; both may be meant. The one woman (ஒருத்தி) is taken as Shakti, who removes the inner obstacle. The three times a day may be the three breath-turns or the three daily rites.

reading: As the kite and the parrot beat the drum, well-adorned women were married; taking form like a spirit of great penance, they rejoice in the fortune they gained.
nuance: A wedding with birds for drummers. The kite and parrot may be two breaths or two powers, and the marriage a union in yoga; பூதம் may mean the elements rather than a goblin. Very uncertain.

reading: What is it like when a flocking bird pecks its food and, entering into it, cuts off its food? For those who know the way of the lamp, which drinks ghee thrown on the heat and spits out soot, the fruit is easy.
nuance: The second half describes a lamp: it takes in ghee and gives off black soot (மை) while giving light. Tradition may read it as the yogi who takes in and burns away. The first image is obscure.

reading: No leaf, yet there is a flower; no swarm of bees here; no top, yet a root; no stalk, no cluster of flowers, yet a flower to pluck; no head to wear it; and the low-hanging branch never withers.
nuance: A plant described by what it lacks, like 2885. It is commonly read as the formless reality, or the flower of inner worship that needs no head to wear it. The unwithering branch suggests what does not perish.

reading: Seeing a banyan standing on the far shore, they praise the Naked One and take its fruit in the middle; the eminent, seeing the five sorrows, go there, and the worthy lie prostrate.
nuance: நக்கர் is Siva as the naked one, and the banyan recalls Siva as teacher under the banyan. The far shore is release, the middle perhaps the central channel. அஞ்சு துயரம் (five sorrows) are not named.

reading: By the calling river there is a hard forest two leagues long, where guarding thieves have mingled; the honest ones, chasing the guarding thieves, took back a roof that had turned back at the call.
nuance: The guarding thieves (காப்பிடு கள்ளர்) are likely the senses, which seem to guard but steal, and வெள்ளர் the pure-minded who pursue them. The roof (கூரை) may be the body. Very tentative.

reading: In a pond where kotti and water-lily bloom stand the bitter etti and neem and a sweet banana; those who will not eat jaggery and honey mixed together waste away for the etti fruit.
nuance: எட்டி is the poisonous strychnine tree. The verse does not name what the sweet and the bitter stand for; read as a riddle, the sweet may be the Lord or true knowledge and the bitter the pleasures of sense. The plain point is choosing the bitter with the sweet at hand.

reading: The female bee and the male bee, and the one who enjoyed the form of the bond under a canopy on a coloured pedestal: the last bee itself drinks, and the female bee whose eyes met it gained joy.
nuance: The pair of bees may be Shakti and Siva, or the soul and the Lord; பீடிகை (pedestal) suggests an image in worship. The syntax is unclear and the reading is a guess.

reading: Unless one drives the cows grazing in the field past its boundary, gathers them to the Lord's feet, works strongly and weighs one's strength, the heart that kills will not know the mark.
nuance: The cows may be the senses, as in 2883, or the souls (பசு in the Siddhanta sense), led past the bounds of the world to the Lord's feet. கொல்லசெய் நெஞ்சம் (the killing heart) and குறி (the mark, the goal) are unclear.

reading: A lotus bloomed in the water on a plate; a blue lily rose in the water of a deep pond; for those who can shine within the beam, a colocynth is near in the pond.
nuance: Lotus and lily are common names for centres in the body; விட்டம் (beam, crossbar, or diameter) may be the space in the head. கொம்மட்டி is a bitter gourd, so the last line may be ironic. I can't fix it.

reading: Six birds are within five, and a hundred birds sit on the topmost branch; after crossing the seven great cities that rise, one may enter the house without returning.
nuance: The seven cities are commonly taken as the six adharas and the crown, after which one reaches the home (மனை) without change or return (மாறுதல் இன்றி). The six, five and hundred are unexplained. ஐந்தக்து is a garbled form.

reading: In the well one bathes in, the round earth comes and seeps; tying it with rope and keeping it close, it becomes a light to all.
nuance: கொட்டனம், வட்டனம், கட்டனம், ஒட்டனம் rhyme across the lines and their senses are unclear. I can give only the outline.

reading: The seven encircling seas, the eight great mountain ranges, the deep sky with its fire, rain and wind, and the low wide earth: seeing their nature, if one thinks to live, it becomes a temple.
nuance: The verse may mean that the whole cosmos is the Lord's temple, or that the body, which holds these seas, mountains and elements, is. The last line (வாழ நினைக்கில் அது ஆலயம் ஆமே) is compressed, and the third line is garbled (தன்மை ய்துகண்டு).

reading: Embracing, burning the inner self, setting the furrow at the trident, they put away pride of place; after setting the staff here, the well-birds, placing their confusion here, it is the way before and after.
nuance: சூலம் (trident) and கோல் (staff) may be the central channel; burning within (அகம் சுட) suggests yogic heat. The syntax of the last two lines is unclear and I can't give a reliable reading.

reading: The drum and the marriage thread are two, and they say the crowbar is stronger than both; than all three, drum, thread and crowbar, they say the Lord's grace, his love, is stronger.
nuance: Drum and tali are the marks of a wedding; the crowbar (பாரை) may be force or effort. The closing is plain: இட்டம் (love, favour) and ஈசன் அருள் outweigh all. What the three stand for is the tradition's guess.

reading: Those who have seen a carp stay seeing; those who have seen a hare, all three are saved; one man holds the drum and the clamour, like the form a Veda has seen.
nuance: கயல் (carp) is a stock image for the eye and முயல் (hare) for the moon; these may point to inner sight and the moon of yoga. The second half is obscure.

reading: In a pond where sedge rose, the water-clover spread and clung; not as a heron lies in wait, the Lord settles there while the rock lies.
nuance: The heron waiting for fish is a stock image of feigned stillness; the Lord's stillness is said not to be that. What the pond, sedge and rock stand for is unclear.

reading: A field of three leagues and a forest of half a league: two paths lie with their boundary confused; for those who can move without confusing the boundary, passing quickly, they may enter the town.
nuance: The two paths may be the two breaths or the two ways of the world and of release; keeping their boundary clear lets one reach the town, which tradition takes as Siva's abode. The measures are unexplained.

reading: When ploughing and sowing are done together the rain does not fall; the lady of the wide earth embraces and works yet yields nothing; the one of growing matted hair goes on without fail.
nuance: The plain image is labour without rain, effort without grace. The lady of the earth may be Shakti or the body; வளர்சடையோன் is Siva. Whether the last line means he stays unmoved or passes by is unclear.

reading: The leaping tiger, even while crouching, covers twelve leagues; the tide of the cool sea that drew back flows again; the honeyed nectar wells up, and he went and surrounded the five common ones.
nuance: Twelve is the traditional measure, in finger-breadths, of the outgoing breath, so the tiger may be the breath; the welling nectar is a known yogic image. The five are probably the senses, hemmed in. These are traditional keys.

reading: A son grew by boarding a boat, going to sea, trading and giving; when his heart falters before Neeli, the father gives like a hailstone fruit.
nuance: நீலி may be the dark goddess or a deceiving woman; ஆலிப்பழம் (hailstone) melts at once. The son may be the soul trading in the sea of births, and the father the Lord. The text may be corrupt (நீலிக்கு இறையுமே).

reading: In a river three leagues long there are three banana trees, ripened in the oil-press, which bore the three impurities as fruit; and, in an obscure line, the maidens, laughing, ate the flowers and stood in the middle.
nuance: திரிமலம் (the three impurities) is named outright, so the three bananas are probably the soul's three bonds. The third line (பக்கனார் மிக்கார் படங்கினார்) is obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: An aaththi tree complete from root to crown, at whose tip is a three-headed bamboo; flag, weapon and the planets' arrows, five fives; the right-whorled conch came that way.
nuance: ஆத்தி (bauhinia) is a garland flower of Siva, and the three-headed bamboo may be the trident or the three channels. ஐஐந்து (twenty-five) may be a tattva count. I can't give a reliable reading.

reading: For the herd of little jackals lying scattered, with the pig, the snake, the cow and the monkey, after weighing them on a balance without loss, the weight is brought down to a kunri seed.
nuance: The beasts may be passions or faculties, weighed and reduced to the weight of a குன்றி seed, the smallest jeweller's weight. The reading of the beasts is a guess.

reading: There is a bud that rose budding; if its binding is loosed and it runs free, one can see it bloom; looking with attachment let go, so that that house falls to waste, it cannot be seen except by those who have loosed the bond.
nuance: கட்டுவிட்டு (loosing the bond) frames the verse: the bud opens when untied, and only the unbound see. அம்மனை பாழ்பட நோக்கினால் is unclear; it may mean seeing the house of the body or household as empty.

reading: There is green in a land watered without water, and no one can ever know it; the water that pours where the sharp rain does not fall, if you search, does not stay on high ground.
nuance: Water without rain may be the inner nectar of yoga, which greens the body; that it does not stay on the high ground may mean it must be held. Very uncertain.

reading: When the owl climbs the kurundham tree and practises its nature, at the time the world perceives delusion, a snake too speaks in the middle; he becomes both the mahout and the one of good nature.
nuance: The snake speaking in the middle may be kundalini in the central channel and the mahout the controller of the mind. குருந்தம் is also the tree under which Siva is said to have taught Manikkavasagar. I can't fix the code.

reading: The banana and the thorny soorai came and took the place, and they say the soorai is stronger than the banana; but cutting both into hard pieces, the banana takes the place and lives.
nuance: The plain image is a fruitful plant and a thorny weed competing for ground, the weed thought stronger yet the banana winning. Tradition may read them as knowledge and impurity, or good and evil deeds; the verse does not say.

reading: Splitting the land and driving out the long sea, the plump fish the hill-hunter of the field caught: light it up for all; if wanted it will not lessen, and it cooks without cost.
nuance: The images of hunter, field and fish are mixed and the syntax is unclear. அருத்தமும் இன்றி may mean without cost or without meaning. I can give only a tentative outline.

reading: In the goldsmith's house there is a child that sprouts and a conch that calls, seeking the king's bed; to the potters who rejoice and the titled men, it gives a measure, to those who examine and take it.
nuance: The goldsmith's house recurs from 2876; the calling conch may be inner sound. The rest is obscure.

reading: The temple buffalo left the canopy and came out; seeing the army, it turned back halfway; the owner, the minister and the townsfolk: the long gates that cannot be shut are five and four.
nuance: Five and four are nine, the body's nine openings, which tradition calls its gates; the town is then the body, its owner the soul and its minister the mind. The buffalo may be the mind or death. Tentative.

reading: Eight that go out and eighteen that come in made the nine gates; the snake with the eight and the four horses: if the mahout does not let go, it may even become a pig.
nuance: The going and coming numbers suggest breath measures, and the nine gates the body's openings, as in 2925. பத்தெட்டு may be eighteen or ten and eight. The last line seems to warn of a low birth; I can't be sure.

reading: In a pond overgrown with moss, a shy heron seeks its food and eats; when the warrior of the vanguard reaches it with his companion, the bond lies there trembling.
nuance: The heron fishing in a mossy pond may be the soul feeding in the world, and the vanguard warrior death, at whose coming the bond (பாசம்) trembles. பாசம் is also Yama's noose. Tentative; பாடர்ந்து is a misprint for படர்ந்து.

reading: On the pot-mountain a branch has risen, and beyond the branch a wind blows; within a flower that bloomed freshly, Isan lies as a bee and takes its fragrance.
nuance: கும்பம் (pot) may be the head, or கும்பகம், the held breath; the wind beyond is the breath and the flower a centre in the head. The last line is plain: the Lord dwells as a bee in the flower. பூவக்குள் is a misprint for பூவுக்குள்.

reading: The vina and its staff mingle and hum music, and the pillar too joined and filled the head; before the trade was settled, the holding there is mixed in.
nuance: The vina's staff (தண்டு) is a known image for the spine, and its music for inner sound; தாணு (the pillar) is a name of Siva. The trade and holding in the last two lines are unclear.

reading: It traded with those who entered Kongu; none examine and know it except when it enters the ship; they did not know that when the moon enters it becomes dark; some who entered and stayed are ascetics.
nuance: திங்கள் (the moon) entering and darkness following may refer to the moon-breath or a phase of breath control. கொங்கு and வங்கு (Kongu or pollen; ship) are puns I can't resolve.

reading: Dawn broke and turned golden; the two banks where punnai trees open their pollen shimmer; this is the path where the flawless Isan moves, the circle where the lady dwells.
nuance: The two banks may be the two side channels with the path between them the central one, and the மண்டலம் where the lady dwells a centre of Shakti. The first line reads புலர்fந்தது, a corruption of புலர்ந்தது.

reading: The people who sit with their king, desiring among themselves, set things within and bear at the door; the guide who does not leave the deathless boundary shows the way, and at our rebuke the five may be eaten.
nuance: The king and people may be the soul and its faculties, the guide the guru, and the five the senses brought under rebuke. ஐந்துண்ணலாம் is unclear: the five may be enjoyed, or consumed. Very tentative.

reading: When the mango in the garden has been dug out and fallen, what will calling the jackal on the edge of the land do? That is how those who kindled it, set the First One before them and showed it, let it go.
nuance: காட்டிக் கொடுத்தல் is to betray or to point out; கைவிடுதல் to abandon. The verse may speak of those who showed the Lord and then forsook him, or of a teacher who shows and lets go. I can't settle it.

reading: Birds cry out that dawn has come and the flowering creeper clings saying dawn has come; for the lonely man who enjoys pleasure with her in his longing, dawn has never broken.
nuance: புலர்ந்தது போது (dawn has come) is repeated, and the last line denies it: புலர்ந்திலை போதே. Read as a riddle, dawn is awakening, which the pleasure-taker never meets. புலம்பன் is also the Sangam name for the hero of the seashore, so the verse borrows the love-poetry frame.

reading: There is a boat to be let out at the ferry; with the woman standing pressing it and the five planting their poles, for traders on the way in the river, if the pin is shaken, this becomes that.
nuance: The boat is commonly the body, the five the senses who pole it, and the ஆணி (pin, linchpin) what holds it together. வாணி may be the goddess of speech or a woman. The last phrase (அது இது வாமே) is open: the boat may become something else, or the world be lost.

title: மோன சமாதி
theme: Silent samadhi (மோன சமாதி): the state beyond posture, speech and the grades of the Lord's forms, given only by the guru and known only by having it, as a taste is known by eating or a wife's joy by the wife; in it self, mind and the knower dissolve, and the one who stands united sees the Supreme and the ages.
structure_note: Opening verses set the state beyond posture and book learning (2936, 2937); a run describes the Lord met there beyond turiya and beyond every named form (2939 to 2943); three verses argue that the experience can't be told, by the images of marriage and the bitter fruit (2944 to 2946, with 2950); the chapter ends in first-person dissolution and union (2951 to 2953).

reading: For those who have gone on there is no saying that they stood, sat or lay: their mind is silent samadhi; there is one hidden thing that dwells in the hall, and this is how those who went there and drew near join it.
nuance: The first line denies the postures of the body: the state isn't a matter of how one sits. மன்று (the hall) is traditionally Siva's dance-hall at Chidambaram, taken also as the inner space; மறைப்பொருள் is a hidden or secret thing, or the meaning of the Veda (மறை).

reading: What use is it to write down on the outside of a palm leaf that cause which lies beyond every sign that points and every mark? Unless guru Nandi joins one to it, it is like the hanging teat on a goat's neck.
nuance: ஏட்டின் புறத்தில் is book learning, writing on the leaf's surface. The goat's-neck image, ஆட்டின் கழுத்தில் அதர், is usually taken as the fleshy tags under a goat's throat, which look like teats and give no milk: knowledge on the page looks like the real thing and feeds no one. அதர் for these tags is the traditional gloss.

reading: To those who have awareness the world appears; to those who have awareness no sorrow comes; at the moment those who have awareness realised, they realised and saw.
nuance: Every line opens with உணர்வுடையார், and the last two lines turn back on themselves, perhaps to say that realising and seeing are one act. உலகமும் தோன்றும் may mean the world is seen as it is, or that a further world (Siva's) shows itself; the verse doesn't settle which.

reading: The good lord of the wondrous land, who stands as forgetting itself, the great gracious one free of birth, the glorious one, sleeps with the holy lady in an enjoyment that has no sleep.
nuance: மறப்பது வாய்நின்ற may be the Lord as concealment, one of his five acts, or as the forgetting of the world in samadhi. மாய நன்னாடன் is the lord of maya's land or of a wondrous land. The last line is a paradox, a sleep that is no sleep, the tradition's name for the yogic sleep of union.

reading: The light that shines beyond the three turiyas, and beyond the rare turiya above them as a third, swallowing and spitting out expansion and contraction, is within the experience beyond speech.
nuance: துரியம் is the fourth state of consciousness; the three turiyas are traditionally the soul's, Shakti's and Siva's, but the count in lines 1 and 2 is hard to fix. விரிவு குவிவு (spreading and drawing in) may be the world's emanation and withdrawal or the mind's going out and coming back, as in 2981. உரையில் அநுபூதி is direct experience that words don't reach.

reading: The formless one, without flesh, without any lack, without wealth, without evil, god of the gods, without equal, master of the army of goblins, the one who clings to nothing, came and entered my mind.
nuance: A string of negatives in -இலி. திருவிலி is odd in praise: it may mean he needs no fortune or ornament, or that he is without Tiru (Lakshmi), unlike Vishnu. மருவிலி may be 'without attachment' or 'without mixture'. The ending turns the list of absences into a personal arrival.

reading: No one has seen and known Nandi who is in the body, yet those of the eight directions praise him as the Lord; we do not know the ford where his servants scooped up the measureless bliss beyond the worlds.
nuance: துறை is a bathing ghat or landing place, the way down to the water; முகந்த is scooping water in the hands. The speaker includes himself among those who don't know, perhaps in modesty, perhaps to say the way can't be shown.

reading: He is not the Supreme, not Sadasiva, not the formless, not the state with form; becoming a wonder, like the desire of lovers in their enjoyment, he stands mingled without imagining.
nuance: தற்பரம், சதாசிவன், நிட்களம் and சகளம் are the Siddhanta names for the grades of the Lord's being, formless to embodied; the verse denies each. அனுபோகக் காமம் போல் compares union to sexual joy known only in the act, an image the chapter repeats in 2944 and 2950. கற்பனை இன்றி may mean without mental construction on the knower's side.

reading: Fools see with the eyes in their faces; seeing with the eye within is bliss; if a daughter says 'tell me', how can a mother tell her the joy she had with her husband?
nuance: The marriage image makes the claim concrete: the bliss is real and private, and the one who has it can't hand it on in words, as the next verse but one also argues.

reading: The Father joining like salt in water, leaving both the Parapara that is spoken of and the Supreme one reaches, the clinging word and its state dissolving in that mingling: as it is, so it is, that is the way.
nuance: Salt dissolved in water is the classic image of union without remainder. பராபரம் and பரம் are grades of the Supreme. கப்புறு is obscure, perhaps 'branching' or 'clinging'; சொற்பதம் may be word and meaning or the levels of speech. எப்படி அப்படி, 'how, so', gives up description.

reading: The nux vomica fruit is lovely to those who look at it, but its taste is known to those who eat it; when a girl has come to full womanhood and is a young wife, the man who took her knows her many qualities.
nuance: காஞ்சிரம் is the strychnine tree, whose fruit is handsome and bitter. Both images say the same thing, that only the one who has it knows a thing's nature; the chapter applies this to samadhi. The first image may also warn that a pleasing look deceives.

reading: Nandi sat in the middle street, and the junctions and the samadhis ceased of themselves; I joined, with my understanding, the light that rises and springs up within the navel.
nuance: நடுவுத் தெரு is traditionally the central channel of the yogic body (sushumna); சந்தி may be the junctions of the breaths or of the day kept in sandhya worship. உந்தி (the navel) is a seat of fire in the body. The plain sense is that, once the Lord is at the centre, rites and practised samadhis fall away.

reading: Staying apart without being shaken and examining, studying the ancient Veda without haste, he subsides into the void that shook off that imagining which passed beyond the void that cried out.
nuance: கதறிய பாழ் (the void that cried out) and உதறிய பாழ் (the void that shook off) are obscure; they may be grades of the three voids of earlier chapters. The subject of ஒடுங்குகின்றான் may be the seeker or the Lord.

reading: The red feet adorned with unfading flowers, which the gods do not reach: for those on the path of dharma to rejoice day by day, going within the bright flame in the full lotus, the nectar flows for those who seek, and it is the nectar the seekers seek.
nuance: நாடார் can be 'those who seek' or 'those who do not seek', and the last line plays on both; it could also say the nectar is not for those who don't seek. சேடார் கமலம், the lotus full of petals, is traditionally a centre of the yogic body, often the crown. வானவர் கூடார் may also be read as the gods who gather.

reading: As desire shows itself suddenly even on hearing the words of two who sat together for that purpose, so the Lord with the honeyed konrai garland gives his wealth, then and there, to look upon those who have suddenly made themselves ready apart.
nuance: பொதுக்கென and சதுக்கென are sound-words for suddenness. The comparison is again sexual: desire is kindled at once by hearing of it, and grace comes as fast. அன்றே may be 'that very day' or an emphatic ending.

reading: Self destroyed, wealth destroyed, the long-lasting flesh destroyed, life destroyed with it, the sky destroyed and the mind destroyed, I do not know that I too was destroyed.
nuance: The list runs from outer to inner and ends in a paradox: the one who would know of his own undoing is gone. தான் and நான் may be distinguished, the self as agent and the knower. வான் may be the element space or the heavens.

reading: Turning away both darkness and the open light, becoming the thing within the thing and fitted within, I stood with a stone-like mind that no longer rolls, joined to the feet of the Father by whose grace things are undone.
nuance: இருளும் வெளியும் may be ignorance and knowledge, or the states of the soul alone and in the body. உருளாத கன்மனம் can be a mind fixed and steady, or the hard heart that would not melt, offered in humility. What அருளால் அழிந்திடும் destroys isn't said.

reading: Standing united, I knew the Parapara within; standing united, I knew the way of Siva within; standing united, I knew awareness itself within; standing united, I have seen many ages.
nuance: ஒன்றிநின்று (standing as one) opens every line. பல ஊழி கண்டேன் may be the timelessness of the state, or, in tradition, Tirumular's own long life in yoga.

title: வரையுரை மாட்சி
theme: The worth of speech about the limitless (வரையுரை மாட்சி): once one has lost one's limits and become the Lord, there is nothing left to bound, think of or choose; those who talk of the unspeakable are mutes, while the Lord is plain to a mind as clear as still water, and the truth is to rest in examining oneself once the mind's maya dies.
structure_note: Three verses: questions to those who would describe the state (2954), the mutes who talk of it against the still mind (2955), and the mind's maya, whose ending is the truth (2956). The title's sense is uncertain: வரை can be limit, and also choosing in marriage.

reading: Once one's own limits are gone, whom is there to limit? Once one has become He, whom is there to think of? Whom does the eye that conquered Kama favour? Tell me that word, you of pure speech.
nuance: வரைவு is limit or bounding, and in love poetry also the choosing of a bride, so the first line may also ask 'whom is there to wed?' The eye that conquered Kama is Siva's third eye, which burned the god of love, or the jnani's eye that has mastered desire. The closing line is likely ironic, addressed to those who think the state can be spoken.

reading: You mutes who speak of the one that is beyond speech, can the shore of what has no shore be seen? To those whose thought grows clear like water without waves, the one with twisted matted hair stays without any veil.
nuance: The talkers are called mutes because their words reach nothing. புரையற்று can mean without fault or without any hiding place; with the image of clear, still water, being seen plainly fits better.

reading: The mind's maya is maya, and this maya is delusion; when the mind's maya itself dies there is nothing else, nothing dies after that, and no need to babble: to remain having examined oneself is the truth.
nuance: தத்துவம் here likely means the real or the truth rather than one of the thirty-six tattvas, though the technical sense may also be heard. பிதற்றவும் வேண்டா echoes the previous verse's mutes.

title: அணைந்தோர் தன்மை
theme: The nature of those who have reached (அணைந்தோர் தன்மை): told mostly in the first person, they are free of stain, pride, caste and bonds; the Lord has entered and ruled them, birth and karma are cut, Yama can be fought off, worldly sweetness turns sour beside his bliss, and the mind's spreading and drawing in, stilled with speech, is release.
structure_note: Verses in the first person of one who has reached alternate with descriptions of such people (2957, 2969, 2970). Several verses chain by repeated words (பணிந்துநின்றேன், பிணக்கறுத்தான்). The last verse (2981) sums the mind's movement as tapas, breath and life, and its end as mukti.
source_issues: 2978: line 2 reads விளக்கிக் தகளிசெய், where the doubled க் before த looks like a misprint (perhaps விளக்குத் தகளி or விளக்கித் தகளி).
2969: line 3, சுத்தும் சிலகும், is obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: For those who by knowledge set Nandi firmly in love, holding steady, there is no impurity, no stain, no pride or self-regard, no caste, no qualities to take on, no good to seek.
nuance: குலமில்லை denies caste or lineage to the one who has reached. நலமில்லை is surprising after a list of faults; it may mean no worldly good is needed, or that such a one is past good and bad alike. பலமன்னி is obscure, perhaps 'abiding in strength' or 'with the fruit secured'.

reading: I have left birth and the bond called kinship; I am free; God and I have become one; I want no more gain that comes and perishes; I have seen Siva, the rich refuge.
nuance: உறவு என்னும் பாசம் makes kinship itself a bond. கடவுளும் நானும் ஒன்றானேன் is a plain statement of union, though how 'one' is meant (identity or inseparability) is the long dispute between Vedanta and Siddhanta, which the verse doesn't enter.

reading: Our land has cane in the mill, nectar, sugar and the cool water of groves; the lovely woman who makes a form like the eye of a peacock's feather lacks for nothing.
nuance: The verse reads at first as praise of a fertile land and a fortunate woman. In this chapter it is likely symbolic: the land as the body or the state reached, its sweets and waters as bliss and nectar, the woman as Shakti or the soul. பீலிக்கண் (the eye of a peacock feather) is sometimes taken as a light seen in meditation. None of this can be fixed from the verse.

reading: From now no one can harm me; the glorious Lord came and entered my mind; I have come to know the knowledge in which, apart from wandering there in joy, I go near no one now.
nuance: Lines 3 and 4 are hard: சீராடி may be playing like a cherished child, and யார்படும் சாரா may be 'not approaching anyone' or 'what no one reaches'.

reading: I have parted from the bond that Brahma tied; I have learned the state that goes on the way of Siva; I have cut down karma with the sharp sword of the mind; I have broken the city and press on ahead.
nuance: Brahma's bond is birth into a body. புரம் (the city) may be the body, or may echo Siva's burning of the three cities, taken as the three malas. அயில் மன வாள் (the sharp sword of mind) parallels the sword of knowledge in 2968.

reading: See, there is one God for the world; see, the one is what is life to the world; see that it is good: now, having eaten the fruit நமசிவாய, how sweet it has been to me!
nuance: Each line opens with a call to 'see' (கண்டீர்) and the last turns to the speaker's own tasting (கண்டேற்கு). The five-letter mantra as a fruit makes knowing it a matter of taste, as in 2946.

reading: The one with matted hair who wears the moon with the snake came and ruled me and became a jewel-lamp, the rare thing with neither end nor beginning; he settled in my mind and cut away my confusion.

No one knows the purpose of the Lord who was within us of old, who stays there seeing tall Mal and Brahma; if he breaks forth and appears there and the mind becomes empty, what stood there as a fragment becomes a mere thicket.
nuance: The verse is obscure. One reading takes Vishnu and Brahma as lesser lords the inner Lord oversees, and the last line as saying that, to a mind emptied, the separate gods are as worthless as scrub. விண்டு may be 'splitting open' or a form of Vishnu's name.

reading: Apart from the love that Mother and Father bore, who knows Mother and Father, and who knows me? With Mother and Father and me together, I came to serve the Mother and the Father.
nuance: Mother and Father are traditionally Shakti and Siva. என்னை may be 'me' or 'what'. புரிந்தேன் can be served, desired or understood, so the last line may also say the speaker came to understand them.

reading: The whorl it took, the summit of the great mountain, the gods, the lord of the gods, the First and those of the eight directions came and are in the palm of my hand; now I am saved and done.
nuance: கொண்ட சுழி may be the coil of kundalini or the crown's whorl, and குலவரை உச்சி the summit of Meru, often taken as the top of the head in yogic reading. The whole cosmos held in the hand is a claim to mastery, or to the cosmos being found within. உண்டனர் is read as 'they are there'; it could also be 'they ate'.

reading: He himself stands as the directions and the gods; he himself stands as the northern mountain and the origin; he himself stands as body, life and tattvas; he himself is also the Lord in the world.
nuance: தானே may be the Lord, as in many such lists, or, in this chapter, the one who has reached and become all, following 2966. The verse doesn't say which.

reading: If Yama comes I will strike him with the sword of knowledge; if Siva comes, it is sure I will go with him; I cut long ago the strong karma that brings birth; who can stand against a mind into which tapas has come?
nuance: The two comings set death and Siva side by side: one is driven off, the other followed. பவம் is birth or worldly becoming.

reading: Those whose minds have become Siva and who have destroyed the three malas become pure Siva and do not touch the bondage of malam; they see no turning, no wavering, no strife, holding that sound and the supreme bindu are themselves.
nuance: The three malas are traditionally anava, karma and maya. சுத்தும் சிலகும் is obscure and may be corrupt. The last line may say that nada and parabindu are themselves, or that they are He; either way it places these states within, not as things to reach.

reading: In the heart of those without thinking and forgetting dwells the Pure One who cuts away karma's clinging; if one goes seeking that Pure One and gets to think of him, he becomes far off.
nuance: The paradox: he dwells where neither thinking nor forgetting is, so to think of him is to set him at a distance. நீளியன் may instead mean 'vast' or 'great', which would make the last line praise rather than warning.

reading: When I called and praised him as Siva Peruman, he came and stood as the Lord of tapas; the Lord of undoing, the master who owns me: I stood bowing to the Lord of becoming.
nuance: The verse plays on names: சிவ, தவ, அவ and பவ before பெருமான். பவன் (Bhava) is a name of Siva; அவ may be 'the destroyer', from அவம் (undoing), though its sense is unsure.

reading: I stood bowing to the Lord, first and supreme; I stood resolved, wanting nothing else from now; I stood having put on the primal Lord as my body; I stood calmed, having seen the nature of Siva.
nuance: Each line opens a stance with நின்றேன். அணிந்து நின்றேன் உடல் ஆதிப்பிரானை may be wearing the Lord as one's body (taking his form), or adorning the body with him, as with ash and emblems.

reading: When my heart joined the Lord's two feet and I praised him beforehand, birth was cut away entirely; the Lord, who has no mind of his own, broke up the fate written for me and ended my discord.
nuance: தலைவிதி is fate, the writing on the head. தன் நெஞ்சம் இல்லாத் தலைவன் is obscure: the Lord beyond mind, or one without self-interest. பிணக்கு can be discord, entanglement or the strife of rival creeds.

reading: Nandi ended my discord, cut away disease, old age and the reckoning that is counted, and ruled me; when he ended my discord and the sorrow that had come along with me from before, I fell to bowing: it was Siva who had come.
nuance: The verse picks up பிணக்கறுத்தான் from 2973. எண்ணும் கணக்கு may be the counting of one's days or the account of karma; முன்வந்த துன்பம் (sorrow come with me from before) is likely the karma of past births.

reading: Siva came with the throng of gods, cut off the bond that stood so that birth would come, and he, my Father, the First Lord who ruled and graced me, came and was caught within me.
nuance: அகப்பட்டவாறு (how he got caught) turns the usual picture round: the soul seized by the Lord here holds the Lord.

reading: In a body where cane and honey are mixed, the bliss that is bud and fragrance: once the heart, longing, saw it laid open, the cane turned bitter and the honey sour.
nuance: Cane and honey are first the body's sweet pleasures, then spoiled by the greater bliss. வெளியுற may be 'openly' or 'in the inner space'. The verse sets Siva's bliss against worldly pleasure, as the concept's gloss has it, rather than condemning the body.

reading: Having followed chariyai and the rest and then turned back, singing the riches the Generous One set in me in his love, since I see all that is done as Siva, I have passed beyond the womb with nothing in my hands.
nuance: Chariyai and the rest are the four Saiva paths. மீட்டு may mean turning back from them or being brought back. கைவளம் இன்றி may be 'without any wealth in hand' (without merit of my own) or 'without the skill of my hands'.

reading: When, turned back, the fire went deep into the lotus and was set in the bowl as a lamp that needs no trimming, one woman, crown-jewel of the worlds, took it on, and it came into the hand of a man who had died.
nuance: Very obscure. The lamp that needs no trimming (தூண்டா விளக்கு) is a common image of the self-lit inner light; the lotus is a centre of the yogic body; the woman is likely Shakti; the man who died may be the one who has died to self. Any fuller reading would be invented.

reading: There is a river, a waterfall and a tank within; Siva's way is fine, and so is its colour; the excellent thing is a share with the lady slender as a creeper, with rounded breasts, and also stays apart.
nuance: ஆறு may be river or six, the six centres of the yogic body; the waterfall and inner tank are likely the nectar's flow. நூறே may be 'fine as powder' or 'a hundred'. The last lines give Siva as half of the Goddess and yet distinct, the Siddhanta position.

reading: Melting in love I weep and cry out; with my very bones melting I praise him night and day; my golden gem, the Lord, Isa: I will eat him, bite him, and he sets me right.
nuance: The eating and biting are a devotee's hunger for the Lord, as in 2962's fruit. திருத்துவன் may be the Lord correcting the devotee or the devotee savouring him; the subject is unclear.

reading: The mind spread out and drew in: that is great tapas; the mind spread out and drew in: that is the breath; the mind spread out and drew in: that is the abiding soul; the mind that spread out, and speech, died: that is mukti.
nuance: The same movement is named three ways, as tapas, breath and life, and the fourth line ends it. மாதவம் is read as மா தவம், great tapas. The link of mind and breath echoes earlier yogic chapters, where where the mind goes the breath goes.

title: தோத்திரம்
theme: Praise (தோத்திரம்): the Lord pervades the elements, the lights, the worlds and souls, is great beyond the gods' measure and small within the flesh, yet is found within the body and in his devotees' hearts; his feet are every heaven, and naming and praising him cut away deeds, desire and the sea of births.
structure_note: Devotional verses of the speaker's own seeking and finding (2982 to 2999), with a short linked chain in which each verse begins with the last word of the one before (2992 to 2995), then a run of verses on the Lord's pervasion of elements, lights and worlds and his being beyond them (3000 to 3024), ending with a riddle verse (3025).
source_issues: 2999 line 2 (தானிடர் மானுடர் கீழது மாதுஅனங் கானது) is broken in its word division and may be corrupt.
2998 line 4 (பதியது வவ்விட்டது அந்தமும் ஆமே) and 3025 (பிண்டாலம், குண்டாலம், குதிரை) are obscure and may be corrupt.
2982 line 4 (காயம்மின்) and 3001 line 1 (ஒத்ததஉயர், with a doubled syllable) look misdivided or misprinted.

reading: Those who drove the long chariot of the mind in search of the elusive one went off without knowing the land and lament; I, having wandered through countries and lands, found our treasured Lord within the land of the body.
nuance: மாயன் is usually Vishnu, but here may simply mean the elusive one whom seekers chase. காயம் (body) is the key word: the search outward fails and the find is within. காயம்மின் is odd; it may be காயம் with an emphatic or a misdivided word, and some take மின் as the flash of light seen within.

reading: If you ask who sat on the mountain-like rutting elephant while sweet music was sung, know from the songs that they were those who had recited the name of the First One of the time before.
nuance: The verse promises honour, pictured as a royal elephant ride with music, to those who repeat the Lord's name. Later tradition might see Sundarar's ride to Kailasa on a white elephant here, but that would make the verse later than Tirumular is usually placed; read it as a general image.

reading: They say of me, crying out because I cannot see the Father, the pearl of pearls, the young budding sun, the Lord whom all the gods praise: 'this one is a madman'.
nuance: பித்தன் (madman) is also a name of Siva himself, so the devotee mocked as mad shares a name with the Lord he longs for. The verse turns on longing for one not seen (காணாது அரற்றுகின்றேன்).

reading: Our holy form has entered and stays; our knower who knows has entered and stays; he has entered and stays in the hearts of his devotees; it is the one who entered and stays that I praise.
nuance: புகுந்துநின்றான் (entered and stays) opens every line. போதறிவாளன் may mean the one who knows the right time, or the one whose knowledge is pure awareness.

reading: He has not entered the mirror of the elements, yet he is there in awareness; in the mirror of the Veda he appears otherwise; in the mirror of justice he is in the minds of those who think of him; in the mirror of song I heard him and stood.
nuance: கண்ணாடி (mirror) structures the verse: the elements do not reflect him, the Veda shows him in a different form, right conduct and thought hold him, and song lets him be heard. போதுளன் may mean 'he is in awareness' or 'he is in the flower' (of the heart); both are traditional.

reading: Recite the Lord's thousand names and you will be held within a thousand protections; those who can perform a thousand fire offerings have seen their thousand desires and are done with them.
nuance: ஏமம் is protection or delight. கண்டொழிந்தார் can mean they saw their desires through and were done with them, or that they saw desire and left it; the plain promise is release from desire by naming and offering.

reading: I praise, and praising I make known the renowned knowledge; I make sure the red feet of the Lord of the mind; I proclaim Siva-yoga, hear it; I praise, calling him our Lord.
nuance: அறையோ is a call for attention, as a crier's or a challenge's. The four verbs (போற்று, தேற்று, சாற்று, போற்று) frame the work as a teacher's proclamation as well as a devotee's praise.

reading: Seek Nandi in many ways: passing through the lotus of the flesh and beyond it, coming back after the heavenly world has worshipped, you may drink honey to your fill and be sated.
nuance: ஊனார் கமலம் (lotus of the flesh) is traditionally a centre of the yogic body and தேன் (honey) the nectar the yogi tastes. A plain devotional reading also stands: seek him by every means and the sweetness comes.

reading: The rare treasure has come and stands for his devotees; even if Indra and the other gods ask for him, he is beyond the sky of space, and they get nothing but the sound of beautiful women.
nuance: The contrast is between devotees, to whom he comes, and the gods, whose pleasures (the clamour, துழனி, of heavenly women) are all they have. The construction of line 3 is loose and the reading is a guess.

reading: Like water muddied by earth, people muddied in their thoughts do not say 'this is the Lord'; Siva is the one who scoops from the pond within, sets the mud to one side, and makes the water clear.
nuance: The image is of clearing muddy water: the mind is the pond, and the Lord does the settling. உண்ணிற் குளம் (the pond within) is read as the inner mind; the phrasing of line 3 is compressed.

reading: To one who longs for the one of true penance he is like a gooseberry come into the palm; seeking the pure one, the Father of the gods who stood as the pure way, I have settled and come to rest.
nuance: கைத்தலம் சேர் நெல்லிக்கனி (a gooseberry in the hand) is proverbial for what is plainly seen and surely held. அமைந்தொழிந்தேன் (I settled and ceased) opens the chain of linked verses that follows.

reading: I have settled; I have been made complete in a knowledge of measureless renown; there is no wavering at all; the holy one, coming near the smoking earth, is the bountiful one who apportions and gives.
nuance: தடுமாற்றம் ஒன்றில்லை (no wavering) states the settled state. புகைந்தெழும் பூதலம் (the earth rising in smoke) is obscure: it may be the earth as the burning ground, or the world of distress.

reading: The bountiful chief, lord of the good heavenly land, first of the Veda with flood-water in his matted hair, wondering whether the deceitful will see him, hides within the heart and rules there.
nuance: கள்ளப் பெருமக்கள் (deceitful folk) are those with hidden guile; the Lord hides from them, yet rules from within the heart. The verse may also play on the Lord as himself the hidden thief of hearts.

reading: Those who worship daily the God who gave his ruling flower-feet stand in goodness; I have laid with my mind the sword of the lord who cuts away the planets and deeds.
nuance: கோள் (the planets, their bad influence) and வினை (deeds) are what the Lord cuts. வாளும் மனத்தொடும் வைத்தொழிந்தேன் can mean that I set his sword in my mind, or that I laid down my sword and my mind before him in surrender.

reading: For those who can praise his feet with effort: if they desire it, his feet are the heroes' heaven; if they join them, the world of merit; if they are reformed, the holy water too.
nuance: The feet stand in for every reward promised elsewhere: the heaven of warriors fallen in battle, the world earned by merit, and the bathing places that wash away sin. வருந்தி (with effort, with longing) qualifies the praise.

reading: He who cut through the heavens is in this world a solitary teacher with no house of his own; I have held to the light, sweet as a drink, that comes within as one eats the forest plantain fruit.
nuance: போதகன் (teacher) and தானகம் இல்லா (with no dwelling of his own) suggest the Lord as a wandering teacher. கானக வாழைக்கனி and பானகச் சோதி (a light like a sweet drink) are images of sweetness taken within; their exact reference is not clear.

reading: That is the destiny where the gods above dwell; that is the place where the flowing Ganga is; that praise removes the clinging of old deeds; that place, having seized them, is also the end.
nuance: பதி may be a holy place (some think of Kasi on the Ganga) or the Lord himself, which the word also means in Siddhanta. Line 4 (வவ்விட்டது அந்தமும்) is obscure.

reading: Above are the gods, below the great ascetics, below them humans in distress; the one whose fragrant matted hair wears the bilva garland does all this and is my dear life.
nuance: Line 2 (மாதுஅனங் கானது) is broken and could not be read; the ranking of beings above and below is the plain outline. The last line makes the Lord the life of the speaker's life.

reading: He whose throat swallowed the poison of the encircling dark sea is the Lord unborn in the seven and the two; he is there in the lute, the spring and the forest, and is also the king who lives in the seven and five.
nuance: ஏழும் இரண்டும் and எழுந்தைந்து are counts (seven and two; seven and five) whose referents, worlds or regions or tattvas, the verse does not fix.

reading: The First Lord is like the world and the earth, like the high wind, like the fire of spreading rays, like the water of the great clouds, and like their passing away again: he is the lord of the gods of the directions.
nuance: The list runs through the elements: earth, wind, fire and water, with செலவு (going) perhaps standing for space or for dissolution. ஒத்து (being like) is weaker than 'being': the verse compares rather than identifies.

reading: Knowing the right manner, he is there as fire and sun; knowing it, he is there as the Lord in the wind; knowing it, as the great moon; and knowing the manner of knowledge, that is how he spreads that land.
nuance: பரிசறிந்து (knowing the manner) opens each line. The last line is compressed; பாரிக்கும் may mean spreads out or sustains.
