reading: Even beyond the end he stands as each thing that is; in the bound world he is the great treasure of those below; the Supreme himself pervades all the worlds he gave: this is the glory of his coming to create.
nuance: பந்த உலகு (the bound world) and கீழோர் (those below) suggest bound souls, for whom he is the treasure. அதுஅதுவாய் நிற்கும் (stands as each thing) is a phrase of pervasion that Siddhanta reads as indwelling rather than identity.

reading: Though the three eggs and the two eggs are his crown, the Father's form is said to be the seven worlds, and his red feet reach as far as the underworld; the intoxicated do not know this and rejoice in it.
nuance: முத்தண்ண ஈரண்டம் (three and two world-eggs) is a cosmological count that cannot be fixed here. மத்தர் (the intoxicated, the deluded) are those who miss the cosmic form.

reading: The First Lord, our Lord, Lord of light of the wide world, stands as the light of the three lights; the First Lord is beyond the cosmos and below it; the First Lord stands in the middle.
nuance: சுடர் மூன்று (the three lights) are traditionally sun, moon and fire. ஆதிப்பிரான் (the First Lord) opens three of the four lines.

reading: He is great, rising high beyond the cosmos, and small in a birth beyond the body; each time his servants see the ringing anklet that walked, he stands as the pure way, hanging there for them.
nuance: The pairing of பெருமையன் and சிறுமையன் (great and small) is the point, as in 3024. பிண்டம் கடந்த பிறவிச் சிறுமையன் and தூங்கிநின்றான் (stood hanging, or stood intent) are hard to fix.

reading: The Lord, whose roving gaze is ringed by the great sea, has filled the whole land; he first created all its strength, and stands as the whole field of the senses in golden colour.
nuance: உலவுசெய் நோக்கம் (the roaming gaze) and புலம் (the field, or the senses) are uncertain; பலம் may be fruit or strength.

reading: As the supreme and the lower through many aeons, as the Supreme bearing this wide world, people do not grasp how he stood as bearer of the earth; he stands full as one who needs no support.
nuance: The verse plays on -பரன்: பராபரன் (supreme and lower), தராபரன் (bearer of the earth) and நிராபரன் (without support, or without ornament).

reading: The great god who is praised is he alone, there is no other; he is the force and the sound and the subsiding of sound; he is always the body that is other too; that is the great god; the Lord stands mingled as the breath.
nuance: ஓசை ஒடுக்கம் (the subsiding of sound) may point to the resolution of nada in yoga. வேற்றுடல் (the other body) is obscure. காற்று (wind, breath) is taken as the life-breath.

reading: If all the directions are Siva, he alone, there is no need, men, to say anything more; as all smoke gathers outside in fire, all buds are our First Lord.
nuance: The image of smoke and fire in line 3 is unclear: it may mean that every rising thing goes back to its source in the Lord. முகை (bud) may stand for all that is yet to unfold.

reading: He spread out, the seven wide worlds becoming one; he stands so that one may say 'this is he' and yet is not easily had; Siva himself, becoming many, many souls, is also the trusted one who spoke and lives in the world.
nuance: சிவன்தான் பலபல சீவனுமாகி (Siva himself becoming many souls) sounds like identity of the Lord and souls. Siddhanta tradition takes such lines as his pervading souls without being one with them; both readings stand on the words.

reading: Seek the chief who stands beyond the three kalas, the lord of the tattvas; he has no price; even speaking with the gods there are no words for him; he is the one who dwells within.
nuance: கலை ஒரு மூன்றும் (the three kalas) may be the kalas of sun, moon and fire or three of the five kalas of Siddhanta cosmology; the verse does not say.

reading: Cutting the bond made by Brahma of the earth, cutting the attachment to smallness made by the tall one, removing the deeds done in thicket-like penance, he saved me his servant and took me in love.
nuance: நெடியான் (the tall one) is Vishnu; Brahma's bond is taken as birth and Vishnu's as attachment to sustained life. செடியார் தவம் (penance thick as a thicket) may be austerities that themselves bind; the verse says the Lord removes even these.

reading: The eight directions moved crying 'Lord'; the unfailing one rises as sound from sound; there one land and its nine rich regions: he dwells in them as fragrance in a flower.
nuance: ஓசையில் நின்றெழு சத்தம் (sound rising from sound) may refer to nada; செழுங்கண்டம் ஒன்பதும் (the nine regions) is a traditional division of the earth.

reading: Our Lord is neither non-existent nor existent; his vision splits open the good heart; ancient, pure, unshaken, a pure gem, the light beyond words, he stands, continuing.
nuance: இல்லனும் அல்லன் உளன் அல்லன் (not non-being, not being) places him beyond both categories. நெஞ்சம் பிளந்திடும் காட்சி (a vision that splits the heart) is overwhelming sight.

reading: The thief-chief called 'I', within the heart where it subsides and outside too, and Nandi of the fragrant matted hair: for those who proclaim the greatness of his bounty, he has cut through the sea of mire.
nuance: நானெனும் கள்ளத் தலைவன் (the thief-chief called I) is read as the ego. அள்ளற் கடல் (the sea of mire) is taken as the sea of births or of sin. The syntax joining the ego and Nandi in lines 1 and 2 is unclear.

reading: The gods and the asuras, opposed to each other, every day recount and seek his ringing anklet; he wells up within their hearts and outside, and, making them distinct, there becomes the light of a lamp.
nuance: வேறுசெய்து (making distinct) may mean that he separates them from their bonds or that he stands apart from them; the verse does not settle it.

reading: He is not the open space that came in the sky, yet has a form; not an object that came to the eye, yet is seen; not the fruit that came from melody, yet of its nature: our Lord is bliss beyond reckoning.
nuance: Each line denies a sensory category and then grants the Lord a likeness to it (மேனியன், காட்சியன், பான்மையன்).

reading: The highest one, the great sea that delights everywhere, of pearl's light and of blue-black, the siddhas and gods think on the Lord through all time and still do not know him fully.
nuance: தேர்ந்தறியார் (they do not know by searching) sets even the siddhas and the gods short of him.

reading: As many colours as there are, so is the Lord; as many virtues, so much joy; as many wrongs, so much sin; though people see many outward things, they do not praise him.
nuance: மறம் here is the opposite of அறம் (wrongdoing), not valour. The middle lines pair virtue with joy and wrong with sin as if to measure them one for one.

reading: He stood here, he stood there: where is he? He rose up, the lord of the worlds, the holy one; he stood in the night as the sun and the great moon; the Lord stands everywhere like rain.
nuance: The verse answers its own question (எங்குளன், where is he) with the rain, which falls on every place.

reading: What perceives is the breath, being the highest; what perceives our Lord is subtle knowledge; what joins him is breath, and is slight; he stands as perception, body and cosmos.
nuance: வாயு (breath) and நுண்ணறிவு (subtle knowledge) are both named as means of knowing; the yogic sense of breath as what reaches the Lord is traditional. புல்லியதாயும் (being slight, or clinging) is uncertain.

reading: By his own strength he bore the seven worlds; by his own strength he is lighter than the atom; by his own strength he leans on none of the eight mountains; by his own strength he is the wide sea.
nuance: தன்வலியால் (by his own strength) opens every line: nothing holds him up, while he holds all. The eight mountains are the traditional mountains at the quarters that bear the earth.

reading: Though our Lord is great beyond all others, he is there mingled within the flesh in smallness too; the great god is not of the measure the gods know; he himself knows the measure of penance.
nuance: The last line can be read as 'he alone knows how much penance is done' or 'he is known only in the measure of one's penance'.

reading: The great sprout risen from the seed of the banyan of the body: in the pot-like body the horse has ripened; the senseless fools ate it, and caught within the body they quarrel.
nuance: This is a riddle verse in the style of Tirumular's hidden-meaning songs. பிண்டாலம் (body-banyan), குண்டாலம் and குதிரை (horse, perhaps the breath or the mind) cannot be fixed; the plain sense is only that fools caught in the body consume its fruit and quarrel.

title: சர்வ வியாபி
theme: The all-pervader (சர்வ வியாபி): the Lord is the inner light in the body, the elements, the sun, the breath and the gods, spread through every direction, world and sea, near and far, many and yet one, and no one can trace his course. The chapter, and the book's last tantra, closes with a verse on Mulan's three thousand Tamil verses.
structure_note: The Lord as the light within the body and its lights (3026 to 3031); the Lord as all things, gods, directions, worlds and elements, often in refrains on அவனே and நின்றனன் (3032 to 3045); a closing verse on Mulan's work (3046). The grouping is mine. 3035 repeats 2857 and 3044 is close to 1722.
source_issues: 3035 repeats 2857 with two variants that change the sense: புணர்வும் for புணரும் and புலனும் (the senses) for புலவி (lovers' sulking).

3044 is a variant of 1722: line 1 அதுஅறி வானவன் ஆதிப் புராணன் for அது வுணர்ந் தோன்ஒரு தன்மையை நாடி, line 3 பொதுஅது வான for புதுஉணர் வான, and line 4 ends with Nandi as 'our lord' instead of the Lord taking the poet's body as his temple.
3042: line 2 reads தன்னடு ஒங்க, probably for தன்னொடு ஓங்க.
3031: line 4 is divided மற்றவ னாய்னி ன்ற, a misprint for மற்றவ னாய்நின்ற.
3026, 3029 (பல்கோரை), 3030, 3036 (விலமை) and 3041 (lines 3 and 4) are obscure and may be corrupt; 3034 line 4 (ஒழிந்திலகு) may be a misreading.

reading: This is the Siva-enjoyment that fits; apart from it, the one light and the knowing awareness, through the limiting adjunct of maya, take on what is great and what is made, and his pervasion is his own.
nuance: சிவபோகம் (the enjoyment of Siva), மாயா உபாதி and வியாபகம் are technical, and lines 3 and 4 (ஏய பரிய புரியும் தனதுஎய்தும் சாயும்) are too compressed to construe with confidence. The verse seems to say that the pervasion is the Lord's own, while its appearance as many comes through maya's adjunct; that is a reading, not the verse's plain words.

reading: There is no room to seek that reality by my own knowing, and knowing it there one swells on the way; when the bright flame that breathes within, knowing the flesh, itself knows, one can reach him there too.
nuance: The first line denies that 'I' can find him by searching; the last puts the knowing in the inner flame (ஒண்சுடர்), usually taken as the soul lit by grace, or as the Lord within. விம்மிடும் (swells, overflows) may be the swelling of joy or of weeping.

reading: In this noisy world ringed by the sea, living in the body and seeking the light within, one can see the god who dwells inside the body as plainly as the crowding waves of the sea.
nuance: கடல் frames the verse: the sea round the world in line 1 and the sea's crowding waves in line 4. Whether the waves are an image of plainness, of the Lord's countless forms, or of the restless mind through which he is seen is not fixed by the verse. கௌவை may be 'noise' or 'scandal'.

reading: The lord of the gods, who is the inner light in the three great lights and stands knowingly as the body, leaves the great flame and goes along with every place of strife, as sedge spreads far and wide.
nuance: The three great lights are traditionally sun, moon and fire. பல்கோரை (many sedges) and இகலிடம் (places of strife) are obscure; the sedge that spreads and goes with the water may picture a pervasion that reaches even the world's conflicts.

reading: Those who fell in the end, caught in the inner karma that came in with their resolve, are a wound; the divine form is the inner light in the small one, and for those who gain it the higher beings become the great flame.
nuance: Each line turns on a -தியின் form (உறுதியின், இறுதியின், சிறுதியின், பெறுதியின்) made for the rhyme, and their senses are guesses. இரணம் may be 'wound' or 'debt'. The plain contrast is between those who fall by karma and those who gain the inner light.

reading: The supreme flame, supreme within what one holds, the threefold light that ripens in all things and sprouts, gives a steady place as thought within the forehead; that is the great ascetic who stood as the other one.
nuance: நெற்றியின் உள்ளே நினைவாய் is taken by tradition as meditation fixed between the brows. மூன்றொளி is again the three lights, and மாதவன் may be 'the great ascetic' (Siva) or Mal (Vishnu); மற்றவனாய் நின்ற (who stood as the other) allows either.

reading: He is the god in each of the ten directions, the one who commands the seven worlds of wide waters, the one who comes to be, seated in every world, and as the one with the tongue he speaks.
nuance: Each line ends on a -வன் noun (தேவன், ஏவன், ஆவன், நாவன்), so the verse makes its claim by naming him in four roles; நாவனும் ஆகி நவிற்றுகின்றான் makes the Lord the speaker in all speech, and perhaps in this book.

reading: The watching Garuda and the lord of the earth who guards the seven worlds in an instant are in him; my spotless one, the unborn, removes karma, and does not join in going and coming.
nuance: Garuda is traditionally the one whose glance draws out snake poison, and the lord who guards the worlds is taken as Vishnu, whom Garuda bears. Read so, the verse sets the gods' protection beside the Lord's removal of karma; போக்கும் வரவும் (going and coming) is birth and death.

reading: The one of rich matted hair, whose body is like red gold, though withdrawn joins with everything together; the Lord is gone from nowhere and born nowhere, and stands equally with the seven shining worlds.
nuance: ஒழிந்தனனாயும் (though withdrawn, or though he has ceased) against ஒருங்குடன் கூடும் gives the paradox of the one apart who is with all. ஒழிந்திலகு in line 4 is unclear: perhaps ஒளிர்ந்திலகு (shining).

reading: He is awareness and he is life, he is union and he is the senses; though bound up with all he cannot be reached by thought, and he stays close as scent in a cluster of flowers.
nuance: A repeat of 2857 with two different words: புணர்வும் (union) for புணரும் and புலனும் (the senses) for புலவி (lovers' sulking). Here the pair is no longer love's union and quarrel but union and the senses, which fits this chapter's pervasion of all the faculties. The scent in the flower is the one image for being in all and unseen.

reading: Our father, the holy one without the scent of sense-knowledge, is in goodness the practice of the way of knowledge, and spreads everywhere in the many forms the Vedic seers speak of, keeping within.
nuance: Each line opens with a -மையின் or -மையில் form (புலமை, நலமை, விலமை, பலமை); விலமை is not an ordinary word and line 3 cannot be construed with confidence. புலமையின் நாற்றமில் may mean 'untouched by the senses' or 'not smelling of learning'.

reading: As the heavenly one he is above the seven worlds, as the earthly one he is for the seven seas that circle; as the cool one he stands in his own nature, and becoming the eye he stands mingled.
nuance: The refrain of -அவன் names (விண்ணவன், மண்ணவன், தண்ணவன், கண்ணவன்) moves from heaven to earth to his own nature to the eye that sees. தண்ணவன் (the cool one) may hint at the moon he wears, and கண்ணவன் at his being the seer within all seeing.

reading: He stood as Mal and as the four-faced one, stood as the earth below and above, stood as the tall great mountains and the seven seas, and stood as rich fruit.
nuance: நின்றனன் opens every line, the chapter's main refrain. He stands as the other gods of creation and preservation and not only above them; the last line's ripe fruit (வளம் கனி) may be the fruit of the world or the sweetness he is to those who reach him.

reading: Our father, the great holy one, is lord of the worlds; he is the mighty driver who presses on in the world, he becomes the many rare souls, and that is how people came to be bewildered into calling him alone God.
nuance: அரும்பல சீவனும் ஆகும் (he becomes the many souls) is as strong a statement of oneness as the book makes; within Siddhanta it is taken as his pervading the souls, not being them. மாலுற்றவாறே is unclear: மால் may be bewilderment, love, or Mal (Vishnu), giving 'how Mal came to call him God' or 'how love made us call him God'.

reading: He stands as the unwasting breath that shines within, as the lord of spreading rays who moves in the sky, and as the wind that moves over the earth; he is the thought that moves out from the eye.
nuance: The verse matches places to powers: within, the breath; in the sky, the sun; on earth, the wind; in the eye, thought or meaning (கருத்து). பிராணன் and வாயு are both the breath, the one inside and the one outside.

reading: The Supreme who made number and letter, the kinds of action, the music and the skill in that way: in the thought that the eye takes in, this and that, he stands within, melts one, and becomes one's company.
nuance: The first two lines make the arts of knowledge his creation. Lines 3 and 4 are obscure: அதுஇது (that, this) may be the things perceived, and ஓர் ஆயமும் ஆமே may mean he becomes a companion, a crowd, or a gain (ஆயம் as income).

reading: He who wears the holy konrai on his rich matted hair dwelt mingled everywhere, with the seed, so that the eight directions, the cosmic sphere and the underworld that exist rise up with form together with him.
nuance: கருக்கொடு (with the embryo or seed) suggests that he is in things as their seed, as in the bindu chapter, but the verse doesn't say so. Line 2 (உருக்கொடு தன்னடு ஓங்க) reads தன்னடு, probably for தன்னொடு.

reading: No one knows the course of the Lord through the whole world that has gone along with many things; he is far and near, the unwavering Sankara, the first, our first, skilled in standing as the one that is not many.
nuance: சேயன் அணியன் (far one, near one) is a common pairing in Saiva hymns. பலவிலதாய் நிற்கும் closes the verse that opened with பலவுடன்: present with many things, he stays not-many.

reading: He who is that knowledge is the primal ancient one; the Lord stood so that nothing could know him; Nandi, who knows this, is our lord, and he is the eight worlds common to all.
nuance: Close to 1722: lines 2 and 3 share most words, but 1722 ends with the Lord taking the poet's body as his temple and this verse ends with Nandi, the guru, as the one who knows. பொதுஅது வான (become common) for 1722's புதுஉணர்வான (of new awareness) changes the epithet of the eight worlds.

reading: He is water, earth, sky, fire and wind, and the light that dwells in the body; his name is the Supreme beyond the supreme, Pinakan, our Lord, and he who rides is the all-containing, the unwasting.
nuance: The five elements and the light in the body echo the old list of the Lord's eight forms, though the verse names only six. தூரும் and ஊரும் சகலன் are unclear: ஊரும் may be 'who rides (the bull)' or 'whose town'; சகலன் may mean the all-containing or, in Siddhanta usage, the one in the sakala state.

reading: The three thousand Tamil verses Mulan spoke, the three hundred mantras Mulan spoke, the thirty teachings Mulan spoke: the three that Mulan spoke are one.
nuance: The verse speaks of Mulan in the third person, like 99, and may be a later colophon. It doesn't say what the three hundred mantras and thirty teachings are; they are sometimes taken as other works ascribed to Tirumular and sometimes as parts of this one. The claim is their unity, not their contents.

title: வாழ்த்து
theme: Benediction (வாழ்த்து): the book closes by blessing the feet of Nandi, the guru who cut away impurity, and of the Lord of true knowledge who has none.

reading: May they live, may they live: my Nandi's holy feet, the feet of the one who cut away impurity, the feet of the one of true knowledge, the feet of the one without impurity.
nuance: Each line repeats வாழ்கவே வாழ்க and names a different holder of the feet. மலமறுத்தான் (who cut away impurity, for others) and மலமிலான் (who has none) can be read as the guru and Siva, or as one being under four names; Tirumular often makes Nandi both.
